comments.text:
/-!
# The 70-language register

The design documents speak of a "70-language tapestry" with one braid strand per language.  This
file fixes a concrete register of 70 languages, chosen to cover every way of laying text on a
surface that QBX has to handle, and connects each entry to the formal results:

* strand `i : Fin 70` carries `language i`; the labelled `70 × 70` linking matrix of a pure braid
  on these strands can be any symmetric integer matrix with zero diagonal
  (`seventy_language_matrix`, `PureLinkingMatrix.lean`);
* every language gets the line layout of its script (`LangInfo.layout`), interpreted relative to
  the direction of the first line, and the layout results of `TextLayout.lean` apply to it.

Directions covered: left-to-right (42), right-to-left (21), top-to-bottom columns (5: Literary
Chinese and Japanese with columns right-to-left; Mongolian, Manchu and SignWriting with columns
left-to-right), bottom-to-top (2: Hanunó'o, Ogham).  Layouts: uniform (64), boustrophedon (archaic
Greek, Sabaean, Hieroglyphic Luwian), reverse boustrophedon (rongorongo, conventionally associated
with Rapa Nui), Ogham edge writing, and Egyptian hieroglyphs whose direction is set by the facing
of the signs (`variable`).  The register also records whether the language is tonal, whether it
is living, and its modality (one signed language, written in SignWriting).

The same table is in `QBX/data/languages/languages70.json` for the Python side.  The data
(directions, tonality, ISO 639-3 codes) are standard reference facts entered by hand; they are not
derived in Lean.  What Lean checks is everything stated about the table: its size, that the codes
are distinct, the counts per class, and the consequences for braids below.

Main results:

* `languages_length`, `languages_iso_nodup` and the class counts;
* `layout_rigid_iff` — a language's layout is rigid exactly when it is not boustrophedon (the
  mirrored lines of boustrophedon are reflections);
* `read_eq_flatten_of_uniform` — for the 65 languages with uniform or sign-resolved layout, the
  surface reading of any text is its logical reading;
* `nonuniform_layout_not_faithful` — for each of the 5 remaining languages there is a two-line
  text whose surface reading closes up to a different number of components, so those texts must
  be normalised to logical order before braiding.
-/

comments.text:
/-!
# Phase 1: soundness and completeness of the limit / colimit checker

The Phase 1 limit engine (`qbx.categorical.limits`, migration `007_limits_colimits.sql`) is given
a diagram `F : J ⥤ C`, recorded as a graph of nodes and arrows, and a candidate cone: an apex `L`
and legs `π_j : L ⟶ F(j)`.  It checks

* **commutativity** (write-time tier): `π_i ≫ F(f) = π_j` for every recorded arrow `f : i ⟶ j`;
* **existence** (batch tier): every other cone `(X, σ)` has a mediator `m : X ⟶ L` with
  `m ≫ π_j = σ_j` for every node `j`;
* **uniqueness** (batch tier): the legs are *jointly monic* — two morphisms `m, m' : X ⟶ L`
  with `m ≫ π_j = m' ≫ π_j` for every `j` are equal.

Colimits are checked dually (cocone commutativity, a mediator out of the colimit apex, legs
jointly epic).

Results:

* `coneOfGenerators`, `coneOfEdges` (and the cocone duals): commutativity checked only on a
  generating set of arrows — for a diagram presented by a graph, on its edges — already yields a
  cone (and cocone), with exactly the checked legs.
* `nonempty_isLimit_iff`, `nonempty_isColimit_iff`: a cone is a limit **iff** existence and
  joint monicity hold (dually for colimits).  So the checks are sound and complete, and
  "exactly one mediator for every cone" may be split into the two checks above; the uniqueness
  half needs no enumeration of cones.
* `isLimitOfChecks`, `isColimitOfChecks`: the packaged soundness statements.
* `existence_not_sufficient`, `jointlyMonic_not_sufficient`: neither half implies that the cone
  is a limit (empty diagram in `Type`: apex `Bool`, resp. apex `PEmpty`), so both are checked.
-/

/-- The cone with apex `X` and legs `π`, when the triangles `π_i ≫ F(f) = π_j` commute on a set
`S` of morphisms generating `J`. -/

/-- The cocone with apex `X` and legs `ι`, when the triangles `F(f) ≫ ι_j = ι_i` commute on a
set `S` of morphisms generating `J`. -/

/-- **Graph-presented diagrams.**  For a diagram out of the path category of a quiver (a diagram
recorded as nodes and arrows), commutativity on each arrow gives a cone. -/
/-- Dual of `coneOfEdges`. -/

/-- **Limit check, sound and complete.**  A cone is a limit iff every cone has a mediator into
it and its legs are jointly monic. -/

/-- **Colimit check, sound and complete.**  A cocone is a colimit iff it has a mediator into
every cocone and its legs are jointly epic. -/

/-- **Soundness, packaged.**  Legs commuting on a generating set of arrows, with a mediator for
every cone and jointly monic legs, form a limit cone with apex `L` and exactly these legs. -/
/-- Dual of `isLimitOfChecks`. -/

/-- **Existence alone is not enough.**  Over the empty diagram in `Type`, the cone with apex
`Bool` receives a mediator from every cone, but it is not a limit (its legs, there are none, are
not jointly monic: `id` and `fun _ => true` agree on every leg). -/

/-- **Joint monicity alone is not enough.**  Over the empty diagram in `Type`, the cone with
apex `PEmpty` has jointly monic legs, but it is not a limit (the cone with apex `PUnit` has no
mediator into it). -/

/-!
# Lineages, trees and witnesses (milestones M2–M3 of the cross-domain plan)

Second Lean layer of `docs/CROSS_DOMAIN_INVARIANTS_PLAN_2026-10-14.md`.

**F. Tree or network?  The four-point condition** (plan W2.1).
* `FourPoint d`: for every four points the largest of `d a b + d c d`, `d a c + d b d`,
  `d a d + d b c` is attained twice (each is at most the maximum of the other two).  Decidable for
  finite tables of natural numbers, so a data table can be checked with `decide`.
* `splitMetric`: the distance obtained from a family of weighted splits (bipartitions); two points
  are at distance the total weight of the splits that separate them.  The edges of a weighted tree
  give exactly such a family, and the family is then pairwise `Compatible`.
* `fourPoint_of_compatible`: **every compatible split system gives a four-point metric.**  This is
  the direction "descent along a tree ⇒ the four-point condition".
* `cycle4_not_fourPoint`, `cycle4_eq_splitMetric`: the 4-cycle metric (contact between neighbours)
  fails the condition, and it is the split metric of two *incompatible* splits.  Failure of the
  four-point condition is the signature of reticulation (borrowing, contact).

**G. Duality of the regular solids** (plan W5.2).
* `platonicVEF_dual`: `{p, q} ↦ {q, p}` swaps `V` and `F` and keeps `E`, for every `p, q`.
* `spherical_comm`, `flat_comm`: the dual of a regular solid (tiling) is again one.

**H. Error correction beyond simple majority** (plan W1.1–W1.3).
* `unique_decoding`: in a code of minimum distance `d`, a word within distance `< d/2` of a
  codeword is strictly closer to it than to any other codeword.
* `no_decoder_beyond_half`: sharpness, for any two codewords `c ≠ c'` there is a word within
  distance `⌈dist(c,c')/2⌉` of both, so no decoder corrects every pattern of that weight.
* `branch_majority`: one vote per independent branch recovers the archetype when fewer than half
  of the branches are corrupted (this is `majority_unique` applied to branches).
* `naive_outvoted`, `stemma_counterexample`: counting every surviving manuscript instead can be
  outvoted by a single prolific corrupted branch.
* `shared_error_common_ancestor`, `shared_error_needs_no_homoplasy`: Lachmann's shared-error
  criterion holds when each error arises only once; without that hypothesis it fails.

What is **not** formalized: the converse of `fourPoint_of_compatible` (Buneman: every four-point
metric comes from a tree), and the correspondence between compatible split systems and trees.
-/
/-! ## F. The four-point condition -/

/-- A split of `X` is a two-colouring `s : X → Bool`.  It separates `x` and `y` when they get
different colours.  `sepW s x y` is `1` if separated, `0` otherwise. -/
/-- The distance generated by a finite family of weighted splits. -/

/-- Two splits are compatible when one of the four quadrants `{s = u, t = v}` is empty.  The
splits cut out by the edges of one tree are pairwise compatible. -/
/-- The split `s` cuts the quartet as `ab | ce`. -/
/-- Two compatible splits cannot cut the same quartet in two different ways. -/

/-- Per-split contribution, when the split cuts neither `ab|ce` nor `ac|be`: the first two
pair-sums get the same contribution and the third gets no more. -/

/-- Core lemma: if no split of the family cuts `ab|ce` or `ac|be`, then the first two pair-sums
are equal and dominate the third. -/
/-- The split metric is symmetric. -/

/-- **Tree metrics satisfy the four-point condition.** If the splits are pairwise compatible and
the weights nonnegative, the split metric satisfies `FourPoint`. -/
-- the three ways to cut the quartet are mutually exclusive across the family

/-- The 4-cycle metric `0 – 1 – 2 – 3 – 0`: neighbours at distance 1, opposite points at
distance 2 (four groups each in contact with two neighbours). -/
/-- **Contact breaks the four-point condition.** -/

/-- The 4-cycle metric is the split metric of the two splits `{0,1}|{2,3}` and `{1,2}|{3,0}`
with weight 1 each. -/
/-- … and these two splits are incompatible: each of the four quadrants is inhabited. -/
/-! ## G. Duality of the regular solids -/

/-- **Duality.** Exchanging `p` and `q` swaps the vertex and face counts and keeps the edge
count, for every Schläfli symbol `{p, q}`. -/
/-- The dual of a regular solid is a regular solid. -/
/-- The dual of a regular tiling is a regular tiling. -/
/-! ## H. Error correction: codes, branches and stemmata -/

/-- **Unique decoding radius.** In a code `C` whose distinct codewords are at Hamming distance at
least `d`, a word `y` with `2 · dist(y, c) < d` is strictly closer to `c` than to any other
codeword.  Nearest-codeword decoding therefore corrects every error pattern of weight `< d/2`. -/

/-- **Sharpness.** For any two words `c, c'` there is a word `y` within distance
`⌈dist(c,c')/2⌉` of both.  So if `c, c'` are codewords at the minimum distance `d`, no decoder
can correct every error pattern of weight `⌈d/2⌉`: whatever it outputs on `y` is wrong for one of
the two. -/
/-- Two different readings cannot both hold a strict majority. -/

/-- **One vote per branch.** `r j` is the reading of the head of branch `j` (an independent
descendant of the archetype).  If fewer than half of the `m` branches are corrupted, the
archetype reading `a` is the only strict-majority reading among the branches. -/

/-- **Counting manuscripts instead of branches.** Witness `i` is a copy of the head of branch
`par i` (copied faithfully, so it inherits that branch's reading).  If one branch accounts for
more than half of all surviving witnesses, the naive vote over witnesses returns that branch's
reading, whatever the other branches say. -/

/-- **A concrete stemma where the naive vote fails.** Three branches read `a, a, b` (only one
corrupted branch, below the branch threshold), but the corrupted branch survives in three copies
and the others in one each.  The branch vote returns `a`; the vote over the five witnesses
returns `b`. -/

/-- A copying history: `anc u v` says that `u` is `v` or one of its ancestors, `root` is the
archetype, and `intro u` is the set of errors first made in copy `u`. -/
/-- Copy `v` carries error `e` when some ancestor (or `v` itself) introduced it. -/

/-- **Lachmann's shared-error criterion.** Assume the archetype introduces no errors and every
error is introduced in only one copy (no independent repetition of the same error).  Then two
copies sharing an error have a common ancestor other than the archetype. -/

/-- **The no-repetition hypothesis is needed.** Archetype `0` with two independent copies `1, 2`
that each make the same error: they share the error, but their only common ancestor is the
archetype. -/

/-!
# The strand-crossing (linking) matrix of a braid

`QBX/docs/design/plan_2.md` proposes a symmetric matrix of integer linking numbers between strands
as a gauge-invariant summary of a multi-strand braid (the "70 × 70 cross-language linking
matrix").  This file builds that matrix on the QBX braid group and proves it is well defined.

**Scope of the invariance.**  The matrix is an invariant of the *braid* (it is unchanged by the
rewrite rules R01–R03 and depends only on the braid group element), but it is **not** an invariant
of the closed link: a single Markov conjugation move changes it, even up to relabelling the strands
(`crossMatrix_not_markov_invariant`, `crossMatrix_not_markov_invariant_up_to_relabel` in
`StrandMatrixMarkov.lean`).  The link invariants are the linking numbers between closure
components (`ClosureLinking.lean`).

For a braid, `crossMatrix g a b` is the signed number of crossings between the strands that
*start* at positions `a` and `b`: each crossing `σᵢ^{±1}` adds `±1` to the entry of the two
strands currently at positions `i, i + 1`.  Together with the permutation this is a map into the
semidirect product `ℤ^{n×n} ⋊ Sₙ` (`Sₙ` relabels rows and columns).

* `crossHom` — the homomorphism `Bₙ →* ℤ^{n×n} ⋊ Sₙ` (the braid relations are checked on
  generators: `crossGen_braid`, `crossGen_comm`), so the matrix depends only on the braid.
* `crossHom_right` — its permutation part is the existing `permHom`.
* `crossMatrix_symm`, `crossMatrix_diag` — the matrix is symmetric with zero diagonal.
* `Word.crossMatrix_eq_of_eqvGen` — words related by the QBX rewrite rules R01–R03 have the same
  crossing matrix.
* `crossMatrix_sigma_sq` — for the Hopf-link braid `σ₁²` the off-diagonal entry is `2`.

For a pure braid the closure has one component per strand and the linking number of components
`a ≠ b` is `crossMatrix g a b / 2` (so the Hopf link has linking number 1); in general the linking
number of two closure components `C, D` is `½ Σ_{a ∈ C, b ∈ D} crossMatrix g a b`.  The closure
components, the integrality of these linking numbers and their invariance under both Markov moves
are proved in `ClosureLinking.lean`.
-/
/-- Integer matrices indexed by strand labels, written multiplicatively. -/
/-- Relabelling rows and columns by a permutation. -/
/-- The pattern of one crossing between the strands labelled `a` and `b`. -/
/-- The image of the generator `σᵢ`. -/
/-- The crossing-matrix homomorphism `Bₙ →* ℤ^{n×n} ⋊ Sₙ`. -/
/-- The strand-crossing matrix of a braid group element. -/
/-- Symmetric with zero diagonal. -/
/-- The Hopf-link braid `σ₁²`: the two strands cross twice positively. -/
/-- The crossing matrix is symmetric. -/
/-- The crossing matrix has zero diagonal. -/
/-- The crossing matrix of a word. -/
/-- Words related by the rewrite rules R01–R03 have the same crossing matrix. -/

/-!
# Audit of two structural claims in `logos-8.md`

`QBX/docs/design/logos-8.md` proposes a "geometric language" in which hashes are projected to
`ℝ⁸` / `T⁸`.  Most of its 108 "predictions" are empirical statistics of a Python engine that is
not in this repository, so they cannot be checked here.  Two claims are structural and can be
settled exactly:

1. **Negation as an orthogonal involution.**  §4 of the note says the negation `¬A` of a statement
   is an orthogonal (Weyl) reflection of `v_A` with `⟨v_A, v_{¬A}⟩ = 0`.  A reflection is an
   involution (`¬¬A = A`).  `no_involutive_orthogonal_negation`: in any real inner product space,
   an additive map `N` with `N ∘ N = id` and `⟨v, N v⟩ = 0` for *every* `v` exists only on the
   zero space.  So the two requirements cannot both hold for all propositions; at most one of
   them can be kept (`orthogonal_negation_example` shows the orthogonality alone is fine: a
   quarter turn, which squares to `-1`, not `1`).

2. **Information content.**  The note credits a token with "≥ 3,520 bits" of continuous field
   data derived from a 256-bit digest.  `card_range_le`: whatever the encoding, a deterministic
   function of a 256-bit digest takes at most `2²⁵⁶` distinct values, so the tokens carry at most
   256 bits; the extra floating-point coordinates are redundant re-descriptions, not information.
   (`envelope_card`: the discrete envelope `240 · 30 · 33 · 5 · 16 = 19 008 000` states, which is
   the stated `≈ 24.18` bits, is correct arithmetic.)

See `QBX/docs/design/BRAID_BIOLOGY_STEIN_TWIN.md` §6.
-/
/-- **No involutive negation is orthogonal to every statement** (unless the space is `0`). -/

/-- Orthogonality alone is possible: the quarter turn of `ℝ²` is orthogonal to every vector —
but it squares to `-1`, so `¬¬A = -A`, not `A`. -/
/-- **A token computed from a 256-bit digest carries at most 256 bits.** -/
/-- The discrete envelope of a Logos-8 word: root × petal × charge × shell × formant. -/

/-!
# WS1 — the geometry of `Q_n □ T^k_M`, formally

Lean counterpart of the four guarantees of `foundation/ws1_geometry/README.md` (properties
P1.1–P1.4 of `PROPERTIES.md`), built on `Addr`, `cycDist` and `addrDist` of
`QBX/Formal/HypercubeGates.lean`.

* **Metric (guarantee 1, P1.1).** `cycDist_triangle`, `cycDist_comm`, `cycDist_eq_zero_iff`;
  `addrDist_triangle`, `addrDist_comm`, `addrDist_eq_zero_iff`.  `cycDist_eq_min` is the Python
  formula `min(d, m − d)`.
* **The graph.** `addrGraph n k M`: vertices are addresses, edges are single moves (`IsMove`: a bit
  flip or a `±1` step on one cycle — the moves of `MixedRadixSpace.neighbors`).
  `addrGraph_adj_iff` (adjacent ⟺ distance 1, P1.3), `exists_isMove_addrDist` (a greedy step always
  exists, P1.4).
* **Shortest-path metric (guarantees 1–2, P1.2).** `addrGraph_dist`: the graph distance is
  `addrDist`; `exists_walk_length_eq_addrDist`, `addrDist_le_length`; `addrGraph_connected`.
* **Vertex-transitivity (guarantee 3).** `addrGraph_vertexTransitive`: translations
  (`translateIso`) are graph automorphisms acting transitively (on the whole product, in
  particular on `Q_n` for `k = 0`).
* **Isometric embedding (guarantee 4).** `embedBits : {0,1}^n → T^n_m`; for `m ≠ 1`
  `addrDist_embedBits` (torus metric = Hamming distance), `torus_dist_embedBits` (graph distances
  agree with those of the hypercube graph), `embedBits_injective`.
* **Balls and spheres (P1.5).** `walkBall_eq`, `walkSphere_eq`: the breadth-first ball
  (walks of at most `r` moves) is `{v : d(c,v) ≤ r}`, the sphere is `{v : d(c,v) = r}`.
* **Geodesic convexity (guarantee 4, previously open).** `embedBits_geodesicallyConvex`: every
  shortest walk in `T^n_m` between two points of `{0,1}^n` stays in `{0,1}^n` — for every `m`
  (via the metric betweenness statement `exists_embedBits_of_between`).

All moduli are arbitrary naturals (`ZMod 0 = ℤ` is the infinite line); Python requires `m ≥ 2`.
-/
/-! ### The cycle metric -/
/-- Greedy step on a cycle: one of the two unit steps reduces the distance by exactly one. -/

/-- The Python formula: with `d = (x - y) mod m`, `MixedRadixSpace.distance` uses
`min(d, m - d)` on each cycle; this is `cycDist`. -/
/-! ### The hypercube factor -/
/-- Flip bit `i`. -/
/-- Greedy step on the hypercube: flipping a differing bit reduces the Hamming distance by one. -/
/-! ### The graph `Q_n □ T^k_M` and its metric -/
/-- Flip bit `i` of an address (Python: `step(a, EdgeLabel("bit", i, 1))`). -/
/-- Move along cycle `j` by `δ` (Python: `step(a, EdgeLabel("cycle", j, δ))` with `δ = ±1`). -/

/-- `b` is obtained from `a` by one edge label: a bit flip or a `±1` step on one cycle
(exactly the moves enumerated by `MixedRadixSpace.neighbors`). -/
/-- The graph `Q_n □ T^k_M`: vertices are addresses, edges are single moves. -/

/-- **Greedy routing** (P1.4, `greedy_next`): from `a ≠ b` some single move reduces the
distance to `b` by exactly one. -/
/-- Adjacency in `Q_n □ T^k_M` is exactly distance one (P1.3). -/
/-- A walk of length `addrDist a b` from `a` to `b` (P1.2, `shortest_path`). -/
/-- No walk is shorter than `addrDist`. -/

/-- **WS1 guarantees 1–2.** `addrDist` (`MixedRadixSpace.distance`) is the shortest-path
metric of the graph `Q_n □ T^k_M`. -/
/-! ### Vertex-transitivity -/
/-- Translation by `(c, t)`: xor the bits with `c` and add `t` to the cycles. -/
/-- Translations are graph automorphisms of `Q_n □ T^k_M`. -/

/-- **WS1 guarantee 3 (vertex-transitivity).**  The automorphism group of `Q_n □ T^k_M` acts
transitively: there is no privileged origin.  (For `k = 0` this is the hypercube `Q_n`.) -/
/-! ### The hypercube inside the torus: isometric and geodesically convex -/
/-- The hypercube `Q_n` as the address space with no cycles. -/
/-- The inclusion `{0,1}^n ⊂ (ℤ/m)^n = T^n_m`. -/
/-- Distance in the hypercube is the Hamming distance. -/
/-- The two images of a bit are at cyclic distance at most one. -/

/-- **WS1 guarantee 4, isometry (metric form).**  For `m ≠ 1` (in particular every `m ≥ 2`) the
torus metric restricted to `{0,1}^n` is the Hamming distance. -/

/-- **WS1 guarantee 4, isometric embedding.**  For `m ≠ 1`, `x ↦ embedBits x` is an isometric
embedding of the hypercube graph `Q_n` into the torus graph `T^n_m`. -/
/-- For `m ≠ 1` the inclusion `{0,1}^n ⊂ T^n_m` is injective. -/

/-- Betweenness: a point of the torus lying metrically between two points of `{0,1}^n` lies in
`{0,1}^n`.  (No hypothesis on `m` is needed.) -/

/-- **WS1 guarantee 4, geodesic convexity (the open item of `PROPERTIES.md`).**  Every shortest
walk in the torus graph `T^n_m` between two points of `{0,1}^n` stays inside `{0,1}^n`.
This holds for every `m`; for `m = 2` the two spaces coincide. -/
/-! ### Balls and spheres (P1.5) -/

/-- The ball of `routing.ball`: everything reachable from `c` by a walk of at most `r` moves
(what the breadth-first search with depth limit `r` collects). -/
/-- The sphere of `routing.sphere`: the points of the ball at distance exactly `r`. -/
/-- **P1.5 (ball).** The ball equals `{v : d(c,v) ≤ r}`. -/
/-- **P1.5 (sphere).** The sphere equals `{v : d(c,v) = r}`. -/

/-!
# Phase 1: Governance modalities — Kripke semantics of policy checks

Migration `015_governance_modalities.sql` and `qbx.governance` attach policies to artifacts
through four seeded modal operators: `□` (necessity), `◇` (possibility), `!` (obligation) and
`?` (permission).  Policy checks are evaluated over a finite set of *contexts* (worlds) with two
accessibility relations (`governance_access`): the **alethic** frame for `□`/`◇` and the
**deontic** frame for `!`/`?`.  A check of a policy at a context `w` records an outcome for
contexts; with `p` the set of contexts whose outcome is `true`, the check holds when

* `□`, `!`: every context accessible from `w` is in `p` (`box`);
* `◇`, `?`: some context accessible from `w` is in `p` (`dia`).

The ledger requires the alethic frame to be reflexive and transitive and the deontic frame to be
serial.  This file shows that these are exactly the right conditions:

* `dia_eq_compl_box_compl`, `holds_dual`: `◇ = ¬□¬` and `? = ¬!¬`.
* `box_subset_self_iff`, `box_subset_box_box_iff`, `subset_dia_iff`, `dia_dia_subset_iff`:
  `□p ⊆ p` for all `p` iff the frame is reflexive, `□p ⊆ □□p` iff it is transitive (dually for
  `◇`).  So `□` is a comonad (an interior operator) and `◇` a monad (a closure operator) on the
  poset of propositions exactly when the alethic frame is a preorder: `boxComonad`,
  `diaMonad`, `diaClosure`.
* `box_subset_dia_iff_serial`: `!p ⊆ ?p` for all `p` (deontic axiom D: what is obligatory is
  permitted) iff the deontic frame is serial.
* `result`, `result_eq_pass_iff`: the result the database computes for a check (`pass`, or
  `warn`/`fail` by enforcement level) is `pass` exactly when the modal formula holds.
* `necessity_pass_outcome`, `necessity_pass_stable`, `obligation_pass_permission_pass`: on
  well-formed frames a passed `□` check implies the outcome at the context itself, a passed `□`
  check passes at every accessible context, and a passed `!` check passes as a `?` check.
* `chainHash_injective`: the audit log's hash chain — each record hashes the previous record's
  hash with its own payload — commits to the whole log: if the step hash is injective and never
  returns the genesis value, equal final hashes mean equal logs.
-/
/-! ## Box and diamond -/
/-- `□p` at `w`: every context accessible from `w` satisfies `p`. -/
/-- `◇p` at `w`: some context accessible from `w` satisfies `p`. -/
/-- Axiom T for `□` characterises reflexive frames. -/
/-- Axiom 4 for `□` characterises transitive frames. -/
/-- Axiom T for `◇` characterises reflexive frames. -/
/-- Axiom 4 for `◇` characterises transitive frames. -/
/-- Axiom D (`!p → ?p`) characterises serial frames. -/
/-! ## `◇` as a monad and `□` as a comonad on a preorder frame -/
/-- On a reflexive and transitive frame, `◇` is a closure operator. -/

/-- On a reflexive and transitive frame, `◇` is a monad on the poset category of propositions:
the unit is `p ⊆ ◇p` (T) and the multiplication is `◇◇p ⊆ ◇p` (4). -/

/-- On a reflexive and transitive frame, `□` is a comonad on the poset category of
propositions: the counit is `□p ⊆ p` (T) and the comultiplication is `□p ⊆ □□p` (4). -/
/-! ## Policy checks -/
/-- The four seeded modalities (`modality.kind`). -/
/-- The frame a modality is evaluated on (`governance_seed_modalities().frame`). -/
/-- Universal modalities (`□`, `!`) quantify over all accessible contexts. -/
/-- The modal formula of a check: `p` holds at `w` under modality `k` on frame `R`. -/
/-- Each universal modality has its existential dual: `◇p ↔ ¬□¬p` and `?p ↔ ¬!¬p`. -/
/-- Enforcement levels (`policy.enforcement_level`). -/
/-- Results of a check (`policy_check_log.result`). -/

/-- The result the database computes: `pass` when the formula holds, otherwise `warn` for a
soft policy and `fail` for a hard or blocking one. -/
/-- On a reflexive frame a passed `□` check implies the outcome at the context itself. -/
/-- On a transitive frame a passed `□` check passes at every accessible context. -/
/-- On a serial frame a passed `!` check passes as a `?` check (axiom D). -/
/-! ## The audit hash chain -/

/-- The hash of a log (newest record first): the genesis value for the empty log, and
`step (hash of the older records) payload` for each record. -/
/-- The final hash commits to the whole log. -/

declarations.signature_heuristic:
def monadOfChecks (T : C ⥤ C)
    (η : ∀ X, X ⟶ T.obj X) (μ : ∀ X, T.obj (T.obj X) ⟶ T.obj X)
    (S : MorphismProperty C) (hS : S.multiplicativeClosure = ⊤)
    (hη : ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y), S f → f ≫ η Y = η X ≫ T.map f)
    (hμ : ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y), S f → T.map (T.map f) ≫ μ Y = μ X ≫ T.map f)
    (left_unit : ∀ X, T.map (η X) ≫ μ X = 𝟙 (T.obj X))
    (right_unit : ∀ X, η (T.obj X) ≫ μ X = 𝟙 (T.obj X))
    (assoc : ∀ X, T.map (μ X) ≫ μ X = μ (T.obj X) ≫ μ X) : Monad C where
  toFunctor

    (ε : ∀ X, G.obj X ⟶ X) (δ : ∀ X, G.obj X ⟶ G.obj (G.obj X))
    (S : MorphismProperty C) (hS : S.multiplicativeClosure = ⊤)
    (hε : ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y), S f → G.map f ≫ ε Y = ε X ≫ f)
    (hδ : ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y), S f → G.map f ≫ δ Y = δ X ≫ G.map (G.map f))
    (left_counit : ∀ X, δ X ≫ ε (G.obj X) = 𝟙 (G.obj X))
    (right_counit : ∀ X, δ X ≫ G.map (ε X) = 𝟙 (G.obj X))

  toFunctor

theorem exists_monad_iff_laws (T : C ⥤ C) (η : 𝟭 C ⟶ T) (μ : T ⋙ T ⟶ T) :
    (∃ M : Monad C, M.toFunctor = T ∧ HEq M.η η ∧ HEq M.μ μ) ↔
      (∀ X, T.map (η.app X) ≫ μ.app X = 𝟙 (T.obj X)) ∧
        (∀ X, η.app (T.obj X) ≫ μ.app X = 𝟙 (T.obj X)) ∧
          (∀ X, T.map (μ.app X) ≫ μ.app X = μ.app (T.obj X) ≫ μ.app X)

declarations.name: exists_comonad_iff_laws

    (∃ W : Comonad C, W.toFunctor = G ∧ HEq W.ε ε ∧ HEq W.δ δ) ↔
      (∀ X, δ.app X ≫ ε.app (G.obj X) = 𝟙 (G.obj X)) ∧
        (∀ X, δ.app X ≫ G.map (ε.app X) = 𝟙 (G.obj X)) ∧
          (∀ X, δ.app X ≫ δ.app (G.obj X) = δ.app X ≫ G.map (δ.app X))

/-!
# Phase 1: soundness and completeness of the monad / comonad checker

The Phase 1 monad engine (`qbx.categorical.monad`, migration `006_monad_comonad.sql`) is given
an endofunctor `T : C ⥤ C` and components

* `η_X : X ⟶ T(X)` (the unit) and
* `μ_X : T(T(X)) ⟶ T(X)` (the multiplication).

It checks the naturality squares of `η` and `μ` (migration 004, possibly only on a generating
set of morphisms, `naturality_of_generators`) and three laws, object by object.  In the
database's naming, with composition written diagrammatically (`f ≫ g` = first `f`, then `g`):

* `left_unit`:     `T(η_X) ≫ μ_X = 𝟙 (T X)`;
* `right_unit`:    `η_{T(X)} ≫ μ_X = 𝟙 (T X)`;
* `associativity`: `T(μ_X) ≫ μ_X = μ_{T(X)} ≫ μ_X`.

(Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Monad` names the two unit laws the other way round:
`Monad.left_unit` is `right_unit` here and `Monad.right_unit` is `left_unit` here.)

Results:

* `monadOfChecks` (soundness): data passing every check is a Mathlib `Monad` with the checked
  functor and components; `comonadOfChecks` is the dual for comonads.
* `exists_monad_iff_laws`, `exists_comonad_iff_laws` (soundness and completeness): natural
  transformations are the structure maps of a monad (comonad) iff the three laws hold at
  every object.
* `left_unit_independent`, `right_unit_independent`, `assoc_independent` (necessity): none of
  the three monad laws follows from the other two, even for natural `η` and `μ`; so a checker
  that skips any one of them accepts non-monads.
-/

/-- **Soundness of the monad engine.**  Components `η_X : X ⟶ T X` and
`μ_X : T (T X) ⟶ T X` whose naturality squares commute on a generating set `S` and which
satisfy the three checked laws at every object form a monad with underlying functor `T`. -/

/-- **Soundness of the comonad engine.**  Components `ε_X : G X ⟶ X` and
`δ_X : G X ⟶ G (G X)` whose naturality squares commute on a generating set `S` and which
satisfy the three checked laws (`left_counit`: `δ_X ≫ ε_{G X} = 𝟙`, `right_counit`:
`δ_X ≫ G(ε_X) = 𝟙`, `coassociativity`: `δ_X ≫ δ_{G X} = δ_X ≫ G(δ_X)`) form a comonad with
underlying functor `G`. -/

/-- **The three checks decide monads.**  Natural transformations `η : 𝟭 C ⟶ T` and
`μ : T ⋙ T ⟶ T` are the unit and multiplication of a monad with underlying functor `T` if
and only if `left_unit`, `right_unit` and `associativity` hold at every object. -/
/-- **The three checks decide comonads** (dual of `exists_monad_iff_laws`). -/

/-! ### None of the three monad laws follows from the other two

All three counterexamples are "writer" functors on `Type`: `T X = X × M` for a type `M` with an
element `e` and a binary operation `op`, with `η_X x = (x, e)` and
`μ_X ((x, a), b) = (x, op a b)`.  These are natural for every `e` and `op`, and

* `left_unit` holds iff `e` is a left identity of `op`,
* `right_unit` holds iff `e` is a right identity of `op`,
* `associativity` holds iff `op` is associative.

So a left-zero semigroup, a right-zero semigroup, and a non-associative unital magma separate
the three laws. -/
/-- The writer functor `X ↦ X × M` on `Type`. -/
/-- The unit `x ↦ (x, e)` of the writer functor. -/
/-- The multiplication `((x, a), b) ↦ (x, op a b)` of the writer functor. -/

/-- **`left_unit` is not implied by `right_unit` and `associativity`**, even for natural `η`
and `μ`: the writer monad of the left-zero semigroup `op a b = a` on `Bool`. -/

/-- **`right_unit` is not implied by `left_unit` and `associativity`**, even for natural `η`
and `μ`: the writer monad of the right-zero semigroup `op a b = b` on `Bool`. -/

/-- A unital, non-associative operation on `ℕ`: `0` is a two-sided identity and
`a · b = a + 1` for `a, b ≠ 0`. -/

/-- **`associativity` is not implied by the two unit laws**, even for natural `η` and `μ`:
the writer construction for the unital magma `magmaOp`, where
`(1 · 1) · 1 = 3 ≠ 2 = 1 · (1 · 1)`. -/

/-!
# Multi-edge forks: which simultaneous changes the flatness check can see (F6)

Extends the single-edge result F5 (`perturb_detected_iff_not_isBridge`) to forks that change an
arbitrary set of events.  For two connections `c c'` on the same graph, `diffEdges c c'` is the
set of edges on which their transports differ.

* `diffEdges_eq_levelCut` (**F6, ⇒**): if `c` and `c'` are both flat, the changed edges are
  exactly the edges whose endpoints lie in different level sets of the vertex function
  `φ x = p x * (p' x)⁻¹` (`p`, `p'` potentials of `c`, `c'`) — a union of edge cuts.
* `exists_flat_diffEdges_eq_levelCut` (**F6, ⇐**): conversely every level-set cut of every
  `φ : V → K` is the change set of some flat connection.  (The construction acts on the
  potentials, `x ↦ (φ x)⁻¹ * p x`; the naive gauge action `φ u⁻¹ * c u v * φ v` would also change
  edges with `φ u = φ v` when `K` is non-abelian.)
* `diffEdges_eq_empty_of_isEdgeConnected`, `not_isFlat_of_isEdgeConnected` (**F6a**): on a
  `k`-edge-connected graph, a fork that changes fewer than `k` edges of a flat connection is
  always detected.
* `perturb_detected_of_isEdgeConnected_two` (**F6b**): on a 2-edge-connected graph every
  single-edge fork is detected; `not_isBridge_of_isEdgeConnected_two` connects it to F5.
* `exists_flat_diffEdges_eq_boundary` and `exists_undetectable_fork_of_not_isEdgeReachable`
  (**F6c**): every edge cut carries an undetectable fork, so the threshold `k` of F6a is exact:
  if two connected vertices can be separated by deleting fewer than `k` edges, some flat
  connection differs from `c` on a non-empty set of fewer than `k` edges.
-/
/-- The edges on which two connections disagree. -/
/-- The pure-gauge connection with potentials `p`. -/
/-- The edges whose endpoints take different values under `φ` (a union of edge cuts). -/
/-- The edge boundary of a vertex set `A`: the edges with exactly one endpoint in `A`. -/
/-- Two descriptions of a set of edges agree if they agree pointwise on adjacent pairs. -/
/-- Group identity behind F6: `a'⁻¹ b' = a⁻¹ b ↔ a a'⁻¹ = b b'⁻¹`. -/

/-- **F6 (⇒).** Two flat connections differ exactly on the level-set cut of
`φ x = p x * (p' x)⁻¹`, for any potentials `p` of `c` and `p'` of `c'`. -/
/-- **F6 (⇒).** If `c` and `c'` are both flat, the set of changed edges is a level-set cut. -/

/-- **F6 (⇐), explicit.** Re-gauging the potentials by `φ` changes exactly the level-set cut
of `φ`. -/

/-- **F6 (⇐).** Every level-set cut of every `φ : V → K` is the change set of a flat
connection. -/
/-- A function that is constant along every edge of `H` is constant on `H`-reachable pairs. -/

/-- **F6a.** On a `k`-edge-connected graph, two flat connections that differ on fewer than `k`
edges are equal on every edge. -/

/-- **F6a, detection form.** On a `k`-edge-connected graph, changing a flat connection on a
non-empty set of fewer than `k` edges always breaks flatness: such a fork is detected. -/
/-- A 2-edge-connected graph has no bridges. -/

/-- **F6b.** On a 2-edge-connected graph every non-trivial single-edge fork of a flat
connection is detected (via F5 and `not_isBridge_of_isEdgeConnected_two`). -/

/-- The level-set cut of the indicator-like function `k` on `A`, `1` elsewhere, is the edge
boundary of `A` (for `k ≠ 1`). -/

/-- **F6c.** Every edge cut carries an undetectable fork: for any vertex set `A` there is a flat
connection differing from `c` exactly on the edge boundary of `A`. -/
/-- A walk from inside `A` to outside `A` crosses the edge boundary of `A`. -/

/-- **F6c, exactness of F6a.** If `u` and `v` are connected but can be separated by deleting
fewer than `k` edges (`¬ G.IsEdgeReachable k u v`), then some flat connection differs from the
flat connection `c` on a non-empty set of fewer than `k` edges: a fork of that size that no
holonomy check detects.  Together with F6a, the minimum size of an undetectable fork on a
connected graph is exactly its edge connectivity. -/

/-!
# Polytope-fold channel: paths on the permutohedron and the Garside fold

Channel 1 of the five-channel machine (`QBX/docs/design/MULTIPROVER.md`).  The vertices of the
permutohedron `Pₙ` are the permutations of `n` letters, and its edges join `p` and
`p · sᵢ` for the adjacent transpositions `sᵢ`: the 1-skeleton is the Cayley graph of `Sₙ`.

* `foldPath w`: the vertices visited by the word, one letter at a time.  Consecutive vertices
  are joined by a permutohedron edge (`foldPath_step`), the walk starts at the identity
  (`foldPath_head`) and ends at `permHom n w.eval` (`foldPath_last`).
* `foldVertex_eq_one_iff`: the walk closes up exactly when the braid is pure — the
  *kernel test*.  Two words with the same endpoint differ by a pure braid ("hidden" element),
  which the walk cannot see.
* The **Garside fold** `leftNormalForm w = (k, [A₁, …, A_m])` (`BraidNormalForm.lean`) is a
  power of the half twist `Δ` (the long diagonal of `Pₙ`) followed by a path of permutohedron
  vertices `A_i ∉ {1, Δ}`, consecutive ones left-weighted.  Unlike the walk it is a complete
  invariant: `fold_eq_iff` — two words have the same fold iff they are the same braid
  (soundness `eval_eq_of_leftNormalForm_eq` + Garside uniqueness `leftNormalFormComplete`,
  registry H-055–H-057).
-/

/-- The walk of a braid word on the 1-skeleton of the permutohedron: the vertex reached after
each prefix of the word. -/

/-- **Each letter moves along one edge of the permutohedron**: the `(k+1)`-st vertex is the
`k`-th one times the adjacent transposition of the `k`-th letter. -/
/-- The vertex where the walk ends. -/
/-- **Kernel test**: the walk closes up iff the braid is pure. -/
/-- The walk is a braid invariant (it only sees the permutation). -/

/-- **The Garside fold is a complete invariant**: two words have the same fold (normal form,
a path of permutohedron vertices after a power of `Δ`) iff they represent the same braid. -/

/-!
# Faithfulness of the reduced Burau representation of `B₃`

The anchor channel of the five-channel machine (`MULTIPROVER.md`) reads the reduced Burau
matrix.  For three strands this channel is **complete**: the representation is faithful.  This
classical fact was cited in earlier sessions; here it is proved.

Proof outline (all steps formal):

* `bZ_central` : the full twist `Δ² = (σ₁σ₂σ₁)²` is central; `bY_cube` : `(σ₁σ₂)³ = Δ²`.
* `inNF_all` — **normal form**: every `β ∈ B₃` can be written
  `Δ^{2k} · Δ^{ε} · y^{e₁} Δ y^{e₂} Δ ⋯ Δ y^{e_m} · Δ^{ε'}` with `y = σ₁σ₂`, `eᵢ ∈ {1, 2}`,
  `ε, ε' ∈ {0, 1}` and no `Δ Δ` (i.e. `B₃ / ⟨Δ²⟩ ≅ ℤ/2 * ℤ/3` is generated as a free product).
* `coreMat_X_Y` — **ping-pong** at `t = -1`: `ψ(y), ψ(y²)` map the quadrant `xy < 0` of `ℤ²`
  into `xy > 0` and `ψ(Δ)` maps `xy > 0` into `xy < 0`; hence a non-empty core is never `±1`
  (`coreMat_ne_pm_one`) and, by a conjugation that uses `|ℤ/3| = 3`, never `±ψ(Δ)`
  (`coreMat_ne_pm_D`).
* `eq_Zpow_of_psi_eq_one` : if the Burau matrix at `t = -1` is the identity, `β = Δ^{2k}`.
* the writhe of `β` is read from `det ρ̄(β)(2) = (-1)^{len} 2^{writhe}`; `Δ^{2k}` has writhe
  `6k`, so `k = 0`.
* `burau_faithful_three` : `B₃ →* GL₂(ℤ[t, t⁻¹])` is injective; `burau_faithful_word` : a word
  whose Burau matrix is the identity represents the trivial braid.
-/
/-! ### The Garside element and the centre of `B₃` -/
/-- The half twist `Δ = σ₁σ₂σ₁`. -/
/-- The full twist `Δ² = (σ₁σ₂σ₁)²`. -/
/-- **`Δ²` is central in `B₃`.** -/
/-! ### A normal form for `B₃` -/
/-- The core `y^{e₁} Δ y^{e₂} Δ ⋯ Δ y^{e_k}`. -/
/-- `Δ^{2k} · Δ^{pre} · core · Δ^{post}`. -/
/-- Reducedness: an empty core cannot be flanked by two `Δ`s. -/
/-- `g` has a reduced normal form. -/
/-- **Every element of `B₃` has a reduced normal form** `Δ^{2k} Δ^{ε} y^{e₁} Δ ⋯ Δ y^{e_m} Δ^{ε'}`. -/
/-! ### The image in `SL(2, ℤ)` at `t = -1` and ping-pong -/
/-- The image of a core. -/
/-- The quadrants `xy < 0` and `xy > 0`. -/
/-- **Ping-pong**: a core maps the quadrant `xy < 0` into `xy > 0`. -/
/-- A core is never `±ψ(Δ)` (conjugation trick using `|ℤ/3| = 3`). -/
-- `coreMat (e :: es) = ymat e * R`
/-- A non-trivial reduced normal form never maps to `±1` at `t = -1`. -/
/-! ### Faithfulness -/
/-- The reduced Burau representation of `B₃` at `t = -1`, over `ℤ`. -/
/-- At `t = -1`, only the powers of `Δ²` are killed up to sign: if `ψ(β) = 1` then `β = Δ^{2k}`. -/
/-- The full twist has writhe `6`. -/

/-- **Faithfulness of the reduced Burau representation of `B₃`** (word form): a braid word on
three strands whose Burau matrix over `ℤ[t, t⁻¹]` is the identity represents the trivial braid. -/
-- specialise to `t = -1`
-- specialise to `t = 2` over `ℚ`: the writhe vanishes

/-- **Faithfulness of the reduced Burau representation of `B₃`**: the representation
`B₃ →* GL₂(ℤ[t, t⁻¹])` is injective. -/

/-!
# Fano lines and a ten-point configuration for the channels (research questions 3.1, 3.5)

`alphabet_theory/next_steps_distilled.md` asks:

* **3.1** — is there a natural three-way identity for each line of a Fano plane of channels, or
  is the Fano structure imposed?
* **3.5** — is there a canonical ten-point configuration for the tenfold way, analogous to the
  Fano plane for seven?

**Steiner triple systems.** The Fano plane is the Steiner triple system on 7 points: a set of
3-element *lines* such that every two points lie on exactly one line (`IsSTS`).
* `IsSTS.card_mul_card_pred` and `IsSTS.even_card_pred` — the classical counting conditions:
  `v (v − 1) = 6 b` and `v − 1` is even, hence `v ≡ 1, 3 (mod 6)` (`IsSTS.card_mod_six`).
* `fano_isSTS` — the Fano plane is one; `no_sts_five`, `no_sts_ten` — **there is none on 5 or
  on 10 points**.  So five channels cannot carry a Fano-type structure, and the tenfold way has
  no Fano-type analogue (3.5, negative half).
* `desargues_config` — what does exist on ten points is a *configuration* `(10₃)`: the
  Desargues configuration (points = 2-subsets of a 5-set, lines = 3-subsets, incidence =
  inclusion) has 10 lines of 3 points, 3 lines through each point, and two points on at most
  one line (`desargues_two_points`).  It is not a Steiner system: some pairs of points lie on
  no line (`desargues_not_sts`).  Several non-isomorphic `(10₃)` configurations exist (cited,
  not proved here), so none of them is canonical without a further choice.

**Identities among the five existing channels (3.1).** Say a set `S` of channels *determines*
a channel `c` on `n` strands if any two words that agree in every channel of `S` agree in `c`
(`Determines`).  A triple is an *identity line* if any two of its channels determine the third
(`IsIdentityLine`).  On three strands:
* `fold_determines`, `anchor_determines_three` — the fold channel (every `n`) and the anchor
  channel (`n = 3`, Burau faithfulness) each determine every channel;
* `identityLine_fold_anchor` — hence `{fold, anchor, x}` is an identity line for **every**
  third channel `x`;
* `not_identityLine_fold`, `not_identityLine_anchor` — a triple with fold or anchor and two of
  `link`, `harmonic`, `oscillator` is **not** an identity line (`σ₁²` vs `σ₂²`,
  `sq_sq_partial`);
* `identityLines_not_linear` — the identity lines `{fold, anchor, link}` and
  `{fold, anchor, harmonic}` share two points, which two lines of a Steiner triple system never
  do.

So the identities that hold among the existing channels are not the lines of any Fano plane:
the Fano structure would be imposed, not discovered.  That `{link, harmonic, oscillator}` is
not an identity line either, and the full classification, are in `IdentityLines.lean`.
-/
/-! ## Steiner triple systems -/

/-- A Steiner triple system on `α`: lines of three points, every two points on exactly one
line. -/

/-- **Counting pairs.** `v (v − 1) = 6 b` for a Steiner triple system with `v` points and `b`
lines. -/

/-- **Counting through one point.** The lines through a point pair off the other points, so
`v − 1` is even. -/
/-- A Steiner triple system on a non-empty set has `v ≡ 1` or `3 (mod 6)` points. -/
/-- There is no Steiner triple system on five points. -/
/-- There is no Steiner triple system on ten points. -/
/-- The Fano plane: lines `{i, i + 1, i + 3} mod 7`. -/
/-! ## The Desargues configuration -/
/-- Points: the 2-subsets of `Fin 5`. -/
/-- Lines: the 3-subsets of `Fin 5`, a point lies on a line if it is contained in it. -/

/-- **The Desargues configuration is a `(10₃)`**: 10 points, 10 lines of 3 points, 3 lines
through every point. -/
/-- Two points lie on at most one line. -/
/-- The Desargues configuration is not a Steiner triple system. -/
/-! ## Identities among the five channels -/
/-- On `n` strands, the channels in `S` determine the channel `c`. -/
/-- Any two channels of the triple determine the third. -/
/-- The fold channel determines every channel (Garside uniqueness). -/
/-- On three strands the anchor channel determines every channel (Burau is faithful on `B₃`). -/
/-- `{fold, anchor, x}` is an identity line for every channel `x`. -/
/-- `link`, `harmonic` and `oscillator` together determine neither fold nor anchor. -/

/-- **The identity lines are not the lines of a linear space**: two distinct identity lines
share the two points `fold` and `anchor`. -/

/-!
# The Clifford channel: braids as multivectors

The Kauffman–Lomonaco *Clifford braiding theorem*: in a Clifford algebra with anticommuting
generators `c₁, …, cₙ` (all squaring to the same sign), the rotors

  `τₖ = (1 + cₖ₊₁cₖ)/√2`   (and the cyclic one `τₙ = (1 + c₁cₙ)/√2`)

satisfy the braid relations.  This file proves that theorem over any field containing `√2`
(`Setup`, built on Mathlib's `CliffordAlgebra` of the diagonal form `Σ wᵢ vᵢ²`), turns it into a
group homomorphism `Bₙ → Cl(n)ˣ`, and reads off its structure.

| result | statement |
|---|---|
| `rotor_braid`, `tauAt_braid`, `tau_braid`, `tau_comm`, `tau_cyclic` | the braid relations (linear, far, cyclic) |
| `rep`, `rep_eval`, `word_eq_of_eval_eq` | the Clifford channel `Bₙ →* Cl(n)ˣ` and its word reading `τ(β)` |
| `word_mem_even` | every `τ(β)` lies in the even part `Cl⁺(n)` |
| `reverse_word`, `word_norm` | reversion is `β ↦ β⁻¹`, and `τ(β) τ(β)† = 1` |
| `tauUnit_mem_lipschitz`, `word_mem_spinGroup` | `τₖ = ι(u) ι(eₖ)` is a product of two vectors; `τ(β) ∈ Spin(n)` |
| `letter_conj`, `word_conj`, `perm_eq_of_word_eq` | `τ(β) cⱼ τ(β)⁻¹ = ± c_{π(j)}` with `π = perm β`: the Clifford reading determines the fold permutation |
| `tau_sq`, `tau_pow_four`, `rep_sigma_pow_eight`, `rep_not_injective` | `τₖ² = cₖ₊₁cₖ`, `τₖ⁴ = -1`, `σₖ⁸ ↦ 1`: the channel is not faithful (`n ≥ 2`) |
| `tlFamily`, `tau_eq_kauffman`, `ising_qInt`, `ising_jw` | with `ι² = -1`, `eₖ = (1 + ι cₖ₊₁cₖ)/√2` is a Temperley–Lieb family with loop value `√2`; `τₖ` is a fixed scalar times the Kauffman crossing `a + a⁻¹eₖ` (`-a² - a⁻² = √2`); Jones–Wenzl `p₁, p₂, p₃` exist and `[4] = 0` |

Concrete algebras (`Cl(n,0)`, `Cl(0,n)`, `Clₙ(ℂ)`), the consistency theorem with the oscillator
channel at `r = 4`, the three-fold-way type on three strands, and the sixth channel of the
machine are in `CliffordSixChannel.lean`.
-/
/-! ## 1. Rotors `(1 + x)/s` for bivectors `x² = -1` -/
/-- The rotor `(1 + x)/s`; with `s = √2` and `x² = -1` this is `exp(π x / 4)`. -/

/-- **Braid relation for rotors**: if `x² = y² = -1` and `xy = -yx`, then the rotors satisfy
`τₓ τ_y τₓ = τ_y τₓ τ_y`. -/
/-- Rotors of commuting bivectors commute. -/
/-- `τₓ τ₋ₓ = 1` when `x² = -1` and `s² = 2`. -/
/-- `τₓ² = x`: the square of a rotor is its bivector (a quarter turn squared is a half turn). -/
/-- Conjugating an element that anticommutes with `x` by the rotor `τₓ` gives `-v x`. -/
/-- Conjugating an element that commutes with `x` by `τₓ` fixes it. -/
/-- The Temperley–Lieb element `(1 + ι x)/s` (with `ι² = -1`, `x² = -1`, so `(ι x)² = 1`). -/

/-- **Rotor = Kauffman crossing at the Ising point**: if `a² = (ι - 1)/s` then
`(1 + x)/s = ((1 + ι)/(s a)) · (a + a⁻¹ (1 + ι x)/s)`. -/
/-- **The Ising loop value**: if `a² = (ι - 1)/s` then `-a² - a⁻² = s` (`= √2`). -/
/-! ## 2. The Clifford algebra `Cl(n)` and its anticommuting generators -/

/-- Data of a Clifford braid setting: a field `K` containing `√2`, and the diagonal signature
`w` of the quadratic form `Q(v) = Σ wᵢ vᵢ²` on `Kⁿ`.  The hypothesis `wᵢ wⱼ = 1` says that all
generators square to the same sign: `w = 1` is `Cl(n,0)`, `w = -1` is `Cl(0,n)`. -/
/-- The quadratic form `Q(v) = Σ wᵢ vᵢ²`. -/
/-- The Clifford algebra `Cl(Kⁿ, Q)`. -/
/-- The generator `cᵢ = ι(eᵢ)`. -/
/-- **The Clifford relation** `cᵢ cⱼ = -cⱼ cᵢ` for `i ≠ j`. -/
/-- The bivector `cⱼ cᵢ` (the rotation generator of the `(i, j)`-plane). -/
/-- A bivector squares to `-1`. -/
/-- A generator anticommutes with a bivector containing it (first slot). -/
/-- A generator anticommutes with a bivector containing it (second slot). -/
/-- A generator commutes with a bivector not containing it. -/
/-- Bivectors on disjoint planes commute. -/
/-- Bivectors on adjacent planes `(a, b)`, `(b, c)` anticommute. -/
/-! ## 3. The Kauffman–Lomonaco braid generators `τₖ = (1 + cₖ₊₁cₖ)/√2` -/
/-- The rotor of the `(a, b)`-plane, `(1 + c_b c_a)/s`. -/

/-- **Clifford braiding theorem, adjacent form**: for distinct `a, b, c` the rotors of the
planes `(a, b)` and `(b, c)` satisfy the braid relation.  Both the linear relations
`τₖτₖ₊₁τₖ = τₖ₊₁τₖτₖ₊₁` and the cyclic ones involving `τₙ = (1 + c₁cₙ)/√2` are instances. -/
/-- **Clifford braiding theorem, far form**: rotors of disjoint planes commute. -/
/-- `τₖ` for the braid generator `σₖ` (0-indexed): the rotor of the plane `(k, k+1)`. -/
/-- **Clifford braiding theorem (Kauffman–Lomonaco), linear relations.** -/
/-- **Clifford braiding theorem, far commutation.** -/

/-- **The cyclic generator** `τₙ = (1 + c₁cₙ)/√2` closes the braid relations into a cycle
(for `n ≥ 3`): it braids with `τₙ₋₁` and with `τ₁`. -/
/-! ## 4. The Clifford channel: a homomorphism `Bₙ → Cl(n)ˣ` -/
/-- `τₖ` as a unit, with inverse `τₖ⁻¹ = (1 - cₖ₊₁cₖ)/√2`. -/
/-- **The Clifford channel** as a group homomorphism `Bₙ → Cl(n)ˣ`, `σₖ ↦ τₖ`. -/
/-- The multivector of a letter: `τₖ` or `τₖ⁻¹`. -/
/-- **The Clifford reading of a braid word**: the multivector `τ(β) = τ_{i₁}^{±1} ⋯ τ_{iₖ}^{±1}`. -/
/-- **Soundness of the Clifford channel**: equal braids have equal Clifford readings. -/
/-! ## 5. Grades: the channel lives in the even part `Cl⁺`, and has unit norm -/

/-- **The braid generators live in the even part**: every Clifford reading `τ(β)` lies in
`Cl⁺(n)` (scalars, bivectors, 4-vectors, …). -/
/-- Reversion `cⱼcᵢ ↦ cᵢcⱼ` negates a bivector. -/
/-- Reversion of a letter is its inverse letter. -/
/-- **Clifford conjugation reverses the word**: `τ(β)† = τ(β⁻¹)`. -/
/-- **Unit norm**: `τ(β) τ(β)† = 1` and `τ(β)† τ(β) = 1` for every braid word. -/

/-! ## 6. The vector action: the Clifford channel covers the fold channel

Conjugation by `τ(β)` maps each generator `cⱼ` to `± c_{π(j)}`, where `π` is the permutation of
`β` read by the fold channel.  So the Clifford reading determines the fold permutation: the
image of `Bₙ` in `SO(n)` under the spin cover consists of signed permutation matrices. -/
/-- **One crossing acts on vectors as a signed transposition.** -/

/-- **Clifford covers fold**: for every braid word `β` and strand `j`,
`τ(β) cⱼ τ(β)⁻¹ = ± c_{π(j)}` with `π = perm β`, the permutation read by the fold channel. -/
/-- Distinct generators are not proportional. -/

/-- **The Clifford reading determines the fold permutation**: braids with the same Clifford
reading have the same permutation. -/
/-! ## 7. The Clifford channel lands in the spin group -/
/-- A vector `v` with `ι(v)² = q ≠ 0`, as a unit of `Cl`. -/

/-- **Each braid generator is a product of two vectors**:
`τₖ = ι(u) ι(eₖ)` with `u = (eₖ₊₁ + wₖ eₖ)/√2`, so `τₖ` is in the Lipschitz group. -/

/-- **The Clifford channel lands in `Spin(n)`**: every reading `τ(β)` is an even product of
vectors with `τ(β)* τ(β) = 1` (Mathlib's `spinGroup`). -/
/-! ## 8. The Clifford channel is not faithful: `τₖ⁸ = 1` -/
/-- `τₖ² = cₖ₊₁cₖ`: two quarter turns make the half-turn bivector. -/

/-- `σₖ⁴ ↦ -1`: the Clifford channel sends the fourth power of a crossing to the central
element `-1`. -/

/-- **The Clifford channel is not faithful** (for `n ≥ 2`): `σ₁⁸ ≠ 1` but both have Clifford
reading `1`. -/

/-! ## 9. Ising: Temperley–Lieb inside the Clifford algebra at loop value `√2`

With `ι² = -1`, the elements `eₖ = (1 + ι cₖ₊₁cₖ)/√2` form a Temperley–Lieb family with loop
value `δ = √2 = 2 cos(π/4)`, the oscillator's loop value at `r = 4` (Ising).  The Clifford braid
generators are, up to one common scalar, the Kauffman crossings `a + a⁻¹ eₖ` of this family. -/
/-- The Temperley–Lieb generators `eₖ = (1 + ι cₖ₊₁cₖ)/s` (zero past the last strand). -/
/-- **The Clifford algebra contains a Temperley–Lieb family with loop value `s`.** -/

/-- **Clifford channel = Kauffman bracket at the Ising point.**  If `a² = (ι - 1)/s`, then the
loop value of the Clifford Temperley–Lieb family is `-a² - a⁻²` (the Kauffman relation), and
every Clifford braid generator is a fixed scalar multiple of the Kauffman crossing:
`τₖ = ζ · (a + a⁻¹ eₖ)` with `ζ = (1 + ι)/(s a)`. -/
/-- The quantum integers at the Ising loop value: `[1] = 1`, `[2] = √2`, `[3] = 1`, `[4] = 0`. -/

/-- **Jones–Wenzl projectors in the Clifford algebra**: at the Ising point the projectors
`p₁, p₂, p₃` exist (Wenzl's theorem) on the Clifford Temperley–Lieb family. -/

comments.text:
/-!
# The Clifford channel as the sixth channel of the machine

Builds on `CliffordChannel.lean`.

* `euclid n`, `antiEuclid n`, `complexSetup n`: `Cl(n,0)`, `Cl(0,n)` over `ℝ` and `Clₙ(ℂ)`.
* `ising_consistency`, `ising_consistency_four`: **Clifford = oscillator at `r = 4` on generators.**
  In `Clₙ(ℂ)` the Temperley–Lieb family `eₖ = (1 + i cₖ₊₁cₖ)/√2` has loop value
  `√2 = quantumDim 4 2 = q + q⁻¹` (`q = e^{iπ/4}`, the oscillator's root of unity at `r = 4`), and
  each Clifford braid generator is one fixed scalar `ζ` times the Kauffman crossing
  `a + a⁻¹ eₖ` with `-a² - a⁻² = √2`.  (The Jones *value* is not compared: that needs a Markov trace
  on the Clifford algebra, which is not formalized here.)
* `pauliHom`, `spinRep`, `clifford_three_type`: on three strands `cᵢ ↦ σᵢ` (Pauli) gives
  `Cl(3,0) → M₂(ℂ)`; the image of the Clifford channel is of **quaternionic** type and not real
  (`J v = ε v̄` commutes and `J² = -1`).
* `burau_neg_one_not_orthogonal`: `ρ̄(σ₁)(-1) = [[1,1],[0,1]]` is not orthogonal.
* `SixChannel`, `resonance_iff_six`, `clifford_agree_perm`, `clifford_incomplete`,
  `anchor_refines_clifford_three`: the sixth channel is sound, reads the fold permutation, is
  incomplete (`σ₁⁸` vs `1`), and on `B₃` is strictly refined by the anchor channel.
* `squierForm_quad_neg_one`, `squierForm_transpose_iff`, `burauIsometry`, `burau_clifford_one`: the
  Squier form is symmetric only at `t = 1`, its quadratic form vanishes at `t = -1`, and at `t = 1`
  each Burau matrix is an isometry of the `A₂` form and so acts on `Cl(K², q_{A₂})`.
-/
/-! ## 1. The concrete Clifford algebras -/
/-- `Cl(n,0)` over `ℝ`: generators with `cᵢ² = +1`, rotors with `s = √2`. -/
/-- `Cl(0,n)` over `ℝ`: generators with `cᵢ² = -1`. -/
/-- The complex Clifford algebra `Clₙ(ℂ)` (generators with `cᵢ² = 1`). -/
/-! ## 2. Consistency with the oscillator channel at `r = 4` (Ising) -/

/-- **Clifford channel = oscillator channel at `r = 4`, at the level of generators.**
In the complex Clifford algebra on `n` strands:
* the Temperley–Lieb family `eₖ = (1 + i cₖ₊₁cₖ)/√2` has loop value `√2 = quantumDim 4 2`, which
  is the oscillator's loop value `q + q⁻¹` at `q = e^{iπ/4}`;
* there are `a, ζ` with `-a² - a⁻² = √2` such that every Clifford braid generator is `ζ` times the
  Kauffman crossing `a + a⁻¹ eₖ`. -/
/-- The four-strand case asked for explicitly. -/

/-! ## 3. Three strands: the spinor representation `Cl(3,0) → M₂(ℂ)` is quaternionic

The Pauli matrices satisfy the Clifford relations of `Cl(3,0)`, so `cᵢ ↦ σᵢ` extends to an
algebra map.  On the Clifford channel's image, `J v = ε v̄` commutes with every matrix and
`J² = -1`, and no commuting antilinear `J` has `J² = +1`. -/
/-- The Pauli matrices `σ₁, σ₂, σ₃`. -/
/-- The antiunitary commutation property `ε M̄ = M ε`. -/
/-- The spinor representation of the Clifford channel on `3` strands. -/
/-- **Three-fold-way type of the Clifford channel on `3` strands: quaternionic, not real.** -/

/-! ## 4. The anchor channel at `t = -1` is not orthogonal

`ρ̄(σ₁)(-1) = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]` on `3` strands: an integral unipotent matrix, not an orthogonal
one.  (At `t = -1` the Burau matrices are integral, i.e. of real type, `harmonic_pi_isReal`; that
is a different statement.) -/
/-! ## 5. The sixth channel -/

/-- The five channels of the machine plus the Clifford channel.  (A new type rather than a new
constructor of `Channel`, so that the five-channel classification results stay as proved.) -/
/-- Agreement in a channel; the Clifford channel compares the multivectors `τ(β) ∈ Cl(n,0)`. -/
/-- Every one of the six channels is sound. -/
/-- **Resonance theorem with six channels**: a braid identity holds iff all six agree. -/

/-- **The Clifford channel reads the permutation of the fold channel**: Clifford agreement
forces equal strand permutations. -/
/-- The word `σ₁⁸`. -/
/-- **The Clifford channel is incomplete**: `σ₁⁸` and the empty word agree in it. -/

/-- **On three strands the anchor channel strictly refines the Clifford channel**: whenever the
anchor channel agrees, so does the Clifford channel, but `σ₁⁸` versus the empty word is seen by
the anchor and missed by the Clifford channel. -/

/-! ## 6. The Squier form as a Clifford form: only at `t = 1`

The Squier form `P(t) = [[1+t, t], [1, 1+t]]` is symmetric only at `t = 1`; at `t = -1` its
quadratic form vanishes identically (so its Clifford algebra would be the exterior algebra).
At `t = 1` it is the `A₂` form `2(v₀² + v₀v₁ + v₁²)`, the Burau matrices preserve it
(`squier_word` at `t = 1`) and hence act on the Clifford algebra `Cl(K², q_{A₂})`. -/
/-- The `A₂` quadratic form `q(v) = v P(1) vᵀ = 2(v₀² + v₀v₁ + v₁²)`. -/
/-- The Burau matrix at `t = 1` as an isometry of the `A₂` form (acting on row vectors). -/

/-- **At `t = 1` the anchor channel acts on a Clifford algebra**: each braid word gives an
algebra endomorphism of `Cl(K², q_{A₂})` extending `v ↦ v ρ̄(β)(1)`. -/

/-!
# Harmonic sweep: Burau eigenvalues of `B₃` on the unit circle

Channel 4 of the five-channel machine (`QBX/docs/design/MULTIPROVER.md`).  For `β ∈ B₃` the
reduced Burau matrix `ρ̄(β)(t)` is `2 × 2`; sweeping `t = e^{iθ}` around the circle, a
*resonance* is a `θ` at which an eigenvalue lies on the unit circle.

* `squier_word`: every braid preserves the form `P(t) = [[1+t, t], [1, 1+t]]`:
  `ρ̄(β)(t⁻¹) · P(t) · ρ̄(β)(t)ᵀ = P(t)`, over any commutative ring (Squier's form for `B₃`).
* `trace_identity`: hence, at every non-zero `t` in any field,
  `det ρ̄(β)(t) · tr ρ̄(β)(t⁻¹) = tr ρ̄(β)(t)` (proved generically over `ℤ[t, t⁻¹]`, where
  `det P = 1 + t + t² ≠ 0`, then specialised).
* `det_mul_conj_trace`: on the circle, `det · conj(tr) = tr`, i.e. `tr²/det = |tr|² ≥ 0`.
* `resonance_iff_trace` — **resonance criterion**: an eigenvalue of `ρ̄(β)(e^{iθ})` lies on the
  unit circle iff `|tr ρ̄(β)(e^{iθ})| ≤ 2`; so one eigenvalue resonates iff both do, and off
  resonance `|λ₁| · |λ₂| = 1` with one inside and one outside (`norm_mul_partner`).
* `resonance_universal` — **universal resonance arc**: if `cos θ > -1/2`, every eigenvalue of
  every braid is on the unit circle (`P(e^{iθ})` is definite there, `squier_quad_ne_zero`).
  Resonances can only discriminate braids on the arc `cos θ ≤ -1/2`.
-/
/-- The (unnormalised) Squier form of the reduced Burau representation of `B₃`. -/

/-- The Squier form is preserved by every braid word of `B₃`:
`ρ̄(β)(t⁻¹) · P(t) · ρ̄(β)(t)ᵀ = P(t)`. -/
/-- A `2 × 2` identity: if `N P Mᵀ = P` then `det P · (det M · tr N - tr M) = 0`. -/
/-- The generic trace identity, over `ℤ[t, t⁻¹]`: `det ρ̄(β)(t) · tr ρ̄(β)(t⁻¹) = tr ρ̄(β)(t)`. -/

/-- **Trace identity** for `B₃`, at every nonzero `t` in every field:
`det ρ̄(β)(t) · tr ρ̄(β)(t⁻¹) = tr ρ̄(β)(t)`. -/
/-! ### The harmonic sweep `t = e^{iθ}` -/
/-- The reduced Burau matrix of `β` at the point `t = e^{iθ}` of the unit circle. -/
/-- On the unit circle, `t⁻¹ = t̄`, so `ρ̄(β)(t⁻¹)` is the entrywise conjugate of `ρ̄(β)(t)`. -/

/-- **Reality of the normalised trace.** For `β ∈ B₃` and `t = e^{iθ}`,
`det ρ̄(β) · conj (tr ρ̄(β)) = tr ρ̄(β)`; equivalently `tr² / det = |tr|²` is real and `≥ 0`. -/

/-- The elliptic/hyperbolic dichotomy of a quadratic `X² - τX + D` with `|D| = 1` and
`D · τ̄ = τ`: a root is on the unit circle iff `|τ| ≤ 2`. -/
-- the reality condition: `m (|l|² - 1) + l (|m|² - 1) = 0`
/-- `l` is an eigenvalue of a `2 × 2` matrix iff it is a root of `X² - tr·X + det`. -/

/-- **Resonance criterion for `B₃`.**  At `t = e^{iθ}` an eigenvalue `λ` of `ρ̄(β)` lies on
the unit circle iff `|tr ρ̄(β)(e^{iθ})| ≤ 2`.  In particular one eigenvalue is resonant iff
both are. -/

/-- **Off resonance the eigenvalues straddle the circle.**  The two eigenvalues `λ, D/λ`
satisfy `|λ| · |D/λ| = 1`; so off resonance exactly one is inside the unit circle. -/
/-- The Squier form is definite on the arc `Re t > -1/2` of the unit circle. -/

/-- **Universal resonance arc.**  For every braid `β ∈ B₃` and every `θ` with `cos θ > -1/2`
(i.e. `|θ| < 2π/3` mod `2π`), every eigenvalue of `ρ̄(β)(e^{iθ})` lies on the unit circle:
the braid preserves the definite Squier form there.  So on two thirds of the circle a
resonance carries no information about `β`; only the arc `cos θ ≤ -1/2` can discriminate. -/
-- an eigenvector of `Mᵀ`
-- the Squier form is preserved

/-!
# Harmonic sweep for every strand count: Squier's form and the universal resonance arc

`HarmonicSweep.lean` treats `B₃`.  Here the two structural results are extended to `B_n` for
every `n`.

* `squierJ t` : the tridiagonal matrix with `1 + t` on the diagonal, `-t` above and `-1` below.
* `squierJ_word` — **Squier's form for `B_n`**: for every braid word on `n` strands, over any
  commutative ring, `ρ̄(β)(t)ᵀ · J(t) · ρ̄(β)(t⁻¹) = J(t)`.
  (For `n = 3`, `J(t)` is the adjugate of the form `P(t)` of `HarmonicSweep.lean`.)
* `path_quadratic_le` : `Σ yᵢ yᵢ₊₁ ≤ cos(π/(m+1)) Σ yᵢ²` for every real sequence of length
  `m` (the spectral radius of the path graph), proved with the Perron vector `sin((i+1)π/(m+1))`.
* `resonance_universal_n` — **universal resonance arc for `B_n`**: if `|θ| < 2π/n`, every
  eigenvalue of `ρ̄(β)(e^{iθ})` lies on the unit circle, for every braid `β` on `n` strands.
  For `n = 3` this is the arc `cos θ > -1/2` of `resonance_universal`; as `n` grows the arc on
  which the harmonic channel is silent shrinks like `2π/n`.
-/
/-- The coefficient function of Squier's tridiagonal form. -/
/-- Squier's tridiagonal form `J(t)` on `Fin m`. -/
/-- Entries of `(1 + rowM r a)ᵀ · J · (1 + rowM r a')`. -/
/-- Squier's form is preserved by every generator and its inverse. -/
/-- **Squier's form for `B_n`**: `ρ̄(β)(t)ᵀ · J(t) · ρ̄(β)(t⁻¹) = J(t)` for every word. -/
/-- Extension of a vector on `Fin m` by zero to all of `ℕ`. -/
/-- The tridiagonal action of `J(t)` in coordinates. -/
/-- The Hermitian expansion of Squier's form. -/

/-- **Spectral radius of the path graph**: `Σ_{i<k} yᵢ yᵢ₊₁ ≤ cos(π/(k+2)) Σ_{i≤k} yᵢ²` for every
real sequence (Perron vector `sin((i+1)π/(k+2))`). -/

/-- **Definiteness of Squier's form on the arc** `|φ| < 2π/(k+2)`: the Hermitian form
`x ↦ x^H J(e^{iφ}) x` on `ℂ^{k+1}` does not vanish on non-zero vectors (its rotation by
`e^{-iφ/2}` has real part `≥ 2(cos(φ/2) − cos(π/(k+2)))‖x‖² > 0`). -/
-- positivity of S
-- the path bound on the cross term
-- the arc condition
-- rotate by conj h

/-- **Universal resonance arc for `B_n`.**  If `|θ| < 2π/n`, every eigenvalue of
`ρ̄(β)(e^{iθ})` lies on the unit circle, for every braid word `β` on `n` strands: the braid
preserves the definite Hermitian form `J(e^{-iθ})`. -/
-- an eigenvector
-- the invariant form at `t⁻¹ = e^{-iθ}`

/-!
# The last open identity line, and the dual hypergraph of the channels (research question 3.1)

`ChannelGeometry.lean` showed that on three strands `{fold, anchor, x}` is an identity line for
every channel `x`, that a triple containing fold or anchor and two of the weak channels `link`,
`harmonic`, `oscillator` is not, and left one triple open: `{link, harmonic, oscillator}`.

**The open triple is not an identity line** (`not_identityLine_weak`).  The braids `σ₁` and
`σ₁³` on three strands agree in the link channel (both close up to two components with linking
number `0`) and in the harmonic channel (every power of `σ₁` resonates at every angle), but the
oscillator channel separates them: at `q = e^{iπ/4}` the closures (unknot ⊔ unknot and
trefoil ⊔ unknot) have Jones values `q + q⁻¹` and `−(q + q⁻¹)` (`weak_pair_separates`).  So
`link` and `harmonic` together do not determine `oscillator`.

The Jones computation is done for every field: shifting a braid one strand to the right
multiplies the Jones value by `q + q⁻¹` (`jonesQT_shift`, an extra unlinked circle), and the
two-strand trefoil has value `q⁻² + q⁻⁶ − q⁻⁸` (`jonesQT_trefoil_two`).

**Complete classification on three strands** (`isIdentityLine_three_iff`): a triple of
distinct channels is an identity line exactly when it contains both fold and anchor.  So there
are exactly three identity lines (`identityLines3`), not seven as in a Fano plane.

**The dual hypergraph** (points ↔ lines): its points are the three identity lines, and each
channel becomes the edge of identity lines through it (`dualEdge`).  Fold and anchor give the
full edge (degree 3), each weak channel a single point (degree 1) (`dualEdge_card`).  Two points
of the dual lie on two common edges (`dual_not_linear`), so the dual is not a linear space
either.  The complements of the identity lines in the five channels are the three edges of a
triangle on `{link, harmonic, oscillator}` (`identityLine_compl`), pairwise meeting in one
point.  The identity structure is therefore "two complete channels plus three independent weak
probes"; nothing Fano-like is latent in it.

**The three involutions of the Fano plane** (for comparison):
* `fano_polarity` — a polarity `p ↦ {−p, 1−p, 3−p}`: a bijection from points to lines with
  `p ∈ π(q) ↔ q ∈ π(p)`; its absolute points `p ∈ π(p)` form a line (`fano_absolute_line`);
* `fano_selfDual` — hence points and lines can be swapped preserving incidence;
* `fano_compl` — the complements of the lines are seven 4-sets meeting pairwise in exactly two
  points, while the lines meet pairwise in exactly one.
-/
/-! ## Jones values: an extra unlinked strand and the trefoil -/
/-- The quantum trace of `I ⊗ A` is `(q + q⁻¹)` times that of `A`. -/

/-- **Split union with an unknot**: adding an idle strand on the left multiplies the Jones
value by `q + q⁻¹`. -/
/-- `σ₁` on two strands. -/
/-- The closure of `σ₁ ∈ B₂` is the unknot. -/
/-- The right-handed trefoil `σ₁³ ∈ B₂`: `V = q⁻² + q⁻⁶ − q⁻⁸`. -/

/-- `σ₁^k ∈ B₃` is conjugate to `σ₂^k = shift(σ₁^k)`, so its Jones value is that of the
two-strand braid times `q + q⁻¹`. -/
/-! ## The open triple `{link, harmonic, oscillator}` -/
/-- `σ₁` on three strands. -/
/-- `σ₁³` on three strands. -/
/-- Two components with linking number `0`. -/

/-- **The weak pair separated by the oscillator alone**: `σ₁` and `σ₁³` on three strands agree
in the link and harmonic channels and disagree in the oscillator channel (at `r = 4`). -/
/-- `link` and `harmonic` together do not determine `oscillator` on three strands. -/
/-- **The last open triple is not an identity line**: `{link, harmonic, oscillator}`. -/
/-! ## Classification of the identity lines on three strands -/

/-- **Complete classification**: on three strands, three distinct channels form an identity line
exactly when the triple contains both fold and anchor. -/
/-- The three identity lines on three strands. -/

/-- **Exactly three identity lines**: a triple of distinct channels is an identity line iff it
is one of the three triples in `identityLines3`. -/
/-! ## The dual hypergraph -/
/-- In the dual hypergraph, the channel `c` is the edge of identity lines through `c`. -/

/-- **Degrees in the dual**: fold and anchor lie on all three identity lines, each weak channel
on exactly one. -/

/-- The dual edges of fold and anchor are both the whole point set of the dual, and the dual
edges of the weak channels are three distinct single points. -/

/-- **The dual is not a linear space**: two distinct points of the dual (identity lines) lie on
two common edges (fold and anchor). -/

/-- **Complements of the identity lines** in the five channels: the three edges of a triangle
on the weak channels, any two meeting in exactly one point. -/
/-! ## The three involutions of the Fano plane -/
/-- The polarity of the Fano plane `{i, i+1, i+3}`: `p ↦ {−p, 1−p, 3−p}`. -/

/-- **Polarity**: `fanoPolarity` is a bijection from points onto lines with
`p ∈ π(q) ↔ q ∈ π(p)`. -/
/-- The absolute points of the polarity (`p ∈ π(p)`) are `0, 4, 5`, and they form a line. -/

/-- **Self-duality**: there is a bijection `δ` from points to lines with
`p ∈ l ↔ δ⁻¹(l) ∈ δ(p)`, i.e. swapping points and lines preserves incidence. -/

/-- **Complements**: the seven complements of the Fano lines are 4-sets meeting pairwise in
exactly two points, while the lines meet pairwise in exactly one. -/

/-!
# Kelly tick allocation for a graduated portfolio of partial deciders

The multi-prover runs several *tiers* (cheap refuters, expensive complete deciders) on the same
claim.  This file adds the missing control layer: a tick budget per tier, allocated in
proportion to the clipped Kelly fraction `Sovereign.Organism.kellyQ` of the tier's observed
decision rate, with a guaranteed floor.

## The allocation rule

* Every tier keeps `TierStats` (attempts, decisions).  Its decision rate is the Laplace estimate
  `(decisions + 1) / (attempts + 2)` (`TierStats.rate`), which lies strictly between `0` and `1`.
* Its weight is the Kelly fraction `kellyQ rate b`, where `b > 0` is the tier's payoff (value of
  a decision relative to the ticks a failed attempt wastes).
* Out of `total` ticks, every tier first gets `floor`; the rest (`spare`) is split in proportion
  to the weights, rounded down (`tickShare`).  If every weight is `0` the spare is split evenly.

## Main results

* `floor_le_tickShare`, `allocTicks_sum_le` — every tier gets at least `floor`, and (when
  `floor · #tiers ≤ total`) the budgets never exceed `total`.
* `tickShare_dead` — a tier with Kelly weight `0` (while some tier is alive) gets exactly the
  floor; `tickShare_mono` — a larger weight never gets fewer ticks.
* `kellyWeight_eq_zero_of_failures` — a tier with payoff `b` that has failed every one of at
  least `b - 1` attempts is dead.
* `runTiers_sound`, `kellyRun_sound` — **allocation never affects correctness**: if every tier is
  sound, any answer of the portfolio is the truth, whatever the statistics.
* `kellyRun_decides` — **the floor never starves a decider**: if some sound, fuel-monotone tier
  decides the claim within `floor` ticks, the portfolio decides it.
* `kellyLoopWith_sound`, `kellyLoopWith_complete`, `kellyLoopWith_valid` — the online loop
  (allocate, run, update the statistics, next task) is sound on every task, complete under the
  floor condition, and keeps `decisions ≤ attempts`, for *every* statistics-update rule that
  keeps the tiers (`kellyLoop` is the instance with the portfolio rule `updateStats`).
* `graduatedRun_eq`, `graduatedLoop_eq` — **the graduated prover**: Kelly-allocated refuters
  first, a complete decider on the survivors.  Every answer is the truth, for every allocation,
  statistics and update rule; dead refuters can be cut below their cost and simply skipped.
-/
/-! ### Per-tier statistics -/
/-- Running statistics of one tier. -/
/-- Laplace estimate of the decision rate. -/
/-- Record one attempt, which decided the claim or not. -/
/-- Consistency: never more decisions than attempts. -/
/-- The Kelly weight of a tier with statistics `s` and payoff `b`. -/

/-- **Dead tiers.**  A tier with payoff `b > 0` that has never decided, after at least `b - 1`
attempts, has Kelly weight `0`. -/

/-- **Alive tiers.**  A tier with payoff `b > 0` has positive Kelly weight iff its decision rate
exceeds `1 / (b + 1)`. -/
/-! ### Tick allocation -/
/-- The effective weights: the Kelly weights, or all `1` if they are all `0`. -/
/-- The effective total weight. -/
/-- Ticks left after every tier has received its floor. -/

/-- **The tick share** of a tier of weight `w` among tiers of weights `ws`: the floor plus its
proportional part of the spare ticks, rounded down. -/
/-- The allocation of all tiers. -/
/-- **Dead tiers get exactly the floor** (as long as some tier is alive). -/
/-- **Monotonicity**: a larger weight never receives fewer ticks. -/
/-- The proportional parts never exceed the spare ticks. -/
/-- **Budget conservation**: if the floors fit, the allocation never exceeds the total. -/
/-! ### Graduated portfolio of partial deciders -/

/-- A tier: a fuel-bounded partial decision procedure on claims of type `α`
(`some v`: decided with answer `v`; `none`: undecided within the fuel). -/
/-- A tier is sound for the truth assignment `truth` if every answer it gives is the truth. -/
/-- More fuel never loses a decision. -/
/-- Run the tiers with their budgets; the answer is the first decision in list order. -/
/-- A tier together with its statistics and payoff. -/
/-- The Kelly weights of a portfolio. -/
/-- The budgeted portfolio: every tier with its Kelly tick share. -/
/-- **The Kelly-allocated run** of a portfolio on a claim. -/
/-- **Allocation never affects correctness.** -/

/-- **The floor never starves a decider.**  If one sound, fuel-monotone tier of the portfolio
decides the claim within `floor` ticks, the Kelly-allocated run returns the truth. -/
/-! ### The online loop -/

/-- Update the statistics of every tier after running the portfolio on `a` (each tier ran with
its own budget; it is credited with a decision iff it decided). -/

/-- **The online Kelly loop**, for any statistics-update rule `upd`: for each task, allocate,
run, record the answer, update the statistics.  Returns the answers and the final portfolio.
(`updateStats` is the portfolio rule; a sequential runtime that only charges the tiers it
actually ran, or that adds exploration probes, is another `upd`.) -/
/-- The loop with the portfolio update rule `updateStats`. -/
/-- An update rule *preserves the tiers* if it only changes statistics (and payoffs). -/

/-- **Statistics stay consistent** through the loop, for any update rule that keeps them
consistent. -/

/-- **The loop is sound**: every answer is the truth, for every update rule that keeps the
tiers. -/

/-- **Completeness of the loop**: if one sound, fuel-monotone tier decides every task within
`floor` ticks, the loop answers every task, correctly — for every update rule that keeps the
tiers. -/

/-! ### The graduated prover: Kelly-allocated refuters, then a complete decider

The cheap tiers are *refuters* with Kelly budgets; a claim that none of them decides goes to a
complete (total) decider.  Dead refuters (weight `0`) are cut to the floor, which may be below
their cost, so they are skipped; the decider is never budget-limited. -/
/-- The graduated run: the Kelly portfolio first, the complete decider `dec` on the survivors. -/

/-- **The graduated prover is correct** for every allocation: sound refuters and a correct
decider give the truth on every claim. -/
/-- The decider runs only on claims that no refuter decided. -/
/-- The graduated online loop, for any update rule. -/

/-- **The graduated loop answers every claim correctly**, whatever the statistics, payoffs,
budgets and update rule (as long as the update keeps the tiers). -/

/-! ### A worked allocation

Three tiers, `100` ticks, floor `5`: weights `1/2`, `0` (dead), `1/4`.  The spare `85` ticks are
split `2 : 0 : 1`, rounded down. -/
/-- A fresh tier (rate `1/2`) with payoff `3` has Kelly weight `1/3`. -/
/-- After `2` failed attempts, a tier with payoff `3` is dead. -/

/-!
# The Kelly-allocated multi-prover

`QBX.Formal.MultiProver.Scheduler` runs the chunks of a braid word in parallel and combines them
correctly, but every claim gets the same treatment.  This file makes the five channels of the
machine into *tiers* of a graduated portfolio (`QBX.Formal.MultiProver.KellyAllocation`) whose
tick budgets follow the Kelly fractions of their observed decision rates.

A channel `c` with cost `cost c` (ticks needed to compute its reading on both sides) is the
partial decider `channelTier cost c`:

* with fewer than `cost c` ticks it answers nothing;
* if the two readings disagree, it answers `false` (a refutation, `Channel.agree_of_eval_eq`);
* if they agree and `c` is the complete fold channel, it answers `true` (Garside uniqueness);
* if they agree and `c` is one of the four incomplete channels, it answers nothing.

## Main results

* `channelTier_sound`, `channelTier_monotone` — each channel is a sound, fuel-monotone tier for
  the truth `w.eval = w'.eval`.
* `kellyRun_channels_sound` — whatever the statistics, payoffs and budgets, every answer of the
  Kelly-allocated machine is correct.
* `kellyRun_channels_eq_verdict` — **no starvation**: if the floor covers the cost of the fold
  channel, the Kelly-allocated machine always answers, and its answer is the machine's verdict.
* `kellyLoop_channels` — the same for the online loop: for every list of claims, every answer
  equals the verdict, while the statistics adapt (`kellyLoop_valid`).
* `graduated_channels_eq_verdict`, `graduatedLoop_channels_eq_verdict` — the graduated machine
  (incomplete channels as Kelly-allocated refuters, then the fold channel) returns the verdict
  for every allocation and every statistics-update rule.
-/
/-- The truth of a claimed braid identity. -/
/-- A channel as a fuel-bounded partial decider. -/
/-- The fold channel decides every claim once it has `cost .fold` ticks. -/
/-- The answer of the decider, as a Boolean, agrees with the machine's verdict. -/
/-- The machine's channels as a Kelly portfolio: `stats`, `payoff` per channel. -/
/-- **Kelly allocation never makes the machine wrong.** -/

/-- **No starvation.**  If the fold channel is in the portfolio and the floor covers its cost,
the Kelly-allocated machine answers every claim with the machine's verdict, for any statistics,
payoffs and total budget. -/

/-- **The online Kelly loop on braid claims.**  Starting from any statistics, if the fold channel
is in the portfolio and the floor covers its cost, the loop answers every claim with the
machine's verdict. -/

/-! ### The graduated machine

The incomplete channels (`link`, `anchor`, `harmonic`, `oscillator`) are Kelly-allocated
refuters; the fold channel decides whatever they leave.  This is the runtime design of
`multiprover.py` (`KellyMultiProver`): no floor condition is needed, so dead refuters can be
skipped entirely. -/
/-- The fold channel as a total decider. -/

/-- **The graduated machine returns the verdict**, for every list of refuting channels, all
costs, statistics, payoffs, budgets and floors. -/

/-- **The graduated online loop on braid claims returns the verdict on every claim**, for every
statistics-update rule that keeps the channels. -/
