/-!
# Holonomy, hidden symmetry and map distortion (milestones M4–M5 of the cross-domain plan)

Third Lean layer of `docs/CROSS_DOMAIN_INVARIANTS_PLAN_2026-10-14.md`.

**I. Holonomy is the signature of a hidden fibre** (plan W5.3).
* `overlap_smul`: the overlap `⟨a|b⟩` of two state vectors changes by the phases chosen for them,
  so a single overlap has no gauge-independent phase (`overlap_not_gauge_invariant`).
* `bargmann_gauge`: the three-state product `⟨a|b⟩⟨b|c⟩⟨c|a⟩` (Bargmann invariant) is unchanged
  by any choice of unit phases.  Its phase is the discrete Berry / Pancharatnam phase.
* `bargmann_example`: and it can be non-real: for `(1,0), (1,1), (1,i)` it equals `1 + i`
  (phase `π/4`).  A hidden fibre shows itself through such loop products, not through any single
  base point.

**J. The inverse-square law has a hidden conserved vector** (plan W5.1).
* `runge_lenz_conserved`: for motion under `ṗ = −k r / |r|³`, `ṙ = p / m`, the
  Laplace–Runge–Lenz vector `p × L − m k r / |r|` (with `L = r × p`) is constant in time;
  `angular_momentum_conserved` is the companion statement for `L`.

**K. Every flat map distorts** (plan W4.1).
* `gramDet_planar`: four points of the plane satisfy one polynomial relation among their six
  squared distances (the Gram determinant of three difference vectors vanishes).
* `no_isometric_flat_map`: no map from the unit sphere to the plane preserves great-circle
  distances; four points of the sphere already rule it out.

**L. Stereographic chart = Hopf base** (plan W4.2).
* `hopfC_eq_of_ratio`: on the unit sphere of `ℂ²`, the Hopf image `hopfC z w` depends only on the
  ratio `z : w` (the point of `ℂ ∪ {∞}` that the stereographic chart displays).

**M. Quasi-periodic escape** (plan W4.3).
* `mech_not_eventually_periodic`: a mechanical (Sturmian) word with irrational slope is never
  eventually periodic.
* `fibWord_not_eventually_periodic`: in particular the Fibonacci word (slope `1/φ²`) is not;
  `fibWord_eq_subst` checks that it agrees with the substitution `0 ↦ 01, 1 ↦ 0` on its first
  100 letters.  Together with `Perspectives.crystallographic_restriction`, this is why 5- and
  10-fold ornament (girih) cannot be periodic and quasi-periodic order is the way out.
-/
/-! ## I. Bargmann invariant -/
/-- The overlap `⟨a|b⟩ = ∑ conj(aᵢ) bᵢ`. -/
/-- The Bargmann three-state invariant `⟨a|b⟩⟨b|c⟩⟨c|a⟩`. -/

/-- A single overlap is not gauge invariant: rephasing `a` by `i` changes it whenever it is
nonzero. -/
/-- **Gauge invariance of the Bargmann invariant.** -/

/-- **A nontrivial holonomy.** For the three rays `(1,0)`, `(1,1)`, `(1,i)` of `ℂ²` the Bargmann
invariant is `1 + i`: its phase `π/4` is gauge independent and nonzero. -/
/-! ## J. The Runge–Lenz vector -/
/-- One component of the Runge–Lenz derivative computation, in coordinates. -/
/-- One component of the angular-momentum derivative computation. -/
/-- Euclidean length `√(r ⬝ r)` of a vector of `ℝ³`. -/
/-- The Laplace–Runge–Lenz vector `p × (r × p) − (m k / |r|) r`. -/

/-- **The Runge–Lenz vector is conserved** under the inverse-square law `ṙ = p / m`,
`ṗ = −(k / |r|³) r`, along any motion that avoids the origin.  This extra conserved vector is the
hidden `SO(4)` symmetry behind closed Kepler orbits and the degeneracy of hydrogen levels. -/

/-- **Angular momentum `L = r × p` is conserved** for every central force
`ṗ = −c(t) r` (any scalar `c`). -/
/-! ## K. Every flat map distorts -/

/-- Gram determinant of the three vectors `Pᵢ − P₀` (`i = 1, 2, 3`), written through the six
squared distances `dᵢⱼ = |Pᵢ − Pⱼ|²` (polarization: `⟨Pᵢ−P₀, Pⱼ−P₀⟩ = (d₀ᵢ + d₀ⱼ − dᵢⱼ)/2`). -/

/-- **Four points of the plane obey a distance relation**: three vectors in a 2-dimensional
space have vanishing Gram determinant. -/
/-- Great-circle distance between two unit vectors. -/

/-- **Every flat map distorts.** No map from the unit sphere in `ℝ³` to the plane preserves all
great-circle distances.  The four points north pole, `(1,0,0)`, `(0,1,0)` and the midpoint
`(1,1,0)/√2` of the equator arc between them already make it impossible: their distances violate
`gramDet_planar`. -/
/-! ## L. Hopf image depends only on the ratio -/

/-- **The Hopf image is a function of `z : w`.** If `(z, w)` and `(z', w')` lie on the unit
sphere of `ℂ²` and define the same point of `ℂ ∪ {∞}` (`z w' = z' w`), they have the same Hopf
image.  So the base `S²` of the Hopf fibration is the Riemann sphere of ratios, which the
stereographic chart draws as the plane. -/
/-! ## M. Quasi-periodic escape: the Fibonacci word -/
/-- The mechanical (Sturmian) word of slope `α`: letter `n` is `⌊(n+1)α⌋ − ⌊nα⌋`. -/

/-- **Irrational slope ⇒ never periodic.** A mechanical word with irrational slope is not
eventually periodic: periodicity would force the slope to be rational. -/
/-- The Fibonacci word `0100101001001…`, as the mechanical word of slope `2 − φ = 1/φ²`. -/
/-- **The Fibonacci word is not eventually periodic.** -/
/-- Integer formula for `⌊n (2 − φ)⌋` (`n ≥ 1`), computable with `Nat.sqrt`. -/
/-- `⌊n (2 − φ)⌋ = fibFloorNat n` for `n ≥ 1`. -/
/-- Computable form of the Fibonacci word. -/
/-- The Fibonacci substitution `0 ↦ 01`, `1 ↦ 0` (`false = 0`, `true = 1`). -/
/-- Ten iterations of the substitution from `0`: a prefix of length 144. -/

/-- The mechanical description agrees with the substitution on the first 100 letters (checked by
the kernel; the general identity is not formalized). -/

/-!
# Writing direction as a symmetry of braids

Scripts are written left-to-right (Latin), right-to-left (Hebrew, Arabic), top-to-bottom
(traditional Chinese, Mongolian), bottom-to-top along an edge (Ogham, Hanunó'o), or alternately
(boustrophedon: archaic Greek, Sabaean; reverse boustrophedon: Rapa Nui rongorongo).  This file
asks what such changes of direction do to a QBX braid, and answers it exactly.

A braid diagram drawn on a page can be changed by three independent operations:

* `flipHom` — renumber the strand positions from the other side (`σᵢ ↦ σ_{n-2-i}`): the diagram
  seen *from behind the page* (a rigid rotation about the vertical axis);
* `revB` — read the word in the opposite order (`σ_{i₁} ⋯ σ_{iₖ} ↦ σ_{iₖ} ⋯ σ_{i₁}`): the diagram
  turned upside down about a horizontal axis in the page (a rigid rotation);
* `mirrorHom` — change every crossing sign (`σᵢ ↦ σᵢ⁻¹`): reflection in the plane of the page.

`flipHom` and `mirrorHom` are automorphisms of `Bₙ`, `revB` is an anti-automorphism, all three are
involutions and they commute, so they generate a group `(ℤ/2)³` (`Dir`).  The planar page
symmetries are composites: the left–right reflection is `flip ∘ mirror`, the top–bottom
reflection is `rev ∘ mirror` (which is exactly the group inverse, `revB_mirror_eq_inv`), and the
half-turn in the plane (how a rongorongo tablet is turned between lines) is `flip ∘ rev`.

Main results (`Dir.act` is the action on braid group elements, `Dir.actWord` on words):

* `Dir.eval_actWord` — the word-level action computes the group-level one.
* `Dir.writhe_act` — writhe is preserved by rigid moves and negated by reflections.
* `Dir.numComponents_act` — the number of closure components is preserved by all eight moves.
* `Dir.linkingSpectrum_act` — the linking spectrum of the closure is preserved by the four rigid
  moves (`d.mirror = false`) and negated entry-wise by the four reflections.

So: **reading direction never changes the closed-link data of a single braid; chirality does.**
The text-layout consequences (boustrophedon, edge writing) are in `TextLayout.lean`.
-/
/-! ### The three operations on letters -/
/-- Renumber the crossing position from the other side. -/
/-! ### The three operations on the braid group -/
/-- Seeing the diagram from behind: `σᵢ ↦ σ_{n-2-i}`. -/
/-- Reflection in the page: every crossing changes sign, `σᵢ ↦ σᵢ⁻¹`. -/
/-- Reading in the opposite order, as a homomorphism into the opposite group. -/
/-- Reading a braid in the opposite order (an anti-automorphism of `Bₙ`). -/

/-- Turning the page upside down and reflecting it is the group inverse:
`rev (mirror g) = g⁻¹`, equivalently `rev g = (mirror g)⁻¹`. -/
/-! ### Involutions and commutation -/
/-! ### Writhe and permutation -/
/-! ### The crossing matrix -/
/-! ### Closure invariants under relabelling, sign change and reversal -/

/-- **Relabelling lemma.** If `g'` is `g` with strands renamed by `R` (both the permutation and
the crossing matrix), then the closures have the same number of components and the same linking
spectrum. -/
/-- Reflection in the page negates every linking number of the closure. -/
/-- Reading in the opposite order does not change the linking spectrum of the closure. -/
/-! ### The direction group `(ℤ/2)³` -/

/-- A change of writing/viewing direction: any combination of seeing the page from behind
(`flip`), reading it in the opposite order (`rev`) and reflecting it in its own plane
(`mirror`). -/
/-- Every direction change is its own inverse. -/
/-- Rigid moves (no reflection) preserve the link type. -/
/-- Seeing the page from behind (rotation about the vertical axis). -/
/-- Turning the page upside down about a horizontal axis in the page. -/
/-- Half-turn in the plane of the page (the rongorongo tablet turn). -/
/-- Reflection in the plane of the page (crossing change). -/
/-- Left–right reflection of the page (the picture of an LTR line read as RTL). -/
/-- Top–bottom reflection of the page. -/
/-- Apply `flipHom` if `b`. -/
/-- Apply `mirrorHom` if `b`. -/
/-- Apply `revB` if `b`. -/
/-- The action on braid group elements. -/
/-- The action on words. -/
/-- `Dir` acts on `Bₙ` (as a set): `(d * e) • g = d • (e • g)`. -/
/-- The top–bottom reflection of the page is the group inverse. -/
/-- Writhe: preserved by rigid moves, negated by reflections. -/
/-- The number of closure components is unchanged by every direction change. -/

/-- **Direction theorem.** The linking spectrum of the closed braid is unchanged by the four
rigid direction changes and negated by the four reflections. -/

/-!
# Seal lane S5 — polynomial-coded decoding (Lagrange interpolation)

Phase 4 (`docs/phase_4_fast_track.md` §6, Sprint 4 `engine/coded.py`) distributes a matrix
computation as evaluations of a matrix polynomial `P(x) = Σ_{e<k} A_e xᵉ` at `n` distinct points,
one per worker, so that the result survives stragglers.  Item S5 asks for:

> polynomial-coded decoding: any `k` of `n` evaluations of a degree `< k` matrix polynomial
> recover it (Lagrange interpolation uniqueness).

A matrix polynomial is represented entrywise, as a matrix `P : Matrix m m' F[X]` with entries of
degree `< k`; its value at `x` is `P.map (eval x)`.  This file proves:

* `coded_unique` — two such matrix polynomials that agree at any `k` distinct points are equal;
* `coded_decode` (**S5**) — such a matrix polynomial equals the entrywise Lagrange interpolant of
  its values on *any* `k` of the evaluation points, so the master can decode from whichever `k`
  workers answer first;
* `coded_decode_of_workers` — the straggler form: with `n` workers at distinct points, any set of
  at least `k` responding workers determines `P`.
-/
/-- The value of an entrywise matrix polynomial at a point. -/
/-- All entries of `P` have degree `< k`. -/
/-- Two matrix polynomials of degree `< k` that agree at `k` (or more) distinct points are equal. -/

/-- **Seal lane S5.** A matrix polynomial of degree `< k` is the entrywise Lagrange interpolant
of its values at any `k` (or more) distinct evaluation points. -/

/-- **Seal lane S5, straggler form.** With `n` workers evaluating at pairwise distinct points
`α : Fin n → F`, the responses of any set `R` of at least `k` workers determine a degree `< k`
matrix polynomial: it is the Lagrange interpolant through those responses. -/

/-- With fewer than `k` responses decoding is impossible: for any set `s` of points, with
`k = s.card + 1`, there are two different polynomials of degree `< k` with the same values at
every point of `s`. -/

/-!
# Seal lane S6 — the "final chord" depends only on the braid

Phase 4 sonifies a braid word (`docs/phase_4_fast_track.md` §3.1): when the rewrite engine has
settled, it plays a *final chord* built from

* the cycle type of the braid's permutation (the chord's voicing),
* the writhe (stereo position),
* the eigenphases of a matrix representation (drone partials).

Item S6 asks that this chord depend only on the braid group element, so that equal braids sound
equal however they were written.  Here the eigenphase data is the characteristic polynomial of
the reduced Burau matrix at a chosen unit `t` (over a field: its multiset of roots, the
eigenvalues).  This file proves:

* `braidChord` — the chord, defined directly on the braid group `B_n`;
* `Word.chord_eq_braidChord` — the chord computed letter by letter from a word equals the chord
  of the braid the word represents;
* `Word.chord_eq_of_eval_eq` (**S6**) — two words for the same braid have the same final chord;
* `Word.eigenphases_eq_of_eval_eq` — over a field, the same holds for the eigenvalue multiset;
* `Word.chord_eq_of_step` — in particular, every rewrite step of the engine preserves the chord.
-/

/-- The final chord data: permutation cycle type, writhe, and the characteristic polynomial of
the reduced Burau matrix. -/
/-- The final chord of a braid group element. -/
/-- The final chord of a word, computed letter by letter as the engine does. -/
/-- The letter-by-letter chord of a word is the chord of the braid it represents. -/
/-- **Seal lane S6.** Two words representing the same braid have the same final chord. -/
/-- Every rewrite step of the engine preserves the final chord. -/

/-- Over a field, the eigenvalues (with multiplicity) of the reduced Burau matrix of a word
depend only on the braid. -/

/-!
# Seal lane S4 — finite Kleene iteration and chaotic iteration

Phase 4 (`docs/phase_4_fast_track.md` §6) runs the engine as a fixed-point iteration of a
monotone update `F` on a finite lattice of states, both synchronously and asynchronously.
Item S4 asks for:

> the fixed-point iteration of a monotone `F` on a finite lattice reaches the least fixed point
> from `⊥` (Kleene, finite) and the chaotic asynchronous version reaches the same point.

This file proves:

* `iterate_bot_le_lfp` — every iterate `F^[k] ⊥` is below the least fixed point;
* `iterate_card_bot_eq_lfp` (**S4, synchronous**) — on a finite complete lattice,
  `F^[card α] ⊥ = lfp F`: at most `card α` rounds are needed;
* `chaotic_eventually_lfp` (**S4, chaotic**) — for a product state `ι → β` (one component per
  node), updating one component at a time according to any *fair* schedule (every component
  is updated infinitely often) eventually reaches, and then stays at, the same least fixed point.
-/
/-- Every Kleene iterate from `⊥` is below the least fixed point. -/
/-- The Kleene iterates from `⊥` increase. -/
/-- A Kleene iterate that is a fixed point is the least fixed point. -/
/-- Once a Kleene iterate is fixed, all later iterates equal it. -/

/-- **Seal lane S4 (synchronous).** On a finite complete lattice, `card α` rounds of Kleene
iteration from `⊥` reach the least fixed point of any monotone map. -/
-- among the `card α + 1` iterates `0, …, card α`, two coincide (pigeonhole)

/-- **Seal lane S4 (synchronous, existence form).** Kleene iteration from `⊥` reaches the least
fixed point after finitely many rounds and stays there. -/
/-- One asynchronous step: node `i` recomputes its own component from the current state. -/
/-- The chaotic (asynchronous) iteration from `⊥` along the schedule `s`. -/
/-- A schedule is fair when every node is scheduled infinitely often. -/
/-- Invariant of chaotic iteration: the state is below its own update and below `lfp F`. -/
/-- Chaotic iteration is monotone in time. -/

/-- **Seal lane S4 (chaotic).** On a finite product lattice, chaotic asynchronous iteration
from `⊥` along any fair schedule eventually reaches the least fixed point of `F` and stays
there — the same point as synchronous Kleene iteration. -/

/-!
# Seal lane S3 — merges of lattice states are order-independent

Phase 4 ("QBX Live", `docs/phase_4_fast_track.md` §6) keeps engine state in a join-semilattice
and lets replicas merge states in whatever order messages arrive (CALM-style).  Item S3 asks
for the guarantee behind that design:

> monotone merge of lattice states is order-independent: any interleaving of merges reaches the
> same state.

A *merge schedule* is a binary tree whose leaves are the states received (in any order, any
bracketing, with repetitions allowed).  This file proves:

* `MergeTree.eval_le_iff` — the merged state is the least upper bound of the leaves;
* `MergeTree.eval_eq_of_mem_iff` (**S3**) — two schedules with the same *set* of leaves give the
  same state: order, bracketing and duplicate deliveries do not matter;
* `MergeTree.eval_eq_foldr` — every schedule agrees with the sequential merge of its leaves;
* `MergeTree.le_eval` — merging never loses information (every leaf is below the result).
-/
/-- A merge schedule: leaves are received states, nodes are merges. -/
/-- The states that a schedule merges (in delivery order, with repetitions). -/
/-- The state reached by running a merge schedule. -/
/-- The merged state is the least upper bound of the merged states. -/
/-- Merging never loses information: every received state is below the merged state. -/

/-- **Seal lane S3.** Two merge schedules that merge the same set of states reach the same
state, whatever the delivery order, bracketing or number of duplicate deliveries. -/
/-- Sequential merging of a list into a starting state is its least upper bound. -/
/-- Every merge schedule agrees with merging its leaves one at a time into the first one. -/

/-!
# Phase 4 seal lane, items S3–S6

The Lean claims the QBX Live engine relies on (`docs/phase_4_fast_track.md` §6).  S1 (Garside
normal form decides braid equality, `GarsideUniqueness.lean`) and S2 (the rewrite loop
terminates, `BraidTrace.lean`) were already proved.

* `MergeOrder` — **S3**: merges of join-semilattice states are independent of order, bracketing
  and duplicate delivery.
* `KleeneFinite` — **S4**: Kleene iteration of a monotone map on a finite lattice reaches the
  least fixed point within `card` rounds; fair chaotic (asynchronous) iteration reaches the same
  point.
* `CodedDecoding` — **S5**: any `k` evaluations of a degree `< k` matrix polynomial recover it
  (Lagrange interpolation), and fewer cannot.
* `FinalChord` — **S6**: the sonification's final chord (cycle type, writhe, Burau
  characteristic polynomial / eigenvalues) depends only on the braid group element.
-/

/-!
# Phase 1: the sheaf-condition checker (sheaf cohomology, degree 0)

The Phase 1 sheaf module (`qbx.categorical.sheaf`, migration `012_sheaf_cohomology.sql`) records a
finite topological space (its open sets), covers `{Uᵢ}` of open sets, and set-valued presheaves
given by their sections and restriction maps.  For each presheaf it checks the **sheaf
condition** on a cover `{Uᵢ}` of `U = ⋃ Uᵢ` in two separately reported halves:

* **locality** (`sheaf_locality`): two sections over `U` that agree on every `Uᵢ` are equal;
* **gluing** (`sheaf_gluing`): every compatible family (`sᵢ ∈ F(Uᵢ)` agreeing on the overlaps
  `Uᵢ ∩ Uⱼ`) has a gluing `s ∈ F(U)` restricting to every `sᵢ`;

and in particular the **empty cover of the empty open set** (`sheaf_empty_open`): `F(∅)` must have
exactly one section.  The degree-0 Čech cohomology of a cover is the set of compatible families;
the database checks recorded `H⁰` descriptors against it.

Results (for presheaves of types on a topological space, as in Mathlib):

* `SheafLocality`, `SheafGluing`, `isSheaf_iff_locality_and_gluing`: the two halves, taken over
  every cover, are together exactly Mathlib's `IsSheaf` — sound and complete.
* `uniqueBot`: a sheaf has exactly one section over `⊥` (the empty cover), which is
  the `sheaf_empty_open` check.
* `constBool_gluing_not_locality`, `constEmpty_locality_not_gluing`: neither half implies the
  other, on every space — so the checker needs both.  These are the constant presheaves with
  two sections and with none; the tests use both.
* `sectionsEquivCompatible`, `card_compatible_eq`: for a sheaf, the sections over
  `⋃ Uᵢ` are in bijection with the compatible families on `{Uᵢ}` (degree-0 Čech cohomology), so
  a recorded `H⁰` cardinality must equal the number of sections over the covered set.
* `presheafToTypes_locality_and_gluing`: the presheaf of all (dependent) functions passes both
  halves — the tests use it as an oracle on finite spaces.
-/

/-- The locality half of the sheaf condition (`sheaf_locality` in migration 012): two sections over
`⋃ Uᵢ` that agree on every `Uᵢ` are equal. -/

/-- The gluing half of the sheaf condition (`sheaf_gluing` in migration 012): every compatible family
on `{Uᵢ}` has a gluing over `⋃ Uᵢ`. -/
/-- The restrictions of one section form a compatible family. -/
/-- The checker's two halves, over every cover, are exactly Mathlib's sheaf condition. -/
/-- A sheaf has exactly one section over the empty open set (the `sheaf_empty_open` check). -/
/-- The constant presheaf with two sections. -/
/-- The constant presheaf with no sections. -/

/-- Gluing does not imply locality: the constant presheaf `Bool` glues every compatible family
but has two sections over `⊥` that agree on the empty cover. -/

/-- Locality does not imply gluing: the constant empty presheaf satisfies locality vacuously but
the empty family on the empty cover has no gluing. -/
/-- Neither half of the sheaf condition implies the other (on every space). -/

/-- For a sheaf, the sections over `⋃ Uᵢ` are in bijection with the compatible families on `{Uᵢ}`
(the degree-0 Čech cohomology of the cover), by restriction. -/

/-- For a sheaf, the number of compatible families on a cover (the cardinality of `H⁰`) equals the
number of sections over the covered set. -/

/-- The presheaf of all dependent functions passes both halves of the check (oracle used by the
tests on finite spaces). -/

/-!
# Short first-return loops decide flatness

`ws2_gauge.holonomy.brute_force_closed_walks conn root L` enumerates the holonomies of the
closed walks at `root` of length `≤ L` that return to `root` only at their end (a walk is not
extended after it comes back).  On its own this is a one-sided check: a flat connection gives
the identity on every such walk.  This file shows that the check becomes **exact** once `L` is
large enough, which is what the WS7 harness (`ws7_benchmarks.harness.brute_force_flat`) uses.

* `IsFirstReturn p` — the closed walk `p` at `r` visits `r` exactly once after its start
  (so only at its end), i.e. it is one of the walks enumerated by the brute force.
* `exists_firstReturn_of_holonomy_ne_one` — a closed walk with non-trivial holonomy contains
  a first-return closed walk, no longer, with non-trivial holonomy.
* `isFlat_iff_short_firstReturn` — fix roots `r` (constant along edges) and walks `w v` from
  `r v` to `v` of length `≤ D (r v)` (e.g. BFS paths, `D` = BFS depth of the component).
  Then the connection is flat iff every first-return closed walk at a root `ρ` of length
  `≤ 2 · D ρ + 1` has trivial holonomy.
-/

/-- A closed walk at `r` that returns to `r` only at its end: `r` occurs exactly once in the
support after the starting vertex.  These are the walks enumerated by
`brute_force_closed_walks`. -/

/-- A closed walk with non-trivial holonomy contains a first-return closed walk at the same
vertex, of at most the same length, whose holonomy is non-trivial. -/

/-- **Short first-return loops suffice.**  With roots `r` constant along edges and walks
`w v : r v ⟶ v` of length `≤ D (r v)`, a connection is flat iff every first-return closed walk
at a root `r v` of length `≤ 2 · D (r v) + 1` has trivial holonomy. -/

/-- Contrapositive form used by the harness: a non-flat connection has, at some root, a
first-return closed walk of length `≤ 2 · D + 1` with non-trivial holonomy. -/

/-!
# Simple braids: reduced positive words and the half twist

Background for the Garside normal form (`BraidNormalForm.lean`, migration 021), for every
strand count `n`:

* `inversions`, `IsDescent`: the inversion count of a permutation and its starting generators;
  `inversions_mul_transposition`: one adjacent transposition changes the inversion count by
  exactly `±1`.
* `Reduced`: a positive word whose length is the inversion count of its permutation.
  `eval_eq_of_reduced`: two reduced words with the same permutation are equal in `B_n`
  (Matsumoto's theorem for the symmetric group, in its positive braid form).
* `simpleBraid p`, the braid of the word `simple_word` of `qbx_ir.algebra.garside`, does not
  depend on the reduced word chosen (`simpleBraid_eq`); a starting generator splits off its
  front (`simpleBraid_descent`) and a generator outside the finishing set can be appended
  (`simpleBraid_mul_of_not_finishing`).
* `deltaBraid` is the half twist `Δ`; conjugation by `Δ` sends `σ_i` to `σ_{n-i}`
  (`deltaBraid_mul_sigma`) and simple braids to simple braids (`deltaBraid_mul_simpleBraid`).

Registry: H-054.
-/
/-! ### Inversions and descents -/

/-- The number of inversions of a permutation: pairs of strands that cross in its simple
braid. -/

/-- `i` is a starting generator of the simple braid of `p` (`p` sends the strand starting at
position `k` to position `p k`). -/
/-- Far generators: positions of `σ_j` are fixed by the transposition of `σ_i`. -/
/-- Adjacent generators that are both descents. -/
/-! ### Positive words and reduced words -/
/-- The positive braid word `σ_{i₁} σ_{i₂} ⋯` of a list of generators. -/

/-- The permutation of a positive word, in the convention of `qbx_ir.algebra.garside`: the
strand starting at position `k` ends at position `permOf u k`. -/

/-- A positive word is *reduced* when its length is the number of inversions of its
permutation (each pair of strands crosses at most once). -/

/-- **Positive braids with a reduced word.** Two reduced words with the same permutation are
equal in the braid group (Matsumoto's theorem for the symmetric group, positive form). -/
-- far commutation
-- adjacent generators: the braid relation
/-! ### Simple braids -/
/-- The first starting generator of `p` (`none` iff `p = 1`). -/

/-- `simple_word` of `qbx_ir.algebra.garside` with explicit fuel: repeatedly strip the first
starting generator. -/

/-- The positive word of the simple braid of `p` (`simple_word`); the fuel `n * n` bounds the
number of inversions, so it never runs out (`simpleWord_spec`). -/
/-- **Reduced words of a permutation are equal braids.** -/
/-- The simple (positive permutation) braid of a permutation. -/
/-- A starting generator can be split off the front of a simple braid. -/
/-- A generator outside the finishing set can be appended to a simple braid. -/
/-! ### The half twist `Δ` -/
/-- The permutation of the half twist `Δ` (`_delta`): position `k` goes to `n - 1 - k`. -/
/-- Conjugation by `Δ` on permutations (`_tau`). -/
/-- The half twist `Δ ∈ B_n`. -/
/-- Conjugation by `Δ` sends a simple braid to the simple braid of `tau`. -/

/-- `Δ σ_i⁻¹` is the simple braid that the normal form pushes past `Δ⁻¹` (`X_i` of
`left_normal_form_from_short`, conjugated by `Δ`). -/

/-!
# UV (Fano) completion of braid words

The Fano plane `PG(2, 𝔽₂)` has the points `1 … 7` (the nonzero vectors of `𝔽₂³`, written in
binary) and the seven lines `{i, j, i xor j}`.  It is the multiplication table of the imaginary
octonions (`SovKernel.Fano.fano_line_octonion`).  On eight strands, the generator `σᵢ`
(`i = 1 … 7`) is identified with the Fano point `i`.

## Main statements

* `completion_unique` : two distinct points determine a unique third point on their line —
  the "healed" generator is `i xor j` and no other point works.
* `completion_octonion` : the octonion product `eᵢ eⱼ = ± e_k` lands exactly on the completed
  point `k = i xor j`, with an orientation sign that flips under exchange (`completion_sign`).
* `closure_sizes`, `closure_idem`, `closure_full_iff` : the Fano closure of any set of points is a
  projective subspace (`∅`, a point, a line or the whole plane); it is the whole plane exactly
  when the set contains three non-collinear points.  A word has a **UV gap** when the closure of
  its generator support is not the whole plane.
* `hamming_card`, `hamming_min_weight`, `hamming_lines`, `single_error_syndrome`,
  `decode_corrects` : using the seven points as the columns of a parity-check matrix gives the
  **[7, 4, 3] Hamming code**; its 7 weight-3 codewords are exactly the Fano lines and the
  syndrome of a single error names the flipped position, so single errors are corrected.
* `simplex_weights`, `simplex_orthogonal` : the dual code spanned by the rows of the parity-check
  matrix is the **[7, 3, 4] simplex code** (every nonzero word has weight 4).
  (So the Fano plane gives both codes; the error-correcting one is `[7, 4, 3]`.)

All statements are finite and checked by evaluation (`decide`).
-/
/-! ### Completion of a pair of points -/

/-- **Fano completion is unique**: for distinct points `i, j`, the point `i xor j` lies on their
line, differs from both, and is the only such point. -/
/-- **Octonion anchor**: the product of two distinct imaginary units is `±` the completed unit. -/
/-- The orientation sign of the completion flips when the two points are exchanged. -/
/-! ### Closure -/
/-- One XOR-closure step: add `a xor b` for all distinct `a, b`. -/
/-- The Fano closure of a set of points (the nonzero part of its `𝔽₂`-span). -/
/-- All sublists of a list (as subsets). -/
/-- Closures stay inside the plane. -/
/-- **Closures are projective subspaces**: they have `0`, `1`, `3` or `7` points. -/
/-- The closure is XOR-closed: one more step adds nothing. -/
/-- The closure of two distinct points is their line. -/

/-- **UV completeness criterion**: the closure is the whole plane iff the set contains three
non-collinear points. -/
/-! ### Braid words on eight strands -/
/-- The Fano point of a letter of `B₈`: `σᵢ^{±1} ↦ i`. -/
/-- The generator support of a word, as a set of Fano points. -/
/-- The UV span of a word. -/
/-- A word is **UV complete** if its generator support spans the whole Fano plane. -/
/-- `σ₁ σ₂` spans only the line `{1, 2, 3}`; the healed generator is `σ₃`. -/
/-- `σ₁ σ₂ σ₄` spans the whole plane. -/
/-! ### The Hamming code of the Fano plane -/
/-- Hamming weight of a 7-bit word. -/
/-- The syndrome: XOR of the Fano points `j + 1` at the set bits `j`. -/
/-- The Hamming code: 7-bit words with zero syndrome. -/
/-- The 7-bit mask of a set of points. -/
/-- 16 codewords: dimension 4. -/
/-- Minimum distance 3. -/
/-- **The weight-3 codewords are exactly the seven Fano lines.** -/
/-- **The syndrome of a single error is the Fano point of the flipped position.** -/
/-- Syndrome decoding. -/
/-- **Single errors are corrected.** -/
/-- The three rows of the parity-check matrix (bit `r` of each point). -/
/-- The dual (simplex) code: all XOR combinations of the rows. -/

/-- **The dual code is the `[7, 3, 4]` simplex code**: 8 distinct words, all nonzero ones of
weight exactly 4. -/
/-- Simplex words are orthogonal (even overlap) to Hamming codewords. -/

/-!
# Gap filling: harmonic (exact anchor) and Fano candidates

A word with one **gap** is `u ++ ? :: v`.  Two independent ways to fill it:

* **Anchor candidate.**  The gap letter is determined by the expected braid
  (`gap_unique`: `u a v = u b v` in `B_n` forces `a = b`), and even by the Burau anchor alone,
  for every `n` (`anchor_gap_unique`), although Burau is not faithful for `n ≥ 5`: on single
  letters it is injective (`burauGen_two_injective`).
* **Fano candidate** (eight strands, `σᵢ ↦` Fano point `i`).  If the word carries a zero
  Fano checksum (XOR of the points of its letters, i.e. its points sum to `0` in `𝔽₂³`), the
  erased generator is the checksum of the rest (`fano_erasure`) and the writhe anchor gives its
  sign (`sign_of_writhe`); `fanoCandidate_correct` packages this.
* **Agreement / conflict.**  On balanced words both candidates return the true letter; so a
  disagreement certifies that the input was inconsistent (`conflict_detects`).

Caveat (`checksum_not_invariant`): the checksum is a property of the transmitted *word*, not of
the braid — braid relations change it — so it is used as an error-detecting code on words, as
in the Hamming-code view of `UVCompletion`.
-/
/-- Distinct letters are distinct braids. -/
/-- **A single gap is determined by the exact anchor.** -/
/-! ### The Burau anchor fixes a single gap, for every strand count -/
/-- The diagonal entry of a generator matrix at `t = 2` decides the letter. -/

/-- **A single gap is determined by the Burau anchor**, on any number of strands (although the
Burau representation is not faithful for `n ≥ 5`). -/
/-! ### The Fano checksum: recovering an erased generator -/
/-- The Fano checksum of a word on eight strands: XOR of the Fano points of its letters. -/

/-- **Fano erasure recovery**: if a word carries zero checksum, an erased letter's generator is
the checksum of the remaining letters. -/
/-- The writhe of the full word fixes the sign of the gap letter. -/

/-- The **Fano candidate** for a gap between `u` and `v`: generator from the checksum, sign from
the writhe anchor `wr`. -/
/-- **The Fano candidate is correct** on checksum-balanced words. -/

/-- **Harmonic/Fano agreement and conflict detection.**  On a checksum-balanced word with one
gap, the exact anchor (`gap_unique`) and the Fano candidate select the same letter.  Hence if the
letter `b` selected by the anchor differs from the Fano candidate, the input was not
checksum-balanced: the conflict certifies an inconsistency. -/

/-- The checksum is a transmission check, **not** a braid invariant: `σ₁σ₂σ₁ = σ₂σ₁σ₂` but the
checksums are `2` and `1`. -/

/-!
# Harmonic healing I: the spectral (Burau-eigenvalue) energy

The harmonic energy of a braid word at the point `t = e^{iθ}` of the unit circle is

  `E_θ(β) = Σᵢ |λᵢ − 1|²`,  `λᵢ` the eigenvalues of the reduced Burau matrix `ρ̄(β)(e^{iθ})`

(with multiplicity).  This file proves that it is a sound "distance to the identity":

* `specEnergy_eq_zero_iff` / `unipotent_of_specEnergy_eq_zero` : zero energy means every
  eigenvalue is `1`, i.e. the matrix is unipotent.
* `eq_one_of_unipotent_of_form` : a unipotent matrix preserving an *anisotropic* sesquilinear
  form is the identity.
* `burauAt_eq_one_of_specEnergy` : on the universal arc `|θ| < 2π/n` Squier's form is
  anisotropic (`HarmonicSweepN`), so **zero energy forces `ρ̄(β)(e^{iθ}) = 1`**.
* `specEnergy_arc_iff` : for every `n`, the energy vanishes on the whole arc iff the symbolic
  Burau matrix over `ℤ[t, t⁻¹]` is the identity (a Laurent polynomial with infinitely many
  zeros on the arc vanishes).
* `specEnergy_arc_iff_trivial_three` : **for `B₃`, the energy vanishes on the arc iff the
  braid is trivial** (faithfulness of Burau on `B₃`, `BurauFaithful`).
* `specEnergy_sigmaOneSq_zero`, `sigmaOneSq_ne_one` : one point is not enough — at `θ = 0`
  the energy of `σ₁²` is zero, yet `σ₁² ≠ 1`.

The time integral `∫₀¹ E(γ(t)) dt` of the design note is a non-negative combination of these
pointwise energies; it is not formalized here.  For `n ≥ 5` the Burau representation is not
faithful, so "Burau trivial" is strictly weaker than "braid trivial" there; the theorem
`specEnergy_arc_iff` is stated accordingly.
-/

/-- The **spectral (harmonic) energy** of a matrix: `Σ |λᵢ − 1|²` over the eigenvalues
(with multiplicity). -/
/-- Zero spectral energy means the matrix is unipotent. -/

/-- A unipotent matrix preserving a sesquilinear form that is anisotropic (`x^H K x ≠ 0` for
`x ≠ 0`) is the identity. -/
/-! ### From spectral energy on the arc to the trivial Burau matrix -/
/-- **Energy zero on the universal arc forces the Burau matrix to be the identity.** -/
/-- Evaluation of integer Laurent polynomials at a nonzero complex number. -/
/-- An integer Laurent polynomial vanishing on an infinite set of nonzero points is zero. -/
/-- Points `e^{iθ}`, `0 < θ < ε ≤ π`, form an infinite set. -/

/-- **Harmonic energy vanishes on the whole universal arc iff the Burau matrix is trivial**,
for every strand count. -/

/-- **Harmonic healing criterion for `B₃`: energy zero on the arc iff the braid is trivial.**
For three strands, the spectral energy `Σ |λᵢ − 1|²` of `ρ̄(β)(e^{iθ})` vanishes for every
`|θ| < 2π/3` exactly when `β = 1` in `B₃` (uses the faithfulness of the Burau representation
of `B₃`). -/
/-- The two-letter word `σ₁²` on three strands. -/
/-- **A single point does not suffice**: at `θ = 0` (`t = 1`) the energy of `σ₁²` vanishes. -/
/-- …although `σ₁²` is not the trivial braid (its writhe is `2`). -/

/-!
# Harmonic healing II: the healing flow

Two discrete flows used by the healing loop, with proved convergence/stability.

**Phase flow (eigenvalue healing).**  On the universal arc the Burau eigenvalues are unimodular
(`resonance_universal_n`), `λ = e^{iφ}`.  Its contribution to the spectral energy is
`|e^{iφ} − 1|² = 2 − 2 cos φ` (`phaseEnergy_eq`).  The gradient step
`φ ↦ (1 − κ) φ` (`0 < κ ≤ 1`) is the explicit Euler step for `∂ₜφ = −φ`:

* `phaseEnergy_le_sq` : `|e^{iφ} − 1|² ≤ φ²`;
* `phaseFlow_energy_le` : after `k` steps the energy is at most `(1 − κ)^{2k} φ₀²` —
  **geometric convergence of the eigenvalue to `1`**;
* `phaseFlow_energy_antitone` : for `|φ₀| ≤ π` the energy decreases monotonically.

**Heat flow on a cyclic signal.**  A braid word read as a periodic signal `x : ℤ/m → ℝ`
(e.g. its exponent sequence) is smoothed by the explicit heat step
`x ↦ x + α Δx`, `Δx(i) = x(i−1) − 2x(i) + x(i+1)`:

* `heatStep_sum` : the total (hence the mean, e.g. the writhe) is preserved;
* `heatStep_mem_Icc` : for `0 ≤ α ≤ 1/2` the discrete maximum principle holds.

The healing flow moves real-valued data (phases, smoothed signals); returning to an exact braid
word is the job of the anchors (`GapFilling.HarmonicFano`).  The geometric-neural-operator layer
of the design note (learned metric/curvature) is an optional numerical component and is not
part of these proofs.
-/
/-! ### Phase flow -/
/-- The energy of a unimodular eigenvalue `e^{iφ}`. -/
/-- The phase after `k` healing steps of rate `κ`. -/
/-- **Geometric convergence**: after `k` steps the energy is at most `(1 − κ)^{2k} φ₀²`. -/
/-- The healing energy tends to `0`: the eigenvalue converges to `1`. -/
/-- **Monotone healing**: for `|φ₀| ≤ π` the energy never increases along the flow. -/

/-!
# The strand crossing matrix is not a link invariant

`LinkingMatrix.lean` builds the strand crossing matrix `crossMatrix g` of a braid `g` and proves it
is well defined on the braid group (invariant under the rewrite rules R01–R03).  It is **not** an
invariant of the closed link: Markov moves change it.

* `crossMatrix_not_markov_invariant`: `σ₂ σ₁² σ₂⁻¹` and `σ₁²` (3 strands) are related by one
  conjugation move but have different crossing matrices (`(0, 1)` entry `0` vs `2`);
* `crossMatrix_not_markov_invariant_up_to_relabel`: `σ₂ σ₁ σ₂⁻¹` and `σ₁` are related by one
  conjugation move, and no relabelling of the strands carries one crossing matrix to the other.

What *is* invariant under Markov moves is the data per closure component: the number of
components and the multiset of linking numbers between components (`numComponents_markov`,
`linkingSpectrum_markov` in `ClosureLinking.lean`).  For a pure braid conjugation acts on the
labelled linking matrix by relabelling (`linkMatrix_conj` in `PureLinkingMatrix.lean`).
-/
/-- `σ₁²` on three strands (a Hopf link plus a separate unknot). -/
/-- Its conjugate `σ₂ σ₁² σ₂⁻¹`. -/

/-- The strand crossing matrix is not invariant under Markov moves: `σ₂ σ₁² σ₂⁻¹` and `σ₁²` are
related by one conjugation move but have different `(0, 1)` entries. -/
/-- `σ₁` on three strands (closure: an unknot and a separate unknot). -/
/-- Its conjugate `σ₂ σ₁ σ₂⁻¹`. -/

/-- **Not even up to relabelling the strands**: `σ₂ σ₁ σ₂⁻¹` and `σ₁` are related by one
conjugation move, but no permutation of the strand labels carries the crossing matrix of one to
that of the other (the first has an entry `-1`, the second has none).  The invariants of the
closure are the linking numbers *between closure components* (`linkingSpectrum_markov`). -/

/-!
# The strand-indexed torus `Q_n □ (T²_m)ⁿ` (WS9 A-3, amendment FA-052, register item X-05)

Through `torusGate` (`TorusBraid.lean`) a torus braid only shows its *total* winding. Following
recommendation (b) of register item X-05, every strand gets its own torus factor `ZMod m × ZMod m`.
The shadow group `S_n ⋉ (ℤ²)ⁿ` then acts by the **wreath-product action**: bit `j` and the torus
pair of strand `j` move to position `π j`, and afterwards strand `i` is translated by its winding
`w i` (read mod `m`). This is the Lean counterpart of the Python `WreathGate`
(`foundation/ws5_braid_ops/wreath.py`).

* `wreathAct`, `wreathAct_one`, `wreathAct_mul`: an action of `Shadow n`;
* `strandGate`, `strandGate_one`, `strandGate_mul`: hence an action of `B_n(T²)`;
* `strandGate_ofPlanar`: planar braids only permute (no translation);
* `strandGate_ta`, `strandGate_tb`: `a`, `b` translate strand `0` by one step;
* `strandGate_sees_strand_winding`: for `n ≥ 2`, `m ≥ 2` the gates of `a` and of its conjugate
  `σ₁ a σ₁⁻¹` (strand `1` winds instead of strand `0`) differ, although `torusGate` cannot
  distinguish them (`torusGate_conj_eq`: they have the same total winding).
-/
/-- An address of `Q_n □ (T²_m)ⁿ`: `n` bits and one torus point per strand. -/
/-- Reduction of a winding pair mod `m`. -/
/-- The wreath-product action of `S_n ⋉ (ℤ²)ⁿ`. -/
/-- The gate of a torus braid on the strand-indexed torus. -/
/-- `β ↦ strandGate β` is an action of `B_n(T²)`. -/
/-- Planar braids only permute strands. -/

/-- The total-winding gate `torusGate` does not distinguish the loop of strand `0` from its
conjugate by a crossing. -/
/-- The zero address. -/

/-- **Strand windings are visible.** For `n ≥ 2`, `m ≥ 2`, the torus loop `a` of strand `0` and
its conjugate `σ₁ a σ₁⁻¹` (the loop of strand `1`) act differently on `Q_n □ (T²_m)ⁿ`, although
`torusGate` cannot tell them apart (`torusGate_conj_eq`). -/

declarations.name: upW
declarations.signature_heuristic:
def upW (s : ℕ → G) : ℕ → ℕ → G
  | _, 0 => 1
  | a, L + 1 => s a * upW s (a + 1) L

declarations.name: upW_succ_right
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem upW_succ_right (s : ℕ → G) : ∀ a L, upW s a (L + 1) = upW s a L * s (a + L)
  | a, 0 => by simp [upW]
  | a, L + 1 => by
    rw [upW, upW_succ_right s (a + 1) L, upW, mul_assoc, show a + 1 + L = a + (L + 1) by ring]

/-- An element commuting with each letter commutes with the word. -/

declarations.name: commute_upW
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem commute_upW {s : ℕ → G} {x : G} :
    ∀ b L, (∀ j, b ≤ j → j < b + L → x * s j = s j * x) → x * upW s b L = upW s b L * x
  | _, 0, _ => by simp [upW]
  | b, L + 1, h => by
    rw [upW, ← mul_assoc, h b le_rfl (by omega), mul_assoc,
      commute_upW (b + 1) L (fun j h1 h2 => h j (by omega) (by omega)), mul_assoc]

/-- The relations of the Artin group of type `B_k`, on generators `τ` and `s 1, …, s (k-1)`. -/

declarations.name: TypeBRels
declarations.signature_heuristic:
structure TypeBRels (τ : G) (s : ℕ → G) (k : ℕ) : Prop where
  four : 2 ≤ k → τ * s 1 * τ * s 1 = s 1 * τ * s 1 * τ
  tcomm : ∀ i, 2 ≤ i → i < k → τ * s i = s i * τ
  three : ∀ i, 1 ≤ i → i + 1 < k → s i * s (i + 1) * s i = s (i + 1) * s i * s (i + 1)
  two : ∀ i j, 1 ≤ i → i + 2 ≤ j → j < k → s i * s j = s j * s i

variable {τ : G} {s : ℕ → G} {k : ℕ}

/-- Pushing a letter through an ascending word lowers its index by one. -/

declarations.name: upW_shift
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem upW_shift (h : TypeBRels τ s k) :
    ∀ L a i, 1 ≤ a → a + 1 ≤ i → i + 1 ≤ a + L → a + L ≤ k →
      s i * upW s a L = upW s a L * s (i - 1)
  | 0, a, i, _, h1, h2, _ => by omega
  | L + 1, a, i, ha, h1, h2, hk => by
    rw [upW]
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge (a + 1) i with hi | hi
    · rw [← mul_assoc, ← h.two a i ha (by omega) (by omega), mul_assoc,
        upW_shift h L (a + 1) i (by omega) (by omega) (by omega) (by omega), mul_assoc]
    · obtain rfl : i = a + 1

declarations.name: upW_word_shift
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem upW_word_shift (h : TypeBRels τ s k) {L : ℕ} (hL : L + 1 ≤ k) :
    ∀ len b, 2 ≤ b → b + len ≤ L + 1 →
      upW s b len * upW s 1 L = upW s 1 L * upW s (b - 1) len
  | 0, b, _, _ => by simp [upW]
  | len + 1, b, hb, hlen => by
    rw [upW, mul_assoc, upW_word_shift h hL len (b + 1) (by omega) (by omega), ← mul_assoc,
      upW_shift h L 1 b le_rfl (by omega) (by omega) (by omega), mul_assoc,
      show b + 1 - 1 = b by omega]
    obtain ⟨b', rfl⟩ : ∃ b', b = b' + 1

declarations.name: typeBDelta
declarations.signature_heuristic: def typeBDelta (τ : G) (s : ℕ → G) (L : ℕ) : G

declarations.name: typeB_shift
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeB_shift (h : TypeBRels τ s (L + 1)) {i : ℕ} (h2 : 2 ≤ i) (hi : i ≤ L) :
    s i * typeBDelta τ s L = typeBDelta τ s L * s (i - 1)

declarations.name: typeB_wrap
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeB_wrap (h : TypeBRels τ s (L + 1)) (hL : 1 ≤ L) :
    s 1 * typeBDelta τ s L ^ 2 = typeBDelta τ s L ^ 2 * s L

declarations.name: typeB_shift_pow
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeB_shift_pow (h : TypeBRels τ s (L + 1)) :
    ∀ j i, j + 1 ≤ i → i ≤ L → s i * typeBDelta τ s L ^ j = typeBDelta τ s L ^ j * s (i - j)
  | 0, i, _, _ => by simp
  | j + 1, i, h1, h2 => by
    rw [pow_succ', ← mul_assoc, typeB_shift h (by omega) h2, mul_assoc,
      typeB_shift_pow h j (i - 1) (by omega) (by omega), ← mul_assoc, ← pow_succ',
      show i - 1 - j = i - (j + 1) by omega]

/-- Every `sᵢ` (`1 ≤ i ≤ L`) commutes with `δ^{L+1}`. -/

declarations.name: typeB_s_mul_delta_pow
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeB_s_mul_delta_pow (h : TypeBRels τ s (L + 1)) {i : ℕ} (h1 : 1 ≤ i) (hi : i ≤ L) :
    s i * typeBDelta τ s L ^ (L + 1) = typeBDelta τ s L ^ (L + 1) * s i

declarations.name: typeB_delta_pow_central
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeB_delta_pow_central (h : TypeBRels τ s (L + 1)) :
    (∀ i, 1 ≤ i → i ≤ L → s i * typeBDelta τ s L ^ (L + 1) = typeBDelta τ s L ^ (L + 1) * s i) ∧
      τ * typeBDelta τ s L ^ (L + 1) = typeBDelta τ s L ^ (L + 1) * τ

declarations.name: upW_eq_prod
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem upW_eq_prod (s : ℕ → G) : ∀ a L, upW s a L = ((List.range' a L).map s).prod
  | _, 0 => rfl
  | a, L + 1 => by rw [upW, upW_eq_prod s (a + 1) L, List.range'_succ]; simp

/-- The descending word `downW s j = s_j s_{j-1} ⋯ s_1` (`j` letters). -/

declarations.name: downW
declarations.signature_heuristic:
def downW (s : ℕ → G) : ℕ → G
  | 0 => 1
  | j + 1 => s (j + 1) * downW s j

declarations.name: commute_downW
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem commute_downW {x : G} :
    ∀ j, (∀ i, 1 ≤ i → i ≤ j → x * s i = s i * x) → x * downW s j = downW s j * x
  | 0, _ => by simp [downW]
  | j + 1, h => by
    rw [downW, ← mul_assoc, h (j + 1) (by omega) le_rfl, mul_assoc,
      commute_downW j (fun i h1 h2 => h i h1 (by omega)), mul_assoc]

/-- The Coxeter words `e_j = (s_j ⋯ s₁ τ)(s_{j+1} ⋯ s_L)`, interpolating between
`e₀ = δ = τ s₁ ⋯ s_L` and `e_L = s_L ⋯ s₁ τ`. -/

declarations.name: typeBE
declarations.signature_heuristic: def typeBE (τ : G) (s : ℕ → G) (L j : ℕ) : G

declarations.name: typeBE_succ
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeBE_succ (h : TypeBRels τ s (L + 1)) {j : ℕ} (hj : j < L) :
    typeBE τ s L (j + 1) = (downW s j * τ)⁻¹ * typeBE τ s L j * (downW s j * τ)

declarations.name: typeBE_pow
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeBE_pow (h : TypeBRels τ s (L + 1)) :
    ∀ j, j ≤ L → typeBE τ s L j ^ (L + 1) = typeBDelta τ s L ^ (L + 1)
  | 0, _ => by simp [typeBE, downW, typeBDelta]
  | j + 1, hj => by
    obtain ⟨hs, hτ⟩

declarations.name: bn_entry
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem bn_entry {L a b : ℕ} (ha : a < L + 1) (hb : b < L + 1) :
    CoxeterMatrix.Bₙ (L + 1) ⟨a, ha⟩ ⟨b, hb⟩ =
      if a = b then 1 else if (a = L ∧ b + 1 = L) ∨ (b = L ∧ a + 1 = L) then 4
        else if b + 1 = a ∨ a + 1 = b then 3 else 2

declarations.signature_heuristic: theorem natGen_of_lt {a : ℕ} (h : a < n) : natGen M a = σ ⟨a, h⟩

declarations.name: natGen_two
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem natGen_two {a b : ℕ} (ha : a < n) (hb : b < n) (h : M ⟨a, ha⟩ ⟨b, hb⟩ = 2) :

declarations.name: natGen_three
declarations.signature_heuristic:

declarations.name: natGen_four

theorem natGen_four {a b : ℕ} (ha : a < n) (hb : b < n) (h : M ⟨a, ha⟩ ⟨b, hb⟩ = 4) :

declarations.signature_heuristic: abbrev ArtinBn (L : ℕ)

declarations.name: bnS
declarations.signature_heuristic: def bnS (L : ℕ) (i : ℕ) : ArtinBn L

declarations.name: bn_typeBRels
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem bn_typeBRels (L : ℕ) : TypeBRels (natGen _ L : ArtinBn L) (bnS L) (L + 1) where

declarations.name: bnCox
declarations.signature_heuristic: def bnCox (L : ℕ) : ArtinBn L

declarations.name: range'_map_sub
declarations.signature_heuristic: theorem range'_map_sub (L : ℕ) : (List.range' 1 L).map (fun i => L - i) = (List.range L).reverse

declarations.name: bnCox_eq_typeBDelta
declarations.signature_heuristic: theorem bnCox_eq_typeBDelta (L : ℕ) : bnCox L = typeBDelta (natGen _ L) (bnS L) L

declarations.name: bn_downW
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem bn_downW (L : ℕ) : ∀ j, j ≤ L → downW (bnS L) j = natLift _ (List.range' (L - j) j)

/-!
# Type `Bₙ` for every `n`: `δ^n` is central, so `c^{2n} = Δ²`

In the Artin group of type `B_k` (generators `τ, s₁, …, s_{k-1}`, with `τ s₁ τ s₁ = s₁ τ s₁ τ`,
`sᵢ sᵢ₊₁ sᵢ = sᵢ₊₁ sᵢ sᵢ₊₁`, all other pairs commuting) let

  `δ = τ s₁ s₂ ⋯ s_{k-1}`   (a Coxeter element; the Coxeter number of `B_k` is `h = 2k`).

**Theorem** (`typeB_delta_pow_central`): `Δ := δ^k` commutes with every generator, hence is central,
and `c^h = Δ²` for `c = δ`.  The proof is pure braid-relation algebra, for every `k`:

* `upW_shift`: `sᵢ (s_a ⋯ s_{a+L-1}) = (s_a ⋯ s_{a+L-1}) sᵢ₋₁` for `a < i < a + L`;
* `typeB_shift`: `sᵢ δ = δ sᵢ₋₁` for `2 ≤ i ≤ k - 1`;
* `typeB_wrap`: `s₁ δ² = δ² s_{k-1}` (here the relation `τ s₁ τ s₁ = s₁ τ s₁ τ` is used);
* combining: `sᵢ δ^k = δ^{i-1} s₁ δ² δ^{k-1-i} = ⋯ = δ^k sᵢ`, and `τ = δ (s₁⋯s_{k-1})⁻¹`;
* `typeBE_pow`: the Coxeter words `e_j = (s_j ⋯ s₁ τ)(s_{j+1} ⋯ s_L)` are successive conjugates,
  so all of them (from `δ` to `s_L ⋯ s₁ τ`) have the same `k`-th power.

Applied to Mathlib's `CoxeterMatrix.Bₙ (L + 1)` (whose special node is `L`), with
`c = σ_L σ_{L-1} ⋯ σ₀` (`bnCox`), `c' = σ₀ σ₁ ⋯ σ_L` (`bnCoxAsc`) and `Δ = c^{L+1}` (`bnDelta`):

* `bnDelta_central`: **`Δ` is central**, for every `n = L + 1`;
* `bnCox_pow_coxeterNumber`, `bnCoxAsc_pow_coxeterNumber`: **`c^{2n} = c'^{2n} = Δ²`**;
* `bnCoxAsc_pow`: `c'^n = c^n`;
* `bnDelta_degree`, `bnDelta_pow_ne_one`: `Δ` has degree `n²` (the number of positive roots) and
  infinite order.

Every generator divides `Δ`, on both sides with the same positive cofactor of length `n² - 1`, for
every `n`: `bnDelta_gen_dvd` in `ArtinDivisors.lean` (before, this was checked by certificates for
`n = 3, 4, 5` only, `QBX.Formal.Streams.ArtinB3` etc.).
-/
/-- The ascending word `upW s a L = s_a s_{a+1} ⋯ s_{a+L-1}` (`L` letters). -/
/-- An element commuting with each letter commutes with the word. -/
/-- The relations of the Artin group of type `B_k`, on generators `τ` and `s 1, …, s (k-1)`. -/
/-- Pushing a letter through an ascending word lowers its index by one. -/
/-- Pushing a whole ascending word `s_b ⋯ s_{b+len-1}` (`b ≥ 2`) through `s₁ ⋯ s_L`. -/
/-- The Coxeter element `δ = τ s₁ ⋯ s_L` of `B_{L+1}`. -/
/-- `sᵢ δ = δ sᵢ₋₁` for `2 ≤ i ≤ L`. -/
/-- Iterating `typeB_shift`: `sᵢ δ^j = δ^j s_{i-j}` for `j < i ≤ L`. -/
/-- Every `sᵢ` (`1 ≤ i ≤ L`) commutes with `δ^{L+1}`. -/
/-- **`Δ = δ^{L+1}` commutes with every generator of `B_{L+1}`** (including `τ`). -/
/-- The descending word `downW s j = s_j s_{j-1} ⋯ s_1` (`j` letters). -/

/-- The Coxeter words `e_j = (s_j ⋯ s₁ τ)(s_{j+1} ⋯ s_L)`, interpolating between
`e₀ = δ = τ s₁ ⋯ s_L` and `e_L = s_L ⋯ s₁ τ`. -/
/-- All the Coxeter words `e_j` have the same `(L+1)`-st power `δ^{L+1}`. -/
/-! ## Mathlib's `CoxeterMatrix.Bₙ` -/
/-- The Artin group of Mathlib's `Bₙ` with `n = L + 1` generators. -/
/-- The generators in "type `B` order": `τ = σ_L` is the special node, `sᵢ = σ_{L-i}`. -/
/-- The Coxeter element `c = σ_L σ_{L-1} ⋯ σ₀` of `B_{L+1}` (special node first). -/
/-- The Coxeter element `c' = σ₀ σ₁ ⋯ σ_L` (special node last). -/
/-- An element commuting with `τ` and all `sᵢ` is central in `ArtinBn L`. -/
/-- **`Δ = c^n` is central in the Artin group of type `Bₙ`, for every `n = L + 1`.** -/
/-- **The other Coxeter element gives the same `Δ`**: `(σ₀σ₁⋯σ_L)^{L+1} = (σ_L⋯σ₁σ₀)^{L+1}`. -/
/-- The Garside element `Δ = c^n` of `Bₙ` (`n = L + 1`). -/
/-- **`c^h = Δ²`** with `h = 2n` the Coxeter number of `Bₙ`, for `c = σ_L⋯σ₀`. -/
/-- **`c'^h = Δ²`** for the other Coxeter element `c' = σ₀σ₁⋯σ_L`. -/
/-- **`Δ` is central in the Artin group of type `Bₙ`.** -/
/-- `Δ` has degree `n²`, the number of positive roots of `Bₙ`. -/
/-- `Δ` has infinite order. -/

declarations.name: dropAlt
declarations.signature_heuristic:
def dropAlt (i j : ℕ) : ℕ → List ℕ → Option (List ℕ)
  | 0, w => some w
  | _ + 1, [] => none
  | k + 1, a :: w => if Nat.beq a i then dropAlt j i k w else none

/-- Replace `i j i ⋯` (`k` letters) at position `p` by `j i j ⋯`. -/

declarations.name: altStep
declarations.signature_heuristic:
def altStep (i j k : ℕ) : ℕ → List ℕ → Option (List ℕ)
  | 0, w =>
    match dropAlt i j k w with
    | some r => some (altWord j i k ++ r)
    | none => none
  | _ + 1, [] => none
  | p + 1, a :: rest =>
    match altStep i j k p rest with
    | some w => some (a :: w)
    | none => none

/-- Apply the move `(p, i, j)` (indices `i, j < n`) with exponent `m i j`. -/

declarations.name: applyMoveGen
declarations.signature_heuristic: def applyMoveGen (m : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) (w : List ℕ) (p i j : ℕ) : Option (List ℕ)

declarations.name: runCodeGen
declarations.signature_heuristic:
def runCodeGen (m : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ → List ℕ → Option (List ℕ)
  | 0, _, w => some w
  | k + 1, c, w =>
    match applyMoveGen m n w (c % 8192 / 64) (c % 8192 / 8 % 8) (c % 8192 % 8) with
    | some w' => runCodeGen m n k (c / 8192) w'
    | none => none

/-- The certificate check: running the `k` packed moves `c` from `u` ends exactly at `v`. -/

declarations.name: checkCodeGen
declarations.signature_heuristic: def checkCodeGen (m : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) (u v : List ℕ) (k c : ℕ) : Bool

declarations.name: dropAlt_eq
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem dropAlt_eq : ∀ {i j k : ℕ} {w r : List ℕ}, dropAlt i j k w = some r →
    w = altWord i j k ++ r
  | _, _, 0, w, r, h => by simp only [dropAlt, Option.some.injEq] at h; subst h; rfl
  | _, _, _ + 1, [], _, h => by simp [dropAlt] at h
  | i, j, k + 1, a :: w, r, h => by
    simp only [dropAlt] at h
    split_ifs at h with ha
    rw [Nat.eq_of_beq_eq_true ha, dropAlt_eq h]
    rfl

declarations.name: altStep_sound
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem altStep_sound {i j k : ℕ}
    (hr : ((altWord i j k).map g).prod = ((altWord j i k).map g).prod) :
    ∀ (p : ℕ) {w w' : List ℕ}, altStep i j k p w = some w' →
      (w.map g).prod = (w'.map g).prod
  | 0, w, w', h => by
    simp only [altStep] at h
    split at h
    · next r hd =>
      cases h
      rw [dropAlt_eq hd]
      simp only [List.map_append, List.prod_append, hr]
    · cases h
  | _ + 1, [], _, h => by simp [altStep] at h
  | p + 1, a :: rest, w', h => by
    simp only [altStep] at h
    split at h
    · next w hw =>
      cases h
      simp only [List.map_cons, List.prod_cons, altStep_sound hr p hw]
    · cases h

declarations.name: applyMoveGen_sound
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem applyMoveGen_sound (hg : BraidRels m n g) {w w' : List ℕ} {p i j : ℕ}
    (h : applyMoveGen m n w p i j = some w') : (w.map g).prod = (w'.map g).prod

declarations.name: runCodeGen_sound
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem runCodeGen_sound (hg : BraidRels m n g) :
    ∀ (k c : ℕ) {u v : List ℕ}, runCodeGen m n k c u = some v →
      (u.map g).prod = (v.map g).prod
  | 0, _, u, v, h => by cases h; rfl
  | k + 1, c, u, v, h => by
    simp only [runCodeGen] at h
    split at h
    · next w' hw => rw [applyMoveGen_sound hg hw, runCodeGen_sound hg k _ h]
    · cases h

/-- **Soundness of the general certificate check.** -/

declarations.name: checkCodeGen_sound
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem checkCodeGen_sound (hg : BraidRels m n g) {u v : List ℕ} {k c : ℕ}
    (h : checkCodeGen m n u v k c = true) : (u.map g).prod = (v.map g).prod

declarations.name: coxExpOf
declarations.signature_heuristic:
def coxExpOf : List (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ
  | [], i, j => if i.beq j then 1 else 2
  | (a, b, k) :: es, i, j =>
    if (i.beq a && j.beq b) || (i.beq b && j.beq a) then k else coxExpOf es i j

comments.text:
/-!
# Braid-move certificates for arbitrary Coxeter exponents

`QBX.Formal.Streams.checkCode` only handles exponents `2` and `3` (simply-laced types).  This file
gives the same kind of kernel-checkable certificate for **any** exponents, so that it also covers
the types `B`, `F₄` and `H` (exponents `4` and `5`).

A move `(p, i, j)` replaces the alternating block `i j i ⋯` (`m i j` letters) starting at
position `p` of a word by `j i j ⋯`.  Moves are packed into one natural number exactly as for
`runCode` (one base-`2^13` digit `p * 64 + i * 8 + j` per move, least significant first).

* `checkCodeGen_sound`: a successful check proves that the two words have the same product in
  every group satisfying the braid relations;
* `natLift_eq_gen`: the version for the Artin group of a Coxeter matrix on `Fin n`.
-/
/-- If `w` starts with the alternating word `i j i ⋯` (`k` letters), return the rest. -/
/-- Replace `i j i ⋯` (`k` letters) at position `p` by `j i j ⋯`. -/
/-- Apply the move `(p, i, j)` (indices `i, j < n`) with exponent `m i j`. -/
/-- Apply `k` moves packed into `c` (same packing as `runCode`). -/
/-- The certificate check: running the `k` packed moves `c` from `u` ends exactly at `v`. -/
/-- **Soundness of the general certificate check.** -/

comments.text:
/-!
# The dihedral Artin groups `I₂(k)`: `c^k = Δ²` for every `k ≥ 2`

Mathlib's `CoxeterMatrix.I₂ₘ m` is the rank-two Coxeter matrix with off-diagonal entry
`k = m + 2`; it covers `A₂ = I₂(3)`, `B₂ = I₂(4)`, `H₂ = I₂(5)` and `G₂ = I₂(6)`.  Its Artin group
has two generators `σ₀, σ₁` and the single relation `σ₀σ₁σ₀⋯ = σ₁σ₀σ₁⋯` (`k` letters each).

With the Coxeter element `c = σ₀σ₁` (Coxeter number `h = k`) and the Garside element
`Δ = σ₀σ₁σ₀⋯` (`k` letters, the number of positive roots), we prove for **every** `k`:

* `dihCox_pow`: **`c^k = Δ²`**;
* `σ_mul_dihDelta_even`, `σ_mul_dihDelta_odd`: `σᵢ Δ = Δ σᵢ` if `k` is even, and
  `σ₀ Δ = Δ σ₁`, `σ₁ Δ = Δ σ₀` if `k` is odd (the diagram flip);
* `dihDelta_central`: `Δ` is central when `k` is even; `dihDelta_not_central`: it is not when `k`
  is odd (detected in the dihedral group of order `2k`);
* `dihDelta_sq_central`: `Δ²` is always central;
* `dihCox_rev_pow`: the other Coxeter element `σ₁σ₀` also satisfies `(σ₁σ₀)^k = Δ²`;
* `dihDelta_degree`, `dihDelta_pow_ne_one`: `Δ` has degree `k` and infinite order.

The proof is by hand: no certificates are needed.
-/
/-- An alternating word of even length `2t` multiplies out to `(xy)^t`. -/
/-- An alternating word of odd length `2t+1` multiplies out to `x(yx)^t`. -/
/-- The Artin group of type `I₂(m + 2)`. -/
/-- The Coxeter element `c = σ₀σ₁`. -/
/-- The Garside element `Δ = σ₀σ₁σ₀⋯` (`m + 2` letters). -/
/-- The defining relation: `Δ = σ₁σ₀σ₁⋯` as well. -/
/-- Even case: `Δ = (σ₀σ₁)^t = (σ₁σ₀)^t` where `m + 2 = 2t`. -/
/-- Odd case: `Δ = σ₀(σ₁σ₀)^t = σ₁(σ₀σ₁)^t` where `m + 2 = 2t + 1`. -/
/-- **`c^k = Δ²`** in the Artin group of type `I₂(k)`, `k = m + 2` (the Coxeter number). -/
/-- Even `k`: every generator commutes with `Δ`. -/
/-- Odd `k`: `σ₀ Δ = Δ σ₁`. -/
/-- Odd `k`: `σ₁ Δ = Δ σ₀`. -/
/-- Odd `k`: conjugation by `Δ` swaps the two generators. -/
/-- **For even `k`, `Δ` is central.** -/
/-- `Δ²` commutes with every generator. -/
/-- **`Δ²` is central** (for every `k`). -/
/-- The other Coxeter element: `(σ₁σ₀)^k = Δ²`. -/
/-! ## The dihedral quotient (used to show `Δ` is not central for odd `k`) -/
/-- Products of alternating words of reflections in the dihedral group. -/

/-- For odd `k = m + 2`, the Artin group of `I₂(k)` maps onto the dihedral group of order `2k`,
with `σᵢ ↦ srᵢ`. -/
/-- **For odd `k`, `Δ` is not central** (it swaps `σ₀` and `σ₁` under conjugation). -/
/-- `Δ` has degree `k` (the number of positive roots of `I₂(k)`). -/
/-- `Δ` has infinite order. -/

/-!
# Every generator divides `Δ`: types `Bₙ` and `Dₙ`, for every `n`

For the Coxeter element `c = σ_L σ_{L-1} ⋯ σ₀` and `Δ = c^n` (type `B_n`, `n = L + 1`) or
`Δ = c^{n-1}` (type `D_n`), we exhibit, for every generator `σₜ`, an explicit positive word `Xₜ`
of length `|Δ| - 1` with

* type `B` (`bnDelta_gen_dvd`): `Δ = σₜ Xₜ = Xₜ σₜ`;
* type `D` (`dnDelta_gen_dvd`): `Δ = σₜ Xₜ = Xₜ σ_{ε t}`, with `ε = dnFlip` the diagram flip.

Method: `c` begins with `σ_L` (and, for `D`, also with `σ_{L-1}`, which commutes with `σ_L`) and
ends with `σ₀`; pushing the final `σ₀` of one factor `c` through `c^j` turns it into `σⱼ`
(`sᵢ c = c sᵢ₋₁`), so `σⱼ` right-divides `c^{j+1}`.  The twisted commutation of `Δ` with the
generators (`bnDelta_central`, `σ_mul_dnDelta`) then transfers divisibility from one side to the
other with the same cofactor.
-/
/-- If `g d = d g'` and `d = x g'`, then `d = g x`. -/
/-- If `g d = d g'` and `d = g x`, then `d = x g'`. -/
/-- The word of `c = σ_L ⋯ σ₀`. -/
/-- The cofactor of `σⱼ` (`j < L`): `c^{L-j} · (σ_L ⋯ σ₁) · c^j`. -/
/-- The cofactor of `σ_L`: `(σ_{L-1} ⋯ σ₀) · c^e`. -/

/-- If `x = Y σ₀` and `σ₀ x^j = x^j σⱼ` (`j ≤ e`), then `x^{e+1}` is the product of the right
cofactor word and `σⱼ`. -/

/-- **Every generator divides `Δ` in the Artin group of type `B_n`, for every `n = L + 1`**: for
each `σₜ` there is a positive word `Xₜ` of length `n² - 1` with `Δ = σₜ Xₜ = Xₜ σₜ`. -/
/-- The cofactor of `σ_{L-1}` in type `D`: `σ_L (σ_{L-2} ⋯ σ₀) · c^e`. -/

/-- **Every generator divides `Δ` in the Artin group of type `D_n`, for every `n = L + 1 ≥ 2`**:
for each `σₜ` there is a positive word `Xₜ` of length `n(n-1) - 1` with
`Δ = σₜ Xₜ = Xₜ σ_{ε t}` (`ε = dnFlip`, the identity when `n` is even). -/
-- `j ≤ L - 2`: right divisor, `ε` fixes `j`
-- `σ_{L-1}` left-divides `c = σ_{L-1} σ_L σ_{L-2} ⋯ σ₀`
-- `σ_L` left-divides `c`

declarations.name: TypeDRels
declarations.signature_heuristic:
structure TypeDRels (u : G) (s : ℕ → G) (N : ℕ) : Prop where
  u1 : u * s 1 = s 1 * u
  u2 : 2 ≤ N → u * s 2 * u = s 2 * u * s 2
  ucomm : ∀ i, 3 ≤ i → i ≤ N → u * s i = s i * u
  three : ∀ i, 1 ≤ i → i + 1 ≤ N → s i * s (i + 1) * s i = s (i + 1) * s i * s (i + 1)
  two : ∀ i j, 1 ≤ i → i + 2 ≤ j → j ≤ N → s i * s j = s j * s i

variable {u : G} {s : ℕ → G} {N : ℕ}

declarations.name: TypeDRels.mono
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem TypeDRels.mono (h : TypeDRels u s N) {K : ℕ} (hK : K ≤ N) : TypeDRels u s K where
  u1

declarations.name: typeD_four
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeD_four (h : TypeDRels u s N) (hN : 2 ≤ N) :
    u * s 1 * s 2 * (u * s 1) * s 2 = s 2 * (u * s 1) * s 2 * (u * s 1)

declarations.name: typeD_typeBRels
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeD_typeBRels (h : TypeDRels u s N) : TypeBRels (u * s 1) (fun i => s (i + 1)) N where
  four hk

declarations.name: upW_shift_index
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem upW_shift_index (s : ℕ → G) : ∀ a L, upW (fun i => s (i + 1)) a L = upW s (a + 1) L
  | _, 0 => rfl
  | a, L + 1 => by rw [upW, upW, upW_shift_index s (a + 1) L]

/-- The Coxeter element `δ_L = u s₁ s₂ ⋯ s_L` of `D_{L+1}`. -/

declarations.name: typeDDelta
declarations.signature_heuristic: def typeDDelta (u : G) (s : ℕ → G) (L : ℕ) : G

declarations.name: typeDDelta_eq_typeB
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeDDelta_eq_typeB (u : G) (s : ℕ → G) (M : ℕ) :
    typeDDelta u s (M + 1) = typeBDelta (u * s 1) (fun i => s (i + 1)) M

declarations.name: dW
declarations.signature_heuristic:
def dW (s : ℕ → G) : ℕ → ℕ → G
  | _, 0 => 1
  | t, len + 1 => s t * dW s (t - 1) len

declarations.name: dW_succ_right
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem dW_succ_right (s : ℕ → G) : ∀ t len, dW s t (len + 1) = dW s t len * s (t - len)
  | t, 0 => by simp [dW]
  | t, len + 1 => by
    rw [dW, dW_succ_right s (t - 1) len, dW, mul_assoc, show t - 1 - len = t - (len + 1) by omega]

declarations.name: commute_dW
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem commute_dW {s : ℕ → G} {x : G} :
    ∀ t len, (∀ i, t < i + len → i ≤ t → x * s i = s i * x) → x * dW s t len = dW s t len * x
  | _, 0, _ => by simp [dW]
  | t, len + 1, h => by
    rw [dW, ← mul_assoc, h t (by omega) le_rfl, mul_assoc,
      commute_dW (t - 1) len (fun i h1 h2 => h i (by omega) (by omega)), mul_assoc]

/-- `sᵢ δ_L = δ_L sᵢ₋₁` for `3 ≤ i ≤ L`. -/

declarations.name: typeD_shift
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeD_shift (h : TypeDRels u s N) {L i : ℕ} (hL : L ≤ N) (h3 : 3 ≤ i) (hi : i ≤ L) :
    s i * typeDDelta u s L = typeDDelta u s L * s (i - 1)

declarations.name: typeD_dW_shift
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeD_dW_shift (h : TypeDRels u s N) {L : ℕ} (hL : L ≤ N) :
    ∀ len t, t ≤ L → 3 + len ≤ t + 1 →
      dW s t len * typeDDelta u s L = typeDDelta u s L * dW s (t - 1) len
  | 0, t, _, _ => by simp [dW]
  | len + 1, t, ht, hlen => by
    rw [dW, mul_assoc, typeD_dW_shift h hL len (t - 1) (by omega) (by omega), ← mul_assoc,
      typeD_shift h hL (by omega) ht, mul_assoc, dW, show t - 1 - 1 = t - 1 - 1 from rfl]

/-- `δ_{L+1}^j = δ_L^j · (s_{L+1} s_L ⋯ s_{L+2-j})` for `1 ≤ j ≤ L`. -/

declarations.name: typeD_delta_succ_pow
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeD_delta_succ_pow (h : TypeDRels u s N) {L : ℕ} (hL : L + 1 ≤ N) :
    ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → j ≤ L →
      typeDDelta u s (L + 1) ^ j = typeDDelta u s L ^ j * dW s (L + 1) j
  | 0, h0, _ => by omega
  | 1, _, _ => by
    simp [typeDDelta, dW, upW_succ_right, mul_assoc, show 1 + L = L + 1 by ring]
  | j + 2, _, hj => by
    have ih

declarations.name: typeDQ
declarations.signature_heuristic: def typeDQ (u : G) (s : ℕ → G) (L : ℕ) : G

declarations.name: typeD_pow_succ
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeD_pow_succ (h : TypeDRels u s N) {L : ℕ} (hL1 : 1 ≤ L) (hL : L + 1 ≤ N) :
    typeDDelta u s (L + 1) ^ (L + 1) = typeDDelta u s L ^ L * typeDQ u s L

declarations.name: typeDQ_swap
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeDQ_swap (h : TypeDRels u s N) {L : ℕ} (hL1 : 1 ≤ L) (hL : L + 1 ≤ N) :
    u * typeDQ u s L = typeDQ u s L * s 1 ∧ s 1 * typeDQ u s L = typeDQ u s L * u

declarations.name: typeDZ
declarations.signature_heuristic: def typeDZ (u : G) (s : ℕ → G) (L : ℕ) : G

declarations.name: typeDZ_u
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeDZ_u (h : TypeDRels u s N) :
    ∀ L, 1 ≤ L → L ≤ N → u * typeDZ u s L = typeDZ u s L * (if Even L then s 1 else u)
  | 0, h0, _ => by omega
  | 1, _, _ => by simpa [typeDZ, typeDDelta, upW, mul_assoc] using h.u1
  | L + 2, _, hL => by
    have ih

declarations.name: typeDZ_comm
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeDZ_comm (h : TypeDRels u s N) {L : ℕ} (hL1 : 1 ≤ L) (hL : L ≤ N) :
    (∀ i, 2 ≤ i → i ≤ L → s i * typeDZ u s L = typeDZ u s L * s i) ∧
      u * s 1 * typeDZ u s L = typeDZ u s L * (u * s 1)

declarations.name: typeDZ_s1
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem typeDZ_s1 (h : TypeDRels u s N) {L : ℕ} (hL1 : 1 ≤ L) (hL : L ≤ N) :
    s 1 * typeDZ u s L = typeDZ u s L * (if Even L then u else s 1)

comments.text:
/-!
# Type `Dₙ` for every `n`: `Δ = c^{n-1}` twists the generators, so `c^h = Δ²` with `Δ²` central

In the Artin group of type `D_{L+1}` (generators `u, s₁, …, s_L`: the `sᵢ` form a chain, `u` is
attached to `s₂` and commutes with all other generators) let

  `δ = u s₁ s₂ ⋯ s_L`   (a Coxeter element; the Coxeter number of `D_n` is `h = 2(n - 1) = 2L`)

and `Δ = δ^L`.  The proof is pure braid-relation algebra, for every `L`:

* `typeD_typeBRels`: `τ = u s₁` and `s₂, …, s_L` satisfy the type-`B_L` relations, and `δ` is the
  type-`B` Coxeter element `τ s₂ ⋯ s_L`; so (`ArtinBn.lean`) `Δ` commutes with `s₂, …, s_L` and
  with `u s₁` (`typeDZ_comm`);
* `typeD_pow_succ`: `δ_{L+1}^{L+1} = δ_L^L · Q` with `Q = s_{L+1} ⋯ s₂ u s₁ s₂ ⋯ s_{L+1}`, and
  `typeDQ_swap`: `u Q = Q s₁`, `s₁ Q = Q u`;
* hence by induction on `L` (`typeDZ_u`, `typeDZ_s1`): **`u Δ = Δ u`, `s₁ Δ = Δ s₁` for `L` odd,
  and `u Δ = Δ s₁`, `s₁ Δ = Δ u` for `L` even**.

Applied to `coxDn n` (chain `0 — ⋯ — (n-2)`, node `n-1` attached to `n-3`; it agrees with
`coxD4`, `coxD5`, `coxD6`: `coxDn_four` etc.), with `c = σ_L ⋯ σ₀` (`dnCox`), `c' = σ₀ ⋯ σ_L`
(`dnCoxAsc`) and `Δ = c^L` (`dnDelta`), for every `n = L + 1 ≥ 2`:

* `σ_mul_dnDelta`: **`σₜ Δ = Δ σ_{ε t}`**, where `ε` (`dnFlip`) swaps the two short legs
  `n - 2 ↔ n - 1` when `n` is odd and is the identity when `n` is even;
* `dnDelta_central` (`n` even) and `dnDelta_sq_central` (all `n`): `Δ`, resp. **`Δ²`, is central**;
* `dnCox_pow_coxeterNumber`, `dnCoxAsc_pow_coxeterNumber`: **`c^{2(n-1)} = c'^{2(n-1)} = Δ²`**,
  with `dnCoxAsc_pow`: `c'^{n-1} = c^{n-1}`;
* `dnDelta_degree`, `dnDelta_pow_ne_one`: `Δ` has degree `n(n-1)` (the number of positive roots)
  and infinite order.

Every generator divides `Δ` (on both sides): `dnDelta_gen_dvd` in `ArtinDivisors.lean`.
That `Δ` is *not* central when `n ≥ 3` is odd: `dnDelta_not_central` in `ArtinDnTwist.lean`
(via the signed-permutation action of `W(D_n)`); `dnDelta_central_iff` there combines both.
-/

/-- The relations of the Artin group of type `D_{N+1}` on generators `u, s 1, …, s N`: the `sᵢ`
form a chain, `u` commutes with `s 1` and with `sᵢ` for `i ≥ 3`, and `u s₂ u = s₂ u s₂`. -/

/-- `(u s₁) s₂ (u s₁) s₂ = s₂ (u s₁) s₂ (u s₁)`: the folded pair `u s₁, s₂` satisfies the `B₂`
relation. -/
/-- The type-`B_N` relations satisfied by `τ = u s₁` and `s₂, …, s_N` (folding `D_{N+1}`). -/
/-- The Coxeter element `δ_L = u s₁ s₂ ⋯ s_L` of `D_{L+1}`. -/
/-- The descending word `dW s t len = s_t s_{t-1} ⋯ s_{t-len+1}` (`len` letters). -/
/-- `sᵢ δ_L = δ_L sᵢ₋₁` for `3 ≤ i ≤ L`. -/
/-- Pushing a descending word through `δ_L` lowers its indices by one. -/
-- `s_{L+1}` commutes with `P`
-- `s_{L+1}` commutes with the descending word `s_{L-1} ⋯ s_{L+1-j}`
/-- The loop element `Q_{L+1} = (s_{L+1} ⋯ s₂) · δ_{L+1} = s_{L+1} ⋯ s₂ u s₁ s₂ ⋯ s_{L+1}`. -/
/-- `u Q = Q s₁` and `s₁ Q = Q u`: conjugation by the loop element swaps `u` and `s₁`. -/

/-- The diagram flip of `D_{L+1}` induced by `Z_L`: it swaps `u` and `s₁` exactly when `L` is
even. -/
/-- `Z_L` commutes with `s₂, …, s_L` and with `u s₁` (from the folding to type `B_L`). -/
/-- The companion statement for `s₁`. -/
/-! ## The Artin group of type `D_n`, for every `n` -/

/-- The Coxeter matrix of type `D_n`: a chain `0 — 1 — ⋯ — (n-2)`, and `n - 1` attached to `n - 3`
(the convention of `coxD4`, `coxD5`, `coxD6`; for `n = 3` this is `A₃`, for `n = 2` two
commuting nodes). -/
/-- The Artin group of type `D_n` with `n = L + 1` generators. -/

/-- The generators in "type `D` order": `u = σ_L`, `sᵢ = σ_{L-i}` (so `s₁ = σ_{L-1}` and `u` are
the two short legs of the fork, both attached to `s₂ = σ_{L-2}`). -/
/-- The Coxeter element `c = σ_L σ_{L-1} ⋯ σ₀` of `D_{L+1}`. -/
/-- The Coxeter element `c' = σ₀ σ₁ ⋯ σ_L`. -/
/-- The Garside element `Δ = c^{n-1}` of `D_n` (`n = L + 1`). -/

/-- The diagram automorphism of `D_{L+1}` induced by `Δ`: the swap of the two short legs
`L - 1 ↔ L` when `L` is even (`n` odd), the identity when `L` is odd (`n` even). -/
/-- **`σₜ Δ = Δ σ_{ε t}`** for every generator of `D_n` (`n = L + 1 ≥ 2`), where `ε = dnFlip`. -/
-- `σ_a = s_{L-a}` with `L - a ≥ 2`
/-- **`Δ` is central when `n = L + 1` is even.** -/
/-- **`Δ²` is central**, for every `n = L + 1 ≥ 2`. -/
/-- **`c^h = Δ²`** with `h = 2(n - 1)` the Coxeter number of `D_n`, for `c = σ_L ⋯ σ₀`. -/
/-- **The other Coxeter element gives the same `Δ`**: `(σ₀σ₁⋯σ_L)^L = (σ_L⋯σ₁σ₀)^L`. -/

/-!
# Words for the `E₇` Garside element

Indices follow Mathlib's `CoxeterMatrix.E₇`, whose diagram is the restriction of the `E₈` diagram
(`QBX.Formal.Streams.e8Edge`) to `{0, …, 6}`; so the `E₈` exponents `e8Exp` are used with bound
`7`.

* `e7WordA = [0, 3, 5]` and `e7WordB = [1, 2, 4, 6]`: the two colour classes of the diagram.
* `e7DeltaWordAB = (AB)^9` (63 letters, the number of positive roots of `E₇`).
* `e7RestWord s`: a word `X` with `Δ = σₛ X = X σ_{ε s}` (certified in `ArtinE7.Cert*`), where
  `ε` is the identity.
* `e7ConjWord`, `e7StdWord`: a conjugating word and the standard Coxeter word `[0, 1, …, 6]`.

Generated by `QBX/scripts/gen_e67_artin_certificates.py`.
-/
/-- First colour class of the `E₇` diagram. -/
/-- Second colour class of the `E₇` diagram. -/
/-- A word `X` with `Δ = σₛ X = X σ_{ε s}` (a reduced word for `s · w₀`). -/
/-- A word `g` with `c_bip · g = g · c_std` (commutation moves only). -/
/-- The standard-order Coxeter word `[0, 1, …, 6]`. -/

comments.text: /-- The Artin group of type `E₇`. -/
/-- The bipartite Coxeter element `c = σ₀σ₃σ₅ · σ₁σ₂σ₄σ₆`. -/
/-- The Garside element `Δ = (ab)⁹`. -/
/-- Every generator left-divides `Δ`: `Δ = σₛ Xₛ`. -/
/-- Every generator right-divides `Δ` with the same cofactor: `Δ = Xₛ σₛ`. -/
/-- Every generator commutes with `Δ`. -/
/-- **`Δ` is central in the `E₇` Artin group.** -/
/-- `Δ²` is central. -/
/-- **`c¹⁸ = Δ²`** for the bipartite Coxeter element (`18` = Coxeter number of `E₇`). -/
/-- Cyclic rotation of a word preserves `p¹⁸ = Δ²`. -/
/-- The standard-order Coxeter element `σ₀σ₁⋯σ₆`. -/
/-- `Δ` has degree 63 (the number of positive roots of `E₇`). -/
/-- `Δ` has infinite order. -/

/-!
# The `E₈` Artin group: the Garside element `Δ` and `c³⁰ = Δ²`

`ArtinE8` is the Artin group (generalised braid group) of Mathlib's Coxeter matrix
`CoxeterMatrix.E₈`.  With the colour classes `A = {0, 3, 5, 7}`, `B = {1, 2, 4, 6}` of the diagram
and `a = σ₀σ₃σ₅σ₇`, `b = σ₁σ₂σ₄σ₆`, the bipartite Coxeter element is `c = ab` and

  `Δ = (ab)¹⁵`   (120 letters, the positive lift of the longest element of `W(E₈)`).

Main results:

* `e8Delta_eq_ba`: `(ab)¹⁵ = (ba)¹⁵`;
* `e8Delta_eq_gen_mul`, `e8Delta_eq_mul_gen`: every generator divides `Δ` on both sides with the
  same cofactor, `Δ = σₛ Xₛ = Xₛ σₛ`;
* `e8Delta_central`: **`Δ` is central** (for `E₈` the diagram automorphism induced by `Δ` is
  trivial);
* `e8CoxBip_pow_fifteen`, `e8CoxBip_pow_thirty`: `c¹⁵ = Δ` and **`c³⁰ = Δ²`** (`30` is the Coxeter
  number of `E₈`);
* `e8CoxStd_pow_thirty`: the same for the standard-order Coxeter element `σ₀σ₁⋯σ₇`;
* `pow_thirty_rotate`: cyclically rotating any word whose product `p` has `p³⁰ = Δ²` keeps
  this property;
* `e8Delta_degree`, `e8Delta_pow_ne_one`: `Δ` has degree 120, so `Δ` (and `c`) have infinite order.

The word identities are proved by braid-move certificates checked in the kernel
(`QBX.Formal.Streams.checkCode_sound`, files `ArtinE8/Cert*.lean`).  The classical statement for
every finite Coxeter type (Brieskorn–Saito, Deligne) is cited, not proved here; this file proves
the `E₈` case.
-/

/-! ## The Garside element -/

/-- **`Δ` is central in the `E₈` Artin group.** -/
/-- **`c³⁰ = Δ²`** for the bipartite Coxeter element (`30` = Coxeter number of `E₈`). -/
/-- `Δ²` is central. -/
/-! ## Other Coxeter elements -/

/-!
# Artin (braid-type) groups of a Coxeter matrix, and checkable braid-move certificates

For a Coxeter matrix `M` on an index type `B`, the Artin group `ArtinGroup M` has one generator
`σ i` per index and, for every pair `i, j`, the braid relation

  `σ i σ j σ i ⋯ = σ j σ i σ j ⋯`   (`M i j` letters on each side).

(For `M i j = 0`, i.e. `∞`, the relation is empty; for `i = j` it is trivial.)  For the type `A`
matrix this is the classical braid group; for `E₈` it is the Artin group used in
`QBX.Formal.Streams.ArtinE8`.

The second half is a small, kernel-checkable certificate format.  A *move* `(p, i, j)` replaces
the alternating block `i j i ⋯` (`m i j` letters) starting at position `p` of a word by
`j i j ⋯`.  `runCode` applies a list of moves; `checkCode_sound` says that if it succeeds then
the starting and final words have the same product in **every** group whose elements satisfy the
braid relations.  Only `m i j ∈ {2, 3}` is supported (enough for simply-laced types such as
`E₈`).  Words are lists of natural numbers so that the checker runs quickly in the kernel; the
moves are packed into one natural number (`runCode`).
-/
/-! ## Alternating words -/
/-- `altWord i j m = [i, j, i, …]` with `m` letters. -/
/-! ## The Artin group of a Coxeter matrix -/
/-- The braid relators `(σᵢσⱼσᵢ⋯)(σⱼσᵢσⱼ⋯)⁻¹`, one for each ordered pair of indices. -/
/-- The **Artin group** (generalised braid group) of the Coxeter matrix `M`. -/
/-- The standard generator `σᵢ`. -/
/-- The braid relation `σᵢσⱼσᵢ⋯ = σⱼσᵢσⱼ⋯` (`M i j` letters on each side). -/
/-- Two generators with `M i j = 2` commute. -/
/-- Two generators with `M i j = 3` satisfy `σᵢσⱼσᵢ = σⱼσᵢσⱼ`. -/
/-- The degree homomorphism to `ℤ` (written multiplicatively) sending every `σᵢ` to `1`. -/
/-- The degree of a positive word is its length. -/
/-! ## Braid-move certificates -/
/-- Boolean equality of lists of naturals (written out so that it reduces well in the kernel). -/

/-- Apply the move `(p, i, j)` when `i` and `j` commute (`m i j = 2`, `three = false`) or satisfy
the length-three braid relation (`m i j = 3`, `three = true`): replace `i j` (resp. `i j i`) at
position `p` by `j i` (resp. `j i j`).  The suffix after the block is shared, not copied. -/
/-- Apply the move `(p, i, j)` (indices `i, j < n`, and `m i j ∈ {2, 3}`). -/

significant digit first. -/
/-- The certificate check: running the `k` packed moves `c` from `u` ends exactly at `v`. -/
/-- Braid relations for `g 0, …, g (n-1)` with exponents `m`. -/

/-- **Soundness of the certificate check**: a successful check proves that the two words have
the same product in every group satisfying the braid relations. -/

/-!
# Words with natural-number letters in an Artin group on `Fin n`

Generic glue between the kernel certificate checker (`QBX.Formal.Streams.checkCode`, which works
on `List ℕ`) and the Artin group `ArtinGroup M` of a Coxeter matrix `M` on `Fin n`, used for the
types `E₆` and `E₇` (`QBX.Formal.Streams.ArtinE6`, `QBX.Formal.Streams.ArtinE7`).

* `natGen M i` is `σᵢ` for `i < n` (and `1` otherwise); `natLift M w` is the product of a word.
* `natLift_eq`: a successful certificate check proves equality of the two products, provided the
  exponent function `m` used by the checker agrees with `M` on `Fin n`.  (Mathlib numbers `E₆`,
  `E₇` and `E₈` compatibly: the `E₆` and `E₇` diagrams are the restrictions of the `E₈` diagram to
  `{0, …, 5}` and `{0, …, 6}`, so the `E₈` exponents `e8Exp` serve for all three.)
* `central_of_forall_σ`: an element commuting with every generator is central.
* Coxeter side: `length_toCoxeter_natLift`, `toCoxeter_natLift_reverse`, `reflRep_toCoxeter_natLift`.
-/
/-- The generator with natural-number index (`σᵢ` for `i < n`, `1` otherwise). -/
/-- The product of a word in the generators. -/
/-- An element commuting with every generator is central. -/
/-- Cyclic rotation of a word preserves `p ^ h = z` when `z` is central. -/
/-! ## The Coxeter side -/
/-- A word of length `k` maps to an element of Coxeter length at most `k`. -/
/-- The image of a reversed word is the inverse of the image (each `sᵢ` is an involution). -/
/-- The matrix of the generator with natural-number index (`1` out of range). -/
