/-!
# The toric code has distance `m`

Target L-3 of the WS9 integration register (item T-03). On the `m × m` torus, every Pauli
operator that commutes with all stars and plaquettes but is not (up to phase) a product of
stabilizers acts non-trivially on at least `m` qubits (`toric_distance`). The bound is attained:
`Z_A` has weight exactly `m` (`pauliWeight_ZA`), so the code distance is exactly `m`
(`toric_distance_eq`).

Proof: such an operator `Q` pairs non-trivially with one of `Z_A, Z_B, X_A, X_B` (otherwise its
logical coordinates all vanish and `Q` lies in the stabilizer group,
`mem_stabSpan_of_symp_logicals`). Say it anticommutes with `X_A`. Every column operator
`colX s` differs from `X_A` by stabilizers (`ToricTranslation.lean`), so `Q` anticommutes with
each of the `m` disjoint columns and must have support on each of them.
-/
/-- The weight of a Pauli operator: the number of qubits on which it acts non-trivially. -/
/-- If `m` distinct edges `f s` all lie in the support of `Q`, the weight of `Q` is at least `m`. -/

/-- Pairing with an operator that commutes with all stabilizers only depends on the class of the
first argument modulo stabilizers. -/

/-- An operator that commutes with all stabilizers and with all four logical operators is a
product of stabilizers. -/
/-- Pairing of `colX s` with `Q`: the parity of `Q.z` on the column `h(s, ·)`. -/

/-- **L-3 (code distance).** Every Pauli operator on the `m × m` torus that commutes with all
stars and plaquettes but is not, up to phase, a product of stabilizers acts non-trivially on at
least `m` qubits. -/
-- `Q` anticommutes with every column `colZ s`: support on `v(s, ·)` for every `s`
/-- `Z_A` acts on exactly the `m` edges `h(·, 0)`. -/
/-- `Z_A` is a non-trivial logical operator. -/

/-- **The toric code distance is exactly `m`**: the minimum weight of a non-trivial logical
operator is `m`. -/

/-!
# Kitaev's toric code on the `m × m` torus: stabilizer rank and logical sectors (T3)

Formal target **T3** of `QBX/foundation/ws6_certificates/SPEC.md` (property P4.4 of
`QBX/foundation/ws4_toric/PROPERTIES.md`), in the conventions of `QBX/Formal/ToricCode.lean`
(edges `Bool × ZMod m × ZMod m`, Pauli operators as pairs of `ZMod 2`-vectors, `star`,
`plaquette`, `ZA ZB XA XB`).  Every statement holds for every `m ≥ 1` (`[NeZero m]`); the Python
code `toric_code.py` uses `m ≥ 2`.

* `finrank_star_span` (**T3a**): the `m²` star `X`-supports span a space of dimension `m² − 1`;
  the only relation is that all stars sum to zero (`ker_starMap`: the kernel of the star
  coboundary is the constants, because the torus graph is connected).
* `finrank_plaquette_span` (**T3b**): the same for the plaquette `Z`-supports (`ker_plaqMap`).
* `toric_stabilizer_rank` (**T3**): the stabilizer group `stabSpan m`, a `Submodule (ZMod 2)` of
  the symplectic space `(Edge m → ZMod 2) × (Edge m → ZMod 2)`, has `finrank = 2m² − 2`
  (`ToricCode.stabilizer_rank()`); hence `toric_logical_qubits` (`2m² − rank = 2`) and
  `toric_degeneracy` (`2 ^ (2m² − rank) = 4`, `ToricCode.degeneracy()`).
* `toric_logicals_independent`, `toric_logicals_linearIndependent` (**T3c**): `Z_A, Z_B, X_A, X_B`
  are linearly independent modulo the stabilizer group (`ToricCode.logicals_independent()`).
* `toric_centralizer_eq`, `commutes_all_iff_mem_stab_sup_logical`: the operators commuting with
  every stabilizer are exactly the products of stabilizers and the four logicals; the
  centralizer has dimension `2m² + 2` (`finrank_centralizer`).
-/
/-- Vertices (and, dually, plaquettes) of the `m × m` torus. -/
/-- Star coboundary: `f ↦ ∑_v f v • X-support(A_v)`. -/
/-- Plaquette coboundary: `f ↦ ∑_p f p • Z-support(B_p)`. -/
/-- A function on the torus invariant under both unit translations is constant. -/
/-- The only relation among the stars: their kernel is the constants. -/
/-- The only relation among the plaquettes: their kernel is the constants. -/
/-- **T3a.** The `m²` star `X`-supports span a space of dimension `m² − 1`. -/
/-- **T3b.** The `m²` plaquette `Z`-supports span a space of dimension `m² − 1`. -/
/-- The symplectic vector `(x | z)` of a Pauli operator. -/

/-- The stabilizer group, as the `ZMod 2`-span of the symplectic vectors of the `2m²`
generators in the symplectic space `(Edge m → ZMod 2) × (Edge m → ZMod 2)`. -/
/-- A product of submodules is linearly equivalent to the product of the two modules. -/

/-- **T3 (stabilizer rank).** The stabilizer group of the toric code on the `m × m` torus has
`ZMod 2`-rank `2m² − 2`. -/
/-- There are `2m²` physical qubits. -/
/-- **T3 (logical qubits).** `n − rank = 2` logical qubits. -/

/-- **T3 (degeneracy).** The code space has dimension `2^(n − rank) = 4`
(`ToricCode.degeneracy()`). -/
/-- The symplectic form on `(x | z)` vectors; `symp P Q = sympVec P.toVec Q.toVec`. -/

/-- The symplectic form vanishes between the stabilizer span and any operator that commutes
with every stabilizer generator. -/

/-- **T3c (independence).** No nontrivial combination of the four logical operators
`Z_A, Z_B, X_A, X_B` lies in the stabilizer group (`ToricCode.logicals_independent()`). -/

/-- **T3c (quotient form).** The images of `Z_A, Z_B, X_A, X_B` in the quotient of the
symplectic space by the stabilizer group are linearly independent. -/
/-- The symplectic form as a bilinear form on `(Edge m → ZMod 2) × (Edge m → ZMod 2)`. -/
/-- The four logical operators as symplectic vectors. -/
/-- The span of the four logical operators. -/

/-- An operator commutes with every stabilizer generator iff its symplectic vector is
orthogonal to the stabilizer span. -/

/-- The centralizer of the stabilizer group (all operators commuting with every stabilizer)
has dimension `2m² + 2`. -/

/-- **T3 (logical sectors).** The centralizer of the stabilizer group is exactly the span of
the stabilizers and the four logical operators. -/

/-- **T3 (logical operators, Pauli form).** A Pauli operator commutes with every star and every
plaquette iff it is, up to phase, a product of stabilizers and of `Z_A, Z_B, X_A, X_B`. -/

/-!
# WS9 integration: torus translations act trivially on the toric-code logical sectors

Couples work stream 5 (torus translations `shift_gate`, the only torus gates of the gate set)
with work stream 4 (the toric code, `QBX/Formal/ToricCode.lean`, `QBX/Formal/ToricRank.lean`).
Register item X-11.

Identify the toric-code lattice with a two-cycle torus factor `ZMod m × ZMod m` and translate
every edge by `(s, t)` (`transEdge`).  The induced map on symplectic Pauli vectors is `transL s t`.

* `transL_mem_stabSpan`: translations preserve the stabilizer group (stars go to stars,
  plaquettes to plaquettes).
* `transL_logical_sub_mem`: each of `Z_A, Z_B, X_A, X_B` is moved to an operator that differs from
  it by a product of stabilizers (the difference of two parallel non-contractible loops bounds a
  strip of plaquettes, or of stars).
* `transL_sub_mem_of_commutes`: hence for **every** Pauli operator `Q` that commutes with all
  stabilizers (every logical operator, `commutes_all_iff_mem_stab_sup_logical`), the translate of
  `Q` equals `Q` up to stabilizers.  Translations act as the identity on the four logical sectors.

Design consequence: torus-translation gates can neither corrupt nor manipulate the protected
memory; a logical gate set for the toric memory must come from elsewhere (braiding of defects or
anyons, lattice surgery, …).
-/
/-- Translation of edges of the `m × m` torus by `(s, t)`. -/
/-- The translation acting on `ZMod 2`-vectors on edges: `f ↦ f ∘ (transEdge s t)⁻¹`. -/
/-- The translation acting on symplectic Pauli vectors `(x | z)`. -/
/-- **Translations preserve the stabilizer group.** -/
/-! ### Telescoping -/
/-- If consecutive differences of `f : ZMod m → W` lie in `S`, so do all differences. -/
/-! ### The four logical classes are translation invariant -/
/-- `Z` on the horizontal row `h(·, t)`. -/
/-- `Z` on the vertical column `v(s, ·)`. -/
/-- `X` on the column `h(s, ·)`. -/
/-- `X` on the row `v(·, t)`. -/
/-- **Each logical operator is translation invariant up to stabilizers.** -/
/-- Translations fix every vector of `stabSpan ⊔ logicalSpan` up to stabilizers. -/

/-- **Torus translations act trivially on the logical sectors.** For every Pauli operator `Q`
commuting with all stars and plaquettes, translating `Q` by any `(s, t)` changes it only by a
product of stabilizers. -/

comments.text:
/-!
# The braid group of the torus `B_n(T²)` and its shadow (Phase D workstream D3; registry H-085)

`TorusBraidGroup n` is the group presented by generators `σ_1, …, σ_{n-1}` (here `tsigma i`,
`i : Fin (n - 1)`, 0-indexed as in `Braid.lean`) and `a`, `b` (`ta`, `tb`: the first strand travels
once around the first, resp. second, cycle of the torus), subject to the relations of the genus-1
case of Bellingeri, *On presentations of surface braid groups*, J. Algebra 274 (2004), Theorem 1.2
(closed orientable surfaces; 1-indexed there):

* braid relations and far commutation of the `σ_i`;
* (R1) `a σ_i = σ_i a`, `b σ_i = σ_i b` for `i ≠ 1`;
* (R2) `σ_1⁻¹ a σ_1⁻¹ a = a σ_1⁻¹ a σ_1⁻¹`, and the same for `b`;
* (R4) `σ_1⁻¹ a σ_1⁻¹ b = b σ_1⁻¹ a σ_1`;
* (TR) `a b⁻¹ a⁻¹ b = σ_1 σ_2 ⋯ σ_{n-1}² ⋯ σ_2 σ_1`.

(R3) of Bellingeri relates different handles and is empty for genus 1. These relations were checked
line by line against the paper (arXiv:math/0110129v2, in `QBX/docs/reference/`), and
`TorusBraidBellingeri.lean` proves that this group is isomorphic to the group given by Theorem 1.2,
written out for every genus, at `g = 1` (`torusBraidEquivBellingeri`). That this presentation is
`π₁` of the configuration space is taken from the literature, not proved here.

Main results:

* `shadow`: the **shadow homomorphism** `B_n(T²) →* S_n ⋉ (ℤ²)ⁿ` (`Shadow n`), sending `σ_i` to
  the transposition `(i i+1)` and `a`, `b` to one turn of strand `0` around each cycle; it is well
  defined because every relator maps to `1` (`shadow_rels`).
* `ofPlanar`, `shadow_ofPlanar`: planar braids map into `B_n(T²)`, and there the shadow is the
  existing permutation shadow `permHom` with zero winding.
* `torusGate`, `torusGate_mul`, `torusGate_one`, `torusGate_ofPlanar`: the action on
  `Q_n □ T^k_M` (bits permuted by the strand permutation, torus translated by the total winding),
  extending `braidGate`.
* `heisRep`, `tsigma_sq_ne_one`, `ta_tb_ne`, `shadow_not_injective`: a Heisenberg representation
  shows what the shadow forgets — for `n ≥ 2`, `σ_i² ≠ 1` and `a b ≠ b a`, although both pairs
  have the same shadow.
-/
/-! ## The presentation -/

/-- Generators of `B_n(T²)`: the planar crossings `σ_i` and the two torus loops `a`, `b`
of the first strand. -/
/-- `σ_i` in the free group. -/
/-- `a` in the free group. -/
/-- `b` in the free group. -/
/-- The word `σ_1 σ_2 ⋯ σ_{n-1}`, 1-indexed (`σ_0 ⋯ σ_{n-2}` here). -/
/-- The word `σ_{n-1} ⋯ σ_2 σ_1` (1-indexed). -/
/-- The right-hand side of the torus relation, `σ_1 σ_2 ⋯ σ_{n-1}² ⋯ σ_2 σ_1` (1-indexed). -/
/-- The relators of `B_n(T²)` (genus `1` case of Bellingeri 2004, Theorem 1.2). -/
/-- The braid group of the torus. -/
/-! ## The shadow group `S_n ⋉ (ℤ²)ⁿ` -/
/-- Net winding of each strand around the two cycles of the torus. -/
/-- `S_n` acts on windings by moving the winding of strand `j` to strand `π j`. -/
/-- The shadow group `S_n ⋉ (ℤ²)ⁿ`. -/
/-- In a group, `l.prod * l.reverse.prod = 1` when every factor is an involution. -/
/-- Under any assignment sending every `σ_i` to an involution, the loop word maps to `1`. -/

/-- The mixed relation (R2) holds for `s`, `x` as soon as `s` is an involution and `s x s`
commutes with `x`. -/

/-- The mixed relation (R4) holds for `s`, `x`, `y` as soon as `s` is an involution and
`s x s` commutes with `y`. -/
/-- A winding on the first strand only. -/

/-- The shadow of a generator: `σ_i ↦ (i i+1)`, `a ↦` one turn of strand `0` around the first
cycle, `b ↦` one turn around the second cycle. -/
/-- An `inr` that fixes strand `0` commutes with windings of strand `0`. -/

/-- **The shadow homomorphism** `B_n(T²) →* S_n ⋉ (ℤ²)ⁿ`: every relator of the presentation maps
to `1`, so `σ_i ↦ (i i+1)`, `a ↦ (1, (1,0)·e₀)`, `b ↦ (1, (0,1)·e₀)` is well defined. -/
/-! ## Generators and relations in `B_n(T²)` -/
/-- `a` in `B_n(T²)`: the first strand travels once around the first cycle of the torus. -/
/-- `b` in `B_n(T²)`: the first strand travels once around the second cycle of the torus. -/
/-- The torus relation: `[a, b⁻¹] = σ_1 ⋯ σ_{n-1}² ⋯ σ_1`. -/
/-- The planar braid group maps to the torus braid group (strands confined to a disc). -/
/-- On planar braids the shadow is the permutation shadow `permHom` with zero winding. -/
/-! ## Total winding and the gate action on `Q_n □ T^k` -/
/-- The total winding of all strands, a homomorphism `S_n ⋉ (ℤ²)ⁿ →* ℤ²`. -/

/-- The gate of a torus braid on `Q_n □ T^k_M`: permute bits by the strand permutation and
translate the torus by the total winding, read through `t : ℤ² →+ ∏ ZMod (M j)` (for example
`a ↦` one step on cycle `0`, `b ↦` one step on cycle `1`). -/
/-- `β ↦ torusGate t β` is an action of `B_n(T²)` on addresses. -/
/-- On planar braids the torus gate is the existing braid gate. -/

/-! ## A finer invariant: a Heisenberg representation

`Heis N` is `ℤ × ℤ × ZMod N` with `(x, y, z) (x', y', z') = (x + x', y + y', z + z' + 2 x y')`.
Sending every `σ_i` to the central element `S = (0, 0, 1)`, `a` to `X = (1, 0, 0)` and `b` to
`Y = (0, 1, 0)` respects every relation when `N = 2n`. It detects what the shadow forgets:
`σ_i² ↦ (0, 0, 2) ≠ 1` and `[a, b] ↦ (0, 0, 2) ≠ 1` for `n ≥ 2`. -/
/-- The Heisenberg-type group `ℤ × ℤ × ZMod N` with cocycle `2 x y'`. -/
/-- First coordinate. -/
/-- Second coordinate. -/
/-- Central coordinate. -/
/-- The central element `(0, 0, 1)`. -/
/-- The Heisenberg representation on generators. -/
/-- The Heisenberg representation `B_n(T²) →* Heis (2n)`. -/

/-- **The shadow forgets braiding.** For `n ≥ 2`, `σ_i² ≠ 1` in `B_n(T²)`, although its shadow
is trivial. -/

/-- **The shadow forgets the torus relation.** For `n ≥ 2`, `a` and `b` do not commute in
`B_n(T²)`, although their shadows do. -/
/-- The shadow is not injective once there are two strands. -/

/-!
# Lower central series of the torus braid group (registry H-120, SPEC TB6)

Source: P. Bellingeri, S. Gervais, J. Guaschi, *Lower central series for surface braid groups*,
J. Algebra 319 (2008) 1409–1427 (HAL hal-00015415v2, in `QBX/docs/reference/`), Theorem 1 at
genus `g = 1`.  Their `Γ_i` is Mathlib's `lowerCentralSeries G (i - 1)`: `Γ_1 = G` is index `0`,
`Γ_2 = [G, G]` is index `1`, `Γ_3` is index `2`, and so on.

For `B_n(T²)` (`TorusBraidGroup n`, the genus-1 Bellingeri presentation of `TorusBraid.lean`):

* `abelianizationEquiv` (Theorem 1(a), `n ≥ 2`): `B_n(T²)/Γ_2 ≅ ℤ² ⊕ ℤ/2`, via the total
  winding around each cycle and the parity of the number of crossings (the sign of the strand
  permutation).  In particular the planar writhe does **not** extend to torus braids: only its
  parity survives.
* `lowerCentralSeries_eq_ker_heisRep` (`n ≥ 3`): for every `k ≥ 2` the term `Γ_{k+1}` is the
  kernel of the Heisenberg representation `heisRep : B_n(T²) →* Heis (2n)` of `TorusBraid.lean`.
  Hence
  * `quotientLowerCentralSeriesTwoEquiv`: `B_n(T²)/Γ_3 ≅ Heis (2n)` (the presentation (10) of the
    paper at `g = 1`);
  * `commutatorQuotientEquiv` (Theorem 1(b)): `Γ_2/Γ_3 ≅ ℤ/n`, sending the class of `[a, b]`
    (equal to the class of `σ_1²`) to `1`;
  * `lowerCentralSeries_three_eq_two` (Theorem 1(c), first part): `Γ_3 = Γ_4`, and in fact
    `Γ_3 = Γ_k` for every `k ≥ 3` (`lowerCentralSeries_eq_two`);
  * `not_residuallyNilpotent` (Theorem 1(d)): `⋂ Γ_k ≠ 1`; the element `σ_1 σ_2⁻¹` lies in every
    `Γ_k` but is not `1`.
* `exists_factor_heisRep` (`n ≥ 3`): **every homomorphism from `B_n(T²)` to a nilpotent group
  factors through `heisRep`.**  So `heisRep` is the finest nilpotent invariant of torus braids;
  anything it cannot see (such as `σ_1 σ_2⁻¹`, `nilpotent_invariant_tsigma_mul_inv`) is invisible
  to every nilpotent quotient.
* `not_exists_writhe` (`n ≥ 2`): no homomorphism `B_n(T²) →* ℤ` sends `σ_1` to `1`;
  `commGroup_tsigma_sq`: in every abelian quotient `σ_1² = 1`.
* `mk_tsigma_sq_eq_mk_commAB`: `σ_1²` and `[a, b]` have the same class in `Γ_2/Γ_3`.

For comparison, the last section treats the planar braid group `B_n` (the paper's Proposition 4):
`braid_lowerCentralSeries_eq_ker_writhe` (`Γ_{k+1}(B_n)` is the kernel of the writhe for `k ≥ 1`,
`n ≥ 2`), `braidAbelianizationEquiv` (`B_n/Γ_2 ≅ ℤ`), `braid_exists_factor_writhe` (the writhe is
the universal nilpotent invariant of planar braids) and `braid_not_residuallyNilpotent` (`n ≥ 3`).

The proof follows the paper: in any quotient `B_n(T²)/Γ_k` the braid relation identifies all the
`σ_i` (`mul_inv_mem_lowerCentralSeries_of_braid`, the argument of the paper's Proposition 4), the
relations (R1) make `σ` central, and (R4) and (TR) give `[a, b] = σ²`, `σ^{2n} = 1`.  These are
the relations of `Heis (2n)`, so `heisRep` factors through every `B_n(T²)/Γ_k` (`Heis.lift`).
The paper's statements for `n ≥ 5` (perfectness of `Γ_3`, which uses Gorin–Lin) and its
Theorem 3 on `B_2(T²)` are not formalized here.
-/
/-! ## A general fact: braid-related elements agree modulo every `Γ_k` -/

/-- If `x y x = y x y` in a group `G`, then `x y⁻¹` lies in every term of the lower central series
(the argument of Bellingeri–Gervais–Guaschi, Proposition 4): modulo `Γ_{k+1}`, `t = x y⁻¹ ∈ Γ_k`
is central, and the braid relation for `x = t y` forces `t = 1`. -/
/-- Conjugating `B^y` by `A` when `A B A⁻¹ = c B` with `c` central. -/
/-- If `A B = c B A` with `c` central, then `A^x B^y = B^y A^x c^{x y}`. -/
/-! ## The Heisenberg group is nilpotent of class two, and its universal property -/
/-- The subgroup `{(0, 0, 2m)}` of `Heis N`: it contains every commutator. -/
/-- `Heis N` is nilpotent of class at most two: `Γ_3 = 1`. -/
/-- `z ↦ s^z` for `s^N = 1`, as an additive map `ZMod N →+ Additive Q`. -/

/-- The universal property of `Heis N`: in a group `Q`, a central `s` with `s^N = 1` and elements
`A`, `B` with `A B = s² B A` determine a homomorphism `Heis N →* Q`, `(x, y, z) ↦ s^z B^y A^x`. -/
/-- Every element of `Heis N` is `S^z Y^y X^x`. -/
/-! ## Relations (R1) and (R4) in `B_n(T²)` -/
/-- Relation (R4): `σ_1⁻¹ a σ_1⁻¹ b = b σ_1⁻¹ a σ_1`. -/
/-! ## Every quotient `B_n(T²)/Γ_k` receives `Heis (2n)` -/
/-- `σ_i σ_{i+1}⁻¹` lies in every term of the lower central series. -/
/-- Modulo `Γ_k`, all the `σ_i` agree. -/
/-- The common class of the `σ_i` in `B_n(T²)/Γ_k`. -/
/-- The class of `a`. -/
/-- The class of `b`. -/
/-- (R4) modulo a central `σ`: `σ⁻¹ a σ⁻¹ b = b σ⁻¹ a σ` becomes `a b = σ² b a`. -/
/-- The loop word `σ_1 ⋯ σ_{n-1}² ⋯ σ_1` is `σ^{2(n-1)}` modulo `Γ_k`. -/
/-- The homomorphism `Heis (2n) →* B_n(T²)/Γ_k`. -/
/-- The kernel of the Heisenberg representation lies in every `Γ_k`. -/
/-! ## The lower central series of `B_n(T²)` -/
/-- `Heis (2n)` is nilpotent of class two, so `Γ_3` lies in the kernel of `heisRep`. -/

/-- **The lower central series of `B_n(T²)` stops at `Γ_3`, which is the kernel of `heisRep`**
(`n ≥ 3`; Mathlib index `k ≥ 2` is the paper's `Γ_{k+1}`). -/
/-- **Bellingeri–Gervais–Guaschi, Theorem 1(c) at genus 1:** `Γ_3(B_n(T²)) = Γ_4(B_n(T²))`. -/
/-- The intersection of the lower central series is the kernel of `heisRep`. -/
/-- `σ_1 σ_2⁻¹ ≠ 1`: its strand permutation is a 3-cycle. -/
/-- `σ_1 σ_2⁻¹` lies in every term of the lower central series. -/

/-- **Bellingeri–Gervais–Guaschi, Theorem 1(d) at genus 1:** `B_n(T²)` is not residually
nilpotent for `n ≥ 3`: the intersection of its lower central series is not trivial. -/
/-- `heisRep` is surjective for `n ≥ 2`. -/

/-- **`B_n(T²)/Γ_3 ≅ Heis (2n)`** for `n ≥ 3` (the presentation (10) of Bellingeri–Gervais–Guaschi
at genus 1: `a`, `b`, `σ` with `σ` central, `[a, b] = σ²`, `σ^{2n} = 1`). -/

/-- **`heisRep` is the universal nilpotent invariant of torus braids** (`n ≥ 3`): every
homomorphism from `B_n(T²)` to a nilpotent group factors through `heisRep`. -/
/-- Consequently no nilpotent invariant of torus braids sees `σ_1 σ_2⁻¹`. -/
/-- The commutator `[a, b] = a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹` as an element of `Γ_2`. -/

/-- **Bellingeri–Gervais–Guaschi, Theorem 1(b) at genus 1:** `Γ_2(B_n(T²))/Γ_3(B_n(T²)) ≅ ℤ/n`
for `n ≥ 3`, generated by the class of `[a, b]` (which equals the class of `σ_i²`). -/
/-! ## The abelianization `B_n(T²)/Γ_2 ≅ ℤ² ⊕ ℤ/2` -/
/-- The abelian invariant on generators: `a ↦ (1, 0, 0)`, `b ↦ (0, 1, 0)`, `σ_i ↦ (0, 0, 1)`. -/

/-- **The abelian invariant of torus braids**: total winding around the two cycles and the parity
of the number of crossings. -/
/-- In a commutative quotient, braid-related elements are equal. -/
/-- The inverse map `ℤ² ⊕ ℤ/2 → B_n(T²)/Γ_2`, `(x, y, s) ↦ a^x b^y σ_1^s`. -/

/-- **Bellingeri–Gervais–Guaschi, Theorem 1(a) at genus 1:** for `n ≥ 2`,
`B_n(T²)/Γ_2 ≅ ℤ² ⊕ ℤ/2`, via the total winding around each cycle and the crossing parity. -/
/-- In every abelian quotient of `B_n(T²)` the crossing `σ_1` has order dividing `2`. -/

/-- **The planar writhe does not extend to the torus**: for `n ≥ 2` there is no homomorphism
`B_n(T²) →* ℤ` sending `σ_1` to `1` (only the writhe modulo `2` survives, as `abHom`). -/

/-- For `n ≥ 3`, the classes of `σ_1²` and `[a, b]` agree in `Γ_2/Γ_3`, so `σ_1²` also generates
`Γ_2/Γ_3 ≅ ℤ/n` (as stated in Bellingeri–Gervais–Guaschi). -/

/-! ## The planar braid group (Bellingeri–Gervais–Guaschi, Proposition 4)

For comparison with the torus: in `B_n` every term `Γ_{k+1}`, `k ≥ 1`, of the lower central series
is the kernel of the writhe, so the writhe is the finest nilpotent invariant of planar braids and
`B_n/Γ_2 ≅ ℤ`. -/
/-- Modulo any `Γ_k`, all the `σ_i` of `B_n` agree. -/
/-- The commutator subgroup of `B_n` lies in the kernel of the writhe. -/
/-- For `n ≥ 2`, the kernel of the writhe lies in every term of the lower central series. -/

/-- **The lower central series of the planar braid group** (`n ≥ 2`): `Γ_{k+1}(B_n)` is the
kernel of the writhe for every `k ≥ 1`; in particular `Γ_2(B_n) = Γ_3(B_n)`
(Bellingeri–Gervais–Guaschi, Proposition 4). -/
/-- `B_n/Γ_2 ≅ ℤ` via the writhe, for `n ≥ 2`. -/

/-- **The writhe is the universal nilpotent invariant of planar braids** (`n ≥ 2`): every
homomorphism from `B_n` to a nilpotent group factors through the writhe. -/
/-- For `n ≥ 3`, `B_n` is not residually nilpotent: `σ_1 σ_2⁻¹ ≠ 1` lies in every `Γ_k`. -/

/-!
# The two-strand torus braid group `B_2(T²)` (registry H-121, SPEC TB8)

Source: P. Bellingeri, E. Godelle, *Questions on surface braid groups* (arXiv:math/0503658,
in `QBX/docs/reference/`), §4, and Bellingeri–Gervais–Guaschi, *Lower central series for surface
braid groups* (2008), Theorem 3.

In `B_2(T²)` (`TorusBraidGroup 2`, generators `σ = σ_1`, `a`, `b`) put
`t = σ⁻¹`, `P = σ⁻¹ a`, `Q = σ⁻¹ b`, `C = t P Q`. Then the D3 relations become those of
Bellingeri–Godelle, Corollary 4.1 (`δ_1 = P`, `δ_2 = Q`, their `σ_1` is our `t`):
`P² t = t P²`, `Q² t = t Q²`, `t P Q t = Q P`, `Q t P = P t⁻¹ Q`.  From these:

* `P_sq_central`, `Q_sq_central`, `C_sq`: `P²`, `Q²` are central and `C² = P² Q²`
  (their Corollary 4.3: `a = Q`, `b = P`, `c = C`).
* `toW : B_2(T²) →* W`, where `W = ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/2` (`W = ⟨u, v, w ∣ u², v², w²⟩`), sends
  `P ↦ v`, `Q ↦ u`, `C ↦ w`; it is surjective (`toW_surjective`) and its kernel lies in the
  subgroup generated by the central elements `P²`, `Q²` (`ker_toW_le`).
* `windHom : B_2(T²) →* ℤ²`, the total winding.
* **`toW_prod_windHom_injective`**: `(toW, windHom) : B_2(T²) →* W × ℤ²` is injective. Hence
  two 2-strand torus braids are equal iff they have the same image in `ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/2` and the
  same total winding (`eq_iff_toW_windHom`; Bellingeri–Godelle, Corollary 4.7).
* **`lowerCentralSeriesEquivW`** (Bellingeri–Gervais–Guaschi, Theorem 3(b)(i)): for every `i ≥ 2`
  (Mathlib index `k ≥ 1`), `Γ_i(B_2(T²)) ≅ Γ_i(ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/2)`, via `toW`.
-/
/-- The crossing `σ_1`. -/
/-! ## The relations of `B_2(T²)` -/
/-! ## Bellingeri–Godelle generators -/
/-- `C = t P Q` (their `c`). -/
/-! ## Centrality of `P²` and `Q²` -/
/-- An element commuting with `σ`, `a`, `b` is central in `B_2(T²)`. -/
/-- From commuting with `t`, `P`, `Q`. -/
/-- `P²` is central (Bellingeri–Godelle, Corollary 4.3). -/
/-- `Q²` is central (Bellingeri–Godelle, Corollary 4.3). -/
/-- `C² = P² Q²` (Bellingeri–Godelle, Corollary 4.3). -/
/-! ## The free product `W = ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/2` -/
/-- The relators `x_i²` of `W`. -/
/-- `W = ⟨u, v, w ∣ u², v², w²⟩`, the free product of three copies of `ℤ/2`. -/
/-- The generator `u` of `W` (image of `Q`). -/
/-- The generator `v` of `W` (image of `P`). -/
/-- The generator `w` of `W` (image of `C`). -/
/-- Images of `σ`, `a`, `b` in `W`: `σ = t⁻¹ ↦ v u w`, `a = σ P ↦ v u w v`, `b = σ Q ↦ v u w u`. -/

/-- The surjection `B_2(T²) → ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/2`, `P ↦ v`, `Q ↦ u`, `C ↦ w`
(Bellingeri–Godelle, §4). -/
/-! ## The kernel of `toW` -/
/-- `B_2(T²) / ⟨P², Q²⟩` receives `W`. -/

/-- The kernel of `toW` lies in the central subgroup generated by `P²` and `Q²`
(Bellingeri–Godelle, Proposition 4.4: `B_2(T²) / ⟨P², Q²⟩ ≅ ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/2`). -/
/-! ## Total winding -/
/-- The total winding `B_2(T²) → ℤ²`. -/
/-! ## Main results -/

/-- **A 2-strand torus braid is determined by its image in `ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/2` and its total
winding** (Bellingeri–Godelle, Corollary 4.7). -/
/-- `toW` is injective on the commutator subgroup. -/
/-- The image of the lower central series under a surjective homomorphism. -/

/-- **Bellingeri–Gervais–Guaschi, Theorem 3(b)(i):** for `k ≥ 1` (i.e. `Γ_i`, `i ≥ 2`, in their
indexing) the lower central series of `B_2(T²)` is isomorphic, via `toW`, to that of
`ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/2`. -/

/-!
# WS9 integration: a `ℤ/2` ledger on the torus — flatness versus logical sectors

Couples the consensus layer (work streams 2/3: a ledger is consistent iff its connection is flat,
iff it is pure gauge, `Gauge.Connection.isFlat_iff_isPureGauge`) with the toric code (work
stream 4).  Register item X-12.

Take the structure group `ℤ/2` and the `m × m` torus graph whose edges are the toric-code
qubits.  A `ℤ/2` connection is a vector `c : Edge m → ZMod 2` (transport `c e`, its own inverse).
* its holonomy around the face `(i, j)` is `faceHol c i j` (the sum over the four edges of the
  plaquette `B_{(i,j)}`);
* its holonomies around the two non-contractible loops `h(·, 0)` and `v(0, ·)` are `holA c`,
  `holB c` (the supports of `Z_A`, `Z_B`);
* it is pure gauge iff `c = starMap p` for vertex potentials `p` (the transport of `u — v` is
  `p u + p v`).

Results:
* `isPureGauge_iff`: **pure gauge ⟺ flat on every face and trivial around both
  non-contractible loops.**  Face flatness alone is not enough on the torus.
* `faceFlat_iff_commutes`: the face-flat connections are exactly the `X`-type Pauli operators
  that commute with every stabilizer, i.e. the `X`-type logical operators up to stabilizers.
* `exists_faceFlat_hol`: every value of `(holA, holB) ∈ (ℤ/2)²` is attained by a face-flat
  connection (`X_A`, `X_B` and their sum).

Design consequence: a consensus check that inspects only local loops (faces) misses exactly
two bits of global inconsistency, and those two bits are precisely what the toric memory uses
to store its `X`-logical information.  "Fork" for the ledger and "data" for the memory are the

  {H : ∀ {c c' : C} {d d' : D}, (c ⟶ c') → (d ⟶ d') → (F c d ⟶ F c' d')}

/-!
# Phase 1: the 2-category checker

The Phase 1 2-category engine (`qbx.categorical.two_category`, migration
`009_two_categories.sql`) records 2-cells `α : f ⇒ f'` between parallel 1-morphisms, their
vertical composites `β ∘ᵥ α` and their horizontal composites `β ⋆ α` (for `α` between 1-morphisms
`A → B` and `β` between 1-morphisms `B → C`).  Besides the associativity and unit laws of each
composition it checks

* **identity preservation** `1_g ⋆ 1_f = 1_(g ∘ f)`, and
* the **interchange law** `(β' ∘ᵥ β) ⋆ (α' ∘ᵥ α) = (β' ⋆ α') ∘ᵥ (β ⋆ α)`.

Results:

* `HCompLaws F H`: the two laws for a horizontal composition `H` on hom-categories, written in
  Mathlib's diagrammatic order (`α ≫ α'` is `α' ∘ᵥ α`).
* `bifunctorOfLaws`, `laws_of_bifunctor`, `exists_bifunctor_iff`: a horizontal composition is the
  morphism part of a functor `Hom(B, C) × Hom(A, B) ⥤ Hom(A, C)` **iff** identity preservation and
  interchange hold — the two checks are sound and complete for functoriality.
* `interchange_not_implied`, `identity_preservation_not_implied`: neither law implies the other,
  so the checker needs both.
* `eckmannHilton_two_cells`: on the 2-cells of an identity 1-morphism the laws force vertical and
  horizontal composition to coincide and to be commutative (Eckmann–Hilton).  The test suite uses
  this as an oracle: a non-commutative group recorded as such 2-cells must fail interchange.
-/

/-- The two laws the checker verifies for a horizontal composition `H` with object part `F`:
identity preservation and the interchange law (diagrammatic order: `f ≫ f'` is `f` then `f'`). -/
/-- Soundness: a horizontal composition passing both checks is a bifunctor. -/
/-- Completeness: the morphism part of any bifunctor passes both checks. -/

/-- **The checks are sound and complete**: `H` is the morphism part of a functor
`C × D ⥤ E` with object part `F` iff identity preservation and interchange hold. -/

/-- Interchange is not implied by identity preservation: on the one-object category of the
symmetric group `S₃`, horizontal composition `H a b = a * b` preserves identities but fails
interchange (it would force `S₃` to be commutative). -/

/-- Identity preservation is not implied by interchange: on the one-object category of the
monoid `(ℕ, *)`, the constant horizontal composition `H a b = 0` satisfies interchange
(`0 = 0 * 0`) but `H 1 1 = 0 ≠ 1`. -/

/-- **Eckmann–Hilton for 2-cells of an identity 1-morphism.**  If vertical composition `v` and
horizontal composition `h` on the 2-cells `1_A ⇒ 1_A` are unital (with units `e₁`, `e₂`; in a
2-category both are the identity 2-cell of `1_A`) and satisfy the interchange law, then they are
the same operation and it is commutative. -/

/-!
# The lattice of simple braids (weak order on permutations)

Background for Garside's uniqueness theorem (`GarsideUniqueness.lean`, registry H-057).

A simple braid is described by its permutation `p`; two strands starting at positions `a < b`
cross in it exactly when `p b < p a` (`Crosses`).  The prefix order of simple braids is the
inclusion of crossing sets (`PermLe`); with the composition convention of the project
("`p` then `r`" is the permutation `r * p`):

* `simpleProduct_iff_inversions`: `p` followed by `r` is again simple (no pair of strands
  crosses twice, `SimpleProduct p r`) iff the inversion counts add up;
  `simpleBraid_mul_of_simpleProduct` is the corresponding identity in `B_n`.
* `exists_perm_of_crossing`: a relation on positions that is transitive and co-transitive is
  the crossing set of a permutation; from it come joins (`permJoin`, the transitive closure
  of the union of crossing sets) and meets (`permMeet`).
* `compl` (`∂p`, the simple braid with `p · ∂p = Δ`), the prefix-shift lemma
  `permLe_mul_iff` and the atoms `transposition i` (`permLe_transposition_iff`).
-/
/-! ### Crossings and flips -/
/-- Strands starting at positions `a < b` cross in the simple braid of `p`. -/
/-- The positions `a`, `b` change order under `p` (for `a ≠ b`). -/
/-- `p` followed by `r` is simple: no pair of strands crosses twice. -/
/-! ### Counting crossings -/
/-- Indicator of crossings. -/
/-- Indicator of the crossings of `p` that are undone by `r`. -/

/-- The inversion count of a product: `inv (r * p) = inv p + inv r - 2 · #(pairs crossing
twice)`. -/
/-- `p` followed by `r` is simple iff the inversion counts add up. -/
/-- The braid identity behind simple products: `simple (p then r) = simple p · simple r`. -/
/-! ### The prefix order -/
/-- `p ≼ q`: the simple braid of `p` is a prefix of that of `q` (inclusion of crossing sets). -/
/-- **Prefix shift**: for simple products, `t u ≼ t v ↔ u ≼ v`. -/
-- the pair of positions sorted
/-! ### Crossing sets are the transitive, co-transitive relations -/

/-- A relation on positions that is contained in `<`, transitive and co-transitive is the
crossing set of a permutation. -/
-- `R a b`: strand `a` ends to the left of strand `b`
/-! ### Joins and meets -/
/-- The union of two crossing sets. -/
/-- The join (least common multiple) of two simple braids. -/
/-- The meet (greatest common prefix) of two simple braids. -/
/-! ### Complements, `Δ` and atoms -/
/-- `∂p`: the simple braid completing `p` to `Δ` (`p` then `∂p` is `Δ`). -/
/-- `p` followed by `r` is simple iff `r` is a prefix of `∂p`. -/
/-- The atoms: `σ_i` is a prefix of `p` iff `i` is a starting generator of `p`. -/
/-- Two simple braids have trivial meet iff they share no starting generator. -/
/-- `σ_i` can be appended to the simple braid of `a` iff `i` is not a finishing generator. -/

/-!
# How far a window statistic diverges when the collars are dropped

`QBX.Formal.TextManifold.windowSum_atlas` says that a `k`-local statistic is computed *exactly*
chart by chart, provided every chart carries a collar of the next `k - 1` letters.  This file
measures what happens without the collars, as a concrete instance of the divergence bounds of
`Sovereign/Analysis/ApproximateHomomorphism.lean`:

* `windowSum_isApproxAdd` — if every window has value of norm at most `B`, the window sum is
  additive up to `(k - 1) B`: only the at most `k - 1` windows straddling the cut are lost.
* `windowSum_chunks_no_collar` — hence summing the window statistic over `n ≥ 1` chunks *without
  collars* is off by at most `(n - 1)(k - 1) B`.
-/

/-- The windows of `a` are a prefix of the windows of `a ++ c`, and at most `c.length` windows
are added. -/

/-- **Window sums are approximately additive.**  If every window has value of norm at most `B`,
cutting a text in two loses at most the `k - 1` straddling windows. -/

/-- **Dropping the collars.**  Computing a `k`-local statistic chunk by chunk on `n ≥ 1` chunks
*without* collars is off by at most `(n - 1)(k - 1) B`, where `B` bounds the value of a single
window (compare the exact `windowSum_atlas`, which uses collars). -/

/-!
# The witness rule of the consensus protocol leaves no blind spots

Layer 9 (`foundation/ws9_protocol/`, integrated from Phase D work stream D4), property P9.1,
whose paper proof is `ws9_protocol/docs/WITNESS.md`. When a payload message `u → v` is delivered
along an edge of `Q_n □ T^k_M`, the protocol asks for three witness messages around the square
spanned by the payload edge and a second, transverse dimension `d`:
`v → v'`, `v' → u'`, `u' → u`, where `x' = step x d` (flip bit `d`, or advance cycle `d` by
`+1`). The payload event and its three witnesses enter the ledger together or not at all
(`ws9_protocol/witness.py`).

`witnessGraph P` is the event graph produced by any set `P` of finalised payloads: the union of
their squares. We prove:

* `witnessGraph_le_addrGraph`: every event is an edge of the address graph;
* `witnessGraph_not_isBridge`: if every payload's witness dimension is transverse to its payload
  edge and every cycle length is `≠ 1`, the event graph has **no bridges** — each event lies on the
  4-cycle of its square (claims 1–2 of `WITNESS.md`);
* `witnessGraph_perturb_detected`: hence every single-event fork of a flat ledger on the event
  graph is detected (F5, `perturb_detected_iff_not_isBridge`).

The protocol chooses `d = (d_payload + 1) mod (n + k)`; the theorems hold for every transverse
choice, and for payloads in either direction of a cycle.
-/

/-- **An edge on a 4-cycle is not a bridge.** If `x — y` is an edge and `x — p — q — y` is a
path with `p ≠ y` and `q ≠ x`, then `x — y` is not a bridge. -/
/-- A dimension of `Q_n □ T^k_M`: a bit `i` or a cycle `j`. -/

/-- A move label: flip bit `i`, or step cycle `j` by `+1` (`up = true`) or `−1`. These are the
edge labels of the address graph. -/
/-- The dimension a move label acts in. -/
/-- Apply a move label to an address. -/

/-- The witness step along a dimension: flip the bit, or advance the cycle by `+1`
(`move(x, d)` of `ws9_protocol/witness.py`). -/
/-- Two addresses agree in coordinate `d`. -/
/-- Witness steps commute with every move. -/
/-- Every edge of the address graph carries a move label. -/

/-- A finalised payload: the message `u → applyMove u l`, witnessed around the square spanned by
`l` and the dimension `d`. -/
/-- The sender. -/
/-- The payload edge label (the receiver is `applyMove u l`). -/
/-- The witness dimension. -/
/-- The four events of a finalised payload: `u → v`, `v → v'`, `v' → u'`, `u' → u`. -/
/-- The event graph of a ledger built by the witness rule from the finalised payloads `P`. -/
/-- Every event of a witness-rule ledger is an edge of the address graph. -/
/-- The four corners of a square with transverse witness dimension are pairwise distinct. -/
-- coordinate `d`: changed by the step, untouched by the move
-- coordinate `l.dim`: changed by the move, untouched by the step

/-- **Witness rule, claims 1–2 of `WITNESS.md`.** If every finalised payload is witnessed along a
dimension transverse to its payload edge, and no cycle has length `1`, then the event graph of the
ledger has no bridges: every event lies on the 4-cycle of its square. -/
-- each side of the square, via the other three sides

/-- **Witness rule: no undetected single-event fork.** On the event graph of a witness-rule
ledger, changing the transport of any one event of a flat ledger by `κ ≠ 1` makes it non-flat. -/

/-- The protocol's choice of witness dimension, `d = (d_payload + 1) mod (n + k)`, is transverse
whenever there are at least two dimensions. Dimensions are numbered as in `witness.py`: bit `i` is
`i`, cycle `j` is `n + j`. -/

/-- The protocol's witness dimension for a payload along `d`: the next dimension,
`(d + 1) mod (n + k)`. -/

/-- **The protocol as implemented has no blind spots.** With at least two dimensions, no cycle of
length `1`, and every payload witnessed along the next dimension `(d + 1) mod (n + k)`
(`ws9_protocol/witness.py`), the event graph has no bridges. -/

/-!
# Quantum representations of `B_n` from solutions of the Yang–Baxter equation

This is the formal (mode V3, QBX.md §24) counterpart of `qbx_ir.quantum`: for **every**
braided R-matrix `Ř` on `V ⊗ V` (`V = K^d`, `K` any commutative ring) that is invertible and
satisfies the Yang–Baxter equation, the assignment

  `σ_i ↦ I^{⊗ i} ⊗ Ř ⊗ I^{⊗ (n - i - 2)}`

extends to a group homomorphism `B_n →* GL(V^{⊗ n})`, for every number of strands `n`
(`braidRep`).  Consequently every QBX rewrite preserves the quantum operator of a word
(`Step.repOp_eq`): the proof obligation `ρ(B₁) = ρ(B₂)` of QBX.md §35 is discharged once and for
all by the Yang–Baxter equation.

Conventions.  `V^{⊗ n}` is modelled as functions on basis states `s : Fin n → Fin d`, and `Ř`
is given by its matrix entries `R a b c e = ⟨a b| Ř |c e⟩`.  The operator `localOp R i j`
acts on the tensor factors at sites `i` and `j` by the matrix `Ř`.
-/

/-- **The quantum representation.**  An invertible solution `Ř` of the Yang–Baxter equation

so(8) = 𝔤₂ ⊕ 7 ⊕ 7 (adjoint + vector + spinor), and G₂-instantons with parallel spinors.
-/

/-!
# Integer certificates for the decomposition `so(8) = 𝔤₂ ⊕ 7 ⊕ 7`

This file contains the finite integer data behind the decomposition of `so(8)` under
`𝔤₂ = Der(𝕆)`:

* an explicit list of 14 skew-symmetric integer matrices `g2BasisZ r` (each of the form
  `± E_{ab} + E_{cd}` with `E_{ab} = e_{ab} − e_{ba}`) that are derivations of `𝕆`;
* for every elementary skew matrix `E_{pq}`, integer coefficients expressing
  `6 E_{pq}` as a combination of these 14 derivations plus `L_a + R_b` with `a, b`
  imaginary.

All statements here are finite identities between integers, checked by evaluation. They are
used in `G2Decomposition.lean`.
-/
/-- The elementary skew-symmetric integer matrix `E_{pq} = e_{pq} − e_{qp}`. -/
/-- First index pair and sign of the `r`-th basis derivation. -/
/-- Second index pair of the `r`-th basis derivation. -/
/-- The `r`-th basis element of `𝔤₂` as an integer matrix: `σ E_{ab} + E_{cd}`. -/
/-- Every basis matrix `g2BasisZ r` is a derivation of the integral octonions. -/
/-- `6 E_{pq} = ∑_r decC p q r · G_r + L_{decA p q} + R_{decB p q}`. -/
/-- The vectors `decA p q` and `decB p q` are imaginary. -/

comments.text:
/-!
# `so(8) = 𝔤₂ ⊕ 7 ⊕ 7`

Over any field `K` of characteristic zero we define

* `so8 K` — the Lie algebra `so(8)` of skew-symmetric `8 × 8` matrices (Mathlib's
  `LieAlgebra.Orthogonal.so`), acting on the octonions `𝕆 = K⁸`;
* `g2 K` — the compact form of `𝔤₂`: the skew-symmetric derivations of `𝕆`
  (the Lie algebra of `G₂ = Aut(𝕆) ⊂ SO(8)`);
* `imOct K` — the imaginary octonions `Im 𝕆 ≅ K⁷` (the vector representation of `𝔤₂`);
* `vec7 K = {L_a − R_a : a ∈ Im 𝕆}` and `spin7 K = {L_a + 2 R_a : a ∈ Im 𝕆}`.

and prove:

* `so8_decomposition` : every `A ∈ so(8)` is uniquely `D + v + s` with `D ∈ 𝔤₂`,
  `v ∈ vec7`, `s ∈ spin7`;
* `finrank_so8 = 28`, `finrank_g2 = 14`, `finrank_vec7 = 7`, `finrank_spin7 = 7`;
* `𝔤₂`-invariance: `⁅D, L_a − R_a⁆ = L_{Da} − R_{Da}`, `⁅D, L_a + 2R_a⁆ = L_{Da} + 2R_{Da}`,
  so both 7-dimensional pieces are copies of the vector representation `Im 𝕆` of `𝔤₂`,
  while `𝔤₂` itself is the adjoint representation.

The labels "vector" and "spinor" are justified in `G2Triality.lean`:
`g2 ⊕ vec7` is the vector `so(7)` (the stabiliser of `1 ∈ 𝕆`), and `g2 ⊕ spin7` is its image
under triality, the spinor `spin(7)`.
-/
/-! ### The Lie algebras -/
/-- `so(8)`: skew-symmetric `8 × 8` matrices acting on the octonions `K⁸`. -/
/-- **`𝔤₂`**, the Lie algebra of `G₂ = Aut(𝕆)`: skew-symmetric derivations of the octonions. -/
/-- The imaginary octonions `Im 𝕆 = {a | a₀ = 0} ≅ K⁷`. -/
/-- The "vector" `7`: `{L_a − R_a : a ∈ Im 𝕆}` (the operators `ad_a = [a, ·]`). -/
/-- The "spinor" `7`: `{L_a + 2 R_a : a ∈ Im 𝕆}`, the triality image of `vec7`. -/
/-! ### Transport of the integer certificates -/
/-- The `r`-th basis element of `𝔤₂` over `K`. -/
/-! ### Skew-symmetry of `L_a`, `R_a` for imaginary `a` -/
/-! ### Existence of the decomposition `A = D + L_a + R_b` -/
/-- Coefficient of the `r`-th basis derivation in `12 A`. -/
/-- The vector `a` with `12 A = … + L_a + …`. -/
/-- The vector `b` with `12 A = … + R_b`. -/
/-! ### Derivations kill `1`; the defect of `ad_a` -/
/-- A derivation kills `1`. -/
/-- The derivation defect of `ad_{e_m} = L_{e_m} − R_{e_m}` (integer table). -/
/-- Witness indices detecting the `m`-th coordinate of `a` in the defect of `ad_a`. -/
/-- `derDefect` at fixed indices, as a linear functional. -/
/-! ### `𝔤₂`-module structure -/
/-- `⁅D, L_a⁆ = L_{Da}` for a derivation `D`. -/
/-- `⁅D, R_b⁆ = R_{Db}` for a derivation `D`. -/
/-- `𝔤₂` preserves the imaginary octonions: `Im 𝕆` is a `𝔤₂`-module (the vector `7`). -/
/-- The vector `7` is the vector representation: `a ↦ L_a − R_a` is `𝔤₂`-equivariant. -/
/-- The spinor `7` is again the vector representation: `a ↦ L_a + 2R_a` is equivariant. -/
/-- `vec7` is a `𝔤₂`-submodule of `so(8)`. -/
/-- `spin7` is a `𝔤₂`-submodule of `so(8)`. -/
/-- `𝔤₂` is a `𝔤₂`-submodule of `so(8)` (the adjoint `14`). -/
/-! ### Existence and uniqueness (characteristic zero) -/
/-- **Existence**: every `A ∈ so(8)` is `D + L_a + R_b` with `D ∈ 𝔤₂` and `a, b ∈ Im 𝕆`. -/
/-- If `ad_a` is a derivation for an imaginary octonion `a`, then `a = 0`. -/
/-- **Uniqueness** of `A = D + L_a + R_b`. -/
/-! ### The decomposition `so(8) = 𝔤₂ ⊕ 7_v ⊕ 7_s` -/
/-- Existence of `A = D + v + s`. -/
/-- Uniqueness of `A = D + v + s`: the three pieces are independent. -/

/-- **The decomposition `so(8) = 𝔤₂ ⊕ 7 ⊕ 7`**: a matrix lies in `so(8)` iff it is a sum
`D + v + s` with `D ∈ 𝔤₂`, `v ∈ vec7`, `s ∈ spin7`, and this decomposition is unique. -/
/-! ### Dimensions -/

/-- `so(8)` is 28-dimensional: a skew matrix is determined by its 28 entries above the
diagonal. -/
/-- The linear map `𝔤₂ × 7_v × 7_s → Mat₈`, `(D, v, s) ↦ D + v + s`. -/

/-- **Headline: `28 = 14 + 7 + 7`.** Under `𝔤₂ = Der(𝕆)`, the adjoint representation
`so(8)` splits as the direct sum of the adjoint `𝔤₂` (dimension 14) and two copies `vec7`,
`spin7` of the 7-dimensional representation `Im 𝕆`, each stable under `𝔤₂`. -/

comments.text:
/-!
# `G₂`-instantons, parallel spinors and the BPS bound

We work pointwise on a `G₂`-manifold, i.e. on the model tangent space `ℝ⁷ = Im 𝕆` with its
associative 3-form `φ_{abc} = ⟨e_a e_b, e_c⟩` and coassociative 4-form `ψ = ⋆φ`. The
spinor bundle is modelled on `𝕆 = ℝ⁸`, on which `Cl(ℝ⁷)` acts by left octonion
multiplication; the unit `η = 1 ∈ 𝕆` is the `G₂`-invariant spinor, which on a manifold with
holonomy in `G₂` is the parallel spinor.

A curvature 2-form component `F` is a skew matrix `F_{ab}` (`F = ½ F_{ab} e^{ab}`). We prove:

* `starPhi_hodge` : the tensor `starPhi` is exactly the Hodge dual `⋆φ`
  (`(⋆φ)_{abcd} = (1/3!) ε_{abcdefg} φ_{efg}`), and it is totally antisymmetric;
* `topDensity_eq` : the top-degree coefficient of `F ∧ F ∧ φ` equals
  `¼ ∑ (⋆φ)_{abcd} F_{ab} F_{cd}`;
* **`instanton_iff`** : for a 2-form `F` the following are equivalent:
  1. `F ∈ 𝔤₂` (the curvature takes values in the holonomy algebra: `F` is a `G₂`-instanton);
  2. `F · η = 0` (the curvature annihilates the parallel spinor — the gaugino
     supersymmetry variation `δχ = F · η` vanishes);
  3. `F ⌟ φ = 0`;
  4. `½ ∑_{cd} (⋆φ)_{abcd} F_{cd} = F_{ab}` (`F ∈ Λ²₁₄`, the `+1` eigenspace of the operator
     `F ↦ ½ (⋆φ) ⌟ F` on 2-forms);
* **`energy_identity`** : `|F|² = top(F) + ¼ |F · η|²`, where `|F|²` is the coefficient of
  `F ∧ ⋆F` and `top(F)` that of `F ∧ F ∧ φ`;
* **`bps_bound`** / **`bps_saturation_iff`** : `|F|² ≥ top(F)`, with equality iff `F` is a
  `G₂`-instanton; the same for gauge-algebra-valued curvatures (`ym_ge_top`, `ym_eq_top_iff`)
  and for the integrated Yang–Mills action against any measure (`action_ge_charge`,
  `action_eq_charge_iff`).

So on parallel spinors the *non-topological* part `F ∧ ⋆F − F ∧ F ∧ φ = ¼|F·η|² vol` of the
Yang–Mills density vanishes: supersymmetric (instanton) configurations saturate the BPS bound
and minimise the Yang–Mills action among configurations with the same value of
`∫ F ∧ F ∧ φ`. The literal claim "`F ∧ ⋆F` vanishes on parallel spinors" is false:
`F ∧ ⋆F = |F|² vol` vanishes only for `F = 0` (`energy_eq_zero_iff`), while non-flat
instantons exist (`exists_nonflat_instanton`).
-/
/-! ### The associative 3-form, its Hodge dual and the Levi-Civita symbol -/
/-- The associative 3-form `φ_{abc} = ⟨e_a e_b, e_c⟩` on `Im 𝕆 = ℝ⁷`. -/
/-- Number of inversions of a list of naturals. -/
/-- The Levi-Civita symbol `ε_{abcdefg}` in seven dimensions. -/

/-- The coassociative 4-form `ψ = ⋆φ`, in the form
`ψ_{abcd} = δ_{ac}δ_{bd} − δ_{ad}δ_{bc} − ∑_k φ_{abk} φ_{cdk}`. -/
/-- `φ` is a 3-form (totally antisymmetric). -/
/-- `⋆φ` is a 4-form (totally antisymmetric). -/

/-! The Hodge-dual identity is checked by the kernel.  To keep the check small, the sum over
`e, f, g` is first restricted to indices different from `a, b, c, d` (all other terms vanish
because `ε` has a repeated index), which cuts the `7⁴ · 7³` evaluations by roughly a factor of
eight. -/
/-- The indices left free by `a, b, c, d`. -/
/-- **`starPhi` is the Hodge dual of `φ`**: `(⋆φ)_{abcd} = (1/3!) ∑ ε_{abcdefg} φ_{efg}`. -/
/-! ### 2-forms, the Clifford action and the parallel spinor -/
/-- A (curvature) 2-form on `ℝ⁷`: a skew-symmetric matrix `F_{ab}`. -/
/-- A 2-form on `Im 𝕆`, viewed as an element of `so(7) ⊂ so(8)` acting on `𝕆 = ℝ ⊕ Im 𝕆`. -/
/-- The imaginary unit `e_{a+1} ∈ 𝕆`. -/

/-- **Clifford action** of a 2-form on spinors `η ∈ 𝕆`: `F · η = ∑ F_{ab} e_a (e_b η)`,
with `Cl(Im 𝕆)` acting on `𝕆` by left multiplication. -/
/-- The parallel (`G₂`-invariant) spinor `η = 1 ∈ 𝕆`. -/
/-- The contraction `(F ⌟ φ)_k = ∑ F_{ab} φ_{abk}`. -/
/-- The linear functional `A ↦ ∑_{ij} A_{ij} e_i e_j` on `8 × 8` matrices. -/
/-! ### `c8` on `𝔤₂` and on the vector `7` -/
/-- Table of `c8 (L_{e_m} − R_{e_m})`. -/
/-- `c8` as a linear map. -/
/-- Every element of `𝔤₂` is a combination of the 14 basis derivations. -/
/-- Contraction of a 2-form with `⋆φ`: `∑_{cd} (⋆φ)_{abcd} F_{cd} = 2 F_{ab} − ∑_k φ_{abk} (F ⌟ φ)_k`. -/
/-! ### The instanton condition -/

/-- **`G₂`-instantons.** For a 2-form `F` on `ℝ⁷` the following are equivalent:
(1) `F ∈ 𝔤₂` (curvature in the holonomy algebra), (2) `F · η = 0` for the parallel spinor
`η`, (3) `F ⌟ φ = 0`, (4) `½ ∑_{cd} (⋆φ)_{abcd} F_{cd} = F_{ab}` (i.e. `F ∈ Λ²₁₄`). -/
/-! ### `F ∧ ⋆F`, `F ∧ F ∧ φ` and the BPS bound -/

/-- The Yang–Mills energy density `|F|² = ½ ∑ F_{ab}²`: the coefficient of
`F ∧ ⋆F = |F|² vol`. -/

/-- The top-degree coefficient of `F ∧ F ∧ φ` (with `F = ½ F_{ab} e^{ab}`,
`φ = (1/3!) φ_{abc} e^{abc}`): `(1 / (2!·2!·3!)) ∑ ε_{abcdefg} F_{ab} F_{cd} φ_{efg}`. -/
/-- `F ∧ F ∧ φ = ¼ (⋆φ)_{abcd} F_{ab} F_{cd} vol`. -/

/-- **Energy identity**: `|F|² = top(F) + ¼ |F · η|²`, i.e.
`F ∧ ⋆F = F ∧ F ∧ φ + ¼ |F · η|² vol` for the parallel spinor `η`. -/
/-- `F ∧ ⋆F` vanishes only for `F = 0`. -/
/-- **BPS bound**: `F ∧ ⋆F ≥ F ∧ F ∧ φ` pointwise. -/

/-- **Saturation of the BPS bound**: `F ∧ ⋆F = F ∧ F ∧ φ` iff `F · η = 0` iff `F` is a
`G₂`-instanton. -/

/-- The literal statement "`F ∧ ⋆F = 0` for every instanton" is false: there are non-flat
`G₂`-instantons, whose energy density `F ∧ ⋆F = |F|² vol` is non-zero. -/
/-! ### Gauge-algebra-valued curvature and the Yang–Mills action -/

/-- Yang–Mills density `−tr(F ∧ ⋆F)` for a curvature `F = ∑_α F^α T_α` written in an
orthonormal basis `T_α` of the gauge Lie algebra. -/
/-- The topological density `−tr(F ∧ F) ∧ φ` in the same basis. -/

/-- A gauge field strength is a `G₂`-instanton iff all its components annihilate the parallel
spinor. -/
/-- BPS bound for gauge fields: `−tr(F ∧ ⋆F) ≥ −tr(F ∧ F) ∧ φ` pointwise. -/
/-- The BPS bound is saturated exactly by `G₂`-instantons (supersymmetric configurations). -/

/-- **Vacuum stability (BPS bound for the action)**: for any measure (e.g. the Riemannian
volume of a `G₂`-manifold), the Yang–Mills action is bounded below by the `φ`-weighted
topological charge `∫ −tr(F ∧ F) ∧ φ`. -/

/-- **The action equals the topological charge iff the field is a `G₂`-instanton almost
everywhere**, i.e. iff it annihilates the parallel spinor almost everywhere
(supersymmetric vacua are exactly the minimisers saturating the bound). -/

/-!
# The octonions in coordinates

This file sets up the octonion algebra `𝕆 = K⁸` over a commutative ring, with the
canonical basis `e₀ = 1, e₁, …, e₇` multiplying by the Cayley–Dickson rule
`e_i e_j = σ(i, j) e_{i ⊕ j}` (`⊕` = bitwise xor), together with

* left and right multiplication matrices `L_a`, `R_b`;
* derivations of `𝕆` and their characterisation by the finite table `derDefect`;
* the two linearised alternative laws `a(xy) = (ax + xa)y − x(ay)` and
  `(xy)b = x(yb + by) − (xb)y`, which are the identities behind infinitesimal triality.

It is the common foundation of the files `G2Decomposition`, `G2Triality` and
`G2Instanton`.
-/

/-- The sign table `σ(i, j)` of the octonion basis: `e_i e_j = σ(i, j) e_{i ⊕ j}`.
It is the level-3 table of the Cayley–Dickson product (see `octSign_eq_cdSign` in
`G2Triality.lean` for the comparison with the tower already in the project). -/
/-- The index `i ⊕ j` (bitwise xor) of the product `e_i e_j`. -/
/-- Structure constants of the octonions: `e_i e_j = ∑_k octC i j k • e_k`. -/
/-- Octonion multiplication on `R⁸`, bilinear with structure constants `octC`. -/
/-- The unit octonion `1 = e₀`. -/
/-- Matrix of left multiplication `L_a : x ↦ a x`. -/
/-- Matrix of right multiplication `R_b : x ↦ x b`. -/
/-- Octonion multiplication as a bilinear map. -/
/-- `a ↦ L_a` as a linear map. -/
/-- `b ↦ R_b` as a linear map. -/
/-! ### Derivations -/
/-- A matrix `D` is a **derivation** of the octonions if `D(xy) = (Dx)y + x(Dy)`. -/
/-- The defect `D(e_i e_j) − (D e_i) e_j − e_i (D e_j)`, component `k`. -/
/-- The derivation defect, expanded bilinearly. -/

/-- **Derivations are detected by a finite table**: `D` is a derivation iff
`derDefect D i j k = 0` for all basis indices. -/
/-- The commutator of two derivations is a derivation. -/
/-! ### Linearised alternative laws -/
/-- Table form of `a(xy) = (ax + xa)y − x(ay)` on basis vectors. -/
/-- Table form of `(xy)b = x(yb + by) − (xb)y` on basis vectors. -/
/-- **Linearised left alternative law**: `a(xy) = (ax + xa)y − x(ay)` for all octonions. -/
/-- **Linearised right alternative law**: `(xy)b = x(yb + by) − (xb)y` for all octonions. -/

comments.text:
/-!
# Infinitesimal triality, `so(7)`, `spin(7)` and `𝔤₂`

For `A ∈ so(8)` acting on the octonions `𝕆 = K⁸`, a **related triple** is a pair
`(B, C) ∈ so(8) × so(8)` with

  `A(xy) = (Bx)y + x(Cy)`   for all `x, y ∈ 𝕆`.

This is the infinitesimal form of Cartan's principle of triality. We prove:

* `principle_of_triality` : every `A ∈ so(8)` has a unique related pair `(B, C)`;
* the resulting maps `θ₁ : A ↦ B`, `θ₂ : A ↦ C` are linear and preserve brackets
  (`triB_lie`, `triC_lie`), and are given explicitly on the decomposition
  `A = D + L_a + R_b` of `G2Decomposition.lean` by
  `θ₁(A) = D + L_a + R_a − R_b`, `θ₂(A) = D − L_a + L_b + R_b`;
* `𝔤₂` is exactly the set of `A` with `θ₁ A = A` and `θ₂ A = A` (`g2_eq_triality_fixed`):
  the derivations are the self-related triples `(D, D, D)`;
* the vector `so(7)` (stabiliser of `1 ∈ 𝕆`) is `𝔤₂ ⊕ vec7` (`mem_so7v_iff`), its triality image
  `spin(7) = θ₁(so(7))` is `𝔤₂ ⊕ spin7` (`mem_spin7Alg_iff`), `θ₁` maps `vec7` onto `spin7`
  (`triB_vec7`), and
* `𝔤₂ = so(7) ∩ spin(7)` and `𝔤₂` is the stabiliser in `spin(7)` of the spinor `1 ∈ 𝕆`
  (`g2_eq_spin7_stab`) — the Lie-algebra statement that `G₂ ⊂ Spin(7)` is the stabiliser of a
  (parallel) spinor, which is why `G₂`-holonomy 7-manifolds and `Spin(7)`-holonomy
  8-manifolds carry parallel spinors.

Finally `octSign_eq_cdSign` identifies the octonion table used here with level 3 of the
Cayley–Dickson tower already present in the project.
-/

/-- The octonion sign table is level 3 of the Cayley–Dickson sign cochain `cdSign`
of `SedenionCocycle.lean`, and `octIdx` is the bitwise xor used there. -/
/-- `(A, B, C)` is a **related triple**: `A(xy) = (Bx)y + x(Cy)` for all octonions. -/
/-- The bracket of related triples is a related triple. -/
/-- Derivations are self-related: `(D, D, D)`. -/
/-- `(L_a, L_a + R_a, −L_a)` is a related triple (left alternative law). -/
/-- `(R_b, −R_b, L_b + R_b)` is a related triple (right alternative law). -/
/-- If the associator `(x, u, y)` vanishes identically then `ad_u` is a derivation. -/

/-- **Uniqueness in triality**: if `(Bx)y + x(Cy) = 0` for all `x, y` with `B, C ∈ so(8)`,
then `B = C = 0`. -/
-- `u` is imaginary because `C = L_u` is skew

/-- Existence of a related triple for every `A ∈ so(8)`, with the explicit formula on the
decomposition `A = D + L_a + R_b`. -/

/-- **The principle of triality** (infinitesimal form): every `A ∈ so(8)` has a unique pair
`(B, C) ∈ so(8) × so(8)` with `A(xy) = (Bx)y + x(Cy)` for all octonions `x, y`. -/
/-- The triality map `θ₁ : so(8) → so(8)`, `A ↦ B`. -/
/-- The triality map `θ₂ : so(8) → so(8)`, `A ↦ C`. -/
/-- `(θ₁ A, θ₂ A)` is characterised by the triality relation. -/
/-- Explicit triality on the decomposition `A = D + L_a + R_b`. -/
/-- `θ₁` and `θ₂` are additive on `so(8)`. -/
/-- `θ₁` and `θ₂` are homogeneous on `so(8)`. -/
/-- **Triality preserves brackets**: `θ₁ ⁅A, A'⁆ = ⁅θ₁ A, θ₁ A'⁆`, and likewise for `θ₂`. -/

/-- **`𝔤₂` is the fixed algebra of triality**: `A ∈ so(8)` is a derivation of `𝕆` iff
`θ₁ A = A` and `θ₂ A = A`. -/
/-- The vector `so(7) ⊂ so(8)`: the stabiliser of `1 ∈ 𝕆`, i.e. `so(Im 𝕆)`. -/

/-- The spinor `spin(7) ⊂ so(8)`: the image `θ₁(so(7))` of the vector `so(7)` under triality
(this is how `Spin(7)` acts on its 8-dimensional spin representation `𝕆`). -/
/-- Triality maps the vector `7` onto the spinor `7`: `θ₁(L_a − R_a) = L_a + 2 R_a`. -/
/-- `spin(7) = 𝔤₂ ⊕ spin7`. -/

/-- **`G₂` is the stabiliser of a spinor in `Spin(7)`** (Lie algebra version):
`𝔤₂ = {B ∈ spin(7) : B · 1 = 0}`. -/

/-- **`𝔤₂ = so(7) ∩ spin(7)`**: the vector and spinor `so(7)`'s inside `so(8)` meet exactly
in `𝔤₂`. -/

declarations.name: HeckeSystem
declarations.signature_heuristic:
structure HeckeSystem (k : ℕ) (a : ℕ → R) : Prop where
  /-- normalisation -/
  one : a 1 = 1
  /-- multiplicativity on coprime arguments -/
  mul_coprime : ∀ m n : ℕ, Nat.Coprime m n → a (m * n) = a m * a n
  /-- the recursion at prime powers -/
  prime_pow : ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ j : ℕ,
    a (p ^ (j + 2)) = a p * a (p ^ (j + 1)) - (p : R) ^ (k - 1) * a (p ^ j)

variable {k : ℕ} {a b : ℕ → R}

/-- The eigenvalue at `p ^ j` is a polynomial in the single eigenvalue `a p`: two systems that
agree at `p` agree at all powers of `p`. -/

/-- The multiplicative structure of the Hecke eigenvalue system of a normalised eigenform of
weight `k`, over a commutative ring `R`. -/
/-- normalisation -/
/-- multiplicativity on coprime arguments -/
/-- the recursion at prime powers -/

/-- The eigenvalue at `p ^ j` is a polynomial in the single eigenvalue `a p`: two systems that
agree at `p` agree at all powers of `p`. -/
/-- The `S`-smooth numbers: the positive integers all of whose prime factors lie in `S`. -/

/-- **Multiplicative closure.**  If two Hecke systems of the same weight agree at every prime of
`S`, they agree at every positive integer built out of the primes of `S`. -/
/-- The same statement, phrased with `Smooth`. -/

/-- **`T 2` and `T 3` pin down the whole `3`-smooth part.**  Two Hecke systems of the same weight
with the same eigenvalues at `2` and at `3` agree at every `n = 2 ^ i * 3 ^ j`. -/
/-- **Agreement at all primes is agreement everywhere.** -/

/-- **Finite truncation / baby multiplicity one.**  Agreement at the finitely many primes `p ≤ N`
forces agreement at every `n ≤ N`. -/

/-- **Weak multiplicity one for a finite family.**  Given finitely many Hecke systems of a fixed
weight, there is a single bound `N` such that agreement at the primes `p ≤ N` already forces two
members of the family to be equal at every positive integer.  This is a pigeonhole statement, not
an analytic one: the bound is extracted from the finitely many places where the members differ,
and nothing here gives an effective `N` in terms of the weight. -/

/-- **`a 0` really is undetermined**, so the restriction to `n ≠ 0` above cannot be dropped:
changing the value of a Hecke system at `0` to an arbitrary `c` gives a Hecke system again. -/

/-! ### The low-degree eigenvalues

`4`, `6`, `9`, `12` and `27` are the arguments produced by the five words `T2`, `T3`, `T2T3`,
`T2T3T2`, `T3T3T3` of `RequestProject.Hecke.Words`; each eigenvalue there is a polynomial in
`a 2` and `a 3` alone. -/
/-- `6 = 2 · 3`: the eigenvalue at six is the product of the eigenvalues at two and three. -/
/-- `9 = 3 ^ 2`: the third member of the trinity is already determined by `T 3`. -/

/-- **The axioms are not vacuous.**  The divisor-counting function `n ↦ d(n)` is a Hecke system
of weight `1` over any commutative ring (it is the eigenvalue system of the weight-`2` Eisenstein
family in disguise). -/

/-!
# Five Hecke words: `T2`, `T3`, `T2 T3`, `T2 T3 T2`, `T3 T3 T3`

Start from an eigenform `f` of weight `k` with eigenvalue system `a` and apply the two smallest
Hecke operators in the five patterns

```
  T2 ,  T3 ,  T2 T3 ,  T2 T3 T2 ,  T3 T3 T3 .
```

Each of the resulting five modular forms is again a multiple of `f`, and the multiplier is the
product of the eigenvalues of the letters (`wordEigenvalue`).  The content of the file is the
translation of each of those five products back into the *basis* `T 1, T 2, T 3, …` of the Hecke
algebra, i.e. the answer to "which single Hecke operators does this word cost?":

* `T2` and `T3` are already basis elements;
* `T2 T3 = T 6` — coprime letters just multiply;
* `T2 T3 T2 = T 12 + 2 ^ (k-1) * T 3` — the repeated letter produces an echo;
* `T3 T3 T3 = T 27 + 2 * 3 ^ (k-1) * T 3` — the same letter three times produces two echoes.

Both sides are proved twice, and independently.

1. Eigenvalue level (`eigen_*`): identities between the eigenvalue products and the eigenvalues
   `a 6`, `a 12`, `a 27`, valid in every Hecke system.
2. Hecke-algebra level (`hmul_*`): in the formal algebra `ℕ →₀ R` with the classical structure
   constants `T m * T n = ∑_{d ∣ gcd m n} d ^ (k-1) * T (m n / d ^ 2)`, where the same three
   identities are computations with divisor sets.

`evalT_word_*` says the two descriptions agree, and `eigen_polynomial_*` records each multiplier
as an explicit polynomial in `a 2` and `a 3` alone.  `delta_values` instantiates the five words
at the discriminant form, where `a 2 = τ(2) = -24` and `a 3 = τ(3) = 252`.
-/
/-! ## 1. The eigenvalue side -/

/-- The multiplier by which the word `w` (read left to right, each letter a prime) scales an
eigenform with eigenvalue system `a`: the product of the eigenvalues of the letters. -/
/-- Word 3: `T2 T3` acts by `a 6` — the letters are coprime, so nothing is lost. -/
/-! ## 2. The Hecke algebra side -/
/-- The formal Hecke operator `T n`, as a basis vector of the Hecke algebra `ℕ →₀ R`. -/
/-- The structure constants: `T m * T n = ∑_{d ∣ gcd m n} d ^ (k-1) T (m n / d ^ 2)`. -/
/-- Multiplication in the weight-`k` Hecke algebra, the bilinear extension of `basisMul`. -/
/-- On basis vectors, `hmul` is given by the structure constants. -/
/-- A scaled basis vector on the left. -/
/-- **Word 3, in the algebra**: `T2 * T3 = T 6`. Coprime letters cost nothing. -/
/-- **Word 4, in the algebra**: `(T2 T3) T2 = T 12 + 2 ^ (k-1) T 3`. -/
/-- `T3 * T3 = T 9 + 3 ^ (k-1) T 1`: the first echo. -/
/-- **Word 5, in the algebra**: `(T3 T3) T3 = T 27 + 2 · 3 ^ (k-1) T 3`. -/

/-! ## 3. The two sides agree

An eigenvalue system `a` turns a Hecke algebra element into a scalar; the two descriptions of
each word — the product of eigenvalues, and the expansion into basis operators — are then the
same number. -/

/-- Evaluate a Hecke algebra element at the eigenvalue system `a`: `T n ↦ a n`, extended
linearly. For an eigenform `f` with system `a`, this is the scalar by which the operator acts. -/
/-- Word 3: the two computations agree. -/
/-- Word 4: the two computations agree. -/
/-- Word 5: the two computations agree. -/
/-! ## 4. The five multipliers as polynomials in `a 2` and `a 3` -/

/-! ## 5. A concrete anchor: the discriminant form

For `Δ` of weight `12` the eigenvalues are Ramanujan's `τ`, with `τ 2 = -24` and `τ 3 = 252`.
The five words then take the values below — every number in them is forced by the two inputs. -/

/-!
# Higgs inflation with a non-minimal coupling `ξ |H|² R`: exact slow-roll analysis

Jordan-frame action (reduced Planck mass `M`, unitary-gauge Higgs `h`, quartic `λ`):

`S_J = ∫ √g [ −½ (M² + ξ h²) R + ½ (∂h)² − ¼ λ h⁴ ]`.

The Weyl rescaling `g ↦ Ω² g`, `Ω² = 1 + ξ h²/M²` gives an Einstein-frame action with a
canonically normalised inflaton `χ`, where

* `(dχ/dh)² = K(h) = (Ω² + 6 ξ² h²/M²)/Ω⁴`             (`fieldMetric`),
* `U(h) = λ h⁴ / (4 Ω⁴)`                                 (`einsteinPotential`).

The slow-roll parameters are the Einstein-frame ones, `ε = ½ M² (U_χ/U)²` and
`η = M² U_χχ/U`, rewritten with `d/dχ = K^{-1/2} d/dh`:

* `ε = ½ M² (U'/U)² / K`                                  (`epsilonSR`),
* `η = M² (U'' − U' K'/(2K)) / (K U)`                     (`etaSR`),
* `N(h₁, h₂) = ∫_{h₁}^{h₂} U K /(M² U') dh`  (number of e-folds, `efolds`),
* `r = 16 ε`                                              (`tensorToScalar`).

All derivatives are genuine `deriv`s; we compute them in closed form:

* `ε = 8 M² / (h² A)`, `A = 1 + ξ(1+6ξ) h²/M²`            (`epsilonSR_eq`),
* `η = 12 M²/(h² A) − 4ξ/A − 4 ξ(1+6ξ) Ω²/A²`             (`etaSR_eq`),
* `N(h₁,h₂) = F(h₂) − F(h₁)`, `F(h) = (1+6ξ)h²/(8M²) − ¾ log(1 + ξh²/M²)` (`efolds_eq`).

Main results:

* `tensorToScalar_le`: `r ≤ 12/N² + 2/(ξ N²)` whenever the field value `h` lies at least
  `N` e-folds before any other field value (in particular before the end of inflation);
* `tensorToScalar_lt_planck`: for `ξ ≥ 1/50` and `N ≥ 60`, `r < 0.036` (Planck/BICEP bound);
* `tensorToScalar_lt_planck_fifty`: for `ξ ≥ 1/25` and `N ≥ 50`, `r < 0.036`;
* `abs_etaSR_le`, `epsilonSR_le`: both slow-roll parameters are small (`≪ 1`);
* `conformal_no_inflation`: for the *conformal* value `ξ = −1/6` there is no slow roll at
  all: `ε(h) > 1` on the whole physical domain `0 < h² < 6 M²`.
-/
/-- Conformal factor `Ω² = 1 + ξ h²/M²` of the Weyl rescaling to the Einstein frame. -/
/-- Einstein-frame potential `U(h) = λ h⁴ / (4 Ω⁴)`. -/
/-- Einstein-frame field-space metric `K(h) = (dχ/dh)² = (Ω² + 6ξ²h²/M²)/Ω⁴`. -/
/-- First slow-roll parameter `ε = ½ M² (dU/dχ / U)² = ½ M² (U'/U)²/K`. -/
/-- Second slow-roll parameter `η = M² (d²U/dχ²)/U = M² (U'' − U'K'/(2K))/(K U)`. -/
/-- Tensor-to-scalar ratio `r = 16 ε`. -/

/-- Number of e-folds between field values `h₁` and `h₂`:
`N = ∫_{h₁}^{h₂} (U / (M² dU/dχ)) dχ = ∫_{h₁}^{h₂} U K / (M² U') dh`. -/
/-- Closed-form e-fold potential `F(h) = (1+6ξ) h²/(8M²) − ¾ log(1 + ξ h²/M²)`. -/
/-- The combination `A = Ω² + 6ξ²h²/M² = 1 + ξ(1+6ξ)h²/M²`. -/
/-- **Closed form of `ε`**: `ε(h) = 8 M² / (h² A(h))`, `A = 1 + ξ(1+6ξ)h²/M²`. -/

/-- **Closed form of `η`** (for `ξ ≥ 0`):
`η(h) = 12 M²/(h² A) − 4ξ/A − 4ξ(1+6ξ) Ω²/A²`. -/

/-- **Exact number of e-folds**: `N(h₁, h₂) = F(h₂) − F(h₁)` with
`F(h) = (1+6ξ)h²/(8M²) − ¾ log(1 + ξh²/M²)`. -/

/-- Pure algebra behind the `r` bound: if `(1+6ξ)s ≥ 8N`, then
`128 / (s (1 + ξ(1+6ξ)s)) ≤ 12/N² + 2/(ξN²)`. -/
/-- Pure algebra behind the `η` bound. -/
-- the three pieces
-- bounds

/-- **Tensor-to-scalar ratio bound.** If the field value `h` at horizon exit lies at least
`N > 0` e-folds before some field value `hEnd` (e.g. the end of inflation), then

/-- **Planck/BICEP constraint `r < 0.036`** for `ξ ≥ 1/50` and at least 60 e-folds. -/

/-!
# Diagonal (multiplication) operators on `ℓ²`

For an index set `ι` and a family of complex numbers `μ : ι → ℂ` we construct the (generally
unbounded) diagonal operator `diagOp μ` on the Hilbert space `ℓ²(ι)`, with its maximal domain
`{f | (μ i * f i)ᵢ ∈ ℓ²}`, and prove:

* every basis vector `e_i` is an eigenvector with eigenvalue `μ i`;
* the eigenvalues (point spectrum) are exactly the values `μ i`;
* `diagOp μ` is self-adjoint (as an unbounded operator, `T† = T` including domains)
  if and only if every `μ i` is real.
-/
/-- The Hilbert space `ℓ²(ι; ℂ)`. -/
/-- Maximal domain of the diagonal operator with entries `μ`. -/

/-- The diagonal operator `(T f) i = μ i * f i`, as a partially defined linear operator on
`ℓ²(ι)` with its maximal domain. -/
/-- The finitely supported vectors lie in the domain, so the domain is dense. -/
/-- The basis vector `e_i` is an eigenvector of `diagOp μ` with eigenvalue `μ i`. -/

/-- `E` is an eigenvalue of a partially defined operator `T`: there is a nonzero vector in the
domain with `T x = E • x`. -/
/-- The eigenvalues of `diagOp μ` are exactly the entries `μ i`. -/

/-- **Self-adjointness criterion.** The diagonal operator (with its maximal domain) is
self-adjoint, `T† = T`, if and only if all of its diagonal entries are real. -/
-- symmetry on the domain
-- the adjoint's domain is contained in the domain

/-!
# `ζ` has no zeros on the real interval `(0, 1)`

We prove `riemannZeta σ ≠ 0` for real `0 < σ < 1` via the Dirichlet eta function
`η(s) = ∑_{k ≥ 0} ((2k+1)^{-s} - (2k+2)^{-s})`:

* the series defines a holomorphic function on `Re s > 0`;
* `η(s) = (1 - 2^{1-s}) ζ(s)` for `Re s > 1`, hence (identity theorem) on the slit
  half-plane `{Re s > 0} \ [1, ∞)`;
* for real `σ ∈ (0,1)` every term of `η(σ)` is positive, so `η(σ) ≠ 0`.
-/
/-- The paired terms of the Dirichlet eta series. -/
/-- The Dirichlet eta function (as a series, meaningful for `Re s > 0`). -/
/-- Mean value bound: `|a^{-s} - (a+1)^{-s}| ≤ |s| a^{-Re s - 1}` for `a ≥ 1`, `Re s > 0`. -/
/-- The slit half-plane `{Re s > 0} \ [1, ∞)`. -/
/-- The slit half-plane is star-shaped about `1/2`, hence connected. -/
/-- Identity theorem: `η(s) = (1 - 2^{1-s}) ζ(s)` on the whole slit half-plane. -/
/-- For real `σ > 0` every paired term of the eta series is positive, so `Re η(σ) > 0`. -/

/-!
# A Hilbert–Pólya Hamiltonian for the Riemann zeta function

We build the Hilbert space `ℓ²(Z)`, where `Z` is the set of nontrivial zeros of `ζ`, and the
(unbounded) diagonal Hamiltonian `H` with eigenvector `e_ρ` of eigenvalue `ρ (1 - ρ)`.

* `hamiltonian_isEigenvalue_iff` : the eigenvalues of `H` are exactly the numbers `ρ (1 - ρ)`.
* `spectralDet_eq_zero_iff` : the spectral determinant `Zeta_H(s) = det(H - s(1-s))` vanishes
  (i.e. `s (1 - s)` is an eigenvalue of `H`) exactly at the nontrivial zeros of `ζ`
  (this uses the functional equation `Λ(1 - s) = Λ(s)`).
* `spectralDet_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re` : by the Euler product, it does not vanish for `Re s > 1`.
* `hamiltonian_isSelfAdjoint_iff`, `eigenvalues_real_iff` : `H` is self-adjoint, equivalently
  all eigenvalues of `H` are real, iff every nontrivial zero lies on `Re s = 1/2` or on the
  real axis.
* `riemannHypothesis_iff_spectrum` : unconditionally, the Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to
  `H` being self-adjoint with spectrum bounded below by `1/4`.
* `riemannHypothesis_iff_eigenvalues_real` : the Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to all
  eigenvalues of `H` being real (equivalently, `H` being self-adjoint). This uses that `ζ` has
  no zeros on the real interval `(0,1)` (proved in `RealAxis.lean`), so that no nontrivial zero
  is real.
-/
/-- `s` is a nontrivial zero of `ζ` (the same convention as Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis`). -/
/-- The set of nontrivial zeros, used as the index set of the eigenbasis. -/
/-- The spectral parameter `E = s (1 - s)` (equal to `1/4 + t²` when `s = 1/2 + i t`). -/

/-- The Hilbert–Pólya Hamiltonian on `ℓ²(nontrivial zeros)`, with eigenvalue `ρ (1 - ρ)` on the
basis vector `e_ρ`, defined on its maximal domain. -/
/-- `Zeta_H(s) = det(H - s(1-s)) = 0`, i.e. `s (1 - s)` is an eigenvalue of `H`. -/
/-! ### Symmetry of the zeros under `s ↦ 1 - s` -/
/-! ### The spectral determinant reproduces the zeta zeros -/

/-- **The spectral determinant `det(H - s(1-s))` vanishes exactly at the nontrivial zeros
of `ζ`.** -/

/-- By the Euler product (`ζ(s) = ∏_p (1 - p^{-s})⁻¹ ≠ 0` for `Re s > 1`), the spectral
determinant has no zeros in the half-plane of absolute convergence. -/
/-! ### Reality of the spectrum and the critical line -/
/-- `s (1 - s)` is real iff `s` is real or `s` lies on the critical line. -/
/-- `s (1 - s)` is real and `≥ 1/4` iff `s` lies on the critical line. -/
/-- All eigenvalues of `H` are real iff every nontrivial zero is on the critical line or real. -/

/-- **Self-adjointness of the Hilbert–Pólya Hamiltonian.** `H` (on its maximal domain) is
self-adjoint iff every nontrivial zero is on the critical line or real. -/

/-- **Unconditional spectral form of the Riemann Hypothesis.** RH holds iff every eigenvalue
of `H` is real and at least `1/4`, i.e. `H` is self-adjoint with `H ≥ 1/4` on its eigenbasis. -/

/-- No nontrivial zero is real (since `ζ` has no zeros on `(0,1)` and the nontrivial zeros lie in
the open strip `0 < Re s < 1`). -/

/-- **Hilbert–Pólya criterion.** The Riemann Hypothesis holds iff all eigenvalues of the
Hamiltonian `H` are real, i.e. iff the spectral determinant `det(H - s(1-s))` vanishes only at
real values of the spectral parameter `s(1-s)`. -/
/-- Same, phrased with self-adjointness. -/

/-- **Main theorem (spectral-determinant form).** The Riemann Hypothesis holds iff at every zero
`s` of the spectral determinant `Zeta_H(s) = det(H - s(1-s))` the corresponding eigenvalue
`s(1-s)` of `H` is real. -/

/-!
# `RequestProject.HilbertPolya`

Hilbert-Pólya spectral interpretation connecting acoustic/quantum wave resonances to
the distribution of prime numbers and the Riemann hypothesis.
-/

/-!
# The Poincaré ball of curvature `-c`

Hyperbolic neural networks usually work in the Poincaré ball
`𝔻_c = {x | c ‖x‖² < 1}` of curvature `-c` (`c > 0`), with

* `x ⊕_c y = ((1 + 2c⟪x,y⟫ + c‖y‖²) x + (1 - c‖x‖²) y) / (1 + 2c⟪x,y⟫ + c²‖x‖²‖y‖²)`,
* `r ⊗_c x = tanh (r artanh (√c ‖x‖)) x / (√c ‖x‖)`,
* `d_c(x,y) = (2/√c) artanh (√c ‖(-x) ⊕_c y‖)`,
* `λ^c_x = 2 / (1 - c‖x‖²)`,
* `exp^c_x v = x ⊕_c tanh (√c λ^c_x ‖v‖ / 2) v / (√c ‖v‖)`,
* `log^c_x y = 2/(√c λ^c_x) artanh (√c ‖(-x) ⊕_c y‖) ((-x) ⊕_c y) / ‖(-x) ⊕_c y‖`.

We show that all these operations are conjugate, through the dilation `x ↦ √c x`, to the
curvature `-1` operations studied in the other files. As a consequence all the results
(closure, left cancellation, triangle inequality, the `cosh` distance formula, the
exp/log inverse relations and `d_c(x, exp^c_x v) = λ^c_x ‖v‖`) hold in every curvature.
When `c = 0`, Möbius addition degenerates to vector addition.
-/
/-- Möbius addition in the Poincaré ball of curvature `-c`. -/
/-- Möbius scalar multiplication in the Poincaré ball of curvature `-c`. -/
/-- The hyperbolic distance in the Poincaré ball of curvature `-c`. -/
/-- The conformal factor `λ^c_x = 2 / (1 - c‖x‖²)`. -/
/-- The exponential map at `x` in the Poincaré ball of curvature `-c`. -/
/-- The logarithmic map at `x` in the Poincaré ball of curvature `-c`. -/
/-- In the flat limit `c = 0`, Möbius addition is ordinary vector addition. -/
/-- Möbius addition of curvature `-c` is conjugate to that of curvature `-1`. -/
/-- The ball `√c ‖x‖ < 1` is closed under `⊕_c`. -/
/-- Left cancellation law in curvature `-c`. -/
/-- Möbius scalar multiplication of curvature `-c` is conjugate to that of curvature `-1`. -/
/-- The distance of curvature `-c` is a rescaling of the curvature `-1` distance. -/
/-- Closed formula `cosh (√c d_c(x,y)) = 1 + 2c‖x - y‖² / ((1 - c‖x‖²)(1 - c‖y‖²))`. -/
/-- Triangle inequality in curvature `-c`. -/
/-- The exponential map of curvature `-c` is conjugate to the curvature `-1` one. -/
/-- The logarithmic map of curvature `-c` is conjugate to the curvature `-1` one. -/
/-- `exp^c_x ∘ log^c_x = id` on the ball of curvature `-c`. -/
/-- `log^c_x ∘ exp^c_x = id` on the tangent space. -/
/-- `d_c(x, exp^c_x v) = λ^c_x ‖v‖`. -/

/-!
# Einstein addition and the Klein gyrogroup

Einstein velocity addition on the Klein ball, written with `γ_u = 1/√(1 - ‖u‖²)`:
`u ⊕_E v = (u + v/γ_u + γ_u/(1+γ_u) ⟪u,v⟫ u) / (1 + ⟪u,v⟫)`.

Main results:
* `poincareToKlein_mobiusAdd`: the doubling map `x ↦ 2x/(1+‖x‖²)` is an isomorphism from
  Möbius addition to Einstein addition, `2⊗(x ⊕_M y) = (2⊗x) ⊕_E (2⊗y)`;
* the Klein ball is closed under `⊕_E`, and `⊖u ⊕_E (u ⊕_E v) = v`;
* the Klein distance is the Einstein gyrodistance `d_K(u,v) = artanh ‖⊖u ⊕_E v‖`;
* `KleinBall E` is a gyrocommutative gyrogroup under Einstein addition, and the isometry
  `KleinBall E ≃ᵢ PoincareBall E` is a gyrogroup isomorphism.
-/
/-- Einstein addition `u ⊕_E v = (u + √(1-‖u‖²) v + ⟪u,v⟫/(1 + √(1-‖u‖²)) u) / (1 + ⟪u,v⟫)`. -/
/-- **Möbius and Einstein addition are isomorphic** via `x ↦ 2x/(1+‖x‖²) = 2 ⊗ x`. -/
/-- Einstein addition, transported from Möbius addition. -/
/-- The Klein ball is closed under Einstein addition. -/
/-- Left cancellation for Einstein addition: `⊖u ⊕_E (u ⊕_E v) = v`. -/
/-- `artanh ‖2 ⊗ z‖ = 2 artanh ‖z‖`. -/
/-- **The Klein distance is the Einstein gyrodistance**: `d_K(u, v) = artanh ‖⊖u ⊕_E v‖`. -/
/-! ### The Einstein gyrogroup structure on the Klein ball -/
/-- The Klein-to-Poincaré isometry, as a map. -/
/-- Einstein addition on `KleinBall E`. -/
/-- Negation on `KleinBall E`. -/
/-- The origin of `KleinBall E`. -/
/-- Einstein gyration, transported from the Möbius gyration. -/
/-- The Einstein gyrogroup structure on the Klein ball. -/
/-- The isometry `KleinBall E ≃ᵢ PoincareBall E` is a gyrogroup isomorphism. -/
/-- In gyrogroup notation, `d_K(a, b) = artanh ‖⊖a ⊕_E b‖`. -/
/-- Left Einstein gyrotranslations are isometries of the Klein model. -/

/-!
# The Einstein midpoint and its relation with the Lorentzian centroid

Hyperbolic attention mechanisms aggregate points `u_i` of the Klein ball with weights
`ν_i ≥ 0` by the (weighted) *Einstein midpoint*
`m = Σ ν_i γ(u_i) u_i / Σ ν_i γ(u_i)`, where `γ(u) = 1 / √(1 - ‖u‖²)` is the Lorentz factor.

Main results:
* `norm_einsteinMidpoint_lt_one`: the Einstein midpoint lies in the Klein ball;
* `lorentzFactor_toKlein`: for `p` on the hyperboloid, `γ(p⃗ / p₀) = p₀`;
* `toKlein_lorentzCentroid`: the gnomonic projection of the Lorentzian centroid of points
  `x_i ∈ ℍ` is the Einstein midpoint of their projections, with the same weights.
  So the two aggregation schemes coincide under the isometry `ℍ ≃ 𝕂`.
-/
/-- The Lorentz factor `γ(u) = 1 / √(1 - ‖u‖²)`. -/
/-- The weighted Einstein midpoint `m = Σ ν_i γ(u_i) u_i / Σ ν_i γ(u_i)`. -/
/-- The Einstein midpoint of points of the Klein ball lies in the Klein ball. -/
/-- For `p` on the hyperboloid, the Lorentz factor of its gnomonic projection is `p₀`. -/
/-- `γ(p⃗/p₀) · (p⃗/p₀) = p⃗` on the hyperboloid. -/

/-- **Lorentzian centroid = Einstein midpoint.** The gnomonic projection of the Lorentzian
centroid of `x_i ∈ ℍ` (weights `ν_i`) is the Einstein midpoint of the projected points with
the same weights. -/

/-!
# Gyrolines are geodesics of the Poincaré ball

For points `x, y` of the Poincaré ball, the *gyroline* through `x` and `y` is
`t ↦ x ⊕ (t ⊗ (⊖x ⊕ y))`. It passes through `x` at `t = 0` and through `y` at `t = 1`.

Main results:
* `poincareDist_gyroline`: `d(γ(s), γ(t)) = |t - s| · d(x, y)`, i.e. the gyroline is a
  constant-speed geodesic (a scaled isometric embedding of `ℝ`);
* `poincareDist_gyroline_add`: points on the gyrosegment realise equality in the triangle
  inequality, `d(x, γ(t)) + d(γ(t), y) = d(x, y)` for `t ∈ [0, 1]`;
* the gyromidpoint `x ⊕ (½ ⊗ (⊖x ⊕ y))` is equidistant from `x` and `y`, at distance
  `d(x,y)/2`.
-/
/-- The gyroline through `x` and `y`: `γ(t) = x ⊕ (t ⊗ (⊖x ⊕ y))`. -/
/-- Distance between two Möbius multiples of the same vector. -/
/-- **Gyrolines are constant-speed geodesics**: `d(γ(s), γ(t)) = |t - s| · d(x, y)`. -/
/-- Points of the gyrosegment realise equality in the triangle inequality. -/
/-- The gyromidpoint `x ⊕ (½ ⊗ (⊖x ⊕ y))`. -/
