/-!
# The finite spectral triple of the Pati–Salam model

This file extends `RequestProject.NCGSMTriple` (the finite spectral triple of the
Noncommutative Standard Model) to the Pati–Salam gauge group
`G_PS = SU(4) × SU(2)_L × SU(2)_R`.

* **The algebra.** The classification of finite irreducible geometries leads to the algebra
  `M₂(ℍ) ⊕ M₄(ℂ)`. The grading condition `[γ, π(a)] = 0` reduces `M₂(ℍ)` to its diagonal part
  `ℍ_R ⊕ ℍ_L` (`M2H_commute_grading_iff`), so the algebra acting on the finite Hilbert space is
  `A_PS = ℍ_R ⊕ ℍ_L ⊕ M₄(ℂ)` (`APS`). Its unitary group gives `SU(2)_R × SU(2)_L × U(4)`.
* **The representation.** On the same `32N`-dimensional space `H_F` as the Standard Model,
  `ℍ_R` and `ℍ_L` act on the right- and left-handed isospin doublets of particles, and `M₄(ℂ)`
  acts on the colour index of antiparticles. Here leptons are the fourth colour, since the
  colour index of `H_F` is `Col = Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3` (`repPS`).
* **The Standard Model inside Pati–Salam.** `smToPS : A_SM → A_PS`,
  `(λ, q, m) ↦ (λ, q, diag(λ, m))`, is an injective `*`-homomorphism, and
  `π_PS ∘ smToPS = π_SM` (`repPS_smToPS`).
* **The triple.** With the Dirac operator `D_F`, the grading `γ_F` and the real structure
  `J_F` of the Standard Model, `(A_PS, H_F, D_F, J_F, γ_F)` satisfies every axiom of a real even
  spectral triple of KO-dimension `6` except the first-order condition (`psFiniteTriple`).
* **Symmetry breaking through the Dirac operator.** Assume the Majorana mass `Y_R` is nonzero
  and the Yukawa couplings satisfy the Pati–Salam relations `Y_ν = Y_u`, `Y_e = Y_d`. Then
  `a ∈ A_PS` satisfies the first-order condition against every `b ∈ A_PS` exactly when `a` lies
  in the Standard Model subalgebra (`ps_firstOrder_iff_mem_SM`). So the first-order condition
  of the Majorana part of `D_F` breaks `A_PS` to `A_SM = ℂ ⊕ ℍ ⊕ M₃(ℂ)`. The full Pati–Salam
  triple violates the first-order condition (`psFiniteTriple_not_firstOrder`). On `A_SM` it
  holds (`ps_firstOrder_on_SM`).
* **Inner fluctuations.** Inner fluctuations `D ↦ D + A + J A J⁻¹` with
  `A = Σ π(aᵢ)[D, π(bᵢ)]` built from Standard Model elements leave the Majorana block
  `M = majo Y_R` unchanged (`innerFluct_SM_majorana`). Pati–Salam fluctuations produce a
  rescaled Majorana block (`innerFluct_PS_majorana`). The Majorana entry is
  therefore a dynamical field, the Pati–Salam scalar `Σ`, only in the Pati–Salam model. Its
  vacuum value `Y_R ≠ 0` is what breaks `A_PS` to `A_SM`.
-/
/-! ## The algebra `M₂(ℍ) ⊕ M₄(ℂ)` and the grading condition -/
/-- The grading of `ℍ² = ℍ_R ⊕ ℍ_L`, `diag(1, -1)`. -/

/-- **The grading condition reduces `M₂(ℍ)` to `ℍ_R ⊕ ℍ_L`.** An element `X ∈ M₂(ℍ)` commutes
with the grading `diag(1, -1)` exactly when it is diagonal. This is why the part of
`M₂(ℍ) ⊕ M₄(ℂ)` that commutes with `γ` is `ℍ_R ⊕ ℍ_L ⊕ M₄(ℂ)`. -/

/-- **The Pati–Salam algebra** `A_PS = ℍ_R ⊕ ℍ_L ⊕ M₄(ℂ)`, the even part of `M₂(ℍ) ⊕ M₄(ℂ)`.
An element is written `(q_R, q_L, m)`. `M₄(ℂ)` acts on the four "colours"
`Col = Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3`, where lepton number is the fourth colour. -/
/-- The embedding `ℍ_R ⊕ ℍ_L ↪ M₂(ℍ)`, `(q_R, q_L) ↦ diag(q_R, q_L)`. -/
/-- The image of `ℍ_R ⊕ ℍ_L` in `M₂(ℍ)` is exactly the commutant of the grading. -/
/-! ## The representation of `A_PS` on `H_F` -/
/-- `q_R ∈ ℍ_R` acting on right-handed isospin. -/
/-- `q_L ∈ ℍ_L` acting on left-handed isospin. -/
/-- `m ∈ M₄(ℂ)` acting on the four colours (lepton number as the fourth colour). -/
/-- `A_PS` acting on particles: `q_R` on right-handed and `q_L` on left-handed isospin. -/
/-- `A_PS` acting on antiparticles: `m ∈ M₄(ℂ)` on the colour index. -/

/-- **The representation `π_PS : A_PS → B(H_F)`** of the Pati–Salam algebra on the
`32N`-dimensional finite Hilbert space of the Standard Model. -/
/-! ## The Standard Model subalgebra -/
/-- `ℂ ↪ ℍ`, `a + b i ↦ a + b i + 0 j + 0 k`, as a real `*`-homomorphism. -/

/-- **The Standard Model algebra inside the Pati–Salam algebra**:
`A_SM = ℂ ⊕ ℍ ⊕ M₃(ℂ) → A_PS`, `(λ, q, m) ↦ (λ, q, diag(λ, m))`. Here `λ ∈ ℂ ⊂ ℍ_R`, and
`diag(λ, m) ∈ M₄(ℂ)` acts as `λ` on leptons and as `m` on the three quark colours. -/
/-- **`π_PS` restricts to `π_SM`**: `π_PS(smToPS x) = π_SM(x)` for all `x ∈ A_SM`. -/
/-- `smToPS` is injective, so `A_SM` is a subalgebra of `A_PS`. -/
/-! ## The finite Pati–Salam triple (without first-order condition) -/

/-- **A finite real even pre-spectral triple of KO-dimension 6**: all axioms of
`KO6Triple` except the first-order condition. The Pati–Salam triple is of this kind. -/
/-- The `*`-representation of `A` on `H = ℂⁿ`. -/
/-- The finite Dirac operator. -/
/-- The grading. -/
/-- The unitary part of the real structure `J = U ∘ K`. -/
/-- Order-zero condition `[a, J b J⁻¹] = 0`. -/
/-- The first-order condition `[[D, a], J b J⁻¹] = 0` for a pair `(a, b)`. -/
/-- The first-order condition for all pairs. -/
/-- The one-form `A = Σᵢ π(aᵢ)[D, π(bᵢ)]` of an inner fluctuation. -/
/-- **The inner fluctuation** `D_A = D + A + J A J⁻¹` of the Dirac operator. -/
/-- Every `KO6Triple` is a pre-triple that satisfies the first-order condition. -/

/-- **The finite Pati–Salam triple** `(A_PS, H_F, D_F, J_F, γ_F)`. For every Yukawa datum `Y`
(with symmetric Majorana matrix), `A_PS = ℍ_R ⊕ ℍ_L ⊕ M₄(ℂ)` acts on `H_F = ℂ^{32N}` through
`repPS`. With the Dirac operator, grading and real structure of the Standard Model, every
axiom of a real even spectral triple of KO-dimension `6` holds except the first-order
condition: the Dirac operator is self-adjoint, `γ² = 1`, `[γ, π(a)] = 0`, `γD = -Dγ`,
`J² = 1`, `JD = DJ`, `Jγ = -γJ`, and the order-zero condition holds. -/
/-! ## Symmetry breaking by the first-order condition -/

/-- The first-order condition holds on the Standard Model subalgebra: for `a, b ∈ A_SM`,
`[[D_F, π_PS(a)], J_F π_PS(b) J_F⁻¹] = 0`. -/

/-!
# A lower bound on the right-handed gauge boson mass from `ΔF = 2` meson mixing

After the breaking `SU(2)_R × U(1)_{B-L} → U(1)_Y`, the Pati–Salam model has a heavy
right-handed charged gauge boson `W_R`. Box diagrams with one `W_L` and one `W_R` exchange give
a left–right contribution to `K⁰–K̄⁰` mixing (`ΔS = 2`). This contribution is chirally
enhanced through the operator `Q_LR = (s̄_R d_L)(s̄_L d_R)`.

**The model used here.** We take the heavy-`W_R`, charm-dominated form of the left–right box
amplitude relative to the Standard Model `W_L W_L` charm box:

`|M₁₂^LR / M₁₂^SM| = 8 (g_R/g_L)² (M_W/M_{W_R})² R_χ η |1 + ln x_c|`,  `x_c = m_c²/M_W²`.

Here `R_χ = |⟨K̄|Q_LR|K⟩| / |⟨K̄|Q_LL|K⟩|` is the ratio of hadronic matrix elements and `η` the
ratio of QCD correction factors `η_LR/η_cc`. The `ΔF = 2` constraint requires this ratio to be
at most `κ`, the fraction of `M₁₂^SM` that new physics may contribute (`DeltaF2Constraint`).

* `MWR_lower_bound_general`: for any inputs,
  `M_{W_R} ≥ M_W √(8 R_χ η |1 + ln x_c| / κ)` when `g_R = g_L`.
* `MWR_gt_4800`: with the inputs recorded in `KaonMixingInputs`
  (`80.3 ≤ M_W ≤ 80.5 GeV`, `1.2 ≤ m_c ≤ 1.4 GeV`, `R_χ ≥ 16`, `η ≥ 1.4`, `κ ≤ 1/3`) and
  `g_R = g_L`, the constraint forces `M_{W_R} > 4800 GeV = 4.8 TeV`.
* `ps_MWR_gt_4800`: the equality `g_R = g_L` is not assumed here. It is the Pati–Salam
  spectral unification condition (`ps_gauge_unification_pos`), so the bound holds for every
  canonically normalised Pati–Salam spectral action.
* `MWR_bound_needs_inputs`: the numerical value depends on these inputs. With the older inputs
  `R_χ = 7.7`, `η = 1`, `κ = 1`, a `W_R` of mass `2 TeV` satisfies the constraint.

The numbers in `KaonMixingInputs` are modelling assumptions that we chose. They are not
derived in Lean: the hadronic ratio and the QCD factors are external inputs, and the value
`4.8 TeV` holds under exactly these assumptions.
-/

/-- **Inputs for `K⁰–K̄⁰` mixing** (masses in GeV).
* `MW`: the `W_L` mass, `80.3 ≤ M_W ≤ 80.5`.
* `mc`: the charm quark mass, `1.2 ≤ m_c ≤ 1.4`.
* `Rchi`: the hadronic ratio `|⟨K̄|Q_LR|K⟩| / |⟨K̄|Q_LL|K⟩| ≥ 16`.
* `eta`: the ratio of QCD correction factors `η_LR/η_cc ≥ 1.4`.
* `kappa`: the largest allowed `|M₁₂^LR / M₁₂^SM|`, with `0 < κ ≤ 1/3`. -/

/-- **The left–right to Standard Model ratio of `K⁰–K̄⁰` mixing amplitudes**
`|M₁₂^LR / M₁₂^SM| = 8 (g_R/g_L)² (M_W/M_{W_R})² R_χ η |1 + ln(m_c²/M_W²)|`
(heavy `W_R`, charm dominance). -/

/-- **The `ΔF = 2` constraint**: the left–right contribution is at most the fraction `κ` of the
Standard Model amplitude. -/

/-- **General lower bound.** If `g_R = g_L ≠ 0`, `M_{W_R} > 0`, `κ > 0` and the `ΔF = 2`
constraint holds, then `M_{W_R}² ≥ M_W² · 8 R_χ η |1 + ln x_c| / κ`. -/

/-- **General lower bound, square-root form**:
`M_{W_R} ≥ M_W √(8 R_χ η |1 + ln x_c| / κ)` for `g_R = g_L`. -/
/-- For the inputs of `KaonMixingInputs`, `ln x_c = ln(m_c²/M_W²) < -8`. -/
/-- For the inputs of `KaonMixingInputs`, `|1 + ln x_c| ≥ 7`. -/

/-- **`M_{W_R} > 4.8 TeV` from `K⁰–K̄⁰` mixing.** Take the inputs of `KaonMixingInputs` and
equal left and right gauge couplings `g_R = g_L ≠ 0`. If the left–right box contribution is
at most `κ` times the Standard Model amplitude, then `M_{W_R} > 4800 GeV`. -/

/-- **`M_{W_R} > 4.8 TeV` in the Pati–Salam spectral model.** The Pati–Salam spectral action
is canonically normalised at `Λ_GUT` (`PSCanonicalGauge`), which gives `g_R = g_L`
(`ps_gauge_unification_pos`). With the inputs of `KaonMixingInputs`, the `ΔF = 2` constraint
then forces `M_{W_R} > 4800 GeV`. -/
/-- For central values `m_c = 1.3`, `M_W = 80.4`: `-9 < ln x_c < -1`. -/

/-- The hypotheses of `MWR_gt_4800` can be met: for the central inputs
(`M_W = 80.4`, `m_c = 1.3`, `R_χ = 16`, `η = 1.4`, `κ = 1/3`) and `g_L = g_R = 0.65`, a `W_R`
of mass `10 TeV` satisfies the `ΔF = 2` constraint. -/

/-- **The numerical bound depends on the inputs.** With the older inputs `R_χ = 7.7`
(vacuum insertion with heavier strange quark), `η = 1` and `κ = 1`, and `M_W = 80.4`,
`m_c = 1.3`, `g_L = g_R`, a `W_R` of mass `2 TeV` satisfies the `ΔF = 2` constraint. So
`M_{W_R} > 4.8 TeV` is not a consequence of the constraint alone: it rests on the inputs
`R_χ ≥ 16`, `η ≥ 1.4`, `κ ≤ 1/3` of `KaonMixingInputs`. -/

/-!
# Baryon number conservation and proton stability in the Noncommutative Standard Model

1. **Exact `U(1)_B` symmetry of the spectral model.** Let `U_u` act on `H_F` by the phase `u` on
   quarks, `ū` on antiquarks and `1` on leptons (`baryonPhase`). For every unit complex number
   `u`, every choice of Yukawa and Majorana couplings and every inner fluctuation
   `A = Σ π(a)[D_F, π(b)]`:
   * `U_u` commutes with `π(A_F)`, with `D_F` and with the fluctuated Dirac operator
     `D_A = D_F + A + J A J⁻¹` (`baryonPhase_commute_fluctuated`);
   * `U_u` is unitary and commutes with the real structure `J_F`;
   * the fermionic action `⟨Jψ, D_A ψ⟩` is invariant under `ψ ↦ U_u ψ`
     (`fermionAction_baryon_invariant`).
2. **Selection rule.** Every operator commuting with `U_i` has no matrix element between states
   of different baryon number (`baryon_selection_rule`). In particular `D_A` never changes
   baryon number (`fluctuated_dirac_conserves_baryon`), so the spectral model has no
   baryon-number-violating interaction of any mass dimension: its tree-level proton decay rate
   is `0` and the proton lifetime is infinite (`spectral_proton_lifetime`), above the
   Super-Kamiokande bound `τ(p → e⁺π⁰) > 10³⁴` years.
3. **No dimension-5 proton decay operators.** Consider effective operators built from the NCG
   field content (the fermions of `H_F`, the Higgs doublet, gauge field strengths and covariant
   derivatives). Every such operator of mass dimension `≤ 5` that satisfies the necessary
   conditions for gauge and Lorentz invariance (colour triality zero, even number of fermions)
   conserves baryon number (`dim5_conserves_baryon`). The bound is sharp: the dimension-6
   operator `QQQL` is admissible and has `B = 1` (`dim6_QQQL_violates_baryon`). The Weinberg
   operator `LLHH` shows that dimension 5 does allow `ΔL = 2` (`weinberg_operator`).
4. **Lifetime estimate.** Suppose dimension-6 operators are generated at a scale `M` with
   coupling `α_U`. The standard estimate is `τ_p ≈ M⁴/(α_U² m_p⁵)`. For `M ≥ 10¹⁶ GeV` and
   `α_U ≤ 1/25` it gives `τ_p > 10³⁴` years (`lifetime_estimate_gt`). At the scale where the
   spectral relation `sin²θ_W = 3/8` actually holds under one-loop running (`10¹²–10¹⁴ GeV`,
   `NCG.GaugeRunning.sin2W_three_eighths_scale`), the same estimate with `α_U ≥ 1/100` gives
   `τ_p < 10³⁴` years (`lifetime_estimate_at_spectral_scale_lt`). So the Super-Kamiokande
   bound is met because baryon number is exactly conserved (item 1), not because the
   unification scale is high.
-/
/-! ## The baryon-number phase on `H_F` -/

/-- **The baryon-number phase** `U_u = e^{iθB}` with `u = e^{iθ/3}`: the phase `u` on quarks
(baryon number `1/3`), `ū` on antiquarks (baryon number `-1/3`) and `1` on leptons. -/

/-- `U_u` commutes with the finite Dirac operator `D_F`, for all Yukawa and Majorana
couplings. -/
/-- `U_u` commutes with the representation `π` of `A_F`. -/
/-- `U_u` is unitary when `|u| = 1`. -/
/-- `U_u` commutes with the real structure `J_F = U_F ∘ K`: `U_F conj(U_u) = U_u U_F`. -/
/-- If `X` commutes with `U_u` then so does `J X J⁻¹ = U_F X̄ U_F`. -/
/-- **Inner fluctuation** `A = Σ_k π(a_k)[D_F, π(b_k)]` of the finite Dirac operator. -/
/-- **The fluctuated Dirac operator** `D_A = D_F + A + J A J⁻¹`, where `J A J⁻¹ = U_F Ā U_F`. -/

/-- **Exact `U(1)_B` symmetry of the fluctuated Dirac operator.** For all Yukawa and Majorana
couplings and every inner fluctuation, `D_A = D_F + A + J A J⁻¹` commutes with the baryon
phase `U_u`. -/

/-- **The fermionic action** `⟨Jψ, D ψ⟩` of the spectral model, with `J = U_F ∘ K` and
`⟨v, w⟩ = Σ v̄ᵢ wᵢ`. -/

/-- **The fermionic action is baryon-number invariant**: `⟨J U_u ψ, D_A U_u ψ⟩ = ⟨Jψ, D_A ψ⟩`
for every unit complex `u`, all couplings and every inner fluctuation. -/
/-! ## Selection rule and proton stability -/
/-- Baryon phase on the colour index: `1` on leptons, `u` on quarks. -/
/-- Baryon phase on particle states. -/
/-- The colour operator `diag(1, u·1)` is diagonal with entries `vPhase`. -/
/-- Diagonal entries of `U_u` on `H_F`: `u` on quarks, `ū` on antiquarks, `1` on leptons. -/
/-- `U_u` is the diagonal matrix `hfPhase`. -/
/-- Three times the baryon number on the colour index: `0` for leptons, `1` for quarks. -/

/-- **Three times the baryon number** of a basis state of `H_F`: `+1` for quarks, `-1` for
antiquarks, `0` for leptons and antileptons. -/
/-- For `u = i` the three values `1, i, -i` of the phase separate the three baryon numbers. -/

/-- **Baryon-number selection rule.** An operator on `H_F` that commutes with `U_i` has vanishing
matrix elements between basis states of different baryon number. -/

/-- **The fluctuated Dirac operator conserves baryon number.** For all Yukawa and Majorana
couplings and every inner fluctuation `A`, the matrix elements of `D_A = D_F + A + J A J⁻¹`
between states of different baryon number vanish. So the spectral model has no
baryon-number-violating vertex: no proton decay operator of any mass dimension, in particular
none of dimension 5 or 6. -/

/-- Total squared strength of the baryon-number-violating matrix elements of an operator,
`Σ_{B(i) ≠ B(j)} |X_ij|²`. A tree-level proton decay rate is proportional to it. -/
/-- The spectral model has zero baryon-number-violating strength. -/
/-- Lifetime `1/Γ ∈ [0, ∞]` of a decay rate `Γ` (in inverse years). -/

/-- **The proton is stable in the spectral model.** Take any decay rate proportional to the
baryon-number-violating strength of `D_A`, with any kinematic prefactor `κ` (in inverse years).
Its lifetime is infinite, so it exceeds `10³⁴` years, the Super-Kamiokande bound on
`p → e⁺π⁰`. This holds for all couplings and all inner fluctuations. -/
/-! ## Effective operators of dimension at most 5 -/

/-- **The field content of the NCG Standard Model** available for effective operators: the
sixteen left-handed Weyl fermions of `H_F` per generation (`Q, u^c, d^c, L, e^c, ν^c`), the
Higgs doublet `H` (the scalar inner fluctuation of `D_F`) and the gauge field strengths
`B, W, G` (the vector inner fluctuations). There are no other fields: in particular no
colour-triplet scalars. -/
/-- Whether the field is a fermion. -/
/-- Twice the mass dimension: `3` for fermions, `2` for `H`, `4` for field strengths. -/

/-- Colour triality (`N`-ality of `SU(3)`): `1` for the triplet `Q`, `2` for the antitriplets
`u^c, d^c`, `0` for colour singlets and for the adjoint `G`. -/
/-- Three times the baryon number. -/
/-- Lepton number. -/
/-- Hypercharge (convention `Q = T₃ + Y`), from `NCG.Anomaly.smY`. -/
/-- Triality equals baryon number modulo 3, field by field. -/
/-- Only fermions carry baryon number, at most `1/3` each. -/
/-- A fermion has mass dimension `3/2`. -/

/-- **A local operator** built from the NCG fields: a list of fields (each possibly conjugated)
and a number of covariant derivatives. -/
/-- Sign of a charge for a conjugated (`true`) or unconjugated (`false`) field. -/
/-- Twice the mass dimension of an operator. -/
/-- Total colour triality of an operator. -/
/-- Three times the baryon number of an operator. -/
/-- Lepton number of an operator. -/
/-- Total hypercharge of an operator. -/
/-- Number of fermion fields in an operator. -/

/-- **Necessary conditions for a gauge- and Lorentz-invariant operator**: an `SU(3)` singlet
has total triality `0`, and a Lorentz scalar contains an even number of fermion fields. -/

/-- **No dimension-5 proton decay operators.** Every operator of mass dimension `≤ 5` built from
the NCG field content and satisfying the necessary invariance conditions conserves baryon number.
It contains at most two fermions, so `|3B| ≤ 2`, and `3B ≡ triality ≡ 0 (mod 3)`. -/
/-- The dimension-6 operator `QQQL`. -/

/-- **The dimension bound is sharp**: `QQQL` is admissible, hypercharge neutral, of dimension 6,
and has `B = 1`, `L = 1`. -/
/-- The Weinberg operator `LLHH`. -/

/-- **Dimension 5 allows `ΔL = 2` but not `ΔB ≠ 0`**: the Weinberg operator is admissible,
hypercharge neutral, of dimension 5, with `B = 0` and `L = 2`. -/
/-! ## Proton lifetime estimates -/
/-- Proton mass in GeV. -/
/-- `ħ` in GeV·s. -/
/-- Seconds per (Julian) year. -/

/-- **Standard dimensional estimate of the proton lifetime** from dimension-6 operators
generated at scale `M` (GeV) with coupling `α_U`: `τ_p ≈ M⁴/(α_U² m_p⁵)`, converted to years. -/
/-- The estimate as `M⁴/α_U²` times a positive constant. -/
/-- **`τ_p > 10³⁴` years if `M ≥ 10¹⁶ GeV` and `α_U ≤ 1/25`.** -/
/-- **`τ_p < 10³⁴` years if `M ≤ 10¹⁴ GeV` and `α_U ≥ 1/100`.** -/

/-- **The naive estimate at the spectral scale is too short.** Let `Λ` be the scale where the
spectral relation `sin²θ_W = 3/8` (`α₁ = α₂`) holds under one-loop running from the measured
couplings. If dimension-6 operators were generated at `Λ` with `α_U ≥ 1/100`, then
`τ_p < 10³⁴` years. So the Super-Kamiokande bound is met in the spectral model only because
baryon number is exactly conserved (`NCG.spectral_proton_lifetime`). -/

comments.text:
/-!
# One-loop running of the gauge couplings of the finite spectral triple

The gauge group of the finite spectral triple `(A_F, H_F, D_F)` is (locally)
`U(1) × SU(2) × SU(3)`, and its fermion content is read off `H_F`:
the left-handed particle states `Fin 2 × W N` form `|W N| = 4N` isospin doublets
(`N` lepton doublets and `3N` quark doublets), and the quark states form `4N` colour
triplets (as left-handed Weyl fermions).  The Higgs field of the spectral action is one
complex isospin doublet.

The one-loop coefficient of a gauge group `G` is
`b = -11/3 C₂(G) + 2/3 Σ_{Weyl fermions} T(R) + 1/3 Σ_{complex scalars} T(R)`,
and the one-loop renormalization group equation for the coupling `g` at scale
`μ = μ₀ eᵗ` is `dg/dt = b g³ / (16 π²)`.

Main results:
* `b2_SM : b₂ = -19/6`, `b3_SM : b₃ = -7`, `b1_SM : b₁ = 41/10` (three generations);
  `b2_neg_iff : b₂ < 0 ↔ N ≤ 5`.
* `inv_sq_eq_of_rge` : every positive solution of the RGE satisfies
  `1/g(t)² = 1/g₀² - b t / (8π²)`.
* `asymptotic_freedom` : if `b < 0` the explicit solution exists for all `t ≥ 0`
  (no ultraviolet Landau pole), solves the RGE, decreases and tends to `0` as `t → ∞`.
* `no_landau_pole_of_neg` : if `b < 0` every positive solution on `[0, T)` stays below its
  initial value, whatever `T`.
* `landau_pole_of_pos` : if `b > 0` no positive solution can exist beyond
  `t* = 8π² / (b g₀²)`, and the explicit solution blows up at `t*`.  This applies to the
  hypercharge coupling (`b₁ = 41/10 > 0`), so the assertion "no Landau poles" holds for
  `SU(2)` and `SU(3)` but not for `U(1)`.
-/
/-- One-loop β-function coefficient: `-11/3 C₂(G) + 2/3 Σ_Weyl T(R) + 1/3 Σ_scalars T(R)`. -/

/-- `b₂` for `SU(2)` with the fermion content of `H_F` (`N` generations): `C₂(SU(2)) = 2`,
`|W N| = 4N` Weyl doublets of index `1/2`, one complex Higgs doublet of index `1/2`. -/

/-- `b₃` for `SU(3)`: `C₂(SU(3)) = 3`, `4N` Weyl triplets of index `1/2`
(one for each of the `4 N` isospin-chirality-generation labels `Fin 2 × Fin 2 × Fin N`
of the quark states in `H_F`), no coloured scalars. -/

/-- `b₁` for hypercharge in GUT normalization (`3/5` factor): per generation
`Σ_Weyl Y² = 10/3`, and the Higgs doublet contributes `2 · (1/2)² = 1/2`. -/
/-- **`b₂ = -19/6`** for the three-generation Standard Model. -/
/-- `b₃ = -7` for the three-generation Standard Model. -/
/-- `b₁ = 41/10` for the three-generation Standard Model. -/
/-- `b₂ < 0` for the Standard Model. -/

/-- `SU(2)` is asymptotically free at one loop exactly when there are at most five
generations. -/

/-- `SU(3)` is asymptotically free at one loop exactly when there are at most eight
generations. -/
/-! ### The one-loop renormalization group equation -/

/-- `g` solves the one-loop RGE `dg/dt = b g³/(16π²)` with `g > 0` on `[0, T)` and
`g 0 = g₀`. -/

/-- `g` solves the one-loop RGE with `g > 0` for all `t ≥ 0` (a global ultraviolet
solution: no Landau pole at any finite scale above `μ₀`). -/
/-- The explicit one-loop solution `g(t) = g₀ / √(1 - b g₀² t / (8π²))`. -/
/-- Every positive solution of the one-loop RGE has `1/g² = 1/g₀² - b t/(8π²)`. -/
/-- The explicit solution solves the RGE wherever `1 - b g₀² t/(8π²) > 0`. -/

/-- **Asymptotic freedom at one loop.** If `b < 0` and `g₀ > 0`, the one-loop solution
exists for all `t ≥ 0` (the denominator never vanishes: no ultraviolet Landau pole),
solves the RGE there, is positive, is antitone, and tends to `0` as `t → ∞`. -/

/-- **No Landau pole for `b < 0`.** Every positive solution of the one-loop RGE with
`b < 0`, on any interval `[0, T)`, is bounded by its initial value `g₀`. -/

/-- **Landau pole for `b > 0`.** If `b > 0`, no positive solution of the one-loop RGE
exists on `[0, T)` with `T > t* = 8π²/(b g₀²)`, and the explicit solution blows up as
`t → t*⁻`. -/

/-- **Asymptotic freedom of the `SU(2)` coupling of the finite spectral triple.**
With `b₂ = -19/6 < 0` (three generations), for every initial coupling `g₀ > 0` the one-loop
running coupling exists for all energies above the reference scale, solves the RGE, and
tends to zero in the ultraviolet; moreover every positive solution on any `[0, T)` is
bounded by `g₀`, so there is no ultraviolet Landau pole. -/

/-- The hypercharge coupling (`b₁ = 41/10 > 0`) does have a one-loop Landau pole:
no positive solution survives past `t* = 8π² / (b₁ g₀²)`. -/

/-!
# The finite spectral triple of the Standard Model is a KO-dimension 6 real spectral triple

We verify all axioms of `NCG.KO6Triple` for the data
`(A_F, H_F, D_F, J_F, γ_F) = (AF, HF N, DSM Y, USM N ∘ K, γSM N)`
for every number of generations `N` and every choice of Yukawa couplings `Y`.
-/
/-! ### Colour structure -/
/-- Every "isospin-diagonal, colour-blind" Yukawa matrix commutes with the colour action. -/
/-- The colour operator `diag(1 ⊗ (c ⊗ 1), 1 ⊗ (c ⊗ 1))` on particle space, `c = diag(x, y)`. -/
/-! ### Particle/colour commutation (order zero) -/
/-! ### The Majorana block -/
/-! ### Chirality -/
/-! ### Auxiliary identities -/

/-- The commutator `[D_F, π(a)]` only has a particle–particle block: the Majorana part of
`D_F` commutes with `A_F`, and so does the antiparticle Yukawa block. -/
/-! ### The main theorem -/

/-- **The finite spectral triple of the Noncommutative Standard Model.**
For every number `N` of generations and every choice of Yukawa couplings `Y`
(with symmetric Majorana mass matrix), the data
`(A_F = ℂ ⊕ ℍ ⊕ M₃(ℂ), H_F = ℂ^{32N}, D_F, J_F, γ_F)` form a real even finite spectral
triple of KO-dimension `6`: all of `D_F = D_F*`, `γ_F² = 1`, `[γ_F, π(a)] = 0`,
`γ_F D_F = -D_F γ_F`, `J_F² = 1`, `J_F D_F = D_F J_F`, `J_F γ_F = -γ_F J_F`, the order-zero
condition and the first-order condition hold. -/

/-- The representation of `A_F = ℂ ⊕ ℍ ⊕ M₃(ℂ)` on `H_F` is faithful (for at least one
generation), so the triple `smFiniteTriple` genuinely involves the whole algebra `A_F`. -/

/-- The "colour" index: `Fin 1` for leptons, `Fin 3` for the three quark colours. -/

/-- The lepton projection on the colour index. -/
/-- The quark projection on the colour index. -/

comments.text:
/-!
# Torsion and the spectral Dirac operator `D + T`

This file adds a torsion term `T` to the Dirac operator of a spectral triple (in particular of
the almost-commutative geometry `M × F` of the Noncommutative Standard Model, whose gauge
running is treated in `RequestProject.NCGRunning` / `RequestProject.NCGUnification`, and whose
spectral distance is treated in `RequestProject.SpectralDistanceFinite`).

On a spin manifold with a metric connection with torsion, the Dirac operator changes by a
term of order zero, `D ↦ D + T` with `T = (i/4)·T_{abc} γ^a γ^b γ^c` pointwise. The only
algebraic property of `T` used below is that **it commutes with the algebra** (it is a
multiplication operator on spinors that acts trivially on the finite space `F`, so it commutes
with `C^∞(M) ⊗ A_F`).

## 1. Gauge–gravity compatibility of `D + T` (abstract part)

For a torsion term `T` commuting with the algebra:
* the gauge one-forms (inner fluctuations) `A = Σ aᵢ [D, bᵢ]` of `D + T` are exactly those of
  `D` (`oneForm_add_torsion`): torsion creates no new gauge fields and removes none;
* the gauge transformation law is unchanged: for a unitary `u` of the algebra,
  `u (D + T + A) u* = D + T + A^u` with the *same* `A^u = u A u* + u [D, u*]` as for `D`
  (`gauge_covariance_add_torsion`), and `T` itself is gauge invariant;
* the first-order condition `[[D, a], b°] = 0` holds for `D + T` iff it holds for `D`
  (`firstOrder_add_torsion_iff`);
* the spectral distance of a finite spectral triple is unchanged by `T`
  (`FiniteSpectralTriple.dist_addTorsion`);
* the spectral action `Tr f(D + T)` (polynomial cutoff `f`) is invariant under diffeomorphisms,
  implemented by unitaries `U` acting covariantly on both `D` and `T`
  (`spectralAction_diffeo_invariant`).

These statements are what we mean by "`D + T` preserves the gauge–gravity duality": the
gauge sector obtained from inner fluctuations, and its gauge transformation law, are the same
for `D + T` as for `D`, while gravity (the unitary equivalence class of `D + T`) is acted on
covariantly.

## 2. Torsion-induced four-fermion contact interaction

At each point, with Minkowski product `η(v, w) = v⁰w⁰ − v¹w¹ − v²w² − v³w³`, the part of the
Einstein–Cartan–Dirac Lagrangian containing the axial torsion vector `t` is
`L(t) = −(4/(3κ)) η(t, t) + η(t, J)`, where `J_a = ψ̄ γ₅ γ_a ψ` is the axial fermion current
(the normalisation `4/(3κ)` of the quadratic term is the one obtained from the
Einstein–Cartan action restricted to the axial part of torsion). Torsion has no kinetic term,
so it is eliminated algebraically:
* `L` has a unique stationary point `t* = (3κ/8) J` (`torsion_variation_eq_zero_iff`);
* `L(t*) = (3κ/16) η(J, J)`: an effective **four-fermion contact interaction**
  (`torsion_effective_lagrangian`), homogeneous of degree `4` in the spinor `ψ`
  (`effective_fourFermion_homogeneous`);
* torsion is non-vanishing exactly when the axial current is (`torsionSol_ne_zero_iff`);
* everything is **local Lorentz covariant**: under any `η`-isometry `Λ`, `t*(ΛJ) = Λ t*(J)` and
  the effective interaction is a scalar (`effective_lorentz_invariant`). A pointwise
  (derivative-free) scalar built from tensors is invariant under diffeomorphisms, so the
  contact interaction does not break diffeomorphism invariance.

The totally antisymmetric torsion `T_{abc} = ε_{abcd} t^d` is a `2`-form in its last two indices
(`axialTorsion_antisymm`), and is recovered from its axial part (`axialTorsion_contract`).
-/
/-! ### 1. Abstract gauge–gravity compatibility -/
/-- The commutator `[x, y] = x y - y x`. -/

/-- **Gauge one-forms of a Dirac operator** (inner fluctuations): for a finite list of pairs
`(aᵢ, bᵢ)` of algebra elements, `A = Σᵢ aᵢ [D, bᵢ]`. -/
/-- A torsion term `T` *commutes with the algebra* `S` (a set of operators). -/

/-- **Torsion does not change the gauge fields.** If `T` commutes with the algebra, the inner
fluctuations `Σ aᵢ [D + T, bᵢ]` of `D + T` coincide with those of `D`. -/

/-- **Gauge covariance of `D + T`.** For a unitary `u` of the algebra (`u u* = u* u = 1`)
commuting with `T`, conjugating the fluctuated operator `D + T + A` by `u` gives
`D + T + A^u` with `A^u = u A u* + u [D, u*]`: exactly the gauge transformation law of the
gauge fields of `D` alone. -/
/-- The torsion term itself is gauge invariant: `u T u* = T`. -/

/-- **First-order condition.** If `T` commutes with `a`, the double commutator
`[[D + T, a], b']` equals `[[D, a], b']`; hence `D + T` satisfies the first-order condition
iff `D` does. -/
/-! ### Spectral action and diffeomorphism invariance -/
/-- The **spectral action** `Tr f(X)` of an operator `X` for a polynomial cutoff function `f`. -/
/-- The spectral action is invariant under unitary conjugation. -/

/-- **Diffeomorphism invariance of the spectral action with torsion.** A diffeomorphism is
implemented by a unitary `U`, acting covariantly on the Dirac operator and on the torsion
term, `D ↦ U D U*`, `T ↦ U T U*`. The spectral action `Tr f(D + T)` is invariant. -/
/-! ### Spectral distance is unchanged by torsion -/

/-- If `T` commutes with the represented algebra, the commutator seminorm of `D + T` equals
that of `D`. -/
/-- The finite spectral triple with Dirac operator `D + T`, for a self-adjoint torsion term. -/

/-- **Torsion does not change Connes' spectral distance**: if `T` commutes with the algebra,
`d_{D+T}(p, q) = d_D(p, q)` for all points. -/
/-! ### 2. Four-fermion contact interaction from torsion -/
/-- Minkowski inner product `η(v, w) = v⁰w⁰ − v¹w¹ − v²w² − v³w³`. -/
/-- `η` is non-degenerate. -/

/-- The **torsion Lagrangian** at a point: `L(t) = −(4/(3κ)) η(t, t) + η(t, J)`, for the axial
torsion vector `t`, the gravitational coupling `κ = 8πG` and the axial current `J`. -/
/-- The first variation `δL(t)[s]` of the torsion Lagrangian in the direction `s`. -/
/-- `torsionVariation` is the derivative of `L` along the line `t + ε s`. -/
/-- The solution of the torsion field equation: `t* = (3κ/8) J`. -/

/-- **The torsion field equation is algebraic**: the first variation of `L` vanishes in every
direction iff `t = (3κ/8) J`. -/
/-- Completing the square: `L(t* + s) = (3κ/16) η(J, J) − (4/(3κ)) η(s, s)`. -/
/-- The **effective four-fermion interaction** `L_eff(J) = (3κ/16) η(J, J)`. -/

/-- **Torsion induces a four-fermion contact interaction.** Substituting the solution of the
torsion field equation back into the Lagrangian gives `L(t*) = (3κ/16) η(J, J)`. -/
/-- The torsion is non-vanishing exactly when the axial current is non-vanishing. -/
/-- A linear map `Λ` is a **Lorentz transformation** if it preserves `η`. -/
/-- The torsion Lagrangian is a Lorentz scalar when `t` and `J` transform as vectors. -/

/-- **Local Lorentz covariance of the induced interaction.** The solution of the torsion field
equation transforms as a vector, `t*(ΛJ) = Λ t*(J)`, and the effective four-fermion interaction
is a Lorentz scalar. -/

/-- The **axial current** `J_a = Re(ψ† Γ_a ψ)` of a Dirac spinor `ψ` (at one point), for given
matrices `Γ_a` (in the Dirac representation `Γ_a = γ⁰ γ₅ γ_a`). -/

/-- **The induced interaction is a four-fermion term**: it is homogeneous of degree `4` in the
spinor, `L_eff(J(cψ)) = |c|⁴ L_eff(J(ψ))`. -/
/-! ### The torsion 2-form of the axial torsion -/
/-- The **Levi-Civita symbol** `ε_{abcd}` on `Fin 4`. -/

/-- The **totally antisymmetric torsion** determined by the axial torsion vector `t`:
`T_{abc} = ε_{abcd} t^d`. -/
/-- `T_{abc}` is antisymmetric in `b, c`: for each `a` it is a `2`-form `½ T^a_{bc} e^b ∧ e^c`. -/
/-- The axial vector is recovered from the torsion 2-form: `Σ_{abc} ε_{abcd} T_{abc} = 6 t_d`. -/
/-- Non-vanishing axial torsion vector gives a non-vanishing torsion 2-form. -/

/-!
# Gauge coupling unification in the Noncommutative Standard Model

This file combines the spectral-action boundary condition of
`RequestProject.SpectralActionSMMasses` (`gauge_unification`: `g₃² = g₂² = (5/3) g'²` at the
cutoff scale `Λ`) with the renormalization group running of `RequestProject.NCG.GaugeBeta`.

* **`sin²θ_W = 3/8` at the spectral scale** (`spectral_sin2W_three_eighths`). In GUT
  normalisation (`α₁ = (5/3) α'`) the spectral action forces `α₁ = α₂ = α₃` at `Λ`, and
  `sin²θ_W = 3/8` holds exactly there. The normalisation `5/3` is the ratio of the hypercharge
  and isospin traces over one generation. This is checked independently on the `16 ⊂ 27` of
  `E₆` from `RequestProject.NCG.E6StandardModel`: `Σ Y² = 10/3`, `Σ T₃² = Σ (λ₃/2)² = 2`
  (`rep16_trace_normalisation`).
* `sin²θ_W = 3/8` holds exactly when `α₁ = α₂` (`sin2W_eq_three_eighths_iff`).
* **Where the relation holds, given measured couplings.** Run the couplings at one loop, with
  the NCG Standard Model coefficients `(41/10, -19/6, -7)`, from inputs at `M_Z` that contain
  the measured values:
  - `α₁ = α₂`, equivalently `sin²θ_W = 3/8`, occurs only at a scale between `10¹²` and
    `10¹⁴ GeV` (`sin2W_three_eighths_scale`);
  - `α₂ = α₃` occurs only between `10¹⁶` and `10¹⁸ GeV` (`alpha2_alpha3_crossing_scale`);
  - so the three couplings never meet at a single scale (`no_one_loop_unification`);
  - at `μ = 10¹⁶ GeV`, `sin²θ_W > 3/8` strictly (`sin2W_at_1e16_gt`).

  So the claim "`sin²θ_W = 3/8` at `Λ_GUT ≈ 10¹⁶ GeV`" does not hold under one-loop running
  of the Standard Model couplings. What is proved is that the relation holds exactly at the
  scale `Λ` where the spectral boundary condition is imposed, and that this scale lies between
  `10¹²` and `10¹⁴ GeV`.
-/
/-! ## The weak mixing angle -/

/-- The weak mixing angle in terms of the GUT-normalised fine-structure constants `α₁, α₂`:
`sin²θ_W = g'²/(g'² + g²)`, with `g'² = (3/5) g₁²`. -/
/-- `sin²θ_W = 3/8` exactly when `α₁ = α₂`. -/
/-- `sin²θ_W > 3/8` exactly when `α₁ > α₂`. -/
/-! ## The spectral boundary condition -/

/-- **`sin²θ_W = 3/8` at the spectral scale.** Suppose the Yang–Mills term of the spectral action
is canonically normalised at the cutoff `Λ` (`NCG.SpectralAction.CanonicalGauge`, where `g1` is
the hypercharge coupling `g'`). Then, with `α₁ = (5/3) g'²/(4π)` (GUT normalisation),
`α₂ = g₂²/(4π)` and `α₃ = g₃²/(4π)`:
`α₁ = α₂ = α₃`, `sin²θ_W = 3/8`, and `sin²θ_W = g'²/(g'² + g₂²)`. -/

/-- **The GUT normalisation from `E₆`.** On the `16 ⊂ 27`, which is one generation of `H_F`
(`E6SM.rep16_eq_HF_generation`), `Σ Y² = 10/3` and `Σ T₃² = Σ (λ₃/2)² = 2`. So the three
generators have equal traces after `Y ↦ √(3/5) Y`, which is the normalisation behind
`g₁² = (5/3) g'²` and `sin²θ_W = 3/8`. -/
/-! ## One-loop running from `M_Z` -/

/-- **Inputs at the `Z` mass.** Intervals for `M_Z` and for the GUT-normalised inverse couplings
`α_i⁻¹(M_Z)` that contain the measured values (`M_Z = 91.19 GeV`, `α₁⁻¹ ≈ 59.0`,
`α₂⁻¹ ≈ 29.6`, `α₃⁻¹ ≈ 8.5`, from `α_em⁻¹(M_Z) ≈ 127.95`, `sin²θ_W(M_Z) ≈ 0.2312`,
`α_s(M_Z) ≈ 0.118`). -/

/-- One-loop running of the inverse couplings of the NCG Standard Model from `M_Z` to `μ`:
`α_i⁻¹(μ) = α_i⁻¹(M_Z) - b_i ln(μ/M_Z)/(2π)`. By `oneLoop_alphaInv_solution`, this is the
unique solution of the one-loop RG system. -/

/-- **`sin²θ_W = 3/8` only at a scale between `10¹²` and `10¹⁴ GeV`.** At one loop, from the
measured inputs at `M_Z`, `α₁(μ) = α₂(μ)` forces `10¹² GeV < μ < 10¹⁴ GeV`. -/
/-- **`α₂ = α₃` only at a scale between `10¹⁶` and `10¹⁸ GeV`** (one loop, measured inputs). -/

/-- **No one-loop unification.** From the measured inputs, there is no scale at which the three
inverse couplings of the NCG Standard Model coincide. So the full spectral boundary condition
`α₁ = α₂ = α₃` (`spectral_sin2W_three_eighths`) cannot hold exactly at any scale under
one-loop Standard Model running. -/

/-- **At `μ = 10¹⁶ GeV`, `sin²θ_W > 3/8`.** Under one-loop running from the measured inputs,
both couplings are positive at `10¹⁶ GeV` and `sin²θ_W(10¹⁶ GeV) > 3/8` strictly. So
`sin²θ_W = 3/8` does not hold at `10¹⁶ GeV`. -/

/-!
# The Higgs–top renormalization group system of the Noncommutative Standard Model

This file sets up the objects used in `RequestProject.NCGHiggsStability`,
`RequestProject.NCGTopFixedPoint` and `RequestProject.NCGHiggsTopMasses`.

* **Boundary condition for the Higgs quartic** (`lambdaGUT`). The quartic term of the spectral
  action comes from the Seeley–DeWitt coefficient `a₄(D_A²)`, with prefactor
  `f₀/(8π²) = higgsLambda` (`RequestProject.SpectralActionProduct`). The boundary condition
  requested for the quartic coupling at `Λ_GUT` is
  `λ(Λ_GUT) = 2 g₂⁴/(g₁² + g₂²) · f₀/(2π²)`.
  - `lambdaGUT_eq_a4` : `f₀/(2π²) = 4 · higgsLambda`, so the boundary value is
    `8 g₂⁴/(g₁²+g₂²) · higgsLambda`.
  - `lambdaGUT_of_canonical` : with the spectral gauge normalisation (`CanonicalGauge`,
    `g₃² = g₂² = (5/3)g₁²`, `f₀g₂² = 3π²/(2N_g)`) the value is `15/(16 N_g)`,
    and `lambdaGUT_SM` : it is `5/16` for three generations.
  - `lambdaGUT_eq_half_cos2` : whenever `f₀ g₂² = π²/2`, `λ(Λ_GUT) = ½ cos²θ_W`.
* **Spectral top boundary condition** (`spectral_top_boundary`): the spectral mass relation
  `m_t² = (8/3) M_W²` (`top_W_Z_Higgs_mass_relation`) is equivalent to `y_t² = (4/3) g₂²`.
* **The running couplings.** `t = ln(μ/M_Z)`. The gauge couplings are the exact one-loop
  solutions from the measured inputs at `M_Z` (`MZInputs`, `alphaInvAt` of
  `RequestProject.NCGUnification`): `g₃²`, `g₂²` and the hypercharge coupling
  `g'² = (3/5) g₁²_GUT`.
* **One-loop β-functions** (`betaLambda`, `betaTop`), in the convention
  `V = λ (|H|² − v²/2)²`, `m_H² = 2λv²`, `m_t = y_t v/√2`:
  - `16π² dλ/dt = 24λ² − 6y_t⁴ + (3/8)(2g₂⁴ + (g₂² + g'²)²) + λ(12y_t² − 9g₂² − 3g'²)`,
  - `16π² dy_t/dt = y_t ((9/2) y_t² − 8g₃² − (9/4) g₂² − (17/12) g'²)`.
  `IsHiggsTopFlow` says that `(λ, y_t)` solves this system on an interval.
* **Scales.** `tGUT = ln(10¹⁶ GeV/M_Z) ∈ (32, 33)`, `tPl = ln(M_Pl/M_Z) ∈ (39, 40)` with
  `M_Pl = 1.22 × 10¹⁹ GeV`.
* **Barrier (comparison) lemmas** `barrier_fwd`, `barrier_bwd`, and explicit bounds on the
  gauge couplings over a range of scales (`g3sq_le`, `le_g3sq`, ...).
-/
/-! ## The boundary condition at `Λ_GUT` -/

/-- **Boundary condition for the Higgs quartic at `Λ_GUT`** (as requested):
`λ(Λ_GUT) = 2 g₂⁴/(g₁² + g₂²) · f₀/(2π²)`, where `f₀ = f(0)` is the moment of the cutoff
function multiplying the Seeley–DeWitt coefficient `a₄(D_A²)` and `g₁` is the hypercharge
coupling in the normalisation of `CanonicalGauge`. -/

/-- **The boundary value in terms of the `a₄` quartic coefficient.** The Higgs quartic term
of the spectral action, `f₀ tr Φ⁴/(8π²)`, comes from `a₄(D_A²)`; its coefficient is
`higgsLambda c = f₀/(8π²)`. Then `λ(Λ_GUT) = 8 g₂⁴/(g₁² + g₂²) · higgsLambda c`. -/

/-- **`λ(Λ_GUT) = ½ cos²θ_W`** whenever `f₀ g₂² = π²/2` (the spectral normalisation for three
generations), where `cos²θ_W = g₂²/(g₁² + g₂²)`. -/

/-- **The spectral boundary value** `λ(Λ_GUT) = 15/(16 N_g)`. With the spectral normalisation
of the Yang–Mills term (`CanonicalGauge`: `g₂² = (5/3)g₁²` and `f₀g₂² = 3π²/(2N_g)`,
`gauge_unification`), the requested boundary condition takes this value. -/
/-- **`λ(Λ_GUT) = 5/16`** for the three-generation spectral Standard Model. -/

/-- **The spectral top boundary condition.** With `m_t = y_t v/√2` and `M_W² = g₂² v²/4`, the
spectral mass relation `m_t² = (8/3) M_W²` (`top_W_Z_Higgs_mass_relation`) holds exactly when
`y_t² = (4/3) g₂²`. -/
/-! ## Running gauge couplings -/
/-- One-loop inverse couplings `α_i⁻¹` at `t = ln(μ/M_Z)` (GUT normalisation for `i = 0`). -/
/-- Hypercharge coupling `g'²(t) = (3/5) · 4π/α₁⁻¹(t)` (Standard Model normalisation). -/
/-! ## One-loop β-functions of the Higgs quartic and the top Yukawa coupling -/

/-- **The one-loop Higgs–top RG flow** of the Noncommutative Standard Model on
`t ∈ [a, b]` (`t = ln(μ/M_Z)`), in the gauge background given by the measured inputs `I`. -/
/-- The top-Yukawa equation alone (the `λ`-equation does not feed back into it). -/
/-! ## Scales -/

/-!
# Vacuum stability of the Noncommutative Standard Model up to the Planck scale

We run the Higgs quartic `λ` and the top Yukawa coupling `y_t` with the one-loop Standard
Model β-functions (`IsHiggsTopFlow`, `RequestProject.NCGHiggsRG`), in the gauge background
obtained from the measured couplings at `M_Z`. The boundary conditions are imposed at
`Λ_GUT = 10¹⁶ GeV`:

* `λ(Λ_GUT) = λ₀` with `1/4 ≤ λ₀ ≤ 1`. This covers the requested value
  `λ(Λ_GUT) = 2g₂⁴/(g₁²+g₂²) · f₀/(2π²)`, which is `5/16` with the spectral gauge
  normalisation (`lambdaGUT_SM`), and `½cos²θ_W(Λ_GUT)` with the gauge couplings from `M_Z`;
* `y_t(Λ_GUT)² = (4/3) g₂²(Λ_GUT)`, the spectral relation `m_t² = (8/3)M_W²`
  (`spectral_top_boundary`).

**Main result** (`higgs_quartic_pos_up_to_planck`): every solution has `λ(μ) > 0` for all
`M_Z ≤ μ ≤ M_Pl = 1.22 × 10¹⁹ GeV`.

The argument uses barrier (comparison) functions:

* Below `Λ_GUT`, `y_t² ≥ y_t(Λ_GUT)²` (the top coupling grows towards the infrared) and
  `y_t² ≤ 81/25` (`topSq_bounds_below_GUT`). The first bound makes the pure-coupling part of
  `β_λ`, `−6y_t⁴ + (3/8)(2g₂⁴ + (g₂²+g'²)²)`, negative. Then `λ` can only increase as `μ`
  decreases, up to a linear term, and `λ(t) ≥ λ₀ e^{(t − t_GUT)/2} > 0`
  (`lam_lower_below_GUT`).
* Above `Λ_GUT`, `y_t² ≤ y_t(Λ_GUT)²`, so `β_λ > −0.03`. Since `t_Pl − t_GUT < 8`,
  `λ(t) ≥ λ₀ − 0.03 (t − t_GUT) > 0` (`lam_lower_above_GUT`).

In the ordinary Standard Model, with the measured `m_H` and `m_t` as low-energy input, `λ`
becomes negative around `10¹⁰–10¹¹ GeV` (metastability). Here, instead, `λ` is fixed by the
spectral boundary condition at `Λ_GUT`. The price is that the resulting low-energy masses
disagree with experiment; see `RequestProject.NCGHiggsTopMasses`.
-/
/-- Bounds on the boundary value `y_t(Λ_GUT)² = (4/3) g₂²(Λ_GUT)`. -/

/-- **The top coupling below `Λ_GUT`.** With the spectral boundary value
`y_t(Λ_GUT)² = (4/3)g₂²(Λ_GUT)`, for `M_Z ≤ μ ≤ Λ_GUT`:
`y_t(Λ_GUT)² ≤ y_t(μ)² ≤ 81/25`. -/
-- lower bound
-- upper bound
/-- **The top coupling above `Λ_GUT`.** For `Λ_GUT ≤ μ ≤ M_Pl`, `y_t(μ)² ≤ y_t(Λ_GUT)²`. -/

/-- **`λ` below `Λ_GUT`.** For `M_Z ≤ μ ≤ Λ_GUT`, `λ(t) ≥ λ₀ e^{(t − t_GUT)/2}`, where
`λ₀ = λ(Λ_GUT) ∈ (0, 1]`. -/

/-- **`λ` above `Λ_GUT`.** For `Λ_GUT ≤ μ ≤ M_Pl`, `λ(t) ≥ λ₀ − 0.03 (t − t_GUT)`, where
`λ₀ = λ(Λ_GUT) ∈ [1/4, 1]`. -/

/-- **Vacuum stability up to the Planck scale.** Take any solution `(λ, y_t)` of the one-loop
Higgs–top RG system for `M_Z ≤ μ ≤ M_Pl`, with the gauge couplings run from the measured
values at `M_Z`, and with the boundary conditions at `Λ_GUT = 10¹⁶ GeV`:
`y_t(Λ_GUT)² = (4/3) g₂²(Λ_GUT)` (spectral relation `m_t² = (8/3)M_W²`) and
`1/4 ≤ λ(Λ_GUT) ≤ 1`. Then `λ(μ) > 0` for all `M_Z ≤ μ ≤ M_Pl`. -/

/-- **Vacuum stability in terms of the energy scale `μ`**: `λ(ln(μ/M_Z)) > 0` for all
`M_Z ≤ μ ≤ M_Pl`, under the hypotheses of `higgs_quartic_pos_up_to_planck`. -/

/-- **Vacuum stability with the spectral boundary value** `λ(Λ_GUT) = 5/16`. If the requested
boundary condition `λ(Λ_GUT) = 2g₂⁴/(g₁²+g₂²) · f₀/(2π²)` is imposed with the spectral gauge
normalisation (`CanonicalGauge f₀ 3 g₁ g₂ g₃`, so `λ(Λ_GUT) = 5/16` by `lambdaGUT_SM`), then
`λ(μ) > 0` for all `M_Z ≤ μ ≤ M_Pl`. -/

/-!
# Threshold corrections at the unification scale and two-loop running

This file extends the Higgs–top cluster of the Noncommutative Standard Model
(`RequestProject.NCGHiggsRG`, `RequestProject.NCGHiggsStability`,
`RequestProject.NCGTopFixedPoint`, `RequestProject.NCGHiggsTopMasses`) in three ways.

* **Two-loop β-functions** (`betaLambda2`, `betaTop2`, `IsHiggsTopFlow2`). The one-loop
  β-functions of `RequestProject.NCGHiggsRG` are supplemented by the two-loop terms built from
  `λ`, `y_t` and `g₃` (convention `V = λ(|H|² − v²/2)²`):
  - `(16π²)² β_λ⁽²⁾ = −312λ³ − 144λ²y_t² − 3λy_t⁴ + 30y_t⁶ + 80λg₃²y_t² − 32g₃²y_t⁴`,
  - `(16π²)² β_{y_t}⁽²⁾ = y_t(−12y_t⁴ + 36g₃²y_t² − 108g₃⁴ + 6λ² − 12λy_t²)`.
  The two-loop electroweak terms and the two-loop running of the gauge couplings are not
  included (the gauge couplings remain the one-loop solutions from the measured values at
  `M_Z`).
* **A scalar singlet threshold** (`singletPotential`). The singlet `σ` of the spectral
  Standard Model (the field whose vacuum value gives the Majorana mass `M_R`) couples to the
  Higgs through `V = λ_h x² + λ_σ s² + 2λ_{hσ} x s`, with `x = |H|² − v²/2` and
  `s = σ² − w²/2`. Integrating out `σ` at tree level (`singlet_threshold_min`) leaves the
  Higgs potential `(λ_h − λ_{hσ}²/λ_σ) x²`: the quartic coupling is shifted by
  `−λ_{hσ}²/λ_σ ≤ 0` (`singletShift`).
* **Right-handed neutrino (Majorana sector) thresholds in the spectral action.** With the
  Yukawa invariants `a = 3y_t² + y_ν²`, `b = 3y_t⁴ + y_ν⁴` of the spectral action (top and a
  dominant Dirac neutrino Yukawa coupling `y_ν` of the right-handed neutrino), the spectral
  constraint `a = 4g₂²` gives `y_t² = (4g₂² − y_ν²)/3` (`spectral_top_with_neutrino`), and the
  quartic boundary value becomes `λ = lambdaGUT · 3b/a²` (`lambdaSpectralNu`). The factor
  `3b/a²` lies in `[3/4, 3]` and equals `3/4` exactly when `y_ν² = y_t²`
  (`neutrinoFactor_ge`, `neutrinoFactor_eq_min_iff`).

The threshold-corrected boundary conditions at `Λ_GUT` are collected in
`ThresholdParams.BoundaryCondition`; they contain a free parameter `δ` standing for every
further (higher-order) threshold correction to the quartic coupling.
-/
/-! ## Two-loop β-functions -/

/-- Two-loop part of `β_λ`, multiplied by `(16π²)²`: the terms built from `λ`, `y_t` and
`g₃` (`g32 = g₃²`). -/
/-- Two-loop part of `β_{y_t}`, multiplied by `(16π²)²`. -/

/-- **Two-loop β-function of the Higgs quartic**:
`β_λ = β_λ⁽¹⁾ + β_λ⁽²⁾/(16π²)²` with `β_λ⁽¹⁾ = betaLambda`. -/

/-- **Two-loop β-function of the top Yukawa coupling**:
`β_{y_t} = β_{y_t}⁽¹⁾ + β_{y_t}⁽²⁾/(16π²)²` with `β_{y_t}⁽¹⁾ = betaTop`. -/

/-- **The two-loop Higgs–top RG flow** on `t ∈ [a, b]` (`t = ln(μ/M_Z)`) in the one-loop gauge
background given by the measured inputs `I`. -/
/-- Dropping the two-loop terms gives back the one-loop β-function of `λ`. -/
/-- Dropping the two-loop terms gives back the one-loop β-function of `y_t`. -/
/-! ## The scalar singlet threshold -/

/-- **Higgs–singlet potential** of the spectral Standard Model with the singlet `σ`:
`V = λ_h x² + λ_σ s² + 2λ_{hσ} x s`, where `x = |H|² − v²/2` and `s = σ² − w²/2`. -/
/-- **The tree-level singlet threshold shift** `−λ_{hσ}²/λ_σ` of the Higgs quartic. -/

/-- **Integrating out the singlet.** For `λ_σ > 0`, the potential is bounded below in `s` by
`(λ_h − λ_{hσ}²/λ_σ) x²`, with equality at `s = −λ_{hσ} x/λ_σ`. So below the singlet
threshold the Higgs quartic is `λ_h + singletShift λ_σ λ_{hσ}`. -/
/-- The singlet threshold can only lower the Higgs quartic. -/

/-- **Stability of the Higgs–singlet potential.** For `λ_σ > 0`, `V ≥ 0` everywhere iff the
Higgs quartic below the threshold, `λ_h − λ_{hσ}²/λ_σ`, is non-negative. -/
/-! ## Right-handed neutrino thresholds in the spectral action -/

/-- Yukawa invariant `a = Tr(Y†Y)` of the spectral action, keeping the top coupling (three
colours) and the Dirac Yukawa coupling `y_ν` of the right-handed neutrino. -/
/-- Yukawa invariant `b = Tr((Y†Y)²)` of the spectral action. -/
/-- The factor `3b/a²` by which the neutrino sector rescales the spectral quartic. -/

/-- **Spectral quartic boundary value with the neutrino sector**:
`λ(Λ_GUT) = lambdaGUT g₁ g₂ f₀ · 3b/a²`. -/
/-- Without the neutrino Yukawa coupling, the old boundary value is recovered. -/
/-- **The neutrino factor is at least `3/4`** (for `y_t ≠ 0`). -/
/-- **The neutrino factor is at most `3`.** -/
/-- **The largest reduction** `3b/a² = 3/4` happens exactly for `y_ν² = y_t²`. -/

/-- **Spectral top boundary condition with the neutrino sector.** The spectral constraint
`a = 4g₂²` is `y_t² = (4g₂² − y_ν²)/3`; with `y_ν = 0` it is `y_t² = (4/3)g₂²`
(`spectral_top_boundary`). -/
/-! ## Threshold-corrected boundary conditions at `Λ_GUT` -/

/-- **Threshold parameters at the unification scale**: the cutoff moment `f₀`, the gauge
couplings `g₁, g₂` of the spectral normalisation, the neutrino Yukawa coupling `y_ν`, the
singlet couplings `λ_σ > 0`, `λ_{hσ}`, and a free parameter `δ` for all further
(higher-order) threshold corrections to the Higgs quartic. -/

/-- **Threshold-corrected boundary conditions at `Λ_GUT`** for the values `lamG = λ(Λ_GUT)`
and `ytG = y_t(Λ_GUT)` of the low-energy couplings, given the gauge coupling `g22 = g₂²(Λ_GUT)`
of the running:
* `λ(Λ_GUT) = lambdaGUT g₁ g₂ f₀ · 3b/a² − λ_{hσ}²/λ_σ + δ`,
* `y_t(Λ_GUT)² = (4g₂² − y_ν²)/3`. -/

/-- **Threshold corrections can realise any boundary value.** For any `λ(Λ_GUT)` and any
`y_t(Λ_GUT)` with `y_t² ≤ (4/3)g₂²`, some choice of threshold parameters gives exactly these
boundary values. So the boundary data at `Λ_GUT` are not constrained by the threshold
corrections; only the running below `Λ_GUT` matters. -/

/-!
# Threshold corrections at `Λ_GUT` cannot reconcile `m_H`, `m_t` and vacuum stability

**Question.** With threshold corrections at the unification scale (scalar singlet and
right-handed neutrino thresholds of the spectral action, plus arbitrary higher-order
corrections, `ThresholdParams`) and two-loop running (`IsHiggsTopFlow2`), can the spectral
Standard Model give `m_H ≈ 125 GeV` and `m_t ≈ 172.5 GeV` while keeping `λ(μ) > 0` up to
`M_Pl`?

**Answer: no, in this model.** Take any solution of the two-loop Higgs–top flow whose
couplings at `μ = M_Z` give (tree-level, `m_t = |y_t|v/√2`, `m_H = √(2λ)v`, with
`246 ≤ v ≤ 246.5 GeV`) `m_t ∈ [171, 174.5]` GeV and `m_H ∈ [124, 126.5]` GeV. Then
`λ(M_Z e²⁰) < 0`. Here `M_Z e²⁰ < 10¹¹ GeV`, far below `Λ_GUT = 10¹⁶ GeV`
(`quartic_negative_below_GUT`). Below `Λ_GUT` the running is fixed by the low-energy data,
and threshold corrections at `Λ_GUT` enter only through the boundary values there. So no
choice of thresholds at `Λ_GUT` can make `λ` positive on `[M_Z, M_Pl]`
(`not_thresholdReconciliation`).

**Method.** Every solution is enclosed, on 200 pieces of `t = ln(μ/M_Z) ∈ [0, 20]`, between
linear barriers for `y_t²` and `λ` (`RequestProject.NCGHiggsThresholdPiece`). Each piece is
checked by the Lean kernel with exact rational interval arithmetic
(`RequestProject.NCGHiggsThresholdEncA` … `EncD`). The upper barrier of `λ` ends at
`λ(M_Z e²⁰) < −0.008`.
-/

/-- Test that the barriers of the piece `q` start outside the end values of the barriers of
`r`, at the same scale. -/

/-- **Validated enclosure of the two-loop flow.** If `0.9624 < y_t(M_Z)² < 1.0064` and
`0.1265 < λ(M_Z) < 0.1323`, then `λ(M_Z e²⁰) < −0.008` for every solution of the two-loop
Higgs–top flow on `t ∈ [0, 33]`. -/
/-- The scale `M_Z e²⁰` lies below `10¹¹ GeV`. -/

/-- From the tree-level masses to the couplings: `m_t ∈ [171, 174.5]` and
`246 ≤ v ≤ 246.5` give `0.9624 < y_t² < 1.0064`. -/

/-- From the tree-level masses to the couplings: `m_H ∈ [124, 126.5]` and
`246 ≤ v ≤ 246.5` give `0.1265 < λ < 0.1323`. -/

/-- **The Higgs quartic turns negative below `Λ_GUT`.** For every solution of the two-loop
Higgs–top flow on `M_Z ≤ μ ≤ M_Z e³³` whose couplings at `μ = M_Z` give the measured masses
`m_t ∈ [171, 174.5]` GeV and `m_H ∈ [124, 126.5]` GeV (tree level, `246 ≤ v ≤ 246.5` GeV),
there is a scale `M_Z ≤ μ < 10¹¹ GeV` with `λ(μ) < 0`. -/

/-- **The requested reconciliation claim**, for the measured gauge inputs `I`: there are
threshold parameters at `Λ_GUT` (`ThresholdParams`: singlet couplings, right-handed neutrino
Yukawa coupling, arbitrary higher-order correction `δ`), a solution `(λ, y_t)` of the two-loop
flow on `[M_Z, M_Pl]` satisfying the threshold-corrected boundary conditions at `Λ_GUT`, and
`246 ≤ v ≤ 246.5` GeV, such that at `μ = M_Z`
`m_H ∈ [124, 126.5]` GeV and `m_t ∈ [171, 174.5]` GeV, and `λ(μ) > 0` for all
`M_Z ≤ μ ≤ M_Pl`. -/

/-- **The reconciliation claim is false.** For every admissible set of measured gauge inputs,
no threshold corrections at the unification scale reconcile `m_H ∈ [124, 126.5]` GeV and
`m_t ∈ [171, 174.5]` GeV with `λ > 0` up to `M_Pl` in the two-loop model: `λ` already turns
negative below `10¹¹ GeV`, whatever the boundary values at `Λ_GUT`. -/

/-!
# Validated enclosure steps for the two-loop Higgs–top flow

A `Piece` is a piece `[s₁, s₂]` of the scale axis (`t = ln(μ/M_Z)`) together with four linear
barrier functions, lower and upper for `q = y_t²` and for `λ`. `Piece.ok` is a Boolean test,
computed in `ℚ` with interval arithmetic (`RequestProject.IntervalBarrier`), which checks that
at each barrier the flow points strictly inwards. `Piece.step` : if the test passes and the
couplings start strictly inside the barriers at `s₁`, they end strictly inside at `s₂`.
`chain_step` chains a list of pieces.

The two-loop β-functions are rewritten as polynomials `PqR`, `PlR` in
`(λ, q, g₃², g₂², g'², κ)` with `κ = 1/(16π²)`:
`d(y_t²)/dt = κ · PqR` and `dλ/dt = κ · PlR`.
-/

/-!
# The Higgs and top masses predicted by the spectral boundary conditions

This file tests the claim that the spectral boundary conditions at `Λ_GUT = 10¹⁶ GeV` predict
`m_H` and `m_t` within the experimental error bars. **The claim is false in this model.**
The one-loop RG flow from the spectral boundary conditions gives `m_t > 176 GeV` and
`m_H > 170 GeV`, while the measured values are `m_t ≈ 172.6 GeV` and `m_H ≈ 125.2 GeV`, each
with an uncertainty below `1 GeV`.

**Conventions.** `v ≥ 246 GeV` (the Fermi-constant value is `v ≈ 246.2 GeV`), tree-level
relations `m_t = |y_t| v/√2` (`topMass`) and `m_H = √(2λ) v` (`higgsMass`). The couplings are
evaluated at any scale `M_Z ≤ μ ≤ e·M_Z ≈ 248 GeV`; this range contains both `m_H` and `m_t`.

/-!
# Formalization of the proof certificate `proof_ncg_ko6_*`

This file is a complete formalization of the mathematical content of the proof
certificates

* `proof_ncg_ko6_284023.md` / `.json` (and the 25 further copies
  `proof_ncg_ko6_*.md` / `.json`, which differ only in their `proof_id` and time
  stamp),

titled *"NCG Spectral Triple Axioms (KO-Dimension 6)"*, with target object
`Triple(dim_H=16, KO=6)` and domain `Noncommutative Differential Geometry`.

The certificate lists eight claims about a finite real spectral triple
`(A, H, D; J, γ)` with `dim H = 16`:

* step 1 (`AXIOM`, *Self-Adjointness of Dirac Operator*): `D = D*`;
* step 2 (`AXIOM`, *Isometry / Unitarity of Real Structure J*): `J J* = I`;
* step 3 (`INVARIANT_CHECK`, *KO-Dimension 6 Sign 1*): `J² = -1 · I`;
* step 4 (`INVARIANT_CHECK`, *KO-Dimension 6 Sign 2*): `J D = -1 · D J`;
* step 5 (`AXIOM`, *Grading Involution*): `γ² = I`, `γ = γ*`;
* step 6 (`INVARIANT_CHECK`, *KO-Dimension 6 Sign 3*): `J γ = -1 · γ J`;
* step 7 (`INVARIANT_CHECK`, *Order-Zero Condition*):
  `[a, b⁰] = 0` where `b⁰ = J b* J⁻¹`;
* step 8 (`INVARIANT_CHECK`, *First-Order Condition*): `[[D, a], J b* J⁻¹] = 0`.

The summary reads: *"The candidate triple satisfies all required NCG axioms at
KO-dimension 6 with maximum residual 0.0000e+00. The real structure J and Dirac
operator D form a mathematically consistent spectral triple."*

The certificate only verifies these axioms numerically for one concrete
candidate triple.  Accordingly, this file **constructs** an explicit finite real
spectral triple of exactly this type and **proves** all eight axioms for it.

## The model

The Hilbert space is `H = ℂ^16`, indexed by
`Idx = Fin 2 × Fin 2 × Fin 2 × Fin 2`; we think of the four tensor factors as

`H = ℂ²_J ⊗ ℂ²_a ⊗ ℂ²_b ⊗ ℂ²_x`.

* the algebra is `A = M₂(ℂ)`, acting on the factor `ℂ²_a` (`piL`);
* the real structure `J` is the antilinear map
  `J = (ε ⊗ SWAP_{a,b} ⊗ 1) ∘ (complex conjugation)`, where `ε = [[0,-1],[1,0]]`
  acts on `ℂ²_J` and `SWAP` exchanges the factors `ℂ²_a` and `ℂ²_b`;
* the Dirac operator is `D = σ_x ⊗ (M ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ M) ⊗ 1` with `M = σ_x`;
* the grading is `γ = σ_z ⊗ 1 ⊗ 1 ⊗ 1`.

All operators are represented as (explicitly given) functions `H → H`; the
antilinear operator `J` is genuinely antilinear (`Jop_antilinear`), so no
"complex-linear matrix" cheat is involved.  Sesquilinear pairings are written
with `hip v w = ∑ p, conj (v p) * w p`.

The triple is non-degenerate: `Dop_not_commutes` shows that `[D, a] ≠ 0` for a
suitable algebra element `a`, so the first-order condition of step 8 is not
vacuous.
-/

factors are the tensor factors `ℂ²_J ⊗ ℂ²_a ⊗ ℂ²_b ⊗ ℂ²_x` of the model. -/

/-- The Hilbert space `H = ℂ^16` of the certificate `proof_ncg_ko6_*`

/-- The diagonal of `σ_z`, acting on the factor `ℂ²_J`; this is the grading. -/

formulas `b⁰ = J b* J⁻¹` of steps 7 and 8 of the certificate

/-! ## Step 2: `J J* = I` (antiunitarity of `J`) -/

/-- **Step 2 of the certificate `proof_ncg_ko6_*` ("Isometry / Unitarity of Real

/-!
# The infrared quasi-fixed point of the top Yukawa coupling

Three results on the running of `y_t` towards the infrared (`t = ln(μ/M_Z)` decreasing).

1. **Pendleton–Ross fixed point** (`pendletonRoss_attractive`). In the QCD truncation
   `16π² dy_t/dt = y_t((9/2)y_t² − 8g₃²)`, `16π² dg₃²/dt = −14 g₃⁴` (one-loop QCD with six
   flavours), the ratio `R = y_t²/g₃²` obeys `16π² dR/dt = 9 g₃² R (R − 2/9)`. Hence
   `(R − 2/9)²` is monotone in `t`, so the distance to `R* = 2/9` shrinks towards the infrared,
   and `R ≡ 2/9` is a fixed trajectory (`pendletonRoss_fixed`). The gauge coupling `g₃²` of
   the model obeys the QCD equation exactly (`hasDerivAt_g3sq`).
2. **Infrared focusing in the full one-loop model** (`top_IR_focusing`). For any two solutions
   of the full top equation (QCD and electroweak terms) on `M_Z ≤ μ ≤ Λ_GUT`,
   `|y₁⁻²(M_Z) − y₂⁻²(M_Z)| ≤ e^{−t_GUT/40} |y₁⁻²(Λ_GUT) − y₂⁻²(Λ_GUT)|`, and
   `e^{−t_GUT/40} < e^{−4/5} ≈ 0.45`. So the infrared value depends only weakly on the
   ultraviolet boundary value.
3. **Quasi-fixed-point bound** (`top_quasi_fixed_point_bound`). Whatever the value of `y_t` at
   `Λ_GUT` (however large), `y_t(M_Z)² < 3.06`, i.e. `y_t(M_Z) < 1.75`. In the model this bounds
   the tree-level top mass `y_t v/√2`, independently of the ultraviolet boundary value.
-/
/-! ## 1. The Pendleton–Ross fixed point -/

/-- The running `g₃²` of the model solves the one-loop QCD equation
`16π² dg₃²/dt = −14 g₃⁴` (`b₃ = −7`). -/

/-- **The Pendleton–Ross fixed point is infrared attractive.** Let `G = g₃² > 0` and `y` solve
`16π² dG/dt = −14G²` and `16π² dy/dt = y((9/2)y² − 8G)` on `[a, b]`. Then
`(y²/G − 2/9)²` is monotone non-decreasing in `t`: the ratio `y_t²/g₃²` approaches `2/9`
monotonically as `μ` decreases. -/

/-- **`y_t² = (2/9) g₃²` is a fixed trajectory.** Under the hypotheses of
`pendletonRoss_attractive`, if `y_t² = (2/9)g₃²` at a scale `b`, then this holds at every lower
scale `t ∈ [a, b]`. -/
/-! ## 2. Infrared focusing in the full one-loop model -/

/-- `1/y_t²` obeys the linear equation `16π² d(1/y_t²)/dt = 2G/y_t² − 9`, where
`G = 8g₃² + (9/4)g₂² + (17/12)g'²`. -/

/-- **Infrared focusing of the top Yukawa coupling.** For any two solutions `y₁, y₂` of the
one-loop top equation on `M_Z ≤ μ ≤ Λ_GUT` that do not vanish,

/-!
# The noncommutative 2-torus `A_θ`

This file (together with `NCGTorusTrace`, `NCGTorusHeisenberg`, `NCGTorusConnection`,
`NCGTorusModular` and `NCGTorusMorita`) extends the `NCG` development of the project
(`RequestProject.NCGKO6`, the finite spectral triples of the noncommutative Standard Model) by
the basic example of a noncommutative space: the noncommutative 2-torus.

* `NCG.ePhase θ = e^{2πiθ}`.
* `NCG.NCTorus θ` is the (algebraic, polynomial) noncommutative torus `A_θ`: the universal
  `ℂ`-algebra generated by two units `U`, `V` subject to `V U = e^{2πiθ} U V`, realized as a
  quotient of a free algebra (`RingQuot`). Its universal property is `NCTorus.lift`, and
  homomorphisms out of it are determined by `U` and `V` (`NCTorus.hom_ext`).
* `NCTorus.equivAddInt : A_θ ≃ A_{θ+n}` and `NCTorus.equivNeg : A_θ ≃ A_{-θ}`; hence these are
  Morita equivalent in the sense of Mathlib's `IsMoritaEquivalent`.
* The canonical derivations `δ₁, δ₂` (`δ₁ U = 2πi U`, `δ₁ V = 0`, `δ₂ U = 0`, `δ₂ V = 2πi V`),
  more generally `NCTorus.deriv θ x y` with `δ U = x U`, `δ V = y V`, and the Leibniz rule
  `NCTorus.deriv_leibniz`.

The C*-algebra `A_θ` is the completion of this algebra, and the smooth algebra `A_θ^∞` its
closure under rapidly decaying coefficients; both are beyond what is formalized here.
-/
/-- The phase `e(θ) = exp(2πiθ)`. -/
/-- The four generators `U, U⁻¹, V, V⁻¹` of the free algebra presenting `A_θ`. -/

/-- The defining relations of `A_θ`: `U U⁻¹ = U⁻¹ U = 1`, `V V⁻¹ = V⁻¹ V = 1` and
`V U = e(θ) U V`. -/
/-- The (algebraic) noncommutative torus `A_θ`. -/
/-- The quotient map from the free algebra. -/
/-- The unitary generator `U`. -/
/-- The unitary generator `V`. -/
/-- The defining commutation relation `V U = e(θ) U V`. -/

/-- Induction principle: a predicate stable under sums and products and holding on scalars
and on `U^{±1}`, `V^{±1}` holds everywhere. -/
/-- The assignment of generators used by `lift`. -/

/-- **Universal property of `A_θ`.** Two units `u, v` of a `ℂ`-algebra with
`v u = e(θ) u v` determine an algebra homomorphism `A_θ → A` with `U ↦ u`, `V ↦ v`. -/
/-- Algebra homomorphisms out of `A_θ` are determined by the images of `U` and `V`. -/
/-- If `e(θ) = e(θ')` then `A_θ ≅ A_θ'`. -/
/-- `A_θ ≅ A_{θ + n}` for every integer `n`. -/
/-- `A_θ ≅ A_{-θ}`, exchanging the two generators `U ↔ V`. -/

/-- `A_θ` and `A_{θ+n}` are Morita equivalent (in the sense of Mathlib's
`IsMoritaEquivalent`: equivalent `ℂ`-linear module categories). -/
/-- `A_θ` and `A_{-θ}` are Morita equivalent. -/
/-- The upper triangular unit `[[w, x w], [0, w]]`. -/

/-- The algebra homomorphism `a ↦ [[a, δ a], [0, a]]` encoding the derivation `δ = δ_{x,y}`
with `δ U = x U`, `δ V = y V`. -/
/-- The derivation `δ_{x,y}` of `A_θ` determined by `δ U = x U`, `δ V = y V`. -/
/-- The first canonical derivation `δ₁` (`δ₁ U = 2πi U`, `δ₁ V = 0`). -/
/-- The second canonical derivation `δ₂` (`δ₂ U = 0`, `δ₂ V = 2πi V`). -/

/-!
# Connes' connection on `E_g`, its constant curvature and its Chern number

* `NCTorus.leibniz_extend`: a Leibniz rule checked on the generators `U, V` holds on `A_θ`.
* `HeisenbergData.nabla₁`, `nabla₂`: Connes' connection `∇₁ f = -(2πi s/ν) f`, `∇₂ f = ∂ₛ f`.
* `nabla₁_leibniz`, `nabla₂_leibniz`: `∇ⱼ(f · a) = (∇ⱼ f) · a + f · δⱼ(a)` for all `a ∈ A_θ`
  (a connection on the right `A_θ`-module `E_g`); `nabla₁_leibniz_left`, `nabla₂_leibniz_left`:
  compatibility with the left `A_{θ'}`-action with derivations rescaled by `1/(cθ + d)`.
* `curvature_eq`: **the curvature `[∇₁, ∇₂]` is the constant `2πi c/(cθ + d)`**, non-zero
  (`curvature_ne_zero`), lying in the image of `A_{θ'}` (`curvature_eq_leftAct`).
* `chernNumber_eq`: with the trace of `E_g` normalized by Rieffel's value `τ(E_g) = |cθ + d|`
  (`dimE`, taken as a definition), the Chern number `c₁ = (1/2πi) τ_E(F)` equals
  `sign(cθ + d) · c`, **a non-zero integer** (`chernNumber_int_ne_zero`); it is `c` when
  `cθ + d > 0` (`chernNumber_eq_c`). Also `dimE_mem_lattice`: `τ(E_g) ∈ ℤ + θℤ`.
-/

/-- A Leibniz rule `N φ(a) = φ(a) N + φ(δ a)` that holds on the generators `U`, `V` holds on all
of `A_θ`. -/
/-- The constant `κ = -2πi / ν = -2πi c / (cθ + d)` of the first connection component. -/
/-- **Connes' connection on `E_g`**, first component: `(∇₁ f)(k, s) = -(2πi s / ν) f(k, s)`. -/
/-- **Connes' connection on `E_g`**, second component: `(∇₂ f)(k, s) = ∂ₛ f(k, s)`. -/

/-- Translate a Leibniz rule for the right action `ρ` into one for the homomorphism
`rightAct : A_θ → End(E)ᵐᵒᵖ`. -/

/-- **`∇ = (∇₁, ∇₂)` is a connection on the right `A_θ`-module `E_g`** (Connes):
`∇ⱼ(f · a) = (∇ⱼ f) · a + f · δⱼ(a)` for all `a ∈ A_θ`, `j = 1, 2`. -/
/-- Second component of the Leibniz rule of Connes' connection. -/
/-! ### Compatibility with the left action of `A_{θ'}` -/

/-- **The same `∇` is a connection for the left `A_{θ'}`-action**, with respect to the rescaled
derivations `δⱼ' / (cθ + d)`: `∇ⱼ(x · f) = x · ∇ⱼ f + (cθ + d)⁻¹ (δⱼ' x) · f`. -/
/-- Second component of the left Leibniz rule. -/
/-! ### Curvature -/
/-- The curvature `F = [∇₁, ∇₂]` of Connes' connection. -/
/-- **Constant curvature:** `[∇₁, ∇₂] = (2πi c / (cθ + d)) · 1`. -/
/-- The curvature of Connes' connection on `E_g` is non-zero (for `c ≠ 0`). -/

/-- The curvature is the image under the left action of the scalar
`F₀ = 2πi c / (cθ + d) ∈ A_{θ'}`: it lies in the endomorphism algebra `A_{θ'}` of `E_g`. -/
/-! ### The Chern number -/

/-- Rieffel's value of the canonical trace of `E_g`, `τ(E_g) = |cθ + d|` (the "dimension"
of the projective module). This normalization is taken from the literature (Rieffel,
Connes); it is not derived here from a Hilbert-module inner product. -/
/-- The canonical trace on `End_{A_θ}(E_g) ⊇ A_{θ'}`, `τ_E(x) = τ(E_g) · τ_{θ'}(x)`. -/

/-- **Connes' Chern number** `c₁(E_g, ∇) = (1 / 2πi) τ_E(F)` of the curvature
`F = [∇₁, ∇₂] = F₀ · 1`. -/
/-- **The Chern number is the integer `± c`**: `c₁(E_g) = sign(cθ + d) · c`. -/
/-- For `cθ + d > 0` the Chern number of `E_g` is exactly `c`. -/
/-- The trace `τ(E_g) = |cθ + d|` lies in the range `ℤ + θℤ` of the trace on `K₀(A_θ)`. -/
/-- **The Chern number is a non-zero integer.** -/

/-!
# The Connes–Rieffel (Heisenberg) projective modules `E_g` over `A_θ`

For `g = [[a, b], [c, d]] ∈ SL(2, ℤ)` with `c > 0` and `cθ + d ≠ 0` (`NCG.HeisenbergData θ`),
the module is `E_g = 𝓢(ℝ × ℤ/c) = (ℤ/c → 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ))` (Schwartz functions), with

* right action of `A_θ`: `(f·U)(k, s) = f(k - 1, s + ν)`, `(f·V)(k, s) = e(s + kd/c) f(k, s)`,
  where `ν = (cθ + d)/c`;
* left action of `A_{θ'}`, `θ' = (aθ + b)/(cθ + d)`:
  `(X f)(k, s) = f(k - a, s + 1/c)`, `(Y f)(k, s) = e(s/(cθ + d) + k/c) f(k, s)`.

Main results:

* `opU_mul_opV`, `opY_mul_opX`: the commutation relations, so that `HeisenbergData.rightAct`
  (an algebra map `A_θ → End(E)ᵐᵒᵖ`) and `HeisenbergData.leftAct` (`A_{θ'} → End(E)`) are
  well defined;
* `HeisenbergData.leftAct_commute_ρ`: **the two actions commute**, so `E_g` is an
  `A_{θ'}`–`A_θ` bimodule;
* `E_g` is non-zero.

Not formalized: the `A_θ`-valued inner product, finite generation and projectivity of `E_g` and
the fact (Rieffel) that `E_g` is an imprimitivity bimodule with `End_{A_θ}(E_g) = A_{θ'}`.
-/
/-- The residue of `k - a` in `ZMod c` differs from `k.val - a` by a multiple of `c`. -/
/-- The Schwartz space `𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)` is non-zero (it contains a smooth bump function). -/

/-- Data of an element `g = [[a, b], [c, d]] ∈ SL(2, ℤ)` with `c > 0`, together with a
parameter `θ` such that `cθ + d ≠ 0`. -/
/-- The target parameter `θ' = g · θ = (aθ + b) / (cθ + d)`. -/
/-- The translation length `ν = (cθ + d) / c`. -/
/-- The Connes–Rieffel (Heisenberg) module `E_g = 𝓢(ℝ × ℤ/c) = (ℤ/c → 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ))`. -/
/-- The module `E_g` is non-zero. -/
/-- An operator on `E` of the form `(T f)(k) = T_k (f (σ k))`. -/
/-- The right action of `U`: `(f · U)(k, s) = f(k - 1, s + ν)`. -/
/-- The right action of `V`: `(f · V)(k, s) = e(s + k d / c) f(k, s)`. -/
/-- The left action of the first generator of `A_{θ'}`: `(X f)(k, s) = f(k - a, s + 1/c)`. -/

/-- The left action of the second generator of `A_{θ'}`:
`(Y f)(k, s) = e(s / (cθ + d) + k / c) f(k, s)`. -/
/-- `U ∘ V = e(θ) V ∘ U` as operators, i.e. `(f · V) · U = e(θ) (f · U) · V`. -/
/-! ### The two actions commute -/
/-- A unit of the opposite monoid. -/

/-- The right `A_θ`-module structure of `E_g`, as an algebra homomorphism
`A_θ → End(E)ᵐᵒᵖ`. -/
/-- The operator `f ↦ f · a` of the right action of `a ∈ A_θ` on `E_g`. -/
/-- The left `A_{θ'}`-module structure of `E_g`, `θ' = (aθ + b)/(cθ + d)`. -/

/-- **`E_g` is an `A_{θ'}`–`A_θ` bimodule:** the left action of `A_{θ'}`, `θ' = g · θ`, commutes
with the right action of `A_θ`, i.e. `x · (f · y) = (x · f) · y`. -/

* `GLRelated_iff_lattice`: **`θ' ∈ GL(2, ℤ) · θ` iff `ℤ + θ'ℤ = λ(ℤ + θℤ)` for some `λ > 0`**
  (for all real `θ, θ'`; all rationals are `SL(2, ℤ)`-related, `SLRelated.of_rat`).
* `not_SLRelated_sqrt_three`: `-√3` is **not** in the `SL(2, ℤ)`-orbit of `√3`
  (though it is in the `GL(2, ℤ)`-orbit).
-/
/-- `θ' = (aθ + b) / (cθ + d)` for some `[[a, b], [c, d]] ∈ SL(2, ℤ)` (with `cθ + d ≠ 0`). -/

/-- `θ' = (aθ + b) / (cθ + d)` for some `[[a, b], [c, d]] ∈ GL(2, ℤ)`, i.e. `ad - bc = ±1`
(with `cθ + d ≠ 0`). -/
/-- The subgroup `ℤ + θℤ ⊂ ℝ` (by Pimsner–Voiculescu, the range of the trace on `K₀(A_θ)`). -/
/-- Composition of Möbius transformations. -/
/-- For irrational `θ`, the coordinates of `m + nθ` are unique. -/

/-- **Möbius-equivalent parameters have proportional lattices:** if `θ' = g · θ` with
`g ∈ GL(2, ℤ)`, then `ℤ + θ'ℤ = λ (ℤ + θℤ)` with `λ = 1/|cθ + d| > 0`. -/
-- the lattice is symmetric

/-- **Converse for irrational `θ`:** if `λ (ℤ + θℤ) = ℤ + θ'ℤ` for some `λ`, then
`θ' = g · θ` for some `g ∈ GL(2, ℤ)`. -/
-- `l = p + q θ'` and `l θ = r + s θ'`, expressed back in the basis `(1, θ)`
/-- `SLRelated` is symmetric (inverse matrix `[[d, -b], [-c, a]]`). -/
/-- `0` is `SL(2, ℤ)`-related to every rational number. -/
/-- **All rational parameters are `SL(2, ℤ)`-related.** -/
/-- Rescaling lattices preserves rationality of the parameter. -/

/-- **Lattice criterion.** For every `θ`, `θ'` is `GL(2, ℤ)`-related to `θ` iff

/-- **`θ = √3` and `-√3` are not `SL(2, ℤ)`-related** (although they are `GL(2, ℤ)`-related). -/

/-!
# Morita equivalence of noncommutative tori and the modular group

* `SLRelated.realized`: for every `g ∈ SL(2, ℤ)`, `θ' = g · θ` is realized by an isomorphism
  `A_θ ≅ A_{θ+n}` (`c = 0`) or by a Connes–Rieffel bimodule `E_g` (`c ≠ 0`).
* `MoritaClassificationInput M`: the hypotheses on a relation `M` ("is Morita equivalent to"):
  transitivity, the isomorphisms `A_θ ≅ A_{θ+n}`, `A_θ ≅ A_{-θ}` (proved in `NCGTorus`), and the
  two deep analytic inputs, Rieffel's imprimitivity theorem for `E_g` and the Morita invariance
  of the trace range `τ(K₀(A_θ)) = ℤ + θℤ` (Pimsner–Voiculescu), which are **assumed**.
* `MoritaClassificationInput.iff_GLRelated`: under these inputs,
  **`A_θ ∼ A_θ'` iff `θ' = (aθ + b)/(cθ + d)` with `[[a, b], [c, d]] ∈ GL(2, ℤ)`**;
  `moritaClassificationInput_GLRelated` shows the inputs are consistent.
* `MoritaClassificationInput.not_iff_SLRelated` and
  `not_forall_isMoritaEquivalent_iff_SLRelated`: the statement with `SL(2, ℤ)` in place of
  `GL(2, ℤ)` is **false** (`A_{√3} ≅ A_{-√3}`, but `-√3 ∉ SL(2, ℤ) · √3`).
-/

/-- Every `SL(2, ℤ)`-related pair `θ' = g · θ` is realized either by an algebra isomorphism
`A_θ ≅ A_θ'` (when `c = 0`, i.e. `θ' = θ ± b`) or by a Connes–Rieffel Heisenberg bimodule
`E_g` (when `c ≠ 0`; replacing `g` by `-g` we may take `c > 0`). -/
/-- **"If" direction:** `SL(2, ℤ)`-related parameters give Morita equivalent tori. -/

/-- `GL(2, ℤ)`-related parameters give Morita equivalent tori (an orientation-reversing `g` is
the composite of `θ ↦ -θ` with an element of `SL(2, ℤ)`). -/

/-- **Morita classification of noncommutative tori.** Under the inputs of
`MoritaClassificationInput`, `A_θ` and `A_θ'` are Morita equivalent **iff**
`θ' = (aθ + b) / (cθ + d)` for some `[[a, b], [c, d]] ∈ GL(2, ℤ)`. -/

/-- **The `SL(2, ℤ)` version of the classification is false:** under the same inputs,
`A_{√3}` and `A_{-√3}` are Morita equivalent but `-√3` is not an `SL(2, ℤ)`-transform of `√3`. -/

/-- The inputs of `MoritaClassificationInput` are consistent: they are satisfied by
`GLRelated` itself (so, by `MoritaClassificationInput.iff_GLRelated`, `GLRelated` is the unique
relation satisfying them). -/

/-- For Mathlib's (categorical) Morita equivalence of the algebraic tori `A_θ`, the
`SL(2, ℤ)`-classification also fails: `A_{√3} ≅ A_{-√3}` (so they are Morita equivalent) but
`-√3` is not an `SL(2, ℤ)`-transform of `√3`. -/

/-!
# Monomial basis and canonical trace of `A_θ`

* `NCTorus.W θ m n = U^m V^n` and the product rule `W(a,b) W(c,d) = e(θ)^{bc} W(a+c, b+d)`.
* `NCTorus.basisW`: **the monomials `U^m V^n`, `(m, n) ∈ ℤ²`, form a `ℂ`-basis of `A_θ`**
  (spanning by induction on the presentation, linear independence through the regular
  representation `NCTorus.regRep` on `ℂ^{ℤ×ℤ}`).
* `NCTorus.trace`: the canonical trace `τ(Σ a_{mn} U^m V^n) = a_{00}`, with `τ(1) = 1`,
  `τ(ab) = τ(ba)` (`NCTorus.trace_mul_comm`) and `τ ∘ δ = 0` (`NCTorus.trace_deriv`).
-/
/-- The central unit `e(θ) · 1` of `A_θ`. -/
/-- The monomial `W(m, n) = U^m V^n` (as a unit). -/
/-- Product of monomials: `W(a,b) W(c,d) = e(θ)^{bc} W(a+c, b+d)`. -/
/-- The monomials `U^m V^n` span `A_θ`. -/
/-! ### The regular representation on `ℤ × ℤ → ℂ` -/
/-- The shift `(U g)(m, n) = g(m - 1, n)` of the regular representation. -/
/-- The twisted shift `(V g)(m, n) = e(mθ) g(m, n - 1)` of the regular representation. -/
/-- The regular representation `ρ : A_θ → End(ℂ^{ℤ×ℤ})`. -/
/-- The vector `δ₀ ∈ ℂ^{ℤ×ℤ}` (indicator of the origin). -/
/-- The monomials `U^m V^n` are linearly independent. -/
/-- **`A_θ` has the `ℂ`-basis `{U^m V^n : (m, n) ∈ ℤ²}`.** -/
/-! ### The canonical trace -/
/-- The canonical trace `τ(a) = ⟨δ₀, ρ(a) δ₀⟩`, i.e. the coefficient of `U⁰V⁰`. -/
/-- Induction over the monomial spanning set. -/
/-- **`τ` is a trace:** `τ(ab) = τ(ba)`. -/
/-! ### Derivations on monomials, and invariance of the trace -/
/-- `δ_{x,y}(U^m V^n) = (m x + n y) U^m V^n`. -/
/-- **The trace is invariant under the canonical derivations:** `τ ∘ δ = 0`. -/
