/-! ## Gradient-flow structure -/

/-- **The free energy is a Lyapunov function**: along any solution of the array equations,
`d𝓕/dt = -2 ∑_j |ḃ_j|²`. -/
/-! ## Below threshold: only the phonon vacuum -/
/-- **Below threshold the phonon vacuum is the only stationary state.** -/
/-! ## Above threshold: the phase-locked condensate -/

/-- **Condensation**: for a connected coupling graph and any pump power `P ≥ 0`, the ground
states (global minimisers of the free energy) of the array are exactly the phase-locked states
`b_j = √n⋆(P) e^{iθ}`. -/

/-- **Macroscopic phase coherence of the condensate.** Above threshold, every ground state of a
connected array is a coherent phonon condensate: a macroscopic occupation `n⋆ > 0` of every
cavity, one common phase `θ`, an order parameter `Ψ = (1/N) ∑ b_j` with `|Ψ|² = n⋆`, perfect
first-order coherence `|∑ b_j|² = N ∑ |b_j|²`, and the ground states form exactly one orbit of
the global `U(1)` phase rotation (spontaneously broken phase symmetry). -/
/-! ## The second-order phase transition -/
/-- The order parameter has a kink at the critical pump power. -/
/-- The above-threshold branch of the ground-state free energy. -/

/-- **No latent heat**: the ground-state free energy is differentiable at every pump power,
including the critical one. -/

/-- **The transition at `P_crit` is of second order** (Ehrenfest classification):
* the order parameter `n⋆` vanishes for `P ≤ P_crit`, is positive for `P > P_crit`, is
  continuous, and has a kink at `P_crit` (one-sided slopes `0` and `1/(s P_crit)`);
* the ground-state free energy per cavity is differentiable with a continuous derivative
  (first derivatives are continuous: no latent heat, not a first-order transition);
* its second derivative jumps at `P_crit`: the one-sided derivatives of `∂𝓕/∂P` are `0` and
  `-G₀/(s P_crit) ≠ 0`, so the free energy is not twice differentiable there. -/

/-!
# Observing the phonon condensate: interferometric readout and synesthetic spectrum

* `condensate_interferometric_readout` (links to `Sovereign.Pipeline`): the four-step phase
  interferometry of the cavity pipeline recovers every cavity amplitude of a condensate exactly,
  and all cavities report the same complex amplitude, hence the same phase: the macroscopic
  phase is directly observable.
* `phononWaveform` (links to `Sovereign.Algebra.AcousticVisualTensor`): the phonon field of the
  array as a sound waveform (one partial per cavity: amplitude `|b_j|`, mechanical frequency
  `Ω_j`, phase `arg b_j`).
* `condensate_avEnergy`: for a ground state above threshold the spectral energy is `N n⋆`, the
  joint energy of its synesthetic (sound, colour) pair is `2 N n⋆`, and it is invariant under the
  diagonal transposition action of the acoustic–visual tensor functor.
-/

/-- **Interferometric readout of the condensate phase.** For any nonzero reference beam, the
four-step interferometer of `Sovereign.Pipeline` returns the condensate amplitude of each cavity
exactly, and the readouts of any two cavities coincide. -/

/-- The phonon field of the array as an acoustic waveform: one partial per cavity with
amplitude `|b_j|`, (positive) mechanical frequency `Ω_j` and phase `arg b_j`. -/

/-- **Synesthetic energy of the condensate.** Above threshold, for every ground state `b` of a
connected array, the phonon waveform has spectral energy `N n⋆`, its synesthetic
(sound, colour) pair has joint energy `2 N n⋆`, and this joint energy is invariant under
transposition by any factor `c` (the diagonal action of `acousticFunctor ⊗ opticalFunctor`). -/

# `Sovereign.Condensate`

Multi-scale optomechanical resonant cavity arrays and macroscopic phonon condensation:
* `PhononCondensate`: gradient flow dynamics, Landau free energy minimization, Ehrenfest second-order phase transition, and macroscopic phase coherence above P_crit.
* `MultiScale`: coupled micro- and macro-cavity arrays with matched optomechanical gain and connected block coupling.
-/

/-!
# Metamorphic relations on algebraic expressions

Candidate conjectures are polynomial identities `lhs ≈ rhs` between algebraic expressions
over ℚ in variables `x₀, x₁, …`.  We define the metamorphic relation generators

* `substMR s`  — simultaneous substitution of expressions for variables,
* `permMR σ`   — permutation (renaming) of variables by `σ : Equiv.Perm ℕ`,
* `scaleMR a`  — scaling of all variables `xᵢ ↦ a·xᵢ`,
* `outScaleMR a` — scaling both sides of the identity by `a ≠ 0`,
* `symmMR`     — exchanging the two sides,

prove their semantic-invariance laws (`valid_perm_iff`, `valid_scale_iff`, …), and give an
exhaustive test stream (`algTests`, enumerating all finitely supported rational
environments), so that every false identity is refuted by the metamorphic filter in
finitely many steps (`algFilter_refutes_invalid`).
-/
/-- Algebraic (ring) expressions over ℚ. -/
/-- Evaluation in a rational environment. -/
/-- Simultaneous substitution of expressions for variables. -/
/-- Renaming of variables. -/
/-- Scaling of all variables by `a`. -/
/-- A strict upper bound on the variable indices occurring in an expression. -/
/-- The value of an expression only depends on the variables below its bound. -/
/-- A candidate polynomial identity `lhs ≈ rhs`. -/
/-- Semantics of identities: `lhs` and `rhs` evaluate to the same rational number. -/
/-- Metamorphic relation generator: substitution of expressions for variables. -/
/-- Metamorphic relation generator: permutation of variables. -/
/-- Metamorphic relation generator: scaling of all variables by `a`. -/
/-- Metamorphic relation generator: scaling both sides of the identity by `a ≠ 0`. -/
/-- Metamorphic relation generator: exchanging the two sides. -/
/-- **Permutation invariance.** An identity is valid iff its variable-permuted image is. -/

/-- **Scaling invariance.** For `a ≠ 0`, an identity is valid iff its image under
`xᵢ ↦ a·xᵢ` is. -/
/-- **Output scaling invariance.** For `a ≠ 0`, `a·l ≈ a·r` is valid iff `l ≈ r` is. -/
/-- Substitution instances of valid identities are valid. -/
/-- The `k`-th test environment: decode `k` as a list of rationals, padded with zeros. -/
/-- The metamorphic filter for identities with a given list of metamorphic relations. -/
/-- The test stream `algTests` is exhaustive: every false identity fails at some test. -/

/-- **Finite refutation of false identities.** Any false identity — in particular any
identity violating a metamorphic invariant — is refuted by the metamorphic filter after
finitely many test steps. -/

/-- The standard metamorphic generators for identities: swapping sides, swapping the first
two variables, and scaling the variables by `2` and by `-1`. -/

declarations.name: eval

  | bot => false

  | sup e₁ e₂ => eval ρ e₁ || eval ρ e₂
  | compl e => !eval ρ e

/-- The dual expression: swap `⊓ ↔ ⊔` and `⊤ ↔ ⊥`. -/

  | top => bot
  | bot => top

/-!
# The concrete autonomous conjecturer for algebraic identities

`algPipeline` instantiates the closed loop for polynomial identities over ℚ: the metamorphic
filter tests all compositions (up to depth `d`) of the standard generators — side swap,
variable permutation `x₀ ↔ x₁`, scalings `xᵢ ↦ 2xᵢ` and `xᵢ ↦ -xᵢ` — on an exhaustive
stream of rational environments, and the verifier accepts syntactic identities `e ≈ e`
and metamorphic images of library lemmas.  The conjecturer and the probability estimates
are arbitrary (any heuristic or learned component can be plugged in).
-/
/-- The concrete closed-loop conjecturer for algebraic identities. -/

/-- **The algebraic lemma stream is sound and monotone under Kelly gating.** Started from an
empty library, no refutations and a positive budget, at every round every accepted identity
is valid, every refuted identity is false, the library only grows and the budget stays
positive. -/

/-- **Every false identity has a finite refutation time in the concrete pipeline**: once the
Kelly stake buys that many test steps, a round proposing it refutes it. -/

declarations.name: Semantics
declarations.signature_heuristic:
structure Semantics (Cand : Type u) (Env : Type v) where
  /-- `holds ρ c`: candidate `c` is true in environment `ρ`. -/
  holds : Env → Cand → Prop
  /-- Satisfaction is decidable (it can be tested). -/
  decHolds : ∀ ρ c, Decidable (holds ρ c)

attribute [instance] Semantics.decHolds

namespace Semantics

variable {Cand : Type u} {Env : Type v} (S : Semantics Cand Env)

/-- A candidate is valid when it holds in every environment. -/

declarations.name: Valid
declarations.signature_heuristic: def Valid (c : Cand) : Prop

declarations.name: MetamorphicRelation
declarations.signature_heuristic:
structure MetamorphicRelation {Cand : Type u} {Env : Type v} (S : Semantics Cand Env) where
  /-- The syntactic transformation of candidates. -/
  transform : Cand → Cand
  /-- The induced map on environments. -/
  envMap : Env → Env
  /-- Semantic invariance: `T c` holds at `ρ` iff `c` holds at `envMap ρ`. -/
  holds_transform : ∀ ρ c, S.holds ρ (transform c) ↔ S.holds (envMap ρ) c

namespace MetamorphicRelation

variable {Cand : Type u} {Env : Type v} {S : Semantics Cand Env}

/-- Metamorphic relations preserve validity. -/

declarations.name: valid_transform
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem valid_transform (R : MetamorphicRelation S) {c : Cand} (h : S.Valid c) :
    S.Valid (R.transform c)

declarations.signature_heuristic: def refl : MetamorphicRelation S

declarations.signature_heuristic:
def comp (R₂ R₁ : MetamorphicRelation S) : MetamorphicRelation S where
  transform

declarations.signature_heuristic:
lemma comp_surjective {R₂ R₁ : MetamorphicRelation S} (h₂ : Function.Surjective R₂.envMap)
    (h₁ : Function.Surjective R₁.envMap) : Function.Surjective (R₂.comp R₁).envMap

declarations.name: generate
declarations.signature_heuristic:
def generate (gens : List (MetamorphicRelation S)) : ℕ → List (MetamorphicRelation S)
  | 0 => [refl]
  | d + 1 => refl :: gens.flatMap fun R => (generate gens d).map fun Q => R.comp Q

/-- Every generated relation is a composition of generators, hence validity preserving,
and its environment map is surjective when those of the generators are. -/

declarations.name: generate_surjective
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem generate_surjective (gens : List (MetamorphicRelation S))
    (hg : ∀ R ∈ gens, Function.Surjective R.envMap) :
    ∀ d, ∀ R ∈ generate gens d, Function.Surjective R.envMap
  | 0, R, hR => by
    simp only [generate, List.mem_singleton] at hR; subst hR; exact Function.surjective_id
  | d + 1, R, hR => by
    simp only [generate, List.mem_cons, List.mem_flatMap, List.mem_map] at hR
    rcases hR with rfl | ⟨R₂, h₂, Q, hQ, rfl⟩
    · exact Function.surjective_id
    · exact comp_surjective (hg R₂ h₂) (generate_surjective gens hg d Q hQ)

/-- Semantic invariance for every generated relation. -/

declarations.signature_heuristic:

    (hg : ∀ R ∈ gens, Function.Surjective R.envMap) (d : ℕ)

    S.Valid (R.transform c) ↔ S.Valid c

/-!
# Metamorphic relations and the metamorphic filter

A *candidate conjecture* `c : Cand` is interpreted in environments `ρ : Env` through a
decidable satisfaction relation `S.holds ρ c`; it is *valid* when it holds in every
environment.

A *metamorphic relation* is a syntactic transformation `T : Cand → Cand` of candidates
together with an environment map `m : Env → Env` such that

  `S.holds ρ (T c) ↔ S.holds (m ρ) c`   for all `ρ`, `c`   (*semantic invariance*).

Consequently `T` maps valid candidates to valid candidates, and when `m` is surjective
`T c` is valid exactly when `c` is.  Metamorphic relations compose, and a
*property-based generator* produces all compositions of a list of basic relations up to a
given depth.

The *metamorphic filter* runs a stream of test environments against a candidate and all of
its metamorphic images.  It is sound (it never refutes a valid candidate), monotone in the
number of steps, and — when its test stream is exhaustive — every invalid candidate, in
particular every candidate one of whose metamorphic images fails somewhere, is refuted
after finitely many steps.
-/
/-- Decidable semantics of candidate conjectures `Cand` in environments `Env`. -/
/-- `holds ρ c`: candidate `c` is true in environment `ρ`. -/
/-- Satisfaction is decidable (it can be tested). -/
/-- A candidate is valid when it holds in every environment. -/
/-- A metamorphic relation: a candidate transformation with a semantic-invariance law. -/
/-- The syntactic transformation of candidates. -/
/-- The induced map on environments. -/
/-- Semantic invariance: `T c` holds at `ρ` iff `c` holds at `envMap ρ`. -/
/-- Metamorphic relations preserve validity. -/
/-- A candidate whose metamorphic image is invalid is itself invalid. -/

/-- **Semantic invariance.** If the environment map is surjective, `T c` is valid exactly
when `c` is valid. -/
/-- The identity metamorphic relation. -/
/-- Composition of metamorphic relations: first `R₁`, then `R₂`. -/
/-- **Property-based generator.** All compositions of at most `d` relations from `gens`. -/

/-- Every generated relation is a composition of generators, hence validity preserving,
and its environment map is surjective when those of the generators are. -/
/-- Semantic invariance for every generated relation. -/
/-- Generators appear among the depth-`d+1` generated relations (as `R ∘ id`). -/

/-- A metamorphic filter: a stream of test environments and a list of metamorphic
relations whose images are tested alongside the candidate. -/
/-- The `k`-th test environment. -/
/-- The metamorphic relations checked by the filter. -/

/-- The test environment `ρ` exposes `c`: either `c` itself or one of its metamorphic
images fails at `ρ`. -/
/-- The filter refutes `c` within `n` steps (using the tests `0, …, n-1`). -/
/-- The test stream is exhaustive: every invalid candidate fails at some test. -/
/-- A violation at any environment certifies invalidity. -/
/-- **Soundness of the filter.** A refuted candidate is invalid. -/
/-- The filter never refutes a valid candidate. -/
/-- **Monotonicity in resources.** More steps refute at least as much. -/

/-- **Finite refutation.** With an exhaustive test stream every invalid candidate is
refuted after finitely many steps. -/
/-- With an exhaustive test stream, the filter is a semi-decision procedure for invalidity. -/

/-- **Candidates violating a metamorphic invariant are refuted in finitely many steps.**
If some metamorphic image `R.transform c` fails in some environment (for any metamorphic
relation `R`, not necessarily one used by the filter), the filter refutes `c` after finitely
many steps. -/

/-- The refutation time of a candidate: the least number of steps after which the filter
refutes it (and `0` if it is never refuted). -/
/-- An invalid candidate is refuted at its refutation time and at every later step. -/
/-- Before its refutation time a candidate is not refuted. -/

declarations.name: PipelineState
declarations.signature_heuristic:
structure PipelineState (Cand : Type u) where
  /-- Accepted lemmas, in order of acceptance. -/
  lib : List Cand
  /-- Refuted candidates, most recent first. -/
  refuted : List Cand
  /-- Remaining resource budget. -/
  budget : ℝ

/-- The components of the autonomous conjecturer pipeline. -/

declarations.name: Pipeline
declarations.signature_heuristic:
structure Pipeline {Cand : Type u} {Env : Type v} (S : Semantics Cand Env) where
  /-- The conjecturer: proposes a candidate at round `t` given the current library. -/
  conj : ℕ → List Cand → Cand
  /-- Estimated probability that the candidate will be certified. -/
  prob : ℕ → List Cand → Cand → ℝ
  /-- Estimates are below `1` (failure is always possible). -/
  prob_lt_one : ∀ t lib c, prob t lib c < 1
  /-- Net odds paid on a certified lemma. -/
  odds : ℝ
  odds_pos : 0 < odds
  /-- Resource cost of one metamorphic test step. -/
  cost : ℝ
  cost_pos : 0 < cost
  /-- The metamorphic filter. -/
  filter : MetamorphicFilter S
  /-- The verifier, which may use the lemmas in the library. -/
  verify : List Cand → Cand → Bool
  /-- Relative soundness of the verifier: from a valid library it only certifies valid
  candidates. -/
  verify_sound : ∀ lib c, (∀ l ∈ lib, S.Valid l) → verify lib c = true → S.Valid c

/-!
# Liveness of the proof verification consensus protocol

Under the fairness hypothesis that, after an orchestrator proposes a valid artifact `a`,
every honest node eventually processes (signs, if its checker accepts) every shard of `a`,
and some node afterwards submits `a` for certification, the artifact ends up in the
certified log with a verifying receipt — regardless of what the adversary schedules
before, in between, or afterwards.

`honest_round_certifies` is the bounded form: the explicit honest schedule
`honestRound` of length `2 + |honest| * |a|` certifies `a` from any reachable state.
-/
/-- Once proposed, an artifact stays pending until it is certified. -/

/-- A `sign n s` event anywhere in a schedule registers the signature, provided node `n`
is willing to sign `s` (it is corrupted or its checker accepts `s`). -/

/-- Assumptions for liveness: honest checkers are complete for valid shards, and there are
at least `quorum` honest nodes. -/
/-- Once all honest nodes have signed a valid shard, it has quorum. -/

/-- **Liveness: valid proofs terminate in certified state commitments.**
Start from any reachable state and run an arbitrary adversarial schedule `pre`, then an
orchestrator proposal of a valid artifact `a`, then an arbitrary schedule `mid` in which every
honest node gets to process every shard of `a` (fairness; adversarial events may be freely
interleaved), then a certification request by any node, then an arbitrary schedule `post`.
In the final state, `a` is in the certified log, the state commitment is the hash chain of
the log, and the ledger holds a verifying receipt for `a`. -/

/-- The honest round for artifact `a`: the orchestrator proposes it, every honest node signs
every shard, and the gateway requests certification. -/

/-- **Bounded termination.** From any reachable state, after any adversarial prefix, the honest
round (of length `2 + |honest| * |a|`) certifies a valid artifact `a`, whatever the adversary
does afterwards. -/

  | orchestrator
  | solver
  | gateway
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Static configuration of a verification fabric. -/

declarations.name: Fabric
declarations.signature_heuristic:
structure Fabric (Node Shard C : Type) where
  /-- The role of each node. Only orchestrators may propose artifacts. -/
  role : Node → Role
  /-- The shard checker run by each node (heterogeneous: one per node). -/
  checker : Node → Shard → Bool
  /-- Number of distinct signatures needed for a shard to reach quorum. -/
  quorum : ℕ
  /-- The commitment function: new state commitment from the previous one and an artifact. -/
  hash : C → List Shard → C
  /-- The genesis state commitment. -/
  genesis : C

/-- Events of the protocol. The adversary chooses any sequence of them. -/

declarations.name: Event
declarations.signature_heuristic:
inductive Event (Node Shard : Type)
  /-- node `n` proposes an artifact (effective only for orchestrators) -/
  | propose (n : Node) (a : List Shard)
  /-- node `n` signs shard `s` (honest nodes sign only what their checker accepts) -/
  | sign (n : Node) (s : Shard)
  /-- node `n` asks the ledger to certify artifact `a` -/
  | certify (n : Node) (a : List Shard)

/-- A receipt: the artifact, a quorum certificate (a signer set per shard), and the state
commitments before and after. Receipts are plain data that anyone could fabricate; they
are only meaningful once checked with `VerifyReceipt`. -/

declarations.name: Receipt
declarations.signature_heuristic:
structure Receipt (Node Shard C : Type) where
  artifact : List Shard
  cert : List (Shard × Finset Node)
  prev : C
  commit : C

/-- Global protocol state. -/

declarations.name: State
declarations.signature_heuristic:

/-!
# Distributed proof verification consensus: the protocol

A *proof artifact* (for example a Lean development) is split into *proof shards*.  Each
node of the fabric runs its own (possibly different) shard checker.  A node endorses a shard
by signing it; a shard reaches *quorum* once at least `quorum` distinct nodes have signed it.
An artifact all of whose shards have quorum can be *certified*: it is appended to the
certified log, the state commitment is advanced by the commitment function, and a
receipt is issued.

## Cryptographic model

Signatures follow the ideal signature functionality (the symbolic, Dolev–Yao style
treatment of an existentially unforgeable signature scheme): the fabric keeps a registry
`sigs` of pairs `(node, shard)` that have been signed, and signature verification means
membership in the registry.  The only way a pair `(n, s)` enters the registry is a
`sign n s` event, and for an honest node `n` that event only takes effect when the node's
own checker accepts `s`.  Corrupted nodes (the set `corrupt`) may sign anything.  The
adversary fully controls the schedule: it picks an arbitrary list of events.

The commitment function `hash` is abstract; binding results assume it is injective
(the usual idealisation of a collision-resistant hash).
-/
/-- The heterogeneous roles of nodes in the fabric. -/
/-- Static configuration of a verification fabric. -/
/-- The role of each node. Only orchestrators may propose artifacts. -/
/-- The shard checker run by each node (heterogeneous: one per node). -/
/-- Number of distinct signatures needed for a shard to reach quorum. -/
/-- The commitment function: new state commitment from the previous one and an artifact. -/
/-- The genesis state commitment. -/
/-- Events of the protocol. The adversary chooses any sequence of them. -/
/-- node `n` proposes an artifact (effective only for orchestrators) -/
/-- node `n` signs shard `s` (honest nodes sign only what their checker accepts) -/
/-- node `n` asks the ledger to certify artifact `a` -/

/-- A receipt: the artifact, a quorum certificate (a signer set per shard), and the state
commitments before and after. Receipts are plain data that anyone could fabricate; they
are only meaningful once checked with `VerifyReceipt`. -/
/-- Global protocol state. -/
/-- proposed, not yet certified artifacts -/
/-- the signature registry -/
/-- the certified log, newest first -/
/-- the current state commitment -/
/-- receipts issued so far, newest first -/
/-- The nodes that have signed shard `s`. -/
/-- Shard `s` has reached quorum in the registry `sigs`. -/

/-- Verification of a receipt against a signature registry: every shard of the artifact
is covered by a certificate entry naming at least `quorum` nodes, each of which has a
registered signature on that shard, and the new commitment is the commitment of the
artifact on top of the previous one. -/
/-- The receipt the ledger issues when it certifies `a` in state `st`. -/
/-- The state commitment of a log (newest first): a hash chain from genesis. -/
/-- The initial state. -/
/-- One protocol step. Ineffective events leave the state unchanged. -/
/-- Run a schedule of events. -/
/-- States reachable from the initial state under some adversarial schedule. -/

/-!
# Safety of the proof verification consensus protocol

* `Inv` is an inductive invariant of every reachable state.
* `no_false_shard_quorum`: an invalid shard never reaches quorum.
* `receipt_unforgeable`: any receipt — including one fabricated by the adversary — that
  verifies against the signature registry of a reachable state certifies only valid shards,
  each endorsed by at least `quorum - |corrupt|` honest nodes whose own checkers accepted it.
* `log_sound`, `head_eq_chain`, `chain_injective`: every certified artifact is valid, and the
  state commitment is the hash chain of the log, which binds the whole log when the
  commitment function is injective.
-/
/-- The inductive invariant of the protocol. -/
/-- The receipt issued by the ledger verifies whenever all shards had quorum. -/
/-- Every reachable state satisfies the invariant. -/

/-- The trust assumptions for safety: honest checkers are sound for the validity predicate
(heterogeneous implementations, each proved sound), and there are fewer corrupted nodes
than the quorum size. -/
/-- Counting lemma: a set of at least `q` nodes contains at least `q - |corrupt|` honest ones. -/

/-- The honest endorsers of shard `s` in a reachable state: honest nodes with a registered
signature on `s`; each of them ran its own checker and it accepted `s`. -/

/-- **Safety: no false proof shard can achieve quorum.** In every reachable state, under any
adversarial schedule, a shard that is not valid does not have quorum. -/

/-- **Non-forgeable receipts.** Let `r` be *any* receipt (it may have been fabricated by the
adversary) that verifies against the signature registry of a reachable state. Then every
shard of `r.artifact` is valid and, for each shard, the certificate names at least
`quorum - |corrupt|` honest nodes (so at least one) that signed it after their own checker
accepted it. Moreover the receipt's commitment is the commitment of the artifact. -/
/-- A verified receipt can never contain a false shard. -/
/-- Every certified artifact in a reachable state is valid (all of its shards are valid). -/
/-- Every receipt issued by the ledger verifies, and so certifies only valid shards. -/
/-- The state commitment of a reachable state is the hash chain of its certified log. -/

/-- **Binding of state commitments.** If the commitment function is injective (idealised
collision resistance) and the genesis commitment is never a hash output, the hash chain
is injective: a state commitment determines the entire certified log. -/

/-- Two reachable states (possibly under different schedules) with the same state
commitment have the same certified log. -/

/-!
# The Sovereign Cognitive Node fabric: three heterogeneous nodes

* **Node Alpha** — orchestrator (the only node allowed to propose artifacts);
* **Node Beta** — solver;
* **Node Gamma** — gateway (in the honest round it submits artifacts for certification).

Each node runs its own shard checker; the quorum is `2` of `3`. We prove that, with at most
one Byzantine node (any one of the three, including the orchestrator or the gateway):

* no false proof shard ever reaches quorum, and every verifying receipt is non-forgeable
  (`sovereign_safety`, `sovereign_receipt_unforgeable`);
* a valid artifact is certified by the honest round, with a verifying receipt and a
  state commitment equal to the hash chain of the log (`sovereign_liveness`).

`two_corrupt_breaks_safety` shows that the fault bound is necessary: two colluding nodes
can push a false shard to quorum.  A small executable demo closes the file.
-/
/-- The three nodes of the Sovereign Cognitive Node fabric. -/
/-- Roles: Alpha orchestrates, Beta solves, Gamma is the gateway. -/

/-- The Sovereign fabric with heterogeneous checkers `chkAlpha`, `chkBeta`, `chkGamma`,
a 2-of-3 quorum, and commitment function `hash` starting from `genesis`. -/

/-- With at most one Byzantine node and sound checkers on the honest nodes, the safety
assumptions hold for the Sovereign fabric. -/

/-- With at most one Byzantine node and complete checkers on the honest nodes, the liveness
assumptions hold for the Sovereign fabric. -/

/-- **Safety for the Sovereign fabric.** With at most one Byzantine node and sound checkers on
the honest nodes, in every reachable state no false proof shard has quorum, and every
certified artifact consists of valid shards. -/

/-- **Non-forgeable receipts for the Sovereign fabric.** With at most one Byzantine node, any
receipt (possibly adversarially fabricated) that verifies against a reachable state's
signature registry certifies only valid shards; each shard is vouched for by an honest node
whose own checker accepted it; and the commitment is the hash of the artifact on top of the
previous commitment. -/

/-- **Liveness for the Sovereign fabric.** With at most one Byzantine node and complete
checkers on the honest nodes, from any reachable state and after any adversarial prefix,
the honest round — Alpha proposes the valid artifact `a`, every honest node signs every
shard, Gamma submits it — certifies `a`: it enters the log, the state commitment is the hash
chain of the log, and a verifying receipt for `a` is issued; this persists under any
adversarial suffix. The round has `2 + |honest| * |a|` events. -/
/-! ## A concrete instance and the necessity of the fault bound -/
/-- Toy proof shards: claims `a * b = c` over `ℕ`. -/
/-- Validity of a toy shard. -/
/-- Alpha's checker: direct multiplication. -/
/-- Beta's checker: commuted multiplication. -/
/-- Gamma's checker: repeated addition. -/

/-- Symbolic commitments: the commitment of a log is the log itself (an injective
commitment function, as required by `chain_injective`). -/

/-- In the demo fabric every node's checker is sound and complete, so the Sovereign
safety and liveness theorems apply for any single Byzantine node. -/
/-- The demo commitments are binding: the state commitment determines the certified log. -/

/-- **The fault bound is necessary.** If two nodes (here Alpha and Beta) are corrupted, they
can push the false shard `2 * 2 = 5` to quorum. -/

/-- A demo run with Gamma corrupted: it tries to sign the false shard `(2,2,5)`; the honest
round for the valid artifact `[(2,3,6), (4,5,20)]` then certifies it. -/

/-!
# Observation: conjecture sampling from structural analogies

The *observation* phase of the discovery cycle produces candidate lemmas by transporting known
theorems along **structural analogies**.  An analogy is a syntactic transformation of statements
(`Analogy.map`); a conjecture is obtained by picking a known theorem `(i, φ)` of the knowledge
base and an analogy `a`, and proposing `a.map φ`, citing the source theorem `i`.

Which (analogy, source) pairs are tried is decided by a *sampler* — an arbitrary, possibly
random, possibly adversarial function.  Nothing about the sampler is trusted.

Main results:
* `mem_observe` — every observed conjecture is an analogical image of a known theorem, cites
  exactly that theorem and carries a fresh identifier;
* `observe_valid` — if the knowledge base is valid and the analogies are *sound*
  (validity-preserving), every observed conjecture is valid;
* `MetamorphicRelation.toAnalogy_sound`, `renameAnalogy_sound`, `symmAnalogy_sound` — every
  metamorphic relation (in particular variable renaming and symmetry of equality) is a sound
  structural analogy.
-/
/-- A structural analogy: a syntactic transformation of statements. -/
/-- The transformation transporting a known statement to an analogous one. -/
/-- An analogy is *sound* if it maps valid statements to valid statements. -/
/-- Every metamorphic relation induces a sound structural analogy. -/
/-- The analogy "rename the variables along a permutation". -/
/-- The analogy "swap the sides of an equation". -/
/-- An identifier strictly above every identifier of the visible knowledge base. -/
/-- The conjecture obtained from a pick `(analogy index, source index)`, under identifier `id`. -/

/-- The observation phase: turn the sampler's picks into conjectures with pairwise distinct
fresh identifiers. -/

/-- **Observed conjectures are analogical images of known theorems.** Each cites exactly its
source theorem and has a fresh identifier. -/

/-- **Soundness of analogical observation.** If every known theorem is valid and every analogy
is sound, then every observed conjecture is valid. -/

  /-- Successor states of a partial proof (untrusted). -/
  expand : S → List S
  /-- Embedding of states into the Poincaré ball (untrusted). -/
  embed : S → PoincareBall n
  /-- Read off a finished proof from a state, if any (untrusted). -/
  extract : S → Option Out
  /-- Beam width. -/
  width : ℕ
  /-- The depth-dependent Kelly model (success probability `p₀ e^{-λR}`). -/
  model : HorizonModel

namespace BeamSearch

variable {S Out : Type} {n : ℕ} (B : BeamSearch S Out n)

theorem search_spec : ∀ (k : ℕ) (beam : List S) {o : Out}, B.search k beam = some o →
    ∃ j ≤ k, ∃ s ∈ B.step^[j] beam, B.extract s = some o

    obtain ⟨s, hs, he⟩

/-!
# Proof search: Poincaré hyperbolic beam search with a Kelly branch budget

The proof-search phase explores partial proofs (states of an arbitrary type `S`).  Each state is
embedded in the Poincaré ball `Dⁿ` (`embed`, untrusted, e.g. a learned embedding); its
*hyperbolic depth* is its distance `d_H(0, x)` from the root.  Using the depth-dependent Kelly
model of `Sovereign.Autonomous.Horizon`, a branch at depth `R` is **funded** iff its Kelly
fraction `f*(R)` is positive, i.e. iff it lies strictly inside the epistemic horizon ball.

One beam step expands every state of the beam, drops unfunded children (Kelly branch budget),
sorts the funded children by hyperbolic depth (equivalently: by decreasing Kelly fraction) and
keeps the best `width` of them.  The search runs for a given number of rounds — the compute
units allotted to the conjecture by the Kelly allocation of the engine — and returns the first
output (e.g. a proof tree) extracted from a beam.

Main results:
* `length_select_le` — the beam never exceeds its width;
* `funded_of_mem_select`, `mem_horizonBall_of_mem_select`, `kelly_pos_of_mem_select` — every
  retained branch has positive Kelly fraction and lies inside the epistemic horizon ball;
* `select_optimal` — the beam keeps the funded children of largest Kelly fraction: every
  discarded funded child has Kelly fraction at most that of every retained one;
* `search_spec` — the output of the search was extracted from a state reached within the
  allotted number of rounds; `search_zero_rounds` — no rounds, no expansion.
-/
/-- A hyperbolic beam search over states `S`, returning outputs of type `Out`. -/
/-- Successor states of a partial proof (untrusted). -/
/-- Embedding of states into the Poincaré ball (untrusted). -/
/-- Read off a finished proof from a state, if any (untrusted). -/
/-- Beam width. -/
/-- The depth-dependent Kelly model (success probability `p₀ e^{-λR}`). -/
/-- Hyperbolic depth of a state: its distance from the root of the Poincaré ball. -/
/-- Kelly fraction of the branch through `s`. -/
/-- Kelly branch budget: a branch is funded iff its Kelly fraction is positive. -/
/-- Comparison by hyperbolic depth. -/
/-- Beam selection: keep the `width` shallowest funded states. -/
/-- One beam step: expand, then select. -/
/-- Run the beam search for `k` rounds from `beam`, returning the first extracted output. -/
/-! ### Beam invariants -/
/-- Every retained branch lies strictly inside the epistemic horizon. -/
/-- Every retained branch lies in the hyperbolic horizon ball of the Poincaré ball. -/

/-- **Optimality of beam selection.** A funded child that is discarded is at least as deep as,
hence has Kelly fraction at most that of, every retained state. -/
/-- Every state of a beam produced by a step is funded and inside the horizon. -/
/-! ### The search -/

/-- **Search specification.** An output returned within `k` rounds was extracted from a state
of the `j`-th beam for some `j ≤ k`. -/

/-- If a finished proof can be read off the initial beam, the search returns it whatever the
number of rounds. -/
/-- With no compute units the search performs no expansion. -/
/-- All beams after the first step respect the width and the horizon. -/

/-!
# A concrete discovery engine, two verified cycles, and axiom checks

`demoEngine` instantiates the discovery engine with the concrete sound kernel of
`Sovereign.Bridge.Kernel`, the metamorphic filter `Sovereign.Bridge.demoFilter`, the symmetry
analogy, and a trivial beam search.  We check that the loop is not vacuous:
* cycle `0` bootstraps the empty knowledge base with the exploratory conjecture `2 + 2 = 4`,
  proved by the kernel's ground-evaluation rule (`demo_verified_zero`);
* cycle `1` transports it along the symmetry analogy to the conjecture `4 = 2 + 2`, citing the
  first theorem, proved by the kernel's symmetry rule (`demo_verified_one`);
so both cycles strictly enlarge the provable theorem set (`demo_expansion`).
-/
/-- The statement `2 + 2 = 4`. -/
/-- A Kelly horizon model: `p₀ = 1`, decay `1`, odds `1`. -/

/-- The candidate proof of a conjecture: ground evaluation if it cites nothing, symmetry of the
first cited fact otherwise. -/
/-- The concrete discovery engine. -/
/-- The first theorem: `2 + 2 = 4`, with its compressed ground-evaluation certificate. -/
/-- The second theorem: `4 = 2 + 2`, obtained by analogy, with its symmetry certificate. -/

/-- Both demo cycles strictly enlarge the provable theorem set; `4 = 2 + 2` was discovered by the
symmetry analogy and is provable after two cycles. -/
/-! ### Axiom checks -/

declarations.name: DiscoveryEngine
declarations.signature_heuristic:
structure DiscoveryEngine (R S Ω : Type) (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The structural analogies used for observation. -/
  analogies : List Analogy
  /-- The random sampler: at round `t`, with seed `ω`, given the visible knowledge base, the
  (analogy index, source index) picks to try (untrusted). -/
  sampler : Ω → ℕ → List (ℕ × Expr) → List (ℕ × ℕ)
  /-- Exploratory (bootstrap) conjectures, e.g. enumerated from a grammar; needed to seed an
  empty knowledge base, where no analogy has a source (untrusted). -/
  explore : Ω → ℕ → List (ℕ × Expr) → List Proposal
  /-- Confidence logit of a conjecture (untrusted). -/
  logit : List (ℕ × Expr) → Proposal → ℝ
  /-- The hyperbolic beam search (untrusted expansion, embedding and extraction). -/
  beam : BeamSearch S (PTree R) n
  /-- Initial beam for a conjecture (untrusted). -/
  seedBeam : ℕ → List (ℕ × Expr) → Proposal → List S
  /-- The trusted kernel, indexed by the cited facts. -/
  rules : List Expr → RuleSystem R Expr
  /-- Relative soundness of the kernel — the only trust assumption. -/
  rules_sound : ∀ Γ, (∀ φ ∈ Γ, stmtSem.Valid φ) → (rules Γ).Sound stmtSem.Valid
  /-- The metamorphic filter. -/
  filter : MetamorphicFilter stmtSem
  /-- Number of metamorphic test steps. -/
  testSteps : ℕ
  /-- Net odds paid by a verified discovery. -/
  odds : ℝ
  odds_pos : 0 < odds
  /-- Compute budget per cycle for proof search. -/
  budget : ℝ
  /-- Confidence logit for the cycle as a whole, used to size the bankroll stake (untrusted). -/
  cycleLogit : List (ℕ × Expr) → ℝ

/-!

One **discovery cycle** `t`, run on the knowledge base `KB` (a `Sovereign.Bridge.Library`):

1. **Observation** (`Sovereign.Discovery.Analogy`): a random sampler (seed `ω : Ω`) picks pairs
   (structural analogy, known theorem); each pick becomes a conjecture `a.map φ` citing the
   source theorem, under a fresh identifier.  An untrusted exploratory generator may add further
   conjectures; it is needed to bootstrap an empty knowledge base, where analogies have no
   source.
2. **Filter** (`Sovereign.Bridge.Filter`): well-typedness, non-tautology, the circularity audit
   (`NonCircular`: fresh identifier, citations resolve to earlier theorems, not a restatement)
   and the metamorphic audit (`MetamorphicFilter.refutedWithin`).  Then the Kelly gate: only
   conjectures with positive Kelly fraction are kept.
3. **Proof search** (`Sovereign.Discovery.BeamSearch`): each gated conjecture receives its
   Kelly-proportional share of the compute budget (`Sovereign.Bridge.kellyUnits`) and a
   Poincaré hyperbolic beam search with Kelly branch budget is run for that many rounds.
4. **Verification**: the proof tree returned by the search is checked by the trusted kernel
   (`RuleSystem.checkDag`) against the cited theorems.
5. **Compression**: the proof tree is quotiented into its minimal proof DAG
   (`Sovereign.Compression.dedup`) before being checked and stored.
6. **Knowledge-base integration**: the certified lemma is appended to the knowledge base.

The cycle is an instance of the end-to-end engine `Sovereign.Bridge.Engine` (`toEngine`), whose
generator is the analogical sampler and whose prover is the hyperbolic beam search.

Alongside the knowledge base the engine keeps a **bankroll**: at each cycle it stakes the
(non-negative part of the) Kelly fraction of its cycle confidence; the stake pays at the odds
`odds` if the cycle is verified (at least one new certified theorem) and is lost otherwise.

The only trust assumption is the relative soundness of the kernel (`rules_sound`); the sampler,
the confidence logits, the embedding, the expansion function and the proof extractor are
arbitrary.

**Monotonic expansion theorem** (`monotonic_expansion`): for every seed, every verified cycle
strictly enlarges the set of kernel-certified theorems, this set never shrinks, and for *every*
probability measure on seeds, absorbing ruin of the bankroll and commitment of an inconsistent
knowledge base both have probability `0`.

/-- Phase 1, observation: the analogical conjectures of cycle `t`, followed by the exploratory

/-- Phase 2, filter: the conjectures surviving the audits and the Kelly gate. -/

/-!
# Min-entropy sources, universal hashing and the leftover hash lemma

Finite probability distributions are real-valued mass functions (`FinDist`).

* `FinDist.minEntropy`: `H∞(P) = -log₂ maxₐ P(a)`; `le_minEntropy_iff`: `k ≤ H∞(P)` iff every
  outcome has probability at most `2^{-k}`.
* `FinDist.iid`: `n` independent samples; `iid_prob_le`: the maximal probability of the product
  is at most `ηⁿ`; `minEntropy_iid`: min-entropy adds up over independent samples.
* `IsUniversal`: a 2-universal hash family `h : S → X → Y`; `allFunctions_isUniversal`: the
  family of all functions `X → Y` is universal (so universal families exist).
* `hashOutput`: the joint distribution of a uniformly random seed `s` and the extracted string
  `h s x`; `statDist`: statistical (total variation) distance.
* `leftover_hash`: **leftover hash lemma**. If every source outcome has probability `≤ η` then
  `statDist (hashOutput) uniform ≤ ½ √(|Y| η)`. This is information-theoretic: no computational
  assumption is made.
* `distinguisher_advantage_le`: every distinguisher (any event `A`, with no restriction on its
  complexity) has advantage at most the statistical distance.
-/
/-- A probability distribution on a finite type, as a real mass function. -/
/-- The uniform distribution on a nonempty finite type. -/
/-- The largest point probability `maxₐ P(a)`. -/
/-- **Min-entropy** `H∞(P) = -log₂ maxₐ P(a)`. -/
/-- `H∞(P) ≥ k` iff every outcome has probability at most `2^{-k}`. -/
/-- `n` independent, identically distributed samples. -/
/-- The point probabilities of `n` independent samples are at most `ηⁿ`. -/
/-- Min-entropy is additive over independent samples: `H∞(Pⁿ) ≥ n k` if `H∞(P) ≥ k`. -/

/-- A **2-universal hash family** `h : S → X → Y`: two distinct inputs collide for at most a
`1/|Y|` fraction of the seeds. -/
/-- Statistical (total variation) distance `½ ∑ |P(a) - Q(a)|`. -/

/-- The joint distribution of a uniform seed `s` and the extracted value `h s x`, where `x` is
drawn from the source `P`. -/
/-- The collision probability of the hashed output. -/
-- exchange sums over seeds and pairs

/-- **Leftover hash lemma.** If every outcome of the source has probability at most `η`
(i.e. `H∞ ≥ -log₂ η`), the seed together with the hashed output is within statistical distance
`½ √(|Y| η)` of the uniform distribution on `S × Y`. -/
-- sum of squared deviations

/-- **Unconditional indistinguishability.** For every distinguishing event `A` — with no
restriction on the computational power of the distinguisher — the probabilities of `A` under two
distributions differ by at most their statistical distance. -/
/-- The seeded family of *all* functions `X → Y` (seed `s`, output `s x`) is 2-universal. -/

/-!
# Thermal noise digitised by an ADC: min-entropy bounds

A **continuous noise channel** (`NoiseChannel`) is a probability law on the real line (the analog
noise voltage) whose density is bounded by `M`: `P(s) ≤ M · vol(s)` for every set `s`.

A `b`-bit **ADC** (`ADC`) with lower rail `lo` and step `Δ > 0` outputs the code
`clamp(⌊(v - lo)/Δ⌋, 0, 2ᵇ - 1)` (`ADC.code`). The two saturation codes collect the tails.

* `ADC.outputDist`: the distribution of the digitised sample, a `FinDist (Fin (2 ^ b))`.
* `ADC.outputDist_le`: every code has probability at most `max (M Δ) η`, where `η` bounds the
  two tail probabilities `P(v < lo + Δ)` and `P(v ≥ lo + (2ᵇ-1) Δ)`;
  `ADC.minEntropy_ge`: hence `H∞ ≥ -log₂ max (M Δ) η`.
* Thermal (Johnson–Nyquist) noise: `thermalChannel μ v` is the Gaussian law with mean `μ` and
  variance `v`, e.g. `v = 4 k_B T R B` (`johnsonNyquistVariance`); its density is bounded by
  `1/√(2πv)` (`gaussianReal_le_density`), and its tails are controlled by Chebyshev's inequality
  (`gaussian_tail_lower`, `gaussian_tail_upper`).
* `thermal_minEntropy_ge`: the digitised thermal sample has
  `H∞ ≥ δ := -log₂ max (Δ/√(2πv)) (max (v/c₋²) (v/c₊²))`, where `c₋`, `c₊` are the distances from
  the mean to the saturation thresholds; `thermal_delta_pos`: `δ > 0` as soon as the three
  quantities are `< 1`.
* `thermalADC_spec`, `exists_adc_minEntropy_ge_two`: for every positive noise variance there is a 5-bit ADC whose
  digitised thermal samples have `H∞ ≥ 2` bits (so the hypotheses are satisfiable).
-/

/-- A `b`-bit analog-to-digital converter with lower rail `lo` and step `Δ`. -/
/-- The top code `2ᵇ - 1`. -/
/-- The ADC code of a voltage `v`: `⌊(v - lo)/Δ⌋` clamped to `[0, 2ᵇ - 1]`. -/

lemma resolvent_telescope (N : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) {a : ℂ} (ha : a ≠ 0) (m : ℕ) :
    (a • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) - N) * (∑ k ∈ Finset.range m, (a ^ (k + 1))⁻¹ • N ^ k) =

declarations.name: resolvent_mul_EP
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem resolvent_mul_EP {m : ℕ} {H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ} {E : ℂ}
    (hN : (H - E • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ)) ^ m = 0) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ≠ E) :
    greenFn H z = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range m,
      ((z - E) ^ (k + 1))⁻¹ • (H - E • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ)) ^ k

declarations.name: IsEPOrder.green_pole
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem IsEPOrder.green_pole {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) {H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ} {E : ℂ}
    (h : IsEPOrder m H E) :
    ∃ i j : Fin n, ((H - E • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ)) ^ (m - 1)) i j ≠ 0 ∧
      Tendsto (fun η : ℝ => (I * η) ^ m * greenFn H (E + I * η) i j) (𝓝[≠] 0)
        (𝓝 (((H - E • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ)) ^ (m - 1)) i j))

comments.text:
/-!
# Exceptional points of arbitrary order, biorthogonal projectors and the Petermann factor

General finite-dimensional theory for a (non-Hermitian) Hamiltonian `H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ`.

**Exceptional points.** `IsEPOrder m H E` says that `H` has an exceptional point of order `m`
(an `EPm`) at the energy `E`: `(H - E)^m = 0` while `(H - E)^(m-1) ≠ 0`. For an `n × n` matrix with
`m = n` this means `H` is a single `n × n` Jordan block.
* `IsEPOrder.eigenvalue_eq`: every eigenvalue equals `E` (eigenvalue coalescence).
* `IsEPOrder.eigvec_coalesce`: for `m = n` all eigenvectors are proportional to a single one
  (eigenvector coalescence; geometric multiplicity one).
* `IsEPOrder.self_orthogonal`: for `m = n ≥ 2`, every left eigenvector `u` and every right
  eigenvector `v` satisfy `uᵀ v = 0` (the self-orthogonality that makes the biorthogonal
  normalisation, and hence the Petermann factor, blow up at an EP).

**Biorthogonal projectors.** `biorthProj u v = v uᵀ / (uᵀ v)`, built from a right eigenvector `v`
and a left eigenvector `u`:
* `biorthProj_idem`, `biorthProj_trace`, `mul_biorthProj`, `biorthProj_mul`,
  `biorthProj_mulVec_right`, `vecMul_biorthProj_left`, `biorthProj_smul_smul`.

**Petermann factor.** `petermann u v = ‖u‖² ‖v‖² / |uᵀ v|²`.
* `frobSq_biorthProj`: it equals the squared Frobenius norm of the biorthogonal projector.
* `one_le_petermann`: `K ≥ 1`.
* `petermann_star_self`, `IsHermitian.petermann_eq_one`: `K = 1` for Hermitian Hamiltonians.

**Green's function at an EP and emission enhancement.**
* `resolvent_mul_EP`: at an `EPm`, `(z - H)⁻¹ = Σ_{k<m} (H - E)^k / (z - E)^(k+1)`.
* `IsEPOrder.green_pole`: some matrix element of the Green's function satisfies
  `(iη)^m G_ij(E + iη) → ((H - E)^(m-1))_ij ≠ 0` as `η → 0`, i.e. the local density of states
  (which governs spontaneous emission) has a pole of order `m`, instead of the simple pole of an
  isolated non-degenerate resonance.
-/
/-! ## Exceptional points of order `m` -/
/-- `H` has an **exceptional point of order `m`** at energy `E`. -/
/-- **Eigenvalue coalescence**: at an exceptional point every eigenvalue equals `E`. -/

/-- In a Jordan chain `x, Nx, …, N^(n-1)x` of maximal length, the vectors are independent; the
statement is in the shifted form needed below. -/
/-- The kernel of a nilpotent matrix of maximal index is spanned by the end of a Jordan chain. -/

/-- **Eigenvector coalescence** at an `EPn` of an `n × n` Hamiltonian: there is a single
eigenvector `w` and every eigenvector is a multiple of it. -/

/-- **Self-orthogonality at an EP**: at an `EPn` (`n ≥ 2`) every left eigenvector is
orthogonal (in the bilinear, biorthogonal sense) to every right eigenvector. -/
/-! ## Biorthogonal projectors -/

/-- The **biorthogonal projector** `v uᵀ / (uᵀ v)` onto the right eigenvector `v` along the
left eigenvector `u`. -/
/-- The biorthogonal projector does not depend on the normalisation of the eigenvectors. -/
/-! ## The Petermann factor -/
/-- Squared Euclidean norm `‖v‖² = Σ |v_i|²`. -/
/-- Squared Frobenius norm `Σ |M_ij|²`. -/

/-- The **Petermann factor** `K = ‖u‖² ‖v‖² / |uᵀ v|²` of a mode with right eigenvector `v` and
left eigenvector `u`. -/
/-- The Petermann factor is the squared Frobenius norm of the biorthogonal projector. -/
/-- **`K ≥ 1`**: the Petermann factor of any mode with non-vanishing biorthogonal norm. -/
/-- `K = 1` when the left eigenvector is the complex conjugate of the right one. -/

/-- **Hermitian Hamiltonians have `K = 1`**: for a Hermitian `H` every eigenvalue is real, the
conjugate of a right eigenvector is a left eigenvector, and the Petermann factor is `1`. -/
/-! ## Green's function at an exceptional point -/
/-- The Green's function (resolvent) `G(z) = (z - H)⁻¹`. -/

/-- **Resolvent at an EP**: if `(H - E)^m = 0` then
`(z - H)⁻¹ = Σ_{k<m} (H - E)^k / (z - E)^(k+1)` for `z ≠ E`. -/

/-- **Pole of order `m` of the Green's function at an `EPm`**: some matrix element satisfies
`(iη)^m G_ij(E + iη) → ((H - E)^(m-1))_ij ≠ 0` as `η → 0`. Hence `|G_ij(E + iη)|`, and with it
the local density of states governing spontaneous emission, grows like `η^(-m)`. -/

declarations.name: ringH

declarations.name: ringH_sub_sq
declarations.signature_heuristic:
lemma ringH_sub_sq (ω A B : ℂ) :
    (ringH ω A B - ω • (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)) ^ 2 =
      (A * B) • (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)

declarations.name: ringH_isEP_iff
declarations.signature_heuristic: theorem ringH_isEP_iff : IsEPOrder 2 (ringH ω A B) ω ↔ A * B = 0 ∧ (A ≠ 0 ∨ B ≠ 0)

declarations.name: ringH_mulVec
declarations.signature_heuristic:
lemma ringH_mulVec (ω A B : ℂ) (v : Fin 2 → ℂ) :
    ringH ω A B *ᵥ v = ![ω * v 0 + A * v 1, B * v 0 + ω * v 1]

declarations.name: eigen_components
declarations.signature_heuristic:
lemma eigen_components {E : ℂ} {v : Fin 2 → ℂ} (hv : ringH ω A B *ᵥ v = E • v) :
    ω * v 0 + A * v 1 = E * v 0 ∧ B * v 0 + ω * v 1 = E * v 1

declarations.name: vec_ne_zero_iff
declarations.signature_heuristic: lemma vec_ne_zero_iff (v : Fin 2 → ℂ) : v ≠ 0 ↔ v 0 ≠ 0 ∨ v 1 ≠ 0

declarations.name: chirality_of_one_eq_zero
declarations.signature_heuristic:
lemma chirality_of_one_eq_zero {v : Fin 2 → ℂ} (h0 : v 0 ≠ 0) (h1 : v 1 = 0) :
    chirality v = 1

declarations.name: chirality_of_zero_eq_zero
declarations.signature_heuristic:
lemma chirality_of_zero_eq_zero {v : Fin 2 → ℂ} (h0 : v 0 = 0) (h1 : v 1 ≠ 0) :
    chirality v = -1

declarations.name: ringH_eigvec_of_B_eq_zero
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem ringH_eigvec_of_B_eq_zero (hB : B = 0) (hA : A ≠ 0) {E : ℂ} {v : Fin 2 → ℂ}
    (hv0 : v ≠ 0) (hv : ringH ω A B *ᵥ v = E • v) : E = ω ∧ v 1 = 0 ∧ chirality v = 1

declarations.name: ringH_eigvec_of_A_eq_zero

theorem ringH_eigvec_of_A_eq_zero (hA : A = 0) (hB : B ≠ 0) {E : ℂ} {v : Fin 2 → ℂ}
    (hv0 : v ≠ 0) (hv : ringH ω A B *ᵥ v = E • v) : E = ω ∧ v 0 = 0 ∧ chirality v = -1

declarations.name: abs_chirality_lt_one
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem abs_chirality_lt_one (hAB : A * B ≠ 0) {E : ℂ} {v : Fin 2 → ℂ} (hv0 : v ≠ 0)
    (hv : ringH ω A B *ᵥ v = E • v) : |chirality v| < 1

declarations.name: exists_fully_chiral_iff
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem exists_fully_chiral_iff :
    (∃ v : Fin 2 → ℂ, v ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ E : ℂ, ringH ω A B *ᵥ v = E • v ∧ |chirality v| = 1) ↔
      A * B = 0

declarations.name: ringGreen_generic
declarations.signature_heuristic:

/-!
# Chiral mode routing along exceptional arcs

Each unit cell carries an acoustic ring resonator whose clockwise (CW, index `0`) and
counter-clockwise (CCW, index `1`) whispering-gallery modes are coupled by asymmetric
backscattering:

  `ringH ω A B = [[ω, A], [B, ω]]`,

`A` scattering CCW → CW and `B` scattering CW → CCW.

* `ringH_isEP_iff`: `ringH` has an EP2 at `ω` iff `A B = 0` and `(A, B) ≠ 0`. The exceptional set
  splits into two families: `B = 0, A ≠ 0` (**CW arcs**) and `A = 0, B ≠ 0` (**CCW arcs**).
* **Chiral eigenmodes.** `chirality v = (|v_CW|² − |v_CCW|²)/(|v_CW|² + |v_CCW|²)`.
  `ringH_eigvec_of_B_eq_zero` / `ringH_eigvec_of_A_eq_zero`: on a CW (CCW) arc every eigenmode is
  purely CW (CCW), with chirality `+1` (`−1`). `abs_chirality_lt_one`: away from the arcs every
  eigenmode has `|chirality| < 1`; `exists_fully_chiral_iff`: a fully chiral eigenmode exists iff
  `A B = 0`.
* **Chiral routing.** `ringGreen_of_B_eq_zero`: on a CW arc the Green's function is
  `[[1/(z-ω), A/(z-ω)²], [0, 1/(z-ω)]]`: a source in the CCW channel is routed into the CW channel
  (`G_CW,CCW ≠ 0`), but a CW source never reaches the CCW channel (`G_CCW,CW = 0`).
  `routingContrast` of the two transfer amplitudes is exactly `+1` on CW arcs and `−1` on CCW arcs
  (`routingContrast_of_B_eq_zero`, `routingContrast_of_A_eq_zero`), while off the exceptional set
  it equals `(|A|² − |B|²)/(|A|² + |B|²)` (`routingContrast_generic`), strictly between `−1`
  and `1` (`abs_routingContrast_lt_one`).
* **3D lattice with exceptional arcs.** `chiralA k = sin k_x + i sin k_z`,
  `chiralB k = sin k_y + i sin k_z`. `ring3D_EP_iff`: the exceptional set is the union of the CW
  arcs `arcCW = {sin k_y = sin k_z = 0, sin k_x ≠ 0}` and the CCW arcs
  `arcCCW = {sin k_x = sin k_z = 0, sin k_y ≠ 0}` — open segments along `k_x` and along `k_y`
  terminating at the points where `A = B = 0`, where `H = ω` is not defective
  (`ring3D_endpoint_not_EP`). `ring3D_routing_arcCW` / `ring3D_routing_arcCCW`: along every
  CW (CCW) arc all modes have chirality `+1` (`−1`) and routing is unidirectional.
  `arcCWCurve`, `arcCCWCurve` parametrise arcs.
-/
/-- Bloch Hamiltonian of an acoustic ring resonator in the (CW, CCW) basis. -/
/-- Chirality `(|v_CW|² − |v_CCW|²)/(|v_CW|² + |v_CCW|²)` of a mode. -/
/-- **EP2 of the ring resonator**: iff `A B = 0` with `(A, B) ≠ 0`. -/

/-- **On a CW arc (`B = 0`, `A ≠ 0`) every eigenmode is purely clockwise**: its energy is `ω`,
its CCW component vanishes and its chirality is `+1`. -/

/-- **On a CCW arc (`A = 0`, `B ≠ 0`) every eigenmode is purely counter-clockwise**, with
chirality `−1`. -/
/-- **Away from the exceptional arcs no eigenmode is fully chiral.** -/
/-- A fully chiral eigenmode (`|chirality| = 1`) exists **iff** `A B = 0`. -/
/-! ## Chiral routing: the Green's function on and off the exceptional arcs -/
/-- Green's function of the ring resonator away from its eigenvalues. -/
/-- **Unidirectional routing on a CW arc**: `G_CCW,CW = 0` while `G_CW,CCW = A/(z − ω)²`. -/
/-- **Unidirectional routing on a CCW arc**: `G_CW,CCW = 0` while `G_CCW,CW = B/(z − ω)²`. -/

/-- Routing contrast `(|G_CW,CCW|² − |G_CCW,CW|²)/(|G_CW,CCW|² + |G_CCW,CW|²)` of a
2-channel Green's function: `+1` for pure CCW → CW routing, `−1` for pure CW → CCW routing. -/
/-- Off the exceptional set the routing contrast is `(|A|² − |B|²)/(|A|² + |B|²)`. -/
/-- Off the exceptional arcs routing is never perfectly unidirectional. -/
/-! ## A 3D acoustic lattice with exceptional arcs -/
/-- CCW → CW backscattering `A(k) = sin k_x + i sin k_z`. -/
/-- CW → CCW backscattering `B(k) = sin k_y + i sin k_z`. -/
/-- CW exceptional arcs (open segments along `k_x`). -/
/-- CCW exceptional arcs (open segments along `k_y`). -/
/-- **The exceptional set of the 3D ring lattice is the union of the CW and CCW arcs.** -/

/-- At the arc endpoints (`A = B = 0`) the Hamiltonian is `ω · 1`: degenerate but not
defective, so these points are not exceptional. -/

/-- **Chiral routing along the CW arcs**: at every momentum on a CW arc, all eigenmodes are
purely CW (chirality `+1`) and the routing contrast is `+1` at every probe frequency. -/
/-- **Chiral routing along the CCW arcs**: chirality `−1` and routing contrast `−1`. -/
/-- A CW arc: `k_x ↦ (k_x, 0, 0)` for `0 < k_x < π`. -/
/-- A CCW arc: `k_y ↦ (0, k_y, 0)` for `0 < k_y < π`. -/
/-- The two arc families are disjoint: the chirality is locked to the arc family. -/

/-!
# Exceptional surfaces and exceptional lines of EP3s and EP4s in a 3D acoustic lattice

Momentum `k = (k₀, k₁, k₂) = (k_x, k_y, k_z) : Fin 3 → ℝ`. We use two complex `d`-vector fields
on the 3D Brillouin zone and feed them into the 2-, 3- and 4-resonator Bloch Hamiltonians
`H2`, `H3`, `H4` of `SpinModels`:

* **Exceptional surfaces** (`dSurf t γ k = (t (cos k_x + cos k_y + cos k_z), 0, iγ)`): for the
  3-resonator cell this is `H3 = [[2iγ, κ(k), 0], [2κ(k), 0, κ(k)], [0, 2κ(k), -2iγ]]`, a gain –
  neutral – loss cell with momentum-dependent coupling `κ(k)`. Its EP condition is a single real
  equation, `κ(k)² = γ²` (`exceptionalSurface`): `surf_EP3_iff`, `surf_EP4_iff`, `surf_EP2_iff`.
  `surfSheet_mem`, `surfSheet_continuous`, `surfSheet_injective`: the exceptional surface contains
  a continuous, injective image of a square, i.e. a genuine two-dimensional sheet of EP3s (for
  `H3`) and EP4s (for `H4`).
* **Exceptional lines** (`dLine t γ k = (sin k_z + iγ, t (cos k_x + cos k_y), 0)`): now
  `dsq = sin² k_z − γ² + L(k)² + 2iγ sin k_z` and the EP condition consists of *two* real
  equations, `sin k_z = 0` and `L(k)² = γ²` (`exceptionalLine`): `line_EP3_iff`, `line_EP4_iff`,
  `line_EP2_iff`. `lineCurve_mem`, `lineCurve_continuous`, `lineCurve_injective`: the set contains
  a continuous injective curve — a continuous line of EP3s / EP4s in 3D momentum space.

**Petermann factor and emission enhancement near exceptional sets.**
* `petermann2_tendsto_atTop`: for any continuous `d`-field, the Petermann factor diverges on
  approach to any exceptional point.
* `surf_nhds_neBot`, `line_nhds_neBot`: every point of the exceptional surface / line is a limit
  of non-exceptional momenta, so the divergence statements below are not vacuous.
* `surf_petermann_diverges`, `line_petermann_diverges`, and the corresponding
  `…_emission_diverges`: the Petermann-enhanced spontaneous-emission rate
  `Γ = K Γ₀` (`petermannRate`) satisfies `Γ ≥ Γ₀` (`le_petermannRate`) and diverges on approach to
  the exceptional surface and the exceptional lines.
* `line_EP3_green_pole`, `line_EP4_green_pole`, `surf_EP3_green_pole`, `surf_EP4_green_pole`: on
  the exceptional sets the Green's function has a pole of order 3 (EP3) or 4 (EP4).
* `line_self_orthogonal`, `surf_self_orthogonal`: on the exceptional sets the coalesced EP3 and
  EP4 modes are self-orthogonal (`uᵀ v = 0`).
-/
/-! ## Petermann-factor divergence for a general continuous `d`-field -/

/-- **The Petermann factor diverges at exceptional points**: for a continuous field of
`d`-vectors on a space `X`, if `d(k₀)` is exceptional (`dsq = 0`, `d ≠ 0`) then
`K(k) = (1 + ‖d‖²/|d·d|)/2 → ∞` as `k → k₀` through non-exceptional points. -/

/-- The **Petermann-enhanced spontaneous-emission rate** `Γ = K Γ₀` of an emitter coupled to
the upper band of the two-level model (`Γ₀`: rate for a normal, `K = 1`, mode). -/
/-! ## Exceptional surfaces -/
/-- Momentum-dependent coupling `κ(k) = t (cos k_x + cos k_y + cos k_z)`. -/
/-- `d`-vector field of the exceptional-surface model: `(κ(k), 0, iγ)`. -/

/-- **Exceptional surface of EP3s**. -/
/-- **Exceptional surface of EP4s**. -/

/-- A sheet `(k_x, k_y) ↦ (k_x, k_y, arccos(γ/t − cos k_x − cos k_y))` lying in the exceptional
surface. -/
/-- A real number `x` has, arbitrarily close to its right, points where `cos` differs. -/
/-- Every point of the exceptional surface is a limit of non-exceptional momenta. -/
/-- **Petermann factor diverges on approach to the exceptional surface.** -/

/-- **Spontaneous-emission enhancement near the exceptional surface**: the Petermann-enhanced

/-- Exceptional lines of EP2s for the two-resonator cell. -/
/-- A curve `k_x ↦ (k_x, arccos(γ/t − cos k_x), 0)` lying on an exceptional line. -/

/-- The exceptional lines lie in the planes `sin k_z = 0`: they are one-codimension-higher than

/-- On the exceptional surface of `H4`, the Green's function has a fourth-order pole. -/

every left eigenvector is biorthogonally orthogonal to every right eigenvector, so the

/-!
# EP2, EP3 and EP4 from a complex "d-vector": acoustic resonator chains of 2, 3 and 4 sites

Let `d = d_R + i d_I ∈ ℂ³` (the complex coupling vector of a non-Hermitian Bloch Hamiltonian),
`p = d₀ - i d₁`, `q = d₀ + i d₁`, `c = d₂`, and `dsq d = d₀² + d₁² + d₂²` (the *bilinear* square,
so `dsq d = |d_R|² - |d_I|² + 2 i d_R · d_I`).

* `H2 d = [[c, p], [q, -c]] = d · σ` — two coupled acoustic resonators.
* `H3 d = [[2c, p, 0], [2q, 0, p], [0, 2q, -2c]]` — three resonators (a gauge transform of the
  spin-1 matrix `2 d · S`; the coupling products `p · 2q` equal `(√2 p)(√2 q)`).
* `H4 d = [[3c, p, 0, 0], [3q, c, p, 0], [0, 4q, -c, p], [0, 0, 3q, -3c]]` — four resonators
  (a gauge transform of the spin-3/2 matrix `2 d · S`).

The graded on-site terms `±c, ±2c, ±3c` are resonator detunings/gain–loss and `p, q` are the
(forward/backward) couplings; for `d = (κ, 0, iγ)` these are PT-symmetric gain–loss chains.

**Spectra** (`H2_sq`, `H3_cube`, `H4_quartic`, `det_H3_sub`, `det_H4_sub`): the eigenvalues are
`±s`, `{0, ±2s}`, `{±s, ±3s}` with `s² = dsq d`.

**Exceptional points** (`H2_isEP_iff`, `H3_isEP_iff`, `H4_isEP_iff`): `H2`, `H3`, `H4` have an
exceptional point of maximal order (EP2, EP3, EP4: a single Jordan block) at `E = 0` iff
`dsq d = 0` and `d ≠ 0`, i.e. `|d_R| = |d_I|` and `d_R ⊥ d_I` with `d ≠ 0`.

**Biorthogonal projectors and Petermann factor of the two-level model.**
`projPlus d s = (1 + H2/s)/2` for `s² = dsq d ≠ 0`:
* `projPlus_idem`, `projPlus_mul_projMinus`, `projPlus_add_projMinus`, `H2_mul_projPlus`,
  `projPlus_mul_H2`, `H2_spectral_decomp`.
* `H2_biorthProj_eq_projPlus`: for *any* right/left eigenvectors of `s` with non-zero
  biorthogonal overlap the biorthogonal projector equals `projPlus`; `H2_exists_biorth_pair`
  shows such eigenvectors exist.
* `H2_petermann_eq`: the Petermann factor is `K = (1 + ‖d‖²/|dsq d|)/2` (`petermann2`), and
  `one_le_petermann2`.
-/
/-- Close a polynomial identity that holds modulo `hs : s ^ 2 = …`. -/
/-- The bilinear square `d · d = d₀² + d₁² + d₂²` of a complex 3-vector. -/
/-- Two-resonator Bloch Hamiltonian `d · σ`. -/
/-- Three-resonator Hamiltonian (gauge-equivalent to the spin-1 matrix `2 d · S`). -/
/-- Four-resonator Hamiltonian (gauge-equivalent to the spin-3/2 matrix `2 d · S`). -/
/-- Characteristic polynomial of `H3`: eigenvalues `0, ±2s`. -/
/-- Characteristic polynomial of `H4`: eigenvalues `±s, ±3s`. -/
/-- If `p = q = 0` and `dsq d = 0` then `d = 0`. -/
/-- **EP2 condition**: `H2 d` has an EP2 at `E = 0` iff `dsq d = 0` and `d ≠ 0`. -/

/-- **EP3 condition**: `H3 d` has an EP3 (a single 3×3 Jordan block) at `E = 0` iff
`dsq d = 0` and `d ≠ 0`. -/

/-- **EP4 condition**: `H4 d` has an EP4 (a single 4×4 Jordan block) at `E = 0` iff
`dsq d = 0` and `d ≠ 0`. -/
/-! ## Biorthogonal spectral projectors of the two-level model -/
/-- Spectral (biorthogonal) projector `(1 + H2/s)/2` onto the band with energy `s`. -/
/-- Spectral projector `(1 - H2/s)/2` onto the band with energy `-s`. -/
/-- Biorthogonal spectral decomposition `H2 = s P₊ - s P₋`. -/

/-- **The biorthogonal projector is the spectral projector.** For any right eigenvector `v` and
left eigenvector `u` of `H2 d` with eigenvalue `s ≠ 0` and `uᵀ v ≠ 0`,
`v uᵀ / (uᵀ v) = (1 + H2/s)/2`. -/

/-- Right and left eigenvectors with non-vanishing biorthogonal overlap exist off the
exceptional set. -/
/-! ## The Petermann factor of the two-level model -/
/-- The closed-form Petermann factor `K = (1 + ‖d‖²/|d · d|)/2` of the two-level model. -/
/-- `K ≥ 1` for the two-level model, with equality e.g. for real (Hermitian) `d`. -/

the Poincaré inequality are hypotheses about the flow, not consequences of the

# Non-Associative Sedenion Helicity Conservation Laws (OP-038, HYP-138)

This module formalizes non-associative fluid helicity in 16D sedenion hydrodynamics
and proves its exact conservation under inviscid Euler flow on the zero-divisor variety:

1. Non-Associative Sedenion Fluid Helicity:
   H₁₆ = ∫_Ω ⟨u, ω⟩₁₆ dV, where u is fluid velocity and ω = curl₁₆(u) is vorticity.

2. Non-Associative Lamb Vector & Convective Acceleration:
   The 16D Lamb vector is L₁₆ = ω ×₁₆ u = (1/2)(ω * u - u * ω).
   Under inviscid Euler dynamics:
     ∂_t u = -L₁₆ - ∇Π
     ∂_t ω = -curl₁₆(L₁₆).

3. Helicity Rate of Change Balance:
   Differentiating under the integral sign and using vector identity / integration by parts:
     dH₁₆/dt = -2 ∫_Ω ⟨L₁₆, ω⟩₁₆ dV + (boundary flux).
   Under slip / no-penetration boundary conditions (or decaying fields on ℝ¹⁶),
   the boundary flux vanishes.

4. Exact Helicity Conservation on the Zero-Divisor Variety:
   On ZD₁₆, velocity u and vorticity ω mutually annihilate:
     u * ω = 0  and  ω * u = 0.
   Consequently, L₁₆ = 0 identically everywhere on ZD₁₆.
   Therefore, ⟨L₁₆, ω⟩₁₆ = 0 pointwise, establishing:
     dH₁₆/dt ≡ 0.

5. Off-Manifold Helicity Drift Bound:
   For perturbations at distance δ = dist((u, ω), ZD₁₆) > 0:
     |dH₁₆/dt| ≤ 4 C_assoc δ ||u|| E(t),
   which strictly vanishes as δ → 0.

6. Discrete-Continuous Skeleton Invariants:
   168 basis zero divisors, 8 regularity degree, 672 undirected edges,

/-! ## Vector calculus on `ℝ³` -/
/-- Partial derivative `∂ⱼ f (x)`. -/
/-- Divergence `∇ · F`. -/
/-- Directional derivative `(a·∇)F`, componentwise `Σⱼ aⱼ ∂ⱼ Fᵢ`. -/
/-- The Lamb vector `L = ω × u`. -/
/-- The vortex stretching term `(ω·∇)u`. -/
/-- The vortex advection term `(u·∇)ω`. -/
/-! ## Sedenion embedding -/
/-- `v ↦ v₀ e₁ + v₁ e₂ + v₂ e₃`: `ℝ³` as the imaginary quaternions inside `𝕊`. -/
/-- `v ↦ v₀ e₅ + v₁ e₆ + v₂ e₇`. -/
/-- The basis sedenion `e₄` (the octonionic doubling unit). -/
/-- The associator-kernel condition `∀ x ∈ 𝕊, [ω, x, u] = 0` for `ω, u ∈ ℝ³ ⊂ 𝕊`. -/
/-- `[a, e₄, b] = −2 (a × b)` (placed in the `e₅, e₆, e₇` slots). -/
/-- The sedenion commutator of embedded vectors is twice their cross product. -/

/-- **The Lamb vector is the sedenion commutator**: `ω u − u ω = embV (2 L)`, i.e.
`L = ω × u` is half the commutator `[ω, u]` computed in `𝕊`. -/
/-- **Associator kernel ⟺ vanishing Lamb vector** (Beltrami alignment `ω ∥ u`). -/

/-- **Vanishing of the nonlinear vorticity term.**  If `u` and `ω` are differentiable and
divergence free at `x` and the associator-kernel condition holds near `x`, then
`(ω·∇)u = (u·∇)ω` at `x`: vortex stretching is exactly cancelled by vortex advection, so the
nonlinear term `(ω·∇)u − (u·∇)ω = ∇ × (u × ω)` of the vorticity equation vanishes. -/
/-! ## The stretching term alone does not vanish: the ABC flow -/
/-- The Arnold–Beltrami–Childress flow with `A = B = C = 1`. -/

/-- **The literal claim fails.**  There is a smooth divergence-free velocity field (the ABC
flow) whose vorticity `ω = ∇ × u` lies in the sedenion associator kernel with `u` at every
point, yet whose vortex stretching term `(ω·∇)u` is non-zero, with stretching density
`ω · (ω·∇)u = 3` at the origin. -/

/-!
# Apéry numbers and the Lucas / Dwork property

The Apéry numbers `A(n) = ∑_k C(n,k)² C(n+k,k)²` (the numbers behind Apéry's proof of the
irrationality of `ζ(3)`) share with the quintic coefficients `a(n) = (5n)!/(n!)⁵` the Lucas
(Dwork) property `c(r + p m) ≡ c(r) c(m) (mod p)`, `r < p`.  Any sequence with this property
has the mod-`p` Frobenius structure `F(z) = A_p(z) · F(z^p)` on its generating function over
`𝔽_p` (`frobenius_of_lucas`); this is the arithmetic input shared by the Apéry and the
mirror-quintic periods.
-/
/-- A sequence has the **Lucas property** at `p` if `c(r + p m) ≡ c(r) c(m) (mod p)` for `r < p`. -/
/-- The generating function `∑ c(n) zⁿ` over a ring `R`. -/

/-- **Frobenius structure mod `p` for Lucas sequences**: over `𝔽_p`,
`F(z) = A_p(z) · F(z^p)` with `A_p` the truncation of `F = ∑ c(n) zⁿ` below degree `p`. -/
/-- The quintic coefficients `(5n)!/(n!)⁵` have the Lucas property at every prime. -/
/-! ### Apéry numbers -/
/-- The summand `C(n,k)² C(n+k,k)²` of the Apéry numbers. -/
/-- Lucas' theorem in the form `C(r + p m, s + p j) ≡ C(r, s) C(m, j)` for `r, s < p`. -/

/-- The second binomial factor: `C((r+s) + p(m+j), s + pj) ≡ C(r+s, s) C(m+j, j)`, including
the carry case `r + s ≥ p` where both sides vanish mod `p`. -/
/-- **Lucas (Gessel) congruence for the Apéry numbers**: `A(r + p m) ≡ A(r) A(m) (mod p)`. -/

/-- The Apéry generating function has the same mod-`p` Frobenius structure as the quintic
period: `∑ A(n) zⁿ = A_p(z) · (∑ A(n) z^{pn})` over `𝔽_p`. -/
/-- The first Apéry numbers. -/

/-!
# Apéry's recurrence

The Apéry numbers satisfy
`(n+1)³ A(n+1) = (34n³ + 51n² + 27n + 5) A(n) − n³ A(n−1)`,
proved here by creative telescoping with van der Poorten's certificate
`B(n,k) = 4(2n+1)(k(2k+1) − (2n+1)²) C(n,k)² C(n+k,k)²`.
Equivalently, `∑ A(n) zⁿ` is annihilated by the third-order operator
`θ³ − z(2θ+1)(17θ²+17θ+5) + z²(θ+1)³`, the Apéry analogue of the quintic Picard–Fuchs
operator.
-/
/-- `C(n,k)² C(n+k,k)²` as a rational number. -/
/-- van der Poorten's certificate. -/
/-- The combination whose sum over `k` gives the recurrence. -/
/-- The main case `k + 1 ≤ m + 1` of the telescoping identity. -/
/-- The boundary case `k + 1 = m + 2`. -/
/-- The trivial case `k + 1 > m + 2`. -/
/-- Apéry's third-order operator `θ³ − z(2θ+1)(17θ²+17θ+5) + z²(θ+1)³` on `ℚ⟦z⟧`. -/

/-- **The Apéry generating function is a period of Apéry's operator**:
`(θ³ − z(2θ+1)(17θ²+17θ+5) + z²(θ+1)³) ∑ A(n) zⁿ = 0`. -/

/-!
# A certified engine for instanton numbers of hypergeometric Calabi–Yau families

This file turns the special-purpose computation of `RequestProject/MirrorMap.lean` into a
reusable engine.  A one-parameter hypergeometric family is described by `HypData`:
factorial data `num = [m₁, …]`, `den = [k₁, …]` and the Yukawa normalisation `κ`
(the triple intersection number of the mirror).  From these we build, as power series over `ℚ`:

* the fundamental period `Π₀ = ∑ aₙ zⁿ` with `aₙ = ∏ (mᵢ n)! / ∏ (kⱼ n)!`;
* the power-series part `Π̃₁ = ∑ bₙ zⁿ` of the logarithmic period,
  `bₙ = aₙ (∑ mᵢ H_{mᵢ n} − ∑ kⱼ H_{kⱼ n})` (the `ε`-derivative of `a_{n+ε}/a_ε`);
* the mirror map `q = z exp(Π̃₁/Π₀)`;
* the Yukawa coupling `C_θθθ = κ/(1 − μ z)`, `μ = ∏ mᵢ^{mᵢ} / ∏ kⱼ^{kⱼ}`, and its flat-coordinate
  form `Y = C_θθθ / (Π₀² (θ t)³)`;
* the multiple-cover series `κ + ∑ n_d d³ qᵈ/(1 − qᵈ)`.

`IsInstantonUpTo D N n` says `Y(z) = (κ + ∑ n_d d³ qᵈ/(1-qᵈ))|_{q = q(z)}` modulo `z^{N+1}`.

Generic results:
* `IsInstantonUpTo.unique`: the instanton numbers are determined by the data (for every family).
* `isInstantonUpTo_of_certificate`: a decidable list computation (`Certificate`) implies
  `IsInstantonUpTo`.  The certificate is closed by `decide +kernel`.
* `instanton_isInt_of_check`: *unguided mode* — the engine computes the instanton numbers
  itself (`computeInstantons`); if the certificate and an integrality check on the computed
  list pass, then every sequence satisfying `IsInstantonUpTo D N` is integral in degrees `1..N`.
* `mirrorMap_isInt_of_check`: integrality of the mirror map from a decidable check.

/-- Data of a one-parameter hypergeometric family: `aₙ = ∏ (m n)! / ∏ (k n)!`, and the
Yukawa normalisation `κ`. -/
/-- factorials in the numerator -/
/-- factorials in the denominator -/
/-- the Yukawa normalisation (triple intersection number) -/
/-- The conifold parameter `μ = ∏ m^m / ∏ k^k`; the discriminant is `1 − μ z`. -/
/-- The fundamental period `Π₀`. -/
/-- The power-series part `Π̃₁` of the logarithmic period `Π₁ = Π₀ log z + Π̃₁`. -/
/-- `Π̃₁/Π₀`, so that `t = log z + Π̃₁/Π₀`. -/
/-- The mirror map `q = e^t = z exp(Π̃₁/Π₀)`. -/
/-- The Yukawa coupling `C_θθθ = κ/(1 − μ z)`. -/
/-- The Yukawa coupling in the flat coordinate, `Y = C_θθθ / (Π₀² (θ t)³)`. -/
/-- The sequence `n` reproduces the flat Yukawa coupling of the family `D` through degree `N`. -/
/-! ### Generic facts -/
/-- **Uniqueness** (every family): the instanton numbers `n_1, …, n_N` are determined. -/
/-! ### The certificate -/
/-- Truncated `Π₀`. -/
/-- Truncated `Π₀⁻¹` (candidate). -/

/-- Truncated flat Yukawa coupling. -/
/-- Truncated multiple-cover series. -/

/-- The decidable certificate: the two computed inverses are correct, and the multiple-cover
series composed with the mirror map equals the flat Yukawa coupling modulo `z^N`. -/
/-- **Soundness of the certificate.** -/
/-- **The mirror map from a check.** -/
/-- **Integrality of the mirror map from a check.** -/

/-- **Values from a certified integer table.** If an integer table `L` passes the certificate,
then every sequence of instanton numbers of `D` agrees with `L` in degrees `1, …, N`. -/

/-- **Integrality from a certified table.** If a list `L` passes the certificate and its
entries in degrees `≤ N` are integers, then every sequence of instanton numbers of `D`
is integral in degrees `1, …, N`. -/

/-- **Non-integrality from a certified table.** If a list `L` passes the certificate and its
entry in degree `d` is not an integer, then the degree-`d` instanton number of `D` is not an
integer.  (The hypothesis `IsInstantonUpTo D N n` is satisfiable, by `lget L` itself.) -/

/-- The instanton numbers `[0, n_1, …, n_{N-1}]` computed by the engine. -/

integral, then the instanton numbers of the family are integers in degrees `1, …, N`. -/

/-!
# Instanton numbers of the fourteen hypergeometric Calabi–Yau families

Each family below is a one-parameter hypergeometric family of Calabi–Yau threefolds (the
mirror of a hypersurface or complete intersection in weighted projective space), given to the
engine of `RequestProject/CYEngine.lean` by its factorial data and Yukawa normalisation `κ`.
The instanton tables were **produced by the engine itself** (`computeInstantons`) and are
certified by the Lean kernel through `Certificate`.

For each family `F` we prove, through degree 12:
* `F_isInstantonUpTo`: the integer table reproduces the flat Yukawa coupling via the
  multiple-cover formula;
* `F_instanton_eq`: any sequence doing so equals the integer table (uniqueness + integrality);
* `F_mirrorMap`: the mirror map `q(z)` has the displayed integer coefficients.

The degree-one values `2875, 7884, 29504, 231200, 1053, 1280, 720, 512, 3712, 67104, 15552,
1944, 4992, 678816` agree with the numbers of rational curves of degree one in the literature.
-/

/-!
# Picard–Fuchs equations of the hypergeometric families

For data `D` and exponents `r = [r₁, r₂, r₃, r₄]` we consider the hypergeometric operator
`L_{μ,r} = θ⁴ − μ z (θ + r₁)(θ + r₂)(θ + r₃)(θ + r₄)`.

* `coeffA_succ_mul`: the generic ratio `a_{n+1} Q_den(n) = a_n Q_num(n)` of factorial data,
  with `Q(n) = ∏_m ∏_{j<m} (m n + j + 1)`.
* `hypPF_period_of_poly`: if the polynomial identity
  `(n+1)⁴ Q_num(n) = μ ∏ (n + rᵢ) Q_den(n)` holds, then `L_{μ,r} Π₀ = 0`.
* For each of the fourteen families, the fundamental period used by the engine satisfies its
  fourth-order Picard–Fuchs equation (e.g. `sextic_picardFuchs` with exponents
  `1/6, 1/3, 2/3, 5/6`).  This ties the data given to the engine to the differential equation.
-/
/-- The operator `θ + r` applied along a list: `(θ + r₁) ⋯ (θ + r_k) f`. -/
/-- The hypergeometric Picard–Fuchs operator `θ⁴ − μ z ∏ (θ + rᵢ)`. -/
/-- `Q(n) = ∏_m ∏_{j<m} (m n + j + 1)` over a list of factorial data. -/
/-- **Generic ratio of the coefficients.** `a_{n+1} Q_den(n) = a_n Q_num(n)`. -/
/-- **Picard–Fuchs equation from a polynomial identity.** -/
/-! ### The fourteen families -/
/-- The period of the quintic satisfies `θ⁴ Π₀ = μ z (θ + r₁)⋯(θ + r₄) Π₀` with exponents `1/5, 2/5, 3/5, 4/5`. -/
/-- The period of the sextic satisfies `θ⁴ Π₀ = μ z (θ + r₁)⋯(θ + r₄) Π₀` with exponents `1/6, 1/3, 2/3, 5/6`. -/
/-- The period of the octic satisfies `θ⁴ Π₀ = μ z (θ + r₁)⋯(θ + r₄) Π₀` with exponents `1/8, 3/8, 5/8, 7/8`. -/
/-- The period of the dectic satisfies `θ⁴ Π₀ = μ z (θ + r₁)⋯(θ + r₄) Π₀` with exponents `1/10, 3/10, 7/10, 9/10`. -/
/-- The period of `X₃,₃` satisfies `θ⁴ Π₀ = μ z (θ + r₁)⋯(θ + r₄) Π₀` with exponents `1/3, 1/3, 2/3, 2/3`. -/
/-- The period of `X₄,₂` satisfies `θ⁴ Π₀ = μ z (θ + r₁)⋯(θ + r₄) Π₀` with exponents `1/4, 1/2, 1/2, 3/4`. -/
/-- The period of `X₃,₂,₂` satisfies `θ⁴ Π₀ = μ z (θ + r₁)⋯(θ + r₄) Π₀` with exponents `1/3, 1/2, 1/2, 2/3`. -/
/-- The period of `X₂,₂,₂,₂` satisfies `θ⁴ Π₀ = μ z (θ + r₁)⋯(θ + r₄) Π₀` with exponents `1/2, 1/2, 1/2, 1/2`. -/
/-- The period of `X₄,₄` satisfies `θ⁴ Π₀ = μ z (θ + r₁)⋯(θ + r₄) Π₀` with exponents `1/4, 1/4, 3/4, 3/4`. -/
/-- The period of `X₆,₆` satisfies `θ⁴ Π₀ = μ z (θ + r₁)⋯(θ + r₄) Π₀` with exponents `1/6, 1/6, 5/6, 5/6`. -/
/-- The period of `X₆,₄` satisfies `θ⁴ Π₀ = μ z (θ + r₁)⋯(θ + r₄) Π₀` with exponents `1/6, 1/4, 3/4, 5/6`. -/
/-- The period of `X₄,₃` satisfies `θ⁴ Π₀ = μ z (θ + r₁)⋯(θ + r₄) Π₀` with exponents `1/4, 1/3, 2/3, 3/4`. -/
/-- The period of `X₆,₂` satisfies `θ⁴ Π₀ = μ z (θ + r₁)⋯(θ + r₄) Π₀` with exponents `1/6, 1/2, 1/2, 5/6`. -/
/-- The period of `X₁₂,₂` satisfies `θ⁴ Π₀ = μ z (θ + r₁)⋯(θ + r₄) Π₀` with exponents `1/12, 5/12, 7/12, 11/12`. -/
