/-!
# Simplicial presheaves of proof derivations and weak `ω`-groupoids

The `(∞,1)`-topos of higher stacks on the derivation site `AOpen P` (the Alexandrov opens of a
derivation poset `P`, see `Sovereign.SheafConsensus`) is presented, as usual, by **simplicial
presheaves** `(AOpen P)ᵒᵖ ⥤ SSet` (`SimplicialPresheaf P`). They are simplicially enriched by the
mapping spaces of `MappingSpace.lean`, using the cosimplicial cylinder `presheafCylinder` given by
the constant presheaves `Δ[n]`.

* **Weak `ω`-groupoids** are modelled by Kan complexes (`WeakOmegaGroupoid`): every horn has a
  filler. We derive the first layers of the weak `ω`-groupoid structure: composites of composable
  proof steps exist up to a `2`-cell (`WeakOmegaGroupoid.exists_comp`) and every proof step has an
  inverse (`WeakOmegaGroupoid.exists_inv`).
* A simplicial presheaf is a **presheaf of weak `ω`-groupoids** (`IsKanValued`) when all its
  values are Kan complexes.
* **Proof derivations**: a presheaf of categories of derivations (objects: derivations, morphisms:
  derivation rewrites) gives a simplicial presheaf by taking nerves (`derivationNerve`).
* **Local derivation data** of a multi-agent cover `U` is its Čech nerve (`cechNerve U`), whose
  `n`-simplices over `W` are the `(n+1)`-tuples of agents whose patches all contain `W`.
* A **global consensus derivation certificate** for a consensus stack `Y` over the cover `U` is a
  morphism `cechNerve U ⟶ Y`, i.e. a vertex of `Map(cechNerve U, Y)`. The main theorems of
  `MappingSpace.lean` specialise to `consensus_certificate_exists_unique` and
  `consensus_certificate_homotopy_invariant`.

## Caveat

We use the simplicial presheaf *presentation* of the `(∞,1)`-topos: we do not construct the
(local) model structure, nor the localisation at Čech hypercovers.
-/
/-! ### Weak `ω`-groupoids -/

/-- A **weak `ω`-groupoid**, modelled as a Kan complex: a simplicial set in which every horn
`Λ[n, i] ⟶ X` extends to the simplex `Δ[n]`. -/
/-- the underlying simplicial set -/
/-- the Kan (horn filling) condition -/

/-- **Composition up to a `2`-cell**: two composable proof steps `f : a → b`, `g : b → c` of a weak
`ω`-groupoid are the two outer edges of a `2`-simplex (whose third edge is a composite). -/

/-- **Inverses**: every proof step `f : a → b` of a weak `ω`-groupoid has a reverse step
`b → a`. -/
/-! ### Simplicial sets as an enriched category -/
/-- The cosimplicial cylinder `Δ[•]` on simplicial sets: `Map(X, Y)_n = Hom(X × Δ[n], Y)`. -/

/-- For simplicial sets, `Homotopic` is the usual notion of simplicial homotopy (as in Mathlib's
`SSet.RelativeMorphism.Homotopy`): a map `h : X × Δ[1] ⟶ Y` with `h ∘ ι₀ = f` and
`h ∘ ι₁ = g`. -/
/-! ### Simplicial presheaves on the derivation site -/

/-- **Simplicial presheaves** on the derivation site: the standard presentation of the
`(∞,1)`-topos of higher stacks of proof derivations. -/

/-- The cosimplicial cylinder of constant simplicial presheaves `Δ[•]`, which enriches simplicial
presheaves in simplicial sets. -/

/-- The **derivation nerve**: a presheaf of categories of proof derivations (objects: derivations,
morphisms: derivation rewrites) becomes a simplicial presheaf by taking nerves objectwise. -/

/-- A simplicial presheaf is a **presheaf of weak `ω`-groupoids** (a higher prestack) when all its
values are Kan complexes. -/
/-- The value of a presheaf of weak `ω`-groupoids on an open. -/

/-- The simplicial set of simplices of the Čech nerve of `U` over the open `W`: the `n`-simplices
are the `(n+1)`-tuples of agents whose patches all contain `W`. -/

/-- The **Čech nerve** of a multi-agent cover `U`, as a simplicial presheaf: the local derivation
data of the cover. -/
/-! ### Global consensus derivation certificates -/

/-- A **global consensus derivation certificate** for the consensus stack `Y` over the cover `U`:
a morphism from the Čech nerve of the cover to `Y` (equivalently, `certEquiv`, a vertex of
`Map(cechNerve U, Y)`). -/

/-- **Existence and uniqueness of the global consensus derivation certificate.** If the mapping
space `Map(cechNerve U, Y)` is contractible, a global consensus derivation certificate exists and
any two are homotopic; `π₀ Map(cechNerve U, Y)` is a single point. -/

/-- **Homotopy invariance of the global consensus derivation certificate.** If
`Map(cechNerve U, Y)` is contractible, then for any local derivation data `X` homotopy equivalent
to the Čech nerve and any consensus stack `Y'` homotopy equivalent to `Y`, the global certificate
`X ⟶ Y'` still exists and is unique up to homotopy. -/

/-!
# Higher stacks in terms of the projective structure

`HigherStack.lean` defines higher stacks using its own notion of trivial Kan fibration
(`SSet.IsTrivialFibration`, stated by hand as a lifting condition against `∂Δ[n] ⟶ Δ[n]`), while
`ModelStructure.lean` uses the class `sSetTrivialFibrations` (the right lifting class of Mathlib's
generating cofibrations `SSet.modelCategoryQuillen.I`). This file shows the two notions agree
(`SSet.isTrivialFibration_iff`) and restates the definition of a higher stack in the language of
the projective structure (`isHigherStack_iff`):

> `Y` is a higher stack iff `Y` is projectively fibrant and, for every covering family `U` of an
> open `W`, the descent map `Map(Č{W}, Y) ⟶ Map(Č(U), Y)` is a trivial Kan fibration.

In particular every higher stack is projectively fibrant (`IsHigherStack.projFibrant`).
-/

/-- **The two notions of trivial Kan fibration agree**: the hand-written lifting condition
`SSet.IsTrivialFibration` of `HigherStack.lean` is membership in the class `sSetTrivialFibrations`
of `ModelStructure.lean`. -/

/-- **Higher stacks via the projective structure.** A simplicial presheaf `Y` on the derivation
site is a higher stack iff it is projectively fibrant (`Y ⟶ *` is an objectwise Kan fibration) and
every descent map `Map(Č{W}, Y) ⟶ Map(Č(U), Y)` along a covering family is a trivial Kan
fibration. -/
/-- A higher stack is fibrant in the projective structure. -/

/-!
# The long exact cohomology sequence of the truncation tower

`Postnikov.lean` builds the truncation (Postnikov) tower of a cochain complex
`C → τ^{≥0} C → τ^{≥1} C → τ^{≥2} C → ⋯`, and `LongExact.lean` builds the long exact sequence of a
short exact sequence of cochain complexes. This file puts the two together.

Every tower map `τ^{≥n} C → τ^{≥n+1} C` is degreewise surjective; its kernel is the **`n`-th layer**
`L_n = postnikovLayer C n` of the tower. So every stage of the tower sits in a short exact sequence
```
0 → L_n → τ^{≥n} C → τ^{≥n+1} C → 0                                (postnikovLayer_shortExact)
```
and therefore has a long exact cohomology sequence (`postnikov_tower_long_exact`), with connecting
maps `δᵏ : Hᵏ(τ^{≥n+1} C) → Hᵏ⁺¹(L_n)` (`towerDelta`).

Using this long exact sequence together with the computation of the cohomology of the stages we
determine the cohomology of the layers: **the `n`-th layer is an Eilenberg–MacLane object**
concentrated in degree `n`, with `Hⁿ(L_n) ≅ Hⁿ(C)` (`postnikovLayer_H_subsingleton`,
`postnikovLayerHEquiv`). This is the cochain-level form of the statement that the fibres of a
Postnikov tower are Eilenberg–MacLane spaces `K(Hⁿ, n)`.

The kernel construction is general: `CochainCx.Hom.kerCx` is the kernel of any cochain map, and
`CochainCx.Hom.kerCx_shortExact` gives the short exact sequence `0 → ker φ → X → Y → 0` for any
degreewise surjective `φ`.
-/

/-- The **kernel complex** of a cochain map `φ : X → Y`: `(ker φ)ᵏ = ker (φᵏ)`, with the
restricted differential. -/
/-- The inclusion `ker φ → X`. -/

/-- For a degreewise surjective cochain map `φ : X → Y`, `0 → ker φ → X → Y → 0` is a short exact
sequence of cochain complexes. -/
/-! ### Two diagram lemmas for exact sequences of abelian groups -/

/-- In an exact sequence `A →α B →δ M →ι D →β E`, if `α` is surjective and `β` is injective then
`M = 0`. -/
/-- In an exact sequence `B →δ M →ι D` with `B = 0` and `D = 0`, also `M = 0`. -/
/-! ### The layers of the truncation tower -/
/-- Each tower map `τ^{≥n} C → τ^{≥n+1} C` is degreewise surjective. -/
/-- The **`n`-th layer** `L_n` of the truncation tower: the kernel of `τ^{≥n} C → τ^{≥n+1} C`. -/
/-- The inclusion of the `n`-th layer `L_n → τ^{≥n} C`. -/
/-- **The tower is built from short exact sequences** `0 → L_n → τ^{≥n} C → τ^{≥n+1} C → 0`. -/
/-- The connecting maps `δᵏ : Hᵏ(τ^{≥n+1} C) → Hᵏ⁺¹(L_n)` of the truncation tower. -/

/-- **The long exact cohomology sequence of the truncation tower.** For every stage `n`,
```
0 → H⁰(L_n) → H⁰(τ^{≥n}) → H⁰(τ^{≥n+1}) →δ H¹(L_n) → ⋯ → Hᵏ(L_n) → Hᵏ(τ^{≥n}) → Hᵏ(τ^{≥n+1})
  →δ Hᵏ⁺¹(L_n) → ⋯
```
is exact at every stage. -/

/-- **The layers have no cohomology outside degree `n`**: `Hᵏ(L_n) = 0` for `k ≠ n`. Proved from
the long exact sequence of the tower. -/
-- below the layer: the neighbouring stage groups vanish
-- above the layer: the neighbouring tower maps are isomorphisms (or have zero target)
/-- The inclusion of the layer induces a bijection `Hⁿ(L_n) → Hⁿ(τ^{≥n} C)`. -/

/-- **The `n`-th layer of the truncation tower is concentrated in degree `n`, where its
cohomology is `Hⁿ(C)`.** -/
/-- Summary: the layer `L_n` is an Eilenberg–MacLane object of type `(Hⁿ(C), n)`. -/

/-!
# Beam search over the tree of proof states

The beam search engine explores the proof-state tree level by level. At each depth it

1. **expands** every node of the current beam by all `b` tactics, discarding children whose
   proof state already occurs on their path (`fresh`, so every traversed path is
   non-circular);
2. **scores** every generated child with a guidance score (lower is better) and keeps the
   `width` best ones (`select`);
3. runs the **certification gate** `certB` on every traversed node; the accepted nodes are the
   returned certified proof paths (`search`).

Main results:
* `cost_le` — the number of generated nodes (each is scored once and gated once) up to depth `D`
  is at most `1 + D · width · b`: **linear in the depth**, for any score;
* `mem_layer` / `traversed_nonCircular` — every traversed path is non-circular;
* `search_sound` — every returned path is kernel-certified, cut-free, acyclic and
  non-circular, and its goal is valid whenever the kernel is sound;
* `anc_mem_layer`, `guided_found` — **goal-directed completeness**: if the score is `Guided`
  towards a certified goal node `g` (at every depth, fewer than `width` competitors at that
  depth score at least as well as the ancestor of `g`), the search returns `g` by depth
  `g.length`, after generating at most `1 + g.length · width · b` nodes.
-/

/-- **Rank lemma** for the beam: an element of a duplicate-free list with fewer than `w`
competitors scoring at least as well is kept among the `w` best. -/
/-- Beam configuration: width and guidance score (lower is better). -/
/-- Expansion of a beam: all fresh children of all beam nodes. -/
/-- Selection: the `width` best-scoring candidates. -/
/-- The beam at depth `k`. -/
/-- All nodes traversed up to depth `D`. -/

/-- Cost of the search up to depth `D`: the number of generated nodes, each of which is scored
once and passed through the certification gate once. -/
/-- **The cost of hyperbolic beam search is linear in the depth.** -/
/-- Every node of the depth-`k` beam has depth `k` and a non-circular path. -/
/-- **Every traversed proof path is non-circular.** -/
/-! ### Goal-directed completeness -/

/-- The score is **guided** towards the node `g`: at every depth `k + 1 ≤ g.length`, fewer than
`width` other nodes of that depth score at least as well as the ancestor of `g`. -/

/-- A guidance score that strictly prefers the ancestors of `g` over all other nodes of the same
depth is guided (for every width `≥ 1`). -/
/-- Under guidance, the beam keeps every ancestor of a non-circular target node. -/
/-! ### Certified output -/
/-- Gate one node, packaging acceptance as a certified path. -/
/-- The certified proof paths found up to depth `D`. -/

/-- **Soundness of hyperbolic beam search.** Every returned proof path was traversed, lies in a
closed proof state, is non-circular (no proof state repeats and no sub-derivation proves the
goal itself), is certified by the kernel, is cut-free and a fixed point of cut elimination, and
proves a valid goal whenever the kernel is sound. -/

/-- **Goal-directed completeness with linear cost.** If the goal node `g` passes the
certification gate and the score is guided towards `g`, then hyperbolic beam search returns a
certified proof path at `g` by depth `g.length`, having generated at most
`1 + g.length · width · b` nodes. -/
/-! # Axiom checks for the hyperbolic beam search engine -/

/-!
# Proof-discovery time: hyperbolic beam search versus Euclidean BFS / DFS

An **uninformed** (Euclidean, blind) search visits the nodes of the proof-state tree in a fixed
order that does not depend on where the proof is: breadth-first (`bfsOrder`) or depth-first
(`dfsOrder`). Its **discovery time** (`blindTime`) is the number of nodes visited (each passed
through the certification gate) until the first certified proof path is reached.

Main results, for trees of branching factor `b ≥ 2`:
* `bfs_time_ge` — BFS needs at least `1 + b + ⋯ + b^(d-1) + 1` gate calls to find a proof
  whose only certified node has depth `d`, wherever that node is;
* `blind_worst_case` — *every* complete blind order (in particular BFS and DFS) needs at least
  `b ^ d` gate calls on some proof space whose only certified node has depth `d`;
* `hyperbolic_beam_finds` (in `Embedding.lean`) — hyperbolic beam search with a neural target
  pointing into the goal's sector needs at most `1 + d · w · b` node generations;
* `beam_bound_subExponential`, `blind_bound_not_subExponential`, `beam_div_blind_tendsto_zero` —
  the hyperbolic bound `1 + d w b` is sub-exponential in `d`, the blind bound `b ^ d` is not, and
  their ratio tends to `0`;
* `hyperbolic_speedup` — the combined statement, and `needle` — a family of proof spaces
  (one certified node at a prescribed address) showing that all hypotheses can be met.
-/
/-! ### Blind search orders -/
/-- Breadth-first order of the nodes of depth `≤ D`. -/
/-- Depth-first (pre-)order of the nodes below `v`, down to `D` more levels. -/
/-- Depth-first order of the nodes of depth `≤ D`. -/

/-- The discovery time of a blind search order: the number of nodes visited until the first node
passing the certification gate. -/
/-- The first hit of a predicate that holds exactly at `g` is the first occurrence of `g`. -/
/-- The node `g` is the only node of the order `L` passing the certification gate. -/
/-! ### Lower bounds for blind search -/

/-- **BFS lower bound.** If the only certified node within depth `D` has depth `d`, BFS
passes at least `1 + b + ⋯ + b^(d-1)` other nodes through the gate before finding it. -/

/-- **Worst case of every blind search.** For every search order `L` visiting all nodes of
depth `d` (`b ≥ 1`), some node `g` of depth `d` is visited only after at least `b ^ d - 1`
others: a blind search with `g` as the only certified node takes at least `b ^ d` gate calls. -/
/-- The blind lower bound for a proof space with a unique certified node. -/
/-! ### Sub-exponential versus exponential -/
/-- A function of the depth grows **sub-exponentially** if it is `o(cᵈ)` for every `c > 1`. -/
/-- The cost bound `1 + d · w · b` of hyperbolic beam search is sub-exponential. -/
/-- The blind lower bound `b ^ d` (`b ≥ 2`) is not sub-exponential. -/
/-- The ratio of the hyperbolic cost bound to the blind lower bound tends to `0`. -/
/-! ### Needle-in-a-haystack proof spaces -/
/-- The trivial kernel over one rule and one formula. -/

/-- A proof space whose proof states are the tactic scripts themselves and whose only closed
state, with a certified proof, is the address `g`. -/
/-! ### The speed-up theorem -/

/-- **Sub-exponential speed-up of hyperbolic beam search over Euclidean blind search.** Let
`b ≥ 2`, `w ≥ 1`, and let `L` be any blind search order visiting all nodes of depth `d`
(e.g. `bfsOrder b d` or `dfsOrder b d`). Then there is a node `g` of depth `d` such that for
every proof space `P` in which `g` is the only node of `L` passing the certification gate:
1. the blind search needs at least `b ^ d` gate calls;
2. for every hyperbolic embedding and every neural target of positive radius pointing into the
   sector of `g`, hyperbolic beam search of width `w` returns the certified proof at `g` after at
   most `1 + d · w · b` node generations;
and the ratio of the two bounds tends to `0` as `d → ∞`. -/

/-- The hypotheses of `hyperbolic_speedup` are satisfiable: for the needle proof space at `g`
and the neural target at `g`'s own angle, both conclusions hold. -/

/-!
# Embedding the proof-state tree in `Dⁿ` and hyperbolic guidance

The `b`-ary tree of proof states is embedded in the Poincaré ball `Dⁿ` (`n ≥ 2`, inside the
2-plane of an orthonormal frame) in hyperbolic polar coordinates:

* the node `v` at depth `m` sits at **hyperbolic radius `m ℓ`** (`ℓ > 0` is the hyperbolic edge
  length), so `d_H(0, pos v) = m ℓ` (`dH_origin_pos`; it is the `NeuroBridge` ray point of
  its direction, `pos_eq_rayPoint`);
* its **angle** is the centre of its angular sector: the depth-`m` nodes split `[0, 1]` into
  `b ^ m` consecutive sectors of width `b ^ (-m)`, in the lexicographic order of tactic scripts
  (`idx`), and the sector of a child is contained in the sector of its parent.

A **neural target** is a point of `Dⁿ` (hyperbolic radius and angle) predicted by an untrusted
network for the goal. The **hyperbolic score** of a node is its hyperbolic distance to the
target, and the **hyperbolic beam** is the beam search of `Beam.lean` with this score.

Main results:
* `hyperbolic_guided` — if the target direction lies in the (open) sector of a node `g`, the
  hyperbolic score is guided towards `g` for every width `≥ 1` (at every depth the ancestor of
  `g` is strictly the closest node to the target; this uses the hyperbolic law of cosines);
* `hyperbolic_beam_finds` — consequently, if `g` carries a certified proof, hyperbolic beam
  search returns it after generating at most `1 + g.length · width · b` nodes;
* **negative-curvature volume expansion** (`sibling_separation`, `euclid_adjacent_le`,
  `volume_expansion`): when `ℓ ≥ log b`, any two distinct nodes of the same depth `m ≥ 1` stay at
  hyperbolic distance `≥ arcosh (1 + 1/64)` from each other, uniformly in `m`, although adjacent
  nodes are Euclidean-closer than `b ^ (-m) → 0`; and the hyperbolic ball of radius `k ℓ` has
  volume at least `c · bᵏ` (room for all `bᵏ` nodes, `Sovereign.Autonomous.no_leaf_congestion`).
-/
/-! ### Lexicographic index and angular sectors -/

/-- The index of a node among the nodes of its depth (base-`b` reading of its tactic script,
the most recent tactic being the least significant digit). -/
/-- The angle of a node: the centre of its sector `[idx v / b^m, (idx v + 1) / b^m]`. -/
/-- The direction `θ` lies in the open angular sector of the node `v`. -/
/-- The sector of a node contains the sectors of all its descendants. -/

/-- Inside a unit interval `(A, A + 1)`, the centre `A + 1/2` is strictly the closest of all
the centres `J + 1/2`, `J ∈ ℕ`. -/

/-- If `θ` lies in the sector of `a`, the angle of `a` is strictly the closest to `θ` among the
angles of all nodes of the same depth. -/
/-! ### The hyperbolic embedding and the hyperbolic score -/

/-- A hyperbolic embedding of the `b`-ary proof-state tree in `Dⁿ`: an orthonormal frame
(the plane of the embedding) and a hyperbolic edge length `ℓ > 0`. -/

/-- A goal-direction predicted by an (untrusted) neural network: a point of `Dⁿ` given by its
hyperbolic radius and angle in the plane of the embedding. -/
/-- The position of a node: hyperbolic radius `ℓ · depth`, angle `angle v`. -/
/-- The target point of a neural prediction. -/

/-- The embedded node is the `NeuroBridge` ray point of its direction at hyperbolic depth
`ℓ · depth`. -/
/-- **Depth is hyperbolic radius**: `d_H(0, pos v) = ℓ · depth v`. -/
/-- The hyperbolic guidance score: hyperbolic distance from the node to the neural target. -/
/-- The beam configuration of hyperbolic beam search with width `w`. -/

/-- **Hyperbolic guidance.** If the neural target has positive hyperbolic radius and its
direction lies in the open sector of the node `g`, then at every depth the ancestor of `g` is
strictly the closest node to the target, so the hyperbolic score is guided towards `g`. -/

/-- **Hyperbolic beam search finds a certified proof in linear time.** If the goal node `g`
passes the certification gate and the neural target (of positive radius) points into the
sector of `g`, hyperbolic beam search of any width `w ≥ 1` returns the certified proof path at
`g`, after generating at most `1 + g.length · w · b` nodes. -/
/-! ### Negative curvature: separation and volume expansion -/

/-- **Uniform hyperbolic separation.** If `ℓ ≥ log b` (`b ≥ 2`), any two distinct nodes of the
same depth `m ≥ 1` satisfy `cosh d_H ≥ 1 + 1/64`, i.e. they stay at hyperbolic distance at least
`arcosh (1 + 1/64)`, independently of the depth. -/
-- the angular separation
-- `sinh t ≥ B / 4`
-- conclude with the hyperbolic law of cosines
/-- The uniform separation in terms of the hyperbolic distance. -/

/-- **Euclidean congestion**: two adjacent nodes of depth `m` are Euclidean-closer than
`b ^ (-m)`. -/
/-- Two adjacent nodes at every depth `m ≥ 1` (for `b ≥ 2`). -/

/-- **Negative-curvature volume expansion** for the embedded proof-state tree (`b ≥ 2`,
`ℓ ≥ log b`, `n ≥ 2`):
1. distinct nodes of the same depth `m ≥ 1` are hyperbolically separated by at least
   `arcosh (1 + 1/64)`, uniformly in `m`;
2. at every depth there are adjacent nodes whose Euclidean distance is at most `b ^ (-m)`,
   which tends to `0`;
3. the hyperbolic ball of radius `k ℓ` has volume at least `c · bᵏ` for all large `k`. -/

structure TacticTable (R F : Type) (b : ℕ) where
  /-- the kernel rule justifying tactic `i` -/
  rule : Fin b → R
  /-- the premises left by tactic `i` on a goal, or `none` if it does not apply -/

namespace TacticTable

variable {R F : Type} (T : TacticTable R F b)

/-- Tactic application on goal stacks (the first goal is worked on). -/

declarations.name: step
declarations.signature_heuristic:
def step : Option (List F) → Fin b → Option (List F)
  | some (g :: gs), i => (T.back i g).map (· ++ gs)
  | _, _ => none

/-- Replay a tactic script (in application order) into a proof tree of the goal `g`, returning
the unused rest of the script. -/

declarations.name: build
declarations.signature_heuristic:
def build : ℕ → List (Fin b) → F → Option (PTree R × List (Fin b))
  | 0, _, _ => none
  | _ + 1, [], _ => none
  | fuel + 1, i :: rs, g =>
    match T.back i g with
    | some [] => some (.leaf (T.rule i), rs)
    | some [p] => (build fuel rs p).map fun q => (.unary (T.rule i) q.1, q.2)
    | some [p, p'] => (build fuel rs p).bind fun q =>
        (build fuel q.2 p').map fun q' => (.binary (T.rule i) q.1 q'.1, q'.2)
    | _ => none

end TacticTable

/-!
# The neuro-symbolic hyperbolic beam engine over the existing stack

* `TacticTable` — `b` goal-directed tactics: tactic `i` names a kernel rule and, given the
  current goal, proposes the premises that remain to be proved (backward chaining).
* `goalDirected T K G` — the proof space whose states are goal stacks (`none` for a failed
  tactic); a tactic script is replayed into a proof tree by `TacticTable.build`
  (untrusted: the kernel `K` has the last word).
* `neuroSpace T lib G` — the instance with the strict, `sorry`-rejecting kernel
  `Sovereign.Repair.strict lib`. Every path returned by hyperbolic beam search is a
  `NeuroBridge.CertifiedPath`, contains no `sorry`, and its goal is valid when the library is
  (`neuro_search_sound`).
* A worked example: for the goal `2 = 2` with two tactics, a genuine reflexivity step and a
  `sorry` hole, the gate rejects the hole (`exSpace_rejects_hole`) and hyperbolic beam search
  returns the genuine proof (`exSpace_found`).
-/
/-- A table of `b` goal-directed tactics over kernel rules `R` and formulas `F`. -/
/-- the kernel rule justifying tactic `i` -/
/-- the premises left by tactic `i` on a goal, or `none` if it does not apply -/
/-- Tactic application on goal stacks (the first goal is worked on). -/

/-- Replay a tactic script (in application order) into a proof tree of the goal `g`, returning
the unused rest of the script. -/
/-- The goal-directed proof space of a tactic table, kernel `K` and goal `G`. -/

/-- The neuro-symbolic instance: goal-directed search over the `Sovereign.Bridge` statement
language, certified by the strict (`sorry`-rejecting) kernel over the library `lib`. -/

/-- A certified path of the neuro-symbolic instance is a `NeuroBridge` certified deduction
path. -/

/-- **Soundness of the neuro-symbolic hyperbolic beam engine.** Every proof path returned by
hyperbolic beam search (with any embedding, neural target and width) is a `NeuroBridge`
certified deduction path, contains no `sorry`, also checks under the permissive checker, is
cut-free, non-circular, and proves a valid goal whenever the library is valid. -/
/-! ### A worked example -/
/-- Two tactics for the goal `2 = 2`: `0` is reflexivity, `1` is a `sorry` hole. -/
/-- The example proof space. -/
/-- The reflexivity step closes the goal and passes the gate. -/
/-- The `sorry` step also closes the goal stack, but the gate rejects it. -/

/-- Hyperbolic beam search (any embedding, width `1`, neural target at the sector of the
reflexivity step) returns the genuine proof after generating at most `3` nodes. -/

/-!
# The hierarchical tree of proof states

A goal-directed proof search unfolds a rooted tree of **proof states**: the root is the initial
goal, and applying one of the `b` available tactics to a state yields a child state (a failed
tactic application is simply a dead state that is never closed). Every node of the tree is
addressed by its **tactic script** `v : Addr b`, the list of tactic indices applied so far,
*most recent first*. The tree has branching factor `b`.

* `level b m` enumerates the `b ^ m` nodes at depth `m` (`length_level`, `mem_level`,
  `nodup_level`); `anc v k` is the depth-`k` ancestor of `v`.
* `ProofSpace` packages the search problem: root state, tactic semantics, closedness test, an
  *untrusted* proof reconstruction `extract` (turning a closed tactic script into a proof tree
  `PTree R`), and the trusted kernel `kernel : RuleSystem R F` with the goal formula.
* `trace v` is the list of proof states along the path to `v`; a path is **non-circular**
  (`NonCircular`) when no proof state repeats on it.
* `acyclicB K Γ t` checks that along every branch of the proof tree `t` no formula is derived
  twice (no goal is used, directly or indirectly, in its own derivation);
  `acyclicB_goal_not_reused` states this property.
* `certB v` is the **certification gate** at node `v`: it accepts the reconstructed proof tree
  only if the state is closed, the path is non-circular, the kernel certifies the tree as a proof
  of the goal, and the tree is acyclic. `CertifiedPath` records all of this;
  `CertifiedPath.valid` (soundness), `CertifiedPath.cutFree` (cut-freeness in the sense of
  `Sovereign.Synthesis.CProof`) and `CertifiedPath.nonCircular'` are its guarantees.
-/
/-- Node addresses: tactic scripts, most recent tactic first. -/
/-! ### Levels of the `b`-ary tree -/
/-- The nodes at depth `m` of the `b`-ary tree. -/
/-- The depth-`k` ancestor of a node (for `k ≤ v.length`). -/
/-- The depth-`(k+1)` ancestor is a child of the depth-`k` ancestor. -/
/-! ### Proof spaces -/

/-- A goal-directed proof search problem with `b` tactics, proof states `S`, kernel rules `R` and
formulas `F`. -/
/-- the initial proof state (the goal to prove) -/
/-- tactic semantics: the proof state after applying tactic `i` -/
/-- the proof state has no open goals -/
/-- untrusted proof reconstruction from a tactic script -/
/-- the trusted kernel -/
/-- the formula to prove -/
/-- The proof state at a node. -/
/-- The proof states along the path from a node back to the root. -/
/-- A path is **non-circular** if no proof state repeats along it. -/
/-- Applying tactic `i` at `v` reaches a proof state not yet visited on the path. -/
/-! ### Acyclic (non-circular) proof trees -/
/-- The conclusion of `t` is defined and does not occur among the formulas `Γ`. -/

/-- `acyclicB K Γ t`: along every branch of `t`, no conclusion repeats and none lies in `Γ`
(the formulas being proved by the enclosing derivation). -/
/-- Every subtree occurrence of an acyclic tree proves a formula outside `Γ`. -/
/-- The immediate sub-derivations of a proof tree. -/

/-- **No goal is used in its own derivation**: in an acyclic proof tree, no sub-derivation (at
any depth) proves the formula that the whole tree proves. -/
/-! ### Cut-freeness -/

/-- A proof with cuts (`Sovereign.Synthesis.CProof`) is **cut-free** if it contains neither a
`cut` nor a reference `hyp` to a cut lemma. -/
/-! ### The certification gate -/

/-- The certification gate: the reconstructed proof tree at `v`, if the state is closed, the path
is non-circular, the kernel certifies the tree as a proof of the goal and the tree is acyclic. -/

/-- A **certified proof path**: a node of the search tree together with a proof tree that passed
the certification gate. -/
/-- Package a gate acceptance as a certified path. -/
/-- **Soundness**: with a sound kernel, the goal of a certified path is valid. -/

/-- **Cut-freeness**: the certificate, viewed as a proof with cuts, is cut-free, checks with the
goal as conclusion, and is a fixed point of cut elimination. -/

/-- **Non-circularity**: no proof state repeats along the path, and no sub-derivation of the
certificate proves the goal itself. -/

/-!
# `Sovereign.HyperBeam`

Neuro-symbolic Poincaré beam search engine:
* `ProofTree`: hierarchical tree of proof states, non-circular trace invariants, acyclicity checks.
* `Beam`: goal-directed beam search with sub-exponential node generation bounds.
* `Embedding`: Poincaré ball D^n polar coordinate embedding and hyperbolic guidance.
* `Complexity`: formal proof of sub-exponential speedup over blind BFS/DFS.
* `Instance`: end-to-end integration with strict kernel and verified tactic tables.
* `Checks`: kernel certification of axioms.
-/

/-!
# The lemma-abduction operator: hyperbolic nearest admissible lemma

Candidate lemmas and the broken goal state are embedded in the Poincaré ball `Dⁿ`. To keep the
operator *executable* (so that the kernel can run it with `decide`), embeddings take values in
the lattice points `ZPt n N`: points `v / N` with `v ∈ ℤⁿ` and `‖v‖² < N²`. `ZPt.toBall` maps them
into `Dⁿ`, and all hyperbolic comparisons are carried out exactly in integer arithmetic:

* `closerB_iff`: the integer test `closerB g a b` holds **iff**
  `d_H(g, a) ≤ d_H(g, b)` for the hyperbolic distance of `Sovereign.Autonomous.PoincareBall`.
* `argminB`: a generic executable arg-min; `argminB_mem`, `argminB_min`, `argminB_eq_none`.
* `abduce adm emb g pool`: among the candidates of `pool` accepted by the admissibility test
  `adm` (in the engine: the kernel's relative-induction check), return the one whose embedding
  is at **minimal hyperbolic distance** from the broken goal state `g`. `abduce_spec` proves
  exactly this, and `abduce_eq_none_iff` shows it fails only if no candidate is admissible.
-/
/-- Squared Euclidean norm of an integer vector. -/
/-- Squared Euclidean distance of two integer vectors. -/
/-- A lattice point `v / N` of the Poincaré ball `Dⁿ`. -/
/-- The real point `v / N ∈ ℝⁿ`. -/
/-- The point of `Dⁿ` represented by a lattice point. -/

/-- `d_H` is monotone in `cosh d_H`: comparisons of distances reduce to comparisons of
`coshDist`. -/
/-- Exact integer test for "`a` is at most as far from `g` as `b` is", in hyperbolic distance. -/
/-- **The integer test decides hyperbolic proximity.** -/
/-! ### Executable arg-min -/
/-- Arg-min of a list with respect to a Boolean comparison (ties go to the earlier element). -/
/-- The arg-min is minimal for any real-valued function the comparison decides. -/
/-! ### The abduction operator -/

/-- **Lemma abduction**: the admissible candidate at minimal hyperbolic distance from the broken
goal state `g`. -/

/-- **Specification of abduction**: the abduced lemma comes from the pool, is admissible, and
minimises the hyperbolic distance `d_H(g, ·)` among all admissible candidates. -/
/-- Abduction fails only if no candidate of the pool is admissible. -/

/-!
# Non-circularity of synthesized invariants: vanishing first cohomology

The justification structure of a synthesized certificate `A = [c_k, …, c_1]` is its
**dependency graph** `certGraph A`: vertex `j ≤ k` is the stratum `c_1 ∧ … ∧ c_j` (vertex `0`
is the empty invariant), vertex `k + 1` is the safety goal, and edge `j` is the kernel step
that derives vertex `j + 1` from vertex `j` (a `push c_{j+1}` step, justified by relative
induction over stratum `j` only, or the final `close` step). These are exactly the `k + 2`
inference steps of `certTree A` (`certGraph_card_vertices`).

Using the integral Čech-style cohomology `H¹(G; ℤ)` of `Sovereign.PoUW.CechZ`:

* `pathGraph_H1Z_subsingleton`: the chain graph has `H¹(G; ℤ) = 0` (explicit potentials);
* `certGraph_H1Z_subsingleton`, `certGraph_H1_subsingleton`: vanishing over `ℤ` and `ℚ`;
* `certGraph_not_hasCircularLoop`, `certGraph_not_hasUndirectedCycle`: no circular or
  redundant reasoning; `certGraph_cechCertB`: the executable Čech check accepts it;
* `certGraph_edge_increasing`: every justification points strictly forward (no stratum uses
  a later one);
* `repair_nonCircular`: packages these facts for every proof tree returned by the engine.
-/
/-- The chain graph `0 → 1 → ⋯ → m`. -/
/-- Partial sums of an integer cochain along the chain. -/
/-- **`H¹(chain; ℤ) = 0`**: every integral 1-cochain is a coboundary. -/
/-- The dependency graph of the certificate `A`. -/
/-- The vertices of the dependency graph are the inference steps of the certificate tree. -/
/-- Every justification edge points strictly forward. -/
/-- **Vanishing integral first cohomology** of the certificate's dependency graph. -/
/-- The executable Čech certificate check of `Sovereign.PoUW` accepts the dependency graph. -/

/-- **Non-circularity of every repaired proof**: the returned tree is the certificate tree of
strata synthesized by the engine; each stratum is inductive relative to the earlier strata only;
no sub-derivation re-derives the goal; and the dependency graph has vanishing first cohomology
over `ℤ` (hence no circular or redundant reasoning). -/

theorem synth_perm : ∀ (k : ℕ) (A pool : List C),
    ((P.synth k A pool).1 ++ (P.synth k A pool).2).Perm (A ++ pool)
  | 0, _, _ => List.Perm.refl _
  | k + 1, A, pool => by
    simp only [synth]
    split_ifs
    · exact List.Perm.refl _
    · split

        have hmem

declarations.name: synth_stuck

    goalB P.loop P.sem (P.synth k A pool).1 = true ∨
      ∀ c ∈ (P.synth k A pool).2, relIndB P.loop P.sem (P.synth k A pool).1 c = false
  | 0, A, pool, h => by
    right; simp [synth, List.length_eq_zero_iff.1 (Nat.le_zero.1 h)]
  | k + 1, A, pool, h => by
    simp only [synth]
    split_ifs with hg
    · exact Or.inl hg
    · split
      · rename_i hn
        exact Or.inr (abduce_eq_none_iff.1 hn)
      · rename_i c hc
        apply synth_stuck
        rw [List.length_erase_of_mem (next_spec hc).1]; omega

/-!
# The autonomous invariant synthesizer and proof-repair engine

**Repaired proof trees.** A repaired proof is a proof tree `PTree (IRule C)` in the sense of
`Sovereign.Compression`/`Sovereign.HyperBeam`, checked by the rule system `kernel L sem`:

* `nil` proves `inv []` (the empty invariant);
* `push c` turns a proof of `inv A` into a proof of `inv (c :: A)`, provided `c` is inductive
  relative to `A` (`relIndB`);
* `close` turns a proof of `inv A` into a proof of `safe`, provided `A` implies safety.

`kernel_sound` proves the rule system sound for the intended semantics `IValid`
(`inv A` = "every reachable state satisfies `A`", `safe` = "every reachable state is safe").

**Admission gate.** `admitB t` accepts a tree iff the kernel certifies it as a proof of `safe`
and it is acyclic in the sense of `Sovereign.HyperBeam.acyclicB` (no formula is derived twice
on a branch). `admitted_sound`: **every admitted tree — whoever produced it — proves that all
reachable states of the loop are safe.**

**Synthesis.** `synth` runs the abduction loop: while the current certificate does not close
the goal, `abduce` (`Sovereign.InvariantRepair.Abduction`) picks, among the pool lemmas that are
inductive relative to the current strata, the one at minimal hyperbolic distance from the
broken goal state, pushes it as a new stratum, and removes it from the pool. `repair` runs
`synth` on the whole library and returns the certificate tree only if the gate admits it.

Main guarantees:
* `repair_admitted`, `repair_sound`: the output is admitted, hence verified.
* `repair_eq_some_iff`: the gate only fails when the synthesized strata do not imply safety.
* `synth_stagesOK`, `synth_suffix`, `synth_inductive` — non-circular stratification,
  monotone growth, inductiveness of the synthesized invariant.
* `synth_stuck`: if synthesis stops without closing the goal, no remaining library lemma is
  inductive relative to the synthesized strata.
* Size bounds: `synth_length_le`, `certTree_size`, `csize_synth_le`, `synthCalls_le`.
-/
/-- Formulas of the repair kernel. -/
/-- Rules of the repair kernel. -/
/-- The kernel of the repair engine. -/
/-- The intended semantics of kernel formulas. -/
/-- **The repair kernel is sound.** -/
/-! ### Certificate trees -/
/-- The proof tree of the strata `A` (newest lemma at the root). -/
/-- The repaired proof tree for the certificate `A`. -/
/-- Chain trees of valid strata are acyclic below any context of "later" formulas. -/
/-- **Certificate tree size**: `|A| + 2` inference steps. -/
/-! ### The admission gate -/
/-- The admission gate for repaired proof trees. -/

/-- **Every admitted proof tree is verified**: it proves that all reachable states are safe;
moreover no sub-derivation re-derives its conclusion (non-circularity, `HyperBeam`). -/
/-! ### The synthesis loop -/

/-- An instance of the repair problem: a loop, a lemma library semantics, lemma sizes, the
hyperbolic embedding of lemmas and the embedded broken goal state. -/
/-- One abduction step from strata `A` with remaining pool `pool`. -/
/-- The synthesis loop with fuel; returns the final strata and the remaining pool. -/
/-- The repair engine: synthesize from the whole library, then pass the gate. -/

/-- The number of kernel checks performed by `synth` (one goal check per round plus one
relative-induction check per pool lemma). -/
/-- Certificate size: encoding length of the lemmas (each at least one symbol). -/
/-- **Non-circular stratification is preserved**: synthesis only ever produces valid strata. -/
/-- **Monotone growth**: each round extends the certificate; earlier strata are never revised. -/
/-- Strata and pool together are a permutation of the starting material. -/

/-- **Stuck means genuinely stuck**: with enough fuel, synthesis either closes the goal or no
remaining lemma is inductive relative to the synthesized strata. -/
/-- **Rounds bound**: the synthesized certificate has at most `|library|` lemmas. -/

/-- **Polynomial (linear) certificate size**: the synthesized certificate is no larger than
the library it was drawn from. -/
/-- **Polynomial number of kernel checks**: at most `(|pool| + 1)²`. -/

/-- The synthesized invariant holds initially, is inductive (monotone under transitions) and
holds in every reachable state. -/
/-! ### Guarantees of the repair engine -/
/-- **Every repaired proof tree returned by the engine passes the admission gate.** -/
/-- **Soundness of repair**: a returned proof tree proves that every reachable state is safe. -/
/-- The gate rejects the synthesized certificate only when its strata do not imply safety. -/

/-!
# A worked repair, executed by the Lean kernel

The loop has states `(x, flag) : Fin 4 × Bool`, starts at `(0, false)` and steps
`x ↦ x + 2 (mod 4)`, `flag ↦ flag || (x = 1)`. The safety property is `flag = false`.

The obvious invariant `flag = false` is **not** inductive on its own (from the unreachable state
`(1, false)` the flag gets set), so a direct proof by induction breaks. The library offers four
candidate lemmas embedded in `D²` (lattice points `v / 10`):

| lemma       | meaning        | embedding | inductive?                       |
|-------------|----------------|-----------|----------------------------------|
| `flagFalse` | `flag = false` | `(0, 7)`  | only relative to `xEven`         |
| `notTwo`    | `x ≠ 2`        | `(0, 8)`  | never (`0 ↦ 2`)                  |
| `xEven`     | `x ∈ {0, 2}`   | `(5, 5)`  | yes                              |
| `top`       | `true`         | `(-9, 0)` | yes, but useless                 |

The broken goal state sits at `(0, 9)`. The engine first abduces `xEven` (the closest
admissible lemma: `notTwo` is closer but not inductive, `top` is admissible but farther), then
`flagFalse` (now inductive relative to `xEven`), and closes the goal. Everything below is
checked by `decide`, i.e. by evaluation in the Lean kernel, and `demo_safe` is an ordinary Lean
theorem about the loop obtained from the engine's soundness theorem.
-/
/-- Loop states. -/
/-- The loop. -/
/-- The candidate lemmas. -/
/-- Their meaning. -/
/-- Their embedding in `D²`. -/
/-- The repair problem, with the broken goal state at `(0, 0.9)`. -/
/-- The library. -/
/-- The direct invariant `flag = false` is not inductive: the naive proof is broken. -/
/-- First abduction: `xEven`, although `notTwo` is closer and `top` is also admissible. -/
/-- Second abduction: `flagFalse`, now inductive relative to `xEven`. -/
/-- **The engine repairs the proof**: the synthesized certificate is `[flagFalse, xEven]`. -/
/-- The repaired proof tree passes the admission gate. -/
/-- **The resulting Lean theorem**: every reachable state of the loop is safe. -/
/-- The executable Čech check confirms `H¹ = 0` for the repaired certificate's dependency graph. -/

/-- Without the auxiliary lemma `xEven`, no repair exists within the library and the engine
correctly reports failure. -/

  | x :: y :: t => by

declarations.name: firstDev_spec
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem firstDev_spec (g : PoincareBall n) :
    ∀ (l : List (PoincareBall n)) (i : ℕ), firstDev g l = some i →
      ∃ (hi : i + 1 < l.length), 0 < defect g l[i] l[i + 1] ∧
        ∀ j (hj : j < i), defect g (l[j]'(by omega)) (l[j + 1]'(by omega)) = 0
  | [], i, h => by simp [firstDev] at h
  | [_], i, h => by simp [firstDev] at h
  | x :: y :: t, i, h => by
    have h1

declarations.name: brokenState
declarations.signature_heuristic:
noncomputable def brokenState (g x : PoincareBall n) (t : List (PoincareBall n)) :
    PoincareBall n

declarations.name: brokenState_deviates
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem brokenState_deviates (g x : PoincareBall n) (t : List (PoincareBall n)) {i : ℕ}
    (h : firstDev g (x :: t) = some i) :
    ∃ (hi : i + 1 < (x :: t).length), brokenState g x t = (x :: t)[i] ∧
      dH (brokenState g x t) g < dH (brokenState g x t) ((x :: t)[i + 1]) +
        dH ((x :: t)[i + 1]) g

declarations.name: remaining_eq
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem remaining_eq (g x : PoincareBall n) (t : List (PoincareBall n)) :
    dH (lastPt x t) g = dH x g - pathLen (x :: t) + totalDefect g (x :: t)

/-!
# Proof-failure trajectories as discrete deviations from geodesics in `Dⁿ`

A symbolic proof attempt visits a sequence of proof states. Embedding every state in the
Poincaré ball `Dⁿ` (`Sovereign.Autonomous.PoincareBall`) turns the attempt into a discrete
trajectory `x₀, x₁, …, x_k` of points of `Dⁿ`, and the goal of the proof into a target point `g`.

A successful, non-wasteful attempt moves along the hyperbolic geodesic towards `g`: every step
`xᵢ → xᵢ₊₁` satisfies `d_H(xᵢ, xᵢ₊₁) + d_H(xᵢ₊₁, g) = d_H(xᵢ, g)`. The **step defect**

  `defect g x y = d_H(x, y) + d_H(y, g) - d_H(x, g) ≥ 0`

measures how far one step leaves the geodesic (it is `≥ 0` by the triangle inequality).

* `totalDefect_eq`: the defects telescope — the total defect of a trajectory equals its
  hyperbolic length plus the remaining distance to the goal, minus the initial distance.
* `onGeodesic_iff`: a trajectory follows the geodesic to `g` (length + remaining distance =
  initial distance) iff every step has defect `0`.
* `firstDev`: the index of the first step with positive defect — the point where the proof
  attempt *broke*. `firstDev_eq_none_iff` and `firstDev_spec` characterise it, and
  `brokenState` is the proof state at which the deviation starts; it is the goal state handed
  to the lemma-abduction operator.
-/
/-- The defect of a single step `x → y` relative to the geodesic towards `g`. -/
/-- Hyperbolic length of a discrete trajectory. -/
/-- Total geodesic defect of a trajectory towards `g`. -/
/-- The last point of a nonempty trajectory. -/
/-- **Telescoping**: total defect = length + remaining distance − initial distance. -/

/-- The trajectory follows the hyperbolic geodesic towards `g`: its length plus the remaining
distance equals the initial distance to `g`. -/
/-- All steps of the trajectory have zero defect. -/
/-- **Geodesic characterisation**: a trajectory follows the geodesic to `g` iff no step deviates. -/
/-- Index of the first step with positive defect (the first deviation from the geodesic). -/

/-- **Failure trajectories**: the proof attempt `x :: t` fails to follow the geodesic to `g`
exactly when a first deviation exists. -/

/-- **Specification of the first deviation**: at index `i` the step `lᵢ → lᵢ₊₁` has positive
defect, and all earlier steps have defect `0`. -/

/-- The **broken goal state**: the proof state at which the attempt first leaves the geodesic
(or the final state if the attempt never deviates). -/

/-- At the broken state, the next step of the attempt strictly moves away from the geodesic:
the detour through the next state is strictly longer than going straight to `g`. -/

/-- The remaining distance to the goal after a trajectory equals the initial distance minus the
distance travelled plus the accumulated defect: every unit of deviation is lost progress. -/

declarations.name: Loop
declarations.signature_heuristic:
structure Loop (σ : Type) where
  init : σ → Bool
  step : σ → σ → Bool
  safe : σ → Bool

namespace Loop

variable {σ : Type} (L : Loop σ)

/-- Reachable states of the loop. -/

declarations.name: Reach
declarations.signature_heuristic:
inductive Reach : σ → Prop
  | init {s : σ} : L.init s = true → Reach s
  | step {s t : σ} : Reach s → L.step s t = true → Reach t

end Loop

variable {σ C : Type} (L : Loop σ) (sem : C → σ → Bool)

/-- The conjunction of the lemmas `A` at state `s`. -/

declarations.name: conj
declarations.signature_heuristic: def conj (A : List C) (s : σ) : Bool

declarations.name: conj_eq_true
declarations.signature_heuristic: theorem conj_eq_true {A : List C} {s : σ} : conj sem A s = true ↔ ∀ c ∈ A, sem c s = true

declarations.name: conj_antitone
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem conj_antitone {A B : List C} (h : A ⊆ B) {s : σ} (hB : conj sem B s = true) :
    conj sem A s = true

declarations.name: relIndB
declarations.signature_heuristic: def relIndB (A : List C) (c : C) : Bool

declarations.name: relIndB_iff
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem relIndB_iff {A : List C} {c : C} :
    relIndB L sem A c = true ↔ (∀ s, L.init s = true → sem c s = true) ∧
      ∀ s t, conj sem A s = true → sem c s = true → L.step s t = true → sem c t = true

declarations.name: stagesOK
declarations.signature_heuristic:
def stagesOK : List C → Bool
  | [] => true
  | c :: A => relIndB L sem A c && stagesOK A

declarations.name: stagesOK_cons
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem stagesOK_cons {c : C} {A : List C} :
    stagesOK L sem (c :: A) = true ↔ relIndB L sem A c = true ∧ stagesOK L sem A = true

declarations.name: goalB
declarations.signature_heuristic: def goalB (A : List C) : Bool

declarations.name: goalB_iff
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem goalB_iff {A : List C} :
    goalB L sem A = true ↔ ∀ s, conj sem A s = true → L.safe s = true

declarations.name: checkB
declarations.signature_heuristic: def checkB (A : List C) : Bool

declarations.name: relInd_invariant
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem relInd_invariant {A : List C} {c : C} (hc : relIndB L sem A c = true)
    (hA : ∀ s, L.Reach s → conj sem A s = true) : ∀ s, L.Reach s → sem c s = true

declarations.name: stagesOK_invariant
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem stagesOK_invariant : ∀ {A : List C}, stagesOK L sem A = true →
    ∀ s, L.Reach s → conj sem A s = true
  | [], _, s, _ => rfl
  | c :: A, h, s, hr => by
    obtain ⟨hc, hA⟩

declarations.name: stagesOK_init
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem stagesOK_init {A : List C} (h : stagesOK L sem A = true) {s : σ}
    (hs : L.init s = true) : conj sem A s = true

declarations.name: stagesOK_inductive
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem stagesOK_inductive : ∀ {A : List C}, stagesOK L sem A = true →
    ∀ s t, conj sem A s = true → L.step s t = true → conj sem A t = true
  | [], _, _, _, _, _ => rfl
  | c :: A, h, s, t, hs, hst => by
    obtain ⟨hc, hA⟩

declarations.name: stagesOK_iff_forall
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem stagesOK_iff_forall : ∀ {A : List C}, stagesOK L sem A = true ↔
    ∀ i (hi : i < A.length), relIndB L sem (A.drop (i + 1)) A[i] = true
  | [] => by simp [stagesOK]
  | c :: A => by
    rw [stagesOK_cons, stagesOK_iff_forall]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨hc, hA⟩ i hi
      cases i with
      | zero => simpa using hc
      | succ i => simpa using hA i (by simpa using hi)
    · intro h
      exact ⟨by simpa using h 0 (by simp), fun i hi => by simpa using h (i + 1) (by simpa using hi)⟩

/-- **Soundness of the checker**: an accepted certificate proves that every reachable state of
the loop is safe. -/

declarations.name: checkB_sound
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem checkB_sound {A : List C} (h : checkB L sem A = true) :
    ∀ s, L.Reach s → L.safe s = true

/-!
# Loops, stratified inductive invariants and their exact checker

A loop is a finite transition system `Loop σ` (initial states, a transition relation and a
safety property, all Boolean-valued). An invariant is built from *candidate lemmas* `c : C`,
each denoting a state predicate `sem c : σ → Bool`. Invariants are therefore higher-order
objects — predicates on states assembled from a library of predicates — and they are
certified *stratum by stratum*:

A certificate `A = [c_k, …, c_1]` (newest lemma first) is valid (`stagesOK`) when every lemma
`c_i` is **inductive relative to the earlier strata** `c_1 ∧ … ∧ c_{i-1}`:
`init ⇒ c_i` and `c_1 ∧ … ∧ c_{i-1} ∧ c_i ∧ step ⇒ c_i'` (`relIndB`). The lemma may use itself
(this is the induction step, not a circularity) and the *earlier* strata, never later ones.

* `relIndB_iff`, `stagesOK_iff_forall`: the Boolean checks decide exactly the mathematical
  conditions (the checker is neither too strict nor too lax).
* `stagesOK_invariant`: every stratum holds in every reachable state.
* `stagesOK_inductive` (**monotonicity under transitions**): the synthesised conjunction is
  closed under the loop's transition relation.
* `conj_antitone`: adding lemmas can only shrink the invariant set (strata strengthen
  monotonically).
* `checkB_sound`: a certificate whose final stratum implies the safety property proves that
  every reachable state is safe.
-/
/-- A finite loop / transition system with a safety property. -/
/-- Reachable states of the loop. -/
/-- The conjunction of the lemmas `A` at state `s`. -/
/-- **Strata strengthen monotonically**: more lemmas, smaller invariant set. -/
/-- `c` is inductive relative to the strata `A`. -/
/-- Validity of a stratified certificate (newest lemma first). -/
/-- The final stratum implies safety. -/
/-- The trusted certificate checker. -/
/-- A relatively inductive lemma holds in every reachable state, provided its strata do. -/
/-- **Invariance**: every stratum holds in every reachable state. -/
/-- The initial states satisfy the whole certificate. -/
/-- **Monotonicity under transitions**: the synthesised invariant is inductive. -/
/-- The Boolean certificate check is exactly the stratified relative-induction condition. -/

/-- **Soundness of the checker**: an accepted certificate proves that every reachable state of
the loop is safe. -/

declarations.name: repair_main
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem repair_main (P : Problem σ C n N) (lib : List C) (t : PTree (IRule C))
    (h : P.repair lib = some t) :
    ∃ A : List C, t = certTree A ∧
      -- verification
      admitB P.loop P.sem t = true ∧
      (∀ s, P.loop.Reach s → P.loop.safe s = true) ∧
      -- monotonicity
      (∀ s, P.loop.init s = true → conj P.sem A s = true) ∧
      (∀ s u, conj P.sem A s = true → P.loop.step s u = true → conj P.sem A u = true) ∧
      (∀ s, P.loop.Reach s → conj P.sem A s = true) ∧
      (∀ B, B <:+ A → ∀ s, conj P.sem A s = true → conj P.sem B s = true) ∧
      -- non-circularity
      (∀ i (hi : i < A.length), relIndB P.loop P.sem (A.drop (i + 1)) A[i] = true) ∧
      (∀ p ∈ premises t, ∀ u ∈ p.occurrences, (kernel P.loop P.sem).concl u ≠ some .safe) ∧
      Subsingleton (certGraph A).H1Z ∧ ¬ (certGraph A).HasCircularLoop ∧
      -- polynomial size
      t.size ≤ lib.length + 2 ∧ P.csize A ≤ P.csize lib ∧
      P.synthCalls lib.length [] lib ≤ (lib.length + 1) ^ 2

declarations.name: abduction_geodesic
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem abduction_geodesic (P : Problem σ C n N) (g x : PoincareBall n)
    (traj : List (PoincareBall n)) (hg : P.goal.toBall = brokenState g x traj)
    {A pool : List C} {c : C} (h : P.next A pool = some c) :
    c ∈ pool ∧ relIndB P.loop P.sem A c = true ∧
      ∀ c' ∈ pool, relIndB P.loop P.sem A c' = true →
        dH (brokenState g x traj) (P.emb c).toBall ≤ dH (brokenState g x traj) (P.emb c').toBall

/-!
# Main theorem of the invariant synthesizer and geodesic proof-repair engine

`repair_main` collects, for every repair problem and every lemma library, the guarantees of a
proof tree returned by `Problem.repair`:

1. **verification** — the tree passes the kernel/acyclicity gate and proves that every
   reachable state of the loop is safe;
2. **monotonicity** — the synthesized invariant holds initially, is closed under the transition
   relation, and holds in every reachable state; its strata only strengthen;
3. **non-circularity** — each stratum is inductive relative to earlier strata only, no
   sub-derivation re-derives the goal, and the dependency graph has `H¹(G; ℤ) = 0`;
4. **polynomial size** — at most `|lib| + 2` inference steps, encoding size at most that of the
   library, and at most `(|lib| + 1)²` kernel checks during synthesis.

`abduction_geodesic` states the abduction property relative to a failure trajectory: when the
goal point of the problem is the broken state of a proof attempt that left the geodesic, each
abduced lemma is, among the admissible ones, at minimal hyperbolic distance from that state.
-/

/-- **Main theorem.** Every proof tree admitted and returned by the repair engine is verified,
and the synthesized invariant is monotone, non-circular and of polynomial size. -/
-- verification
-- monotonicity
-- non-circularity
-- polynomial size

/-- **Abduction along a failure trajectory.** If the problem's goal point is the broken state
of a proof attempt `x :: traj` towards `g` (the state where it first leaves the geodesic), then
every abduced lemma is admissible and minimises the hyperbolic distance to that broken state
among all admissible lemmas of the pool. -/

/-!
# `Sovereign.InvariantRepair`

Autonomous higher-order inductive invariant synthesis & Poincaré geodesic proof repair:
* `Geodesic`: proof failure trajectories as discrete deviations from geodesics in D^n.
* `Abduction`: automated lemma abduction operator minimizing hyperbolic geodesic distance.
* `Invariant`: loops, stratified inductive invariants and their exact Boolean checker.
* `Engine`: admission gate and synthesis loop guaranteeing kernel-verified proofs.
* `Cohomology`: vanishing 1-cohomology H^1(G, Z) = 0 and non-circularity.
* `Main`: repair_main theorem guaranteeing sound, non-circular, polynomial proof trees.
* `Examples`: worked repair problem executed by the Lean kernel.
* `Checks`: kernel certification of axioms.
-/

/-!
# The Cayley–Dickson tower `ℝ ⊂ ℂ ⊂ ℍ ⊂ 𝕆 ⊂ 𝕊`

The Cayley–Dickson double of an algebra `A` with involution is `CD A = A × A` with

* `(a, b) * (c, d) = (a c - d* b, d a + b c*)`,
* `(a, b)* = (a*, -b)`,

and we realise it as `WithLp 2 (A × A)`, so that each stage automatically carries the
Euclidean (`L²`) inner product and norm `‖(a, b)‖² = ‖a‖² + ‖b‖²`.

* `Cplx := CD ℝ` (2D), `Quat := CD Cplx` (4D), `Oct := CD Quat` (8D, the octonions),
  `Sed := CD Oct` (16D, the sedenions).
* `Oct.norm_mul`: the octonions are a composition algebra, `‖x y‖ = ‖x‖ ‖y‖`.
* `Oct.star_mul_mul_left`: left alternativity in the form `u* (u x) = ‖u‖² x`.
* `Oct.inner_mul_left`: `⟪u x, u y⟫ = ‖u‖² ⟪x, y⟫`.
* `Oct.inner_mul_left_skew`: left multiplication by a purely imaginary octonion is skew.
* `Oct.not_associative`: `(e₁ e₂) e₄ = -(e₁ (e₂ e₄)) ≠ e₁ (e₂ e₄)`.
* `Sed.zero_divisor`: `(e₃ + e₁₀)(e₆ - e₁₅) = 0` in the sedenions, and
  `Sed.not_norm_mul`: the sedenion norm is not multiplicative.
-/
/-- The Cayley–Dickson double of `A`, carrying the `L²` product norm. -/
/-- First ("real") half. -/
/-- Second ("imaginary") half. -/
/-- Build a Cayley–Dickson element from its two halves. -/
/-- The Cayley–Dickson product `(a, b)(c, d) = (a c - d* b, d a + b c*)`. -/
/-- The Cayley–Dickson conjugation `(a, b)* = (a*, -b)`. -/
/-- The complex numbers as the first Cayley–Dickson double of `ℝ`. -/
/-- The quaternions (4D). -/
/-- The octonions (8D). -/
/-- The sedenions (16D). -/
/-- The octonion with the eight given real coordinates `x₀ + x₁ e₁ + ⋯ + x₇ e₇`. -/
/-- The octonion basis element `eᵢ`. -/
/-- The sedenion basis element `eᵢ` (`i < 8`: `(eᵢ, 0)`, `i ≥ 8`: `(0, e_{i-8})`). -/
/-- The real part of an octonion. -/
/-- The norm squared of an octonion is the sum of the squares of its coordinates. -/
/-- **Octonions form a composition algebra**: `‖x y‖² = ‖x‖² ‖y‖²`. -/
/-- **Octonions form a composition algebra**: `‖x y‖ = ‖x‖ ‖y‖`. -/
/-- Left alternativity: `u* (u x) = ‖u‖² x`. -/
/-- Left multiplication by `u` scales inner products by `‖u‖²`. -/
/-- Left multiplication by a purely imaginary octonion is skew-adjoint. -/
/-- Left multiplication is additive. -/
/-- Left multiplication is `ℝ`-homogeneous. -/
/-- **Octonions are not associative**: `(e₁ e₂) e₄ ≠ e₁ (e₂ e₄)`; in fact they are opposite. -/
/-- The sedenion norm squared, as a sum of the two octonion halves. -/
/-- **Sedenions have zero divisors**: `(e₃ + e₁₀)(e₆ - e₁₅) = 0`. -/

/-- **The sedenion norm is not multiplicative**: the 16D stage of the tower is no longer a
composition algebra. -/

/-!
# Multi-sensor Gaussian fusion attains the Bayesian Cramér–Rao bound

A scalar field parameter `θ` (e.g. one coordinate of the synesthetic octonion at a point) has a
Gaussian prior `N(μ₀, v₀)` and is observed by `K` independent sensors (acoustic, optical,
gravitational, thermal, …) with Gaussian noise: `y_k = θ + n_k`, `n_k ~ N(0, v_k)`.

* `fusionModel`: this is a `BayesianModel` on `ℝ × ℝᴷ` with joint density
  `f(θ, y) = φ(θ; μ₀, v₀) ∏ₖ φ(y_k; θ, v_k)` and score

/-!
# Multi-spectral waves on the synesthetic tensor manifold

Four physical wave channels — **acoustic, optical, gravitational, thermal** — each carry a
complex (phasor) amplitude. With positive channel weights `w_c` (energy per unit squared
amplitude) the multi-spectral energy is `∑_c w_c |a_c|²`.

* `SpectralState.embed`: the embedding `ℂ⁴ ≅ 𝕆`, `a_c ↦ √w_c a_c`, into the 8D octonions;
  it is injective (`embed_injective`) and **isometric for the energy**:
  `‖embed ψ‖² = energy ψ` (`norm_sq_embed`).
* `SpectralState.embedPair`: a pair of multi-spectral states (e.g. a field and its conjugate
  momentum) embeds into the 16D sedenions with `‖·‖² = energy ψ + energy φ`
  (`norm_sq_embedPair`).
* The synesthetic tensor manifold is the trivial bundle `ℝ × ℝ³ × 𝕆` of such amplitudes over
  space-time; its sections are the fields of `WaveSystem Oct 3`.
* `energy_unitRotation`: a non-associative coordinate change (a chain of unit-octonion left
  multiplications) preserves the multi-spectral energy of every state.

## Bridges to the existing development

* `ofSensory`: the acoustic pressure and optical field of a `SensoryConfig` of
  `Sovereign.Taxonomy.SynestheticResonance`; `embed_ofSensory_resonance`: at a synchronized
  resonance point the embedded octonion vanishes at all times.

  tensor functor's action (`norm_embed_avSample_map`).

`rotatingWave`: `ψ(t, x) = g(x₀ + c₀ t) (cos t · v + sin t · e₁ v)` solves the octonionic coupled
system with propagation `Aᵢ = cᵢ · id` and channel coupling `L_{e₁}` (`rotatingWave_solution`),
so the Poynting–Helmholtz theorem applies to a non-trivial, channel-mixing travelling wave.

/-!
# The generalized Poynting–Helmholtz energy theorem

A **symmetric hyperbolic wave system** on a real inner product space `E` of field amplitudes,
over `n` spatial dimensions, is
`∂ₜψ = ∑ᵢ Aᵢ ∂ᵢψ + B ψ` with every `Aᵢ` self-adjoint (propagation) and `B` skew (lossless
coupling between the physical channels).

* `energyDensity ψ = ½ ‖ψ‖²`, `flux i ψ = -½ ⟪ψ, Aᵢ ψ⟫` (the generalized Poynting vector).
* `poynting_helmholtz`: every solution satisfies the local conservation law
  `∂ₜ u + ∇ · S = 0`.

## Non-associative coordinate transformations

A change of field coordinates is any linear isometry `T` of `E`; the system is transported to
`(T Aᵢ T⁻¹, T B T⁻¹)` (`WaveSystem.transport`), solutions to solutions
(`Solution.transport`), and the energy density and flux are *unchanged pointwise*
(`energyDensity_transport`, `flux_transport`); so the conservation law holds with the same
densities in both coordinate systems (`poynting_helmholtz_transport`).

On the octonions `E = 𝕆`, the left multiplication `L_u` by a unit octonion is such an isometry
(`Oct.leftMul`, inverse `L_{u*}` by alternativity), and so is every chain
`L_{u₁} ∘ ⋯ ∘ L_{uₖ}` (`Oct.chain`). Because `𝕆` is not associative, these chains are *not*
left multiplications by the product (`Oct.chain_ne_leftMul`): the transformations form a
genuinely non-associative family, and the energy theorem holds across all of them
(`octonionic_poynting_helmholtz`).
-/
/-- A symmetric hyperbolic, lossless linear wave system. -/
/-- Propagation matrices. -/
/-- Lossless coupling between the channels. -/
/-- The `i`-th coordinate direction of `ℝⁿ`. -/

/-- A (classical) solution: a field with its time and space partial derivatives, satisfying the
system at every event. -/
/-- The energy density `u = ½ ‖ψ‖²`. -/
/-- The generalized Poynting flux `Sᵢ = -½ ⟪ψ, Aᵢ ψ⟫`. -/
/-- The divergence `∇ · S = ∑ᵢ ∂ᵢ Sᵢ`. -/

/-- **Generalized Poynting–Helmholtz theorem**: every solution of a symmetric hyperbolic,
lossless wave system satisfies the local energy conservation law `∂ₜ u + ∇ · S = 0`. -/
/-! ### Transport along isometric coordinate changes -/
/-- The system in the new field coordinates `φ = T ψ`: `(T Aᵢ T⁻¹, T B T⁻¹)`. -/
/-- Solutions are carried to solutions of the transported system. -/
/-- The energy density is invariant under the coordinate change. -/
/-- The Poynting flux is invariant under the coordinate change. -/

/-- **Poynting–Helmholtz across coordinate changes**: in the new coordinates the conservation law
holds, with energy density and flux equal to the original ones at every event. -/
/-! ### Octonionic coordinate changes -/
/-- Left multiplication by an octonion, as a continuous linear map. -/
/-- The unit octonions. -/
/-- Left multiplication by a unit octonion is a linear isometry of `𝕆`, with inverse `L_{u*}`. -/
/-- The composite `L_{u₁} ∘ L_{u₂} ∘ ⋯ ∘ L_{uₖ}` of left multiplications. -/
/-- The unit octonion `eᵢ`. -/

/-- **The octonionic coordinate changes are non-associative**: the chain `L_{e₁} ∘ L_{e₂}` is not
the left multiplication by the product `e₁ e₂`. -/

/-- An octonionic coupled wave system: arbitrary symmetric propagation operators on the 8
real amplitudes, coupled by left multiplication by a purely imaginary octonion `u`. -/

/-- **Octonionic Poynting–Helmholtz theorem**: for every solution of an octonionic wave system
and every chain of unit-octonion left multiplications (a non-associative coordinate change),
the transformed field obeys the conservation law `∂ₜ u + ∇ · S = 0` with energy density and

/-!
# The Bayesian Cramér–Rao bound (Van Trees inequality)

A **Bayesian estimation model** for a real parameter `θ` observed through data `y ∈ Y` is a
joint density `f(θ, y) = p(y | θ) π(θ) ≥ 0` on `ℝ × Y` (w.r.t. `Lebesgue ⊗ ν`), of total mass
`1`, differentiable in `θ` with score `s = ∂_θ log f`, i.e. `∂_θ f = s f`, and with finite
**Bayesian Fisher information** `J = ∫∫ s² f` (`BayesianModel.fisher`).

An estimator `T : Y → ℝ` is *regular* if it has finite Bayesian mean squared error
`mse T = ∫∫ (T(y) - θ)² f` and, for every observation `y`, the functions
`θ ↦ f(θ, y)`, `θ ↦ (T(y) - θ) f(θ, y)` and `θ ↦ (T(y) - θ) ∂_θ f(θ, y)` are integrable (the
usual boundary condition: `(T(y) - θ) f(θ, y)` has integrable derivative, hence integrates it to
zero).

* `BayesianModel.score_identity`: `∫∫ (T(y) - θ) s f = 1` for every regular estimator;
* `BayesianModel.van_trees`: **Van Trees inequality** `mse T ≥ 1 / J` (and `J > 0`);
* `BayesianModel.mse_eq_of_error_eq_score`: if the error of `T` is proportional to the score,
  `T(y) - θ = s(θ, y) / J₀`, then necessarily `J = J₀` and `mse T = 1 / J`: the bound is
  attained.
-/
/-- A Bayesian estimation model with a real parameter. -/
/-- Joint density `p(y | θ) π(θ)`. -/
/-- Score `∂_θ log f`. -/
/-- The Bayesian Fisher information `J = E[s²]` (prior information included). -/
/-- The Bayesian mean squared error `E[(T(y) - θ)²]` of an estimator. -/

/-- A regular estimator: measurable, finite mean squared error, and the per-observation
integrability conditions that justify integrating by parts in `θ`. -/
/-- Integration by parts in `θ` for a fixed observation. -/
/-- **Bayesian score identity**: `E[(T(y) - θ) s(θ, y)] = 1` for every regular estimator. -/

/-- **Van Trees inequality (Bayesian Cramér–Rao bound)**: every regular estimator has Bayesian
mean squared error at least `1 / J`, where `J > 0` is the Bayesian Fisher information. -/

/-- **Attainment**: if the error of a regular estimator is proportional to the score,
`T(y) - θ = s(θ, y) / J₀`, then `J₀` is the Bayesian Fisher information and the estimator
attains the Van Trees bound, `mse T = 1 / J`. -/

/-!
# The CNF engine gate: clausal refutation proofs, as SAT solvers emit them

`LRAGate.lean` and `PropGate.lean` make an external engine attach a checkable witness to every
answer. This file adds the format used by SAT solvers: a formula in conjunctive normal form is
answered either with a **model**, or with a **clausal refutation proof** in the style of
LRAT (reverse unit propagation with hints).

A refutation is a list of steps `(c, hints)`. Each step adds the clause `c` to the database,
after checking that `c` follows by *reverse unit propagation*: assume every literal of `c` is
false, then walk through the hint clauses (all already in the database). Each hint must either
become a unit clause, whose literal is then assumed, or be falsified outright, which closes the
step. The proof is accepted once it adds the empty clause.

Hints name clauses by content, not by index, so the checker only needs membership in the
database. The kernel can evaluate the checker (`decide +kernel`).

Proved here:

* `rupCheck_sound`, `checkRefutation_sound`: an accepted refutation proves that the formula has
  no model.
* `checkVerdict_sound`: an accepted verdict (`unsat` with a proof, or `sat` with a model) is
  correct in both directions.
* `checkRefutation_fullRefutation`, `checkVerdict_complete`: every unsatisfiable formula has an
  accepted refutation. `fullRefutation F` is a computable reference certificate: it derives
  every clause that mentions each variable of `F` once, then shortens these clauses one
  variable at a time down to the empty clause. It has exponential size, but its existence
  shows that a correct engine never needs an unchecked pass.

The Python side is the `cnf` claim kind of `scripts/audit/engine_gate.py`.

The industrial format — numeric clause identifiers, RAT steps and clause deletion — is checked
by `LRATGate.lean` (with DRAT elaboration in `DRATGate.lean` and the `lrat_refute` tactic in
`LRATTactic.lean`); `LRATComplete.lean` translates the refutations of this file into LRAT.
-/
/-! ### Syntax and semantics -/
/-- A literal: a variable with a sign (`pos = true` for `x`, `false` for `¬x`). -/
/-- The complementary literal. -/
/-- A clause is a disjunction of literals; a CNF formula is a conjunction of clauses. -/
/-- A formula in conjunctive normal form. -/
/-- The value of a literal under a total valuation. -/
/-- The value of a clause under a total valuation. -/
/-- `v` satisfies every clause of `F`. -/
/-- `F` has a model. -/
/-! ### Reverse unit propagation with hints -/

/-- Check one step. `α` lists the literals currently assumed true. Each hint must be in the
database `db`. Its literals that are not falsified by `α` must be either none (conflict:
success) or exactly one literal `l`, which is then assumed. -/
/-- A proof step: a clause to add, with the hints that justify it. -/
/-- Check a list of steps from the database `db`; accept at the first empty clause. -/
/-- The gate for refutations: check the proof starting from the formula itself. -/
/-! ### Soundness -/

/-- **Soundness of one propagation step**: if the check succeeds, no model of `db` makes all
literals of `α` true. -/
/-- A clause accepted by reverse unit propagation holds in every model of the database. -/
/-- **Soundness of the refutation gate**: an accepted refutation proves unsatisfiability. -/
/-! ### Completeness: a reference certificate for every unsatisfiable formula -/
/-- The variables of a formula, without repetition. -/
/-- All clauses that contain exactly one literal of each variable of `xs`, in order. -/
/-- The hint for a clause of the top level: a clause of `F` contained in it. -/
/-- The top level: every clause over all variables, justified by a clause of `F`. -/

/-- Remove the variables of `xs` one at a time: a clause over `ys` follows from its two
extensions by the variable `y` in front of `ys`. -/
/-- The reference refutation of `F`. -/
/-! #### Helper lemmas for completeness -/
/-- Propagation only looks hints up in the database, so enlarging it preserves acceptance. -/
/-- Running a block `L` of steps, each justified from `db0` and none empty, then `rest`. -/
/-- If every literal of a clause is falsified, the filter in `rupCheck` leaves nothing. -/
/-- Every clause of `allClauses ys` has exactly the variables `ys`, in order. -/
/-- **Shortening step**: a clause `c` not mentioning `y` follows from `y ∨ c` and `¬y ∨ c`. -/

/-- **Top step**: over all variables of an unsatisfiable `F`, a full clause is justified by a
clause of `F` that it contains. -/
-- the valuation making every literal of `c` false
-- some clause of `F` is falsified by `w`, hence contained in `c`
/-- The shortening levels derive the empty clause from all full clauses over `y :: ys`. -/
/-- **Completeness**: the reference refutation of an unsatisfiable formula is accepted. -/
/-! ### Verdicts and the gate -/
/-- An engine's answer for a CNF formula, with its witness. -/
/-- `F` is unsatisfiable; the witness is a clausal refutation. -/
/-- `F` is satisfiable; the witness lists the variables set to `true`. -/
/-- Whether the verdict claims unsatisfiability. -/
/-- The valuation making exactly the listed variables true. -/
/-- The gate: check the witness attached to the verdict. -/
/-- An accepted model proves satisfiability. -/
/-- An accepted refutation proves unsatisfiability. -/
/-- **Soundness of the gate**: an accepted verdict is correct in both directions. -/
/-- **Completeness of the gate**: every formula has a verdict that the gate accepts. -/
/-- A refutation and a model are never both accepted for the same formula. -/
/-! ### Worked examples, in the form the Python gate generates -/
/-- All four clauses over `x₀, x₁`: `(x₀ ∨ x₁) ∧ (¬x₀ ∨ x₁) ∧ (x₀ ∨ ¬x₁) ∧ (¬x₀ ∨ ¬x₁)`. -/
/-- A three-step clausal refutation: derive `x₁`, then `¬x₁`, then the empty clause. -/
/-- The reference certificate is accepted too. -/
/-- Dropping the last clause leaves a satisfiable formula, with model `x₀ = x₁ = true`. -/

declarations.name: SoundRefuter
declarations.signature_heuristic:
structure SoundRefuter {Φ : Type u} {M : Type v} (Sat : M → Φ → Prop) where
  /-- The Boolean refutation procedure. -/
  refutes : Φ → Bool
  /-- Soundness: a refuted formula has no model. -/
  sound : ∀ φ, refutes φ = true → ∀ m, ¬ Sat m φ

/-- A certified monotone upgrade of the sound refuter `base`: a certificate-producing refuter
whose certificates are validated by a sound checker, and which refutes everything that `base`
refutes. -/

declarations.name: CertifiedMonotoneUpgrade
declarations.signature_heuristic:
structure CertifiedMonotoneUpgrade {Φ : Type u} {M : Type v} (Sat : M → Φ → Prop)
    (base : SoundRefuter Sat) where
  /-- The type of refutation certificates for a formula. -/
  Cert : Φ → Type u
  /-- The certificate checker. -/
  check : (φ : Φ) → Cert φ → Bool
  /-- Soundness of the checker: a checked certificate refutes the formula. -/
  check_sound : ∀ φ c, check φ c = true → ∀ m, ¬ Sat m φ
  /-- The certificate producer. -/
  certify : (φ : Φ) → Option (Cert φ)
  /-- Every produced certificate passes the checker. -/
  certify_checks : ∀ φ c, certify φ = some c → check φ c = true
  /-- Monotonicity: whatever the base refuter refutes, the upgrade refutes (with a certificate). -/
  monotone : ∀ φ, base.refutes φ = true → (certify φ).isSome = true

namespace CertifiedMonotoneUpgrade

variable {Φ : Type u} {M : Type v} {Sat : M → Φ → Prop} {base : SoundRefuter Sat}

/-- The upgraded refuter: refute `φ` iff a certificate is produced for it. It is sound, since
produced certificates pass the sound checker. -/

declarations.name: upgraded
declarations.signature_heuristic:
def upgraded (U : CertifiedMonotoneUpgrade Sat base) : SoundRefuter Sat where
  refutes φ

declarations.name: refutes_mono
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem refutes_mono (U : CertifiedMonotoneUpgrade Sat base) (φ : Φ)
    (h : base.refutes φ = true) : U.upgraded.refutes φ = true

/-!
# Sound refuters and certified monotone upgrades

A *refuter* for a logic with formulas `Φ`, models `M` and satisfaction relation
`Sat : M → Φ → Prop` is a Boolean procedure `refutes : Φ → Bool`; it is *sound* when every
formula it refutes has no model.

A *certified monotone upgrade* of a sound base refuter is a new refuter that
* works by producing certificates `certify φ : Option (Cert φ)`,
* comes with a certificate checker `check` that is sound on its own (a checked certificate
  guarantees that `φ` has no model), and every produced certificate passes the checker,
* is *monotone*: every formula refuted by the base refuter is also refuted by the upgrade.

The upgraded refuter is then automatically sound (`CertifiedMonotoneUpgrade.upgraded`), and its
soundness does not depend on trusting the certificate producer, only the checker.
-/
/-- A sound refutation procedure for formulas `Φ` with respect to `Sat : M → Φ → Prop`. -/
/-- The Boolean refutation procedure. -/
/-- Soundness: a refuted formula has no model. -/

/-- A certified monotone upgrade of the sound refuter `base`: a certificate-producing refuter
whose certificates are validated by a sound checker, and which refutes everything that `base`
refutes. -/
/-- The type of refutation certificates for a formula. -/
/-- The certificate checker. -/
/-- Soundness of the checker: a checked certificate refutes the formula. -/
/-- The certificate producer. -/
/-- Every produced certificate passes the checker. -/
/-- Monotonicity: whatever the base refuter refutes, the upgrade refutes (with a certificate). -/

/-- The upgraded refuter: refute `φ` iff a certificate is produced for it. It is sound, since
produced certificates pass the sound checker. -/
/-- The upgraded refuter refutes at least as much as the base refuter. -/

declarations.name: sweep
declarations.signature_heuristic:
def sweep (α : List Lit) (acc : List Nat) : List (Nat × Clause) → List Lit × List Nat × Bool
  | [] => (α, acc, false)
  | (j, d) :: rest =>
    match d.filter (fun l => !(decide (l.neg ∈ α))) with
    | [] => (α, j :: acc, true)
    | [l] => if l ∈ α then sweep α acc rest else sweep (l :: α) (j :: acc) rest
    | _ => sweep α acc rest

/-- Sweep until a conflict (returning the used clauses, in order) or until nothing changes. -/

declarations.name: findHints
declarations.signature_heuristic:
def findHints (es : List (Nat × Clause)) : Nat → List Lit → List Nat → Option (List Nat)
  | 0, _, _ => none
  | fuel + 1, α, acc =>
    match sweep α acc es with
    | (α', acc', conflict) =>
      if conflict then some acc'.reverse
      else if acc'.length == acc.length then none
      else findHints es fuel α' acc'

/-- RUP hints for `α` from the stored clauses, if unit propagation reaches a conflict. -/

declarations.signature_heuristic:
def elabSteps : ElabDB → Nat → List DStep → List LStep
  | _, _, [] => []
  | s, next, .del c :: rest =>
    match c with
    | [_] => elabSteps s next rest
    | _ =>
      match findByContent s c with
      | some j => .del [j] :: elabSteps (s.erase j) next rest
      | none => elabSteps s next rest
  | s, next, .add c :: rest =>
    let step : LStep
