comments.text: /-! ## 1. Sentence center and geometric dispersion -/
/-- Sentence center `u_t = (1/n) ∑ᵢ h_{t,i}` of the final-layer token embeddings. -/
/-- Geometric dispersion `δ_t = (1/n) ∑ᵢ ‖h_{t,i}‖² − ‖u_t‖²`. -/
/-- **Dispersion is a variance.** `δ_t = (1/n) ∑ᵢ ‖h_{t,i} − u_t‖²`. -/
/-- The geometric dispersion is nonnegative. -/
/-- The dispersion vanishes iff every token embedding equals the sentence center. -/
/-! ## 2. Step velocity and directional consistency -/
/-- Step velocity `v_t = ‖u_t − u_{t−1}‖`. -/

/-- Directional consistency
`c_t = ⟨u_t − u_{t−1}, u_{t−1} − u_{t−2}⟩ / (‖u_t − u_{t−1}‖ ‖u_{t−1} − u_{t−2}‖ + ε)`. -/
/-- For `ε > 0` the directional consistency lies strictly between `−1` and `1`. -/
/-- Consecutive steps pointing in the same direction give positive consistency. -/
/-! ## 3. Predictive entropy -/
/-- Shannon entropy `𝓗(p) = −∑ₖ pₖ log pₖ` of a next-token distribution. -/
/-- Mean predictive entropy `H_t = (1/n) ∑ᵢ 𝓗(p_{t,i})` over the tokens of a sentence. -/
/-- The mean predictive entropy of probability vectors is nonnegative. -/
/-! ## 4. The 4-dimensional state and its normalisation -/
/-- The raw endogenous state `s_t = (δ_t, v_t, c_t, H_t) ∈ ℝ⁴`. -/
/-- Normalisation `m_t = (s_t − μ) / (σ + ε)`, coordinatewise. -/
/-- Undo the normalisation. -/
/-- With nonnegative scales and `ε > 0` the normalisation is injective. -/
/-- The normalised state vanishes exactly at the normalisation center `μ`. -/
/-! ## 5. The 16-dimensional relational descriptor -/

/-- The relational descriptor `d_{t,i} = [m_t; m_i; m_t − m_i; m_t ⊙ m_i] ∈ ℝ¹⁶`
(coordinates `4b + k` hold block `b`, entry `k`). -/
/-- Block `b` of a 16-vector (`b = 0,1,2,3`). -/
/-- The descriptor determines the pair of states `(m_t, m_i)`. -/
/-- Comparing a state with itself: zero drift, and squared coordinates as interaction. -/
/-! ## 6. The controller heads -/
/-- Number of parameters of a dense layer `Linear(i → o)` (weights and biases). -/
/-- Evidence-selection head `φ_sel = Linear(16 → 32) ∘ Linear(32 → 1)`. -/
/-- Stopping head `φ_stop = Linear(4 → 1)`. -/

/-- **Parameter budget.** `Linear(16→32)` has `544` parameters and `Linear(32→1)` has `33`,
so `φ_sel` has `577`; `φ_stop` has `5`; the controller has `582` parameters in all. -/
/-- The logistic sigmoid. -/
/-- Stopping probability `σ(⟨w, m_t⟩ + b)` of the stopping head. -/

/-- **The stopping head is a linear threshold rule.** For `0 < τ < 1`,
`σ(⟨w, m⟩ + b) > τ ↔ ⟨w, m⟩ + b > log (τ / (1 − τ))`. -/
/-! ## 7. The training-free baseline -/
/-- Euclidean norm on `ℝ⁴`. -/

/-- Training-free score
`s^tf_{t,j} = α₁⟨m_t, m_j⟩ − α₂‖m_t − m_j‖ + α₃ c_j − α₄ H_j`. -/

/-- The training-free score is a fixed function of the descriptor: `⟨m_t, m_j⟩` is the sum
of the interaction block and `‖m_t − m_j‖` is the norm of the drift block. -/

/-- With nonnegative weights the training-free score increases with the consistency `c_j`
and decreases with the entropy `H_j`. -/

/-- Training-free stopping rule at step `t`: over the trailing window of the last `r` steps
the entropy and the velocity stay below their thresholds and the consistency is positive. -/
/-- Satisfying the stopping rule on a longer window implies it on a shorter one. -/

/-!
# Basic triples give octonion automorphisms

A *basic triple* (`IsBasicTriple u v z`) is a triple of unit imaginary octonions with
`u ⊥ v`, `z ⊥ u`, `z ⊥ v` and `z ⊥ u v`. For such a triple, `tripleMap u v z` is the linear map
sending the standard basis `1, e₁, …, e₇` of `K⁸` to `1, u, v, uv, z, uz, vz, (uv)z`.

* `isOctonionAut_tripleMap`: `tripleMap u v z` is an octonion automorphism;
* `tripleMap_e1`, `tripleMap_e2`, `tripleMap_e4`: it sends `e₁ ↦ u`, `e₂ ↦ v`, `e₄ ↦ z`.

The argument is Cayley–Dickson doubling. `D = span {1, u, v, uv}` is closed under the product
(`dmap_mul`) and `z ⊥ D`; for `a, c ∈ D` one has `a (c z) = (c a) z`
(`omul_assoc_of_perp`), `(a z) c = (a c̄) z` (`omul_perp_left_of_perp`) and
`(a z)(c z) = − c̄ a` (`omul_perp_perp`). Hence
`(a + b z)(c + d z) = (a c − d̄ b) + (d a + b c̄) z`, which is the Cayley–Dickson product
defining `𝕆 = ℍ ⊕ ℍ`.
-/
/-! ## Multiplication rules for an element orthogonal to a subalgebra -/
/-- If `z` is imaginary and `c ⊥ z`, then `c z = z c̄`. -/
/-- `a (b z) = (b a) z` when `a, b, b a ⊥ z` and `z` is imaginary. -/
/-- `(a z) c = (a c̄) z` when `c ⊥ z` and `z` is imaginary. -/
/-- `(a z)(c z) = − c̄ a` when `a, c, c a ⊥ z` and `z` is a unit imaginary octonion. -/
/-! ## The quaternion subalgebra spanned by an orthonormal imaginary pair -/

/-- The first four coordinates of `f`, as an element of the quaternion subalgebra
`ℍ = span {1, e₁, e₂, e₃}`. -/
/-- The last four coordinates of `f`, shifted into `ℍ`: `f = qlo f + (qsh f) e₄`. -/

/-- The embedding `ℍ → 𝕆` determined by an orthonormal imaginary pair `u, v`:
`1, e₁, e₂, e₃ ↦ 1, u, v, u v` (it only reads the first four coordinates). -/
/-- `dmap u v` is multiplicative: `D = span {1, u, v, u v}` is a quaternion subalgebra. -/
/-- `dmap u v` is an isometry on the first four coordinates. -/
/-- A *basic triple*: unit imaginary octonions `u, v, z` with `u ⊥ v` and `z ⊥ u, v, u v`. -/

/-- The linear map determined by a basic triple:
`1, e₁, e₂, e₃, e₄, e₅, e₆, e₇ ↦ 1, u, v, uv, z, uz, vz, (uv)z`, i.e.
`(p, q) ↦ ι p + (ι q) z` in Cayley–Dickson form, with `ι = dmap u v`. -/
/-- The Cayley–Dickson decomposition of the octonion product in coordinates, first half. -/
/-- The Cayley–Dickson decomposition of the octonion product in coordinates, second half. -/
/-- **A basic triple defines a multiplicative map.** -/
-- the four products appearing in the Cayley–Dickson formula
/-- **A basic triple defines an isometry.** -/
/-- **A basic triple defines an octonion automorphism.** -/

comments.text:
/-!
# `V₂(ℝ⁷) ≅ G₂ / SU(2)`

We realise `G₂` as the subgroup `G2` of the orthogonal group `O(8)` consisting of the matrices
whose linear map is an octonion automorphism (`IsOctonionAut`). It acts on the space
`ImOrthPair` of orthonormal pairs of imaginary octonions, which is a copy of the Stiefel manifold
`V₂(ℝ⁷)`.

* `G2.isPretransitive`: `G₂` acts transitively on orthonormal imaginary pairs;
* `G2.stabilizerMulEquivSU2`: the stabiliser of the base pair `(e₁, e₂)` is isomorphic, as a
  group, to `SU(2) = Matrix.specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ`;
* `G2.imOrthPairHomeomorphQuotient`: `ImOrthPair ≃ₜ G₂ ⧸ Stab(e₁, e₂)`;
* `stiefelV27HomeomorphG2Quotient`: the Stiefel manifold `V₂(ℝ⁷)` (`stiefelV27`) is
  homeomorphic to `G₂ ⧸ Stab(e₁, e₂)`, where `Stab(e₁, e₂) ≃* SU(2)`.
-/
/-! ## Octonion automorphisms form a group -/

/-- A left inverse of an octonion automorphism, which is also a right inverse, is an octonion
automorphism. -/
/-- The matrix of a dot-product-preserving linear map is orthogonal. -/

/-- **`G₂`** as a group of `8 × 8` orthogonal matrices: those whose linear map preserves the
octonion product. -/
/-- The matrix of an element of `G₂`. -/
/-- Every octonion automorphism of `ℝ⁸` is given by an element of `G₂`. -/
/-! ## Orthonormal imaginary pairs -/

/-- Ordered orthonormal pairs `(u, v)` of imaginary octonions: a copy of the Stiefel manifold
`V₂(ℝ⁷) = V₂(Im 𝕆)` inside `ℝ⁸ × ℝ⁸`. -/
/-- `G₂` acts on orthonormal imaginary pairs by `A • (u, v) = (A u, A v)`. -/
/-- The base pair `(e₁, e₂)`. -/
/-! ## Transitivity -/
/-- Every orthonormal imaginary pair extends to a basic triple. -/
/-- Every orthonormal imaginary pair is the image of the base pair `(e₁, e₂)`. -/
/-- **`G₂` acts transitively on orthonormal pairs of imaginary octonions.** -/

/-!
# The stabiliser of an orthonormal imaginary pair in `G₂` is `SU(2)`

Let `Stab = MulAction.stabilizer G2 basePair` be the subgroup of `G₂` fixing `e₁` and `e₂`.

* `G2.stab_mulVec`: an element `A ∈ Stab` is determined by `s = A e₄`, which lies in
  `span {e₄, e₅, e₆, e₇}`, via `A (p + q e₄) = p + q s` in Cayley–Dickson form; equivalently
  `A (p, q) = (p, s q)` for quaternions `p, q` and the unit quaternion `s`;
* `G2.stabToSU2`: the group homomorphism `Stab →* SU(2)` sending `A` to the `2 × 2` complex
  matrix of the unit quaternion `s = A e₄`;
* `G2.stabilizerMulEquivSU2`: this homomorphism is bijective, so `Stab ≃* SU(2)`.
-/

/-- The `2 × 2` complex matrix of the quaternion stored in coordinates `4, …, 7` of `s`:
`a + b j ↦ !![a, b; -b̄, ā]` with `a = s₄ + s₅ i`, `b = s₆ + s₇ i`. -/

/-- The quaternion product `(0, s)(q, 0)`-style composition law: for `s ∈ span {e₄, …, e₇}`,
the matrix of `q s` (with `q = qsh t`) is the product of the matrices of `s` and `t`. -/
/-- A special unitary `2 × 2` matrix has the form `!![a, b; -b̄, ā]`. -/
/-- The stabiliser of the base pair `(e₁, e₂)` in `G₂`. -/

/-- An element of the stabiliser is determined by `s = A e₄`: `A f = qlo f + (qsh f) s`, i.e.
`A (p + q e₄) = p + q s`. -/
/-- The homomorphism `Stab(e₁, e₂) →* SU(2)`, `A ↦` the matrix of the unit quaternion `A e₄`. -/
/-- **The stabiliser of an orthonormal imaginary pair in `G₂` is `SU(2)`.** -/

/-!
# `G₂ = Aut 𝕆` acts on the sedenion zero-divisor locus

An octonion automorphism is modelled as an orthogonal linear map `φ : K⁸ → K⁸` that
preserves the octonion product (`IsOctonionAut`). Over `ℝ` these maps form the compact Lie group
`G₂`. Over any ordered field we prove:

* `IsOctonionAut.map_one`, `IsOctonionAut.map_re`: `φ` fixes `1` and preserves real parts;
* `IsOctonionAut.octMap_conj`: `φ` commutes with octonion conjugation;
* `diagAct_mul`: `φ` acting diagonally on `𝕊 = 𝕆 ⊕ 𝕆` is a sedenion algebra homomorphism,
  `Φ(x y) = Φ(x) Φ(y)`;
* `diagAct_zeroDivisor_iff`: `Φ` maps zero divisors to zero divisors, and non-zero-divisors
  to non-zero-divisors.

So `G₂` acts on the zero-divisor locus by symmetries of the sedenion algebra. This is the
action behind the classical description of the unit locus `V₂(ℝ⁷)` as the homogeneous space
`G₂ / SU(2)`. That `G₂` acts *transitively* on `V₂(ℝ⁷)` with stabiliser `SU(2)` is proved in
`Sovereign.Meta.StateOfThoughtG2Homogeneous`, `…G2Stabilizer` and `…G2Quotient`.

/-!
# `G₂` acts transitively on orthonormal imaginary pairs: the algebra

For an orthonormal triple `u, v, z` of imaginary octonions with `z ⊥ u v` (a *basic triple*),
`tripleMap u v z` is the linear map `K⁸ → K⁸` sending the standard basis
`1, e₁, …, e₇` to `1, u, v, uv, z, uz, vz, (uv)z`. The main theorem is

* `isOctonionAut_tripleMap`: `tripleMap u v z` is an octonion automorphism
  (it preserves the octonion product and the dot product), with
  `tripleMap_e1 : Φ e₁ = u`, `tripleMap_e2 : Φ e₂ = v`, `tripleMap_e4 : Φ e₄ = z`.

The proof is the Cayley–Dickson doubling argument: `D = span {1, u, v, uv}` is a quaternion
subalgebra, `z ⊥ D`, and for `a, c ∈ D`
`a (c z) = (c a) z`, `(a z) c = (a c̄) z`, `(a z)(c z) = − c̄ a`,
so `(a + b z)(c + d z) = (a c − d̄ b) + (d a + b c̄) z`, which is exactly the Cayley–Dickson
product used to define the octonions. These three rules are derived from the linearised
alternative laws `x̄ (y w) + ȳ (x w) = 2⟨x, y⟩ w` and `(w x̄) y + (w ȳ) x = 2⟨x, y⟩ w`, which are
polynomial identities checked coordinatewise.

Everything here holds over an arbitrary field `K`.
-/
/-! ## The octonion product in coordinates -/
/-- Octonion conjugation in coordinates: `x̄ = x₀ − (x₁ e₁ + ⋯ + x₇ e₇)`. -/
/-- Fast coordinatewise check of an identity between vectors of `K⁸`. -/
/-- Fast check of a scalar identity involving octonion coordinates. -/
/-- Coordinatewise check of an identity between vectors of `K⁸`. -/
/-- Check of a scalar identity involving octonion coordinates. -/
/-- Polarised `x x̄ = |x|²`: `x ȳ + y x̄ = 2⟨x, y⟩`. -/
/-- Linearised left alternative law: `x̄ (y w) + ȳ (x w) = 2⟨x, y⟩ w`. -/
/-- Linearised right alternative law: `(w x̄) y + (w ȳ) x = 2⟨x, y⟩ w`. -/
/-- The octonion norm is multiplicative, in polarised form in the left factor. -/

/-- The sedenion dot product in coordinates. -/

/-- **The sedenionic compatibility score is the descriptor dot product.**
`Re (S_{t,i} · S̄_{j,k}) = ⟨d_{t,i}, d_{j,k}⟩`. -/

/-- The sedenionic score splits into the four quaternion-block dot products:
state, history, drift and interaction. -/
/-- The sedenionic score is symmetric. -/

/-- The self-score is the squared norm of the descriptor, and it vanishes only when both
states are zero. -/
/-! ## Zero-divisor traps realised by descriptors -/
/-- Annihilator `c e₁ − a e₃ − c e₁₃ + a e₁₅`. -/
/-- Annihilator `b e₁ − a e₂ − b e₁₃ + a e₁₄`. -/

/-- **Descriptor zero-divisor traps.** If the current normalised state is `m_t = 0` and the
historical state is a nonzero pure-imaginary quaternion `m_i = (0, a, b, c)`, then the
descriptor sedenion `S_{t,i}` is nonzero and is annihilated by a nonzero sedenion:
`S_{t,i} · Y = 0`. -/

/-- **Zero-divisor traps on the raw states.** Suppose the current raw state equals the
normalisation center, `s_t = μ`, and the historical raw state `s_i ≠ μ` has the same
dispersion coordinate as `μ`.  Then the descriptor sedenion built from the normalised states
`m_t, m_i` is a nonzero sedenion zero divisor. -/
/-! ## Inferential curvature: the associator along a trajectory -/

/-- Along the trajectory `m_{t−2} = (1,1,0,0)`, `m_{t−1} = (1,0,0,0)`, `m_t = (0,0,0,1)`,
compared with the reference history `m_i = 0`, the associator of the three descriptor
sedenions is `[S_{t−2}, S_{t−1}, S_t] = 4 e₂ ≠ 0`. -/

declarations.name: pick_le
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem pick_le : ∀ (cs : List α) (best : α), defect (pick defect ok cs best) ≤ defect best
  | [], _ => le_rfl
  | c :: cs, best => by
    simp only [pick]
    refine (pick_le cs _).trans ?_
    split_ifs with h
    · exact h.2.le
    · exact le_rfl

declarations.name: pick_spec
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem pick_spec : ∀ (cs : List α) (best : α),
    pick defect ok cs best = best ∨
      (pick defect ok cs best ∈ cs ∧ ok (pick defect ok cs best) ∧
        defect (pick defect ok cs best) < defect best)
  | [], _ => Or.inl rfl
  | c :: cs, best => by
    simp only [pick]
    split_ifs with h
    · rcases pick_spec cs c with h' | h'
      · exact Or.inr ⟨by simp [h'], by rw [h']; exact h.1, by rw [h']; exact h.2⟩
      · exact Or.inr ⟨List.mem_cons_of_mem _ h'.1, h'.2.1, h'.2.2.trans h.2⟩
    · rcases pick_spec cs best with h' | h'
      · exact Or.inl h'
      · exact Or.inr ⟨List.mem_cons_of_mem _ h'.1, h'.2⟩

declarations.name: pick_optimal
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem pick_optimal : ∀ (cs : List α) (best : α) (c : α), c ∈ cs → ok c →
    defect (pick defect ok cs best) ≤ defect c
  | [], _, _, h, _ => absurd h (List.not_mem_nil)
  | d :: cs, best, c, hc, hok => by
    simp only [pick]
    rcases List.mem_cons.1 hc with rfl | hc
    · refine (pick_le defect ok cs _).trans ?_
      split_ifs with h
      · exact le_rfl
      · push_neg at h
        exact h hok
    · exact pick_optimal cs _ c hc hok

end Pick

/-

# A verified step-selection filter with monotone semantic defect

A reasoning controller proposes, at every step, a finite list of candidate next states.
The filter below keeps a candidate only if it passes a guard and **strictly lowers** the
semantic defect; among the kept candidates it takes one of least defect, and if none is kept
it stays put.

Generic results (any state type, any linearly ordered defect):

* `select_defect_le`, `select_optimal`, `select_lt` : one step never increases the defect,
  is optimal among admissible candidates, and strictly decreases the defect whenever some
  admissible candidate improves on the current state;
* `select_spec` : the selected state is either the current state or a guarded candidate;
* `run_defect_antitone` : along the filtered run the defect is **monotonically
  non-increasing**; `run_move_lt` : every actual move strictly decreases it;
* `run_stabilizes` : for a `ℕ`-valued defect, the run is constant from step `D(s₀)` on.

Sedenion instance (`Window` = the last three descriptor sedenions `(S_{t−2}, S_{t−1}, S_t)`,
semantic defect = `‖[S_{t−2}, S_{t−1}, S_t]‖²`, guard = the new step pair `S_t · S_{t+1}` is not a
zero-divisor trap):

* `sedenionRun_defect_antitone` : the curvature defect is monotone non-increasing;
* `sedenionRun_avoids_traps` : every accepted step avoids a zero-divisor trap;
* `sedenionRun_flat_of_flat` : a run started on a flat window (e.g. three states of a valid
  deductive chain) stays flat forever: the curvature tensor is `0` at every step.
-/

/-- Scan candidates, replacing the incumbent by a candidate that passes the guard `ok` and has
strictly smaller defect. -/
/-- One filtered step from `cur` given the candidate list `cands`. -/
/-- A filtered step never increases the defect. -/

/-- The selected state is the current state, or a guarded candidate of strictly smaller
defect. -/

/-- The selected state is at least as good as every guarded candidate that does not increase
the defect. -/

/-- If some guarded candidate strictly improves on the current state, the step strictly
decreases the defect. -/

/-- The filtered run: at each step the candidates `proposals s` are filtered from the current
state `s`. -/
/-- **Monotone reduction of the defect along the filtered run.** -/
/-- Every step either stays put or moves to a guarded proposal of strictly smaller defect. -/
/-- Every actual move strictly decreases the defect. -/
/-- Once the run stays put, it stays put forever. -/

/-- **Stabilization.** For a natural-number defect `D`, the filtered run is constant from step
`D(s₀)` on. -/
/-! ## The sedenion curvature filter -/
/-- A reasoning window: the last three sedenion states `(S_{t−2}, S_{t−1}, S_t)`. -/

/-- **Semantic defect** of a window: the squared norm of its associator curvature
`‖[S_{t−2}, S_{t−1}, S_t]‖²`. -/
/-- Shift a window by a new state `v`: `(x, y, z) ↦ (y, z, v)`. -/
/-- The trap guard: the new step pair `(S_t, S_{t+1})` must not be annihilating. -/

/-- The sedenion curvature filter: from each window, the proposed next states are pushed and
filtered by `select` with the semantic defect and the trap guard. -/
/-- **Monotone reduction of the semantic defect** along the sedenion filter. -/

/-- Every step of the sedenion filter stays put, or appends a proposed state `v` such that
the new step pair is **not** a zero-divisor trap and the semantic defect strictly drops. -/

/-- **Flatness is preserved.** If the initial window has zero curvature, every window of the
filtered run has zero curvature tensor. -/
/-- A run started on three states of a valid deductive chain stays flat forever. -/

comments.text: /-- A sedenion all of whose 16 coordinates vanish is zero. -/

/-- **`Re a · ‖y‖² = 0` on annihilating pairs.** If `(a, b) y = 0` then `Re a · ‖y‖² = 0`.
(In fact `Re a · ‖y‖² = ⟨x y, y⟩`.) -/
/-- **`Re b · ‖y‖² = 0` on annihilating pairs.** -/
/-- **`⟨a, b⟩ · ‖y‖² = 0` on annihilating pairs with imaginary halves.** -/
/-- The explicit annihilator `y = (‖b‖² c, (a c) b)` of a Stiefel pair `(a, b)`. -/

/-- **Stiefel pairs are zero divisors.** If `a, b` are imaginary octonions with `‖a‖ = ‖b‖`
and `a ⊥ b`, and `c` is orthogonal to `1, a, b, a b`, then
`(a, b) · (‖b‖² c, (a c) b) = 0`. -/

comments.text:
/-!
# Sedenion zero divisors: two-sided characterization and the Stiefel manifold `V₂(ℝ⁷)`

`sedenion_zero_divisor_iff` characterizes the nonzero sedenions `x = (a, b)` with a nonzero
*right* annihilator. This file adds:

* `sedenion_left_zero_divisor_iff`, `sedenion_zero_divisor_two_sided`: the same conditions
  characterize left zero divisors, so all notions of "zero divisor" agree;
* `unitZeroDivisorsHomeomorphStiefel`: the set of zero divisors of Euclidean norm `1` in
  `ℝ¹⁶` is homeomorphic to the Stiefel manifold `V₂(ℝ⁷)` of orthonormal 2-frames in `ℝ⁷`
  (`mem_stiefelV27_iff_orthonormal` identifies `stiefelV27` with Mathlib's `Orthonormal`);
* `isCompact_unitZeroDivisors`: this locus is compact;
* `zeroDivisorsHomeomorphConeStiefel`: the set of all nonzero zero divisors is homeomorphic
  to the open cone `(0, ∞) × V₂(ℝ⁷)`;
* `isOpen_safe16`: the complement of the trap locus (the sedenions accepted by the guard) is
  open in `ℝ¹⁶`.
-/
/-- Split an equation between sedenions into its 16 coordinates. -/
/-- Conjugation reverses sedenion products: `conj (x y) = conj y · conj x`. -/
/-- Conjugation is an involution on sedenions. -/
/-- Conjugation fixes real parts of octonions. -/
/-- `⟨ā, b⟩ = 2 Re a Re b − ⟨a, b⟩` for octonions. -/

/-- **Left zero divisors.** Over any ordered field, a nonzero sedenion `x = (a, b)` has a
nonzero *left* annihilator (`y x = 0` with `y ≠ 0`) iff `Re a = Re b = 0`, `‖a‖ = ‖b‖` and
`⟨a, b⟩ = 0` — the same conditions as for right annihilators. -/

/-- **Two-sided zero divisors.** For a nonzero sedenion, having a nonzero left annihilator,
having a nonzero right annihilator, and the Stiefel conditions
`Re a = Re b = 0 ∧ ‖a‖ = ‖b‖ ∧ ⟨a, b⟩ = 0` are all equivalent. -/
/-! ## The unit zero-divisor locus is the Stiefel manifold `V₂(ℝ⁷)` -/
/-- The squared norm of a sedenion is the sum of the squares of its 16 coordinates. -/
/-- The Stiefel manifold `V₂(ℝ⁷)`: ordered orthonormal pairs `(u, v)` of vectors of `ℝ⁷`. -/

/-- The zero divisors of Euclidean norm `1` in `ℝ¹⁶ ≅ 𝕊`, written in coordinates: the points
`f` of the unit sphere of `ℝ¹⁶` such that the sedenion `ofFn16 f` has a nonzero right
annihilator (equivalently, by `sedenion_zero_divisor_two_sided`, a nonzero left
annihilator). -/
/-- Coordinate form of membership in the unit zero-divisor locus. -/
/-- `(a, b) ↦ (√2 · Im a, √2 · Im b)`, in coordinates. -/

/-- `(u, v) ↦ (u / √2, v / √2)`, placing `u` and `v` in the imaginary parts of the two
octonion halves. -/

/-- **Unit sedenion zero divisors form the Stiefel manifold `V₂(ℝ⁷)`.** The set of sedenion
zero divisors of Euclidean norm `1` (as a subspace of `ℝ¹⁶`) is homeomorphic to the space of
orthonormal pairs in `ℝ⁷`, via `(a, b) ↦ (√2 · Im a, √2 · Im b)`. -/
/-! ## Topology: orthonormal frames, compactness, and the cone over `V₂(ℝ⁷)` -/

/-- `stiefelV27` is exactly the set of orthonormal pairs in the Euclidean space `ℝ⁷`, in the
sense of Mathlib's `Orthonormal`. -/
/-- The Stiefel manifold `V₂(ℝ⁷)` is compact. -/
/-- The unit sedenion zero-divisor locus is compact. -/
/-! ## Scaling and the cone structure of the zero-divisor set -/
/-- Right zero divisors are invariant under nonzero rescaling. -/
/-- All nonzero sedenion zero divisors, in coordinates `ℝ¹⁶`. -/

/-- **The zero-divisor set is the open cone over `V₂(ℝ⁷)`.** The nonzero sedenion zero
divisors form a subspace of `ℝ¹⁶` homeomorphic to `(0, ∞) × V₂(ℝ⁷)`, via
`x ↦ (‖x‖, (√2 · Im a, √2 · Im b) / ‖x‖)`. -/
/-! ## The trap locus is closed: the safe set is open -/

/-- The trap locus in coordinates `ℝ¹⁶`: the sedenions with a nonzero right annihilator
(the nonzero zero divisors together with `0`). -/
/-- The trap locus is cut out by five real polynomial equations. -/
/-- The trap locus is closed in `ℝ¹⁶`. -/

/-- **Robustness of the guard.** The set of safe sedenions (those that are not zero divisors)
is open in `ℝ¹⁶`: every safe state has a neighbourhood of safe states. -/

# The windowed stopping rule as a counter automaton

Roadmap item 2.2 of `docs/STATE_OF_THOUGHT_ROADMAP.md`. The training-free stopping rule
`tfStop` of the appendix fires at step `t` when over the last `r` steps the entropy and the
velocity stay below their thresholds and the consistency is positive.

* `tfStop_mono_threshold` : the rule is monotone in both thresholds;
* `runLen` : a one-counter automaton reading the feature stream (length of the current run of
  "good" steps);
* `tfStop_iff_runLen` : the rule fires at `t` iff `min r (t + 1) ≤ runLen t`, so it can be
  evaluated online with a single counter instead of a window buffer;
* `tfStop_of_good_from` : if the conditions hold at every step from `t₀` on, the rule fires
  at step `t₀ + r − 1`, i.e. within `r − 1` steps (bounded latency);
* `tfStop_not_of_bad` : conversely it never fires while the current step is bad.
-/
/-- The stopping rule is monotone in the thresholds. -/

/-- A step is *good* when entropy and velocity are below threshold and consistency is
positive. -/
/-- The counter automaton: `runLen t` is the length of the run of good steps ending at `t`. -/
/-- `runLen t ≥ k` iff the last `k` steps up to `t` are all good (for `k ≤ t + 1`). -/

/-- **The stopping rule is a counter automaton.** `tfStop` fires at `t` exactly when the
counter `runLen t` has reached `min r (t + 1)`. -/

/-- **Bounded latency.** If the stopping conditions hold at every step from `t₀` on, then the
rule fires at step `t₀ + r − 1` (for `r ≥ 1`). -/
/-- The rule never fires (for `r ≥ 1`) at a step where the conditions fail. -/

comments.text: /-- The 8 coordinates of an octonion. -/
/-- Every three octonions admit a nonzero imaginary octonion orthogonal to all of them. -/

/-- **The sedenion zero-divisor theorem.** Over any ordered field, a nonzero sedenion
`x = (a, b)` has a nonzero right annihilator if and only if its octonion halves are purely
imaginary, of equal norm and orthogonal. -/

/-- **Normalised zero divisors form the Stiefel manifold `V₂(ℝ⁷)`.** If both octonion halves
of `x = (a, b)` have unit norm, then `x` is a zero divisor iff `(a, b)` is an orthonormal pair
of imaginary octonions. -/

/-- **Exact description of descriptor traps.** The descriptor sedenion
`S_{t,i} = (m_t, m_i, m_t − m_i, m_t ⊙ m_i)` has a nonzero right annihilator iff the
dispersion coordinates of both states vanish, `2 ⟨m_t, m_i⟩ = ‖m_t ⊙ m_i‖²`, and
`⟨m_t, m_t − m_i⟩ + ⟨m_i, m_t ⊙ m_i⟩ = 0`. -/

/-- **The off-center trap family.** For `p ≠ 0` with `p² + q² + r² + 4/p = 2`, the states
`m_t = (0, p, q, r)`, `m_i = (0, 2/p, 0, 0)` give a descriptor trap. (`offcenter_trap₁` and
`offcenter_trap₂` are the members `(p,q,r) = (−2,0,0)` and `(−1,1,2)`.) -/

# Convergence of repeated certified shrinking passes

`Sovereign/Meta/CertifiedUpgrade.lean` shows that meaning-preserving, non-increasing passes
compose into certified upgrades.  Here we show that *iterating* such a pass terminates in a
normal form.

* `StrictlyShrinking r cost P`: every application of `P` either leaves its input unchanged
  or strictly decreases `cost` for the relation `r` on costs.
* `iterate_stabilizes`: if `r` is well-founded, then for every input `T` there is `N` with
  `P^[m] T = P^[N] T` for all `m ≥ N`, and `P^[N] T` is irreducible (`P` fixes it).
* `iterate_stabilizes_nat`: for costs in `ℕ` the bound is explicit: `N = cost T` works.
* `not_converges_of_shrinking_only`: the strictness hypothesis cannot be dropped.  A pass
  whose cost never increases but is not strictly shrinking may oscillate forever.
* `Pass.normalForm_*`: for the engine's obligation passes, the normal form proves exactly
  the same goals as the input (`Preserving`) and costs no more (`Shrinking`).
-/

/-- A pass `P` is *strictly shrinking* for the cost `cost : α → β` and the relation `r` on
costs if every application either leaves its input unchanged or strictly decreases the cost. -/
/-- `x` is irreducible for `P` (a normal form): `P` leaves it unchanged. -/
/-- Once an irreducible point is reached, further iteration stays there. -/
/-- Some iterate of a strictly shrinking pass with a well-founded cost is irreducible. -/
/-- If `P^[N] T` is irreducible, the orbit is constant from step `N` on. -/

/-- **Convergence of repeated certified shrinking passes.**  For any well-founded order on
costs, iterating a strictly shrinking pass `P` from any input `T` reaches, after finitely many
steps, an irreducible normal form at which the orbit stays:
`∃ N, (∀ m ≥ N, P^[m] T = P^[N] T) ∧ P (P^[N] T) = P^[N] T`. -/
/-- The same statement for a cost with values in any well-founded order `<`. -/

/-- Along the orbit of a strictly shrinking pass with natural-number cost, each non-fixed step
drops the cost by at least one. -/

/-- **Explicit bound for natural-number costs**: the orbit is constant from step `cost T`
on, and `P^[cost T] T` is irreducible. -/

/-- Non-increasing cost alone does not give convergence: on `Bool` with constant cost,
`not` never increases the cost, yet its orbit oscillates forever. -/
/-- The limit of a convergent orbit. -/
/-- Every property preserved by one pass holds of the normal form. -/
/-! ## Obligation passes of the skeleton engine -/

/-- A pass on proof obligations is *strictly shrinking* when every application that changes
the obligation list strictly lowers its total cost. -/

/-- **Repeated compression terminates.**  Iterating a strictly shrinking obligation pass from any
list `l` is constant from step `cost l` on, at an irreducible list. -/
/-- A strictly shrinking pass never raises the cost. -/

/-- **The limit is faithful and no costlier.**  If a strictly shrinking pass also preserves
meaning, every iterate — in particular the irreducible normal form reached after `cost l`
steps — proves exactly the same goals as `l` and costs no more than `l`. -/

/-- **Repeated certified compression terminates at a faithful irreducible normal form.**
For a meaning-preserving, strictly shrinking pass, the obligation list `nf = p^[cost l] l`
is fixed by all further passes, is irreducible, proves the same goals as `l`, and costs no
more. -/

/-- Running any certified shrinking pass on an engine's output a goal-dependent number of times
(for instance `cost (e φ)` times, which reaches the normal form of a strictly shrinking pass) is a
certified upgrade of the engine. -/
/-! Axiom checks for the upgrade engine development. -/

/-!
# The automated fallback recovery state machine

The upgrade engine runs as a state machine. A state records
* the `active` engine and the `ledger` of verified benchmarks,
* a `checkpoint`: the last known-good engine together with its ledger,
* a `phase` (`stable`, `probation`, `rollback`, `quarantined`) and a count of consecutive
  `failures`.

Two invariants are *fields* of the state, so they hold in every state by construction:
* `ledger_ok`: the active engine refutes every ledger benchmark (no regression, ever);
* `power_ok`: the active engine refutes everything the checkpoint engine refutes.

Events:
* `propose E' gen`: (only in `stable`) the proposer's certificate generator `gen` is run on the
  current ledger and engine. If it produces an `UpgradeCertificate`, the current state is
  checkpointed and `E'` becomes active in `probation`. Otherwise the upgrade *fails*: the state
  is checkpointed, the engine is left untouched, and the machine enters `rollback`.
* `record φ`: (only in `stable`) a formula refuted by the active engine joins the ledger.
* `healthPass` / `healthFail`: the outcome of the post-admission health check in `probation`.
  Passing commits the new engine as checkpoint; failing enters `rollback`.
* `recover`: (only in `rollback`) restore the checkpoint engine and ledger; go back to `stable`,
  or to `quarantined` once `maxRetries` consecutive failures have accumulated.
* `operatorReset`: (only in `quarantined`) manual release back to `stable`.

Main results (for states reachable from an initial engine):
* `Reachable.good`: the reachable-state invariants;
* `propose_admitted_iff`, `exists_gen_admitted_iff`: the machine admits `E → E'` iff a
  certificate is produced, iff the transition is admissible;
* `step_active_cases`: the active engine changes only through a certified admissible upgrade or a
  rollback to the checkpoint;
* `run_ledger_mono`, `run_checkpoint_powerLE`, `run_no_regression`: along every execution the
  ledger only grows, the committed engine's refutation power only grows, and no verified
  benchmark is ever lost;
* `failed_upgrade_recovers`, `probation_fail_recovers`, `autoRecover_settles`: automated
  recovery from failed upgrades returns, in at most two events, to a stable or quarantined state
  running the last known-good engine;
* `quarantined_absorbing`, `Reachable.failures_le`: quarantine only exits by operator reset, and
  the failure counter never exceeds `maxRetries`.
-/

/-- A certificate generator for a proposed engine `E'`: given the current ledger and engine it may
produce a certificate for the transition. -/
/-- A known-good checkpoint: an engine with a ledger it verifies. -/
/-- Phases of the recovery state machine. -/
/-- States of the recovery state machine. -/
/-- No regression: the active engine refutes every ledger benchmark. -/
/-- The active engine is at least as strong as the checkpoint engine. -/
/-- Events of the recovery state machine. -/
/-- The current state as a checkpoint. -/
/-- The initial state for an engine `E`: empty ledger, stable, checkpointed. -/
/-- The transition function of the recovery state machine. -/
/-- Run a list of events. -/
/-! ### Invariants -/
/-- The invariants of reachable states. -/
/-- In `stable` and `quarantined`, the active engine is the checkpoint engine. -/
/-- Outside `stable`, the ledger is the checkpoint ledger (nothing is recorded meanwhile). -/
/-- The checkpoint ledger is contained in the ledger. -/
/-- While `stable` or in `probation`, fewer than `maxRetries` consecutive failures occurred. -/
/-- The failure counter never exceeds `maxRetries`. -/
/-- At least one attempt is allowed. -/
/-- States reachable from the initial state of the engine `E₀`. -/
/-- In every reachable state the failure counter is bounded by `maxRetries`. -/
/-! ### Admission -/

/-- **Machine-level admission.** From a stable state, the machine admits the proposed engine
(enters `probation` with `E'` active) exactly when the proposer produces a certificate. -/
/-- When the machine admits a proposal, the new active engine is the proposed one. -/

/-- **Admission theorem for the machine.** From a stable state, some proposal of `E'` is admitted
iff the transition `σ.active → E'` is admissible, iff a constructive certificate exists. -/
/-- An admitted proposal is an admissible transition. -/

/-- **The active engine only changes in controlled ways**: it is unchanged, or it is the proposed
engine of an admissible (certified) transition, or it is the checkpoint engine restored by a
rollback. -/
/-! ### Monotonicity along executions -/
/-- The committed (checkpoint) engine's refutation power never decreases. -/
/-- The ledger of verified benchmarks never shrinks. -/

/-- **No regression, ever.** A benchmark verified at some point of an execution is refuted by the
active engine at every later point, whatever upgrades, failures and rollbacks happen. -/

/-- In stable and quarantined states the active engine's power dominates every earlier committed
engine. -/
/-! ### Automated fallback recovery -/

/-- **A failed upgrade falls back.** If the proposer produces no certificate, the proposal is
rejected and one `recover` step restores the original engine and ledger; the machine returns to
`stable`, or to `quarantined` once `maxRetries` consecutive failures have accumulated. -/

/-- **A failed health check falls back.** From `probation`, a failed health check followed by
`recover` restores the last known-good engine and keeps the ledger. -/
/-- A successful health check commits the new engine as the checkpoint. -/

/-- The automatic recovery plan for a phase: fail the pending probation and recover, or just
recover, or do nothing. -/
/-- Automated recovery: run the recovery plan of the current phase. -/

/-!
# Self-improving engine upgrades

An `Improver` lets the engine propose its own successor: from the active engine `E` it produces a
candidate `next E`, a certificate generator for the transition `E → next E`, and a health check.
One `round` of self-improvement runs, on the recovery state machine of
`Sovereign.Meta.UpgradeEngine.Fallback`, the events

  `propose (next E) (gen E)`, then `healthPass` or `healthFail`, then `recover`.

If the certificate is missing the proposal is rejected and `recover` falls back to the current
engine; if the health check fails the new engine is rolled back; otherwise the new engine is
committed. `selfImprove` iterates rounds.

Main results, starting from `RState.init E₀` with `0 < maxRetries`:
* `round_success`, `round_rejected`, `round_unhealthy`: the three outcomes of a round;
* `selfImprove_settled`: after every round the machine is `stable` or `quarantined`;
* `selfImprove_powerLE`: the refutation power of the active engine is monotone in the round number;
* `selfImprove_no_regression`: a benchmark verified at round `n` stays refuted at every later round;
* `selfImprove_active_cases`: after each round the active engine is the previous one, or an
  admissible (certified) successor of it.

Finally `lraStrictCertificate` and `lra_selfImprove_example` instantiate the framework with the
Fourier–Motzkin/Farkas upgrade of the propositional skeleton engine: that transition has a strict
certificate, and the machine admits and commits it.
-/
/-- A self-improvement strategy: successor proposal, certificate generation, health check. -/
/-- The successor engine proposed by the engine `E`. -/
/-- The certificate generator for the transition `E → next E`. -/
/-- The post-admission health check. -/
/-- The events of one self-improvement round from the state `σ`. -/
/-- One self-improvement round. -/
/-- Iterated self-improvement. -/
/-- A settled phase: `stable` or `quarantined`. -/
/-- **Successful round**: a certified and healthy successor is committed. -/
/-- **Rejected round**: without a certificate the engine is unchanged (automatic fallback). -/
/-- **Unhealthy round**: a certified successor failing its health check is rolled back. -/
/-- A round from a quarantined state does nothing. -/
/-- Later states of self-improvement are obtained by running events from earlier ones. -/

/-- **Monotone refutation power under self-improvement.** From a good settled state, the active
engine after round `n'` refutes everything the active engine after round `n ≤ n'` refutes. -/

/-- **No regression under self-improvement.** A benchmark verified at round `n` is refuted by the
active engine at every later round. -/
/-- After each round the active engine is either unchanged or an admissible successor. -/
/-- Initial states are good and settled. -/
/-! ### Instance: the Fourier–Motzkin / Farkas upgrade of the propositional skeleton -/

/-- The transition from the propositional skeleton engine to the Farkas-certified linear
arithmetic engine carries a strict certificate: it is monotone, and it refutes
`x₀ ≤ 0 ∧ ¬(x₀ ≤ 1)`, which the skeleton does not. -/

/-- The certificate generator that offers `lraStrictCertificate` when asked about the initial
ledger and the skeleton engine (and uses `UpgradeCertificate.ofCertifiedMonotoneUpgrade` for any
ledger verified by the skeleton). -/

/-- **Worked run.** Starting from the skeleton engine, proposing the linear-arithmetic engine and
passing the health check commits it; the resulting engine is strictly more powerful. -/

/-!
# The upgrade engine: admissible engine transitions and their certificates

An *engine* is a sound refuter (`SoundRefuter Sat`): a Boolean procedure on formulas such that
every refuted formula has no model. An engine transition `E → E'` is judged against a *ledger*
`B : List Φ` of previously verified benchmarks (formulas that have already been refuted).

The transition is **admissible** (`Admissible B E E'`) when
* **no regression**: `E'` still refutes every benchmark of the ledger, and
* **monotone refutation power**: `E'` refutes every formula that `E` refutes.

It is **strictly admissible** when in addition `E'` refutes some formula that `E` does not.

An `UpgradeCertificate B E E'` is the constructive Lean certificate for a transition: a
kernel-checkable Boolean benchmark report (`benchmarkCheck B E' = true`, typically closed by
`decide`/`rfl`) together with a *lifting* proof transporting every refutation of `E` to one of `E'`.
A `StrictUpgradeCertificate` additionally carries an explicit witness formula (data).

Main results:
* `admissible_iff_nonempty_certificate`: admissible iff a certificate exists;
* `strictlyAdmissible_iff_nonempty_strictCertificate`: the strict analogue;
* `UpgradeCertificate.trans`: certificates compose along chains of upgrades;
* `UpgradeCertificate.ofCertifiedMonotoneUpgrade`: every `CertifiedMonotoneUpgrade` yields one;
* `certify?`: for a finite formula universe, a computable certificate search which succeeds
  exactly on admissible transitions (`certify?_isSome_iff`).
-/
/-- An engine is a sound refuter. -/
/-- Refutation power is monotone from `E` to `E'`: whatever `E` refutes, `E'` refutes. -/
/-- Strict increase of refutation power. -/
/-- `E'` has no regression on the ledger `B`: it refutes every benchmark in `B`. -/
/-- The admission criterion for an engine transition `E → E'` against the ledger `B`. -/
/-- The strict admission criterion: admissible with a strict gain of refutation power. -/
/-- The computable benchmark report: does `E'` refute every ledger benchmark? -/
/-- A constructive certificate for the engine transition `E → E'` against the ledger `B`. -/
/-- Kernel-checkable benchmark report: no regression on the ledger. -/
/-- Lifting of refutations: monotonicity of refutation power. -/

/-- A constructive certificate for a strict improvement `E → E'`: an upgrade certificate plus an
explicit formula refuted by `E'` but not by `E`. -/
/-- A formula witnessing the strict gain. -/
/-- A ledger with no regression for `E` stays free of regressions along a power increase. -/
/-- Build the certificate from a proof of admissibility. -/
/-- The identity transition is certified whenever the ledger has no regression. -/
/-- Certificates compose along a chain of upgrades. -/

/-- Every certified monotone upgrade of an engine that has verified the ledger `B` is a certified
transition. -/
/-- Build a strict certificate from a proof of admissibility and an explicit witness. -/

/-- **Admission theorem.** An engine transition `E → E'` is admitted (no regression on the ledger
and monotone refutation power) if and only if there is a constructive upgrade certificate. -/

/-- **Strict admission theorem.** A transition is strictly admitted (no regression and strictly
increasing refutation power) iff there is a strict certificate carrying an explicit witness. -/
/-- On a ledger already verified by `E`, admission reduces to monotonicity of power. -/
/-! ### Computable certificate search over a finite formula universe -/
/-- Computable certificate search: returns a certificate exactly for admissible transitions. -/

comments.text:
/-!
# 3D acoustic metamaterial lattices with sub-wavelength resonant inclusions

We model a macroscopic acoustic metamaterial: a simple cubic lattice (lattice constant `ℓ`)
whose unit cell carries two sub-wavelength resonant inclusions (e.g. Minnaert bubbles or
Helmholtz resonators) of common resonance frequency `ω₀`. Near `ω₀` the acoustic field is
described by the two resonator amplitudes per cell (the standard coupled-resonator /
tight-binding description of locally resonant metamaterials); neighbouring resonators are
coupled through the evanescent near field. The coupled-resonator description is the modelling
assumption of this file; its derivation from the Helmholtz equation (e.g. by capacitance-matrix
asymptotics) is not formalised.

* `AcousticMetamaterial`: lattice constant, host sound speed, inclusion, coupling, mass
  (detuning) term `m` and interlayer coupling `t_z`, with the sub-wavelength conditions
  `ω₀ a < c` (inclusion) and `ω₀ ℓ < π c` (lattice below the Bragg regime).
* `latticeHam`: the real-space coupled-resonator operator on `ℤ³ × {A, B}` with
  nearest-neighbour couplings `T₁ = (σ_z - iσ_x)/2`, `T₂ = (σ_z - iσ_y)/2`, `T₃ = (t_z/2) σ_z`.
* `latticeHam_bloch` (**Bloch theorem**): Bloch waves `e^{ik·R} u` are mapped to
  `e^{ik·R} H(k) u` with the Bloch Hamiltonian `H(k) = d(k)·σ`,
  `d(k) = (sin k₁, sin k₂, m + cos k₁ + cos k₂ + t_z cos k₃)`.
* `exists_eigenvector_iff`: the two acoustic bands are `±|d(k)|`;
  `dynMatrix_eigen_iff`: the eigenfrequencies are `Ω² = ω₀² ± g |d(k)|`.
* `bulkGap_le_dnorm`, `exists_dnorm_eq_bulkGap`: the exact band gap of every `k₃`-slice with
  mass `μ` is `Δ(μ) = min (|μ|) (abs (2 - |μ|))`; `gap_closes_iff`: the gap closes only for
  `μ ∈ {-2, 0, 2}`.
* `bulkGap_sub_le_dnorm_d3`, `AcousticMetamaterial.complete_band_gap`: for `|t_z| < Δ(m)` the
  3D lattice has a complete acoustic band gap around `ω₀²`.
-/
/-! ## The metamaterial -/
/-- A sub-wavelength resonant inclusion of radius `radius` and resonance frequency `omega0`. -/

/-- The Minnaert resonance frequency `ω₀ = √(3 γ P₀ / ρ) / a` of a gas bubble of radius `a`
(polytropic index `γ`, ambient pressure `P₀`, liquid density `ρ`). -/

/-- A Minnaert bubble is sub-wavelength (`ω₀ a < c`) iff `√(3γP₀/ρ) < c`, independently of
its radius. -/

/-- A 3D acoustic metamaterial: a simple cubic lattice of lattice constant `ℓ` in a host fluid
of sound speed `c`, with two resonant inclusions per unit cell. The couplings are measured in
units of `coupling` (dimension frequency²). -/
/-- lattice constant -/
/-- sound speed of the host fluid -/
/-- the resonant inclusions -/
/-- nearest-neighbour evanescent coupling strength (frequency²) -/
/-- dimensionless mass (on-site detuning) term -/
/-- dimensionless interlayer coupling along the stacking direction -/
/-- two inclusions fit into the unit cell -/
/-- the inclusions are sub-wavelength: `k₀ a < 1` -/
/-- the lattice is sub-wavelength (below the first Bragg frequency): `ℓ < λ₀ / 2` -/
/-- The first Bragg frequency `ω_B = π c / ℓ` of the lattice. -/

/-- The resonance lies below the Bragg frequency, so the band gap is of local-resonance
(hybridisation) origin, not a Bragg gap. -/
/-- The inclusion radius is below `1/k₀ = c/ω₀`. -/
/-! ## The real-space lattice and the Bloch theorem -/
/-- Unit cells of the cubic lattice. -/
/-- Acoustic fields: two resonator amplitudes per unit cell. -/
/-- The primitive translation along axis `i`. -/
/-- Nearest-neighbour coupling matrices (in units of the coupling) along `+eᵢ`. -/

/-- The real-space coupled-resonator operator: on-site mass `m σ_z`, coupling `Tᵢ` to the
neighbour at `R + eᵢ` and `Tᵢ†` to the neighbour at `R - eᵢ`. -/
/-- The Bloch phase `e^{i k·R}`. -/
/-- The Bloch Hamiltonian `d·σ` of a vector `d ∈ ℝ³`. -/

/-- The Bloch vector of a `k₃`-slice with mass `μ`:
`d(k₁, k₂) = (sin k₁, sin k₂, μ + cos k₁ + cos k₂)`. -/
/-- The effective mass of the `k₃`-slice: `m + t_z cos k₃`. -/
/-- The 3D Bloch vector `d(k) = (sin k₁, sin k₂, m + cos k₁ + cos k₂ + t_z cos k₃)`. -/
/-- The Fourier transform of the coupling table is the Bloch Hamiltonian `d(k)·σ`. -/

/-- **Bloch theorem** for the metamaterial lattice: a Bloch wave `ψ(R) = e^{ik·R} u` is mapped
by the real-space operator to `e^{ik·R} H(k) u` with `H(k) = d(k)·σ`. -/
/-! ## The acoustic bands -/
/-- The **acoustic band structure**: `e` is an eigenvalue of `d·σ` iff `e = ±|d|`. -/

/-- The dynamical matrix `D(k) = ω₀² + g H(k)` of the metamaterial; its eigenvalues are the
squared eigenfrequencies. -/

/-- The eigenfrequencies of the metamaterial: `Ω²` is an eigenvalue of `D(k)` iff
`Ω² = ω₀² ± g |d(k)|`. -/
/-! ## The band gap -/
/-- The band gap of a slice with mass `μ`: `Δ(μ) = min (|μ|) (abs (2 - |μ|))`. -/
/-- The band gap bounds `|d|²` from below everywhere in the Brillouin zone. -/
/-- No bulk state lies inside the gap: `Δ(μ) ≤ |d(k)|` for every `k`. -/
/-- The gap is exact: `Δ(μ)` is attained. -/
/-- The **gap closes** only at `μ ∈ {-2, 0, 2}` (topological phase transitions). -/
/-- The gap is `1`-Lipschitz in the mass. -/
/-- In 3D, the slice at `k₃` has mass `m + t_z cos k₃`, so its gap is at least `Δ(m) - |t_z|`. -/

/-- **Complete acoustic band gap** of the 3D metamaterial: if `|t_z| < Δ(m)`, then no bulk
eigenfrequency `Ω²` (at any Bloch vector `k ∈ ℝ³`) lies strictly between
`ω₀² - g (Δ(m) - |t_z|)` and `ω₀² + g (Δ(m) - |t_z|)`. -/

/-!
# Chern numbers of the acoustic bands

For a two-band Bloch Hamiltonian `H(k) = d(k)·σ` on the 2D Brillouin torus, the Chern number is
the wrapping number (Brouwer degree) of the Bloch-sphere map `k ↦ d(k)/|d(k)|`. We compute it at
the regular value `+ẑ` (the north pole):

  `C[d] = ∑_{k ∈ BZ, d₁(k) = d₂(k) = 0, d₃(k) > 0} sign det ∂(d₁, d₂)/∂(k₁, k₂)`   (`chernNumber`).

This is the signed count of the zeros of the section `k ↦ P₋(k) e₁` of the lower-band line
bundle (`lowerProjector_mulVec_e₁_eq_zero_iff`), i.e. of the obstruction to a global smooth
Bloch gauge. (This is the orientation convention `C = (1/4π) ∫ d̂·(∂₁d̂ × ∂₂d̂)`; the lower band
has Berry-curvature Chern number `-C` in the convention `A = i⟨u|∇u⟩`. The identification of the
signed zero count with the Berry-curvature integral — the Poincaré–Hopf/degree theorem — is not
formalised here; `chernNumber` is the definition used.)

* `chernNumber_deformedModel`: closed formula for every model `d = (a sin k₁, b sin k₂, d₃(k))`.
* `chernNumber_qwz_of_pos`, `chernNumber_qwz_of_neg`, `chernNumber_qwz_of_two_lt`: the phase
  diagram `C = -1` for `0 < μ < 2`, `C = +1` for `-2 < μ < 0`, `C = 0` for `|μ| > 2`;
  `chernNumber_qwz_ne_zero_iff`: in a gapped phase, `C ≠ 0 ↔ |μ| < 2`.
* `chernNumber_stable`: **robustness against structural lattice defects** — any (translation
  invariant) deformation of the in-plane couplings `a, b > 0` and any perturbation `δ(k)` of the
  mass term with `|δ| < Δ(μ)` leave the Chern number unchanged.
* `sliceChern_eq`, `AcousticMetamaterial.chern_ne_zero`: the 3D metamaterial with
  `0 < |m| < 2`, `|t_z| < Δ(m)` has the same non-zero Chern number `C = -sign m` on every
  `k₃`-slice (Chern vector `(0, 0, C)`).
-/
/-! ## The Chern number of a two-band model -/

/-- A two-band Bloch Hamiltonian on the 2D Brillouin torus, given by its Bloch vector
`d(k₁, k₂) ∈ ℝ³`. -/
/-- The Brillouin zone `[0, 2π)²`. -/
/-- The Jacobian `det ∂(d₁, d₂)/∂(k₁, k₂)` of the in-plane part of the Bloch vector. -/
/-- The preimages of the north pole `d̂ = +ẑ` in the Brillouin zone. -/

/-- The **Chern number** of the two-band model: the degree of `d̂ : T² → S²`, computed as the
signed count of the preimages of the north pole. -/
/-! ## The lower-band projector and the gauge obstruction -/
/-- The spectral projector onto the lower band, `P₋ = (1 - d̂·σ)/2`. -/
/-- `P₋` projects onto the lower band: `(d·σ) P₋ = -|d| P₋`. -/
/-- `P₋` is idempotent. -/

/-- **Gauge obstruction.** The section `k ↦ P₋(k) e₁` of the lower-band bundle vanishes exactly
where `d̂ = +ẑ`, i.e. at the points counted by `chernNumber`. -/
/-! ## Deformed Qi–Wu–Zhang-type acoustic models -/

/-- Acoustic two-band models with in-plane couplings `a, b` and an arbitrary mass term:
`d(k) = (a sin k₁, b sin k₂, d₃(k))`. -/
/-- The four time-reversal-invariant momenta. -/

/-- Closed formula for the Chern number of `d = (a sin k₁, b sin k₂, d₃)`: only the signs of the
mass term at the four time-reversal-invariant momenta matter. -/
/-! ## The phase diagram -/
/-- `C = 0` in the trivial phases `|μ| > 2`. -/

/-- In a gapped phase, the acoustic bands are **topologically non-trivial** (`C ≠ 0`) iff
`|μ| < 2`. -/
/-- The Chern number in the topological phases is `-sign μ`. -/
/-! ## Robustness against structural lattice defects -/

/-- **Topological protection of the Chern number.** Deform the metamaterial by any structural
change that keeps the lattice periodic: rescale the in-plane couplings by `a, b > 0` and perturb
the mass term by any `δ(k)` smaller than the band gap. The Chern number does not change. -/
/-! ## The 3D metamaterial -/
/-- The Chern number of the `k₃`-slice of the 3D lattice. -/
/-- If `|t_z| < Δ(m)`, every `k₃`-slice has the same Chern number as the `t_z = 0` layer. -/

/-- **The 3D acoustic metamaterial is a topological (Chern) insulator.** If `0 < |m| < 2` and
`|t_z| < Δ(m)`, then the bulk has a complete band gap and every `k₃`-slice of the acoustic band
structure carries the same non-zero Chern number `C = -sign m`. -/

/-!
# Gapless chiral acoustic edge (surface) modes and immunity to backscattering

We cut the 3D metamaterial along the plane `R₂ = 0` (the second lattice direction) and keep the
half-space `R₂ ≤ 0` (open, hard-wall boundary: the resonators beyond the surface are absent).
The surface is translation invariant along `e₁` and `e₃`, with conserved Bloch momenta `k₁` and
`k₃`.

* `surfaceMode m t_z k₁ k₃`: the explicit surface state
  `Ψ(R) = e^{i(k₁R₁ + k₃R₃)} (-M)^{-R₂} (1, 1)` for `R₂ ≤ 0` (and `0` outside the material),
  where `M = m + t_z cos k₃ + cos k₁`.
* `surfaceMode_eigen`: `Ψ` is an **exact eigenstate** of the real-space coupled-resonator
  operator `latticeHam` at every site of the half-space, with energy `E = sin k₁`;
  `summable_edgeProfile`: it is square-summable (localised at the surface) iff `|M| < 1`.
* `edge_gapless`: in a topological phase every energy of the bulk gap is carried by a surface
  mode (**gapless edge modes**); `not_isEdgeMomentum_of_two_le`: in the trivial phases there is
  none (bulk–edge correspondence).
* `edge_chirality`: the group velocity `∂E/∂k₁ = cos k₁` of every in-gap surface mode has the
  sign of the Chern number: the surface modes are **chiral** (one-way).
* `edge_momentum_unique`, `no_backscattering`: at every energy in the gap there is exactly one
  surface channel (up to `2π`) and no counter-propagating one, so an elastic
  (energy-conserving) defect has no state to backscatter into.
* `edge_robust`: surface modes survive any mass defect `μ ↦ μ'` with `|μ' - μ| < Δ(μ) - |E|`
  with the same chirality (**immunity to structural lattice defects**).
* `AcousticMetamaterial.topological_surface_modes`: the 3D statement.
-/
/-! ## The surface state -/

/-- The profile of the surface state across the surface: `(-M)^{-n} (1, 1)` inside the material
(`n ≤ 0`), `0` outside. -/
/-- The effective decay parameter `M = m + t_z cos k₃ + cos k₁` of the surface state. -/
/-- The explicit surface state of the half-space metamaterial `R₂ ≤ 0`. -/

/-- **The surface mode is an exact eigenstate** of the real-space metamaterial operator at every
site of the half-space `R₂ ≤ 0`, with energy `E = sin k₁`. -/
/-- The surface state vanishes outside the material. -/

/-- The surface state decays exponentially into the bulk and is square-summable across the
surface when `|M| < 1`. -/
/-- The surface profile is non-trivial. -/
/-! ## Edge branch: gaplessness, chirality, uniqueness -/

/-- `k₁` carries a localised surface mode of the slice with mass `μ`: `|μ + cos k₁| < 1`.
Its energy is `sin k₁`. -/
/-- The group velocity of the surface mode: `∂(sin k₁)/∂k₁ = cos k₁`. -/
/-- In the trivial phases `|μ| ≥ 2` there is no surface mode. -/

/-- **Gapless edge modes.** In a topological phase (`0 < |μ| < 2`), every energy `E` inside the
bulk gap `|E| < Δ(μ)` is the energy of a localised surface mode. -/

/-- **Chirality = Chern number** (bulk–edge correspondence). Every surface mode with energy in
the bulk gap propagates with group velocity `cos k₁` of sign equal to the Chern number. -/

/-- **Uniqueness of the surface channel.** Two surface modes with the same energy in the bulk
gap have the same Bloch momentum modulo `2π`. -/

/-- **No backscattering.** At an energy inside the bulk gap there is no pair of surface modes
propagating in opposite directions: all surface modes move in the same direction. Together with
the absence of bulk states in the gap (`bulkGap_le_dnorm`), an elastic (energy-conserving)
defect has no counter-propagating state to scatter into. -/

/-- **Immunity to structural defects.** A defect that shifts the mass term `μ ↦ μ'` by less
than `Δ(μ) - |E|` preserves the Chern number, and the surface mode at energy `E` survives with
the same chirality. -/
/-! ## The 3D metamaterial -/

/-- **Topological surface modes of the 3D acoustic metamaterial.** Let `0 < |m| < 2` and
`|t_z| < Δ(m)`. For every `k₃` and every energy `E` with `|E| < Δ(m) - |t_z|` (i.e. frequency
`Ω² = ω₀² + g E` inside the complete bulk gap), there is `k₁` such that the surface state
`surfaceMode` of the half-space `R₂ ≤ 0` is an exact eigenstate with energy `E`, it is
square-summable across the surface, and it propagates along `e₁` with velocity of sign
`C = -sign m ≠ 0`. -/

/-!
# Non-reciprocal acoustic metamaterial lattices: 1D and 2D skin effect

Acoustic realisation of the non-Hermitian skin effect: the resonator lattice of an
`AcousticMetamaterial` whose nearest-neighbour couplings are made direction dependent
(`NonReciprocalAcousticLattice`). The squared eigenfrequencies are the eigenvalues of the
dynamical matrix `D = ω₀² + g H` (as in `dynMatrix`), with `H` the non-reciprocal hopping matrix.
That active couplings realize these non-reciprocal hoppings is a modelling assumption.

**2D lattice** `hn2D Nx Ny = H_x ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ H_y` (Hatano–Nelson chains along `x` and `y`):
* `hn2D_product_eigen`, `hn2DMode_eigen`: product modes with energy `E^x_m + E^y_n`;
* `hn2DMode_linearIndependent`: the `N_x N_y` modes are linearly independent (a complete basis);
* `hn2D_corner_skin`: product eigenstates are exponentially localized at a corner,
  `|ψ(i,j)| r_x^{N_x-i} r_y^{N_y-j} ≤ (i+1)(j+1) |ψ(N_x,N_y)|`;
* `gbz2D`, `gbz2D_disjoint_bz2D`: the 2D GBZ torus `|β_x| = r_x`, `|β_y| = r_y` is disjoint from
  the Brillouin torus as soon as one direction is non-reciprocal; `hn2D_energy_on_gbz2D`.

**Acoustic spectra**: `dyn1D_spectrum` (1D OBC squared frequencies
`ω₀² + 2g√(t_R t_L) cos(mπ/(N+1))`, all real), `dyn1D_skin` (every acoustic eigenmode of the open
chain is a skin mode), `dyn2D_mode_eigen` (2D corner modes).
-/
/-! ## Kronecker-sum lattices -/

/-- The 2D open lattice `H = H_x ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ H_y` on `N_x × N_y` sites, with non-reciprocal
Hatano–Nelson hoppings `(t_R^x, t_L^x)` along `x` and `(t_R^y, t_L^y)` along `y`. -/

/-- Product states `ψ(i, j) = u_i w_j` of 1D eigenvectors are eigenstates of the 2D lattice,
with energy `E_x + E_y`. -/
/-- The explicit 2D OBC eigenmodes `ψ_{m,n}(i, j) = hnMode_m(i) · hnMode_n(j)`. -/
/-- Tensor products of linearly independent families are linearly independent. -/

/-- **Extensive 2D skin effect: a complete basis of skin modes.** The `N_x N_y` product modes
are linearly independent eigenstates of the 2D open lattice. -/

/-- **Corner skin effect.** For product eigenstates of the `(N_x+1) × (N_y+1)` open lattice,
`|ψ(i,j)| ≤ (i+1)(j+1) r_x^{-(N_x-i)} r_y^{-(N_y-j)} |ψ(N_x, N_y)|`: for `t_R^x > t_L^x` and
`t_R^y > t_L^y` every such eigenstate is exponentially localized at the corner `(N_x, N_y)`. -/
/-! ## The two-dimensional generalized Brillouin zone -/
/-- The 2D Brillouin zone (torus `|β_x| = |β_y| = 1`). -/

/-- The 2D generalized Brillouin zone: the torus `|β_x| = √(t_R^x/t_L^x)`,
`|β_y| = √(t_R^y/t_L^y)`. -/

/-- **The 2D GBZ is non-unitary**: as soon as the coupling is non-reciprocal in one direction, the
GBZ is disjoint from the Brillouin torus. -/
/-- Every 2D mode energy lies on the non-Bloch band `h_x(β_x) + h_y(β_y)` over the 2D GBZ. -/
/-! ## Acoustic realisation -/

/-- A non-reciprocal acoustic metamaterial: the resonator lattice of an `AcousticMetamaterial`
whose nearest-neighbour couplings are made direction dependent (e.g. by active, non-reciprocal

/-!
# Gor'kov radiation stress on topological edge states and topological levitation traps

The metamaterial occupies the half-space below the surface `x₁ = 0`; the host fluid fills
`x₁ > 0`. A standing pair of topological surface modes with Bloch momenta `(k₁, ±k₃)` (they are
degenerate: `surfaceStanding_eigen`) leaks an evanescent acoustic field into the fluid,

  `p(x) = A e^{i q x₀} e^{-κ x₁} cos(β x₂)`        (`SurfaceWave.pressure`),

with `q = k₁/ℓ`, `β = k₃/ℓ` and decay rate `κ > 0`. (The matching of the lattice mode to this
continuum tail is the modelling assumption of this file.) A small sphere of radius `a` with
monopole/dipole contrast factors `f₁, f₂` feels the Gor'kov potential
`U = 2π a³ (f₁ ⟨p²⟩/(3 ρ₀ c₀²) - f₂ ρ₀ ⟨v²⟩/2)` (`gorkovContrast`; for `f₁ = f₂ = 1` this is
`Sovereign.Taxonomy.gorkov`, `gorkovContrast_one_one`).

* `SurfaceWave.pressureGrad_eq`: the exact gradient of the surface wave.
* `SurfaceWave.gorkovContrast_eq`: the **Gor'kov potential on the edge state**,
  `U(x) = e^{-2κ x₁} (G₀ + G₁ cos²(β x₂))`.
* `SurfaceWave.acousticStress_shift`: the **radiation stress tensor** (`Projector.acousticStress`)
  of the edge state is invariant along the propagation direction and decays as `e^{-2κ x₁}`.
* `SurfaceWave.levitation_trap`: with gravity (effective weight `w > 0`), if `G₀, G₁ > 0` the
  total potential `V = U + w x₁` attains its global minimum exactly on the lines
  `x₁ = h⋆ = log(2κG₀/w)/(2κ)`, `cos(β x₂) = 0`: a **topological levitation trap** (a one-way
  acoustic conveyor along `x₀`), at positive height iff `2κ G₀ > w`.
* `levitation_trapBarrier`, `levitation_trap_isLocalMin`: the trap carries an energy-barrier
  certificate `Sovereign.Taxonomy.TrapBarrier` in the transverse plane.
* `surfaceMode_eq_of_same_energy`: **immunity to backscattering** — every surface state with the
  same in-gap energy is the *same* lattice state as the trapping mode, so elastic scattering on
  a defect can only reproduce the trapping mode.
* `topological_trap_immune_to_defects`: mass defects smaller than the gap margin keep the
  trapping mode (same chirality, same uniqueness).
* `trap_iff_condensed`: when the surface mode is populated by a phonon condensate
  (`Sovereign.Condensate.OptomechArray`), `|A|² = η n⋆(P)`, the levitation trap exists exactly
  above the condensation threshold `P > P_crit`.
-/
/-! ## Standing surface modes -/

/-- The surface modes `(k₁, k₃)` and `(k₁, -k₃)` are degenerate; their sum, a standing wave
along `e₃`, is an exact eigenstate of the half-space metamaterial. -/
/-! ## The evanescent field of the edge state in the fluid -/

/-- The evanescent acoustic field of a standing pair of surface modes in the fluid above the
metamaterial. -/
/-- complex amplitude -/
/-- wave number along the edge (propagation direction `x₀`) -/
/-- decay rate away from the surface -/
/-- standing-wave number along `x₂` -/
/-- `p(x) = A e^{i q x₀} e^{-κ x₁} cos(β x₂)`. -/
/-- The analytic gradient of the surface wave. -/
/-- **The gradient of the edge-state field.** -/
-- along x₀
-- along x₁
-- along x₂
/-! ## The Gor'kov potential with contrast factors -/

/-- The **Gor'kov potential** of a small sphere of radius `a` with monopole and dipole contrast
factors `f₁ = 1 - κ_p/κ₀`, `f₂ = 2(ρ_p - ρ₀)/(2ρ_p + ρ₀)`:
`U = 2π a³ (f₁ ⟨p²⟩/(3 ρ₀ c₀²) - f₂ ρ₀ ⟨v²⟩/2)`. -/
/-- For `f₁ = f₂ = 1` this is the Gor'kov potential `Sovereign.Taxonomy.gorkov`. -/
/-- The coefficient `G₀` of the Gor'kov potential of the edge state (value at the nodes). -/
/-- The coefficient `G₁` of `cos²(β x₂)` in the Gor'kov potential of the edge state. -/

/-- **The Gor'kov potential on the topological edge state**:
`U(x) = e^{-2κ x₁} (G₀ + G₁ cos²(β x₂))`. -/

/-- `G₀ > 0` exactly for particles lighter than the fluid (`f₂ < 0`) in a standing surface
wave (`β ≠ 0`) of non-zero amplitude. -/
/-! ## The radiation stress tensor of the edge state -/

/-- **The Gor'kov/Brillouin radiation stress tensor on the edge state** is uniform along the
propagation direction `x₀` and decays as `e^{-2κ t}` away from the surface:
`Π(x + s e₀ + t e₁) = e^{-2κ t} Π(x)`. -/
/-! ## The topological levitation trap -/

/-- The total potential energy of the particle: Gor'kov potential of the edge state plus the
effective weight `w` (gravity minus buoyancy), which pulls towards the surface `x₁ = 0`. -/
/-- The levitation height `h⋆ = log(2κG₀/w)/(2κ)`. -/

/-- **Topological levitation trap.** If `G₀ > 0` and `G₁ > 0`, the total potential of the
particle attains its global minimum exactly at the height `x₁ = h⋆` on the nodal lines
`cos(β x₂) = 0`, for every position `x₀` along the edge: the particle is levitated and
transversely trapped, and is transported freely only along the one-way edge channel. -/
/-- The trap levitates the particle above the surface (`h⋆ > 0`) iff `2κ G₀ > w`. -/
/-! ## A `LevitationCertificate` energy barrier for the topological trap -/
/-- The transverse potential in the `(x₁, x₂)` plane. -/
/-- The trap potential does not depend on the position `x₀` along the edge. -/

/-- **Energy-barrier certificate** (`Sovereign.Taxonomy.TrapBarrier`) for the topological
levitation trap: in the transverse plane, around the trapping point `(h⋆, π/(2β))`, every
radius `0 < r < π/|β|` carries an energy barrier. Hence (`TrapBarrier.exists_isLocalMin`) the
barrier encloses a trap. -/
/-- The barrier encloses a trap: a local minimum of the transverse potential inside the ball. -/
/-! ## Immunity of the trap to backscattering and to lattice defects -/

/-- **Immunity to backscattering.** Every surface state of the metamaterial with the same energy
in the bulk gap as the trapping mode is *identical* to the trapping mode (as a lattice field).
An elastic, energy-conserving defect therefore cannot scatter the trapping mode into a
different (e.g. counter-propagating) channel: the acoustic field of the trap is unchanged. -/

/-- **Topological levitation traps are immune to structural lattice defects.** Let the trap be
driven at an energy `E` inside the bulk gap of the slice `μ` (the frequency of the trapping
field). Any defect that shifts the mass term to `μ'` with `|μ' - μ| < Δ(μ) - |E|` keeps the
Chern number, and the defected lattice still carries a surface mode at the same energy `E` with
the same chirality; moreover this mode is unique (every surface mode of energy `E` is the same
lattice state), so there is no backscattering channel. -/
/-! ## Macroscopic quantum occupation: the trap switches on at condensation -/

/-- **Condensate-driven levitation.** Suppose the standing surface mode is populated by the
phonon condensate of an optomechanical array `C` (`Sovereign.Condensate.OptomechArray`), so that
its squared pressure amplitude is `|A|² = η n⋆(P)` (`η > 0`: pressure² per phonon). For a
particle lighter than the fluid (`f₂ < 0`) and a standing wave (`β ≠ 0`), the acoustic
levitation coefficient `G₀` is positive — i.e. the topological trap exists — exactly above the
condensation threshold `P > P_crit`. -/

/-!
# Discrete Shannon entropy and mutual information

Finite-alphabet information theory used to state the "no information loss" property of the
synesthetic encoder.

* `entropy p = ∑ₐ -p a log p a` (natural logarithm, i.e. nats).
* `mutualInfo P = ∑ P(a,b) log (P(a,b) / (P₁(a) P₂(b)))` for a joint law `P` on `α × β`, with
  marginals `marginalFst`, `marginalSnd`.
* `pushJoint p f`: the joint law of `(X, f X)` when `X ∼ p`.
* `channelJoint p q dec`: the joint law of `(X, dec X ξ)` when `X ∼ p` and the noise
  `ξ ∼ q` is independent of `X`.

Main results:
* `mutualInfo_pushJoint_of_injective`: `I(X; f X) = H(X)` for injective `f`.
* `channelJoint_eq_pushJoint`: a noisy channel whose output does not depend on the noise
  realisation (on the support of the noise) has the joint law of a deterministic channel.
* `mutualInfo_le_entropy_fst`: `I(X;Y) ≤ H(X)` for every joint law, so an injective encoder
  attains the largest possible mutual information.
* `entropy_uniform`: the uniform law on `n` symbols has entropy `log n`.
-/
/-- A probability mass function on a finite type. -/
/-- Shannon entropy (in nats) of a mass function. -/
/-- First marginal of a joint law. -/
/-- Second marginal of a joint law. -/
/-- Mutual information (in nats) of a joint law on `α × β`. -/
/-- The joint law of `(X, f X)` when `X` has mass function `p`. -/

/-- The joint law of `(X, dec X ξ)` when `X ∼ p` and the noise `ξ ∼ q` is independent
of `X`. -/
/-- **An injective encoder loses no information:** `I(X; f X) = H(X)`. -/

/-- **Mutual information never exceeds the source entropy:** `I(X;Y) ≤ H(X)` for every joint
law with nonnegative masses. -/

/-- A noisy channel whose decoded output equals `f X` for every noise realisation in the support
of the noise law has the same joint law as the deterministic channel `X ↦ f X`. -/
/-- The uniform law on a nonempty finite alphabet of `n` symbols has entropy `log n`. -/

/-!
# Asymptotic stability of transducer phase locking under continuous phase noise

Each transducer channel is phase-locked to its reference by a first-order loop. Its phase
error `e(t)` obeys the linear locking equation driven by a continuous phase-noise signal `w(t)`:

  `e'(t) = -γ e(t) + w(t)`,  `γ > 0`,  `|w(t)| ≤ ν` for `t ≥ 0`.

* `phaseError_bound` (input-to-state stability):
  `|e t| ≤ e^{-γt} |e 0| + (ν/γ)(1 - e^{-γt})` for all `t ≥ 0`.
* `phaseError_stable`, `phaseError_tendsto_zero`: without noise the locked state is Lyapunov
  stable and globally exponentially attractive, i.e. asymptotically stable.
* `phaseError_eventually_lt`: with noise, every tube `|e| < ν/γ + δ` is entered after a time
  depending only on `γ`, `δ` and a bound `R` on the initial error, and never left again.
-/
/-- **Input-to-state stability of the locking loop.** -/
-- `y = e^{γ s} e(s)` has derivative `e^{γ s} w(s)`; compare with `g = (ν/γ) e^{γ s}`.
-- `y - g` is antitone and `y + g` is monotone on `[0, ∞)`.
-- divide by `e^{γ t}`
/-- Without phase noise the locked state is Lyapunov stable: the error never grows. -/
/-- Without phase noise the phase error converges to zero (global asymptotic stability). -/

/-- **Practical asymptotic stability under continuous phase noise.** For every margin `δ > 0`
and every bound `R` on the initial error there is a settling time `T`, depending only on
`γ, δ, R`, after which the phase error stays in the tube `|e| < ν/γ + δ`. -/

/-!
# Synesthetic holographic transduction: the decoding map `Φ`

A frequency-encoded multi-channel neural field (`WavePacket.lean`) is read out through a phased
opto-acoustic transducer array, sampled at `N + 1` instants per frame and perturbed by phase
noise. The **synesthetic holographic decoding map** `holographicDecode` (`Φ`) sends the sampled
spike-train record `w : Fin C → ℕ → ℂ` to a `TopologicalCertificate`: a vector of integer charges
bundled with the proof that each charge is the discrete winding number of its channel.

Main results.
* `discretePhaseSum_polar`: for samples `r_k e^{iθ_k}` (`r_k > 0`) with phase steps below `π`,
  the discrete phase sum is exactly `θ_N - θ_0`.
* `decode_exact`: if the phase noise is bounded by `ν` and `2π|n_c|/N + 2ν < π`, then `Φ`
  returns exactly the encoded charges, whatever the transducer coefficients, the Riemannian
  metric, the envelopes and the probe positions.
* `certificate_eq_windingNumber`: the decoded charge is the winding number of the continuous
  read-out loop of the channel over the frame — a homotopy invariant of loops in `ℂ \ {0}`.
* `synesthetic_mutualInfo`: for any source law on the alphabet of charges `|n_c| ≤ M` and any
  finite law of bounded phase-noise realisations, the source/decoder pair has
  `I(X; Y) = H(X)` (no information loss), hence `I(X; Y) ≥ I₀` whenever `H(X) ≥ I₀`; for the
  uniform source `I(X; Y) = C log(2M+1)`.
* `synesthetic_asymptotic_stability`: when the phase noise is the residual error of the
  transducer phase-locking loops driven by continuous bounded phase noise, there is a settling
  time after which every frame is decoded exactly and `I(X; Y) = H(X)`.
* `condensateTransducer`, `multiScale_transducer`: a ground state of the two-scale phonon
  condensate array (`Sovereign.Condensate.multiScale`) is a valid, phase-coherent transducer.
* `holoFrame`, `norm_sq_holoFrame`: eight transduced channels form a sedenion holographic frame
  (`Sovereign.Manifold.Sed`) whose squared norm is the total optical power.
-/
/-! ## Exact phase unwrapping -/

/-- Samples of the form `r_k e^{iθ_k}` with `r_k > 0` and phase steps below `π` have discrete
phase sum exactly `θ_N - θ_0`. -/
/-- Rounding is exact for perturbations below `1/2`. -/
/-! ## Topological certificates and the decoding map `Φ` -/

/-- A **verified topological invariant certificate** for a sampled spike-train record `w`: a charge
per channel together with the proof that it is the discrete winding number of that channel. -/
/-- The **synesthetic holographic decoding map** `Φ`. -/
/-- Certificates are unique: the data determine the certified charges. -/

/-- **Exact decoding under phase noise.** If every phase-noise sample is bounded by `ν` and
`2π|n_c|/N + 2ν < π`, the decoded charge of channel `c` is exactly `n_c`. -/
/-- The continuous (noise-free) read-out loop of channel `c` over one frame `[t₀, t₀ + Tf]`. -/
/-- The read-out loop is a constant times the standard loop `e^{2πi n_c s}`. -/
/-- The winding number of the continuous read-out loop of channel `c` is the encoded `n_c`. -/

/-- **The decoded certificate is a topological invariant.** Under the noise margin, the charge
certified by `Φ` equals the winding number of the continuous read-out loop of the channel. -/
/-! ## Symbol alphabet and the end-to-end channel -/
/-- Symbols: `C` channels, each carrying a charge in `{-M, …, M}` (stored as `Fin (2M+1)`). -/
/-- The charge vector of a symbol. -/
/-- Reading a decoded integer charge back as a letter of the alphabet (clamped). -/

/-- The end-to-end synesthetic channel: encode symbol `s`, transduce, sample with phase noise `ξ`,
decode with `Φ` and read back the letters. -/
/-- The end-to-end channel is the identity for all phase noise below the margin. -/

/-- **Mutual information is preserved.** Let the source symbol have law `p₀`, and let the phase
noise be drawn, independently, from a finite family of realisations `noise : Ξ → …` with law `q`,
every realisation of positive probability being bounded by `ν`. Under the margin
`2πA/N + 2ν < π`, the source/decoder joint law has `I(X; Y) = H(X)`: no information is lost,
and `I(X; Y) ≥ I₀` for every target `I₀ ≤ H(X)`. -/
/-- For a uniformly distributed source the transmitted information is `C log(2A+1)` nats. -/
/-! ## Asymptotic stability under continuous phase noise -/

/-- **Asymptotic stability of the synesthetic interface.** The phase of every transducer channel
is held by a locking loop `e_c' = -γ e_c + w_c(t)` driven by continuous phase noise with
`|w_c(t)| ≤ ν`; the phase noise on the samples of a frame starting at `t₀` is the residual locking
error `e_c(t₀ + k Tf/N)`. If `2πA/N + 2ν/γ < π`, there is a settling time `T₀` (depending only on
`γ`, the margin and a bound `R` on the initial errors) such that every frame starting after `T₀`
is decoded exactly, and the source/decoder mutual information equals `H(X)`. -/
/-! ## Condensate reference and holographic frame -/

/-- A transducer array whose coefficients are the amplitudes of a phonon condensate state `b`
at the sites `site c`. -/

/-- **Condensate-referenced transducers.** Above the critical pump every ground state of the
two-scale micro/macro phonon condensate array is nowhere zero, all its amplitudes share one
modulus `√n⋆` and one phase `θ`; hence it defines a phase-coherent transducer array. -/

/-- The sedenion holographic frame of eight complex channel read-outs: real parts in the
first octonion, imaginary parts in the second. -/

/-- The holographic frame is power preserving: its squared norm is the total optical power
of the eight channels. -/
/-- The holographic frame is injective: the eight channels can be read back from it. -/

/-!
# Riemannian neural wave packets and phased opto-acoustic transducers

**Neural field channels.** A cortical patch is described in a chart `ℝᵈ` with a constant
Riemannian metric `G` (a positive definite matrix, `RiemannianChart`); `quad v = vᵀ G v` is the
squared Riemannian length of a displacement. The field potential of one neural channel is a
Gaussian wave packet

  `ψ(t, x) = A · exp(-|x - x₀|²_G / 2) · exp(i (k·x - ω t + φ))`,

continuous in `(t, x)`, with modulus `A e^{-|x-x₀|²_G/2}` (`norm_field`), maximal at the centre
and never zero. A multi-channel neural field is a family `Fin C → WavePacket d`.

**Phased transducers.** A phased opto-acoustic metamaterial transducer array assigns to every
channel a nonzero complex transfer coefficient `τ_c = |τ_c| e^{iα_c}` (gain and programmable
phase). The optical read-out of channel `c` is `τ_c ψ_c(t, p_c)` at the element position `p_c`;
the holographic image is the superposition `∑_c τ_c ψ_c(t, x)`.

**Frequency encoding.** A symbol `n : Fin C → ℤ` is written into the field over a frame of
duration `T_f` by tuning channel `c` to the angular frequency `ω_c = -2π n_c / T_f`, so that the
read-out phase of channel `c` winds exactly `n_c` times during the frame (`encodeFrame`).
The frame is sampled at `N` instants, each sample carrying a phase-noise perturbation `ξ c k`
(`spikeSamples`). `spikeSamples_polar` writes each sample as `r e^{iθ}` with `r > 0` and
`θ = θ₀ + 2π n_c k / N + ξ c k`: the envelope, the metric and the transducer gain only affect
the modulus.
-/
/-- A chart of a Riemannian manifold with (locally constant) metric tensor `G`. -/
/-- metric tensor -/
/-- Squared Riemannian length `vᵀ G v` of a displacement. -/
/-- A Gaussian wave packet: amplitude, centre, wave vector, angular frequency, phase. -/
/-- The Gaussian envelope `A e^{-|x - x₀|²_G / 2}`. -/
/-- The phase `k·x - ω t + φ`. -/
/-- The field potential of the packet. -/
/-- Off the centre the modulus is strictly below the peak amplitude. -/
/-- The packet is a continuous field on space-time. -/
/-- Time evolution is a pure phase rotation at the packet's frequency. -/
/-- A multi-channel neural field: one wave packet per recording channel. -/

/-- A phased opto-acoustic metamaterial transducer array: one nonzero complex transfer
coefficient (gain and programmable phase) per channel. -/
/-- A transducer built from gains `a_c > 0` and steering phases `α_c`. -/
/-- Optical read-out of channel `c` at element position `p c`. -/
/-- The synthesised holographic optical field. -/
/-- The holographic field is bounded by the total transduced amplitude. -/

/-- Frequency encoding of a symbol `n` over a frame of duration `Tf`: channel `c` is tuned to
`ω_c = -2π n_c / Tf`. -/

/-- The sampled spike-train record: `N + 1` samples per channel of the transduced read-out of the
encoded frame starting at time `t₀`, each with a phase-noise perturbation `ξ c k`. -/
/-- The reference phase of channel `c` at the start of the frame. -/

/-- **Polar form of the samples.** Each sample is `r e^{iθ}` with `r > 0` and
`θ = θ₀ + 2π n_c k / N + ξ c k`. -/
