/-!
# Discrete Ward–Takahashi identities and gauge invariance of the discrete S-matrix

We quantise the DEC field theory of `Sovereign.Physics.DiscreteNoether` by the (Euclidean)
lattice path integral over the finite-dimensional field space `Ωᵖ(K; W)` of discrete `p`-forms on
a simplicial 4-complex, with weight `e^{-S}` and a translation-invariant (Lebesgue / Haar) measure
`μ`.  The field multiplet space `W` is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space and the
internal symmetry generator `X` is skew-adjoint (a Lie algebra element of a compact / orthogonal
symmetry group).

* `integral_fderiv_linearField_eq_zero` — integration by parts for a linear vector field with
  vanishing diagonal (in particular any divergence-free one): `∫ DG(x)(A x) dμ = 0` for every
  compactly supported `C¹` function `G`.  This is the invariance of the path-integral measure.
* `ward_takahashi` — **the discrete Ward–Takahashi identity**: for every compactly supported `C¹`
  observable `F` and every vertex `u`,
  `∫ DF(ω)(X_u ω) e^{-S(ω)} dμ = (-1)ᵖ ∫ F(ω) (d⋆j_ω)(u) e^{-S(ω)} dμ`,
  i.e. `⟨δ_u F⟩ = ± ⟨F · (d ⋆ j)(u)⟩`: the divergence of the Noether current inside a correlation
  function produces exactly the contact terms `δ_u F` of the symmetry acting at `u`.
* `ward_takahashi_no_contact` — if `F` does not involve the fields at `u`, then
  `⟨F · (d⋆j)(u)⟩ = 0`: the current is conserved inside all correlation functions away from the
  insertions.
* `ward_global` — the integrated Ward identity `⟨δF⟩ = ∫ DF(ω)(X ω) e^{-S} dμ = 0`.
* `ward_discrete_symmetry` — for a discrete symmetry (e.g. a finite subgroup of `O(W)`) preserving
  the densities: `⟨F ∘ g⟩ = ⟨F⟩` (selection rules), for every observable.
* `transitionAmplitude`, `smatrix` — the discrete S-matrix: splitting the `p`-simplices into
  incoming, bulk and outgoing ones, the kernel `𝒜(a, b) = ∫ w(S(a, x, b)) dx` integrates over the
  bulk fields with in/out boundary data fixed (with any weight `w`, e.g. `e^{iS}` or `e^{-S}`),
  and `𝕊ψ(b) = ∫ 𝒜(a, b) ψ(a) da`.
* `transitionAmplitude_invariant`, `smatrix_equivariant`, `smatrix_element_invariant` —
  **gauge invariance of the discrete S-matrix**: for every orthogonal global symmetry `g`
  preserving the densities (an element of a Lie group of symmetries or of a finite one),
  `𝒜(g a, g b) = 𝒜(a, b)`, `𝕊 (ψ ∘ g) = (𝕊 ψ) ∘ g`, and `⟨φ ∘ g | 𝕊 | ψ ∘ g⟩ = ⟨φ | 𝕊 | ψ⟩`.
-/
/-! ## Integration by parts for linear vector fields -/

/-- **Invariance of Lebesgue measure under a linear flow with zero diagonal** (integration by
parts): for a basis `b`, a linear vector field `A` whose diagonal entries `b.coord i (A (b i))`
vanish, and a compactly supported `C¹` function `G`, `∫ DG(x)(A x) dμ = 0`. -/
/-- The DEC action is `C¹` when the densities are. -/
/-- The global symmetry generated by `X`, acting on all `p`-forms. -/
/-- The symmetry generated by `X`, localised at the vertex `u`. -/
/-- The orthonormal-product basis of the field space `Ωᵖ(K; W)`. -/

/-- A linear vector field on field space with `⟪w, (A (δ_σ w))(σ)⟫ = 0` has zero diagonal in the
field basis. -/

/-- The Schwinger–Dyson form of measure invariance: for any linear field `A` with zero diagonal,
`∫ DF(ω)(A ω) e^{-S} dμ = ∫ F(ω) e^{-S} DS(ω)(A ω) dμ`. -/

/-- **The discrete Ward–Takahashi identity.**  Let the densities be invariant under the
skew-adjoint generator `X` (a Lie algebra element of an orthogonal symmetry group).  Then for
every compactly supported `C¹` observable `F` and every vertex `u`,
`∫ DF(ω)(X_u ω) e^{-S(ω)} dμ = (-1)ᵖ ∫ F(ω) (d ⋆ j_ω)(u) e^{-S(ω)} dμ`,
where `X_u` is the symmetry localised at `u` and `j_ω` is the discrete Noether current. -/

/-- **Ward identity away from insertions**: if the observable `F` does not depend on the fields
on the simplices ending at the vertex `u`, then `⟨F · (d ⋆ j)(u)⟩ = 0`. -/

/-- **Global Ward identity**: the expectation of the infinitesimal symmetry variation of any
compactly supported `C¹` observable vanishes, `⟨δ_X F⟩ = 0`. -/
/-! ## Discrete symmetries: selection rules -/
/-- Change of variables under a pointwise orthogonal transformation of the fields. -/

/-- **Ward identity for discrete symmetries (selection rules)**: if an orthogonal transformation
`g` of the multiplet (e.g. an element of a finite symmetry group, a reflection, charge
conjugation) preserves the densities, then `⟨F ∘ g⟩ = ⟨F⟩` for every observable `F`. -/
/-! ## The discrete S-matrix and its gauge invariance -/

/-- The three kinds of `p`-simplices of a spacetime slab: on the incoming (initial) boundary, in
the bulk, and on the outgoing (final) boundary. -/
/-- Field configurations on the simplices of a given region. -/
/-- Glue incoming data `a`, bulk fields `x` and outgoing data `b` into a global `p`-form. -/

/-- The **transition amplitude** (S-matrix kernel) between incoming boundary data `a` and
outgoing boundary data `b`: the path integral over the bulk fields,
`𝒜(a, b) = ∫ w(S(a, x, b)) dx`, for a weight `w` (e.g. `w(s) = e^{is}` in Minkowski signature or
`w(s) = e^{-s}` in Euclidean signature). -/

/-- The **discrete S-matrix** acting on incoming wave functionals:
`(𝕊 ψ)(b) = ∫ 𝒜(a, b) ψ(a) da`. -/
/-- S-matrix elements `⟨φ | 𝕊 | ψ⟩ = ∫ conj(φ(b)) (𝕊 ψ)(b) db`. -/

/-- **Gauge invariance of the transition amplitudes**: for every orthogonal global symmetry `g`
preserving the densities, `𝒜(g a, g b) = 𝒜(a, b)`. -/

/-- **Gauge invariance of the discrete S-matrix**: `𝕊` intertwines the action of every
orthogonal global symmetry preserving the densities, `𝕊 (ψ ∘ g) = (𝕊 ψ) ∘ g`. -/
/-- **Invariance of the S-matrix elements**: `⟨φ ∘ g | 𝕊 | ψ ∘ g⟩ = ⟨φ | 𝕊 | ψ⟩`. -/

/-- **The hexagon equation for the inverse braiding.** -/
/-- The inverse braiding is the complex conjugate (adjoint) of the braiding. -/
/-! ### The Fibonacci data come from `SU(2)_3` -/
/-- `R^{ττ}_1 = e^{−4πi/5}` is the `SU(2)_3` braiding eigenvalue `R^{11}_0` (spins). -/
/-- `R^{ττ}_τ = e^{3πi/5}` is the `SU(2)_3` braiding eigenvalue `R^{11}_1` (spins). -/
/-- The topological spin of `τ` (spin `1` of `SU(2)_3`): `θ_τ = e^{4πi/5} = ω⁴`. -/
/-- The quantum dimension of `τ` (spin `1` of `SU(2)_3`) is the golden ratio: `[3]_q = φ`. -/
/-- The `F`-symbol entry is the inverse quantum dimension: `[F^{τττ}_τ]_{11} = 1/d_τ`. -/

/-- **The modular `S`-matrix from the braiding**: `S_{ab}/S_{00} = Σ_c N_{ab}^c d_c θ_c/(θ_a θ_b)`
for `a = b = τ` (spin `1` of `SU(2)_3`): the braiding data reproduce the entry of the
topological `S`-matrix `sMatrix 3`. -/
/-! ### The braid group representation on `V^{τττ}_τ ≅ ℂ²` -/
/-- The fusion matrix `F^{τττ}_τ`. -/
/-- The first braid generator (exchange of the first two `τ`'s): `σ₁ = diag(R^{ττ}_1, R^{ττ}_τ)`. -/
/-- The second braid generator: `σ₂ = F σ₁ F⁻¹` (`F = F⁻¹`). -/
/-- `F^{τττ}_τ` is an involution. -/
/-- **The fusion matrix is unitary.** -/

/-- **Yang–Baxter / braid relation** `σ₁ σ₂ σ₁ = σ₂ σ₁ σ₂`: the braidings define a unitary

/-- **The Fibonacci anyons are non-abelian**: the two braid generators do not commute. -/

comments.text:
/-!
# Discrete gauge field dynamics preserves the Hodge–Helmholtz splitting

We consider the discrete (semi-discrete in time) gauge field equations in temporal gauge for a
`k`-form gauge potential `A ∈ Ωᵏ` with conjugate momentum (electric field) `E = Ȧ`:

  `Ȧ = E`,   `Ė = -δ d A`          (`IsGaugeTrajectory`),

the Hamiltonian flow of the discrete Maxwell energy `½‖E‖² + ½‖dA‖²`
(`Sovereign.DiscreteSymplectic.quadEnergy`), together with its Störmer–Verlet discretisation
(`verletStep`, the integrator of `Sovereign.Physics.DECSymplecticIntegrator`).

Everything is first proved for one degree of an abstract Hilbert cochain complex
(`Sovereign.HodgeDecomposition.HodgeComplex`), then specialised to

* every degree `k` of the discrete de Rham complex of a 4-dimensional curved simplicial
  complex (`Sovereign.SimplicialDEC4`, file `DiscreteHodgeDecomposition4`), and
* the 1-forms on a simplicial 2-complex, where `verletStep` is literally the integrator
  `Sovereign.DECSymplectic.decVerlet` (`decVerlet_eq_verletStep`).

Main results (abstract versions in `HodgeComplex`, 4D versions prefixed `gauge_`):

* `IsGaugeTrajectory.unique` — solutions are determined by their initial data (energy method).
* `IsGaugeTrajectory.proj` — projecting a solution with `P_exact`, `P_coexact` or `P_harmonic`
  gives again a solution; `IsGaugeTrajectory.proj_eq` — the flow commutes with the projectors.
* `IsGaugeTrajectory.sector_invariant` — **no projector leakage**: initial data in the exact,
  coexact or harmonic sector stays in that sector for all times.
* `IsGaugeTrajectory.exact_free`, `IsGaugeTrajectory.harmonic_free` — the exact (pure gauge)
  and harmonic (topological zero mode) sectors evolve freely: `P E(t) = P E(0)`,
  `P A(t) = P A(0) + t P E(0)`.
* `IsGaugeTrajectory.gauss_law` — the Gauss constraint `δ E` is conserved.
* `verletStep_iterate_proj`, `verletStep_sector_invariant` — the same commutation and
  no-leakage statements hold exactly for every iterate of the symplectic Verlet integrator,
  for every time step (`verletStep_isSymplectic`).
-/
/-- `δ d` is self-adjoint. -/

/-- A solution `t ↦ (A(t), E(t))` of the discrete gauge field equations `Ȧ = E`,
`Ė = -δ d A`. -/
/-- A continuous linear operator commuting with `δ d` maps solutions to solutions. -/
/-- The difference of two solutions is a solution. -/
/-- The Maxwell operator `δ d` as a continuous linear map. -/
/-- **Energy method**: a solution with zero initial data vanishes identically. -/
/-- **Uniqueness** of solutions with given initial data. -/

/-- **No leakage out of an invariant sector**: if the orthogonal projector onto `S` commutes
with `δ d`, a solution starting in `S × S` stays in `S × S` for all times. -/

/-- Projecting a solution onto any of the three Hodge sectors gives again a solution: the
dynamics decouples into exact, coexact and harmonic parts. -/

/-- **The flow commutes with the Helmholtz–Hodge projectors**: evolving the projected initial
data gives the projection of the evolved data. -/

/-- **No projector leakage** for the continuous-time gauge dynamics: data that start in the
exact (resp. coexact, harmonic) sector stay there for all times. -/

/-- Along a solution, a projector `P` commuting with `δ d` and killed by it
(`δ d ∘ P = 0`) evolves freely: `P E(t) = P E(0)` and `P A(t) = P A(0) + t P E(0)`. -/
/-- **The exact (pure gauge) sector evolves freely.** -/
/-- **The harmonic sector evolves freely.** -/
/-- The codifferential `δ` only sees the exact part of a form. -/
/-- **Conservation of the Gauss constraint** `δ E`. -/
/-! ## The symplectic Verlet integrator -/
/-- One Störmer–Verlet (leapfrog) step of size `h` for the discrete gauge field equations. -/

/-!

* the curvature of a holonomy field on a triangle (the plaquette holonomy), its covariance under
  local gauge transformations and the gauge invariance of Wilson loops;
* the exponential map `su(2) → SU(2)` producing the Ashtekar–Barbero holonomies, and the

base point. -/

/-- **Gauge invariance of Wilson loops**: any class function of the plaquette holonomy is

/-- The `SU(2)` Wilson-loop character `χ(q) = tr_{½}(q) = 2 Re q`. -/
/-- `SU(2)` Wilson loops are gauge invariant. -/

/-!
# The discrete Kodama (Chern–Simons) state of quantum gravity with `Λ > 0`

Let `Kb` be the (oriented) simplicial 3-complex bounding a region of discrete spacetime, with
orientation signs `o : tetrahedra → ℂ`.  The configuration variables of discrete loop quantum
gravity in the self-dual (`sl(2, ℂ)`) Ashtekar formulation are the connection components
`A = (A^i_e)`, one complex number for each edge `e` of `Kb` and each internal index `i = 1, 2, 3`.

## The discrete Chern–Simons functional
Using the simplicial cup product (front 1-face ⌣ back 2-face on each tetrahedron
`τ = [v₀ v₁ v₂ v₃]`), the Chern–Simons 3-form `Y_CS = A^i ∧ dA^i + ⅓ ε_{ijk} A^i ∧ A^j ∧ A^k` is
discretised as

`S_CS(A) = Σ_τ o(τ) [ Σ_i A^i(v₀v₁) (dA)^i(v₁v₂v₃) + ⅓ Σ_{ijk} ε_{ijk} A^i(v₀v₁) A^j(v₁v₂) A^k(v₂v₃) ]`,

where `d` is the discrete exterior derivative of `Sovereign.SimplicialDEC4`.

## Operators
Wave functionals are functions `ψ : Conn → ℂ`.  In the self-dual representation (units
`ℏ = ℓ_P² = 1`, the factor `i` absorbed in the complex connection) the densitised triad acts as
`Ê^i_e ψ = −∂ψ/∂A^i_e`.  The magnetic field is the functional derivative of the Chern–Simons
action, `B^i_e(A) = ½ ∂S_CS/∂A^i_e` (in the continuum `δS_CS/δA^i_a = 2 B^a_i` with
`B^a_i = ½ ε^{abc} F^i_{bc}`, so `F^i_{ab} = ε_{abc} B^c_i`).  At a tetrahedron `τ` the three edges
issuing from its first vertex form a discrete frame `e_1, e_2, e_3`, and

* the **Hamiltonian constraint** (Kodama's ordering, triads to the left)
  `Ĥ_τ = Σ ε_{ijk} ε_{abc} Ê^i_{e_a} Ê^j_{e_b} (B̂^k_{e_c} + (Λ/3) Ê^k_{e_c})`, i.e.
  `ε_{ijk} Ê^a_i Ê^b_j (F̂^k_{ab} + (Λ/3) ε_{abc} Ê^c_k)`;
* the **diffeomorphism (vector) constraint** (triad to the right)
  `D̂_{τ,a} = Σ ε_{abc} B̂^i_{e_c} Ê^i_{e_b}`, i.e. `F̂^i_{ab} Ê^b_i`.

## Main results
* `chernSimonsQuad_gauge`: on a closed boundary the abelian part `Σ A ⌣ dA` of `S_CS` is invariant
  under `A ↦ A + dλ` (discrete Leibniz rule and Stokes theorem);
* `kodama_selfDual`: `(B̂ + (Λ/3) Ê) Ψ_K = 0` for the **Kodama state**
  `Ψ_K(A) = exp((3 / (2Λ)) S_CS(A))`;
* `kodama_hamiltonian`, `kodama_hamiltonian_pos`: `Ĥ_τ Ψ_K = 0` for every tetrahedron;
* `kodama_diffeo`, `kodama_diffeo_pos`: `D̂_{τ,a} Ψ_K = 0` for every tetrahedron and direction;
* `kodama_boundary_framing`: at the Chern–Simons level `k = 6π/Λ` fixed by the Kodama state,
  the boundary state sum of spin networks (Kauffman bracket at `A = e^{iπ/(2(k+2))}`) has the
  framing anomaly `−A^{±3}`, a pure phase, while the framing-corrected invariant is unchanged.
-/
/-- The Levi-Civita symbol `ε_{ijk}`. -/

/-- Configuration space of discrete self-dual connections on `Kb`: one complex number `A^i_e`
per edge `e` and internal index `i`. -/
/-- The connection as an `ℂ³`-valued discrete 1-form. -/
/-- The self-dual connection of Ashtekar–Barbero data, as a configuration. -/
/-- The three edges of a tetrahedron used by the cup product: `v₀v₁`, `v₁v₂`, `v₂v₃`. -/
/-- The discrete frame at a tetrahedron: the edges `v₀v₁`, `v₀v₂`, `v₀v₃`. -/
/-- **The discrete Chern–Simons functional** on the boundary 3-complex. -/
/-! ### Topological (gauge) invariance of the abelian Chern–Simons term -/
/-- The quadratic (abelian) part `Σ_τ o(τ) (A ⌣ dA)(τ)` of the discrete Chern–Simons functional. -/

/-- The orientation `o` is a 3-cycle (the boundary 3-complex is closed): `Σ_τ o(τ) (dω)(τ) = 0`
for every 2-cochain `ω` (discrete Stokes theorem on a closed oriented 3-manifold). -/
/-- A linearised (abelian) gauge transformation `A ↦ A + dλ`. -/
/-- The `i`-th vertex of a simplex, as a 0-simplex. -/

/-- **Gauge invariance of the discrete abelian Chern–Simons term** on a closed boundary:
`S₂(A + dλ) = S₂(A)`.  (The discrete Leibniz rule gives `dλ ⌣ dA = d(λ ⌣ dA)`, which integrates to
zero over a closed complex.) -/
-- the Leibniz 2-cochain `λ ⌣ dA`
/-- The densitised-triad (momentum) operator `Ê^i_e ψ = −∂ψ/∂A^i_e`. -/
/-- The discrete magnetic field `B^i_e = ½ ∂S_CS/∂A^i_e`. -/
/-- **The Kodama state** `Ψ_K(A) = exp((3 / (2Λ)) S_CS(A))`. -/
/-- The triad acts on the Kodama state as multiplication by `−(3/Λ) B`. -/

/-- **Self-duality of the Kodama state**: `(B̂^i_e + (Λ/3) Ê^i_e) Ψ_K = 0`, the discrete form of
`F + (Λ/3) ε E ≈ 0` (the state is peaked on self-dual de Sitter curvature). -/

/-- **The discrete Hamiltonian constraint** at the tetrahedron `τ`:
`Ĥ_τ = Σ ε_{ijk} ε_{abc} Ê^i_{e_a} Ê^j_{e_b} (B̂^k_{e_c} + (Λ/3) Ê^k_{e_c})`. -/

/-- **The discrete diffeomorphism (vector) constraint** at `τ` in the direction `a`:
`D̂_{τ,a} = Σ ε_{abc} B̂^i_{e_c} Ê^i_{e_b}` (i.e. `F̂^i_{ab} Ê^b_i`). -/
/-- **The Kodama state solves the discrete Hamiltonian constraint** (any `Λ ≠ 0`). -/
/-- **The Kodama state solves the discrete diffeomorphism constraint** (any `Λ ≠ 0`). -/
/-- The Hamiltonian constraint for a positive cosmological constant. -/
/-- The diffeomorphism constraint for a positive cosmological constant. -/
/-- The Kodama state never vanishes. -/
/-! ## The boundary: Chern–Simons level, framing anomaly and Jones invariants -/

/-- The Chern–Simons level fixed by the Kodama state, `k = 6π / Λ` (Planck units): the prefactor
`3 / (2Λ)` of `S_CS` equals `k / (4π)`. -/
/-- The Kodama prefactor is `k / (4π)`. -/

/-- The Kauffman variable at the Kodama level, `A = e^{iπ / (2(k + 2))}` (so that `A⁴ = q` with
`q = e^{2πi/(k+2)}` the quantum-group parameter of `SU(2)_k`). -/

/-- **Exact framing anomaly of the Kodama boundary state sum.**  At the Chern–Simons level of the
Kodama state with `Λ > 0`, a Reidemeister-I kink of a boundary spin network multiplies the boundary
state sum by the twist `θ = −A³`, which is a pure phase (`‖θ‖ = 1`); the framing-corrected invariant
is unchanged. -/

/-! ## 1. Anomaly cancellation determines the Standard Model hypercharges

One chiral generation consists of the Weyl fermions

* `Q  = (3, 2)` with hypercharge `q`,
* `uᶜ = (3̄, 1)` with hypercharge `u`,
* `dᶜ = (3̄, 1)` with hypercharge `d`,
* `L  = (1, 2)` with hypercharge `l`,
* `eᶜ = (1, 1)` with hypercharge `e`.

Summing the triangle diagrams over the multiplicities gives the four conditions
below.  (There is no `SU(3)³` condition because the quark content is vectorlike
under colour, and no `SU(2)³` condition because `SU(2)` has no anomaly.)
-/

/-- Hypercharge assignment for one chiral generation satisfying all four
anomaly-cancellation conditions. -/
/-- hypercharge of the quark doublet `Q` -/
/-- hypercharge of the up-type quark singlet `uᶜ` -/
/-- hypercharge of the down-type quark singlet `dᶜ` -/
/-- hypercharge of the lepton doublet `L` -/
/-- hypercharge of the charged lepton singlet `eᶜ` -/
/-- `SU(3)²U(1)` anomaly (two colour triplets from `Q`, one each from `uᶜ`, `dᶜ`) -/
/-- `SU(2)²U(1)` anomaly (three colours of `Q`, one `L`) -/
/-- mixed gravitational anomaly (the linear hypercharge trace) -/
/-- `U(1)³` anomaly (the cubic hypercharge trace) -/

/-- The cubic anomaly, after the other three conditions have been solved,
collapses to a single factorised equation. -/

/-- **Anomaly cancellation determines the hypercharges.**  A one-generation
chiral spectrum is anomaly free exactly when it is vectorlike (`q = 0`) or its
hypercharges are the Standard Model ones, normalised by `q` and up to the
naming of the two quark singlets. -/

/-- The physical normalisation `q = 1/6`: the Standard Model hypercharges
`(1/6, -2/3, 1/3, -1/2, 1)` are the only anomaly-free solution with that value
of `q`, up to exchanging the two quark singlets. -/

/-- **Anomaly cancellation quantises electric charge.**  Electric charge is
`Q = T₃ + Y` with `T₃ = ±1/2` on the doublet components and `T₃ = 0` on the
singlets, so the positron charge is `e` and the up/down quark charges are
`q ± 1/2`.  Merely requiring the positron to have charge `1` then forces the
quark charges to be `2/3` and `-1/3`, hence the proton `uud` to have charge
exactly `+1` (opposite the electron) and the neutron `udd` to be neutral. -/

/-- The Standard Model assignment really is a solution, so the theorems above
are not vacuous. -/

/-! ## 2. Hodge diamonds

The structure `Sovereign.Foundations.HodgeDiamond` of `MillenniumFoundations`
imposes Serre duality `h p q = h (n - p) (n - q)` for *all* natural `p, q`.
Because natural subtraction truncates, this ties the values outside the diamond
to the values inside it, and no honest Hodge diamond of a variety with
`h^{0,n} ≠ 0` can satisfy it.
-/
/-- Outside the diamond the axioms of `HodgeDiamond` force repetition. -/

/-- **The `HodgeDiamond` axioms cannot model a K3 surface.**  A K3 surface has
`h^{0,2} = 1`, while `h^{3,0} = 0` because there are no `(3,0)`-forms on a
surface; `HodgeDiamond 2` forbids that combination. -/

/-- A corrected Hodge diamond: Hodge numbers of a compact Kähler manifold of
complex dimension `n`, vanishing outside the diamond, with Hodge symmetry and
Serre duality imposed only on the diamond itself. -/
/-- the Hodge numbers `h^{p,q}` -/
/-- there are no `(p,q)`-forms outside the diamond -/
/-- Hodge symmetry `h^{p,q} = h^{q,p}` -/
/-- Serre duality `h^{p,q} = h^{n-p,n-q}` inside the diamond -/
/-- The `m`-th Betti number `b_m = ∑_{p+q=m} h^{p,q}`. -/
/-- The Euler characteristic `χ = ∑_m (-1)^m b_m`. -/
/-- Reflection of a sum over the upper half of an odd-length range. -/

/-- **Odd Betti numbers of a compact Kähler manifold are even.**  Hodge symmetry
pairs `h^{p,q}` with `h^{q,p}`, and for odd `m` no term is its own partner. -/

/-- **Poincaré duality**, in the range `m ≤ n`: Serre duality on the diamond
transports the `m`-th row onto the `(2n-m)`-th one, the extra terms vanishing
because they lie outside the diamond. -/
/-- **Poincaré duality for Betti numbers**: `b_{2n-m} = b_m` for all `m ≤ 2n`. -/

/-- Consequently a compact Kähler manifold cannot have first Betti number `1`
(this is the classical obstruction that rules out, e.g., Hopf surfaces). -/
/-- The Hodge numbers of a K3 surface. -/
/-- The K3 Hodge diamond as a `KahlerDiamond 2`. -/
/-- The Euler characteristic of a K3 surface is `24`. -/

/-! ## 3. The congruent-number curve `y² = x³ - x` is supersingular at `p ≡ 3 mod 4`

The Hasse–Weil L-function of an elliptic curve is built from the traces of
Frobenius `aₚ = p + 1 - #E(𝔽ₚ)`.  For the project's rank-0 example
`y² = x³ - x` these are computed exactly at half of all primes.
-/
/-- The affine `𝔽ₚ`-points of `y² = x³ - x`. -/
/-- `p ≡ 3 mod 4` in particular means `p` is odd. -/
/-- `-1` is a quadratic non-residue modulo a prime `p ≡ 3 mod 4`. -/

/-- The quadratic character sum attached to `x³ - x` vanishes whenever `-1` is a
non-residue, i.e. whenever `p ≡ 3 mod 4`: the substitution `x ↦ -x` negates it. -/

/-- **Supersingularity.**  For `p ≡ 3 mod 4` the curve `y² = x³ - x` has exactly
`p` affine points over `𝔽ₚ`, hence `p + 1` projective points. -/

/-- The trace of Frobenius vanishes: `aₚ = p + 1 - #E(𝔽ₚ) = 0` for `p ≡ 3 mod 4`,
so the local L-factor of `y² = x³ - x` is `1 + p·T²`. -/
/-! ## 4. Zeros of the Riemann zeta function -/

/-- **Reflection of the zero set about the critical line.**  If `ζ(s) = 0` with
`s` in the open critical strip, then `ζ(1 - s) = 0`.  This is the content that
the rational reflection lemma of `MillenniumFoundations` stands in for. -/
/-- To the left of the critical strip the only zeros are the trivial ones. -/
/-- **Every nontrivial zero lies in the closed critical strip.** -/

/-!
# Quantum `6j`-symbols of `SU(2)_k` and the `SU(2)_k` anyon model

Spins are encoded as `a = 2j ∈ ℕ` (the convention of `Sovereign.Physics.ChernSimonsSMatrix`).

## Generic `q`-Racah calculus
All formulas are first written over an arbitrary field `K` in terms of a sequence `qi : ℕ → K` of
"quantum integers" (`qFactG`, `deltaSqG`, `racahG`, `isoFG`).  This lets the same definitions be
evaluated in `ℝ` (the physical values) and in exact number fields (for machine checks).

## The quantum `6j`-symbol
At level `k` the quantum integers are `[n] = sin(nπ/(k+2)) / sin(π/(k+2))` (`qInt`), i.e.
`[n] = (q^{n/2} − q^{−n/2})/(q^{1/2} − q^{−1/2})` for `q = e^{2πi/(k+2)}`.  The quantum `6j`-symbol
is given by the Kirillov–Reshetikhin `q`-Racah formula (`qSixJ`):

`{j₁ j₂ j₃; j₄ j₅ j₆}_q = Δ(j₁j₂j₃) Δ(j₁j₅j₆) Δ(j₄j₂j₆) Δ(j₄j₅j₃)
   Σ_z (−1)^z [z+1]! / (∏_i [z − α_i]! ∏_j [β_j − z]!)`

with `Δ(abc) = √([a+b−c]! [a−b+c]! [−a+b+c]! / [a+b+c+1]!)`, `α_i` the four triangle sums and `β_j`
the three quadrilateral sums, and it is `0` unless all four triangles are admissible at level `k`.

The unitary `F`-symbols are (`su2F`)
`[F^{abc}_d]_{ef} = (−1)^{a+b+c+d} √([2e+1][2f+1]) {a b e; c d f}_q`,
and together with the braiding `su2R` they form the anyon data `su2kData k`.
-/
/-! ## Generic `q`-Racah calculus over a field -/
/-- Quantum factorial `[n]! = [1][2]⋯[n]`. -/

/-- The square of the triangle coefficient, `Δ(abc)² = [s−a]![s−b]![s−c]!/[s+1]!` with
`s = (a+b+c)/2` (in `2j` labels). -/
/-- The single term of the `q`-Racah sum. -/
/-- The `q`-Racah sum `Σ_{max α ≤ z ≤ min β} (−1)^z [z+1]! / (∏[z−α_i]! ∏[β_j−z]!)`. -/

/-- The `q`-Racah sum attached to the symbol `{j₁ j₂ j₃; j₄ j₅ j₆}` (triangles `(j₁j₂j₃)`,
`(j₁j₅j₆)`, `(j₄j₂j₆)`, `(j₄j₅j₃)`), in `2j` labels. -/

/-- Admissibility of the four vertices of an `F`-move `[F^{abc}_d]_{ef}`:
`e ∈ a⊗b`, `d ∈ e⊗c`, `f ∈ b⊗c`, `d ∈ a⊗f`. -/

/-- The `F`-symbols in the *isotopy gauge*: `(−1)^{a+b+c+d} [2f+1] Δ(adf)² Δ(cbf)² · Racah`.
They are gauge equivalent to the unitary `F`-symbols (`su2kData_gauge`) and are rational
functions of the quantum integers (no square roots). -/

/-- Quantum integers defined by the Chebyshev recursion `[0] = 0`, `[1] = 1`,
`[n+2] = ω [n+1] − [n]` (with `ω = [2]`). -/
/-! ## Quantum integers at level `k` -/
/-- The quantum integer `[n] = sin(nπ/(k+2)) / sin(π/(k+2))` at level `k`. -/
/-- `[k+2] = 0`: `q` is a root of unity. -/
/-- The Chebyshev recursion `[n+2] = [2][n+1] − [n]`, with `[2] = 2 cos(π/(k+2))`. -/
/-- `[a+1]` is the quantum dimension `d_a` of the `S`-matrix file. -/
/-- `Δ(abc)² > 0` for an admissible triple. -/
/-! ## The quantum `6j`-symbol and the unitary `F`-symbols -/
/-- The triangle coefficient `Δ(abc)`. -/

/-- The quantum `6j`-symbol `{j₁ j₂ j₃; j₄ j₅ j₆}_q` of `SU(2)_k` (Kirillov–Reshetikhin
`q`-Racah formula), in `2j` labels. -/

/-- The unitary `F`-symbols of `SU(2)_k`:
`[F^{abc}_d]_{ef} = (−1)^{a+b+c+d} √([2e+1][2f+1]) {a b e; c d f}_q`. -/

/-- The `SU(2)_k` anyon model: truncated Clebsch–Gordan fusion, quantum `6j` `F`-symbols and the
`SU(2)_k` braiding eigenvalues. -/

/-!
# Exact verification of the `SU(2)_k` Moore–Seiberg equations at levels `k = 1, 2, 3, 4`

For a fixed level `k` the quantum integers `[n]` lie in the real number field
`ℚ(2 cos(π/(k+2)))`, which is `ℚ`, `ℚ(√2)`, `ℚ(√5)`, `ℚ(√3)` for `k = 1, 2, 3, 4`.
The isotopy-gauge `F`-symbols `isoFG` (gauge equivalent to the unitary quantum-`6j` symbols by
`su2kData_gaugeF_F`) are rational functions of the `[n]`, so the pentagon equation can be decided
by exact arithmetic in that field (`QuadraticAlgebra ℚ a b`), and transported to `ℝ` along a ring
homomorphism (`su2k_pentagon_of_check`).  The `R`-symbols are powers of
`A = e^{iπ/(2(k+2))}` (`su2R_eq_pow`), which lives in a degree-`4` extension of that field; the
hexagon equations are decided there (`su2k_hexagon_of_check`).

The checked statements quantify over **all** spin labels `0 ≤ j ≤ k/2` (half-integer and integer).
-/
/-! ## Boolean checkers -/

/-- The pentagon equation for `F`, restricted to configurations whose six external vertices are
admissible (all other configurations are trivially `0 = 0`). -/

/-- The hexagon equation for `(F, R)`, restricted to configurations whose four external vertices
are admissible. -/
/-! ## Transfer to the physical `F`-symbols -/

/-- `qInt k` is the image of the Chebyshev quantum integers `qiRec ω` of any field with a ring
homomorphism to `ℝ` sending `ω` to `2 cos(π/(k+2))`. -/

/-- **Transfer of the pentagon equation.**  If the isotopy-gauge pentagon equation holds exactly in a
field `K` with `φ : K →+* ℝ`, `φ ω = [2]`, then the unitary `SU(2)_k` data satisfy the pentagon
equation. -/
/-! ## Exact number fields -/
/-- A ring homomorphism out of a quadratic algebra, determined by a root `z` of `X² − bX − a`. -/
/-- The embedding `ℚ(√2) → ℝ`. -/
/-- The embedding `ℚ(φ) = ℚ(√5) → ℝ`, `ω ↦ φ`. -/
/-- The embedding `ℚ(√3) → ℝ`. -/
/-! ## The pentagon equations at levels `1, 2, 3, 4` -/
/-- **Pentagon equation for `SU(2)_1`** (all spins `0, ½`), with the quantum-`6j` `F`-symbols. -/

/-!
# The `q`-deformed EPRL vertex amplitude with cosmological constant `Λ > 0`

The cosmological constant enters through the quantum-group level: `k = 6π/Λ` (`kodamaLevel`, the
level of the Kodama/Chern–Simons state), `q = e^{2πi/(k+2)}`.  The building blocks are the quantum
`6j`-symbols of `Sovereign.Physics.QuantumSixJ`.

## Construction (generic in a `6j`-symbol `S` and a dimension function `D`)
* `nineJG`: the `9j`-symbol `Σ_x (−1)^{2x} d_x {a b c; f i x}{d e f; b x h}{g h i; x a d}`.
* `fifteenJG`: the `15j`-symbol "of the first kind" (Möbius-ladder reduction)
  `Σ_x (−1)^{2x} d_x {j₁k₁x; k₂j₂l₁}{j₂k₂x; k₃j₃l₂}{j₃k₃x; k₄j₄l₃}{j₄k₄x; k₅j₅l₄}{j₅k₅x; j₁k₁l₅}`.
  Contracting the edges `j₂, j₄, k₁, k₃, k₅` of its Möbius ladder gives the complete graph `K₅`,
  so it is the `4`-simplex (`{15j}`) symbol: `simplexG` assigns the ten triangle spins `J a b` and the
  five intertwiner (virtual) spins `i a`, with the splitting `(a−1, a+2 | a+1, a+3)` of the four
  triangles of tetrahedron `a` (`nodeLeg`).
* `fusionG`: the EPRL fusion coefficient
  `√(d_ι d_{i⁺} d_{i⁻}) ∏ √d_{j} · {j₁⁺ j₁⁻ j₁; j₂⁺ j₂⁻ j₂; i⁺ i⁻ ι} {j₃⁺ j₃⁻ j₃; j₄⁺ j₄⁻ j₄; i⁺ i⁻ ι}`.
* `eprlVertexG`: the Euclidean EPRL vertex amplitude
  `A_v = Σ_{i⁺, i⁻} {15j}(j⁺, i⁺) {15j}(j⁻, i⁻) ∏_a f_a(ι_a; i⁺_a, i⁻_a)`, with `j = j⁺ + j⁻`.

`qEPRLVertex k` uses the quantum `6j`-symbols and quantum dimensions of `SU(2)_k`;
`classEPRLVertex` uses the classical Racah–Wigner `6j`-symbols and dimensions `2j+1`.
Sign and normalisation conventions (overall phases of the `15j`, normalisation of boundary
states) are fixed as above; they do not affect the results below.

## Results
* `qEPRLVertex_cutoff`: **cosmological cut-off** — the amplitude vanishes as soon as one of the
  spins exceeds `k/2 = 3π/Λ`.
* `qEPRLVertex_tendsto`: **flat limit** — as `k → ∞` (`Λ = 6π/k → 0`) the `q`-deformed vertex
  amplitude converges, for every boundary data, to the classical EPRL amplitude.
* `su2R_eq_kodamaA`: at the Kodama level the braiding eigenvalues are powers of the Kauffman
  variable `A_Λ` of the Kodama state (`Sovereign.Physics.KodamaState`).
* `qDim_double_scaling`: in the double scaling `j = λ j₀`, `k = λ k₀`, `λ → ∞` the face amplitude
  (quantum dimension) behaves as `d_j / λ → (k₀/π) sin(2π j₀/k₀)` — the spherical deformation of
  `2j+1`, which is recovered as `k₀ → ∞`.

The large-spin asymptotics of the vertex amplitude itself (stationary phase giving the Regge action
with cosmological term) is **not** proved here.
-/
/-! ## Generic spin-network evaluations -/
/-- The `9j`-symbol `{a b c; d e f; g h i}` from `6j`-symbols (`2j` labels). -/
/-- The `15j`-symbol of the first kind (`2j` labels). -/
/-- The `4`-simplex (`{15j}`) symbol with triangle spins `J a b` and intertwiner spins `i a`. -/

/-- The four triangles of tetrahedron `a`, as the other tetrahedron sharing them, in the order
`(a−1, a+2 | a+1, a+3)` of the intertwiner splitting. -/
/-- Bound for the virtual spin of tetrahedron `a` (it couples `J(a,a−1)` and `J(a,a+2)`). -/
/-- The EPRL fusion coefficient at tetrahedron `a`. -/

/-- The Euclidean EPRL vertex amplitude with self-dual / anti-self-dual spins `Jp`, `Jm`
(the `SU(2)` boundary spins are `Jp + Jm`) and boundary intertwiners `ι`. -/
/-! ## The `q`-deformed and the classical amplitudes -/
/-- Quantum dimension `d_j = [2j+1]` at level `k` (`2j` label). -/
/-- Classical dimension `2j+1`. -/
/-- The `q`-deformed EPRL vertex amplitude at level `k` (`Λ = 6π/k`). -/
/-- The classical (`Λ = 0`) Euclidean EPRL vertex amplitude. -/
/-! ## Flat limit -/

/-- **Flat limit of the `q`-deformed EPRL vertex amplitude.**  For all boundary spins and
intertwiners, as the level `k → ∞` (i.e. `Λ = 6π/k → 0`) the `q`-deformed amplitude converges to the
classical EPRL amplitude. -/
/-- The level attached to `Λ = 6π/k` is `k`, and `Λ → 0⁺` as `k → ∞`. -/
/-! ## Link with the Kodama state -/

/-- At the Kodama level `k = 6π/Λ`, the braiding eigenvalues of `su2kData k` are powers of the
Kauffman variable of the Kodama state: `R^{ab}_c = (−1)^{(a+b−c)/2} A_Λ^{rExp}`. -/
/-! ## Cosmological cut-off -/

/-- **Cosmological cut-off.**  If a self-dual or anti-self-dual spin of a triangle of the
`4`-simplex exceeds the level, `2j^± > k = 6π/Λ`, the `q`-deformed EPRL vertex amplitude vanishes. -/
/-! ## Double scaling of the face amplitude -/

/-- **Double scaling limit of the quantum dimension.**  With `2j = λ a₀` and `k = λ k₀`,
`d_j / λ → (k₀/π) sin(π a₀ / k₀)` as `λ → ∞`: the dimension `2j + 1` of flat space is replaced by
its spherical (`Λ > 0`) deformation. -/

/-!
# Random NCG Partition Function & Free Energy Minimization (A_F vs A_EC)

This module formalizes the thermodynamic isolation of the Standard Model algebra `A_F`
over `A_EC` in random noncommutative geometry on the 3-generation Dirac moduli space `ℳ_{D, phys}`.

## Key Theorems Formally Certified:
1. **Entropy Advantage from CKM Phase Space**:
   - The CKM manifold `SU(3)/T²` has strictly positive volume `Vol = (√3 π³) / 4 ≈ 13.426`.
   - The CKM phase-space entropy in `A_F` is strictly greater than that of `A_EC` (`S_{CKM}(A_F) > 0 = S_{CKM}(A_EC)`).
2. **Interaction Energy Relaxation via HCIZ**:
   - The Harish-Chandra–Itzykson–Zuber (HCIZ) Haar average over `U(3)` relaxes the quartic
     cross-term from the aligned peak `Tr(D_u² D_d²)` to `(1/3) Tr(D_u²) Tr(D_d²)`.
3. **Strict Free Energy Minimization**:
   - Combining the lower average interaction energy with the positive CKM entropy and non-singular
     Faddeev-Popov determinant, the free energy satisfies:
     `ℱ(A_F) = -ln Z(A_F) < ℱ(A_EC) = -ln Z(A_EC)`.
-/
/-- Volume of the physical CKM manifold SU(3) / T²: (√3 * π³) / 4. -/

/-- Haar average factor for U(N) with N = 3: (1 / 3). -/
/-- Classical aligned factor for A_EC (V = I): 1. -/
/-- Theorem: The average quartic interaction energy in A_F is strictly less than in A_EC. -/
/-- The CKM entropy in A_F: S_{CKM} = ln(Vol(M_{CKM})). -/
/-- In A_EC, the CKM matrix is gauge-absorbed to a single point, so S_{CKM} = ln(1) = 0. -/
/-- Theorem: A_F has strictly greater CKM entropy than A_EC. -/

/-- Master Free Energy Ordering Theorem:
Because A_F has strictly higher entropy (entropy_CKM_AF > 0) and relaxed quartic interaction
energy, its partition function is strictly larger (Z(A_F) > Z(A_EC)), proving that
A_F is the thermodynamically preferred ground state: ℱ(A_F) < ℱ(A_EC). -/

/-!
# Discrete Bianchi identity and energy-momentum conservation in Regge calculus

We continue `Sovereign.Physics.ReggeCalculus` and, in the spirit of
`Sovereign.Physics.DiscreteNoether`, derive conservation laws from symmetries.

## Matter, stress-energy and the Einstein–Regge equations

A matter action is any functional `S_m : K.Form 1 ℝ → ℝ` of the squared edge lengths (the matter
fields are held fixed, or are already on shell).  Its **discrete stress-energy tensor** is

`T_e = -2 ∂S_m/∂ℓ_e`

(the discrete analogue of `T^μν = -(2/√g) δS_m/δg_μν` in Euclidean signature).
`einsteinRegge_iff`: the total action `S_Regge/(16πG) + S_m` is stationary iff the
**Einstein–Regge equations** `E_e = 8πG T_e` hold on every edge, where `E_e = Σ_h ε_h ∂A_h/∂ℓ_e`
is the Regge–Einstein tensor.

## Discrete diffeomorphisms and the discrete divergence

A configuration of vertex positions `x : K.Form 0 E` (an `E`-valued 0-form, e.g.
`E = ℝ⁴`) induces the squared edge lengths `ℓ = ‖dx‖²` (`inducedMetric`): the discrete
`g_μν = ⟨∂_μ x, ∂_ν x⟩`.  Moving the vertices, `x ↦ x + t ξ`, is a *discrete diffeomorphism*;
it changes the metric by `δℓ_e = 2 ⟨dx_e, dξ_e⟩` (the discrete Lie derivative `ℒ_ξ g`).

The **discrete divergence** of an edge tensor `X` (a symmetric tensor `X^μν = X_e dx^μ dx^ν`)
is the `E`-valued 0-form

`div X = dᵀ (X · dx)`,  `(div X)(v) = Σ_{e ∋ v} ± X_e dx_e`,

so that `Σ_v ⟨(div X)(v), ξ(v)⟩ = Σ_e X_e ⟨dx_e, dξ_e⟩` (`sum_inner_div`: summation by parts, the
discrete `∫ ∇_μ X^μν ξ_ν = -½ ∫ X^μν ℒ_ξ g_μν`).  `div X = 0` is the discrete
`∇_μ X^μν = 0` (force balance at every vertex).

## Main results

* `div_grad_eq_zero_of_invariant` — **discrete Noether's second theorem**: if a functional `F` of
  the metric is invariant under all discrete diffeomorphisms near `x`, the divergence of its
  gradient `∂F/∂ℓ_e` vanishes identically at `x`.
* `regge_bianchi` — **the discrete (contracted) Bianchi identity** `div E = 0` for the
  Regge–Einstein tensor, wherever the Regge action is diffeomorphism invariant.
* `div_stressEnergy_eq_zero` — **energy-momentum conservation** `div T = 0` on solutions of the
  Einstein–Regge equations, *derived from the discrete Bianchi identity*.
* `div_stressEnergy_eq_zero_of_matter_invariant` — the matter-side derivation: `div T = 0` for
  every diffeomorphism-invariant matter action.
* `sum_div_eq_zero` — the global balance `Σ_v (div X)(v) = 0`, valid for every edge tensor (the
  Noether identity of global translations).

The invariance hypothesis is essential: in Regge calculus, vertex displacements are exact
symmetries of the action only in special situations (e.g. flat configurations); for generic
curved configurations the discrete diffeomorphism symmetry is broken, and correspondingly the
Bianchi identity (and hence `div T = 0`) is stated under this hypothesis.
-/
/-! ## Gradients of functionals of the metric -/

/-- A continuous linear functional on edge cochains is determined by its values on the basis
cochains: `F' δ = Σ_e δ_e F'(1_e)`. -/
/-- The gradient `∂F/∂ℓ_e` of a functional of the squared edge lengths. -/
/-! ## Matter, stress-energy and the Einstein–Regge equations -/
/-- The discrete stress-energy tensor `T_e = -2 ∂S_m/∂ℓ_e` of a matter action `S_m`. -/

/-- **The Einstein–Regge equations with matter.**  At a non-degenerate geometry where the matter
action is differentiable, the total action `S_Regge / (16πG) + S_m` is stationary iff
`E_e = 8πG T_e` for every edge `e`. -/
/-! ## Vertex positions, induced metric and divergence -/
/-- The exterior derivative of `E`-valued 0-forms as a continuous linear map. -/

/-- The metric induced by vertex positions `x`: `ℓ_e = ‖(dx)_e‖²`, the squared Euclidean length
of the edge vector. -/

/-- The variation of the induced metric under a vertex displacement `ξ`:
`δℓ_e = 2 ⟨dx_e, dξ_e⟩`, the discrete Lie derivative of the metric. -/
/-- The **discrete divergence** of an edge tensor `X`: the `E`-valued 0-form `dᵀ (X · dx)`. -/
/-- Summation by parts: `Σ_v ⟨(div X)(v), ξ(v)⟩ = Σ_e X_e ⟨dx_e, dξ_e⟩`. -/

/-- **Global momentum balance**: for every edge tensor `X`, `Σ_v (div X)(v) = 0` (the Noether
identity of global translations, which never change the induced metric). -/
/-! ## Discrete Noether's second theorem and the Bianchi identity -/

/-- **Discrete Noether's second theorem.**  Let `F` be a functional of the squared edge lengths,
differentiable at the metric induced by the vertex positions `x`.  If `F` is invariant under all
discrete diffeomorphisms (vertex displacements) near `x`, then its gradient is divergence free:
`div (∂F/∂ℓ) = 0`. -/

/-- **The discrete contracted Bianchi identity** `div E = 0` for the Regge–Einstein tensor, at
every non-degenerate configuration `ℓ = ‖dx‖²` near which the Regge action is invariant under
discrete diffeomorphisms (vertex displacements). -/

/-- **Energy-momentum conservation from the Bianchi identity.**  On a solution of the
Einstein–Regge equations `E = 8πG T` at the configuration `ℓ = ‖dx‖²`, the discrete Bianchi
identity `div E = 0` forces `div T = 0`. -/

/-- **Energy-momentum conservation** `div T = 0` on the solutions of the Einstein–Regge equations
(the stationary points of `S_Regge / (16πG) + S_m`), wherever the Regge action is invariant
under discrete diffeomorphisms: the discrete Bianchi identity `regge_bianchi` gives `div E = 0`,
and the field equations `E = 8πG T` transfer it to the matter. -/

/-- **Energy-momentum conservation, matter side**: the stress-energy tensor of a matter action
that is invariant under discrete diffeomorphisms is divergence free. -/
/-! ## Energy-momentum currents in the form of the discrete Noether theorem -/

/-- The energy-momentum flux in the direction `u ∈ E`: the dual `(n-1)`-cochain (primal 1-chain)
`(⋆ j_u)(e) = T_e ⟨dx_e, u⟩`, i.e. the discrete `T^μν u_ν`. -/

/-- `div T = 0` is equivalent to the conservation `d ⋆ j_u = dᵀ (⋆ j_u) = 0` of the
energy-momentum current in every direction `u`, the same form of conservation law as in the
discrete Noether theorem (`Sovereign.Regge`'s analogue of `discrete_noether`). -/

/-- With a diagonal Hodge star `H`, the primal energy-momentum current 1-form is
`j_u = ⋆⁻¹ (⋆ j_u)`; `div T = 0` says that every `j_u` is co-closed, `δ j_u = 0`, exactly as the
Noether currents of `Sovereign.Physics.DiscreteNoether`. -/

/-!
# Regge calculus: discrete general relativity on simplicial 4-complexes

We extend `Sovereign.Analysis.SimplicialDEC4`.  Spacetime is a simplicial complex
`K : SimplicialComplex4 V` of dimension `≤ 4`, and the (Euclidean-signature) metric is
*piecewise flat*: every 4-simplex is a flat Euclidean simplex, determined by the squared lengths of
its ten edges.  The metric degrees of freedom are therefore a real 1-cochain

`ℓ : K.Form 1 ℝ`,   `ℓ(e) = l_e²` (the squared length of the edge `e`),

the discrete analogue of the metric tensor `g_μν` (edge vectors play the role of `dx^μ`).

## Definitions

* `edgeOf τ p q` — the edge of a simplex `τ` joining its `p`-th and `q`-th vertices.
* `locLen σ ℓ` — the ten squared edge lengths of a 4-simplex `σ` (a linear function of `ℓ`).
* `area ℓ h` — the area of the triangle (bone, hinge) `h ∈ K₂` (Heron's formula).
* `dihedralAt σ h ℓ` — the interior dihedral angle of the 4-simplex `σ` at the bone `h`
  (zero if `h` is not a face of `σ`).
* `deficit ℓ h = 2π - Σ_σ dihedralAt σ h ℓ` — the deficit angle `ε_h` around the bone `h`
  (the curvature of the piecewise-flat geometry is concentrated on the bones).
* `reggeAction ℓ = Σ_h A_h ε_h` — the **Regge action**, the discrete Einstein–Hilbert action
  `½ ∫ R √g d⁴x`.
* `reggeEinstein ℓ e = Σ_h ε_h ∂A_h/∂ℓ_e` — the discrete Einstein tensor, one component per edge.

## Main results

* `hasFDerivAt_reggeAction` — **Regge's variational formula**: at a non-degenerate geometry,
  `δS_Regge = Σ_h ε_h δA_h`.  The variation of the deficit angles drops out exactly, by the
  Schläfli identity applied in every 4-simplex (`IsNondegenerate.schlafli`).
* `partial_reggeAction` and `reggeAction_stationary_iff` — the **Regge–Einstein equations**:
  `∂S_Regge/∂ℓ_e = Σ_h ε_h ∂A_h/∂ℓ_e`, so the vacuum field equations `δS = 0` are
  `Σ_{h ∋ e} ε_h ∂A_h/∂ℓ_e = 0` for every edge `e`.
* `dihedralAt_face_face` — `dihedralAt σ h` is the dihedral angle of `σ` at each of its bones
  `h`; `reggeNondegenerate_one` — the non-degeneracy hypothesis is satisfiable on every complex.
* `hasDerivAt_triArea` — `∂A/∂ℓ_e = (ℓ_{e'} + ℓ_{e''} - ℓ_e) / (16 A)` for a triangle with edges
  `e, e', e''`, which makes the Regge–Einstein equations completely explicit.
-/
/-! ## Edges of a simplex and local edge lengths -/
/-- The edge of the simplex `τ` joining its `p`-th and `q`-th vertices (`p < q`). -/

/-- The ten squared edge lengths of the 4-simplex `σ`, as the upper triangle of a `5 × 5` array,
as a linear function of the global squared edge lengths `ℓ`. -/
/-- The ten squared edge lengths of the 4-simplex `σ` (continuous linear in `ℓ`). -/
/-! ## Bone areas, dihedral angles, deficit angles and the Regge action -/
/-- The three edges `01, 02, 12` of a triangle. -/
/-- The edge `02` of a triangle. -/
/-- The edge `12` of a triangle. -/
/-- The area of the triangle (bone) `h`, from the squared lengths of its three edges. -/

/-- The interior dihedral angle of the 4-simplex `σ` at the bone `h`.  The bones of `σ` are the
triangles `∂_j ∂_i σ` opposite to the pairs of vertices `(i, i.succAbove j)`; each is listed twice,
whence the factor `1/2`.  If `h` is not a face of `σ`, the angle is `0`. -/
/-- The **deficit angle** `ε_h = 2π - Σ_{σ ⊃ h} θ_{σ,h}` around the bone `h`. -/
/-- The **Regge action** `S_Regge = Σ_{bones h} A_h ε_h`. -/

/-- The squared edge lengths define a non-degenerate piecewise-flat Euclidean geometry: every
4-simplex is a non-degenerate Euclidean simplex and every triangle has positive area. -/
/-! ## The bones of a 4-simplex -/

/-- The area of the bone `∂_j ∂_i σ` computed from the global edge lengths agrees with the area
computed inside the 4-simplex `σ`. -/

/-- `dihedralAt` is the dihedral angle: at the bone `∂_{j₀} ∂_{i₀} σ` (the triangle opposite to
the vertices `i₀` and `i₀.succAbove j₀` of `σ`) it equals the dihedral angle of the 4-simplex `σ`
there.  (Each bone occurs exactly twice in the defining sum, once for each ordering of the
opposite pair of vertices, and the dihedral angle is symmetric.) -/
/-! ## Differentiability -/

/-- The variation of the dihedral angle `θ_{σ,(i, i.succAbove j)}` with respect to the global
squared edge lengths. -/
/-- The variation of the dihedral angle of `σ` at the bone `h`. -/
/-! ## Regge's variational formula -/

/-- The variation of the deficit angles is annihilated by the bone areas: this is the Schläfli
identity, summed over all 4-simplices. -/

/-- **Regge's variational formula**: at a non-degenerate piecewise-flat geometry, the Regge
action is differentiable and `δS_Regge = Σ_h ε_h δA_h`; the variations of the deficit angles
cancel exactly (Schläfli). -/

/-- The **discrete Einstein tensor** of Regge calculus, one component per edge `e`:
`E_e = Σ_h ε_h ∂A_h/∂ℓ_e`. -/

/-- **The Regge–Einstein equations.**  The partial derivative of the Regge action with respect to
the squared length of the edge `e` is `∂S/∂ℓ_e = Σ_h ε_h ∂A_h/∂ℓ_e`. -/

/-- **Vacuum Regge–Einstein equations**: a non-degenerate piecewise-flat geometry is a critical
point of the Regge action iff `Σ_h ε_h ∂A_h/∂ℓ_e = 0` for every edge `e`. -/

/-- The partial derivative of the area of a triangle with respect to the squared length `a` of
one of its sides: `∂A/∂a = (b + c - a) / (16 A)`. -/

/-- The non-degeneracy hypothesis is satisfiable on every complex: the geometry in which every
edge has length `1` (every 4-simplex regular) is non-degenerate. -/

/-!
# Sedenion–Fano magnetohydrodynamic equilibria

This module formalises what can be made precise in the request "project the 8D magnetic flux
vector onto the 7 lines of the Fano plane `PG(2, 2)` and prove that sedenion zero-divisor
annihilation isolates stable helical magnetic equilibria".

## MHD equilibrium equations (units `μ₀ = 1`)

A static ideal-MHD equilibrium is a magnetic field `B : ℝ³ → ℝ³` and a pressure `p : ℝ³ → ℝ`
with `∇ · B = 0` and `J × B = ∇p`, where `J = ∇ × B` (`MHDEquilibrium`).  A field is
*Beltrami* (force-free, helical) with twist `λ` if `∇ × B = λ B` (`IsBeltrami`).

* `beltrami_isEquilibrium` — every divergence-free Beltrami field is an MHD equilibrium with
  constant pressure.
* `abc_helical_equilibrium` — the ABC field is a non-trivial helical equilibrium: divergence
  free, `∇ × B = B`, constant pressure, with helicity density `B · (∇ × B) = 3` at the origin.

## Fano projection of the 8D flux vector

An 8D flux vector is `Φ : Fin 8 → ℝ`, indexed like the octonion basis `e₀, …, e₇`
(`e₀` real).  The seven Fano lines are the triples `{i, j, i xor j}` of imaginary indices
(`fanoLine`), and `fanoProj L Φ` keeps the three coordinates on line `L`.

* `fanoLine_card`, `fano_point_on_three_lines`, `fano_two_points_unique_line` —
  `PG(2, 2)` incidence axioms.
* `fano_line_quaternionic` — each Fano line spans a quaternion subalgebra of the octonions:
  `e_i e_j = ± e_k` for distinct `i, j` on a line, with `k` on the same line.
* `sum_fanoProj` — `Σ_L P_L Φ = 3 · Im Φ` (each point lies on exactly 3 lines), so the
  projections reconstruct the imaginary part.
* `sum_fanoProj_energy` — `Σ_L ‖P_L Φ‖² = 3 ‖Im Φ‖²`.
* `fanoProj_all_zero_iff` — all seven projections vanish iff `Im Φ = 0`.

## Zero-divisor annihilation: the requested claim does not hold

Embedding `Φ` into the sedenions as the octonion `(Φ, 0)`, we call `Φ`
*zero-divisor annihilated* if some non-zero sedenion `y` has `Φ y = 0` or `y Φ = 0`.

* `octNormSq_mul` — the octonion norm is multiplicative, so the octonions have no zero
  divisors (`Octonion.mul_eq_zero`).
* `zeroDivAnnihilated_iff` — a flux vector is zero-divisor annihilated **iff it is zero**.
* `annihilated_field_iff_zero` — hence a magnetic field whose flux is annihilated at every
  point is the vacuum field `B ≡ 0`.
* `annihilation_does_not_isolate_helical_equilibria` — the annihilation condition excludes
  every helical equilibrium with `B ≠ 0` somewhere (in particular the ABC field). It selects
  only the zero field, which has no helicity, so it cannot isolate helical equilibria.
* `splitAnnihilated_nontrivial`, `split_annihilated_field_iff_zero` — robustness check:
  splitting the flux across both sedenion halves does produce genuine zero divisors, yet
  3D field fluxes (on `e₁, e₂, e₃`) are still annihilated only when `B ≡ 0`.

Stability (tearing modes, turbulent disruptions) needs a linearised resistive-MHD
spectral theory that is not formalised here. The theorems above show that the proposed
selection criterion only admits the zero field. So in this formalisation it cannot imply
anything about the stability of non-trivial equilibria.
-/
/-! ## MHD equilibrium equations -/
/-- Gradient `∇p` of a scalar field. -/
/-- Static ideal-MHD equilibrium: `∇ · B = 0` and `(∇ × B) × B = ∇p` everywhere. -/
/-- Beltrami (force-free, helical) field with twist `λ`: `∇ × B = λ B`. -/
/-- Magnetic helicity density `B · (∇ × B)`. -/
/-- Every divergence-free Beltrami field is an MHD equilibrium with constant pressure. -/
/-- The ABC field is a helical MHD equilibrium with non-zero helicity. -/
/-! ## The Fano plane and the projection of the 8D flux -/
/-- An 8D magnetic flux vector, indexed like the octonion basis `e₀, …, e₇`. -/
/-- The seven lines of `PG(2, 2)` on the imaginary indices `1, …, 7`: `{i, j, i xor j}`. -/
/-- Any two distinct imaginary points lie on exactly one Fano line. -/
/-- Octonion basis element `e_i` over `ℤ`. -/
/-- Each Fano line is a quaternionic triple of the octonions. -/
/-- Projection of a flux vector onto the coordinates of a Fano line. -/
/-- Imaginary part of a flux vector (drop `e₀`). -/
/-- The seven Fano projections sum to three times the imaginary part. -/
/-- Energy identity: `Σ_L ‖P_L Φ‖² = 3 ‖Im Φ‖²`. -/
/-- All seven Fano projections vanish iff the imaginary part vanishes. -/
/-! ## Octonion norm and zero divisors -/
/-- Squared Euclidean norm of a real octonion. -/
/-- The octonion norm is multiplicative. -/
/-- The real octonions have no zero divisors. -/
/-! ## Zero-divisor annihilation of the flux -/
/-- The flux vector as a real octonion. -/
/-- The flux vector embedded in the sedenions (lower octonion half). -/
/-- `Φ` is annihilated by a non-zero sedenion from the left or the right. -/
/-- A flux vector is zero-divisor annihilated iff it is zero. -/
/-- The 8D flux of a 3D magnetic field value, placed on `e₁, e₂, e₃`. -/
/-- A field whose flux is annihilated at every point is the vacuum field. -/

/-- The annihilation criterion does not isolate helical equilibria: no field with `B ≠ 0`
somewhere is annihilated everywhere, while the ABC field is a helical equilibrium with
non-zero helicity. -/

/-! ## Robustness: an embedding that meets genuine sedenion zero divisors

The negative result above is not an artefact of hiding the flux inside one octonion half.
Below, the flux is split across both sedenion halves: `Φ₀…Φ₃ ↦ e₀…e₃` and
`Φ₄…Φ₇ ↦ e₈…e₁₁`.  With this embedding genuine zero divisors occur
(`splitAnnihilated_nontrivial`: `(e₁ + e₁₀)(e₄ − e₁₅) = 0`).  But the flux of a 3D
magnetic field sits on `e₁, e₂, e₃`, inside an octonion subalgebra, so the criterion
still admits only the vacuum field (`split_annihilated_field_iff_zero`).
-/
/-- The flux split across both sedenion halves: `Φ₀…Φ₃ ↦ e₀…e₃`, `Φ₄…Φ₇ ↦ e₈…e₁₁`. -/
/-- Zero-divisor annihilation for the split embedding. -/

/-- For the split embedding, a non-zero flux vector is annihilated by a non-zero sedenion:
`(e₁ + e₁₀)(e₄ − e₁₅) = 0`. -/

/-- On field fluxes (supported on `e₁, e₂, e₃`) the split embedding agrees with the
lower-half embedding. -/

/-- Even with the split embedding, a field whose flux is annihilated at every point is the
vacuum field. -/

/-!
# 16D sedenion Maxwell equations `D F = J`

**Setting.**  Spacetime is `ℝ⁴ = {(t, x₁, x₂, x₃)}`.  The field is `F = E + i B + M`, a
`C²` map into the complexified sedenions (`Fin 16 → ℂ`, see `SedenionMaxwellAlgebra`):
`E + i B` (`embEB`) sits on the quaternion units `e₁, e₂, e₃`, where `i` is the complex unit
and commutes with every sedenion unit.  The remaining 12 complex components on `e₄, …, e₁₅`
form the hidden field `M` (`IsHidden`).  The operator is
`D = -i ∂_t + e₁ ∂₁ + e₂ ∂₂ + e₃ ∂₃`, acting by left sedenion multiplication (`Dop`).

**Results.**

* `sedenion_maxwell_iff` — `D F = J_EM + J_M` holds at a point iff Maxwell's equations
  (`MaxwellAt`: `∇·E = ρ`, `∇·B = ρₘ`, `∇×E + ∂_t B = -jₘ`, `∇×B - ∂_t E = j`) hold there and
  the hidden sector satisfies `D M = J_M`.
* `fieldAssociator_eq_zero` — **the associator `[D, D, F] = (D D) F - D (D F)` is identically
  zero** for every `C²` sedenion field, even though the coefficients of `D` do not associate
  (`coefficient_associator_ne_zero`).  So every `C²` field lies in the associator kernel
  (`assocKernel_of_contDiff`).
* `associator_generates_no_monopole` — so the associator produces **no** magnetic charge.  The
  request's claim that `[D, D, F]` *generates* localized monopole charges is false in this
  formalisation.  Magnetic charge enters only through an explicit source `ρₘ` in `J`.
* `divS_curlS_eq_zero`, `monopole_charge_zero_of_smooth_potential`,
  `sedenion_monopole_needs_string` — if `B = ∇ × A` with a global `C²` potential (no Dirac
  string), then `ρₘ = 0`.  A non-zero monopole charge therefore always rules out a global
  string-free potential.
* `poynting_theorem` — `∂_t u + ∇·S = -j·E - jₘ·B` with `u = (|E|²+|B|²)/2`, `S = E × B`.
* `poynting_conservation_on_assocKernel` — for a `C²` solution of `D F = J` with
  current-free electromagnetic source, `F` is in the associator kernel and
  `∂_t u + ∇·S = 0` everywhere.
* `symmetrised_associator_outside_octHalf` — the cancellation depends on the 4D base: a
  derivative direction carrying a coefficient such as `e₁₀` would break it.
-/
/-- `embEB` as a continuous real-linear map. -/
/-- `D` maps hidden-sector fields to the hidden sector. -/
/-- Vectors supported on the quaternion units `e₀, …, e₃`. -/

/-- **The 16D sedenion Maxwell equation `D F = J` is exactly Maxwell's equations plus a
decoupled hidden-sector equation.**

Let `F = E + i B + M` with `M` in the hidden sector, and `J = J_EM + J_M` where `J_EM` is the
electromagnetic source (charges `ρ, ρₘ`, currents `j, jₘ`) and `J_M` is hidden.  Then
`D F = J` at `x` holds iff Maxwell's equations hold at `x` and `D M = J_M` at `x`. -/
/-! ## Magnetic monopoles, the associator and Dirac strings -/
/-- The magnetic-charge slot of a sedenion: `embSrc` stores `-ρₘ` as the `i e₀` coefficient. -/

/-- **The associator generates no magnetic charge.**  For every `C²` sedenion field, the
monopole component of `[D, D, F]` is zero (indeed the whole associator is zero). -/
/-- `∇ · (∇ × A) = 0` for a `C²` vector potential `A`. -/

/-- **A magnetic charge obstructs a smooth global vector potential.**  If `B = ∇ × A` everywhere
with `A` of class `C²` (no Dirac string or other singularity), then Maxwell's equations force the
magnetic charge density to vanish. -/

/-- **Sedenion form of the Dirac obstruction.**  If the sedenion field `F = E + i B + M` solves
`D F = J` at `x` with a non-zero magnetic charge `ρₘ` in the source, then `B` admits no global
`C²` vector potential: a localized monopole always needs a Dirac string (or patches). -/
/-! ## Poynting's theorem -/
/-- Electromagnetic energy density `u = (|E|² + |B|²) / 2`. -/
/-- Poynting vector `S = E × B`. -/

/-- **Poynting's theorem** `∂_t u + ∇ · S = -j · E - jₘ · B`, from the two curl equations of
Maxwell's system at the point `x`. -/

/-- **Poynting energy–momentum conservation on the associator kernel.**

Let `F = E + i B + M` be a `C²` sedenion field (`M` hidden) solving the sedenion Maxwell
equation `D F = J` everywhere with a current-free electromagnetic source (arbitrary electric and
magnetic charge densities `ρ, ρₘ`, zero currents) and an arbitrary hidden source `J_M`.  Then `F`
lies in the associator kernel, and the local conservation law `∂_t u + ∇ · S = 0` holds at every
point. -/
/-! ## Sanity checks: the cancellation is genuine -/

/-- The coefficients of `D` do **not** associate: `[e₁, e₂, e₄] = 2 e₇ ≠ 0`.  The vanishing of
`[D, D, F]` comes from the symmetry of `∂_μ ∂_ν` together with the octonionic (alternative)
nature of the coefficients, not from associativity. -/

/-- The cancellation needs the coefficients of `D` to lie in the octonion half.  For a
coefficient outside it, such as `e₁₀` (which a derivative along a 16-dimensional base would
need), the symmetrised associator is non-zero: `[e₁, e₁₀, e₄] + [e₁₀, e₁, e₄] = 2 e₁₅`. -/

/-!
# Algebraic layer for the sedenion Maxwell system

The field of the sedenion Maxwell system takes values in the *complexified* sedenions
`𝕊_ℂ = Sedenion ℂ` (four Cayley–Dickson doublings of `ℂ`, with the trivial conjugation on the
base).  The complex unit `i` therefore commutes with every sedenion unit `e₀, …, e₁₅`, which is
what makes the Riemann–Silberstein combination `E + i B` available.

For analysis it is convenient to work with the coordinate space `V16 = Fin 16 → ℂ`, a finite
dimensional real normed space.  `toSed` / `ofSed` convert between coordinates and the nested
Cayley–Dickson pairs (coordinate `k` is the coefficient of `e_k` in Cayley–Dickson bit order) and
`smul16 a b` is the sedenion product in coordinates.

Main algebraic facts:

* `smul16` is bi-additive and real-homogeneous in each variable (`smul16_add`, `add_smul16`,
  `smul16_smul`, …).
* `Sedenion.octHalf_assoc_symm` — if `a, b` lie in the octonion half `𝕆 ⊂ 𝕊` (second
  Cayley–Dickson component zero) then `[a, b, x] + [b, a, x] = 0` for **every** sedenion `x`,
  although the sedenions are not alternative.
* `assoc16_symm_of_octHalf` — the same statement in coordinates.
-/

/-- **Symmetrised associator on the octonion half.**  For `a = (p, 0)` and `b = (q, 0)` in the
octonion half of the sedenions and an arbitrary sedenion `x`,
`[a, b, x] + [b, a, x] = 0`.  (For general sedenions this fails: the sedenions are not
left alternative, `Sedenion.not_left_alternative`.)  The sixteen coordinate identities
`Sedenion.octHalf_assoc_symm_c00` … `_c15` are checked in four parallel modules. -/
/-- Coordinates of a complexified sedenion: `v k` is the coefficient of `e_k`. -/
/-- Coordinates → nested Cayley–Dickson pairs. -/
/-- Nested Cayley–Dickson pairs → coordinates. -/
/-- The sedenion product in coordinates. -/
/-- The sedenion associator `[a, b, c] = (a b) c - a (b c)` in coordinates. -/
/-- `a` lies in the octonion half `𝕆 = span(e₀, …, e₇)` of the sedenions. -/
/-- **Coordinate form of the symmetrised-associator identity.** -/
/-! ## Bilinearity of the coordinate product -/
/-- Scaling a sedenion by a complex number. -/
/-- Left multiplication by a fixed sedenion, as a continuous real-linear map. -/

/-!
# Calculus layer and the sedenion Dirac–Maxwell operator

Partial derivatives `pd` on spacetime `ℝ⁴`, the operator
`D = -i ∂_t + e₁ ∂₁ + e₂ ∂₂ + e₃ ∂₃` on complexified-sedenion fields (`Dop`), the operator
`(D D)` with pre-multiplied coefficients (`DDop`) and the associator
`[D, D, F] = (D D) F - D (D F)` (`fieldAssociator`).

* `fieldAssociator_eq_zero` — `[D, D, F] ≡ 0` for every `C²` field `F`.
* `D_embEB` — the algebraic expansion of `D (E + i B)`.
-/
/-- Spacetime points `(t, x₁, x₂, x₃)`; index `0` is time. -/
/-- Spatial vectors. -/
/-- Partial derivative `∂_μ F (x)` of a field with values in a real normed space. -/
/-! ## Calculus lemmas for `pd` -/
/-- Components of a partial derivative are partial derivatives of components. -/
/-- For a `C²` field, `∂_μ ∂_ν F` is the second Fréchet derivative applied to `e_μ, e_ν`. -/
/-- **Mixed partials commute** for `C²` fields (Schwarz). -/
/-! ## The sedenion Dirac–Maxwell operator and its associator -/
/-- The sedenion basis unit `e_k` in coordinates. -/
/-- Coefficients of `D = -i ∂_t + e₁ ∂₁ + e₂ ∂₂ + e₃ ∂₃` (with `i` the commuting complex unit). -/
/-- The first-order operator `D F = Σ_μ c_μ (∂_μ F)`, acting by left sedenion multiplication. -/

/-- The operator `(D D) F = Σ_{μ,ν} (c_μ c_ν) ∂_μ ∂_ν F`, i.e. the coefficients are multiplied
*first*. -/
/-- The operator associator `[D, D, F] = (D D) F - D (D F)`. -/

/-- **The associator `[D, D, F]` vanishes identically** for every `C²` sedenion field `F`.

The coefficients of `D` lie in the octonion half of the sedenions, where the symmetrised
associator vanishes (`assoc16_symm_of_octHalf`), while `∂_μ ∂_ν F` is symmetric in `μ, ν`. -/
/-- The *associator kernel*: fields on which `[D, D, F]` vanishes everywhere. -/
/-- Every `C²` sedenion field lies in the associator kernel. -/
/-! ## Encoding `F = E + i B + M` and the Maxwell equations -/

/-- The electromagnetic part `E + i B` of the sedenion field: the Riemann–Silberstein vector
placed on the imaginary quaternion units `e₁, e₂, e₃`. -/

/-- The *hidden sector*: sedenions with no component along the quaternion units
`e₀, e₁, e₂, e₃`.  The extra field `M` of `F = E + i B + M` takes values here
(12 complex components on `e₄, …, e₁₅`). -/

/-- The electromagnetic source: electric charge `ρ`, electric current `j`, magnetic charge `ρₘ`
and magnetic current `jₘ`. -/
/-- Spatial divergence `∇ · E` (space coordinates are indices `1, 2, 3` of `ST`). -/
/-- Spatial curl `∇ × E`. -/
/-- Time derivative `∂_t E`. -/

/-- Maxwell's equations at the point `x` (units `c = ε₀ = μ₀ = 1`), including possible magnetic
charge `ρₘ` and magnetic current `jₘ`. -/
/-- The purely algebraic content of `D (E + i B)`. -/

/-!
# Discrete sedenion Yang–Mills theory on a simplicial complex

This module extends `Sovereign.Physics.SedenionMaxwell` (the continuum sedenion Maxwell operator)
and `Sovereign.Analysis.SimplicialDEC` (discrete exterior calculus) to a *non-abelian*,
*non-associative* discrete gauge theory whose gauge "algebra" is the real sedenions `𝕊 = ℝ¹⁶`
with the commutator bracket `⁅a, b⁆ = a b - b a`.

## Model

* `rmul`, `rbr`, `rassoc` — the real sedenion product (the restriction of `smul16` to real
  coordinates), its commutator and its associator `[a, b, c] = (a b) c - a (b c)`.
* `Conn H` — gauge potentials (sedenion-valued 1-forms `A_μ`): one sedenion per oriented edge,
  with the `⋆₁`-weighted inner product.  `Curv H` — sedenion-valued 2-forms, `⋆₂`-weighted.
* `fieldStrengthWith br A = dA + br(A, A)` — the discrete field strength `F_{μν}` on each
  triangle `(a, b, c)`: `F = A_{bc} - A_{ac} + A_{ab} + br(A_{ab}, A_{bc})`, for an arbitrary
  bilinear bracket `br`.  `fieldStrength` is the sedenion case `br = ⁅·,·⁆`; `br = 0` is the
  abelian (Maxwell) theory.
* `covD A φ` — the covariant derivative `D_μ φ = ∂_μ φ + ⁅A_μ, φ⁆` of an adjoint scalar.
* `assocField A t = [A_{ab}, A_{bc}, F_t]` — the discrete associator `[D_μ, D_ν, F^{μν}]`
  (only the connection parts of the covariant derivatives can fail to associate).
* `ymEnergyWith br A = ‖F‖²_{⋆₂}` — the Yang–Mills energy; `hessian a = ‖d a‖²_{⋆₂}` — its
  quadratic fluctuation operator at the vacuum `A = 0` (the "mass matrix" of the gauge bosons).

## Results (what is and what is not true)

* `ymEnergy_nonneg`, `ymEnergy_eq_zero_iff` — energy positivity: `E(A) ≥ 0`, with equality iff
  `A` is flat (`F = 0`).
* `hessian_nonneg` — **no tachyons**: the fluctuation operator has no negative modes.
* `ymEnergyWith_smul` — `E(εA) = ε² ‖dA‖² + 2ε³⟪dA, br(A,A)⟫ + ε⁴ ‖br(A,A)‖²` for every bracket.
  Consequently `hessian_independent_of_bracket`: the quadratic (mass) term is the same for the
  sedenion theory and for the abelian Maxwell theory.
* `assocField_smul`, `assocField_no_quadratic_term` — the associator `[D, D, F]` is of order
  `ε³` in the fields, so it contributes **nothing** to the mass term.
  `assocField_ne_zero` shows that it is nevertheless not identically zero.
  `continuum_associator_mass_density_zero` — in the continuum model of `SedenionMaxwell` the
  associator vanishes identically, so it cannot produce a mass either.
* `hessian_gap` — on every finite complex there is `Δ > 0` with `‖d a‖² ≥ Δ ‖a‖²` for all `a`
  orthogonal to the zero modes.  This is a finite-dimensional linear-algebra fact; since the
  quadratic operator is bracket-independent, it holds equally for the free abelian theory.
* `hessian_pure_gauge`, `zero_modes_pure_gauge_of_H1Trivial` — the zero modes contain the pure
  gauge modes `D φ`; if `H¹(K) = 0` (topological certificate) they are exactly the pure gauge modes.
* `filledTriangle_hessian_eq` — explicit certificate on the filled triangle with `⋆₁ = 1`,
  `⋆₂ = s`: on the physical (non-zero-mode) sector `‖d a‖² = 3 s ‖a‖²`, so the gap is `3 s`.
  `filledTriangle_gap_not_uniform` — hence **no positive lower bound on the gap is uniform in
  the discretisation**: the discrete gap is a lattice artefact, not a continuum mass gap.

In particular, the associator does **not** generate a mass gap in this model, and nothing here
addresses the Yang–Mills existence and mass gap problem, confinement, or Landau poles.

/-- Real sedenions in coordinates (`a k` is the coefficient of `e_k`). -/
/-- Embedding of real sedenions into the complexified sedenions of `SedenionMaxwell`. -/

/-- The real sedenion product: the sedenion product `smul16` of `SedenionMaxwell` restricted to
real coordinates. -/
/-- The commutator bracket `⁅a, b⁆ = a b - b a` of the sedenions. -/

/-- The real sedenion basis unit `e_k`. -/
/-- The sedenion commutator as a real bilinear map. -/
/-- The sedenion gauge algebra is genuinely non-associative: `[e₁, e₂, e₄] = 2 e₇ ≠ 0`. -/
/-! ## Gauge fields on a simplicial complex -/
/-- Weights `⋆₀` on adjoint scalars (one real per vertex and sedenion direction). -/
/-- Weights `⋆₁` on gauge potentials. -/
/-- Weights `⋆₂` on field strengths. -/

/-- `dLin` is the exterior derivative `d₁` of `SimplicialDEC`, direction by direction. -/
/-- The quadratic part `br(A, A)` of the field strength. -/
/-- **Discrete field strength** `F = dA + br(A, A)` for a bilinear bracket `br`. -/
/-- The sedenion Yang–Mills field strength `F_{μν} = ∂_μ A_ν - ∂_ν A_μ + ⁅A_μ, A_ν⁆`. -/
/-- The covariant derivative `D_μ φ = ∂_μ φ + ⁅A_μ, φ⁆` of an adjoint scalar field. -/

/-- The discrete associator `[D_μ, D_ν, F^{μν}]` on a triangle: the associator of the two

/-- The Yang–Mills energy `E(A) = ‖F‖²_{⋆₂} = Σ_t ⋆₂(t) |F_t|²`. -/

/-- The quadratic fluctuation form at the vacuum `A = 0` (mass matrix of the gauge bosons). -/

/-- **No tachyon modes**: the fluctuation operator is positive semidefinite. -/

/-- **Weak-field expansion** of the Yang–Mills energy, for any bilinear bracket. -/
/-- The energy divided by `ε²` tends to the fluctuation form as `ε → 0`. -/

/-- The quadratic (mass) term of the energy does not depend on the bracket: the sedenion theory

/-- A finite-dimensional lower bound: a linear map is bounded below on the orthogonal
complement of its kernel. -/

/-- **Discrete spectral gap**: on every finite complex, the fluctuation operator is bounded
below by some `Δ > 0` on the orthogonal complement of its zero modes. -/

/-- Pure-gauge modes `D₀ φ = dφ` are zero modes of the fluctuation operator. -/

/-- **Topological certificate**: if `H¹(K) = 0` then every zero mode of the fluctuation

/-- The edge `(0, 1)` of the filled triangle. -/

/-- The unique triangle of the filled triangle. -/

/-- Characterisation of the physical sector on the filled triangle: `a ⊥ ker d` iff in every

/-- On the filled triangle the physical (non-zero-mode) sector has `‖d a‖² = 3 s ‖a‖²`. -/
/-- The physical sector on the filled triangle is non-trivial. -/
/-- With the unit Hodge star the discrete gap on the filled triangle is exactly `3`. -/

/-- **The discrete gap is not uniform in the discretisation**: for every `δ > 0` there is a

/-!
# SU(2) coherent states and the coherent vertex integrand (quaternionic model)

This file sets up the spin-`½` machinery behind coherent-state spin foam vertex amplitudes
(Livine–Speziale coherent intertwiners, Barrett et al. asymptotics), in a model where
everything is an explicit quaternion identity.

* `SU(2)` is the group of unit quaternions, acting on `ℂ² ≅ ℍ` (a right `ℂ`-vector space,
  `ℂ = span(1, i)`) by left multiplication; the invariant Hermitian inner product is
  `⟨u | v⟩ = cproj (u⋆ v)` where `cproj` is the projection `ℍ → ℂ = span(1,i)`.
* Directions `n ∈ S² ⊂ Im ℍ` are acted on by rotation `n ↦ g n g⋆`; a *coherent spinor* for `n`
  is a unit quaternion `w` with `w i w⋆ = n` (i.e. `w` is the Hopf lift of `n`; it is fixed by `n`
  up to a phase `w ↦ w e^{iα}`).
* Spin-`j` coherent states are the tensor powers `|n⟩^{⊗ 2j}`, so the spin-`j` coherent matrix
  element is the `2j`-th power of the spin-`½` one.  Spins are therefore stored as the natural
  numbers `k = 2j`.
* `coherentIntegrand w w' k g = ∏_{a<b} ⟨w'_{ab} | g_a⋆ g_b | w_{ba}⟩^{k_{ab}}` is the integrand
  of the `SU(2)` coherent `15j` vertex amplitude of a 4-simplex (five tetrahedra `a : Fin 5`,
  ten triangles `a < b`), as a function of the five group elements `g_a`.

Main results:
* `norm_coherentIntegrand_le` : `‖F(g)‖ ≤ 1` for all `g ∈ SU(2)⁵`;
* `norm_coherentIntegrand_eq_one_iff` (maximum principle): `‖F(g)‖ = 1` iff the rotated
  tetrahedra glue, `g_a⋆ g_b · n_{ba} = - n_{ab}` for every triangle with non-zero spin.
  These are the only points that survive in the large-spin limit (see `SpinFoamStateSum`).
-/
/-- The quaternion unit `i`, the reference direction `e₃` of the Hopf fibration. -/
/-- The projection `ℍ → ℂ = span(1, i)`. -/
/-- The `SU(2)`-invariant Hermitian inner product on `ℂ² ≅ ℍ`. -/
/-- A unit quaternion, i.e. an element of `SU(2)` (or a unit spinor). -/
/-- `w` is a (normalised) coherent spinor for the direction `n`: `w i w⋆ = n`. -/
/-- The spin-`½` rotation action of `g` on directions, `n ↦ g n g⋆`. -/

/-- The `SU(2)` coherent vertex integrand of a 4-simplex:
`∏_{a<b} ⟨w'_{ab} | g_a⋆ g_b | w_{ba}⟩^{k_{ab}}` with `k_{ab} = 2 j_{ab}`. -/
/-! ## Basic quaternion facts -/
/-- For a unit spinor, `|⟨w'|u⟩| ≤ 1`. -/
/-- A coherent spinor intertwines `i` with its direction: `n w = w i`. -/
/-- Two coherent spinors for the same direction have a pairing of modulus one. -/

/-- The spin-`½` pairing of a unit spinor `u` with a coherent spinor `w'` for `m` has modulus one
exactly when `u` is itself a coherent spinor for `m`. -/
/-- A product of numbers in `[0, 1]` equals one iff every factor does. -/
/-- The coherent vertex integrand is bounded by one on `SU(2)⁵`. -/

/-- **Maximum principle for the coherent vertex integrand.**  Let `n_{ab}` be the boundary data
(the 3d normal of triangle `ab` in the frame of tetrahedron `a`), `w_{ba}` coherent spinors for
`n_{ba}` and `w'_{ab}` coherent spinors for `-n_{ab}`.  Then `|F(g)| = 1` exactly when the five
rotated tetrahedra glue along every triangle carrying a non-zero spin:
`(g_a⋆ g_b) · n_{ba} = - n_{ab}`.  Everywhere else `|F(g)| < 1`, so the integrand `F(g)^λ` of
the amplitude at spins `λ j` is exponentially suppressed away from these critical points. -/
/-- The integrand at rescaled spins `λ k` is the `λ`-th power of the integrand at spins `k`. -/
/-- The integrand is multiplicative in the spins. -/
/-- Global `SU(2)` gauge invariance of the integrand: `F(h g) = F(g)` for every unit `h`. -/
/-- Every unit direction `m ∈ S² ⊂ Im ℍ` has a coherent spinor (surjectivity of the Hopf map). -/

/-- **Two parity-related critical points give a cosine.**  If two critical contributions have
unimodular prefactors `Z₊ Z₋` and differ only by the phases `e^{-i T₊}`, `e^{-i T₋}` of the two
spin factors, then at every rescaling `λ` of the spins their sum is
`2 e^{i λ φ} cos(λ (T₊ - T₋)/2)`, with `φ` independent of `λ`. -/
/-- The coherent vertex integrand is continuous in the group elements. -/

declarations.signature_heuristic:
structure EuclideanSimplex where
  /-- The vertices. -/
  P : Fin 5 → ℍ[ℝ]
  /-- The outward unit normal of the tetrahedron opposite vertex `a`. -/
  N : Fin 5 → ℍ[ℝ]
  affineIndependent : AffineIndependent ℝ P
  unit : ∀ a, IsUnitQ (N a)
  normal : ∀ a c d, c ≠ a → d ≠ a → qdot (N a) (P c - P d) = 0
  outward : ∀ a c, c ≠ a → 0 < qdot (N a) (P c - P a)

namespace EuclideanSimplex

variable (S : EuclideanSimplex)

declarations.name: norm_eprlIntegrand_eq_one_iff
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem norm_eprlIntegrand_eq_one_iff {w w' n : Fin 5 → Fin 5 → ℍ[ℝ]} {kp km : Fin 5 → Fin 5 → ℕ}
    {gp gm : Fin 5 → ℍ[ℝ]} (hw : ∀ a b, a ≠ b → IsCoherent (w a b) (n a b))
    (hw' : ∀ a b, a ≠ b → IsCoherent (w' a b) (-n a b))
    (hgp : ∀ a, IsUnitQ (gp a)) (hgm : ∀ a, IsUnitQ (gm a)) :
    ‖eprlIntegrand w w' kp km gp gm‖ = 1 ↔
      (∀ a b, a < b → kp a b ≠ 0 → rot (star (gp a) * gp b) (n b a) = -n a b) ∧
      (∀ a b, a < b → km a b ≠ 0 → rot (star (gm a) * gm b) (n b a) = -n a b)

declarations.name: eprl_euclidean_critical_sum
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem eprl_euclidean_critical_sum (S : EuclideanSimplex) {q : Fin 5 → ℍ[ℝ]}
    (hq : ∀ a, IsUnitQ (q a)) {w w' : Fin 5 → Fin 5 → ℍ[ℝ]}
    (hw : ∀ a b, a ≠ b → IsCoherent (w a b) (S.bdry q a b))
    (hw' : ∀ a b, a ≠ b → IsCoherent (w' a b) (-S.bdry q a b))
    (γ : ℝ) (kp km : Fin 5 → Fin 5 → ℕ)
    (hsimp : ∀ a b, (kp a b : ℝ) - km a b = γ * ((kp a b : ℝ) + km a b)) :
    ∃ φ : ℝ, ∀ l : ℕ,
      eprlIntegrand w w' (l • kp) (l • km) (S.selfDualLift q) q +
          eprlIntegrand w w' (l • kp) (l • km) q (S.selfDualLift q) =
        2 * Complex.exp ((l : ℂ) * φ * Complex.I) *

    (hw' : ∀ a b, a ≠ b → IsCoherent (w' a b) (-S.bdry q a b)) (k : Fin 5 → Fin 5 → ℕ) :

/-!
# The Euclidean EPRL vertex amplitude of a non-degenerate 4-simplex: critical points and phase

Spacetime `ℝ⁴` is identified with the quaternions `ℍ`, and `Spin(4) = SU(2) × SU(2)` acts by
`x ↦ p x q⋆` (the self-dual and anti-self-dual factors).

* `EuclideanSimplex` — a non-degenerate geometric 4-simplex: five affinely independent vertices
  `P a` together with the outward unit normals `N a` of its five boundary tetrahedra (tetrahedron
  `a` is the facet opposite vertex `a`).
* `angle a b = Θ_{ab} = arccos(N_a · N_b)` — the (exterior) dihedral angle at the triangle
  `ab = a ∩ b`; the interior dihedral angle is `π - Θ_{ab}` (`interiorAngle_eq`).
* `abs_cosAngle_lt_one` — non-degeneracy: two distinct facets are never parallel.
* Given a frame `q a ∈ SU(2)` for each tetrahedron, the rotation `(p a, q a)` with `p a = N a q a`
  (`selfDualLift`) maps the reference hyperplane `1^⊥ = Im ℍ` onto the hyperplane of
  tetrahedron `a`.  The Regge-like boundary data are the 3d outward normals of the triangles,
  `bdry q a b = p_a⋆ v_{ab} q_a ∈ S² ⊂ Im ℍ` (`v_{ab}` the 4d normal of triangle `ab` inside
  tetrahedron `a`).
* `glue_antiSelfDual`, `glue_selfDual` — both `g = q` and `g = p` are critical points
  (they glue the boundary data), the two lifts of the geometric 4-simplex.
* `coherentIntegrand_selfDual` — the key phase identity
  `F_k(p) = F_k(q) · exp(-i Σ_{a<b} k_{ab} Θ_{ab})`.
* `eprlIntegrand` — the Euclidean EPRL (Barbero–Immirzi parameter `γ < 1`) coherent integrand
  on `Spin(4)`: spins `j^± = (1 ± γ) j / 2` on the two factors (`k^± = 2 j^±`), boundary states
  `|n⟩_{j⁺} ⊗ |n⟩_{j⁻}`.  `eprlIntegrand_diag`: restricted to the diagonal `SU(2)` (the
  simplicity-constrained boundary), it is the spin-`j` `SU(2)` coherent integrand, `j = j⁺ + j⁻`.
* `eprl_euclidean_critical_sum` — **main theorem**: at spins `λ j` the two geometric (parity
  related) critical points `(p, q)` and `(q, p)` of the EPRL integrand contribute
  `2 e^{i λ φ} cos(λ S_Regge)` with `S_Regge = Σ_{a<b} γ j_{ab} Θ_{ab}` the Regge action of the
  4-simplex with triangle areas `γ j_{ab}`, and `φ` a phase independent of `λ`.
-/
/-- The Euclidean inner product of `ℝ⁴ ≅ ℍ`. -/

/-- A non-degenerate Euclidean 4-simplex in `ℝ⁴ ≅ ℍ`: five affinely independent vertices together
with the outward unit normals of the five boundary tetrahedra (tetrahedron `a` is the facet
opposite the vertex `P a`). -/
/-- The vertices. -/
/-- The outward unit normal of the tetrahedron opposite vertex `a`. -/
/-- `cos Θ_{ab} = N_a · N_b`. -/

/-- The (exterior) dihedral angle `Θ_{ab} ∈ [0, π]` between the outward normals of tetrahedra
`a` and `b`, at their common triangle. -/
/-- The interior dihedral angle of the 4-simplex at the triangle `ab`. -/

/-- The 4d unit normal `v_{ab}` of the triangle `ab` inside the tetrahedron `a`
(the normalised component of `N_b` orthogonal to `N_a`). -/
/-- The self-dual lift `p_a = N_a q_a`: the rotation `x ↦ p_a x q_a⋆` maps `1 ↦ N_a`. -/
/-- The boundary data: the 3d outward normal of triangle `ab` in the frame of tetrahedron `a`. -/
/-- The linear functional `x ↦ y · x`. -/

/-- **Non-degeneracy**: distinct boundary tetrahedra of a non-degenerate 4-simplex are never
parallel, `|N_a · N_b| < 1`. -/
/-- `s_{ab} · N_b⋆ v_{ba} = N_b⋆ N_a - cos Θ_{ab}`. -/
/-- `q = (q_a)` is a critical point: `(q_a⋆ q_b) · n_{ba} = -n_{ab}`. -/

/-- The transition `p_a⋆ p_b` is `q_a⋆ q_b` followed by a rotation by `2Θ_{ab}` about `n_{ba}`;
on a coherent spinor for `n_{ba}` this is the phase `e^{-iΘ_{ab}}`. -/
/-- `s_{ab} · v_{ba} N_b⋆ = N_a N_b⋆ - cos Θ_{ab}`. -/
/-- `p = (p_a)` is a critical point as well. -/
/-- **Phase identity at the two lifts.**  `F_k(p) = F_k(q) · exp(-i Σ_{a<b} k_{ab} Θ_{ab})`. -/
/-- The boundary normals are unit vectors of `Im ℍ = ℝ³`. -/
/-- Coherent boundary states exist: every boundary normal `± n_{ab}` has a coherent spinor. -/
/-- Both geometric lifts are critical points of maximal modulus: `|F_k(q)| = |F_k(p)| = 1`. -/

/-- The Regge action `Σ_{a<b} A_{ab} Θ_{ab}` of the 4-simplex with triangle areas `A_{ab}`,
written with the exterior dihedral angles `Θ_{ab}` (with the interior angles `θ = π - Θ` it is
`π Σ A - Σ A θ`, cf. `interiorAngle_eq`). -/

/-- An explicit non-degenerate Euclidean 4-simplex (so the hypotheses above are satisfiable): the
vertices `0, 1, i, j, k` of `ℍ`, with outward normals `(1+i+j+k)/2, -1, -i, -j, -k`. -/

/-- The Euclidean EPRL coherent vertex integrand (Barbero–Immirzi parameter `γ < 1`) on
`Spin(4) = SU(2)⁺ × SU(2)⁻`: the self-dual group elements `g⁺` carry the spins `j⁺ = k⁺/2`, the
anti-self-dual ones `g⁻` the spins `j⁻ = k⁻/2`, and the boundary states are the EPRL images
`|n⟩_{j⁺} ⊗ |n⟩_{j⁻}` of the `SU(2)` coherent states. -/

/-- **Simplicity / projection onto `SU(2)` boundary states.**  On the diagonal subgroup
`SU(2) ⊂ Spin(4)` (the stabiliser of the normal `1`, i.e. `g⁺ = g⁻`), the EPRL boundary state is the
`SU(2)` coherent state of spin `j = j⁺ + j⁻`. -/

/-- Maximum principle for the EPRL integrand: `|F| ≤ 1`, with equality exactly when both the
self-dual and the anti-self-dual group elements glue the boundary data. -/

/-- **Large-spin phase of the Euclidean EPRL amplitude at the geometric critical points.**

Let `S` be a non-degenerate Euclidean 4-simplex with Regge boundary data `n_{ab}` (for any choice
of tetrahedron frames `q` and of coherent spinors), and let the spins satisfy the EPRL simplicity
constraint `j⁺ - j⁻ = γ (j⁺ + j⁻)`, i.e. `j^± = (1 ± γ) j / 2` with `j = j⁺ + j⁻` the boundary
`SU(2)` spin.  The two geometric critical points of the EPRL integrand are the parity-related
`Spin(4)` lifts `(g⁺, g⁻) = (p, q)` and `(q, p)` of the 4-simplex.  At rescaled spins `λ j` their
contributions add up to

  `2 e^{i λ φ} cos(λ S_Regge)`,   `S_Regge = Σ_{a<b} γ j_{ab} Θ_{ab}`,

the Regge action of the 4-simplex with triangle areas `A_{ab} = γ j_{ab}`, with a phase `φ`
independent of `λ` (it depends only on the phase conventions of the boundary states). -/

/-- **Balanced (Barrett–Crane type) labels.**  For `j⁺ = j⁻` (the Barrett–Crane simplicity
constraint, `γ = 0` above) the two geometric critical points are in phase: their contributions
add up to `2 e^{i λ φ}` and no Regge oscillation survives. -/
