# The Lorentzian EPRL vertex amplitude: simplicity map and the two parity-related critical points

Minkowski space `ℝ^{1,3}` is modelled by `2 × 2` Hermitian matrices (`x ↦ x⁰ 1 + x⃗·σ⃗`, with
`det x` the Minkowski norm) and the Lorentz group by `SL(2, ℂ)` acting by `x ↦ X x X†`.

**Simplicity constraints / `Y_γ` map.**  An `SU(2)` spin `j` boundary state is sent to the lowest
`K = SU(2)` type of the `SL(2, ℂ)` principal series representation `(ρ, k) = (γ j, j)`.  In the
homogeneous-function realisation of the principal series, `Y_γ` sends the coherent state `ξ` to
`F_ξ(z) = ⟨z, z⟩^{i ρ/2 - 1 - j} ⟨ξ, z⟩^{2j}` (`yMap`); we prove it has the homogeneity of the
`(γ j, j)` representation (`yMap_homogeneous`) and is `SU(2)`-covariant (`yMap_unitary`), and that
the labels satisfy the (diagonal) simplicity constraint relating the two Casimirs
(`simplicity_casimir`).

**Vertex amplitude.**  In the spinor form of Barrett et al. the Lorentzian EPRL vertex amplitude of
a 4-simplex is an integral over `X ∈ SL(2,ℂ)⁵` and `z_{ab} ∈ ℂ²` of `∏_{a<b} P_{ab}` with
face factor (`lorentzFace`)

  `P_{ab} = ⟨J ξ_{ab}, Z_{ab}⟩^{2j} ⟨Z_{ba}, ξ_{ba}⟩^{2j} / (‖Z_{ab}‖ ‖Z_{ba}‖)^{2j}
           · exp(i γ j log (‖Z_{ba}‖² / ‖Z_{ab}‖²))`,   `Z_{ab} = X_a† z_{ab}`, `Z_{ba} = X_b† z_{ab}`.

**Boundary geometry.**  `LorentzianBoundary` records the `SL(2,ℂ)` frames `X_a` of the five
spacelike tetrahedra, whose time-oriented unit normals are `N_a = X_a X_a†`, with the
non-degeneracy condition that distinct normals are never equal (`N_a · N_b > 1`).
`boost a b = Θ_{ab} = arcosh(N_a · N_b)` is the rapidity between the normals (the magnitude of the
Lorentzian dihedral angle).  The boundary data are the 3d normals `n_{ab}` of the triangles in the
frame of each tetrahedron, and `J ξ_{ab}` resp. `ξ_{ab}` are the `∓ 1` eigenspinors of `n_{ab}`.

**Main result** (`eprl_lorentzian_critical_sum`).  The configuration `X` and its parity image
`X̃_a = (X_a†)⁻¹` (with the corresponding critical `z`) are related by
`P(X̃) = P(X) · exp(i γ Σ_{a<b} 2 j_{ab} Θ_{ab})`, so at spins `λ j` their contributions add up to
`2 |P(X)|^λ e^{iλφ} cos(λ S_Regge)` with `S_Regge = Σ_{a<b} γ j_{ab} Θ_{ab}` (areas `γ j`).
Moreover `|P(X)| = 1` (`norm_lorentzIntegrand_crit`): both are critical points of maximal
modulus.
-/
/-- `2 × 2` complex matrices. -/
/-- Spinors `ℂ²`. -/
/-- The `SU(2)`-invariant Hermitian inner product `⟨u, v⟩ = Σ ū_i v_i`. -/
/-- The squared norm `‖u‖²`. -/

/-- The Minkowski inner product of Hermitian matrices, `⟨A, B⟩ = ½ tr(adj A · B)`
(so that `⟨A, A⟩ = det A`). -/

/-- The boundary geometry of a Lorentzian 4-simplex with spacelike tetrahedra: `SL(2,ℂ)` frames
`X_a` (mapping the reference tetrahedron, with normal `1`, to tetrahedron `a`), such that distinct
time-oriented normals `N_a = X_a X_a†` are never equal: `N_a · N_b > 1`. -/
/-- The frames. -/
/-- The time-oriented unit normal `N_a = X_a X_a†` of tetrahedron `a`. -/
/-- `cosh Θ_{ab} = N_a · N_b`. -/
/-- The boost (Lorentzian dihedral) angle `Θ_{ab} = arcosh (N_a · N_b) > 0`. -/
/-- The unit spacelike normal `v_{ab}` of the triangle `ab` inside tetrahedron `a`. -/

/-- The boundary data: the normal of triangle `ab` in the frame of tetrahedron `a`,
`n_{ab} = X_a⁻¹ v_{ab} (X_a†)⁻¹`. -/
/-- The parity-reflected frames `X̃_a = (X_a†)⁻¹`. -/

/-- The face factor of the Lorentzian EPRL integrand with Barbero–Immirzi parameter `γ` and spin
`j = k/2`, as a function of `J ξ_{ab} = ζ`, `ξ_{ba} = ξ` and `Z_{ab}`, `Z_{ba}`. -/
/-- The Lorentzian EPRL vertex integrand `∏_{a<b} P_{ab}(X, z)`. -/
/-! ## Spinor norms -/
/-- Rescaling `Z_{ba}` by `r > 0` only changes the `γ`-phase of a face factor, by `e^{i γ k log r}`. -/
/-- The face factor at rescaled spin `λ k` is the `λ`-th power of the face factor at spin `k`. -/
/-! ## Geometry of the two critical points -/
/-- The critical spinor `z_{ab}` of the configuration `X`: `X_a† z_{ab} = J ξ_{ab}`. -/
/-- The critical spinor of the parity-reflected configuration `X̃`: `X̃_a† z̃_{ab} = J ξ_{ab}`. -/

/-- **The parity partner rescales `Z_{ba}` by `e^{Θ_{ab}}`.**  If `J ξ_{ab}` is the `-1`
eigenspinor of the boundary normal `n_{ab}`, then `X̃_b† z̃_{ab} = e^{Θ_{ab}} X_b† z_{ab}`. -/
/-! ## The critical points have maximal modulus -/
/-- Lagrange's identity on `ℂ²`: `|⟨u, w⟩|² + |u₀ w₁ - u₁ w₀|² = ‖u‖² ‖w‖²`. -/
/-- Two vectors killed by a non-zero `2 × 2` matrix are proportional. -/
/-- `n_{ab} ≠ 1`: the boundary normal is a genuine spatial direction. -/
/-- `X_b† z_{ab}` is a `+1` eigenspinor of `n_{ba}` at the critical point. -/
-- `N_a η = (c + s) N_b η`

/-- **The critical points have maximal modulus.**  If moreover `ξ_{ba}` is a unit `+1`
eigenspinor of `n_{ba}`, the integrand at the critical point `(X, z)` has modulus one. -/
/-! ## Existence of the coherent boundary spinors -/

/-- Polarisation of `adj A · A = det A`: for `2 × 2` matrices,
`adj A · B + adj B · A = tr(adj A · B) · 1`. -/
/-- The Minkowski product of two Hermitian matrices is real. -/
/-- A square root of the identity other than `-1` has a unit `+1` eigenspinor. -/
/-- The boundary normals square to the identity: `n_{ab}² = 1` (unit spatial vectors). -/

/-- **Coherent boundary spinors exist**: every boundary normal has unit `+1` and `-1`
eigenspinors (`ξ_{ab}` and `J ξ_{ab}`). -/

/-- **Phase relation between the two critical points.**  For boundary spinors `J ξ_{ab}` which are
`-1` eigenspinors of the boundary normals, the Lorentzian EPRL integrand at the parity-reflected
critical point `(X̃, z̃)` equals the integrand at `(X, z)` times `exp(i γ Σ_{a<b} 2 j_{ab} Θ_{ab})`. -/
/-- Two contributions differing by a relative phase `e^{iT}` add up to a cosine of `T/2`. -/
/-- The Regge action `Σ_{a<b} A_{ab} Θ_{ab}` with the boost angles `Θ_{ab}`. -/

/-- **Large-spin phase of the Lorentzian EPRL amplitude at the geometric critical points.**
At spins `λ j` (`k = 2j`), the two parity-related critical points `(X, z)` and `(X̃, z̃)` of the
Lorentzian EPRL integrand contribute

  `2 |P(X)|^λ e^{i λ φ} cos(λ S_Regge)`,   `S_Regge = Σ_{a<b} γ j_{ab} Θ_{ab}`,

the Lorentzian Regge action with triangle areas `γ j_{ab}` and boost angles `Θ_{ab}`, with `φ`
independent of `λ`.  (`norm_lorentzIntegrand_crit` shows `|P(X)| = 1`.) -/

/-- **Large-spin phase of the Lorentzian EPRL amplitude, unimodular form.**  With unit coherent
boundary spinors `ξ_{ab}` (`+1` eigenspinors of `n_{ab}`) and `J ξ_{ab}` (`-1` eigenspinors), the
two parity-related critical points contribute exactly `2 e^{iλφ} cos(λ S_Regge)` at spins `λ j`,
`S_Regge = Σ_{a<b} γ j_{ab} Θ_{ab}`. -/

/-!
# Discrete simplicity constraints and the EPRL map `Y_γ : SU(2) → SL(2, ℂ)`

In spin foam models the `BF` representations on each triangle are restricted by the discrete
simplicity constraints, which force the bivectors to be simple and (in the EPRL model) project
the representations of the 4d rotation group onto `SU(2)` boundary states.

**Lorentzian (`SL(2, ℂ)`).**  Principal series irreps are labelled by `(ρ, k)`, `ρ ∈ ℝ`,
`k ∈ ½ℕ`, with Casimirs `C₁ = k² - ρ² - 1` and `C₂ = ρ k`.
* EPRL: the `SU(2)` spin `j` is sent to `(ρ, k) = (γ j, j)` (`eprlLabel`), and the boundary state
  lives in the lowest `SU(2)` subspace `k = j`.  `simplicity_casimir` is the resulting (diagonal)
  quadratic simplicity constraint `(1 - γ²) C₂ = γ (C₁ + 1)`.
* Barrett–Crane: simple representations `k = 0`, i.e. `C₂ = 0` (`bc_casimir`).
* `yMap γ k ξ` realises `Y_γ` on coherent states in the homogeneous-function model of the
  principal series: `F_ξ(z) = ‖z‖^{2(iρ/2 - 1 - j)} ⟨ξ, z⟩^{2j}` with `ρ = γ j`.  We prove it lies in
  the `(γ j, j)` representation (`yMap_homogeneous`) and that `Y_γ` is `SU(2)`-equivariant
  (`yMap_unitary`), so it embeds the `SU(2)` boundary state as the lowest `K`-type.

**Euclidean (`Spin(4) = SU(2) × SU(2)`).**  Irreps `(j⁺, j⁻)`.
* EPRL (`0 < γ < 1`): `j^± = (1 ± γ) j / 2` (`eprl_euclidean_labels`), so that the boundary spin is
  `j = j⁺ + j⁻` — the top component of `V_{j⁺} ⊗ V_{j⁻}` onto which the boundary state projects
  (see `eprlIntegrand_diag` in `SpinFoamEuclidean`).
* Barrett–Crane: balanced representations `j⁺ = j⁻`.
-/
/-! ## Lorentzian labels -/
/-- The first Casimir of the `SL(2,ℂ)` principal series `(ρ, k)`. -/
/-- The second Casimir of the `SL(2,ℂ)` principal series `(ρ, k)`. -/
/-- The EPRL (Lorentzian) simplicity map on labels: `j ↦ (ρ, k) = (γ j, j)`. -/

/-- **Quadratic simplicity constraint** satisfied by the EPRL labels:
`(1 - γ²) C₂ = γ (C₁ + 1)`. -/

/-- Conversely, for `γ > 0` the linear relation `ρ = γ k` is the only solution of the quadratic
constraint with `ρ, k ≥ 0`. -/
/-- Barrett–Crane simple representations `(ρ, 0)` have vanishing second Casimir. -/
/-! ## Euclidean labels -/

/-- **Euclidean EPRL labels** (`γ < 1`): the constraint `k⁺ - k⁻ = γ (k⁺ + k⁻)` used in
`eprl_euclidean_critical_sum` is equivalent to `j^± = (1 ± γ) j / 2` with `j = j⁺ + j⁻`. -/
/-- Barrett–Crane balanced labels `j⁺ = j⁻` are the `γ = 0` case of the constraint. -/
/-! ## The `Y_γ` map on coherent states -/

/-- `Y_γ` on a coherent state `ξ` of spin `j = k/2`, as a homogeneous function on `ℂ² ∖ 0`:
`F_ξ(z) = ‖z‖^{2(iρ/2 - 1 - j)} ⟨ξ, z⟩^{2j}` with `ρ = γ j`. -/

/-- **`Y_γ ξ` lies in the principal series representation `(ρ, k) = (γ j, j)`**: it is homogeneous,
`F(λ z) = |λ|^{2(iρ/2 - 1 - j)} λ^{2j} F(z) = λ^{-1 + iρ/2 + j} λ̄^{-1 + iρ/2 - j} F(z)`. -/

/-- **`Y_γ` is `SU(2)`-equivariant**: rotating the coherent state by `U ∈ SU(2)` is the same as
acting with `U` on the homogeneous function, `F_{Uξ}(U z) = F_ξ(z)`. -/

declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem eprl_amplitude_localizes (μ : Measure Spin4Config) [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {w w' n : Fin 5 → Fin 5 → ℍ[ℝ]} (hw : ∀ a b, a ≠ b → IsCoherent (w a b) (n a b))
    (hw' : ∀ a b, a ≠ b → IsCoherent (w' a b) (-n a b)) (kp km : Fin 5 → Fin 5 → ℕ)
    {U : Set Spin4Config} (hU : IsOpen U)
    (hcrit : ∀ g : Spin4Config,
      (∀ a b, a < b → kp a b ≠ 0 → rot (star (g.plus a) * g.plus b) (n b a) = -n a b) →
      (∀ a b, a < b → km a b ≠ 0 → rot (star (g.minus a) * g.minus b) (n b a) = -n a b) →
      g ∈ U) :
    ∃ q : ℝ, 0 ≤ q ∧ q < 1 ∧ ∀ l : ℕ,
      ‖eprlAmplitude μ w w' kp km l -
          ∫ g in U, eprlIntegrand w w' (l • kp) (l • km) g.plus g.minus ∂μ‖ ≤
        q ^ l * μ.real Uᶜ

declarations.name: eprl_euclidean_large_spin
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem eprl_euclidean_large_spin (S : EuclideanSimplex) {q : Fin 5 → ℍ[ℝ]}
    (hq : ∀ a, IsUnitQ (q a)) {w w' : Fin 5 → Fin 5 → ℍ[ℝ]}
    (hw : ∀ a b, a ≠ b → IsCoherent (w a b) (S.bdry q a b))
    (hw' : ∀ a b, a ≠ b → IsCoherent (w' a b) (-S.bdry q a b))
    (γ : ℝ) (kp km : Fin 5 → Fin 5 → ℕ)
    (hsimp : ∀ a b, (kp a b : ℝ) - km a b = γ * ((kp a b : ℝ) + km a b)) :
    ‖eprlIntegrand w w' kp km (S.selfDualLift q) q‖ = 1 ∧
    ‖eprlIntegrand w w' kp km q (S.selfDualLift q)‖ = 1 ∧
    (∃ φ : ℝ, ∀ l : ℕ,
      eprlIntegrand w w' (l • kp) (l • km) (S.selfDualLift q) q +
          eprlIntegrand w w' (l • kp) (l • km) q (S.selfDualLift q) =
        2 * Complex.exp ((l : ℂ) * φ * Complex.I) *
          (Real.cos (l * S.reggeAction (fun a b => γ * (((kp a b : ℝ) + km a b) / 2))) : ℂ)) ∧
    ∀ (μ : Measure Spin4Config) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (U : Set Spin4Config), IsOpen U →
      (∀ g : Spin4Config,
        (∀ a b, a < b → kp a b ≠ 0 →
          rot (star (g.plus a) * g.plus b) (S.bdry q b a) = -S.bdry q a b) →
        (∀ a b, a < b → km a b ≠ 0 →
          rot (star (g.minus a) * g.minus b) (S.bdry q b a) = -S.bdry q a b) → g ∈ U) →
      ∃ r : ℝ, 0 ≤ r ∧ r < 1 ∧ ∀ l : ℕ,
        ‖eprlAmplitude μ w w' kp km l -
            ∫ g in U, eprlIntegrand w w' (l • kp) (l • km) g.plus g.minus ∂μ‖ ≤
          r ^ l * μ.real Uᶜ

/-!
# Spin foam state sums on simplicial 4-complexes, and localisation of the vertex amplitude

This module places the vertex amplitudes of `SpinFoamEuclidean` / `SpinFoamLorentzian` on the
simplicial spacetimes of `Sovereign.Analysis.SimplicialDEC4`.

* Spins are discrete 2-forms: a (twice-)spin labelling is a cochain `k : K.Form 2 ℕ` on the
  triangles of the complex `K`.  `pairFace σ h` is the triangle of the 4-simplex `σ` shared by its
  boundary tetrahedra `a ≠ b` (the face opposite the vertices `a`, `b`), and `localSpins k σ` are
  the ten spins `k_{ab}` seen by the vertex amplitude of `σ`.
* `stateSum K Λ A_f A_v = Σ_{k ≤ Λ} ∏_triangles A_f(k_t) ∏_{4-simplices} A_v(σ, k|_σ)` is the spin
  foam state sum (with spin cut-off `Λ`), for any face and vertex amplitudes; `su2FaceAmp`,
  `spin4FaceAmp` and `bcFaceAmp` are the `SU(2)`, `Spin(4)` (EPRL) and Barrett–Crane face

/-!
# The invariant topological attractor of the acoustic–optical cavity

The attractor tube of `closedLoop_convergence` is a *topological* attractor: on it the acoustic
trap field and the optical hologram carry fixed topological charges, and the acoustic trap
potential keeps an energy barrier (hence a levitation trap).

* `modeField u c`: the field along a closed probe loop synthesised from the modal amplitudes
  `c` and the mode shapes `u j : C(I, ℂ)` restricted to the loop.
* `windingNumber_modeField_eq`: Rouché locking — modal amplitudes within `d` of a reference
  whose field stays at modulus `≥ μ > d Σ ‖u j‖` give the same winding number.
* `windingNumber_modeField_const`: along a continuous, non-singular modulation `c(τ)` the charge
  of the target field is constant in time.
* `ProbeLoops`: the acoustic and optical probe loops (mode shapes) together with the
  non-singularity of the modulated targets; `acousticCharge`, `opticalCharge`: the target
  charges.
* **`charge_locked`**: every state in the attractor tube at any frame has acoustic trap field
  of charge `acousticCharge` and optical hologram field of charge `opticalCharge`.
* `TrapCalibration`: the acoustic trap potential (Gor'kov potential of the modal field) with a
  local Lipschitz calibration and an energy barrier with margin along the modulation.
* **`trap_locked`**: every state in the attractor tube has a `TrapBarrier`, hence a levitation
  trap (a local minimum of the potential) inside the certificate ball.
-/
/-! ## Fields synthesised from modal amplitudes -/
/-- The field `Σⱼ cⱼ uⱼ` along the probe loop. -/
/-- **Rouché locking of the topological charge** of a modal field. -/

/-- **Charge conservation along a non-singular modulation**: if the modal amplitudes `c τ`
depend continuously on time and the synthesised field never vanishes on the probe loop, the
charge at time `τ` equals the charge at time `0`. -/
/-! ## Probe loops and the charges of the attractor -/
/-- Lipschitz modulations are continuous. -/

/-- The acoustic and optical probe loops of the cavity: mode shapes restricted to two closed
loops (around the acoustic vortex trap, resp. across the camera), and the non-singularity of the
modulated targets on these loops (field modulus `≥ μ > 0` at all times). -/
/-- The topological charge of the modulated acoustic trap target. -/
/-- The topological charge of the modulated optical hologram target. -/
/-- The target charges do not change during the modulation. -/
/-- The acoustic trap field on the acoustic probe loop. -/
/-- The optical hologram field on the optical probe loop. -/

/-- The admissible attractor levels for the probe loops: small enough that Rouché locking
applies to both fields. -/

/-- **Topological locking in the attractor.** For an admissible level `ρ`, every state in the
attractor tube at any frame has a nonvanishing acoustic trap field and optical hologram field on
the probe loops, whose charges are the target charges. -/
/-! ## The acoustic trap potential -/

/-- Calibration of the acoustic trap potential `U m : Space3 → ℝ` produced by modal amplitudes
`m` (e.g. the Gor'kov potential of the synthesised pressure field) near the modulated target:
continuity, a local Lipschitz bound of size `Λ` for amplitude deviations up to `tol`, and an
energy barrier of level `b` with margin `η` around `center` at all times of the modulation. -/
/-- The attractor levels for which the trap calibration applies. -/

/-- **Trap locking in the attractor**: every state in the attractor tube produces a trap
potential with an energy barrier around the certificate centre, hence a levitation trap (a
local minimum inside the certificate ball). -/

/-!
# Closed-loop tools: tracking contractions, Rouché stability of charges, robust traps

Three general facts used by the hardware-in-the-loop cavity model.

* **Tracking contractions** (`tracking_bound`, `tracking_invariant`, `tracking_entry`): an
  error signal obeying the frame-to-frame recursion `e (k+1) ≤ q e k + β` (`0 ≤ q < 1`)
  satisfies `e k ≤ s + q^k (e 0 - s)` with `s = β / (1 - q)`; every level `ρ ≥ s` is forward
  invariant; and every level `ρ > s` is entered after a number of frames `K` that depends only
  on `q`, `β`, `ρ` and a bound `R` on the initial error — not on the particular trajectory.
* **Rouché stability of the winding number** (`windingNumber_eq_of_norm_sub_lt`): two closed
  loops with `|f - g| < |g|` pointwise have the same winding number.
* **Robust traps** (`TrapBarrier.of_uniform_approx`): a potential uniformly `η`-close on the
  closed ball to a potential with an `η`-margin energy barrier has an energy barrier itself.
-/
/-! ## Tracking contractions -/
/-- **Discrete Grönwall bound for a tracking contraction.** -/
/-- **Invariance of the attractor tube**: every level `ρ ≥ β / (1 - q)` is forward invariant. -/

/-- **Uniform bounded-time entry**: for every level `ρ > β / (1 - q)` and every initial bound
`R`, there is a number of frames `K` such that *every* error signal obeying the recursion with
`e 0 ≤ R` is below `ρ` from frame `K` on. -/
/-! ## Rouché stability of the topological charge -/

/-- **Rouché stability of the winding number**: if `|f t - g t| < |g t|` along two closed loops,
their winding numbers agree. -/
/-! ## Robust energy barriers -/

/-- **Robust trap**: if the reference potential `U₀` has an energy barrier of level `b` with
margin `η` (`U₀ c + η < b` and `b + η ≤ U₀` on the sphere) and `U` is continuous and uniformly
`η`-close to `U₀` on the closed ball, then `U` has an energy barrier of level `b`. -/

/-!
# The hardware-in-the-loop acoustic–optical resonant cavity

We model, in the modal coordinates of a resonant cavity with `n` coupled acoustic/optical
modes, a real-time feedback loop between a phased acoustic transducer array and a laser
interferometric camera.

**Hardware** (`CavityHardware n`):
* `χ j ≠ 0`: the complex resonant susceptibility of mode `j` at the drive frequency; the
  transducer drive phasor `d j` excites the acoustic mode amplitude `m j = χ j d j`;
* `κ ≠ 0`: the acousto-optic coupling: the sound field imprints the phase/amplitude pattern
  `κ m` on the laser beam, so the optical field seen by the camera is `o = h + κ m` where `h`
  is the programmed optical phase hologram (spatial light modulator);
* `ref ≠ 0`: the reference beam of the interferometric camera, which records the four
  phase-stepped frames `fourStepFrames ref (o j)` per mode (plus bounded noise);
* loop gains `0 < gA, gO ≤ 1` and the frame period `Δt > 0`.

**One frame of the loop** (`CavityHardware.step`), at the frame time `tₖ = k Δt`:
1. the camera records the noisy frames and the optical field `ô` is reconstructed
   (`measured`, four-step phase retrieval);
2. the acoustic field is read *optically*: `m̂ = (ô - h) / κ` (`acousticEstimate`);
3. the transducer drive is corrected towards the modulated acoustic target
   `d ← d + gA (A⋆(tₖ) - m̂) / χ`, and the hologram towards the optical target
   `h ← h + gO (O⋆(tₖ) - ô)`.

The acoustic and optical loops are coupled twice: the acoustic loop is closed through the
optical measurement, and every change of the sound field changes the optical field.

**Continuous dynamic phase modulation** (`PhaseModulation n`): the targets `A⋆(t), O⋆(t)` move
continuously with bounded rates `VA, VO` (Lipschitz in time), for instance by modulating the
transducer phases (`PhaseModulation.ofPhases`).

* `errA_step`, `errO_step`: exact frame-to-frame error dynamics of the coupled loop.
* `lyap_step`: the coupled Lyapunov function `V = |eO| + 2|κ| |eA|` contracts:
  `V (k+1) ≤ q V k + β` with `q = max (1 - gO) (1 - gA / 2) < 1` and
  `β = (gO + 3 gA) ν / |ref| + VO Δt + 2 |κ| VA Δt` (camera noise `ν`, modulation rates).
* **`closedLoop_convergence`**: every level `ρ > β / (1 - q)` defines a forward-invariant
  attractor tube, entered by all runs starting in `V ≤ R` within a bounded time `T`
  that does not depend on the run or on the noise realisation.

/-!
# Laser interferometric camera frames: four-step phase-shifting interferometry

A laser interferometric camera does not see the complex optical field `o` at a pixel directly:
it records real intensities `|r e^{iδ} + o|²` of the object field superposed with a reference
beam `r` whose phase is stepped by `δ = 0, π/2, π, 3π/2`.

* `fourStepFrames r o : Fin 4 → ℝ`: the four camera frames at one pixel.
* `retrieve r I`: the classical four-step reconstruction
  `o = r ((I₀ - I₂) + i (I₁ - I₃)) / (4 |r|²)`.
* `retrieve_fourStep`: exact recovery of the complex field (amplitude **and** phase) from the
  four real frames whenever the reference beam is on (`r ≠ 0`).
* `retrieve_add`, `norm_retrieve_le`, `norm_retrieve_noisy_sub_le`: the reconstruction is
  linear, and camera noise of size `ν` per frame produces a field error at most `ν / |r|`.
-/
/-- The four phase-stepped camera frames `Iₖ = |r iᵏ + o|²` (reference phase `k π / 2`). -/
/-- Four-step phase retrieval `r ((I₀ - I₂) + i (I₁ - I₃)) / (4 |r|²)`. -/
/-- The frame differences measure `4 r̄ o`. -/
/-- **Exact phase retrieval**: the four camera frames determine the complex field. -/
/-- The reconstruction is additive in the frames. -/
/-- Frame noise of size `ν` gives a reconstruction of size at most `ν / |r|`. -/

/-- **Noisy phase retrieval**: from noisy camera frames `Iₖ + ηₖ` with `|ηₖ| ≤ ν`, the
reconstructed field is within `ν / |r|` of the true field. -/

/-!
# The acoustic–optical cavity stability certificate and its compiler

A `CavityExperiment n d` bundles everything the real-time pipeline is given:
the cavity hardware (transducer array, acousto-optic coupling, interferometric camera, loop
gains, frame period), the continuous dynamic phase modulation of the targets, the acoustic and
optical probe loops, the calibration of the acoustic trap potential, the camera noise bound
`ν`, a bound `R` on the initial Lyapunov function, and the synesthetic cavity geometry with its
acoustic/optical resonance mode pair (`Sovereign.Taxonomy.SynestheticResonance`).

A `CavityStabilityCertificate X` is a Lean term containing
* a convergence time `T ≥ 0`, an attractor level `ρ ≥ 0`, two integer charges and the
  synesthetic resonance fingerprint of the cavity;
* proofs that every closed-loop run (every noise realisation, every admissible initial state)
  is in the attractor tube from time `T` on, that the tube is forward invariant, that on the
  tube the acoustic trap field and optical hologram have the recorded charges, that the trap
  potential keeps an energy barrier (`Sovereign.Taxonomy.TrapBarrier`) and hence a levitation
  trap, and that the fingerprint is the measured, checkable `SynestheticCertificate`.

Results:
* `CavityExperiment.Budget ρ`: the stability budget — `ρ` exceeds the steady-state
  disturbance level `β / (1 - q)` and is small enough for charge and trap locking.
* `CavityExperiment.compile`: **the certificate compiler**: turns a budget into a certificate.
* **`cavity_stability`**: the end-to-end theorem.
* **`CavityStabilityCertificate.immutable`**: the content of a certificate (charges and
  fingerprint) is uniquely determined by the experiment: all certificates agree, and the
  charges are the charges of the modulated targets.
* `CavityStabilityCertificate.realtime_readout`: in the attractor, the discrete winding numbers
  computed from finitely many samples of the fields reproduce the certified charges.

The `#guard_msgs` checks at the end make the build fail unless the main theorems depend only
on the standard axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.
-/
/-- A hardware-in-the-loop acoustic–optical experiment. -/
/-- camera noise bound -/
/-- bound on the initial Lyapunov function -/
/-- the synesthetic cavity geometry -/
/-- the acoustic/optical resonance mode pair of the cavity -/
/-- The attractor tube of level `ρ`. -/
/-- The **stability budget** for the attractor level `ρ`. -/
/-- The **acoustic–optical cavity stability certificate**. -/
/-- convergence time -/
/-- attractor level -/
/-- topological charge of the acoustic trap on the attractor -/
/-- topological charge of the optical hologram on the attractor -/
/-- synesthetic resonance fingerprint of the cavity -/
/-- bounded-time convergence of every closed-loop run -/
/-- forward invariance of the attractor -/
/-- the acoustic trap charge is locked on the attractor -/
/-- the optical hologram charge is locked on the attractor -/
/-- the acoustic trap potential keeps its energy barrier on the attractor -/
/-- the fingerprint is the measured synesthetic certificate of the cavity modes -/
/-- **The certificate compiler**: from a stability budget, produce the certificate. -/
/-- The state realising the targets exactly at frame `k`. -/
/-- The certified acoustic charge is the charge of the modulated acoustic target. -/
/-- The certified optical charge is the charge of the modulated optical target. -/

/-- **Immutability**: the physical content of a cavity stability certificate — both
topological charges and the synesthetic fingerprint — is uniquely determined by the
experiment; any two certificates agree on it. -/
/-- The fingerprint passes the Boolean checker and decodes to the cavity mode pair. -/

/-- On the attractor the trap potential has a levitation trap: a local minimum inside the
certificate ball. -/
/-- Discrete readout of the charge of a nonvanishing closed loop from exact samples. -/

/-- **Real-time charge readout**: for a state in the attractor, the discrete winding numbers
computed from `N` samples of the acoustic trap field and of the optical hologram field along
the probe loops equal the certified charges for all sufficiently fine samplings. -/

/-- **End-to-end acoustic–optical cavity stability theorem.** For every hardware-in-the-loop
experiment whose stability budget holds at level `ρ`, the pipeline outputs a certificate
`c = X.compile hB` such that, with the convergence time `T = c.T`:

* (**bounded-time convergence**) every closed-loop run — for every camera noise realisation
  bounded by `ν` and every initial state with Lyapunov function `≤ R` — is in the attractor
  tube of level `ρ` at every frame time `tₖ ≥ T`, and the tube is forward invariant;
* (**topological attractor**) on the tube, the acoustic trap field and the optical hologram
  field are nonvanishing on the probe loops with winding numbers equal to the (time-independent)
  charges of the modulated targets;
* (**trap stability**) on the tube, the acoustic trap potential has an energy barrier around
  the certificate centre and hence a levitation trap;
* (**synesthetic fingerprint**) the certificate carries the measured resonance fingerprint of
  the cavity mode pair, which passes the Boolean checker. -/

/-!
# Discrete quantization of sampled phase loops

A nonvanishing continuous loop `f : [0, 1] → ℂ \ {0}` is sampled at the instants `k / N`
(`sampleTime`), possibly with measurement noise. The **discrete phase sum**
`∑ₖ arg (w (k+1) / w k)` of the samples `w` is the discrete analogue of `∮ dθ`, and the
**discrete winding number** is this sum in units of `2π`.

* `discretePhaseSum_eq_of_samples`: if `m > 0` bounds `|f|` from below and the sensor error is
  at most `ε` with `4 ε ≤ m`, then for all sufficiently fine samplings the discrete phase sum is
  *exactly* `2π · windingNumber f` (no rounding, no reconstruction loss).
* `exists_quantization_tolerance`: every such loop admits a positive tolerance and resolution.
* `windingNumber_eq_iff_loopHomotopic`: the winding number is a complete invariant of free
  homotopy classes of loops in `ℂ \ {0}`; `windingNumber_standardLoop`: every integer occurs.
-/

/-- The `k`-th of `N` equally spaced sampling instants `k / N` of the parameter interval
`[0, 1]` (clamped to `[0, 1]`). -/

/-- The **discrete phase sum** of a finite sample sequence `w 0, …, w N`: the sum of the
principal phase increments `arg (w (k+1) / w k)`. -/

/-- The **discrete winding number** of a sample sequence: the discrete phase sum in units of
`2π`, rounded to the nearest integer. -/
/-- A nonvanishing continuous loop has a positive lower bound on its modulus. -/

/-- Two loops are **freely homotopic in the punctured plane** if they are joined by a continuous
family of closed loops none of which passes through `0`. -/
/-- The standard loop `t ↦ e^{2πi n t}` winding `n` times around the origin. -/

/-!
# The `E₈` lattice organism state engine and the harmonic mitosis theorem

This file extends `RequestProject.Roots240D8` (the 240 roots of `E₈`),
`Sovereign.Taxonomy.SynestheticResonance` (synesthetic cavities and their resonance points) and
`Sovereign.Pipeline` (through `SpacetimeStreams` and the negentropy bookkeeping of
`Sovereign.Pipeline.Negentropy`).

## Model

A digital multi-agent organism lives in the Euclidean space `ℝ⁸ ⊇ E₈` (`E8Space`). It is a
finite `Population` of agents, each carrying a mass (its share of the organism) and a position.

* **Riemannian centroid.** On a metric space the Fréchet functional of a population is
  `F(x) = ∑ᵢ mᵢ d(x, pᵢ)²` (`frechet`), and a Riemannian (Fréchet–Karcher) centroid is a
  minimiser of `F` (`IsRiemannianCentroid`). In the flat space `ℝ⁸` we prove the
  variance decomposition `F(x) = F(c) + M ‖x - c‖²` for the weighted mean `c` (`centroid`,
  `frechet_eq_energy_add`), so the weighted mean is *the* (unique) Riemannian centroid
  (`isRiemannianCentroid_iff`). The **energy** of the population is `F(c)`, its Fréchet variance
  about the centroid.
* **Harmonic mitosis.** In generation `k` every agent of mass `m` at `p` splits into two
  daughters of mass `m / 2` at `p ± δₖ r`, where `r` is an `E₈` root chosen by a steering map
  (`mitosis`). The daughters are placed symmetrically about the mother, which is the collective
  coherence mechanism: all generations *share* one Riemannian centroid.
* **State engine.** `OrganismEngine` bundles, for every generation, a sensory feed (a
  distribution on a finite sensory alphabet), a quantizer transmuting it onto the 240-letter
  root alphabet, a steering map and the mitosis step size. `OrganismEngine.run` iterates the
  step, updating the population by mitosis and accumulating the negentropy `ΔS` of each
  transmutation.

## Results

* `run_mass`, `run_centroid`, `run_isRiemannianCentroid`: mass and the shared Riemannian
  centroid are invariant along the whole run.
* `run_energy`: exact energy law `Eₙ = E₀ + 2 M ∑_{k<n} δₖ²` (roots have squared length 2).
* `energy_bounded_of_summable`: for a square-summable schedule the energy is bounded
  (non-divergent) and converges; `harmonic_mitosis`: for the harmonic schedule `δₖ = 1/(k+1)`,
  `Eₙ ≤ E₀ + M π² / 3` for all `n`, and every agent stays within this energy of the centroid.
* `constant_mitosis_diverges`: with a constant step (e.g. staying on the lattice itself) the
  energy diverges, so the square-summable schedule is essential.
* `run_negentropy`, `run_negentropy_mono`: the negentropy is the sum of the gains `ΔS ≥ 0`.
* `resonanceFeed`: the uniform sensory feed on the resonance points of an 8-dimensional
  synesthetic cavity; `log_240_lt_resonanceFeed_shannon`: it always has entropy
  `> log 240` (there are at least `2⁸ = 256` resonance points), so
  `resonanceFeed_transmutation`: *any* transmutation onto the `E₈` roots yields
  `ΔS ≥ log (256/240) > 0`.
* `harmonic_mitosis_integrity`: the combined theorem for an organism fed by a synesthetic cavity
  and dividing harmonically — shared Riemannian centroid, energy bound `E₀ + M π² / 3`, internal
  entropy at most `log 240`, and strictly positive negentropy production
  `ΔS ≥ log (256/240)` in every generation.
-/
/-- An agent of a digital organism: its mass (share of the organism) and its position. -/
/-- A finite population of agents. -/
/-- The total mass of a population. -/
/-- All agents have nonnegative mass. -/
/-- The Fréchet functional `F(x) = ∑ᵢ mᵢ d(x, pᵢ)²`. -/
/-- A Riemannian (Fréchet–Karcher) centroid: a minimiser of the Fréchet functional. -/
/-- The first moment `∑ᵢ mᵢ pᵢ`. -/
/-- The weighted mean `M⁻¹ ∑ᵢ mᵢ pᵢ`. -/
/-- The energy of a population: its Fréchet variance about the centroid. -/
/-- Expansion of the Fréchet functional about an arbitrary point `c`. -/
/-- **Variance decomposition**: `F(x) = E + M ‖x - c‖²` about the centroid `c`. -/
/-- The weighted mean is the unique Riemannian centroid of a population of positive mass. -/
/-- Every agent's weighted squared distance to the centroid is bounded by the energy. -/

/-- **Mitosis**: every agent of mass `m` at `p` splits into two daughters of mass `m / 2` at
`p + δ r` and `p - δ r`, where `r = dir p` is the steering direction. -/
/-- Mitosis raises the Fréchet functional by `δ² ∑ᵢ mᵢ ‖rᵢ‖²` at every point. -/
/-- Mitosis along directions of squared length `2` (the `E₈` roots). -/
/-! ## The organism state engine -/
/-- The state of an `E₈` lattice organism: its population and its accumulated negentropy. -/

/-- The state engine of an organism with sensory alphabet `α`: in generation `k` it receives the
feed `feed k`, transmutes it onto the 240 roots of `E₈` by `quantize k`, and divides with step
size `schedule k` along the roots chosen by `steer k`. -/
/-- The steering direction in generation `k`: the Euclidean root vector chosen at `x`. -/
/-- One generation: harmonic mitosis plus negentropy bookkeeping. -/
/-- The run of the engine from the initial state `s₀`. -/
/-- **Collective coherence**: all generations share the centroid of the founder population. -/
/-- The founder's centroid is the unique Riemannian centroid of every generation. -/
/-- Exact evolution of the Fréchet functional at every point. -/
/-- **Exact energy law**: `Eₙ = E₀ + 2 M ∑_{k<n} δₖ²`. -/
/-- The accumulated negentropy is the sum of the per-generation gains. -/
/-- The organism never loses negentropy. -/

/-- **Non-divergence for square-summable schedules**: the energy stays below
`E₀ + 2 M ∑ₖ δₖ²` and converges to it. -/
/-- The harmonic schedule `δₖ = 1 / (k + 1)`. -/

/-- **Harmonic mitosis theorem.** If the organism divides with the harmonic schedule
`δₖ = 1/(k+1)` along `E₈` roots, then in every generation the energy about the shared
Riemannian centroid satisfies `Eₙ ≤ E₀ + M π² / 3`, and every agent's weighted squared distance
to the centroid obeys the same bound. -/

/-- **Coherent bound at every reference point**: the Fréchet functional of every generation is
at most `E₀ + M π²/3 + M ‖x - c‖²`. -/

/-- **Without a square-summable schedule the energy diverges**: dividing with a constant
nonzero step (for instance, whole lattice steps) makes the energy tend to `+∞`. -/
/-! ## Sensory feeds from an 8-dimensional synesthetic cavity -/
/-- The sensory alphabet: the (finitely many) synchronized resonance points of the cavity. -/
/-- An 8-dimensional cavity has at least `2⁸ = 256` resonance points. -/
/-- The uniform sensory feed over the resonance points of the cavity. -/
/-- The synesthetic feed is **high-entropy** relative to the root alphabet. -/

/-- **Negentropy transmutation of synesthetic feeds**: every quantizer from the resonance
points onto the 240 roots of `E₈` produces `ΔS ≥ log (256/240) > 0`. -/

/-!
# The fidelity theorem: physical field configurations compile into Lean certificates

A `FieldCertificate S cs Q J ℓ φ h N` is a Lean term certifying, for the multi-sensor stream
`S`, the probe loop `ℓ`, the readout channel `φ` and the sample record `h 0, …, h N`:

* the Maxwell–acoustic and energy–momentum constraints `S.PhysicalConstraints cs Q J`;
* admissibility of the probe loop (the readout never vanishes on it);
* that the compiled data `output` is exactly the output of the topological sampler on the
  samples;
* that its winding number is the topological charge of the continuous loop, its Berry phase is
  the continuous phase circulation `∮ dθ = 2π · winding`, and that the samples resolve the loop
  as a single 1-cycle (resolution graph = `N`-cycle, `b₀ = b₁ = 1`).

Results:

* `FieldCertificate.instSubsingleton`: a certificate is unique when it exists.
* `FieldCertificate.sound`: what a certificate proves: the physical constraints, the
  quantization `∮ dθ = 2π n` with `n` the compiled integer, that `n` is a complete homotopy
  invariant of the readout loop among all admissible probe loops, and its conservation along
  every non-singular deformation.
* **`fidelity`**: every physical field configuration satisfying the constraints, probed along an
  admissible loop, has a tolerance `ε > 0` and a resolution `N₀ ≥ 3` such that *every*
  `ε`-accurate sample record with `N ≥ N₀` samples compiles into a `FieldCertificate`.
  `fidelity_exact` is the special case of exact samples.
* `fidelity_streaming`: if the acoustic channel at a fixed point is a band-limited
  `Spectral.SensorFeed`, that channel is Lipschitz in time with the feed's explicit constant and
  the feed has its `Spectral.SensorFeed.DiscreteCertificate` at every Nyquist-admissible rate.

The axiom check at the end of the file (`#guard_msgs` on `#print axioms`) makes the build fail
unless `fidelity` depends only on `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.
-/

/-- A **field certificate** for the stream `S` (with speed of sound `cs`, acoustic source `Q`,
electric current `J`), probe loop `ℓ`, channel `φ` and sample record `h 0, …, h N`. -/
/-- the compiled topological data -/
/-- the compiled data is the output of the topological sampler on the samples -/
/-- the physical field equations -/
/-- the probe loop avoids the phase singularities of the readout -/
/-- the winding number is the topological charge of the continuous probe loop -/
/-- the discrete Berry phase is the continuous phase circulation `∮ dθ` -/
/-- quantization of the Berry phase -/
/-- the samples resolve the probe loop as a single 1-cycle -/
/-- Certificates are unique. -/
/-- **Soundness**: what a field certificate proves about the physical configuration. -/
/-- The energy–momentum balance certified by a field certificate. -/

/-- **The fidelity theorem.** Let `S` be a multi-sensor stream satisfying the Maxwell–acoustic
and energy–momentum constraints, and `ℓ` a probe loop along which the readout `φ` never
vanishes. Then there are a sensor tolerance `ε > 0` and a resolution `N₀ ≥ 3` such that every
`ε`-accurate sample record with `N ≥ N₀` samples compiles into a (unique) field certificate. -/

/-- **Fidelity for exact sampling**: the exact samples of the stream along the probe loop
compile into a field certificate at every resolution `N ≥ N₀`. -/

/-- **Fidelity with a streaming acoustic feed.** If moreover the acoustic pressure at the point
`x₀` is the reading of a band-limited sensor feed `F`, then besides the field certificates, the
acoustic channel of the stream at `x₀` is Lipschitz in time with the feed's explicit constant,
and the feed has its discrete certificate (Lipschitz, bounded-variation, Parseval and `H¹`
bounds) at every Nyquist-admissible rate `M ≥ 2B + 1`. -/

/-!
# Negentropy of sensory transmutation onto the `E₈` root alphabet

We extend the finite distributions `FinDist` of `Sovereign.Entropy.LeftoverHash` with the
**Shannon entropy** `H(P) = ∑ₐ -P(a) log P(a)` (natural logarithm, `FinDist.shannon`) and the
**push-forward** `FinDist.map f P` of a distribution along a deterministic map.

An organism *transmutes* an external sensory feed `P` (a distribution on a finite sensory
alphabet) into an internal state by a deterministic quantizer `q`; the **negentropy gain** is
`ΔS = H(P) - H(q₊P)` (`negentropyGain`).

* `shannon_map_le`: deterministic processing never increases entropy, so `ΔS ≥ 0`
  (`negentropyGain_nonneg`);
* `shannon_le_log_card`: `H(P) ≤ log |α|` (Jensen, concavity of `-x log x`);
  `shannon_uniform`: equality for the uniform law;
* `negentropyGain_ge`: `ΔS ≥ H(P) - log |β|`, hence `negentropyGain_pos`: a feed whose entropy
  exceeds the capacity `log |β|` of the internal alphabet is transmuted with `ΔS > 0`.

Specialised to the internal alphabet `RootAlphabet` of the 240 roots of `E₈`
(`card_rootAlphabet`):
* `rootQuantized_shannon_le`: **structural integrity** — the internal state entropy never
  exceeds `log 240`, whatever the feed;
* `rootTransmutation_pos`: every feed with `H(P) > log 240` yields `ΔS > 0`.
-/
/-- The Shannon entropy `H(P) = ∑ₐ -P(a) log P(a)` (in nats). -/
/-- The push-forward of a distribution along a deterministic map. -/
/-- **Data processing**: deterministic maps never increase Shannon entropy. -/
/-- **Maximum entropy**: `H(P) ≤ log |α|`. -/
/-- The uniform distribution has maximal entropy `log |α|`. -/
/-- The **negentropy gain** `ΔS = H(P) - H(q₊P)` of transmuting the feed `P` by `q`. -/

/-- `ΔS ≥ H(P) - log |β|`: the excess of the feed entropy over the internal capacity is
always removed. -/
/-- A high-entropy feed (`H(P) > log |β|`) is transmuted with strictly positive negentropy. -/
/-- The internal alphabet: the 240 roots of `E₈`. -/

/-- **Structural integrity**: whatever the feed, the internal root-state entropy is at most
`log 240`. -/

/-- **Negentropy transmutation onto `E₈`**: every sensory feed of entropy above `log 240` is
quantized onto the root alphabet with `ΔS ≥ H(P) - log 240 > 0`. -/

/-!
# Physical sensor channels

The sensor state space is the Hilbert space `ℂ³` of (acoustic pressure, optical intensity,
electromagnetic phasor) readings.

* `probeLoop`, `probe_pipeline`: a probe carried around a loop in an acoustic vortex field;
  its compiled certificate is the topological charge (`AcousticVortex`).
* `cubeVortex_pipeline`, `cubeAntivortex_pipeline`: for the cube vortex of `CubeVortex`, the
  certificates are `+1` and `-1`.
* `sweep_quantize_conserved`: certificates are conserved along non-singular deformations
  (frequency sweeps).
* `decodeMode_eq`, `nodal_pipeline`: spatial wave numbers measured within tolerance
  `π / (2 Lᵢ)` compile to the exact nodal signature of `NodalCertificate`.
* `audioVisualTrajectory`: an acoustic–optical sensor trajectory built from a sound; the
  action of the audio-visual functor (transposition) dilates time in the acoustic channel and
  leaves the optical intensity invariant (`audioVisualTrajectory_transpose`).
-/
/-! ### The three-channel sensor space -/

/-- The sensor state space: the Hilbert space `ℂ³` of (acoustic pressure, optical intensity,
electromagnetic phasor) readings. -/
/-- The unit vector of channel `i`. -/

/-- The sensor state with acoustic pressure `p`, optical intensity `q` and electromagnetic
phasor `e`. -/
/-- The acoustic pressure channel. -/
/-- The optical intensity channel. -/
/-- The electromagnetic phasor channel. -/
/-! ### Probing an acoustic field along a closed loop -/

/-- The sensor state recorded at a point of an acoustic field `ψ`: pressure `Re ψ`, intensity
`|ψ|²` and phasor `ψ`. -/

/-- The closed sensor loop recorded by a probe carried around the core-avoiding loop `ℓ` in the
acoustic field `P`. -/

/-- The charge of the probe's sensor loop is the topological charge of the vortex lines
threading the loop. -/

/-- **Pipeline for vortex fields.** Sampling the probe's three-channel sensor stream finely and
accurately enough and quantizing the phasor channel returns exactly the topological charge of
the vortex lines threading the loop. -/

/-- **The cube vortex, end to end.** The sensor stream recorded around the vortex line
`x = y = π/2` of `ψ = ψ_{(2,1,1)} + i ψ_{(1,2,1)}` in the cube `[0, π]³` compiles to the
certificate `+1`. -/
/-- The conjugate field (antivortex) compiles to the certificate `-1`. -/
/-! ### Conservation under non-singular deformations (frequency sweeps) -/

/-- The deformation of sensor loops recorded along a non-singular deformation of the field and
the probe loop. -/

/-- **Conservation of the compiled certificate along a sweep.** For a non-singular deformation
(e.g. a frequency sweep of a multi-mode Chladni field), fine and accurate samplings of the sensor
streams at any two sweep parameters compile to the same integer, namely the conserved charge. -/
/-! ### Nodal certificates from measured spatial frequencies -/
/-- Decode a mode from measured spatial wave numbers: `mᵢ = round (kᵢ Lᵢ / π)`. -/

/-- **Exact decoding up to sensor tolerance.** If every measured wave number is within
`π / (2 Lᵢ)` of the true modal wave number `mᵢ π / Lᵢ`, the decoded mode is exactly `m`. -/

/-- **Nodal pipeline.** From spatial wave numbers measured within tolerance `π / (2 Lᵢ)`, the
compiled nodal signature is exactly the signature measured on the real Chladni geometry
(nodal hyperplanes, vertices, crossings, domains), passes the Boolean checker, and decodes to
the true mode. -/
/-! ### Acoustic–optical streams and the audio-visual functor -/

/-- The optical intensity of the synesthetic colour spectrum of `w`: its total squared
intensity. -/

/-- The **acoustic–optical sensor trajectory** of a sound `w`: the acoustic channel records the
pressure `w(t)`, the optical channel the intensity of the synesthetic colour spectrum of `w`, and
the electromagnetic channel a smooth phasor stream `e`. It is smooth (no breakpoints). -/

/-- **Functoriality of the acoustic–optical stream.** Transposing the sound by `c` (the action
of the audio-visual functor) dilates time in the acoustic channel and leaves the optical
intensity channel unchanged. -/
/-- The optical intensity channel is invariant under time translation of the sound. -/

/-!
# Sensor trajectories in a Hilbert space and their topological certificates

* `SensorTrajectory H`: a continuous, piecewise `C^∞` stream `ℝ → H` in a complex Hilbert space.
* `SensorLoop H`: a closed acquisition window `[0, 1] → H`; a continuous linear channel
  `φ : H →L[ℂ] ℂ` gives the complex phase readout `φ ∘ γ` (`phaseSignal`), and the loop is
  admissible if this readout never vanishes. `charge` is its winding number.
* `quantize φ h N`: the discrete quantization map, from sampled readings `h 0, …, h N ∈ H`
  to an integer. `IsSampling γ ε N h`: the readings are `ε`-accurate samples at `k / N`.
* `quantize_eq_charge`, `exists_tolerance_quantize_eq_charge`: exactness of the quantization
  up to the sensor tolerance `ε` (explicitly: any `ε` with `4 ‖φ‖ ε ≤ min |φ ∘ γ|`).
* `TopologicalCertificate`: a Lean proposition certificate `∮ dθ = 2π n`; it is unique, and
  `pipeline_compiles` produces it from the samples.
* Homotopy: `AdmissibleHomotopy.charge_conserved`, `AdmissibleHomotopy.quantize_conserved`,
  `charge_eq_iff_loopHomotopic`, `quantize_eq_iff_loopHomotopic`, `exists_loop_charge_eq`.
* Differential forms: `integral_phaseForm_eq_quantize`: `∮ (u dv − v du)/(u² + v²)` equals
  `2π` times the compiled integer.
-/
/-! ### Sensor trajectories in a Hilbert space -/

/-- A **piecewise smooth sensor trajectory** in the Hilbert space `H`: a continuous stream
`t ↦ γ t` which is `C^∞` away from a finite set of breakpoints (switching instants). -/
/-- The sensor state at time `t`. -/
/-- The finitely many instants where the stream may fail to be smooth. -/

/-- A **closed sensor loop**: one acquisition window `[0, 1]` of a sensor stream in `H`, starting
and ending in the same state. -/
/-- The stream over the acquisition window. -/
/-- The acquisition window `[0, 1]` of a trajectory, as a closed loop. -/

/-- The complex **phase readout** `t ↦ φ (γ t)` of a sensor loop through the continuous linear
channel `φ` (e.g. the electromagnetic phasor channel). -/

/-- A loop is **admissible** for the channel `φ` if its phase readout never vanishes (the probe
never meets a phase singularity). -/
/-- The **topological charge** of an admissible loop: the winding number of the phase readout. -/
/-- **Quantization of the phase circulation**: `∮ dθ = 2π · charge`. -/

/-- The **discrete quantization map**: from `N + 1` sampled sensor readings `h 0, …, h N ∈ H`
to an integer, the discrete winding number of the phase readouts `φ (h k)`. -/

/-- The readings `h 0, …, h N` are an `ε`-accurate sampling of the loop `γ` at the instants
`k / N`, closing up (`h N = h 0`). -/

/-- **Exactness of the quantization map (explicit tolerance).** Let `m > 0` be a lower bound for
the amplitude `|φ (γ t)|` of the phase readout. For every sensor tolerance `ε` with
`4 ‖φ‖ ε ≤ m` there is a sampling resolution `N₀` such that every `ε`-accurate sampling with
`N ≥ N₀` samples is quantized to exactly the topological charge of the loop: no reconstruction
loss at all. -/

/-- **Exactness of the quantization map.** Every admissible sensor loop has a positive sensor
tolerance `ε` and a resolution `N₀` such that all `ε`-accurate samplings with at least `N₀`
samples are quantized to exactly the topological charge. -/
/-! ### Lean proposition certificates -/

/-- A **topological certificate** for an admissible sensor loop: an integer `n` together with a
proof of the proposition `∮ dθ = 2π n` about the continuous phase readout. -/
/-- The certified topological charge. -/
/-- Certificates are unique: any two certificates for the same loop coincide. -/
/-- The certificate carrying the topological charge. -/

/-- **End-to-end pipeline.** For every admissible sensor loop there are a sensor tolerance
`ε > 0` and a resolution `N₀` such that every `ε`-accurate sampling with `N ≥ N₀` samples
compiles into a certificate of the proposition `∮ dθ = 2π n` whose integer `n` is the quantized
sample sequence, and this integer is exactly the topological charge. -/
/-! ### Homotopy invariance and completeness -/

/-- A **non-singular deformation of sensor loops**: a continuous family of closed loops in `H`
none of which meets the phase-singular set `ker φ`. -/
/-- The family `(t, s) ↦ γ_s t`. -/
/-- The sensor loop at deformation parameter `s`. -/
/-- **Conservation of the topological charge** along a non-singular deformation. -/

/-- **The quantized certificates are homotopy invariant**: sufficiently fine and accurate
samplings of any two loops of a non-singular deformation are quantized to the same integer. -/

/-- **The charge is a complete homotopy invariant**: two admissible sensor loops have the same
topological charge iff their phase readouts are freely homotopic through nonvanishing loops. -/

/-- **The quantization map preserves homotopy type.** For any two admissible sensor loops there
are a tolerance `ε > 0` and a resolution `N₀` such that for all `ε`-accurate samplings with
`N ≥ N₀` samples, the two compiled integers agree iff the phase readouts are homotopic. -/

/-- **Every integer occurs**: for a nonzero channel `φ`, every `n ∈ ℤ` is the topological charge
of some admissible sensor loop. -/
/-! ### Differential-form conservation law -/

/-- **Quantized phase 1-form.** For a `C¹` closed sensor trajectory whose phase readout
`φ ∘ γ = u + i v` never vanishes, the line integral of the closed 1-form
`dθ = (u dv − v du)/(u² + v²)` over the acquisition window is `2π` times the topological charge;
with a fine enough `ε`-accurate sampling, it is `2π` times the compiled integer. -/

/-!
# Multi-sensor streams as bounded continuous fields on space-time `ℝ³ × ℝ`

The three physical sensor modalities of the pipeline are modelled as **bounded continuous
fields** on space-time `Spacetime = ℝ³ × ℝ` (a point is `(x, t)`):

* `pressure : ℝ³ × ℝ →ᵇ ℝ` — the acoustic pressure;
* `spectrum : ℝ³ × ℝ →ᵇ (Fin K → ℝ)` — the optical spectrum, as intensities in `K` bands;
* `faraday : ℝ³ × ℝ →ᵇ (Fin 4 → Fin 4 → ℝ)` — the (antisymmetric) electromagnetic field tensor
  `F_{μν}` in Minkowski coordinates `(t, x₀, x₁, x₂)` with `c = 1`, electric field
  `E_i = F_{i0}` and magnetic field `B = (F_{23}, F_{31}, F_{12})`.

A `MultiSensorStream K` bundles the three fields.  Its **sensor-state field**
`stateField : ℝ³ × ℝ →ᵇ SensorSpace` records, at every event, the vector

/-!
# The discrete topological sampler

From a finite sample sequence `h 0, …, h N` of sensor states (with `h N = h 0`) and a complex
readout channel `φ`, the **topological sampler** extracts:

* `winding` — the conserved homotopy cycle: the discrete winding number `quantize φ h N ∈ ℤ`
  (the class of the sampled phase loop in `π₁(ℂ \ {0}) ≅ ℤ`);
* `berryPhase` — the discrete Berry phase `∑ₖ arg (φ h(k+1) / φ h k)`;
* `betti0`, `betti1` — the Betti numbers of the **resolution graph** of the samples: the cycle
  graph on the `N` sample indices, keeping the edge `k — k+1` iff the step is *resolved*,
  `‖w(k+1) - w(k)‖ < ‖w(k)‖` for `w = φ ∘ h` (the phase increment is then below `π/2`).
  Betti numbers of a finite graph are `b₀ = #components` and `b₁ = #E - #V + b₀` (its cycle
  rank).

`sampler_exact`: for every admissible loop `γ` (readout never vanishing) there are a tolerance
`ε > 0` and a resolution `N₀ ≥ 3` such that every `ε`-accurate sampling with `N ≥ N₀` samples is
mapped to `(charge γ, 2π · charge γ, 1, 1)`: the winding number is the topological charge, the
discrete Berry phase is exactly the continuous phase circulation `∮ dθ`, and the resolution
graph is the full `N`-cycle (`b₀ = b₁ = 1`), i.e. the samples resolve exactly one closed
1-cycle.

For multi-sensor streams on space-time, `MultiSensorStream.sensorLoop S ℓ` is the sensor loop
recorded along a closed space-time probe loop `ℓ`, and `MultiSensorStream.samples S ℓ N` are
its exact samples, which are `ε`-accurate for every `ε ≥ 0`.
-/
/-! ### Betti numbers of finite graphs -/
/-- The zeroth Betti number of a graph: the number of connected components. -/
/-- The first Betti number of a graph: its cycle rank `#E - #V + b₀`. -/
/-- Euler–Poincaré: `b₀ - b₁ = #V - #E`. -/
/-! ### The resolution graph of a sample sequence -/
/-- The step `k → k+1` of a sample sequence is **resolved** if `‖w(k+1) - w(k)‖ < ‖w(k)‖`. -/

/-- The **resolution graph** of `N` samples: the edge `k — k+1 (mod N)` of the `N`-cycle is kept
iff the step from sample `k` is resolved. -/
/-- If all steps are resolved, the resolution graph is the full `N`-cycle. -/
/-- The resolution graph is always a subgraph of the `N`-cycle. -/
/-- Fine and accurate sampling of a nonvanishing loop resolves every step. -/
/-! ### The sampler -/
/-- The output of the topological sampler. -/
/-- the conserved homotopy cycle (discrete winding number) -/
/-- the discrete Berry phase -/
/-- the Betti numbers of the resolution graph -/

/-- The **discrete topological sampler**: from the readings `h 0, …, h N` and the channel `φ`,
the winding number, discrete Berry phase and Betti numbers of the resolution graph. -/

/-- **Exactness of the topological sampler.** For every admissible sensor loop there are a
tolerance `ε > 0` and a resolution `N₀ ≥ 3` such that every `ε`-accurate sampling with
`N ≥ N₀` samples yields winding number `= charge`, discrete Berry phase `= 2π · charge`
`= ∮ dθ`, and Betti numbers `b₀ = b₁ = 1`. -/
/-! ### Probe loops in space-time -/
/-- A closed **probe loop** in space-time. -/
/-- The sensor loop recorded by carrying the sensors along a closed space-time probe loop. -/
/-- The exact samples of the stream at the `N + 1` instants `k / N` of the probe loop. -/
/-- Exact samples are `ε`-accurate for every `ε ≥ 0`. -/

structure VacuumMaxwell3 (E B : (Fin 4 → ℝ) → Fin 3 → ℝ) : Prop where
  smoothE : ContDiff ℝ 2 E
  smoothB : ContDiff ℝ 2 B
  /-- `∇·E = 0` -/
  gaussE : ∀ Y, pd 1 (fun Z => E Z 0) Y + pd 2 (fun Z => E Z 1) Y + pd 3 (fun Z => E Z 2) Y = 0
  /-- `∇·B = 0` -/
  gaussB : ∀ Y, pd 1 (fun Z => B Z 0) Y + pd 2 (fun Z => B Z 1) Y + pd 3 (fun Z => B Z 2) Y = 0
  /-- Faraday: `∂ₜB = -∇×E` -/
  faraday : ∀ Y,
    pd 0 (fun Z => B Z 0) Y = -(pd 2 (fun Z => E Z 2) Y - pd 3 (fun Z => E Z 1) Y) ∧
    pd 0 (fun Z => B Z 1) Y = -(pd 3 (fun Z => E Z 0) Y - pd 1 (fun Z => E Z 2) Y) ∧
    pd 0 (fun Z => B Z 2) Y = -(pd 1 (fun Z => E Z 1) Y - pd 2 (fun Z => E Z 0) Y)
  /-- Ampère–Maxwell: `∂ₜE = ∇×B` -/
  ampere : ∀ Y,
    pd 0 (fun Z => E Z 0) Y = pd 2 (fun Z => B Z 2) Y - pd 3 (fun Z => B Z 1) Y ∧
    pd 0 (fun Z => E Z 1) Y = pd 3 (fun Z => B Z 0) Y - pd 1 (fun Z => B Z 2) Y ∧
    pd 0 (fun Z => E Z 2) Y = pd 1 (fun Z => B Z 1) Y - pd 2 (fun Z => B Z 0) Y

# A worked physical configuration: a cavity sound field with an electromagnetic vortex

This file exhibits a concrete multi-sensor stream satisfying all constraints of the fidelity
theorem, with a probe loop of nonzero topological charge, so that the fidelity theorem is
not vacuous.

  (`Sovereign.Taxonomy.SynestheticResonance`), a free standing wave: `□_{cs} p = 0`.

  cavity field.
* **Electromagnetic channel**: the transverse-electric vacuum mode (`c = 1`)
  `E = (-4 cos 3x sin 4y sin 5t, 3 sin 3x cos 4y sin 5t, 0)`,
  `B = (0, 0, 5 cos 3x cos 4y cos 5t)`, a bounded smooth solution of Maxwell's equations
  (`vortexMaxwell3`; dispersion relation `3² + 4² = 5²`).

At `t₀ = π/10` the transverse phasor `E_x + i E_y` has a phase vortex at the origin: along the
circle of radius `1/4` about the origin in the plane `z = 0` it winds once
(`charge_vortexProbe`).  `vortex_fidelity`: every fine enough exact sampling of this probe loop

/-!
# Integer first cohomology `H¹(G; ℤ)` of a dependency graph

For a dependency graph `G` (vertices `V`, directed edges `E`) we consider the
integral cochain complex `C⁰(G; ℤ) → C¹(G; ℤ)`, `(δ f) e = f (tgt e) - f (src e)`,
and its first cohomology `H1Z G = C¹ / im δ`.  Since `G` is one-dimensional (there are
no 2-cells), this cochain complex is the one computing the Čech cohomology `Ȟ¹(𝒰; ℤ)` of
the open-star cover of the geometric realisation of `G` (whose nerve is `G` itself); here we
work with the combinatorial cochain complex directly and do not formalise the comparison.

Main results:
* `H1Z_subsingleton_iff_forall_isBridge`: `H¹(G; ℤ) = 0` iff every edge is a bridge
  (removing it disconnects its endpoints), i.e. the underlying multigraph is a forest.
* `H1_subsingleton_of_H1Z_subsingleton`: `H¹(G; ℤ) = 0 → H¹(G; ℚ) = 0`.
* `not_hasCircularLoop_of_H1Z_subsingleton`, `not_hasUndirectedCycle_of_H1Z_subsingleton`:
  vanishing integral cohomology excludes circular reasoning loops and redundant (undirected)
  cycles.
* `cechCertB`: a computable certificate check (explicit integral potentials for every edge);
  `H1Z_subsingleton_of_cechCertB` proves it sound.
-/
/-- The integral coboundary `δ : C⁰(G; ℤ) → C¹(G; ℤ)`. -/
/-- Integral first cohomology `H¹(G; ℤ) = C¹(G; ℤ) / im δ`. -/
/-- `u` and `v` are joined by an edge other than `e` (in either direction). -/
/-- `u` and `v` are connected in the underlying undirected multigraph with `e` removed. -/
/-- `e` is a bridge: removing it disconnects its endpoints. -/

/-- A potential constant along every edge other than `e` is constant on the components of
`G ∖ e`. -/
/-- If `e` is not a bridge then its indicator cochain is not a coboundary. -/
/-- The potential of a bridge: the indicator of the component of `tgt e` in `G ∖ e`. -/
/-- **`H¹(G; ℤ) = 0` iff every edge is a bridge** (the underlying multigraph is a forest). -/
/-- `H¹(G; ℤ) = 0` implies `H¹(G; ℚ) = 0`: clear denominators. -/
/-- **Vanishing integral cohomology excludes circular reasoning.** -/
/-- **Vanishing integral cohomology excludes redundant (undirected) cycles.** -/
/-- A circular reasoning loop forces `H¹(G; ℤ) ≠ 0`. -/
/-! ### A computable Čech certificate -/
/-- One round of reachability in `G ∖ e`. -/
/-- The vertices reached from `tgt e` in `G ∖ e` within `|V|` rounds. -/
/-- Everything reached is connected to `tgt e` in `G ∖ e`. -/
/-- A set closed under `reachStep` and containing `tgt e` contains its whole component. -/
/-- The iteration stabilises within `|V|` rounds. -/
/-- Candidate integral potential for the edge `e`. -/

/-- **The Čech certificate check**: for every edge `e`, the computed potential has
coboundary exactly the indicator of `e`. -/
/-- **Soundness of the Čech certificate**: if the check passes, `H¹(G; ℤ) = 0`. -/

/-- **Completeness of the Čech certificate**: if `H¹(G; ℤ) = 0` the check passes, so the
check decides `H¹(G; ℤ) = 0` exactly. -/
/-- A graph with a circular reasoning loop fails the Čech certificate check. -/
/-- A graph with an undirected (redundant) cycle fails the Čech certificate check. -/

/-!
# The Proof-of-Useful-Work ledger: blocks and the state transition function

A block carries a proof contribution (a Swarm `Proposal`: a claim and its derivation DAG).
The *work* of a block is the proof itself: a block is valid on top of a ledger `L` iff

* it sits at the next height and names the digest of `L` as its parent,
* its proposal passes the epistemic filter `accept` against the current knowledge base
  `library P L` = genesis axioms `P.Γ` plus every theorem already on the ledger: the DAG is
  kernel-certified, its propositional network has `H¹(·; ℤ) = 0`, and the claim has positive
  Kolmogorov information content (new, and not a tautology).

Later blocks may cite the theorems proved by earlier blocks, so useful work accumulates.

* `applyBlock` is the state transition function; `ValidChain` is its closure.
* `ValidChain.library_valid`: over valid axioms every ledger theorem is valid.
* `ValidChain.block_sound`: every block on a valid chain is sorry-free, non-circular
  (`H¹ = 0`), non-tautological, and carries a new claim with positive information content.
* `ValidChain.claims_nodup`: no theorem is ever mined twice.
-/

/-- **Block validity.** -/
/-- **The state transition function** of the ledger. -/
/-- A chain every block of which is valid on top of its prefix. -/
/-- The transition function preserves chain validity. -/
/-- Chains built by the transition function from genesis are valid, and conversely. -/
/-- Induction principle for valid chains. -/
/-- **Soundness of the ledger**: over valid axioms, every theorem on a valid chain is valid. -/

/-- **Every block of a valid chain is sound useful work**: kernel-certified and sorry-free,
its propositional network has vanishing Čech cohomology and no circular derivation, and its
claim is new (not an axiom, not previously mined), not a tautology, and has positive

/-- Heights on a valid chain are the positions. -/
/-- **No theorem is mined twice**, and no mined theorem is a genesis axiom. -/

/-!
# The PoUW consensus engine: safety, bounded-depth finality and liveness

The ledger of `Sovereign.PoUW.Chain` is replicated over a finite set of validators `Node`,
some of which (`corrupt`) are Byzantine.  The engine follows the quorum-certificate design of
`Sovereign.Consensus`: signatures are modelled by the ideal registry `votes`
(membership = a valid signature), and `Sovereign.Consensus.signers` collects the endorsers of a
block.

* `vote n b`: validator `n` endorses block `b`.  An honest validator endorses `b` only if `b` is
  a valid PoUW block on top of its own ledger (`validBlock`: next height, correct parent
  digest, kernel-certified non-circular proof DAG with positive information content) and it has
  not endorsed another block at that height.  Byzantine validators endorse anything.
* `commit n b`: validator `n` appends `b` to its ledger.  An honest validator commits `b` only
  if `b` is valid on top of its ledger and *certified*: endorsed by at least `quorum`
  validators.  Byzantine validators may append anything to their own ledgers.

The adversary chooses the entire schedule of events.  Under the Byzantine quorum condition
`|Node| + |corrupt| < 2 · quorum` we prove:

* `honest_ledger_valid`: every honest ledger is a valid PoUW chain;
* `agreement`, `ledgers_prefix`: honest ledgers never fork;
* `finality`: a block committed by some honest validator, at any confirmation depth `k ≥ 0`, is
  never rolled back and is the block at that height in every honest ledger, forever — i.e.
  finality is reached with confirmation depth bound `0`;
* `liveness`: from a synchronised state, a valid block is committed by every honest validator
  after one round of at most `2 · |Node|` events.
-/
/-- Configuration of the consensus engine. -/
/-- PoUW validity parameters -/
/-- number of endorsements certifying a block -/
/-- the Byzantine validators -/
/-- Global state: the endorsement registry and every validator's ledger (oldest first). -/
/-- Events; the adversary schedules any sequence of them. -/
/-- `n` has endorsed some block at height `h`. -/
/-- Block `b` carries a quorum certificate. -/
/-- **The consensus state transition function.** -/
/-- Run a schedule. -/
/-- The genesis state. -/
/-- States reachable from genesis under some adversarial schedule. -/
/-! ### Monotonicity -/
/-- **No rollback**: ledgers only grow. -/
/-! ### The safety invariant -/
/-- The inductive invariant. -/
/-- honest validators endorse at most one block per height -/
/-- honest ledgers are valid PoUW chains -/
/-- every block of an honest ledger is certified -/
/-! ### Safety -/

/-- **Honest ledgers are valid PoUW chains**, so everything proved on the ledger of an honest
validator enjoys `ValidChain.library_valid` and `ValidChain.block_sound`. -/
/-- **Quorum intersection**: at most one block per height is ever certified. -/
/-- **Agreement**: two honest ledgers hold the same block at every common height. -/
/-- **No forks**: of any two honest ledgers, one is a prefix of the other. -/

/-- Block `b` sits in `n`'s ledger at height `i` with at least `k` blocks on top of it
(confirmation depth `k`). -/

/-- Block `b` is *final* at height `i` in state `st`: under every future schedule, every honest
ledger that reaches height `i` holds `b` there. -/

/-- **Finality within bounded confirmation depth**: a block confirmed at depth `k` in an
honest ledger is final, for every `k`; in particular the confirmation depth needed for finality
is bounded by `0` (a block is final as soon as an honest validator commits it). -/
/-- A committed block stays committed at the same height in its own ledger. -/
/-! ### Liveness -/
/-- The honest validators, as a list. -/

/-- One synchronous round for block `b`: every honest validator endorses `b`, then every honest
validator commits it. -/

/-- **Liveness**: if all honest validators hold the same ledger `L`, block `b` is valid on top of
`L`, no honest validator has endorsed anything at `b`'s height yet, and the honest validators
can form a quorum, then after the round `round E b` (at most `2 · |Node|` events) every honest
validator has committed `b`. -/

/-- **Finality within one bounded round**: under the hypotheses of `liveness` and the Byzantine
quorum condition, after at most `2 · |Node|` events block `b` is final at height `|L|`. -/

/-!
# The epistemic anti-tautology verification filter

A candidate contribution is a Swarm `Proposal`: a claimed statement together with a derivation
DAG over the hole-aware repair kernel.  The filter `accept D Γ p` runs three checks against the
current knowledge base `Γ` (the library, which is also the set of statements already known):

1. **Kernel certification**: `Grounded Γ p` — the kernel evaluates every node (no `sorry`
   holes, no dangling or forward references) and the sink is the claim.
2. **Čech anti-circularity**: the *propositional hypergraph network* `propNet Γ p` of the DAG
   (vertices = distinct propositions proved in the DAG, hyperedges = inference steps) has
   vanishing integral Čech 1-cohomology `H¹(propNet Γ p; ℤ) = 0`.  This rejects circular
   reasoning at the level of propositions (re-deriving a proposition from itself through other
   steps), trivial tautological steps `p ⊢ p`, and redundant duplicated premises.
3. **Positive information content**: `0 < info D Γ p.claim`, the Kolmogorov information content
   of the claim relative to the knowledge base (`info`).  This rejects claims that are already
   known and propositional tautologies (`Sovereign.Bridge.Expr.Tautological`).

`accept_iff` characterises the filter; `accept_sound` collects the guarantees of an accepted
proposal; the `accept_eq_false_of_*` theorems are the rejection results.
-/
/-! ### Information content -/

/-- **Kolmogorov information content** of `φ` relative to the knowledge base `K`, measured by
the description method `D` (for instance a universal decoder): statements that are already
known, or are propositional tautologies, carry no information; otherwise the content is the
length of a shortest `D`-description of `φ` (`kc D φ`, `⊤` if there is none). -/
/-- `info` is bounded by the plain description complexity. -/
/-- Decision procedure for positive information content. -/
/-! ### The propositional hypergraph network of a derivation DAG -/
/-- The conclusions computed by the kernel for each DAG node (`[]` if the kernel rejects). -/

/-- The vertex of a proposition: the index of its first occurrence among the conclusions
(propositions proved several times are identified). -/
/-- Distinct proved propositions get distinct vertices. -/
/-- Premise references of DAG node `i`. -/

/-- **The propositional hypergraph network** of a proposal: one vertex per proved
proposition, one hyperedge per DAG node, from the propositions it uses to the one it proves. -/

/-- A DAG node that uses (the conclusion of) node `j` to re-prove that very proposition is a
trivial step of the network. -/
/-! ### The filter -/
/-- **The epistemic anti-tautology filter.** -/

/-- **Soundness of the filter**: an accepted proposal is kernel-certified (hence sorry-free and,
over a valid library, valid), its propositional network has `H¹ = 0` and therefore contains no
circular derivation, no trivial step and no duplicated premise, and its claim is new and not a
tautology. -/
/-- Accepted claims are valid, relative to a valid library. -/
/-- **Trivial tautologies are rejected.** -/
/-- Already-known statements are rejected (no information gain). -/
/-- Circular reasoning is rejected. -/
/-- A DAG node re-proving one of its own premises (`p ⊢ p`) is rejected. -/
/-- A proof containing a `sorry` hole is rejected. -/
/-- The integral cohomology of an accepted proposal also vanishes rationally. -/

/-!
# Propositions as hypergraph networks

A `HyperNet V S` is a directed hypergraph whose vertices `V` are propositions and whose
hyperedges `S` are inference steps: step `s` has a list of premises `prem s` and a
conclusion `concl s`.  Its *Levi (incidence) graph* `levi` is the bipartite dependency
graph on `V ⊕ S` with an edge `p → s` for every premise occurrence and an edge `s → concl s`.

The Čech 1-cohomology of the network is `H¹(levi; ℤ)`.  We show:

* `hasCircularLoop_iff`: the Levi graph contains a circular reasoning loop iff some nonempty
  set of steps derives each of its members from a conclusion of the set (circular
  derivation at the level of propositions);
* `hasCircularLoop_of_trivialStep`: a *trivial tautological step* `p, … ⊢ p`, whose
  conclusion is one of its own premises, is a circular loop;
* `H1Z_nontrivial_of_trivialStep`, `H1Z_nontrivial_of_circular`,
  `H1Z_nontrivial_of_duplicatePremise`: each of these forces `H¹(levi; ℤ) ≠ 0`, so the
  Čech check `cechB` rejects them.
-/
/-- A propositional hypergraph network: inference steps `S` over propositions `V`. -/
/-- the premises of each step -/
/-- the conclusion of each step -/

/-- Edges of the Levi graph: premise occurrence `j` of step `s` (`some j`), or the conclusion
edge of `s` (`none`). -/
/-- The Levi (incidence) graph of the network. -/
/-- Čech 1-cohomology `H¹(N; ℤ)` of the network (of its Levi graph). -/
/-- A trivial tautological step: its conclusion is one of its own premises. -/
/-- A step citing the same premise twice. -/

/-- Circular derivation: a nonempty set of steps, each of which has a premise that is the
conclusion of some step of the set. -/
/-- **Circular loops in the Levi graph are exactly circular derivations.** -/
-- the steps in the core
/-- A trivial tautological step is a circular reasoning loop. -/
/-- **Circular derivations force `H¹(N; ℤ) ≠ 0`.** -/
/-- **Trivial tautological steps force `H¹(N; ℤ) ≠ 0`.** -/
/-- **Redundant premises force `H¹(N; ℤ) ≠ 0`**: two parallel premise edges form a cycle. -/
/-- The Čech check of the network. -/

comments.text:
/-!
# Radiation stresses in curved spatial coordinates

We work pointwise on a 3-dimensional coordinate chart carrying a spatial metric `g_{ij}`
(an arbitrary, possibly position dependent, symmetric positive definite matrix). All field
quantities are given by their **covariant** components, and indices are raised with the inverse
metric `g^{ij} = (g⁻¹)_{ij}`.

* `metricDot g a b = g^{ij} aᵢ bⱼ`, `metricNormSq g a = g^{ij} aᵢ aⱼ`.
* `maxwellStress ε μ g E B`: the **Maxwell stress tensor** in curved coordinates,
  `T_{ij} = ε (Eᵢ Eⱼ - ½ g_{ij} |E|²_g) + μ⁻¹ (Bᵢ Bⱼ - ½ g_{ij} |B|²_g)`.
* `acousticStress M g P w`: the time-averaged (Brillouin) **acoustic radiation stress** of a
  time-harmonic pressure field with complex amplitude `P` and complex covariant gradient
  `wᵢ = ∂ᵢ p`: `Π_{ij} = ρ₀ ⟨vᵢ vⱼ⟩ + 𝓛 g_{ij}`, where `⟨vᵢ vⱼ⟩ = Re(wᵢ w̄ⱼ)/(2 ρ₀² ω²)` and
  `𝓛 = ⟨p²⟩/(2 ρ₀ c₀²) - ρ₀ ⟨v²⟩_g / 2` is the acoustic Lagrangian density.
* `gorkovPt M a g P w`: the **Gor'kov potential** in curved coordinates,
  `U = 2π a³ (|P|²/(6 ρ₀ c₀²) - g^{ij} Re(wᵢ w̄ⱼ)/(4 ρ₀ ω²))`.
* `aoStress`: the combined **acoustic-optical stress tensor** `Θ = Π + T`.

Main pointwise results (a change of coordinates with Jacobian `J` acts by
`g ↦ Jᵀ g J`, covectors `a ↦ Jᵀ a`):

* `maxwellStress_transform`, `acousticStress_transform`, `aoStress_transform`:
  all stresses are covariant 2-tensors, `T ↦ Jᵀ T J`;
* `gorkovPt_transform`: the Gor'kov potential is a scalar;
* `mixed_transform`, `charpoly_mixed_transform`: the mixed tensor `T^i_j = g^{ik} T_{kj}`
  transforms by similarity, so the principal stresses (its characteristic polynomial) are
  coordinate invariants;
* `trace_maxwellStress`: `T^i_i = -u` with `u = ½(ε|E|² + |B|²/μ)` the EM energy density;
* `gorkovPt_one`: in flat Cartesian coordinates `gorkovPt` is the Gor'kov potential of
  `Sovereign.Taxonomy.gorkov`.
-/
/-- Real `3 × 3` matrices (metric and stress components). -/
/-- Covariant components of a covector on a 3-dimensional chart. -/
/-! ## Metric contractions -/
/-- `g^{ij} aᵢ bⱼ`: contraction of two covectors with the inverse metric. -/
/-- `|a|²_g = g^{ij} aᵢ aⱼ`. -/
/-- The inverse-metric contraction of covectors is invariant under changes of coordinates. -/
/-- The mixed tensor `g^{ik} T_{kj}` of a covariant 2-tensor transforms by similarity. -/

/-- **Principal invariants are coordinate independent**: the characteristic polynomial of the
mixed tensor `g^{ik} T_{kj}` (whose roots are the principal stresses) does not depend on the
coordinates. -/
/-! ## The Maxwell stress tensor -/

/-- The **Maxwell stress tensor** in curved spatial coordinates (covariant components):
`T_{ij} = ε (Eᵢ Eⱼ - ½ g_{ij} |E|²_g) + μ⁻¹ (Bᵢ Bⱼ - ½ g_{ij} |B|²_g)`. -/
/-- Electromagnetic energy density `u = ½ (ε |E|²_g + |B|²_g / μ)`. -/
/-- **Covariance of the Maxwell stress tensor**: `T ↦ Jᵀ T J`. -/
/-- The trace of the mixed Maxwell stress is minus the energy density: `T^i_i = -u`. -/
/-! ## Acoustic radiation stress and the Gor'kov potential -/
/-- Real and imaginary parts of a complex covector. -/
/-- Imaginary part of a complex covector. -/

/-- Time-averaged velocity correlation `⟨vᵢ vⱼ⟩ = Re(wᵢ w̄ⱼ)/(2 ρ₀² ω²)` for the velocity
amplitude `v = w/(i ρ₀ ω)` of a pressure field with covariant gradient `w`. -/
/-- Time-averaged squared velocity `⟨v²⟩_g = g^{ij} ⟨vᵢ vⱼ⟩`. -/
/-- Acoustic Lagrangian density `𝓛 = ⟨p²⟩/(2 ρ₀ c₀²) - ρ₀ ⟨v²⟩_g / 2`, `⟨p²⟩ = |P|²/2`. -/

/-- The time-averaged **acoustic radiation stress** (Brillouin tensor) in curved coordinates:
`Π_{ij} = ρ₀ ⟨vᵢ vⱼ⟩ + 𝓛 g_{ij}`. -/

/-- The **Gor'kov potential** of a small sphere of radius `a` in curved coordinates:
`U = 2π a³ (|P|²/(6 ρ₀ c₀²) - g^{ij} Re(wᵢ w̄ⱼ)/(4 ρ₀ ω²))`. -/
/-- Pushing a complex covector through `Jᵀ` (real matrix). -/
/-- **Covariance of the acoustic radiation stress**: `Π ↦ Jᵀ Π J`. -/
/-- **The Gor'kov potential is a scalar**: it does not depend on the coordinates. -/

/-- The Gor'kov potential is the combination `2π a³ (2/3 · 𝓟 - 𝓚)` of potential and kinetic
energy densities: `U = 2π a³ (⟨p²⟩/(3ρ₀c₀²) - ρ₀⟨v²⟩_g/2)`. -/

/-- In flat Cartesian coordinates the curved Gor'kov potential is the Gor'kov potential of
`Sovereign.Taxonomy.gorkov`. -/
/-! ## The combined acoustic-optical stress -/

/-- The combined **acoustic-optical stress tensor** `Θ_{ij} = Π_{ij} + T_{ij}` of a pressure
field (amplitude `P`, covariant gradient `w`) and an optical field (`E`, `B`). -/
/-- **Covariance of the acoustic-optical stress**: `Θ ↦ Jᵀ Θ J`. -/

/-!
# A concrete multi-field projector with a positive critical Reynolds number

`sixEmitterProjector` drives one acoustic frequency through the six-emitter standing-wave array
of `Sovereign.Taxonomy.LevitationStandingWave` (pair phases `θ`) together with a single optical
plane wave of amplitude `A`. The optical dipole potential of a single plane wave is the constant
`-(α/4)|A|²`, so the landscape is the six-emitter Gor'kov potential shifted by a constant.

`sixEmitterProjector_critical_reynolds`: every point of the shifted trap lattice is a stable trap
of the multi-field landscape, it has a positive critical Reynolds number, and below it every
continuous flow perturbation leaves all force-Jacobian eigenvalues strictly negative near the
trap. This shows the hypotheses of the stability theorems are satisfiable by a genuine
acoustic-optical configuration.
-/
/-- Adding a constant does not change stable traps. -/
/-- The six-emitter standing-wave projector with one uniform optical plane wave. -/

/-- **A concrete multi-field trap with a positive critical Reynolds number.** For the six-emitter
standing wave plus a uniform optical plane wave, every point `xₙ - θ/k` of the trap lattice is a
stable trap of the multi-field landscape, and there are a stiffness `s > 0` and a ball around it
such that every continuous flow perturbation with Reynolds number below `Re_c = s / κ` leaves all
eigenvalues of the force Jacobian strictly negative on the ball. -/
