/-!
# Strictly negative Hessian eigenvalues of perturbed acoustic-optical traps

The radiation force on a levitated particle is `F = -∇U`, so its Jacobian is
`∂F/∂x = -Hess U` (`forceJacobian`). A trap is linearly stable exactly when this force Jacobian
has **strictly negative eigenvalues**, i.e. `Hess U` is positive definite
(`Sovereign.Taxonomy.IsStableTrap`).

* `FlowPerturbation Ω`: an arbitrary jointly continuous, time-dependent external perturbation
  `V(t, x)` (`C²` in space), driven by a flow of Reynolds number `Re = ρ u L / η`, whose
  curvature on the region `Ω` is bounded by `κ · Re`.
* `StiffnessCertificate U Ω s`: the (time-dependent) trapping landscape is `C²` with
  `Hess U ≥ s > 0` on `Ω`.
* `StiffnessCertificate.forceJacobian_eigenvalues_neg`: below the critical Reynolds number
  `Re_c = s/κ`, every eigenvalue of `-Hess(U + V)` is `≤ -(s - κ Re) < 0` on `Ω` at all times.
* `StiffnessCertificate.perturbed_isStableTrap`: equilibria of the perturbed landscape in `Ω` are
  stable traps.
* `StiffnessCertificate.exists_perturbed_trap`: an energy barrier (`TrapBarrier` of
  `LevitationCertificate`) with margin `> 2ν` survives perturbations of amplitude `≤ ν`, and the
  perturbed trap inside it is stable with strictly negative force-Jacobian eigenvalues.
* `IsStableTrap.exists_stiffness_ball`, `IsStableTrap.critical_reynolds`: every stable trap of a
  `C²` potential comes with a stiffness `s > 0`, a ball and hence a positive critical Reynolds
  number.
-/

/-- The force Jacobian (negative stiffness matrix) `∂Fᵢ/∂xⱼ = -∂ᵢ∂ⱼU` of the radiation force
`F = -∇U`. -/

/-- If the quadratic form of a symmetric matrix is bounded above by `c |v|²`, all its eigenvalues
are `≤ c`. -/

/-- **Uniform stiffness near a stable trap.** A stable trap `x` of a `C²` potential has a
neighbourhood ball on which the Hessian is uniformly bounded below by some `s > 0`. -/
/-! ## Reynolds number and flow perturbations -/

/-- The Reynolds number `Re = ρ u L / η` of the surrounding flow (fluid density `ρ`, flow
speed `u`, length scale `L`, dynamic viscosity `η`). -/

/-- The critical Reynolds threshold `Re_c = s / κ` of a trap of stiffness `s` against a flow
whose potential curvature grows like `κ · Re`. -/

/-- An **arbitrary continuous external perturbation** of the trapping landscape on the region
`Ω`, driven by a surrounding flow of Reynolds number `Re`: a time-dependent potential
`V(t, x)`, jointly continuous and `C²` in space, whose curvature on `Ω` is bounded by `κ · Re`
(the flow–curvature susceptibility law). -/
/-- Flow density, speed, length scale and viscosity. -/
/-- Curvature susceptibility of the trap to the flow. -/
/-- The perturbing potential. -/
/-- The Reynolds number of the perturbing flow. -/

/-- A **stiffness certificate** for a time-dependent trapping potential `U(t, ·)` on a region
`Ω`: `U(t, ·)` is `C²` and its Hessian is bounded below by `s > 0` on `Ω` at all times. -/
/-- The perturbed trapping landscape `U(t, ·) + V(t, ·)`. -/
/-- Below the critical Reynolds number the stiffness margin `s - κ Re` is positive. -/
/-- Perturbed curvature bound: `v ᵀ Hess(U+V) v ≥ (s - κ Re) |v|²` on `Ω`. -/

/-- **Strictly negative Hessian eigenvalues of the trap.** Under any continuous external flow
perturbation whose Reynolds number is below the critical threshold `Re_c = s/κ`, at every
point of the certified region and at every time, all eigenvalues of the force Jacobian
`∂F/∂x = -Hess(U + V)` are at most `-(s - κ Re) < 0`. -/

/-- Below the critical Reynolds number every equilibrium of the perturbed landscape inside the
certified region is a **stable trap** (and hence a strict local minimum). -/

/-- A trap barrier survives any continuous perturbation of amplitude `ν` when the barrier
margin exceeds `2ν`. -/

/-- **Persistence of the multi-field trap.** If at time `t` the unperturbed landscape has an
energy barrier of margin `> 2ν` on a ball inside the certified region, then for every
continuous flow perturbation of amplitude `≤ ν` on that ball and Reynolds number below the
critical threshold, the perturbed landscape has a stable trap inside the ball, at which all
eigenvalues of the force Jacobian are strictly negative. -/

/-- **Every stable trap has a positive critical Reynolds number.** For a `C²` trapping potential
with a stable trap at `x` there are a stiffness `s > 0` and a ball around `x` such that, for
every continuous flow perturbation on that ball whose Reynolds number is below
`Re_c = s / κ`, all eigenvalues of the perturbed force Jacobian are strictly negative
throughout the ball and at all times. -/

/-!
# The continuous multi-field synesthetic holographic projector

A `HolographicProjector F n m` drives, over a 3-dimensional bounding region `Ω ⊆ ℝ³` carrying
a spatial metric,

* `F` **acoustic frequencies**: for each frequency `ω_f` (medium `media f`) a phased array of `n`
  plane-wave emitters whose phases follow smooth programs `t ↦ phases f t`
  (continuous phase modulation, `Sovereign.Taxonomy.PlaneWaveArray.withPhases`);
* an **optical holographic wavefront** synthesised from `m` plane waves (angular spectrum) with
  complex amplitudes, wave vectors, polarisations and a smooth spatial-light-modulator phase
  program `t ↦ slm t`.

The trapping landscape of a small particle is
`U(t, x) = ∑_f U_Gor'kov(ω_f; t, x) - (α/4) |ψ(t, x)|²`: the time-averaged Gor'kov potentials of
the incommensurate acoustic frequencies add (cross-frequency interference averages out) and the
optical hologram contributes the dipole gradient potential of polarisability `α`.

Main results:

* `contDiff_trapPotential`: the landscape is `C²` at every time;
* `aoField`: at each time and frequency the projector defines a coupled acoustic-optical field
  on the curved chart; `projector_metric_invariance` is the acoustic-optical metric invariance
  theorem for the projector (multi-frequency Gor'kov potential scalar, total
  acoustic-optical stress `∑_f Π_f + T` covariant, principal stresses invariant), and in flat
  coordinates the curved multi-frequency Gor'kov potential is the acoustic part of the landscape
  (`curvedGorkov_flat`);
* `holographic_trap_stability`: under any continuous external flow perturbation below the
  critical Reynolds number, the force Jacobian of the multi-field trap has strictly negative
  eigenvalues throughout the certified region, equilibria are stable traps, and every energy
  barrier with enough margin encloses a strictly stable perturbed trap;
* `holographic_trap_critical_reynolds`: every stable trap of a frozen projector pattern has a
  positive critical Reynolds number;
* `cavity_trap_robust` (link with `Sovereign.Pipeline.Cavity`): the levitation trap certified by
  a `CavityStabilityCertificate` persists, strictly stable, under sub-critical perturbations;
* `trapPotential_reconstruction` (link with `Sovereign.Reconstruction`): the landscape is
  reconstructed from its samples on the grid `δℤ³` within `3 δ² M / 8`.
-/

/-! ## Metric invariance for the projector -/
/-- The coupled acoustic-optical field of acoustic channel `f` and the hologram at time `t`. -/
/-- The multi-frequency Gor'kov potential of a family of acoustic-optical fields. -/

/-- The total acoustic-optical stress `∑_f Π_f + T` (acoustic channels plus the Maxwell stress
of the hologram). -/

/-- In flat Cartesian coordinates the curved multi-frequency Gor'kov potential is the acoustic
part of the trapping landscape. -/
/-! ## Trap stability under continuous perturbations -/

/-- **Acoustic levitation trapping stability of the multi-field holographic projector.**
Suppose the landscape `U(t, ·)` has a stiffness certificate `Hess U ≥ s > 0` on the bounding
region `Ω`. Then for every arbitrary continuous external flow perturbation whose Reynolds
number is below the critical threshold `Re_c = s/κ`:
1. at every time and every point of `Ω` all eigenvalues of the perturbed force Jacobian
   `-Hess(U + V)` are `≤ -(s - κ Re) < 0`;
2. every equilibrium of the perturbed landscape in `Ω` is a stable trap;
3. every energy barrier of `U(t, ·)` inside `Ω` with margin `> 2ν` encloses a perturbed stable

-/

below which every continuous flow perturbation leaves the force-Jacobian eigenvalues strictly
negative near the trap. -/

/-- **Link with `Sovereign.Reconstruction`**: if `‖D²U(t, ·)‖ ≤ M` everywhere, the landscape is
reconstructed from its samples on the grid `δℤ³` within `3 δ² M / 8`. -/

/-- **Robustness of the cavity-certified levitation trap.** For a state in the attractor of a
`CavityStabilityCertificate`, suppose the calibrated trap potential has Hessian `≥ s > 0` on the
certificate ball and its energy barrier has margin `> 2ν`. Then under every continuous flow
perturbation of amplitude `≤ ν` with Reynolds number below `Re_c = s/κ`, the perturbed trap
exists inside the ball, is stable, and has strictly negative force-Jacobian eigenvalues. -/

/-!
# The acoustic-optical metric invariance theorem

Fields now live on a 3-dimensional **bounding chart** `Space3 = ℝ³` equipped with an arbitrary
Riemannian `SpatialMetric` `g(x)` (curved spatial coordinates). An `AOField` bundles

* a time-harmonic acoustic pressure field `p : ℝ³ → ℂ` (medium `M`, particle radius `a`),
* the covariant electric and magnetic fields `E, B : ℝ³ → ℝ³` of an optical wavefront
  (permittivity `ε`, permeability `μ`),

and the physical observables are the curved Gor'kov potential `gorkovField`, its radiation force
covector `F_i = -∂_i U` (`curvedForce`) and the acoustic-optical stress tensor
`Θ_{ij} = Π_{ij} + T_{ij}` (`aoStressField`, acoustic Brillouin stress + Maxwell stress).

A `CoordChange` is a differentiable map `φ` with everywhere invertible Jacobian `J`
(a local diffeomorphism). It pulls back the whole configuration: `g ↦ Jᵀ (g ∘ φ) J`,
`p ↦ p ∘ φ`, `E ↦ Jᵀ (E ∘ φ)`, `B ↦ Jᵀ (B ∘ φ)` (`AOField.pullback`).

**Acoustic-optical metric invariance** (`acoustic_optical_metric_invariance`): after pulling back,

1. the Gor'kov potential is a scalar, `U'(y) = U(φ y)` (the pressure gradient transforms by the
   chain rule, `pressureGrad_comp`);
2. the acoustic-optical stress is a covariant 2-tensor, `Θ'(y) = Jᵀ Θ(φ y) J`;
3. the principal stresses (characteristic polynomial of `Θ^i_j`) and `Θ^i_i` are unchanged;
4. the electromagnetic energy density is a scalar;
5. the radiation force is a covector, `F'(y) = Jᵀ F(φ y)` (`curvedForce_pullback`).

In flat Cartesian coordinates (`g = 1`) the curved Gor'kov potential is exactly
`Sovereign.Taxonomy.gorkov` (`gorkovField_flat`).

**Trap stability is chart independent**: for affine charts `y ↦ A y + b` (`A` invertible),
`Hess(U ∘ φ) = Aᵀ Hess U A` (`hessian_comp_affine`), so stable traps correspond exactly
(`isStableTrap_comp_affine_iff`); for rigid motions the Hessian spectrum is unchanged
(`charpoly_hessian_comp_orthogonal`). With the steering rotations of `Sovereign.Steering`
this gives `steering_trap_invariance`.
-/
/-! ## Jacobians and the chain rule -/
/-- The Jacobian matrix `J_{ij} = ∂φᵢ/∂yⱼ` of a map `φ : ℝ³ → ℝ³`. -/

/-- **Chain rule for the complex pressure gradient**: `∇(p ∘ φ) = Jᵀ (∇p ∘ φ)`, i.e. the
pressure gradient is a covector. -/
/-- Chain rule for gradients of scalars: `∇(f ∘ φ) = Jᵀ (∇f ∘ φ)`. -/
/-! ## Metrics, coordinate changes and acoustic-optical fields -/
/-- A Riemannian metric on the 3-dimensional bounding chart (curved spatial coordinates). -/
/-- Covariant metric components `g_{ij}(x)`. -/
/-- The flat Euclidean metric `g = 1`. -/
/-- A change of coordinates: a differentiable map with everywhere invertible Jacobian. -/
/-- Pullback of a metric: `(φ^* g)(y) = J(y)ᵀ g(φ y) J(y)`. -/
/-- A coupled **acoustic-optical field** on the curved bounding chart. -/
/-- Acoustic medium and driving frequency. -/
/-- Radius of the levitated particle. -/
/-- Permittivity and permeability of the optical medium. -/
/-- The spatial metric. -/
/-- Complex acoustic pressure amplitude. -/
/-- Covariant electric and magnetic fields of the optical wavefront. -/
/-- Pull back all fields along a change of coordinates. -/
/-- The curved **Gor'kov potential** of the acoustic field. -/
/-- The acoustic **radiation force** covector `F_i = -∂_i U`. -/
/-- The acoustic-optical stress tensor `Θ_{ij}` (covariant components). -/
/-- The Maxwell stress tensor `T_{ij}` of the optical field. -/
/-- The mixed acoustic-optical stress `Θ^i_j = g^{ik} Θ_{kj}`. -/
/-- The electromagnetic energy density. -/
/-- The Gor'kov potential is a scalar field: `U' = U ∘ φ`. -/
/-- The radiation force is a covector: `F'(y) = J(y)ᵀ F(φ y)`. -/

/-- The trace of the mixed Maxwell stress is minus the electromagnetic energy density, in any
curved coordinates. -/
/-- In flat Cartesian coordinates the curved Gor'kov potential is `Sovereign.Taxonomy.gorkov`. -/
/-! ## Chart independence of trap stability -/
/-- The linear part `y ↦ A y` of an affine chart as a continuous linear map. -/
/-- An affine change of coordinates `y ↦ A y + b` with `A` invertible. -/
/-- The Hessian transforms as a covariant 2-tensor under affine charts: `Aᵀ Hess U A`. -/

/-- **Stable traps are chart independent**: under an invertible affine change of coordinates,
`x` is a stable trap of `U ∘ φ` iff `φ x` is a stable trap of `U`. -/

/-- For rigid motions (`Aᵀ A = 1`) the Hessian spectrum (principal trap stiffnesses) is
unchanged. -/

/-- **Steering invariance**: rotating the whole acoustic-optical configuration with a steering
rotation `R = exp(θ G)` of `Sovereign.Steering` maps stable traps to stable traps, preserves the
Hessian spectrum, and transports the Gor'kov potential of any differentiable pressure field. -/

/-!
# Non-ergodic beam search on infinite combinatorial trees under Kelly stakes

A **combinatorial tree** (`CTree α`) has a root and a finite list of children for every node,
and every node has at least one child, so the tree is infinite. `level T n` lists the nodes at
depth `n`.

**Beam search** of width `w` keeps, at every depth, the `w` best children of the current beam
according to a scorer. The scorer may change from round to round, and in the stochastic
setting it may depend arbitrarily on the random outcome sequence `ω : ℕ → Bool`. No independence,
stationarity or ergodicity is assumed.

The search is funded by a **verification budget**. At round `n` it stakes a fraction `f n ω` of
its budget at net odds `b n`. The budget is multiplied by `1 + f b` if the round is productive
(`ω n = true`) and by `1 − f` otherwise (`Sovereign.Autonomous.factor`). The **logarithmic
Kelly stake** `f* = (p b − (1 − p)) / b` maximises the expected log-growth
`p log(1 + f b) + (1 − p) log(1 − f)` (`Sovereign.Autonomous.logGrowth_le_kelly`).

The search is **absorbed** at round `n` if its budget is `0` or its beam is empty. Both are
absorbing states: a search with no budget or no candidates can never resume.

## Results

* `beam_sub_level` — soundness: the beam at round `n` consists of depth-`n` nodes;
* `beam_ne_nil` — on an infinite tree a beam of positive width never becomes empty;
* `beam_perm_level`, `beam_complete` — **convergence**: if the width is at least the number of
  nodes at every depth up to `D`, the beam at depth `n ≤ D` is exactly level `n` (up to order),
  so every goal at depth `≤ D` is reached, whatever the scorers are;
* `budget_pos`, `log_budget` — for every stake with `1 + f b > 0` and `f < 1` (in particular the
  Kelly stake) the budget is positive on **every** outcome path, and its logarithm is the sum of
  the per-round log-factors;
* `absorbed_eq_empty`, `absorption_prob_zero`, `ae_never_absorbed` — **almost-sure absorption
  avoidance**: the absorption event is empty, so it has probability `0` under **every**
  probability law of the outcomes;
* `kelly_ae_converges` — under the Kelly stake, for every law `μ`, almost surely the search
  reaches every goal within depth `D` without ever being absorbed;
* `allIn_absorbed_ae` — by contrast, staking everything (`f = 1`) is absorbed almost surely under
  i.i.d. outcomes with success probability `p < 1`.
-/

/-- An infinite, finitely branching combinatorial tree: every node has a non-empty finite list
of children. -/
/-- The nodes at depth `n`, with multiplicity. -/
/-- The expansion of a list of nodes: all their children. -/
/-- Keep the `w` best elements of a list according to `score` (sorted by decreasing score). -/
/-- **Beam search** of width `w` with round-dependent scorers `score n`. -/
/-- **Soundness**: the beam at round `n` only contains depth-`n` nodes. -/
/-- **The beam never empties** on an infinite tree, whatever the scorers. -/

/-- **Wide beams are exhaustive**: if the width is at least the size of every level up to
depth `D`, the beam at depth `n ≤ D` is level `n` up to order. -/

/-- **Convergence of beam search**: with a wide enough beam, every goal at depth `n ≤ D` is in
the beam at round `n`, whatever the scorers. -/
/-! ### The Kelly-staked search process -/

/-- The verification budget under round-dependent, path-dependent stakes `f n ω` at net odds
`b n`. -/
/-- A stake is *hedged* if it can never lose the whole budget in one round. -/
/-- The logarithmic Kelly stake with beliefs `p n` and odds `b n`. -/
/-- Under a hedged stake the budget is positive on every outcome path. -/
/-- **Logarithmic growth, path by path**: `log B_n = ∑_{i<n} log(factor_i)`. -/
/-- With constant stake and odds, `kbudget` is the budget of `Sovereign.Autonomous.Ruin`. -/
/-- The beam of the search along the outcome path `ω`, with random scorers `S n ω`. -/
/-- **The absorption event**: at some round the budget is exhausted or the beam is empty. -/
/-- **No outcome path is ever absorbed** under a hedged stake with positive beam width. -/

/-- **Almost-sure absorption avoidance under every law.** For every measure `μ` on outcome
sequences (not necessarily independent, stationary or ergodic), a hedged beam search is absorbed
with probability `0`. -/

/-- **Almost-sure convergence of Kelly-staked beam search.** Under the logarithmic Kelly stake,
for every law `μ` of the outcomes and all random scorers: almost surely, the search is never
absorbed, its log-budget is the sum of its per-round log-factors, and, if the width covers every
level up to depth `D`, every goal `g` at depth `n ≤ D` is in the beam at round `n`. -/

/-- **All-in staking is absorbed almost surely**: with `f = 1` and i.i.d. outcomes of success
probability `p < 1`, the search is absorbed with probability one. -/

/-!
# Chain complexes and their homology

A **chain complex** `X` over a ring `R` is a sequence of `R`-modules `C₀, C₁, C₂, …` together
with boundary operators `d_k : C_{k+1} → C_k` (written `X.d k`) satisfying `d ∘ d = 0`
(`ChainCx.d_d`). (Our indexing: `X.d k` is the boundary *out of* degree `k + 1`, i.e. the
operator usually written `∂_{k+1}`.)

* `X.cycles k` — the `k`-cycles `Z_k = ker (∂_k)` (all of `C₀` in degree `0`);
* `X.boundaries k` — the `k`-boundaries `B_k = im (∂_{k+1})`, contained in the cycles
  (`boundaries_le_cycles`);
* `X.H k` — the homology module `H_k(X; R) = Z_k / B_k`;
* `X.betti k` — the `k`-th Betti number `b_k = rank_R H_k(X; R)`.

For `R = ℤ` these are the integral homology groups `H_k(X, ℤ)`.
-/
/-- A chain complex of `R`-modules indexed by `ℕ`, with boundary `d k : C (k+1) → C k`. -/
/-- the chain module in degree `k` -/
/-- the boundary operator `∂_{k+1} : C_{k+1} → C_k` -/

/-!
# Homology-preserving proof DAG compression

A proof certificate is a proof DAG `D : Dag R` together with a root index `k`; it certifies the
proof tree `unfold D k`. Its *byte length* is the length of its serialization
(`serialize enc (D, k)`: an 8-byte root index followed by the nodes, each encoded as a tag byte,
the rule's bytes `enc r` and 8-byte premise indices).

More generally we measure a DAG by an **index-free cost model** `cost : DNode R → ℕ` — the cost
of a node depends on its rule and arity but not on the numerical values of its premise indices
(`IndexFree`). The byte cost of `serialize` is index-free (`byteCost_indexFree`).

## Results

* `treeCost_le_of_betti` — **the universal lower bound**: *every* well-formed proof DAG whose
  derivation complex has `b₁ = 0` and which contains a node unfolding to `t` costs at least
  `treeCost cost t`, for every index-free cost model. This holds regardless of how the DAG was
  produced. The reason (`Deps.paths_le_one`) is that `b₁ = 0` forbids two different inference
  paths between two nodes, so every sub-proof occurrence of `t` needs a node of its own.
* `hcompress t` — the homology-preserving compressor (post-order linearisation of `t`):
  it unfolds to `t` (`unfold_hcompress`), is well-formed, its derivation complex has the
  homology of a point (`H₀ ≅ ℤ`, `H_k = 0` for `k ≥ 1`, in particular `b₁ = 0`), the DAG verifier
  returns exactly what the tree verifier returns, and it costs exactly `treeCost cost t`.
* `hcompress_isLeast`, `hcompress_isLeast_bytes` — hence `hcompress` **minimises** the cost, and
  in particular the certificate byte length, among all certificates of `t` with `b₁ = 0`.
* `dedup_betti_pos_of_lt` — the trade-off with unconstrained compression: whenever
  hash-consing (`Sovereign.Compression.dedup`) produces fewer nodes than the tree has, the
  compressed certificate necessarily has `b₁ ≥ 1`. So any size reduction beyond `hcompress`
  must break `b₁ = 0`.
-/
/-! ### Cost models -/

/-- A cost model for DAG nodes is *index-free* if the cost of a node does not depend on the
values of its premise indices. -/
/-- The cost of a proof tree: the sum of the costs of its inference steps. -/
/-- The cost of a proof DAG: the sum of the costs of its nodes. -/
/-- Node weights of a DAG, as a function of the node index. -/
/-! ### The lower bound -/

/-- In a well-formed DAG, every node unfolds to a tree whose cost is the weighted size of the
node in the dependency structure. -/

/-- **Universal lower bound for homology-preserving compression.** Every well-formed proof DAG
with first Betti number `b₁ = 0` that contains a node unfolding to the proof tree `t` costs at
least `treeCost cost t`, for every index-free cost model. -/
/-- Node-count form: a `b₁ = 0` proof DAG representing `t` has at least `t.size` nodes. -/
/-! ### The compressor -/
/-- Post-order linearisation of a proof tree into a proof DAG whose first node has index `o`. -/

/-- **The homology-preserving compressor**: the post-order linearisation of a proof tree,
with its root index. -/

/-- The compressed certificate has the homology of a point: `H₀ ≅ ℤ`, `H_k = 0` for `k ≥ 1`,
`b₀ = 1`, `b₁ = 0`, and no circular reasoning. -/
/-- The compressed certificate verifies to exactly what the proof tree verifies to. -/
/-- The certificates of `t` that preserve vanishing first homology. -/

/-- **Optimality of homology-preserving compression.** For every index-free cost model,
`hcompress t` is a certificate of `t` with `b₁ = 0` of least cost. -/
/-! ### Byte serialization -/
/-- Fixed-width 8-byte little-endian encoding of an index. -/
/-- Serialization of one node: tag byte, rule bytes, premise indices. -/
/-- Serialization of a proof certificate: root index, then all nodes. -/
/-- The byte cost of a node. -/

/-- **Homology-preserving compression minimises certificate byte length.** Among all
certificates of the proof tree `t` whose derivation complex has `b₁ = 0`, the one produced by
`hcompress` has the shortest serialization; its length is `8 + treeCost (byteCost enc) t`. -/
/-! ### Trade-off with unconstrained compression -/

/-- **Sharing breaks `b₁ = 0`.** If hash-consing produces a DAG with fewer nodes than the tree,
that DAG has first Betti number `b₁ ≥ 1`. -/

The proof space is `Sovereign.HyperBeam.exSpace`: goal `2 = 2`, two tactics (`0` =
reflexivity, `1` = a `sorry` hole), certified by the strict, `sorry`-rejecting kernel. The
Poincaré-guided arm proposes nothing (a worst-case guide), so the engine must rely on its
exhaustive hedge and therefore on surviving an unproductive round.

* `kelly_goal_valid` — the certificate returned by the engine yields the Lean theorem that the
  goal `2 = 2` is valid, via soundness of the strict kernel.

/-!
# Homology of formal proof DAGs

A formal proof DAG is stored, as in `Sovereign.Compression.Dag`, as a list of inference nodes,
each referring to its premises by their *indices* in the list. Forgetting the rule labels we
obtain its **dependency structure** `d : Deps = List (List ℕ)` (`d[k]` = premise indices of node
`k`). Its **derivation complex** `Deps.cx d` is the simplicial chain complex (`Digraph.cx`) of
the graph with one vertex per node and one edge from each premise occurrence to the node that
uses it.

* `Deps.WF d` — every node refers only to strictly earlier nodes (the condition enforced by the
  DAG verifier `checkDag`, cf. `Dag.WellFormed` and `wf_deps_iff`);
* `Deps.not_circular` — a well-formed proof DAG never contains circular reasoning;
* `Deps.betti_one_eq_zero` — if moreover no intermediate result is used twice
  (`d.flatten.Nodup`), then `H₁ = 0` and `b₁ = 0`;
* `Deps.TreeShaped d` — well-formed, sharing-free and every non-final node is used: the
  dependency structure of a proof *tree*. Then `H₀ ≅ ℤ` and `H_k = 0` for `k ≥ 1`
  (`Deps.homology_tree`): the derivation complex has the homology of a point;
* `diamond` — a well-formed DAG with a shared lemma has `b₁ ≥ 1` without being circular, so
  `b₁ = 0` is sufficient but not necessary for non-circularity of DAGs *with sharing*.
-/

/-- Edges of the dependency graph: a node together with one of its premise slots that refers
to an existing node. -/

/-- **The derivation complex** of a proof DAG. -/
/-- Every node refers only to strictly earlier nodes. -/
/-- **Well-formed proof DAGs contain no circular reasoning.** -/
/-- Sharing-free proof DAGs: the source map of the dependency graph is injective. -/
/-- **Valid sharing-free derivations have vanishing `H₁`.** -/
/-- **Valid sharing-free derivations have first Betti number `b₁ = 0`.** -/

/-- The dependency structure of a proof tree: well-formed, non-empty, sharing-free, and every
node except the last (the root) is used as a premise. -/
/-- The root (last node) of a non-empty proof DAG. -/

/-!
# Poincaré–Verdier duality for derivation complexes

For a chain complex `X` of finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field `K`, the **dual
cochain complex** has cochains `Cᵏ = (C_k)^∨ = Hom_K(C_k, K)` and coboundary
`δᵏ = (∂_{k+1})^∨ : Cᵏ → Cᵏ⁺¹` (`ChainCx.cod`). Its cohomology `Hᵏ(X^∨)` (`ChainCx.coH`) and Betti
numbers `bᵏ` (`ChainCx.cobetti`) are defined as usual.

* `ChainCx.finrank_coH` — `dim Hᵏ(X^∨) = dim H_k(X)`;
* `ChainCx.duality` — **duality**: `Hᵏ(X^∨) ≅ H_k(X)^∨` for every `k`.

This is the finite-dimensional form of Verdier duality over a point: for a finite complex over
a field, the dualizing complex of a point is `K`, and Verdier duality reduces to
`Hᵏ(Hom(X, K)) ≅ Hom(H_k(X), K)`. (Classical Poincaré duality `Hᵏ ≅ H_{n−k}` needs a closed
oriented `n`-manifold, which a proof DAG is not; the degree-preserving form proved here is
the statement that applies to arbitrary finite complexes.)

For the derivation complex of a graph over `K` (`Digraph.cxOver K`):

* `Digraph.euler` — the **Euler–Poincaré formula** `b₀ + |E| = |V| + b₁`, and hence also
  `b⁰ + |E| = |V| + b¹`;
* `hcompress_duality` — the certificate produced by homology-preserving compression has, over
  every field, `b₀ = b⁰ = 1`, `b₁ = b¹ = 0` and `b_k = bᵏ = 0` for `k ≥ 2`, with
  `Hᵏ ≅ (H_k)^∨` in every degree.
-/
/-- The `k`-cocycles `Zᵏ = ker δᵏ`. -/
/-- The `k`-coboundaries `Bᵏ = im δᵏ⁻¹` (zero in degree `0`). -/
/-- The coboundaries as a submodule of the cocycles. -/
/-- The cohomology `Hᵏ(X^∨) = Zᵏ / Bᵏ` of the dual complex. -/
/-- The `k`-th Betti number of the dual complex. -/
/-- **Dimensions agree**: `dim Hᵏ(X^∨) = dim H_k(X)`. -/
/-- **Duality**: `Hᵏ(X^∨) ≅ H_k(X)^∨` for every `k`. -/
/-- **Euler–Poincaré formula** for a graph over a field: `b₀ + |E| = |V| + b₁`. -/
/-- The Euler–Poincaré formula for the dual (cohomological) Betti numbers. -/
/-! ### Duality for compressed certificates -/

/-- **Poincaré–Verdier duality for compressed certificates.** Over every field `K`, the
derivation complex of `hcompress t` satisfies `Hᵏ ≅ (H_k)^∨` in every degree, with
`b₀ = b⁰ = 1`, `b₁ = b¹ = 0` and `b_k = bᵏ = 0` for `k ≥ 2`. -/

  | 0, d, B => scan P (K.candidates d B)
  | r + 1, d, B =>
    if (scan P (K.candidates d B)).1.isSome then scan P (K.candidates d B)
    else if 0 < B * factorQ K.stake K.odds (win P K d B) then
      ((loop r (d + 1) (B * factorQ K.stake K.odds (win P K d B))).1,
        (scan P (K.candidates d B)).2 +
          (loop r (d + 1) (B * factorQ K.stake K.odds (win P K d B))).2)
    else (none, (scan P (K.candidates d B)).2)

/-!
# The Kelly–Poincaré search engine

The engine searches the tree of proof states of a `Sovereign.HyperBeam.ProofSpace` by iterative
deepening. At depth `d` with verification budget `B` it

1. passes the proposals of the **Poincaré-guided arm** — an arbitrary, untrusted proposal
   function `guide d B` (for instance the hyperbolic beam layer of `Sovereign.HyperBeam`),
   truncated to the beam width — through the certification gate;
2. then passes every node of depth `d` (the **exhaustive hedge**) through the gate;
3. stops as soon as the gate accepts a node, returning the certified proof path;
4. otherwise settles the round's wager with the **Kelly rule**: the budget is multiplied by
   `1 + f·o` if the guided arm proposed a non-circular node and by `1 − f` otherwise (stake
   fraction `f`, net odds `o`), and continues at depth `d + 1` if the budget is still positive
   and the depth bound has not been reached.

Budgets are rational numbers so that the whole engine is executable (and can be run by the Lean
kernel via `decide`); `factorQ_cast` identifies them with the real-valued budget process of
`Sovereign.Autonomous.Ruin`.

Main results (`K` any configuration, the guide arbitrary):
* `loop_cost_le` / `kp_cost_le` — **finite time**: the engine performs at most
  `Σ_{k ≤ D} (w + bᵏ)` certification-gate checks (`w` the beam width, `D` the depth bound);
* `kp_sound` — **certified output**: a returned certificate is accepted by the kernel for the
  goal, is valid for every sound kernel, is cut-free and fixed by cut elimination, never reuses
  its goal, lies on a non-circular path, and its derivation complex has `H₀ ≅ ℤ`, `H_k = 0`
  (`k ≥ 1`), `b₁ = 0` and no circular reasoning;
* `kp_complete` — **completeness under Kelly staking**: with the Kelly stake `f* = (p·o − q)/o`
  (`0 < p < 1`, `o > 0`) the budget never reaches `0`, so whenever some node of depth `≤ D`
  passes the gate, the engine returns a certificate;
* `factorQ_allIn_false` — with the all-in stake `f = 1` a single unproductive round ruins the
  budget (demonstrated in `Sovereign.ProofHomology.Demo`).
-/
/-! ### Rational Kelly staking -/
/-- The Kelly fraction `(p·o − (1 − p)) / o`, over `ℚ`. -/
/-- The budget multiplier of one round: `1 + f·o` on a win, `1 − f` on a loss. -/
/-- **The Kelly multiplier is always positive**, on wins and on losses. -/
/-- The all-in stake `f = 1` loses the whole budget on an unproductive round. -/
/-! ### The engine -/
/-- Configuration of the Kelly–Poincaré engine. -/
/-- the Poincaré-guided proposals at depth `d` under budget `B` (untrusted) -/
/-- beam width: at most this many guided proposals are checked per round -/
/-- depth bound -/
/-- stake fraction -/
/-- net odds of a round -/
/-- The guided proposals of a round, truncated to the beam width. -/
/-- All candidates of a round: the guided arm first, then the exhaustive hedge. -/
/-- The outcome of a round's wager: did the guided arm propose a non-circular node? -/

/-- Pass a list of nodes through the certification gate, stopping at the first acceptance;
returns the certificate (if any) and the number of gate checks performed. -/

/-- The main loop: `r` remaining rounds, current depth `d`, current budget `B`. Returns the
certificate (if any) and the total number of gate checks. -/
/-- **The Kelly–Poincaré engine**: start at depth `0` with budget `1`. -/
/-! ### Properties of the scan -/
/-! ### Finite time -/
/-- **Finite time**: the loop performs at most `Σ_{i ≤ r} (w + b^(d+i))` gate checks. -/

/-- **The engine terminates in finite time**: it performs at most `Σ_{k ≤ D} (w + bᵏ)`
certification-gate (kernel) checks, where `w` is the beam width and `D` the depth bound. -/
/-! ### Certified output -/

/-- Every certificate returned by the loop was accepted by the certification gate at a
candidate of some round. -/

/-- **Soundness of the Kelly–Poincaré engine.** A certificate returned by the engine was
accepted by the certification gate at a candidate of some round `d ≤ D`; it is accepted by the
kernel as a proof of the goal, proves a valid goal whenever the kernel is sound,
is cut-free and a fixed point of cut elimination, never uses the goal in its own derivation, lies
on a non-circular search path, and its derivation complex has the homology of a point
(`H₀ ≅ ℤ`, `H_k = 0` for `k ≥ 1`), vanishing first Betti number and no circular reasoning. -/
/-! ### Completeness under Kelly staking -/

/-- **Completeness of the Kelly–Poincaré engine.** With the Kelly stake `f* = (p·o − q)/o`
(`0 < p < 1`, `o > 0`) the verification budget stays positive in every round, whatever the
outcomes; hence if some node of depth at most `D` passes the certification gate, the engine
returns a certificate (within the finite time bound of `kp_cost_le`). -/

/-!
# The simplicial chain complex of a dependency graph

A finite directed (multi)graph `G` — vertices `V`, edges `E`, each edge `e` running from
`src e` to `tgt e` — is a one-dimensional simplicial (cell) complex. Its integral chain complex
`G.cx` is

`0 ← C₀ = ℤ^V ←∂₁— C₁ = ℤ^E ← 0 ← 0 ← ⋯`,   `∂₁ e = tgt e − src e`

(`Digraph.bd` is the incidence matrix). For proof DAGs the vertices are inference nodes and an
edge runs from each premise to the conclusion it is used for.

Main results:
* `H1Equiv` — `H₁(G; ℤ) ≅ ker ∂₁` (there are no 2-cells), `betti_one` — `b₁ = rank ker ∂₁`;
* `H_subsingleton` — `H_k(G; ℤ) = 0` for `k ≥ 2`;
* `H0Equiv` — `H₀(G; ℤ) ≅ ℤ` when every vertex is joined by a monotone edge path to a root;
* **circular reasoning is homologically visible**: a closed directed walk (`Circular`) yields a
  non-zero `1`-cycle, so `b₁ ≥ 1` (`betti_one_pos_of_circular`); hence `b₁ = 0` rules out circular
  reasoning (`not_circular_of_betti_one_eq_zero`);
* a ranking with `rank (src e) < rank (tgt e)` rules out closed directed walks
  (`not_circular_of_ranked`);
* `ker_bd_eq_bot` — if in addition every vertex is used as a premise (source) at most once, then
  `ker ∂₁ = 0`, i.e. `H₁(G; ℤ) = 0` and `b₁ = 0`.
-/
/-- A finite directed multigraph. -/
/-- the premise end of an edge -/
/-- the conclusion end of an edge -/
/-- The incidence number of edge `e` at vertex `v`: `[tgt e = v] − [src e = v]`. -/
/-- The boundary operator `∂₁ : ℤ^E → ℤ^V`, `∂₁ e = tgt e − src e`. -/
/-- The chain modules of a graph. -/
/-- The boundary maps of a graph: `∂₁` in degree `1`, zero above. -/
/-- **The integral simplicial chain complex of a graph.** -/
/-- `b₁(G) = rank_ℤ ker ∂₁`. -/
/-! ### Degree zero -/
/-- The augmentation `ε : ℤ^V → ℤ`, the sum of all coefficients. -/
/-- The unit vector at a vertex. -/

/-- **Connectivity**: if some vertex `root` is such that every other vertex is the source of an
edge going strictly up in a ranking, then every `0`-chain with coefficient sum `0` is a boundary. -/
-- every `vtx v - vtx root` is a boundary

/-- **`H₀(G; ℤ) ≅ ℤ`** for a graph in which every vertex other than a root is the source of an
edge going strictly up in a ranking. -/
/-! ### Circular reasoning -/

/-- A **closed directed walk** (a circular chain of inferences): a non-empty list of edges in
which each edge ends where the next one starts, and the last ends where the first starts. -/
/-- **Circular reasoning**: the dependency graph has a closed directed walk. -/
/-- The `1`-chain counting the edges of a walk. -/
/-- The edge-count chain of a closed walk is a non-zero `1`-cycle. -/
/-- **Circular reasoning is detected by homology**: a closed directed walk gives `b₁ ≥ 1`. -/
/-- **Vanishing first Betti number rules out circular reasoning.** -/
/-- A strictly increasing ranking along edges rules out closed directed walks. -/

/-- **Tree-shaped dependency graphs have `ker ∂₁ = 0`.** If a ranking increases strictly along
every edge and every vertex is the source of at most one edge (every intermediate result is
used at most once), then there is no non-zero `1`-cycle. -/
/-- Tree-shaped dependency graphs have `H₁(G; ℤ) = 0`. -/
/-- Tree-shaped dependency graphs have first Betti number `b₁ = 0`. -/

/-!
# The chain complex of a dependency graph over an arbitrary coefficient ring

`Sovereign.ProofHomology.Graph` builds the *integral* chain complex of a directed multigraph.
Here we build the same complex with coefficients in any commutative ring `R`
(`Digraph.cxOver R`), with boundary `∂₁ = Digraph.bdR R`, `∂₁ e = tgt e − src e`.

* `bdR_int` — for `R = ℤ` the boundary is the integral boundary `Digraph.bd`;
* `H1EquivOver` — `H₁(G; R) ≅ ker ∂₁`;
* `ker_bdR_eq_bot` — a ranked graph in which every vertex is the source of at most one edge has
  no non-zero `1`-cycles over any `R`;
* `ker_bd_eq_bot_of_betti` — over `ℤ`, `b₁ = 0` forces `ker ∂₁ = 0` (the integral cycle group
  is free, so rank `0` means trivial).
-/
/-- The boundary operator `∂₁ : R^E → R^V` with coefficients in `R`. -/
/-- The unit vector at a vertex, with coefficients in `R`. -/
/-- Over `ℤ`, `bdR` is the integral boundary operator. -/
/-- The chain modules of a graph over `R`. -/
/-- The boundary maps over `R`: `∂₁` in degree `1`, zero above. -/
/-- **The simplicial chain complex of a graph with coefficients in `R`.** -/
/-- **Tree-shaped graphs have no `1`-cycles over any coefficient ring.** -/
/-- Over `ℤ`, a vanishing first Betti number means there are no non-zero `1`-cycles. -/

    (∀ s, L.Reach s → L.safe s = true) ∧
      Nonempty ((Deps.cx (treeDeps t)).H 0 ≃ₗ[ℤ] ℤ) ∧

    (∀ G : Digraph, G.Circular → 0 < G.cx.betti 1) ∧

/-!
# Main theorems: homology of formal proof DAGs and the Kelly–Poincaré engine

* `closedLoop_certificate_homology`, `repair_certificate_homology` — every proof tree emitted by
  the closed-loop synthesizer of `Sovereign.ClosedLoop` and by the repair engine of
  `Sovereign.InvariantRepair` proves the loop safe, and its derivation complex has `H₀ ≅ ℤ`,
  `H_k = 0` for `k ≥ 1`, `b₁ = 0` and no circular reasoning;
* `proof_homology_main` — the homological picture of formal proofs: well-formed proof DAGs are
  never circular, circular reasoning always forces `b₁ ≥ 1`, cut-free proof trees have `b₁ = 0`,
  cut elimination preserves both the conclusion and every integral homology group, and checked
  DAGs are sound by transfinite induction;
* `kelly_poincare_main` — the Kelly–Poincaré engine terminates after a bounded number of kernel
  checks, every returned certificate is kernel-accepted, valid, cut-free, non-circular and has
  `b₁ = 0`, and under Kelly staking it is complete up to its depth bound.
-/
/-- **Certificates of the closed-loop synthesizer have the homology of a point.** -/
/-- **Certificates of the invariant-repair engine have the homology of a point.** -/

/-- **Main theorem of the Kelly–Poincaré search engine.** For every proof space and every
engine configuration (with an arbitrary, untrusted guide) whose stake is the Kelly fraction
`f* = (p·o − q)/o` with `0 < p < 1` and odds `o > 0`:
1. **finite time** — the engine performs at most `Σ_{k ≤ D} (w + bᵏ)` kernel checks;
2. **certified output** — every returned certificate is accepted by the kernel for the goal,
   proves a valid goal for every sound kernel, is cut-free, lies on a non-circular path, and its
   derivation complex has `b₁ = 0` and no circular reasoning;
3. **completeness** — if some node of depth at most `D` passes the certification gate, the
   engine returns a certificate. -/

/-!
# Path counting in proof DAGs, and why `b₁ = 0` forbids sharing

For a dependency structure `d : Deps` and nodes `v, r`, `Deps.paths d v r` counts the directed
inference paths from `v` down to `r`; this is the number of times the sub-proof at `v` occurs in
the proof tree obtained by unfolding node `r`. `Deps.wsize d w r` is the total weight of that
unfolded tree when node `i` carries weight `w i`.

* `sum_paths_mul` — `wsize d w r = ∑_v paths d v r * w v`: every occurrence in the unfolded tree
  is a path in the DAG;
* `exists_path_chain` — a path from `v` to `p` gives a `1`-chain with boundary `p − v`;
* `paths_le_one` — **if the derivation complex has no non-zero `1`-cycles, every node occurs at
  most once in every unfolding**: two different paths from `v` to `r` would differ by a non-zero
  cycle;
* `wsize_le_of_betti` — hence, for a well-formed DAG with `b₁ = 0`, the unfolded tree of any node
  weighs at most as much as the whole DAG.
-/

/-- The number of directed inference paths from node `v` to node `r` (following premise
references, which must point strictly downwards). -/
/-- The weight of the proof tree unfolded from node `r`, when node `i` has weight `w i`. -/

/-- **Occurrences are paths**: the weight of the tree unfolded from `r` is the path-count
weighted sum of the node weights. -/

/-- A list whose terms are at most `1` and sum to at least `2` has two positive terms in
different positions. -/

/-- **A path is a chain**: if there is a path from `v` to `p`, there is a `1`-chain with
boundary `p − v`, supported on edges whose conclusion is at most `p`. -/

/-- **No non-zero `1`-cycles ⇒ no sharing**: in a well-formed DAG whose derivation complex has
no non-zero `1`-cycles over a non-trivial ring, there is at most one inference path between any
two nodes. -/

/-- **`b₁ = 0` bounds the unfolded proof by the DAG.** For a well-formed dependency structure
whose derivation complex has first Betti number `0`, the tree unfolded from any node has total
weight at most the total weight of all nodes. -/

/-!
# Autonomous transfinite-induction verification of proof DAGs

`Sovereign.Synthesis.Ordinal` provides ordinal-ranked proof DAGs (`RankedDag`) and the
transfinite induction principle `RankedDag.induction` with its soundness corollary
`RankedDag.sound`. Here the verifier builds such a ranking **by itself** from a checked
`Sovereign.Compression` proof DAG, with no ranking supplied by the user:

* `RuleSystem.proofSystem S` — the one-step inference relation of a rule system;
* `checkedDag S D hD` — for a well-formed DAG `D`, the nodes accepted by the DAG verifier
  `checkDag` form an ordinal-ranked proof DAG (rank = position in the list, premises = the
  referenced nodes);
* `checkDag_sound_transfinite` — **soundness of DAG verification by transfinite induction**:
  every formula accepted by `checkDag` on a well-formed DAG is valid for every notion of
  validity for which the rules are sound;
* `checkedDag_acyclic` — the same ranking shows that the dependency graph has no circular
  reasoning.
-/

/-- The one-step inference relation of a rule system: `φ` follows from the premises `P` if some
rule applied to a list of formulas from `P` concludes `φ`. -/
/-- The nodes of a DAG accepted by the DAG verifier. -/

/-- **The autonomously ranked proof DAG** of a well-formed DAG: its checked nodes, ranked by
their position, with the referenced nodes as premises. -/

/-- **Soundness of DAG verification by transfinite induction.** For a well-formed DAG, every
formula accepted by the DAG verifier is valid, for every notion of validity for which the rules
are sound. The proof builds the ordinal ranking `checkedDag` and applies the transfinite
induction principle `RankedDag.sound`. -/

/-- The premise relation of the autonomously ranked DAG is well-founded, and the dependency
graph of a well-formed DAG contains no circular reasoning. -/

comments.text:
/-!
# Derivation complexes of proof trees and cut elimination

The *shape* of a proof (`Shape`) records only its premise structure. Flattening a shape in
post-order (`Shape.deps`) yields the dependency structure of the proof, a list of nodes each
referring to its premises by index, with the conclusion last. This applies both to cut-free
proof trees (`PTree R`) and to proofs with cuts (`Sovereign.Synthesis.CProof R`), whose `cut`
nodes have two premises (the lemma and its use) and whose lemma references `hyp i` are leaves.

* `Shape.treeShaped` — the flattening of every shape is tree-shaped (`Deps.TreeShaped`);
* `ptree_homology` — **the derivation complex of every proof tree has `H₀ ≅ ℤ`, `H_k = 0`
  (`k ≥ 1`), `b₁ = 0` and contains no circular reasoning**;
* `elim_preserves_homology` — **cut elimination preserves the integral homology groups**: for a
  proof with cuts `p` and a cut-free tree `t` (in particular its cut elimination
  `t = elim [] p`), `H_k(C(p); ℤ) ≅ H_k(C(t); ℤ)` for every `k`, so all Betti numbers agree;
* `cut_elimination_homology` — for every closed proof with cuts that checks with conclusion `φ`,
  cut elimination succeeds, the cut-free tree proves `φ`, and the homology is preserved.

Both complexes have the homology of a point; this is what makes the preservation hold. The
*sharing* presentation behaves differently: `sharing_betti_pos` exhibits a compressed proof DAG
(`Sovereign.Synthesis.compress`) with `b₁ ≥ 1` whose unfolding, a tree, has `b₁ = 0`.
-/
/-- The premise structure of a proof: unary and binary inference steps over leaves. -/
/-- Number of nodes. -/

/-- Post-order flattening of a shape into a dependency structure; `o` is the index of the
first node. -/
/-- **The flattening of every proof shape is tree-shaped.** -/
/-- The shape of a cut-free proof tree. -/

/-- The shape of a proof with cuts: `cut a b` has the two premises `a` (the lemma) and `b`
(its use); a lemma reference `hyp i` is a leaf. -/
/-- The dependency structure (proof DAG without sharing) of a proof tree. -/
/-- The dependency structure of a proof with cuts. -/

/-- **Valid deductive derivations have vanishing first Betti number.** The derivation complex
of every proof tree has `H₀ ≅ ℤ`, `H_k = 0` for `k ≥ 1`, `b₀ = 1`, `b₁ = 0`, and contains no
circular reasoning. -/

/-- **Cut elimination preserves the integral homology groups** `H_k(C, ℤ)` of the derivation
complex, in every degree `k`: the derivation complex of any proof with cuts `p` and that of any
cut-free proof tree `t` — in particular of `t = elim [] p` — have isomorphic homology. -/

/-- Cut elimination preserves all Betti numbers (for any proof with cuts `p` and any cut-free
tree `t`, in particular `t = elim [] p`). -/

/-- **Cut elimination with homology.** Every closed proof with cuts that checks with conclusion
`φ` is transformed by cut elimination into a cut-free proof tree of `φ`; the integral homology
of the derivation complex is preserved in every degree, and the cut-free derivation has
`b₁ = 0` and no circular reasoning. -/
/-! ### Sharing creates homology that cut elimination removes -/

/-- The compressed (shared) proof DAG of the one-cut chain `cut (leaf ()) (binary () #0 #0)`:
the lemma is stored once and used twice. -/

/-- **Sharing is visible in `H₁`.** The compressed proof DAG of the one-cut chain has `b₁ ≥ 1`
(the lemma node is joined to its user by two parallel edges), while the cut-free tree obtained
by cut elimination has `b₁ = 0`. Neither is circular. -/

comments.text:
/-!
# The universal coefficient theorem for proof chain complexes

For a proof chain complex `X : ChainCx R` over a commutative ring `R` and a coefficient module
`M`, the complex `X.tensorLeft M` has chains `M ⊗ C_k` and boundaries `1 ⊗ ∂`.

* `ChainCx.tor1 X M k = ker (M ⊗ B_k ⟶ M ⊗ C_k)` — the **homological intersection** of the
  boundary branch `B_k` with the coefficient module: the `Tor₁` term. When the complex splits it
  is `ker (M ⊗ B_k ⟶ M ⊗ Z_k)`, i.e. `Tor₁(M, H_k)` computed from the resolution
  `0 ⟶ B_k ⟶ Z_k ⟶ H_k ⟶ 0` (`tor1_eq_ker_resolution`); it vanishes for flat `M`
  (`tor1_eq_bot_of_flat`).
* `ChainCx.uctZero` — `H_0(M ⊗ X) ≃ M ⊗ H_0(X)` (right exactness).
* `ChainCx.uct` — **universal coefficient theorem**: if every boundary map `C_{k+1} ↠ B_k`
  splits (e.g. `B_k` projective, `uct_of_projective`; or `R` a PID and the chains finite free,
  `uct_of_pid`), then
    `H_{k+1}(M ⊗ X) ≃ (M ⊗ H_{k+1}(X)) × Tor₁(M, H_k(X))`,
  i.e. the universal coefficient sequence `0 → M ⊗ H_{k+1} → H_{k+1}(M ⊗ X) → Tor₁ → 0` exists
  and splits.
-/

/-- Homology at the middle of a split short exact sequence `0 → N → A → Q → 0`, where the
outgoing differential factors through `A ↠ Q` and the incoming one through `N ↪ A`. -/
/-- The proof chain complex with coefficients in `M`: chains `M ⊗ C_k`, boundary `1 ⊗ ∂`. -/

/-- The `Tor₁` term of the universal coefficient theorem in degree `k`:
`ker (M ⊗ B_k ⟶ M ⊗ C_k)`. -/
/-- The boundary maps of `X` split: each `C_{k+1} ↠ B_k` has a section. -/
/-- **Universal coefficients in degree `0`**: `H_0(M ⊗ X) ≃ M ⊗ H_0(X)`. -/

/-- **Universal coefficient theorem** for proof chain complexes: if the boundary maps split,
`H_{k+1}(M ⊗ X) ≃ (M ⊗ H_{k+1}(X)) × Tor₁`. -/
/-- Projective boundary modules make the boundary maps split. -/

/-- Over a principal ideal domain, a proof complex of finite free chain modules has split
boundary maps. -/
/-- **Universal coefficient theorem over a PID** for finite free proof complexes. -/
/-- With split boundaries, the cycles are a direct summand of the chains. -/

/-- **`tor1` is `Tor₁` of the homology**: with split boundaries,
`tor1 = ker (M ⊗ B_k ⟶ M ⊗ Z_k)`, the first homology of `M ⊗ (0 ⟶ B_k ⟶ Z_k)`, where
`0 ⟶ B_k ⟶ Z_k ⟶ H_k ⟶ 0` is a resolution of `H_k` by summands of chain modules. -/
/-- `Tor₁` vanishes for flat coefficients. -/
/-- **Flat coefficients**: `H_{k+1}(M ⊗ X) ≃ M ⊗ H_{k+1}(X)` when the boundaries split. -/

comments.text:
/-!
# Main theorems: universal homology-preserving compression, duality, and Kelly beam search

* `universal_compression_main` — for every proof tree `t` and every byte encoding of rules, the
  homology-preserving compressor `hcompress`:
  - produces a certificate of `t` with `b₁ = 0`;
  - has the shortest serialization among **all** certificates of `t` with `b₁ = 0`;
  - verifies exactly like `t` under every rule system;
  - satisfies Poincaré–Verdier duality over every field (`Hᵏ ≅ (H_k)^∨`, `b⁰ = b₀ = 1`,
    `b¹ = b₁ = 0`).
  Moreover, any compression below the tree size by hash-consing forces `b₁ ≥ 1`.
* `share_example` — a concrete instance: the tree `binary () (leaf ()) (leaf ())` is
  hash-consed to 2 nodes with `b₁ ≥ 1`, while its `b₁ = 0`-optimal certificate has 3 nodes.
* `beam_kelly_main` — Kelly-staked beam search on an infinite combinatorial tree is never
  absorbed, under every probability law of the outcomes, and converges (finds every goal within
  the covered depth) almost surely; all-in staking is absorbed almost surely.
* `binTree` — the infinite binary tree of bit strings, with `2ⁿ` nodes at depth `n`; a beam of
  width `2ᴰ` finds every bit string of length `≤ D`.
-/
/-- **Universal homology-preserving proof DAG compression.** -/
/-- The tree `binary () (leaf ()) (leaf ())`: one inference from two identical leaves. -/

/-- **Sharing versus homology, concretely.** Hash-consing stores the repeated leaf once (2
nodes) and thereby creates a `1`-cycle (`b₁ ≥ 1`), while the `b₁ = 0`-optimal certificate has 3
nodes; with an empty rule encoding it is 27 bytes long. -/
/-! ### Beam search -/
/-- **Non-ergodic Kelly beam search: almost-sure absorption avoidance and convergence.** -/
/-- The infinite binary tree of bit strings. -/

/-- **Kelly beam search on the infinite binary tree.** With width `2ᴰ` and any random scorers,
under every law of the outcomes, almost surely every bit string of length `≤ D` is reached at
the round equal to its length, without the search ever being absorbed. -/

/-!
# Sovereign.ProofHomology Root Index

Proof DAG homology, transfinite induction verifiers, universal DAG compression, and Kelly-Poincaré search engines:
- Complex: Chain complexes C_k, boundary maps d_k, homology groups H_k, and Betti numbers
- Graph & GraphRing: Integral and ring-coefficient chain complexes, cycle detection, vanishing H_1
- PathCount: Directed path multiplicity bounds, path uniqueness under vanishing 1-cycles
- Deps: Proof DAG complexes, acyclicity, and non-circularity invariants
- Trees: Proof tree homology (b_1 = 0) and homological invariance under cut-elimination
- Duality: Dual cochain complexes, Poincaré-Verdier duality H^k(X^v) = H_k(X)^v, Euler-Poincaré formula
- DagCompression: Universal minimal byte-length serialization for b_1 = 0 certificates (hcompress)
- Transfinite: Transfinite induction verification of proof DAG validity
- Engine & BeamKelly: Kelly-Poincaré proof search on combinatorial trees, almost-sure absorption avoidance
- Demo: Kernel evaluation of reflection proofs and Kelly stake comparisons
- Universal & Main: Unified interface connecting ClosedLoop and InvariantRepair certificates
- Checks: Kernel certification checking core theorems against standard Lean axioms
-/

# Is the cycle space of the annihilation graph triply even?

Milestone 2.3 of the research plan asks whether the binary cycle space of the sedenion mutual
annihilation graph yields a *triply-even* code (every codeword weight divisible by 8), which
is the condition for a transversal `T` gate on the associated CSS code
(`Sovereign/Quantum/TriplyEvenNecessity.lean`).

The answer is **no**.  The cycle space of a graph contains the edge set of every 4-cycle, and
two vertices with two common neighbours span a 4-cycle.  The annihilation graph `zdGraph` is
`7 × C₆[4]` (`Sovereign/Graph/MutualAnnihilationStructure.lean`), and in `C₆[4]` any two
vertices in the same independent 4-set share 8 common neighbours.

* `cycleSpace G` — the edge sets in which every vertex has even degree.
* `fourCycle_mem_cycleSpace`, `card_fourCycle` — a 4-cycle is a weight-4 element.
* `not_isTriplyEven_of_fourCycle` — a graph containing a 4-cycle has a cycle space that is
  not triply even.
* `hexBlowup_cycleSpace_not_triplyEven`, `zdGraph_cycleSpace_not_triplyEven` — applied to
  `C₆[4]` and to the annihilation graph itself.

a codeword of weight 4. -/

/-!
# Hyperbolic surface codes: encoding rate and distance

A *hyperbolic surface code* is the homological surface code (`SurfaceCode`) of a closed
surface cellulated by a regular `{r, s}` tessellation with `1/r + 1/s < 1/2`: every face is an
`r`-gon, every vertex has degree `s`, every edge has two end-points and borders two faces.
Such a surface is the quotient `𝔻²/Γ` of the hyperbolic disk by a surface group, i.e. a compact
Riemann surface, and the tessellation descends from the `{r, s}` tiling of `𝔻²`.

## Main results

* `IsRegular.faces_mul`, `IsRegular.verts_mul`: double counting `r|F| = 2|E|`, `s|V| = 2|E|`.
* `IsRegular.genus_formula`: `2g - 2 = n (1 - 2/r - 2/s)`.
* `IsRegular.two_le_genus`: a hyperbolic tessellation forces genus `g ≥ 2`.
* `IsRegular.rate_eq`: the exact rate `k/n = 1 - 2/r - 2/s + 2/n`.
* `IsRegular.rate_ge`: **`k/n ≥ 1 - 2/r - 2/s > 0`** (non-vanishing rate).
* `rate_tendsto`: along any family with `n → ∞` the rate converges to `1 - 2/r - 2/s`.
* `IsRegular.area_eq`: Gauss–Bonnet consistency: `|F| · area(tile) = 4π(g - 1)`.
* `distance_ge_systole`: the code distance is at least `sys / ℓ_max`, where `sys` is the
  systole of the hyperbolic surface and `ℓ_max` the larger of the primal/dual edge lengths.
* `distance_isBigOmega_log`: for families of logarithmic systole
  `sys ≥ α log g` (such families are provided by the Buser–Sarnak congruence construction),
  **`d = Ω(log n)`**.
-/
/-- The cellulation is a regular `{r, s}` tessellation. -/
/-- The genus formula for a regular tessellation: `2g - 2 = n (1 - 2/r - 2/s)`. -/
/-- **A hyperbolic tessellation forces genus at least two.** -/
/-- **Exact encoding rate** of a regular `{r, s}` surface code: `k/n = 1 - 2/r - 2/s + 2/n`. -/
/-- **Non-vanishing encoding rate**: `k/n ≥ 1 - 2/r - 2/s > 0` for hyperbolic `{r, s}`. -/
/-- Gauss–Bonnet angle defect of the regular tile, i.e. its hyperbolic area. -/
/-- A hyperbolic `{r, s}` surface code, bundled with its (finite) cellulation. -/
/-- Vertices. -/
/-- Edges (the physical qubits). -/
/-- Faces. -/
/-- The homological code of the cellulated surface. -/
/-- Number of physical qubits. -/
/-- Number of logical qubits. -/
/-- Code distance. -/
/-- Genus of the underlying compact Riemann surface. -/
/-- **Non-vanishing asymptotic encoding rate** of hyperbolic surface codes. -/

/-- Along any family of hyperbolic `{r, s}` codes with growing length the rate converges to
`1 - 2/r - 2/s`. -/

/-- The hyperbolic surface `𝔻²/Γ` carrying the tessellation has systole at least `sys`:
every homologically non-trivial cycle of the primal tessellation (edges of hyperbolic length
`ℓ_{r,s}`) and of the dual tessellation (edges of length `ℓ_{s,r}`) is non-contractible and
hence has hyperbolic length at least `sys`. -/
/-- The larger of the primal and dual edge lengths. -/
/-- **Distance from the systole**: `d ≥ sys / ℓ_max`. -/

/-- **Logarithmic distance** `d = Ω(log n)`: for a family of hyperbolic `{r, s}` codes whose
underlying Riemann surfaces have logarithmic systole `sys_i ≥ α log g_i` (`α > 0`), there are
`c > 0` and `N` such that `d_i ≥ c log n_i` whenever `n_i ≥ N`. -/
-- `log g ≥ log n / 2`

/-!
# Minimum-weight decoding of a CSS sector

For one sector `C : CSSComplex X E Z` of a CSS code we study the minimum-weight decoder:
given the syndrome `A e` of an error `e`, it returns a lowest-weight correction `e'` with the
same syndrome.  Decoding *fails* when the residual `e + e'` is a non-trivial logical operator.

The key combinatorial facts (the Peierls-type argument of Dennis–Kitaev–Landahl–Preskill):

* a *circuit* is a minimal non-empty support of a cycle (`IsCircuit`);
* `exists_nontrivial_circuit`: every non-trivial cycle contains a non-trivial circuit;
* `fails_imp_circuit`: if minimum-weight decoding fails on `e` then there is a non-trivial
  circuit `U` with `|U| ≤ 2 |U ∩ supp e|`, i.e. the error occupies at least half of a
  homologically non-trivial circuit (whose length is therefore at least the distance);
* `IsCircuit.isConnected`: circuits are connected for the adjacency "share a check".
-/
/-- `T` is the support of a cycle (an undetectable error). -/
/-- A circuit: a minimal non-empty cycle support. -/
/-- Two qubits are adjacent if some check acts on both. -/
/-- Every non-trivial cycle contains a non-trivial circuit. -/

/-- A minimum-weight decoder: for every syndrome of an actual error it returns a correction
with that syndrome and of minimal weight among all such corrections. -/
/-- A minimum-weight decoder exists. -/
/-- Decoding the error `e` fails when the residual error is a non-trivial logical operator. -/
/-- **Failure of minimum-weight decoding is witnessed by a half-occupied non-trivial circuit.** -/
-- `e' + ind U` has the same syndrome as `e`, so it is at least as heavy as `e'`
-- compute the weights by splitting along `U`
-- `U \ supp e' ⊆ supp e`
/-- **Circuits are connected** for the adjacency "acted on by a common check". -/
/-- A non-trivial circuit is at least as long as the distance of the sector. -/

/-!
# Counting connected sets (Peierls bound)

For a finite set `E` with an adjacency relation in which every element has at most `D`
neighbours, the number of connected subsets of size `w` containing a fixed element `x` is at
most `2^((D+1) w)`.

The proof is the classical percolation/Peierls trick, here in purely combinatorial form.  To a
connected set `S` associate the family `cyl S` of all subsets `ω ⊆ E` that contain `S` and avoid
its outer boundary `∂S`.  These families are pairwise disjoint for distinct connected sets
through `x`, and `|cyl S| = 2^(|E| - |S| - |∂S|) ≥ 2^(|E| - (D+1)|S|)`.  Summing gives the bound.
-/

/-- `T` is connected for the adjacency `Adj`: it cannot be split into two non-empty parts with
no adjacency between them. -/
/-- The outer boundary of `S`: elements outside `S` adjacent to some element of `S`. -/
/-- All configurations containing `S` and avoiding its outer boundary. -/
-- one of the two sets sticks out of the other
/-- **Peierls bound**: at most `2^((D+1) w)` connected sets of size `w` contain a given point. -/
/-- The number of connected sets of size `w ≥ 1` is at most `|E| · 2^((D+1) w)`. -/

/-!
# `{r, s}` tessellations of the hyperbolic disk

A regular `{r, s}` tessellation tiles a surface of constant curvature by regular `r`-gons,
`s` of which meet at each vertex (interior angle `2π/s`).  The tiling is hyperbolic exactly
when `1/r + 1/s < 1/2`, equivalently `(r - 2)(s - 2) > 4`, equivalently `2r + 2s < rs`.

For a hyperbolic `{r, s}` the regular tile is determined by hyperbolic trigonometry of the
right triangle (centre, edge midpoint, vertex) with angles `π/r`, `π/s`, `π/2`:

* circumradius `R`:  `cosh R = cot(π/r) · cot(π/s)`,
* edge length `ℓ`:   `cosh(ℓ/2) = cos(π/r) / sin(π/s)`.

We prove these quantities exceed `1` **iff** the type is hyperbolic, so the tile exists in
`𝔻²` exactly in the hyperbolic case, and we construct the tile explicitly in the Poincaré disk:
its vertices `tanh(R/2)·exp(2πik/r)` all lie at hyperbolic distance `R` from the origin, the
polygon closes up after `r` steps, and consecutive vertices are at hyperbolic distance exactly
`ℓ`.  The angle defect `(r - 2)π - r·(2π/s)` (the area of the tile by Gauss–Bonnet) is positive
iff the type is hyperbolic.
-/
/-- The Schläfli type `{r, s}` is hyperbolic: `1/r + 1/s < 1/2`. -/
/-- Integer form of the hyperbolicity condition. -/
/-- Equivalent form `(r - 2)(s - 2) > 4`. -/
/-- For instance `{4, 5}` is hyperbolic. -/
/-- The constant `1 - 2/r - 2/s` governing the asymptotic encoding rate. -/

/-- The Euclidean (toroidal) tessellation `{4, 4}` sits exactly on the boundary: its rate
constant vanishes, and it is not hyperbolic. -/
/-- `cosh` of the circumradius of the regular tile: `cot(π/r) cot(π/s)`. -/
/-- `cosh` of half the edge length of the regular tile: `cos(π/r) / sin(π/s)`. -/
/-- The regular tile exists (positive circumradius) **iff** the type is hyperbolic. -/
/-- The edge length is positive **iff** the type is hyperbolic. -/
/-- The hyperbolic circumradius `R` of the regular `{r, s}` tile. -/
/-- The hyperbolic edge length `ℓ` of the regular `{r, s}` tessellation. -/
/-- The `k`-th vertex of the regular `{r, s}` tile centred at the origin of `𝔻²`. -/
/-- Every vertex of the tile lies at hyperbolic distance `R` from the centre. -/
/-- The tile closes up after `r` steps. -/

/-- **Consecutive vertices of the tile are at hyperbolic distance exactly `ℓ`**, the edge
length of the `{r, s}` tessellation. -/
-- `cosh R = (1 + t²)/(1 - t²)`, hence `t² (C + 1) = C - 1`.
-- reduce to the vertices `t` and `t ω`
-- `(C² - 1) sin² a = E² - 1`

/-!
# Fault-tolerance threshold of hyperbolic surface codes under depolarizing noise

## Noise model

Each qubit independently suffers the identity with probability `1 - p` and each of the
Pauli errors `X`, `Y`, `Z` with probability `p/3` (`depolWeight`).  A configuration
`σ : E → Pauli` has probability `configProb p σ = ∏ₑ depolWeight p (σ e)`.  Its `Z`-component
(`Z` or `Y`) is decoded by the vertex checks and its `X`-component (`X` or `Y`) by the face
checks; both are corrected independently by minimum-weight decoding.  The whole recovery
consists of Pauli-type stabilizer measurements, classical decoding and Pauli corrections:
no non-Clifford resource, and in particular **no magic state or magic state distillation**,
enters the protocol analysed here.

## Main results

* `CSSComplex.failure_prob_le`: for one sector, any noise such that every fixed set `A` is
  contained in the error support with probability `≤ q^|A|`, and checks with adjacency degree
  `≤ D`, minimum-weight decoding fails with probability at most
  `∑_{w = d}^{n} n (2^(D+2) √q)^w`.
* `prob_subset_zPart`, `prob_subset_xPart`: under depolarizing noise, `q = 2p/3`.
* `HyperbolicSurfaceCode.failure_prob_le`: `P_fail ≤ 2 n x^d / (1 - x)` with
  `x = 2^(2 max(r,s) + 2) √(2p/3)`.
* `HyperbolicSurfaceCode.threshold`: if the distances grow logarithmically,
  `d ≥ c log n`, then for every `p < p_th = (3/2) (e^{-1/c} / 2^(2 max(r,s)+2))²` the logical
  failure probability tends to `0` as `n → ∞`.
* `HyperbolicSurfaceCode.threshold_of_systole`: the same, with the logarithmic distance
  supplied by the logarithmic-systole hypothesis (`distance_isBigOmega_log`): there is a
  threshold `p_th > 0` below which hyperbolic surface codes with non-vanishing rate protect
  quantum information with vanishing failure probability.
-/

# The Tillich–Zémor hypergraph product of two classical codes

Given two binary parity-check matrices `H₁ ∈ 𝔽₂^{m₁ × n₁}` and `H₂ ∈ 𝔽₂^{m₂ × n₂}`, the
hypergraph product is the CSS code on `N = n₁n₂ + m₁m₂` qubits with check matrices

  `H_X = [H₁ ⊗ I_{n₂} | I_{m₁} ⊗ H₂ᵀ]`,   `H_Z = [I_{n₁} ⊗ H₂ | H₁ᵀ ⊗ I_{m₂}]`.

Earlier modules (`Sovereign/Coding/QLDPC.lean`, `AsymptoticQLDPC.lean`) only record the
parameter formulas as numerals and the commutation as the scalar identity `x + x = 0`.  This
module proves them for the actual matrices, for arbitrary `H₁`, `H₂`.

* `hgpX_mul_hgpZ_transpose` — **`H_X H_Zᵀ = 0` over `𝔽₂`** for all `H₁`, `H₂`, so the
  hypergraph product is a CSS stabilizer code (`hgpCode`).
* `finrank_bothKer` — linear algebra: the space of matrices `Y` with `A Y = 0` and
  `Y Bᵀ = 0` has dimension `dim ker A · dim ker B`.
* `rank_hgpX`, `rank_hgpZ` — `rank H_X = m₁n₂ - k₁ᵀk₂` and `rank H_Z = n₁m₂ - k₁k₂ᵀ`, where
  `kᵢ = dim ker Hᵢ` and `kᵢᵀ = dim ker Hᵢᵀ`.
* `hgpCode_logicalQubits` — **the number of logical qubits is `K = k₁k₂ + k₁ᵀk₂ᵀ`.**
-/
/-! ## Linear algebra: matrices annihilated from both sides -/

/-- The linear maps `V → q` vanishing on a subspace `p` form a space of dimension
`(dim V - dim p) · dim q`. -/
/-- The matrices `Y` with `A Y = 0` and `Y Bᵀ = 0`. -/
/-- `bothKer A B` is the space of linear maps `𝔽ⁿ → ker A` vanishing on the range of `Bᵀ`. -/
/-- The dimension of the code `ker H`. -/
/-- Rank–nullity for a parity-check matrix: `rank H + dim ker H = n`. -/
/-- **Two-sided annihilator dimension**: `dim {Y : A Y = 0, Y Bᵀ = 0} = dim ker A · dim ker B`. -/
/-! ## The hypergraph product check matrices -/
/-- `H_X = [H₁ ⊗ I | I ⊗ H₂ᵀ]`, rows indexed by `(a, b) ∈ [m₁] × [n₂]`. -/
/-- `H_Z = [I ⊗ H₂ | H₁ᵀ ⊗ I]`, rows indexed by `(j, c) ∈ [n₁] × [m₂]`. -/
/-- **Hypergraph product commutation**: `H_X H_Zᵀ = (H₁ ⊗ H₂ᵀ) + (H₁ ⊗ H₂ᵀ) = 0` over `𝔽₂`. -/

/-- The action of `H_Xᵀ` on a vector `y` of `𝔽₂^{m₁ × n₂}`, read as an `m₁ × n₂` matrix `Y`:
`H_Xᵀ y = (H₁ᵀ Y, Y H₂ᵀ)`. -/
/-- The action of `H_Zᵀ`: `H_Zᵀ y = (Y H₂, H₁ Y)` for `Y` the `n₁ × m₂` matrix of `y`. -/
/-- `ker H_Xᵀ` is identified, by currying, with `bothKer H₁ᵀ H₂`. -/
/-- `ker H_Zᵀ` is identified, by currying, with `bothKer H₁ H₂ᵀ`. -/
/-- **Rank of `H_X`**: `rank H_X + k₁ᵀ k₂ = m₁ n₂`. -/
/-- **Rank of `H_Z`**: `rank H_Z + k₁ k₂ᵀ = n₁ m₂`. -/
/-! ## The hypergraph product as a stabilizer code on `n₁n₂ + m₁m₂` qubits -/
/-- Qubit labels: `[n₁] × [n₂] ⊔ [m₁] × [m₂] ≃ Fin (n₁n₂ + m₁m₂)`. -/
/-- `H_X` with rows and qubits relabelled by `Fin`. -/
/-- `H_Z` with rows and qubits relabelled by `Fin`. -/
/-- **The hypergraph product code** `HGP(H₁, H₂)` on `n₁n₂ + m₁m₂` physical qubits. -/
/-- The arithmetic behind the hypergraph-product dimension count. -/

/-- **Logical qubits of the hypergraph product**: `K = k₁k₂ + k₁ᵀk₂ᵀ`, where `kᵢ = dim ker Hᵢ`
and `kᵢᵀ = dim ker Hᵢᵀ`. -/

/-

# Distance of the hypergraph product code

Continues `Sovereign/Quantum/HypergraphProduct.lean`.  Write `dᵢ` for the minimum distance of
the classical code `ker Hᵢ`.

* `clean` — the cleaning lemma, in matrix form: a solution `(X_L, X_R)` of
  `X_L H₂ᵀ + H₁ᵀ X_R = 0` whose `X_L` uses fewer than `d₂` columns is `(H₁ᵀ Y, Y H₂ᵀ)`,
  provided `H₁ᵀ` is injective.
* `hgp_clean_X`, `hgp_clean_Z` — hence low-weight `X`-type (resp. `Z`-type) operators commuting
  with the checks are products of checks.
* `hgpCode_hasDistance` — **if `H₁`, `H₂` have full row rank, every logical operator of
  `HGP(H₁, H₂)` has weight `≥ min d₁ d₂`.**
* `hgpCode_not_hasDistance` — for any `H₁`, `H₂`, nonzero codewords `c₁ ∈ ker H₁`,
  `c₂ ∈ ker H₂` give logical operators `e_j ⊗ c₂` and `c₁ ⊗ e_b` of weights `|c₂|`, `|c₁|`.
* `hgpCode_params` — **`HGP(H₁, H₂)` of two full-rank codes is an
  `[[n₁n₂ + m₁m₂, k₁k₂, min(d₁, d₂)]]` code**, with the distance exact.
* `hgp_hamming7_params` — example: `HGP(Hamming₇, Hamming₇)` is a `[[58, 16, 3]]` code.

For codes whose check matrices are not of full row rank, the general Tillich–Zémor bound
`d ≥ min(d₁, d₂, d₁ᵀ, d₂ᵀ)` is proved in `Sovereign/Quantum/HypergraphProductGeneralDistance.lean`
(`hgpCode_hasDistance_general`).
-/
/-! ## Characteristic-two helpers -/
/-! ## The cleaning lemma -/
/-- The set of columns in which a matrix has a nonzero entry. -/
/-- The vectors supported inside a set of coordinates. -/

/-- **Cleaning lemma** (matrix form).  Let `X_L ∈ 𝔽₂^{n₁ × n₂}`, `X_R ∈ 𝔽₂^{m₁ × m₂}` satisfy
`X_L H₂ᵀ + H₁ᵀ X_R = 0`.  If the columns occupied by `X_L` are fewer than the minimum distance
of `ker H₂`, and `H₁ᵀ` is injective, then `(X_L, X_R) = (H₁ᵀ Y, Y H₂ᵀ)` for some `Y`. -/
/-! ## From vectors to matrices -/
/-- The `[n₁] × [n₂]` block of a vector on the hypergraph-product qubits, as a matrix. -/
/-- The `[m₁] × [m₂]` block of a vector on the hypergraph-product qubits, as a matrix. -/
/-- The number of columns occupied by a block is at most the weight of the vector. -/

/-- **X-type cleaning.**  An `X`-type operator commuting with all `Z` checks, of weight below
the distance of `ker H₂`, is a product of `X` checks, provided `H₁ᵀ` is injective. -/

/-- **Z-type cleaning.**  A `Z`-type operator commuting with all `X` checks, of weight below
the distance of `ker H₁`, is a product of `Z` checks, provided `H₂ᵀ` is injective. -/
/-! ## Relabelling helpers -/
/-! ## The distance of the hypergraph product -/

/-- **Distance of the hypergraph product (lower bound).**  If `ker H₁` and `ker H₂` have minimum
distances at least `d₁` and `d₂`, and `H₁`, `H₂` have full row rank (`H₁ᵀ`, `H₂ᵀ` injective,
i.e. `k₁ᵀ = k₂ᵀ = 0`), then every logical operator of `HGP(H₁, H₂)` has weight at least
`min d₁ d₂`. -/
/-! ## Logical operators of weight `d₁` and `d₂` -/
/-- The `X`-type operator `e_j ⊗ c₂` supported on one row of the `[n₁] × [n₂]` block. -/
/-- The `Z`-type operator `c₁ ⊗ e_b` supported on one column of the `[n₁] × [n₂]` block. -/

/-- **Distance of the hypergraph product (upper bound).**  If `c₁ ∈ ker H₁` and `c₂ ∈ ker H₂`
are nonzero, then `HGP(H₁, H₂)` has logical operators of weights `|c₁|` and `|c₂|`; in
particular its distance is at most `min |c₁| |c₂|`.  No rank assumption is needed. -/
/-! ## The `[[n₁n₂ + m₁m₂, k₁k₂, min(d₁, d₂)]]` theorem -/

/-- **Parameters of the hypergraph product of two full-rank codes.**  Let `ker H₁`, `ker H₂` be
classical `[n₁, k₁, d₁]` and `[n₂, k₂, d₂]` codes (with minimum-weight codewords `c₁`, `c₂`),
and let `H₁`, `H₂` have full row rank.  Then `HGP(H₁, H₂)` is an
`[[n₁n₂ + m₁m₂, k₁k₂, min(d₁, d₂)]]` code: `k₁k₂` logical qubits and distance exactly
`min d₁ d₂`. -/
/-! ## Example: the hypergraph product of the `[7, 4, 3]` Hamming code with itself -/

/-

# The Tillich–Zémor distance bound without rank assumptions

Continues `Sovereign/Quantum/HypergraphProductDistance.lean`, which proved
`d(HGP(H₁, H₂)) ≥ min(d₁, d₂)` only when `H₁`, `H₂` have full row rank.  Here `dᵢ`, `dᵢᵀ`
bound the minimum distances of `ker Hᵢ`, `ker Hᵢᵀ` (a trivial kernel imposes no constraint).

* `clean_general` — generalized cleaning lemma: `(X_L, X_R)` with `X_L H₂ᵀ + H₁ᵀ X_R = 0` is
  `(H₁ᵀ Y, Y H₂ᵀ)` once the columns of `H₂` on `colSupp X_L` and the rows of `H₁` on
  `rowSupp X_R` are independent.  Proof: dual cleaning (`pair_eq_zero_of_cocycle`) moves any
  `Z` cocycle off the support of `(X_L, X_R)` using `Z` stabilizers, so `(X_L, X_R)` is
  orthogonal to `ker H_X`, hence lies in the row space of `H_X`
  (`exists_transpose_mulVec_of_orth`).
* `hgpCode_hasDistance_general'` — `X`-distance `≥ min(d₂, d₁ᵀ)`, `Z`-distance
  `≥ min(d₁, d₂ᵀ)`.
* `hgpCode_hasDistance_general` — **`d(HGP(H₁, H₂)) ≥ min(d₁, d₂, d₁ᵀ, d₂ᵀ)` for arbitrary
  `H₁`, `H₂`.**
* `hgpCode_not_hasDistance_transpose` — nonzero `u ∈ ker H₁ᵀ`, `w ∈ ker H₂ᵀ` give logical
  operators of weights `|u|`, `|w|`.
* `hgpCode_params_general` — the distance is exactly `min(d₁, d₂, d₁ᵀ, d₂ᵀ)` when all four
  kernels are nonzero.
* `hgpCode_distance_sq_le` — square-root barrier `d² ≤ n₁n₂ ≤ N` when `k₁, k₂ > 0`.
-/
/-! ## Linear-algebra helpers -/
/-- Over a field, a vector orthogonal to `ker M` lies in the row space of `M`. -/
/-- A partial left inverse of `H` on the vectors supported in `J`, as a matrix `G`. -/
/-! ## The trace pairing -/
/-- The entrywise pairing `⟪A, B⟫ = Σᵢⱼ Aᵢⱼ Bᵢⱼ`. -/
/-! ## Dual cleaning -/
/-- The set of rows in which a matrix has a nonzero entry. -/

/-- **Orthogonality to cocycles.**  If `X_L H₂ᵀ + H₁ᵀ X_R = 0`, the columns of `H₂` in the
column support of `X_L` are independent, and the rows of `H₁` in the row support of `X_R` are
independent, then `(X_L, X_R)` is orthogonal to every `(Z_L, Z_R)` with
`H₁ Z_L + Z_R H₂ = 0`. -/
-- adding a `Z`-stabilizer does not change the pairing
-- step 1: clean the rows `I` of `Z_R`
-- step 2: clean the columns `J` of `Z_L`, keeping the rows `I` of `Z_R` clean

/-- **Generalized cleaning lemma.**  A solution `(X_L, X_R)` of `X_L H₂ᵀ + H₁ᵀ X_R = 0` is
`(H₁ᵀ Y, Y H₂ᵀ)` as soon as the columns of `H₂` on the column support of `X_L` and the rows of
`H₁` on the row support of `X_R` are linearly independent.  No rank assumption on `H₁`, `H₂`. -/
/-! ## From distances to independence -/

/-- If every nonzero vector of `ker H` has weight `≥ d`, then `H` is injective on the vectors
supported in any set of fewer than `d` coordinates. -/
/-! ## Cleaning in the hypergraph product without rank assumptions -/

/-- **X-type cleaning, general case.**  An `X`-type operator commuting with all `Z` checks, of
weight below both the distance `d₂` of `ker H₂` and the distance `d₁ᵀ` of `ker H₁ᵀ`, is a
product of `X` checks.  No rank assumption. -/

/-- **Z-type cleaning, general case.**  A `Z`-type operator commuting with all `X` checks, of
weight below both the distance `d₁` of `ker H₁` and the distance `d₂ᵀ` of `ker H₂ᵀ`, is a
product of `Z` checks.  No rank assumption. -/
/-! ## The generalized Tillich–Zémor bound -/

/-- **Generalized Tillich–Zémor distance bound (sharp form).**  For arbitrary binary check
matrices `H₁`, `H₂` (no rank assumption), if every nonzero vector of `ker H₁`, `ker H₂`,
`ker H₁ᵀ`, `ker H₂ᵀ` has weight at least `d₁`, `d₂`, `d₁ᵀ`, `d₂ᵀ` respectively, then every
`X`-logical operator has weight `≥ min(d₂, d₁ᵀ)` and every `Z`-logical operator has weight
`≥ min(d₁, d₂ᵀ)`; in particular every logical operator of `HGP(H₁, H₂)` has weight at least
`min(min(d₂, d₁ᵀ), min(d₁, d₂ᵀ))`. -/

/-- **Generalized Tillich–Zémor distance bound.**  For arbitrary binary check matrices
`H₁ ∈ 𝔽₂^{m₁×n₁}`, `H₂ ∈ 𝔽₂^{m₂×n₂}` — not necessarily of full row rank — with `d₁`, `d₂`,
`d₁ᵀ`, `d₂ᵀ` lower bounds on the minimum distances of `ker H₁`, `ker H₂`, `ker H₁ᵀ`,
`ker H₂ᵀ`, every logical operator of `HGP(H₁, H₂)` has weight at least
`min(d₁, d₂, d₁ᵀ, d₂ᵀ)`.

A trivial kernel imposes no constraint (its hypothesis holds for every value), matching the
convention `d(\{0\}) = ∞`; so for full-rank `H₁`, `H₂` this recovers `hgpCode_hasDistance`. -/
/-! ## Logical operators of weight `d₁ᵀ` and `d₂ᵀ` -/
/-- The `X`-type operator `u ⊗ e_c` supported on one column of the `[m₁] × [m₂]` block. -/
/-- The `Z`-type operator `e_a ⊗ w` supported on one row of the `[m₁] × [m₂]` block. -/

/-- **Distance of the hypergraph product (upper bound from the transposed codes).**  If
`u ∈ ker H₁ᵀ` and `w ∈ ker H₂ᵀ` are nonzero, then `HGP(H₁, H₂)` has logical operators of
weights `|u|` and `|w|`; so its distance is at most `min |u| |w|`.  This is the new
contribution of redundant checks, absent when `H₁`, `H₂` have full row rank. -/

/-- **Exact distance of a general hypergraph product.**  Suppose `ker H₁`, `ker H₂`, `ker H₁ᵀ`,
`ker H₂ᵀ` are all nonzero with minimum distances exactly `d₁`, `d₂`, `d₁ᵀ`, `d₂ᵀ` (attained by
`c₁`, `c₂`, `u`, `w`).  Then `HGP(H₁, H₂)` encodes `k₁k₂ + k₁ᵀk₂ᵀ` qubits and its distance is
exactly `min(d₁, d₂, d₁ᵀ, d₂ᵀ)`. -/

/-- **Square-root distance barrier for hypergraph products.**  If `ker H₁` and `ker H₂` are
nonzero (so that `HGP(H₁, H₂)` has `k₁k₂ > 0` logical qubits from the left block) and the code
has distance at least `d`, then `d² ≤ n₁ n₂ ≤ N`, where `N = n₁n₂ + m₁m₂` is the number of
physical qubits. -/

/-

# The hypergraph product preserves sparsity (the LDPC property)

For `H_X = [H₁ ⊗ I | I ⊗ H₂ᵀ]` and `H_Z = [I ⊗ H₂ | H₁ᵀ ⊗ I]`:

* `hammingNorm_hgpX_row` — the `X` check `(a, b)` has weight `|row a of H₁| + |column b of H₂|`.
* `hammingNorm_hgpZ_row` — the `Z` check `(j, c)` has weight `|row c of H₂| + |column j of H₁|`.
* `hammingNorm_hgpX_col_inl`, … — each qubit lies in `|column|` resp. `|row|` many checks.
* `hgp_ldpc` — **if every row and column of `H₁`, `H₂` has weight `≤ w`, then every check of
  `HGP(H₁, H₂)` has weight `≤ 2w` and every qubit is acted on by at most `w` checks of each
  type.**  Together with `hgpCode_hasDistance_general` this gives qLDPC codes from arbitrary
  (redundant) sparse classical checks.
-/
/-- A vector on `α × β` supported on the slice `β = b` has the weight of that slice. -/
/-- A vector on `α × β` supported on the slice `α = a` has the weight of that slice. -/

/-- **Weight of an `X` check.**  Row `(a, b)` of `H_X` has weight
`|row a of H₁| + |column b of H₂|`. -/

/-- **Weight of a `Z` check.**  Row `(j, c)` of `H_Z` has weight
`|row c of H₂| + |column j of H₁|`. -/
/-- A qubit `(j, b)` of the left block lies in `|column j of H₁|` many `X` checks. -/
/-- A qubit `(a, c)` of the right block lies in `|row c of H₂|` many `X` checks. -/
/-- A qubit `(j, b)` of the left block lies in `|column b of H₂|` many `Z` checks. -/
/-- A qubit `(a, c)` of the right block lies in `|row a of H₁|` many `Z` checks. -/

/-- **The hypergraph product of sparse codes is a quantum LDPC code.**  If every row and
every column of `H₁` and `H₂` has weight at most `w`, then every `X` and `Z` check of
`HGP(H₁, H₂)` has weight at most `2w`, and every qubit is acted on by at most `w` checks of
each type. -/

  /-- Majorana operators are self-adjoint. -/

  /-- The Clifford relations `{γ i, γ j} = 2 δ_{ij}`. -/
  anticomm : ∀ i j, γ i * γ j + γ j * γ i = if i = j then 2 else 0
