comments.text:
/-!
# The spectral sequence of a filtered proof complex

Let `X` be a chain complex of `R`-modules (`Sovereign.ProofHomology.ChainCx`, boundary
`∂ : C_{k+1} → C_k`) whose homology `X.H k` are the **global proof homology groups**. A
*local-to-global filtration* is an increasing, `ℤ`-indexed filtration `F_p C_k` by subcomplexes
(`ChainFiltration`). Its spectral sequence is built here from the classical explicit formulas
(homological indexing, `k = p + q` is the total degree):

* `Z r p k = { x ∈ F_p C_k | ∂x ∈ F_{p-r} C_{k-1} }` (`Z`), `B r p k = F_p C_k ∩ ∂(F_{p+r} C_{k+1})`;
* the page `E r p k = Z r p k / (Z (r-1) (p-1) k + B (r-1) p k)` — the term `E^r_{p,q}`, `q = k - p`;
* the differential `d^r : E^r_{p,q} → E^r_{p-r,q+r-1}` induced by `∂` (`dr`), with
  `d^r ∘ d^r = 0` (`dr_comp_dr`).

Main results:

* `E_succ_equiv` — **the spectral sequence property**: `E^{r+1} ≅ H(E^r, d^r)`;
* `E_zero_equiv` — `E^0_p = F_p C / F_{p-1} C` (the associated graded complex);
* `E_equiv_gr` — **convergence**: once the filtration is exhausted at `(p, k)` (`F_{p-r} = 0`
  below and `F_{p+r-1} = C` above), `E^r_{p,q} ≅ F_p H_k / F_{p-1} H_k`, the associated graded of
  the global homology for the induced filtration `Fh`.
-/
/-- An increasing `ℤ`-indexed filtration of a chain complex by subcomplexes. -/
/-- the `p`-th filtration step in degree `k` -/
/-- the filtration is increasing -/
/-- each step is a subcomplex -/
/-- `Z^r_p = { x ∈ F_p | ∂x ∈ F_{p-r} }` (in degree `0` there is no condition on `∂x`). -/
/-- The denominator `Z^{r-1}_{p-1} + B^{r-1}_p` of the page `E^r_p`. -/
/-- The page `E^r_{p,q}` (`q = k - p`) of the spectral sequence. -/
/-- `Z` decreases with the page. -/
/-- `B` increases with the page. -/
/-- Boundaries satisfy every cycle condition: `B^s_p ≤ Z^r_p`. -/
/-- `∂` of anything lies in every `Z` whose filtration condition it meets. -/

/-- The differential `d^r : E^r_{p,q} → E^r_{p-r,q+r-1}` (stated for any target index `q'` with
`p - r = q'`, to avoid casts). -/
/-! ### Homology of a page -/
/-- The kernel of the outgoing differential `d^r` at `E^r_{p,q}` (everything in degree `0`). -/
/-- The image of the incoming differential `d^r : E^r_{p+r,q-r+1} → E^r_{p,q}`. -/
/-- The homology `ker d^r / im d^r` of the `r`-th page at `(p, q)`. -/

/-- If `z ∈ F_q` differs from an element of `Z^t_{p'}` by a cycle, then `z ∈ Z^r_q` as soon as
`p' - t ≤ q - r`. -/
/-- The class in `E^r_p` of an element of `Z^{r+1}_p`. -/
/-- The comparison map `Z^{r+1}_p → H(E^r, d^r)`. -/

/-- **The spectral sequence property**: the `(r+1)`-st page is the homology of the `r`-th page
with respect to `d^r`, `E^{r+1}_{p,q} ≅ ker d^r / im d^r`. -/

/-
**Scope (truth-in-labelling, moved to `Sovereign.Speculative`).** Every quantity in this file
is a natural number or an integer. There is no velocity field, no PDE and no real analysis, so
the header below does not describe what is proved. The theorems are arithmetic facts about
fixed numbers and implications between the stated hypotheses. In particular nothing here
"unconditionally" obstructs finite-time blowup of any Navier–Stokes system. The real-valued
enstrophy decay estimate is proved (from stated hypotheses) in
`Sovereign.Fluid.EnstrophyDecayReal`. The original header follows unchanged.

Non-Associative Hydrodynamics: Global Regularity Obstruction, Viscous Decay Kinetics,
and Beale-Kato-Majda Blowup Suppression on 16D Sedenion Zero-Divisor Subspaces.

Formal verification of:
1. Global Regularity Obstruction Theorem:
   Convective vortex stretching P_stretch = <omega, (omega . grad)u> = 0 vanishes
   identically whenever velocity u and vorticity omega form a zero-divisor
   annihilation pair (u x_16 omega = 0).
2. Viscous Enstrophy Decay Theorem:
   Under the Poincaré inequality D >= lambda_1 E, the enstrophy rate satisfies
   dE/dt = -2 nu D <= -2 nu lambda_1 E, leading to exponential decay
   E(t) <= E(0) e^{-2 nu lambda_1 t}.
3. Beale-Kato-Majda (BKM) Integral Finiteness Theorem:
   Bounded enstrophy and absence of vortex stretching guarantee ||omega(t)||_{L^infty} <= M_0
   for all t in [0, T], ensuring int_0^T ||omega(t)||_{L^infty} dt <= M_0 * T < infty
   for all T > 0, unconditionally obstructing finite-time singularity blowup.
4. Boundary Invariance & Corner Eddy Reconnection Suppression:
   On cylindrical wall boundary r = 1, wall conditions u x_16 n = 0 preserve
   zero-divisor annihilation under the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator Lambda_16,
   and corner eddy reconnection energy density R_recon = ||u x_16 omega||^2 = 0
   vanishes identically across all 672 annihilation edges of Gamma = C_6[K_4_bar].
5. Off-Manifold Perturbation Stability & Critical Reynolds Bound:
   For off-manifold perturbation distance delta > 0, stability is preserved whenever
   delta <= delta_crit(nu) = (2 nu lambda_1) / (C_stretch ||u||) or
   Re <= Re_c(delta) = (2 lambda_1 L) / (C_stretch delta).

Certified with 0 external axioms and 0 unproven assertions (zero sorry) in Lean 4.
-/

/-!
## 1. Zero-Divisor Algebra & Convective Vortex Stretching Vanishing
-/
/-- Dimension of the sedenion algebra: 16. -/
/-- Total number of discrete cross-octet zero divisors in Sedenions: 168. -/
/-- Regularity degree of the zero-divisor annihilation graph Gamma: 8. -/
/-- Total number of undirected zero-divisor annihilation edges: 672. -/
/-- Graph handshake lemma: (168 * 8) / 2 = 672 annihilation edges. -/
/-- Total directed zero-divisor annihilation pairs: 1,344. -/

/-- Sedenion commutator cross-product in an algebra with subtraction:
    u x_16 v = (u * v) - (v * u). -/

/-- Theorem 1.1: Commutator cross-product vanishes identically for any
    mutually annihilating zero-divisor pair (u * v = 0 and v * u = 0). -/
/-- Lamb vector L_16 = omega x_16 u. -/

/-- Theorem 1.2: Lamb vector vanishes identically when velocity u and vorticity omega
    form an annihilating zero-divisor pair. -/

/-- Theorem 1.4 (Global Regularity Obstruction Theorem):
    Whenever velocity u and vorticity omega satisfy u x_16 omega = 0,
    the convective vortex stretching P_stretch = <omega, (omega . grad)u>
    vanishes identically. -/

/-- Theorem 1.5 (Bilinear Vortex Stretching Annihilation):
    In any formulation where P_stretch = B(grad_omega, u x_16 omega)
    for a bilinear pairing B that is zero on the right argument zero,
    P_stretch vanishes identically on zero divisors. -/

/-- Theorem 1.6 (Cauchy Forward Trajectory Zero-Divisor Preservation):
    If the temporal evolution preserves the zero-divisor cross product subspace,
    an initial zero-divisor state u0 x_16 omega0 = 0 remains a zero-divisor state
    for all future times t. -/

/-!
## 2. Viscous Enstrophy Decay & Poincaré Dissipation
-/
/-- Fluid state parameters for enstrophy balance. -/

/-- Theorem 2.1 (Enstrophy Derivative Balance):
    The enstrophy derivative satisfies dE/dt = P_stretch - 2 * nu * D. -/

/-- Theorem 2.2 (Viscous Enstrophy Decay under Poincaré Inequality):
    Under the Poincaré inequality D >= lambda_1 * E and vanishing vortex stretching
    P_stretch = 0, the enstrophy rate satisfies dE/dt = -2 nu D <= -2 nu lambda_1 E. -/

/-- Theorem 2.3 (Strict Monotonic Enstrophy Dissipation):
    For any non-negative viscosity nu >= 0, Poincaré constant lambda_1 >= 0,
    and non-negative enstrophy E >= 0, the decay upper bound is strictly non-positive:
    -2 nu lambda_1 E <= 0. -/

/-- Theorem 2.4 (Inviscid Euler Stability on Zero Divisors, nu_c = 0):
    Even in the ideal inviscid limit nu = 0, vortex stretching absence guarantees
    dE/dt = 0, proving unconditional enstrophy conservation and zero critical viscosity. -/

/-- Theorem 2.5 (Discrete Grönwall Exponential Decay):
    If at each discrete time step the enstrophy satisfies
    rho_den * E(n + 1) <= rho_num * E(n) with contraction ratio rho_num / rho_den,
    then after n steps: (rho_den^n) * E(n) <= (rho_num^n) * E(0). -/

/-- Theorem 2.6 (Continuous Integrating Factor Grönwall Bound):
    For an integrating factor I(t) > 0 with I(0) = 1, if the product W(t) = E(t) * I(t)
    satisfies non-increasing monotonicity W(t) <= W(0) = E(0),
    then E(t) * I(t) <= E(0), certifying exponential decay E(t) <= E(0) / I(t). -/

/-!
## 3. Beale-Kato-Majda (BKM) Integral Finiteness & Singularity Obstruction
-/
/-- Discrete Riemann sum representing the BKM integral int_0^T ||omega(t)||_{L^infty} dt. -/

/-- Theorem 3.1 (BKM Integral Finiteness on Zero Divisors):
    Since vortex stretching vanishes identically, the vorticity maximum principle
    guarantees ||omega(t)||_{L^infty} <= M_0 for all t.
    Consequently, the BKM integral satisfies int_0^T ||omega(t)||_{L^infty} dt <= M_0 * T
    for every finite time horizon T. -/

/-- If a Riemann sum is bounded by `M0 * T_star` at every `T ≤ T_star`, it cannot exceed that
bound at some `T ≤ T_star`: the two hypotheses contradict each other.

*Scope (truth-in-labelling):* this was named `unconditional_blowup_obstruction` and described as
ruling out finite-time blowup. The bound is an assumption, the sums are over natural numbers,
and no fluid equation is involved. -/

/-- Theorem 3.3 (Hou-Chen Critical Rate Divergence vs Sedenion Stability):
    The classical 3D Euler singularity exhibits self-similar blowup with exponent gamma = 1,
    while sedenion zero divisors enforce gamma = 0 (bounded vorticity).
    The gap 1 - 0 = 1 certifies complete stabilization. -/

/-- *Scope (truth-in-labelling):* `1 - 0 = 1` for the two constants defined above. Formerly
named `blowup_rate_suppression`. It does not show that any blowup rate is suppressed. -/

/-!
## 4. Boundary Invariance & Corner Eddy Reconnection Suppression
-/
/-- Dirichlet-to-Neumann zero mode wavenumber and eigenvalue. -/
/-- Positivity of DtN eigenvalues for strictly positive wavenumbers k >= 1. -/

/-- Theorem 4.2 (Boundary Wall Condition Preserves Annihilation):
    Under wall boundary condition u x_16 n = 0, the boundary normal derivative
    Lambda_16(u) preserves zero-divisor alignment with vorticity omega. -/
/-- Corner eddy vortex reconnection energy density: R_recon = ||u x_16 omega||^2. -/

/-- Theorem 4.3 (Corner Eddy Reconnection Energy Vanishing):
    On all zero-divisor pairs, the corner eddy vortex reconnection energy density
    R_recon = ||u x_16 omega||^2 vanishes identically. -/

/-- Theorem 4.4 (Total Reconnection Dissipation over Annihilation Graph):
    Sum of reconnection energy density over all 672 zero-divisor edges is exactly zero:
    672 * 0 = 0. -/

/-- Theorem 4.5 (Boundary No-Penetration Condition):
    Tangential flow satisfies u_tau . n = 0 on cylindrical wall r = 1. -/

/-!
## 5. Off-Manifold Perturbation Stability & Critical Reynolds Bound
-/
/-- Fundamental algebraic lemma: If A * L <= B * L and L > 0, then A <= B. -/
/-- Off-manifold perturbation stability parameters. -/
-- Perturbation distance
-- Stretching prefactor
-- Velocity norm
-- Viscosity
-- First Poincaré eigenvalue
-- Reynolds number
-- Characteristic domain length

/-- Theorem 5.1 (Off-Manifold Enstrophy Growth Rate Bound):
    When perturbed off the zero-divisor manifold by distance delta > 0,
    the residual vortex stretching is bounded by C_stretch * delta * ||u|| * E.
    The net enstrophy growth rate sigma satisfies
    sigma <= C_stretch * delta * ||u|| - 2 * nu * lambda_1. -/

/-- Theorem 5.2 (Critical Perturbation Stability Threshold):
    Whenever delta satisfies C_stretch * delta * ||u|| <= 2 * nu * lambda_1,
    the net enstrophy growth rate is non-positive (stability is preserved). -/

/-- Theorem 5.3 (Critical Viscosity Bound for Off-Manifold Perturbations):
    For a fixed perturbation distance delta > 0, stability is guaranteed
    whenever the viscosity satisfies 2 * nu * lambda_1 >= C_stretch * delta * ||u||. -/

/-- Theorem 5.4 (Critical Reynolds Number Bound):
    Under the Reynolds scaling relation Re * nu = ||u|| * L with L > 0 and nu >= 0,
    the Reynolds stability bound (C_stretch * delta) * Re <= 2 * lambda_1 * L
    implies the physical dissipation stability bound
    (C_stretch * delta) * ||u|| <= 2 * nu * lambda_1. -/

/-- Theorem 5.5 (Critical Reynolds Implication for Net Growth Rate):
    Combining Reynolds bound with perturbation stability shows that
    Re <= Re_c(delta) guarantees non-positive net enstrophy growth rate. -/

/-- Theorem 5.6 (Asymptotic Recovery of Unconditional Stability):
    As the perturbation distance vanishes (delta = 0), the critical Reynolds
    number condition C_stretch * 0 * Re <= 2 * lambda_1 * L is satisfied for
    arbitrarily high Reynolds number (Re -> infty), recovering unconditional
    global regularity on the exact zero-divisor manifold. -/

  `ω₀, T ≥ 0`). They do not establish regularity, Beltrami flows or turbulence spectra for any
  Navier–Stokes system, and they do not settle OP-037, OP-039 or OP-042. The original header

  **Epistemic Classification:** [A] Arithmetic Identities

/-! ## 1. OP-037: Global Regularity of Sedenion Navier–Stokes -/
/-- On the zero-divisor variety, the non-associative Lamb vector vanishes identically. -/
/-- Convective vortex stretching power vanishes on zero divisors. -/
/-- Enstrophy dissipation rate is strictly non-positive for any viscosity nu >= 0. -/

/-- The product of two non-negative reals is non-negative: `0 ≤ ω₀ * T`.

*Scope (truth-in-labelling):* this was named `op037_sedenion_navier_stokes_regularity_settled`
and described as bounding the Beale–Kato–Majda integral and establishing global regularity.
The statement is only the inequality above. It involves no vorticity field and does not
settle OP-037. -/
/-! ## 2. OP-039: Sedenion Beltrami Flows & Orthogonal Helicity -/
/-- A generalized sedenion Beltrami flow satisfies u x_16 omega = 0. -/

/-- In 16D sedenion fluids, zero-divisor pairs yield orthogonal Beltrami flows:
    <u, omega> = 0 while u x_16 omega = 0. -/
/-- For orthogonal Beltrami flows, kinetic helicity is identically zero. -/

/-- *Scope (truth-in-labelling):* this theorem checks fixed numerical facts about the finite model
defined in this file. It has no universally quantified variable and does not settle an open
problem. Formerly named `op039_sedenion_beltrami_flows_settled`.

**Master Theorem for OP-039**:
    Sedenion hydrodynamics admits non-trivial orthogonal Beltrami flows
    supported on the 1344 directed zero-divisor pairs with identically vanishing Lamb vector. -/
/-! ## 3. OP-042: Sedenion Turbulence & Kolmogorov Spectra -/
/-- Ramanujan spectral gap ratio lambda_2 / d = 4 / 8 = 1/2. -/
/-- Kolmogorov cascade exponent alpha_K = 5/3. -/
/-- Kraichnan enstrophy cascade exponent alpha_Omega = 3. -/
/-- Universal cascade exponent bounds: alpha in [5/3, 3]. -/

**Master Theorem for OP-042**:
    In 16D non-associative turbulence, energy is conserved across Fano triads,

# `Sovereign.Speculative`

Modules whose prose describes continuum physics (Navier–Stokes regularity, blowup, turbulence)
that their Lean statements do not model. They are kept, and they still build and are audited,
but they are separated from the verified core so their headers are not mistaken for results.

* `GlobalRegularity`: every quantity is a natural number or an integer. There is no velocity

Neither module settles an open problem (see `docs/OPEN_PROBLEM_AUDIT.md`).

This module is an index: it imports every module of the cluster.
-/

/-!
# The Gosset lattice `E₈` and its root reflections

We use **doubled coordinates**: a vector `x ∈ ℝ⁸` is recorded as `y = 2x ∈ ℤ⁸`. The Gosset
lattice is
`E₈ = {x | all xᵢ ∈ ℤ or all xᵢ ∈ ℤ + ½, and ∑ xᵢ ∈ 2ℤ}`,
i.e. in doubled coordinates `{y | all yᵢ even or all yᵢ odd, and 4 ∣ ∑ yᵢ}` (`E8`). The
Euclidean inner product is `⟨x, x'⟩ = (y ⬝ᵥ y') / 4`.

* `E8`: an additive subgroup of `ℤ⁸`, so the decoder can step along lattice vectors
  (`latticeStep_mem`).
* `E8_norm_even`: `E₈` is an **even** lattice: `⟨x, x⟩ ∈ 2ℤ`, i.e. `8 ∣ y ⬝ᵥ y`;
  `E8_inner_int`: it is integral, `⟨x, x'⟩ ∈ ℤ`, i.e. `4 ∣ y ⬝ᵥ y'`.
* `E8_norm_ge`: every nonzero lattice vector has `⟨x, x⟩ ≥ 2`; the **roots** (`IsE8Root`) are
  the lattice vectors with `⟨x, x⟩ = 2`, i.e. the minimal vectors. `root_type1`,
  `root_type2`: examples of both root shapes `(±1, ±1, 0⁶)` and `(±½)⁸`.
* `reflect r`: the Weyl reflection `x ↦ x - ⟨x, r⟩ r` in a root `r`; it preserves `E₈`
  (`reflect_mem`), preserves the inner product (`reflect_dotProduct`), is an involution
  (`reflect_reflect`) and sends `r` to `-r` (`reflect_self`).
-/
/-- The Gosset lattice `E₈` in doubled coordinates. -/
/-- `E₈` is an even lattice: `⟨x, x⟩ ∈ 2ℤ`. -/
/-- `E₈` is integral: `⟨x, x'⟩ ∈ ℤ`. -/
/-- Nonzero lattice vectors have `⟨x, x⟩ ≥ 2`. -/
/-- A root of `E₈`: a lattice vector with `⟨x, x⟩ = 2` (doubled: `y ⬝ᵥ y = 8`). -/
/-- A root of shape `(½, …, ½)`. -/
/-- The Weyl reflection `x ↦ x - ⟨x, r⟩ r` in a root `r` (doubled coordinates). -/
/-- A lattice step of `c` counts along the root `r`. -/

/-!
# Tactile steering: quadrature encoders, rotational geodesics and the Stiefel manifold

## Rotational geodesics

A **rotation generator** (`RotGenerator`) is a skew-symmetric matrix `A` with `A³ = -A`; the
basic example is `planeGen e f = f eᵀ - e fᵀ` for an orthonormal pair `(e, f)`
(`RotGenerator.ofPlane`), the infinitesimal rotation of the plane `span {e, f}`.

`planeRotation A θ = 1 + sin θ · A + (1 - cos θ) · A²` is the closed form of `exp (θ A)`
(Rodrigues' formula):

* `planeRotation_zero`, `planeRotation_add`: `θ ↦ planeRotation A θ` is a one-parameter group;
* `hasDerivAt_planeRotation`: it solves `R' = A R`, `R 0 = 1`, i.e. it is the one-parameter
  subgroup generated by `A` — a geodesic of the rotation group for its bi-invariant metric;
* `planeRotation_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup`: every `planeRotation A θ` lies in `SO(n)`.

## The Stiefel manifold and the symplectic form

* `Stiefel2 n`: the Stiefel manifold `V₂(ℝⁿ)` of orthonormal 2-frames `(u, v)`;
  `frameAct G` the action of a matrix on frames; `frameAct_mem_stiefel`: orthogonal matrices act
  on `V₂(ℝⁿ)`.
* `omega`: the canonical symplectic form `Ω((u,v),(u',v')) = ⟨u,v'⟩ - ⟨v,u'⟩` on
  `ℝⁿ × ℝⁿ ⊇ V₂(ℝⁿ)` (bilinear: `omegaForm`); `omegaForm_isAlt`, `omegaForm_nondegenerate`:
  it is alternating and **non-degenerate**; `omega_frameAct`: orthogonal steering preserves it;
  `blockDiag_mem_symplecticGroup`: the steering matrix `diag(G, G)` lies in Mathlib's
  `symplecticGroup`.
* `quadPhase`: the quadrature phase rotation `(u, v) ↦ (cos φ u - sin φ v, sin φ u + cos φ v)`
  also preserves `V₂(ℝⁿ)` and `Ω`.

## Quadrature encoders and the steering operator

* `QuadState`: the two channel levels `(A, B)` of a quadrature encoder, with Gray-code phase
  `QuadState.phase : ZMod 4`; `decodeStep` the ×4 quadrature decoder (`+1`, `-1`, or `0`);
  `pulseCount` the net count of a sampled pulse train.
* `pulseCount_mod`: on valid traces (at most one Gray step between samples) the count tracks the
  phase modulo 4; `pulseCount_forward`/`pulseCount_backward`: turning the knob forward
  (backward) `N` quarter-cycles gives `±N`; `pulseCount_append`: counts add under
  concatenation.
* `TactileSteering`: a generator together with the angle `θ₀` per count;
  `TactileSteering.steer`: the frame after the pulse train, obtained by moving along the
  rotational geodesic by `count · θ₀`.
  `steer_mem_stiefel`, `steer_omega`: steering keeps frames in `V₂(ℝⁿ)` and preserves `Ω`;
  `steer_append`: steering along a concatenated pulse train is the composite of the steerings.
* `TwinSteering`: two encoders steering two (possibly different) planes;
  `TwinSteering.steer_mem_stiefel`, `TwinSteering.steer_omega`.
-/
/-! ### Rotation generators and their one-parameter groups -/
/-- A unit rotation generator: skew-symmetric with `A³ = -A`. -/
/-- The infinitesimal rotation `f eᵀ - e fᵀ` of the plane spanned by `e` and `f`. -/
/-- The rotation generator of the plane spanned by an orthonormal pair. -/
/-- The rotation of the coordinate plane `(i, j)`, `i ≠ j`. -/
/-- Rodrigues' formula: the rotation `exp (θ A) = 1 + sin θ · A + (1 - cos θ) · A²`. -/
/-- The rotations along a generator form a one-parameter group. -/
/-- Every rotation along a generator is a proper rotation: it lies in `SO(n)`. -/

/-- The rotations solve `R' = A R`: `θ ↦ planeRotation A θ` is the one-parameter subgroup
`exp (θ A)` (stated entrywise). -/
/-! ### The Stiefel manifold `V₂(ℝⁿ)` -/
/-- The Stiefel manifold `V₂(ℝⁿ)` of orthonormal 2-frames. -/
/-- The action of a matrix on 2-frames. -/
/-- Orthogonal matrices preserve the dot product. -/
/-! ### The canonical symplectic form on `ℝⁿ × ℝⁿ` -/
/-- The canonical symplectic form `Ω((u,v),(u',v')) = ⟨u,v'⟩ - ⟨v,u'⟩`. -/
/-- `Ω` as a bilinear form. -/
/-- `Ω` is alternating. -/
/-- `Ω` is **non-degenerate**. -/
/-- Orthogonal steering of both frame vectors preserves `Ω`. -/
/-- The block matrix `diag(G, G)` acting on `ℝⁿ ⊕ ℝⁿ`. -/
/-- For orthogonal `G`, `diag(G, G)` is a symplectic matrix. -/
/-- The quadrature phase rotation of a frame (the right `SO(2)`-action on `V₂(ℝⁿ)`). -/
/-! ### Quadrature encoders -/
/-- The levels `(A, B)` of the two channels of a quadrature encoder. -/
/-- Gray-code phase of a quadrature state: `00 ↦ 0`, `10 ↦ 1`, `11 ↦ 2`, `01 ↦ 3`. -/
/-- The quadrature state with a given Gray-code phase. -/

/-- The ×4 quadrature decoder: `+1` for a forward Gray step, `-1` for a backward step, `0`

/-- The net count of a sampled pulse train `w 0, …, w N`. -/
/-- A transition is valid if the phase moves by at most one Gray step. -/
/-- A sampled pulse train is valid if every transition is. -/

/-- Counts add under concatenation of pulse trains. -/
/-- Turning the knob forward through `N` quadrature steps yields the count `N`. -/
/-- Turning the knob backward through `N` quadrature steps yields the count `-N`. -/
/-! ### The tactile steering operator -/
/-- A tactile steering operator: a rotation generator and the steering angle `θ₀` per count. -/

/-- The rotation reached after a net count `c`: the point at parameter `c θ₀` of the rotational

comments.text:
/-!
# Heterogeneous prover agents in a shared Poincaré metric space

Every agent of the swarm sits at a point of the shared Poincaré ball `Dⁿ`
(`Sovereign.Autonomous.PoincareBall`, with its hyperbolic distance `dH`) and carries its own
**epistemic risk profile**: a depth-dependent Kelly model (`HorizonModel`: success probability
`p₀ e^{-decay·R}` at hyperbolic distance `R`, payoff odds) together with a hard stake cap
`cap < 1`.  Different agents may have different positions, success models and caps.

An agent stakes on a lemma located at `x` the clipped Kelly fraction
`stake A x = max 0 (min cap (f*(dH A.pos x)))`.

* `stake_mem_Icc`, `stake_lt_one`: every stake lies in `[0, cap] ⊆ [0, 1)` — no agent ever
  commits its whole budget.
* `stake_pos_iff`: an agent funds exactly the lemmas inside the open hyperbolic ball of radius
  its epistemic horizon `R_H` around its position (and only if its cap is positive).
* `funds_of_near`: the metric is shared — if agent `A` funds `x` and
  `dH A.pos B.pos + dH A.pos x < R_H(B)`, then agent `B` funds `x` as well (triangle inequality).
* `swarmStake_mem`: the swarm's pooled stake (the average of the agents' stakes) lies in
  `[0, max cap] ⊆ [0, 1)`.
-/
/-- An epistemic risk profile: a depth-dependent Kelly model and a stake cap below `1`. -/
/-- A prover agent: a position in the shared Poincaré ball and a risk profile. -/
/-- The epistemic horizon radius of an agent. -/

/-- The stake an agent places on a lemma located at `x`: its Kelly fraction at hyperbolic
distance `dH A.pos x`, clipped to `[0, cap]`. -/
/-- No agent ever stakes its whole budget. -/

/-- **Funding region**: an agent funds a lemma iff the lemma lies strictly inside its
epistemic horizon (and its cap is positive). -/
/-- **Shared metric**: funding propagates between agents that are hyperbolically close. -/
/-- A more cautious agent (same position, smaller horizon) funds fewer lemmas. -/
/-- Beyond its horizon an agent stakes nothing. -/
/-- The largest stake cap in a (nonempty) swarm. -/
/-- The pooled stake of the swarm on a lemma at `x`: the average of the agents' stakes. -/
/-- The pooled stake lies in `[0, max cap]`, hence strictly below `1`. -/
/-! Axiom audit of the main results of `Sovereign.Swarm`. -/

comments.text:
/-!
# Convergence of the adversarial consensus protocol

The game is played in rounds.  In round `k` the adversary first runs an arbitrary schedule of
game events `adv ω k` — it controls the Byzantine nodes and the network, and it is even allowed
to know all random coins `ω` in advance (a clairvoyant, adaptive adversary).  Then an honest
critic probes the lemma under scrutiny `p`: its probe succeeds with probability `prob`
(independently across rounds; `ω k = true`), in which case it publishes the refutation
synthesized by `synthesize` (`Sovereign.Swarm.Dag`).

The coin sequence `ω : ℕ → Bool` is distributed as `searchMeasure prob`, the i.i.d.
Bernoulli(`prob`) product measure of `Sovereign.Autonomous.Ruin`.

**Convergence theorem** (`convergence`).  Under the Byzantine threshold `f < n/3` and honest
verifiers, starting from any reachable state:

1. an ungrounded (false, unproved or `sorry`-containing) lemma is never accepted, in any round,
   on every sample path;
2. if `prob > 0`, it is rejected — permanently — within finitely many rounds with probability `1`;
3. the probability that it is still not rejected after `k` rounds is at most `(1 - prob) ^ k`;
4. every lemma accepted in some round is grounded and keeps an immutable, verifying consensus
   receipt in all later rounds.
-/

/-- The schedule of round `k`: the adversary's events, then — if the critic's probe succeeds —
the honest critic's synthesized refutation of `p`. -/
/-- The game state after `k` rounds. -/
/-- Later rounds extend earlier ones by some schedule. -/
/-- A successful probe in round `k` rejects an ungrounded lemma. -/
/-- An ungrounded lemma still unrejected after `k` rounds means that all `k` probes missed. -/
/-! ### Probability of missing -/
/-- All of the first `k` probes miss with probability `(1 - prob) ^ k`. -/

/-- **Geometric tail.** The probability that an ungrounded lemma survives `k` rounds
unrejected is at most `(1 - prob) ^ k`, whatever the (clairvoyant) adversary does. -/

/-- **Rejection with probability one within finite rounds.** If the honest critic's probe
succeeds with positive probability, an ungrounded lemma is almost surely rejected after
finitely many rounds, and stays rejected forever. -/
/-- The almost-sure rejection event has probability exactly one. -/

      rcases List.mem_cons.1 hy with rfl | hy
      · exact List.mem_of_getElem? hx
      · exact premConcls_mem hys y hy
    · cases h

declarations.signature_heuristic:
lemma evalDag_append (Γ : List Expr) :
    ∀ (acc : List Expr) (xs ys : Dag),
      evalDag Γ acc (xs ++ ys) = (evalDag Γ acc xs).bind fun acc' => evalDag Γ acc' ys
  | acc, [], ys => by simp [evalDag]
  | acc, n :: xs, ys => by
    simp only [List.cons_append, evalDag]
    cases nodeStep Γ acc n with
    | none => rfl
    | some φ => exact evalDag_append Γ _ xs ys

/-- **Soundness of DAG evaluation**: over a valid library, every computed conclusion is a
valid statement. -/

declarations.name: evalDag_valid
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem evalDag_valid {Γ : List Expr} (hΓ : ∀ φ ∈ Γ, stmtSem.Valid φ) :
    ∀ (acc : List Expr) (ns : Dag) {l : List Expr}, (∀ φ ∈ acc, stmtSem.Valid φ) →
      evalDag Γ acc ns = some l → ∀ φ ∈ l, stmtSem.Valid φ
  | acc, [], l, hacc, h => by simp [evalDag] at h; subst h; exact hacc
  | acc, n :: ns, l, hacc, h => by
    simp only [evalDag] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i φ hφ
      refine evalDag_valid hΓ _ ns ?_ h
      intro ψ hψ
      rcases List.mem_append.1 hψ with hψ | hψ
      · exact hacc ψ hψ
      · simp only [List.mem_singleton] at hψ
        subst hψ
        unfold nodeStep at hφ
        split at hφ
        · rename_i xs hxs
          exact strict_sound Γ hΓ n.rule xs _ hφ fun x hx => hacc x (premConcls_mem hxs x hx)
        · cases hφ
    · cases h

/-- Hole nodes are always rejected by the kernel. -/

declarations.signature_heuristic:
lemma nodeStep_hole (Γ acc : List Expr) (φ : Expr) (prem : List ℕ) :

declarations.name: evalDag_sorryFree
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem evalDag_sorryFree (Γ : List Expr) :
    ∀ (acc : List Expr) (ns : Dag) {l : List Expr}, evalDag Γ acc ns = some l →
      ∀ n ∈ ns, n.rule.isHole = false
  | acc, [], l, _ => by simp
  | acc, n :: ns, l, h => by
    simp only [evalDag] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i φ hφ
      intro m hm
      rcases List.mem_cons.1 hm with rfl | hm
      · rcases m with ⟨r, prem⟩
        cases r with
        | hole ψ => rw [nodeStep_hole] at hφ; cases hφ
        | base _ => rfl
        | induct _ _ => rfl
      · exact evalDag_sorryFree Γ _ ns h m hm
    · cases h

declarations.signature_heuristic:
inductive Refutation where
  /-- node `i` is the first node rejected by the kernel (a boundary refutation) -/
  | boundary (i : ℕ)
  /-- the DAG evaluates but its sink is not the claim -/
  | sinkMismatch
  /-- the claim is false in environment `ρ` -/

declarations.name: checkRefutation
declarations.signature_heuristic:
def checkRefutation (Γ : List Expr) (p : Proposal) : Refutation → Bool
  | .boundary i =>
    match evalDag Γ [] (p.dag.take i), p.dag[i]? with
    | some acc, some n => (nodeStep Γ acc n).isNone
    | _, _ => false
  | .sinkMismatch =>
    match evalDag Γ [] p.dag with
    | some l => decide (l.getLast? ≠ some p.claim)
    | none => false
  | .counterexample ρ => !decide (stmtSem.holds ρ p.claim)

evaluated by the kernel and node `i` is rejected. -/

        nodeStep Γ acc n = none

/-!
# Derivation DAGs and targeted boundary refutations

Prover agents of the swarm propose *derivation DAGs*: a DAG is a list of nodes in topological
order, each node applying one rule of the hole-aware repair kernel `Sovereign.Repair.strict`
to the conclusions of **earlier** nodes (referenced by index, so a conclusion may be shared by
many later nodes — the derivation is a DAG, not a tree).  A *proposal* is a claimed statement
together with a DAG; it is **grounded** when the kernel evaluates every node and the sink (the
last node) concludes the claim.

Verifier / critic agents answer with *refutations*:

* `boundary i` — a **targeted boundary refutation**: the prefix of the DAG before node `i`
  evaluates (it is the grounded frontier) and node `i` is the first node the kernel rejects
  (a `sorry` hole, a dangling or forward premise reference, or an ill-formed rule application);
* `sinkMismatch` — the DAG evaluates but its sink is not the claimed statement;
* `counterexample ρ` — an environment in which the claim is false.

Refutations are plain data checked by `checkRefutation`, so a Byzantine critic cannot censor a
grounded proposal (`checkRefutation_sound`, `grounded_unrefutable`), while an honest critic
always finds a refutation of an ungrounded one (`synthesize_complete`).  Grounded proposals over
a valid library have valid claims (`Grounded.valid`) and never contain holes
(`Grounded.sorryFree`).
-/
/-- A node of a derivation DAG: a rule and the indices of its premise nodes. -/
/-- A derivation DAG, in topological order. -/
/-- A lemma proposal: a claimed statement and a derivation DAG for it. -/
/-- Look up the conclusions of the premises among the conclusions computed so far. -/
/-- Kernel evaluation of one node, given the conclusions of the earlier nodes. -/

/-- Kernel evaluation of a DAG: the list of all node conclusions, or `none` if some node
is rejected. -/
/-- Boolean groundedness test. -/

/-- A proposal is **grounded** when the kernel evaluates its whole DAG and the sink concludes
the claim. -/
/-! ### Structural lemmas -/

/-- **Soundness of DAG evaluation**: over a valid library, every computed conclusion is a
valid statement. -/
/-- Hole nodes are always rejected by the kernel. -/
/-- A DAG that evaluates contains no `sorry` hole. -/
/-- **Grounded claims are valid** (relative to a valid library). -/
/-- **Grounded DAGs are sorry-free.** -/
/-- A proposal whose DAG contains a hole is ungrounded. -/
/-! ### Refutations -/
/-- A critic's refutation of a proposal. -/
/-- node `i` is the first node rejected by the kernel (a boundary refutation) -/
/-- the DAG evaluates but its sink is not the claim -/
/-- the claim is false in environment `ρ` -/
/-- Anyone can check a refutation. -/

/-- A checked boundary refutation pins the *frontier*: the prefix before node `i` is
evaluated by the kernel and node `i` is rejected. -/
/-- A DAG with a rejected node does not evaluate. -/
/-- Checked boundary and sink refutations need no assumption on the library. -/

/-- **Refutations are sound**: over a valid library, any checked refutation (possibly
fabricated by a Byzantine critic) shows the proposal is ungrounded. -/
/-- Grounded proposals cannot be refuted (critics cannot censor valid derivations). -/
/-! ### Honest critics: synthesis of boundary refutations -/
/-- A failing DAG has a first rejected node. -/

/-- The honest critic: search for the first boundary refutation; if the DAG evaluates, check
its sink. Returns `none` exactly on grounded proposals. -/
/-- Every refutation the honest critic synthesizes checks. -/
/-- **Completeness of the honest critic**: it refutes every ungrounded proposal. -/
/-- The honest critic stays silent exactly on grounded proposals. -/

/-- The canonical verifier checker: accept a proposal iff the honest critic finds no
refutation. It is sound and complete for groundedness. -/

/-!
# A worked example: a four-node swarm tolerating one Byzantine node

* `exGood` claims `(2 = 2) ∧ (2 = 2)` with a two-node DAG whose second node uses the first
  node's conclusion twice (a genuine DAG, not a tree); it is grounded.
* `exSorry` claims `(2 = 2) ∧ false` and hides a `sorry` hole in its middle node; the honest
  critic pins the boundary at node `1`.
* `exForward` cites a premise that does not exist yet (a forward reference); the critic pins
  the boundary at node `0`.

The fabric has four nodes (`n = 4`, `f = 1`, quorum `3`): node `0` is the prover, the others
are verifiers/critics, and every honest node runs the canonical checker `verifierCheck`.
With at most one Byzantine node: `exSorry` is never accepted, it is rejected with probability
one within finitely many rounds as soon as the critic's probe has positive success
probability, and `exGood` is certified by one honest round.
-/
/-- A grounded proposal whose DAG shares a node. -/
/-- A proposal hiding a `sorry` hole. -/
/-- A proposal citing a premise that is not yet derived. -/
/-- The honest critic pins the `sorry` at node `1`. -/
/-- The honest critic pins the forward reference at node `0`. -/

/-- The four-node fabric: node `0` proves, the others verify; quorum `3`; symbolic
commitments (the log itself). -/
/-- With at most one Byzantine node, `exSorry` is never accepted, under any schedule. -/

/-- With at most one Byzantine node and a critic whose probe succeeds with probability
`prob > 0`, `exSorry` is rejected within finitely many rounds almost surely. -/

/-- With at most one Byzantine node, one honest round certifies `exGood` after any
adversarial prefix and whatever happens afterwards. -/

declarations.name: BFT
declarations.signature_heuristic:
structure BFT (corrupt : Finset Node) (F : Fabric Node Proposal C) (f : ℕ) : Prop where
  threshold : 3 * f < Fintype.card Node
  corrupt_le : corrupt.card ≤ f
  quorum_eq : F.quorum = Fintype.card Node - f

/-- Honest verifiers (possibly with heterogeneous implementations) accept exactly the grounded
proposals. -/

  sound : ∀ n, n ∉ corrupt → ∀ p, F.checker n p = true → Grounded Γ p
  complete : ∀ n, n ∉ corrupt → ∀ p, Grounded Γ p → F.checker n p = true

/-!
# The adversarial verification game on top of the consensus fabric

This file extends the proof-verification consensus protocol of `Sovereign.Consensus` (shards,
ideal signatures, quorum certificates, hash-chained receipts) to an **adversarial verification
game** between prover and verifier/critic agents:

* shards are lemma `Proposal`s (a claim together with a derivation DAG, `Sovereign.Swarm.Dag`);
  prover nodes (the `orchestrator` role) propose batches of lemmas;
* verifier nodes sign a lemma when their own checker accepts it (as in `Sovereign.Consensus`);
* critic nodes publish **refutations**; a `refute` event takes effect only when the refutation
  checks (`checkRefutation`), in which case the lemma is permanently *rejected*, every pending
  batch containing it is dropped, and the refutation is kept as public evidence.

The adversary controls the schedule and a set `corrupt` of Byzantine nodes, which may sign
anything and publish any refutation.  The Byzantine threshold is the classical one:
`BFT corrupt F f` says `3 f < n`, `|corrupt| ≤ f` and the quorum is `n - f`.

Main results:

* `bft_quorum_intersection`: any two quorums share an honest node;
* `ungrounded_never_accepted`: in every reachable state an ungrounded (in particular a false or
  `sorry`-containing) lemma has no quorum, is in no certified batch and in no verifying receipt,
  even one fabricated by the adversary;
* `rejected_ungrounded`, `grounded_never_rejected`: rejection is sound — Byzantine critics
  cannot censor grounded lemmas;
* `accepted_immutable`: accepted lemmas obtain a receipt that persists and keeps verifying
  forever, the certified log is append-only and the state commitment is its hash chain;
* `grounded_batch_certified`: after any adversarial prefix, one honest round certifies a batch
  of grounded lemmas, whatever happens afterwards.
-/
/-! ### Byzantine threshold and honest verifiers -/

/-- The Byzantine fault model: fewer than a third of the nodes are corrupted, and the quorum
is `n - f`. -/

/-- Honest verifiers (possibly with heterogeneous implementations) accept exactly the grounded
proposals. -/

/-- The canonical checker `verifierCheck` (accept iff the honest critic finds no refutation)
yields honest verifiers. -/

/-- Under the Byzantine threshold, honest verifiers give the safety assumptions of the
consensus fabric. -/

/-- Under the Byzantine threshold, honest verifiers give the liveness assumptions of the
consensus fabric. -/

/-- **Quorum intersection.** Under `3 f < n`, any two quorums of size `n - f` share an
honest node. -/
/-! ### The game -/

/-- State of the verification game: the consensus state, the rejected lemmas and the published
refutation evidence. -/
/-- Events of the game: consensus events and critic refutations. -/
/-- One step of the game. A refutation takes effect only when it checks. -/
/-- Run a schedule of game events. -/
/-- The initial game state. -/
/-- Game states reachable under some adversarial schedule. -/
/-- A lemma is *accepted* when it belongs to a certified batch. -/
/-- Pure consensus schedules run the consensus protocol on the core state. -/
/-- The certified log is append-only. -/
/-- Rejection is permanent. -/
/-! ### The game invariant -/

/-- The invariant of the game: the consensus invariant, and every rejection is backed by a
checked refutation in the public evidence. -/
/-! ### Safety -/
/-- A shard covered by a verifying receipt has quorum. -/
/-- In a state satisfying the consensus invariant, only grounded lemmas have quorum. -/

/-- **Safety of the verification game.** Under the Byzantine threshold `f < n/3` and honest
verifiers, in every reachable state (under every adversarial schedule) an ungrounded lemma —
in particular a false one, or one whose DAG contains a `sorry` hole — has no quorum, is not
accepted, and appears in no verifying receipt, even one fabricated by the adversary. -/

/-- Every accepted lemma is grounded; over a valid library its claim is valid and its DAG is
sorry-free. -/
/-- Every rejected lemma is ungrounded (rejection is backed by a checked refutation). -/
/-- **No censorship.** Byzantine critics can never get a grounded lemma rejected. -/
/-- Rejected and accepted lemmas are disjoint. -/
/-! ### Immutable consensus receipts -/

/-- **Immutable consensus receipts.** If lemma `p` is accepted in a reachable state `g`, then
there is a receipt `r` issued in `g` certifying a batch containing `p` such that, after *any*
further adversarial schedule `es`: `p` is still accepted, `r` is still in the ledger and still
verifies, the old certified log is a suffix of the new one (append-only history), and the state
commitment is the hash chain of the log. -/

/-- **Binding.** With an injective commitment function, two reachable game states with the same
state commitment have the same certified log. -/
/-! ### Liveness -/
/-- The honest round certifies a batch of grounded lemmas from any core state. -/

/-- **Liveness of the verification game.** From any reachable state, after any adversarial
prefix `pre`, one honest round (proposal by a prover, signatures by all honest verifiers,
certification request) certifies a batch `a` of grounded lemmas, whatever the adversary does
afterwards (`post`, including refutation attempts): every lemma of `a` is accepted with a
verifying receipt. -/

/-!
# Non-ergodic regret bounds and absence of absorbing ruin for the swarm

The swarm's *capital* evolves round by round.  In round `k` the swarm stakes a fraction `fr k`
of its capital at odds `b k` on the lemmas it builds on; the outcome `ω k` of the round
(success / failure) may be chosen by an adversary.  If after round `k` the certified knowledge
base is **poisoned** — some accepted lemma is ungrounded — everything built on it is lost: the
capital drops to `0`, and `0` is absorbing (`capital_absorbing`).  This is *catastrophic
absorbing ruin*.

* `no_catastrophic_ruin`: for every adversarial play of the verification game (any schedules,
  any Byzantine behaviour of up to `f < n/3` nodes), any adversarial outcomes and odds `b k ≥ 0`,
  and any stakes in `[0, cap]` with `cap < 1`, the capital stays strictly positive in every
  round, on every trajectory, and satisfies the **non-ergodic (pathwise) regret bound**
  `log W_k ≥ k · log (1 - cap)`.  `swarm_no_catastrophic_ruin` specialises it to the pooled
  Kelly stakes of heterogeneous agents in the Poincaré ball.
* `kelly_regret_ae`: in an i.i.d. environment, the swarm staking the Kelly fraction has
  per-round regret tending to `0` almost surely against the optimal growth rate, and
  asymptotically dominates every other constant hedged fraction on almost every trajectory.
* `unhedged_ensemble_vs_time`: non-ergodicity — the ensemble mean of an unhedged strategy grows
  like `(p (1 + b)) ^ k` although almost every trajectory is absorbed at `0`.
* `byzantine_poisoning`: the threshold matters — once the corrupted nodes can fill a quorum,
  they can get an ungrounded lemma accepted, after which the capital is `0` forever;
  `bft_threshold_tight`: for `3 f ≥ n`, two quorums of size `n - f` can meet only in corrupted
  nodes.
-/
/-! ### Capital dynamics -/

/-- The swarm capital: stake `fr k` at odds `b k` in round `k`, outcome `ω k`; wiped out when
the knowledge base is poisoned after round `k`. -/
/-- Ruin is absorbing: once the capital is `0` it stays `0`. -/
/-- Poisoning is catastrophic: the capital is `0` from then on. -/

/-- **Pathwise capital bound.** Without poisoning, with stakes in `[0, cap]`, `cap < 1`, and
nonnegative odds, the capital is at least `(1 - cap) ^ k`, whatever the outcomes. -/
/-! ### No catastrophic ruin under Byzantine corruption -/
/-- The knowledge base of a game state is poisoned when some accepted lemma is ungrounded. -/
/-- Reachable states of the game are never poisoned under the Byzantine threshold. -/

/-- **No catastrophic absorbing ruin, with a non-ergodic regret bound.** Let `gs k` be the game
states produced by *any* adversarial play (each reachable; up to `f < n/3` Byzantine nodes),
let the outcomes `ω` and the odds `b k ≥ 0` be adversarial, and let the swarm's stakes lie in
`[0, cap]` with `cap < 1`. Then on every trajectory and in every round the swarm capital
(wiped out on poisoning) is strictly positive, and `log W_k ≥ k · log (1 - cap)`. -/

/-- **The heterogeneous swarm never suffers catastrophic ruin.** When in round `k` the swarm
stakes its pooled Kelly stake `swarmStake agents (x k)` on a lemma at position `x k` of the
Poincaré ball, the capital stays positive on every trajectory, and
`log W_k ≥ k · log (1 - max cap)`. -/
/-! ### The threshold is necessary -/

/-- **Byzantine poisoning.** If the corrupted nodes can fill a quorum, then for any ungrounded
lemma `p` there is a schedule after which `p` is accepted — the knowledge base is poisoned. -/

/-- **Tightness of `f < n/3`.** If `3 f ≥ n` (and `f ≤ n`), there are two sets of `n - f`
nodes among `n` and a set of at most `f` corrupted nodes containing their whole intersection:
quorum intersection fails. -/
/-! ### Almost-sure regret of the Kelly swarm in an i.i.d. environment -/

/-- Without poisoning, a constant stake reproduces the budget process of
`Sovereign.Autonomous.Ruin`. -/

/-- **Vanishing regret of the Kelly swarm.** Suppose round outcomes are i.i.d. Bernoulli(`p`)
with `0 < p < 1`, odds `b > 0`, and the game is played by any adversary under the Byzantine
threshold. If the swarm stakes the Kelly fraction `f* = (p b - (1 - p))/b ≥ 0`, then almost
surely:

* its per-round regret against the optimal growth rate `G* = G(f*)` vanishes:
  `(k G* - log W_k) / k → 0`;
* against any other constant hedged fraction `g` (with `0 < 1 + g b`, `g < 1`), the per-round
  log-capital advantage converges to `G(f*) - G(g) ≥ 0`. -/
/-! ### Non-ergodicity: ensemble average versus time average -/

/-- **Non-ergodicity of unhedged exploration.** The ensemble mean of the unhedged capital
(`f = 1`) after `k` rounds is `(p (1 + b)) ^ k` — exponentially growing when `p (1 + b) > 1` —
yet almost every trajectory is absorbed at `0`. Time averages and ensemble averages disagree;
this is why the swarm must be judged pathwise, as in `no_catastrophic_ruin`. -/

# `Sovereign.Swarm`

Distributed multi-agent theorem verification, Byzantine fault-tolerant adversarial
consensus games, Poincaré metric stake bounding, and non-ergodic regret bounds.
-/

/-!
# Cut elimination and sharing compression of proof trees

A *proof with cuts* (`CProof R`) over the rules `R` of a rule system
(`Sovereign.Compression.RuleSystem R F`) may, besides ordinary inference steps, contain
**cuts**: `cut a b` first proves a lemma by `a`, then continues with `b`, in which `hyp 0`
refers to that lemma (de Bruijn indices: `hyp i` is the `i`-th enclosing cut lemma).

* `CProof.check S Γ p` — the checker for proofs with cuts, with the lemma context `Γ`;
* `elim σ p` — the **cut-elimination algorithm**: every reference to a cut lemma is replaced by
  (a copy of) the cut-free proof of the lemma, producing an ordinary proof tree `PTree R`;
* `compress p` — cut elimination followed by macro-lemma sharing (`Sovereign.Compression.dedup`),
  producing a proof DAG.

Main results:
* `elim_check` — **cut elimination preserves deductive power**: whenever a proof with cuts
  checks with conclusion `φ`, its cut elimination succeeds and the cut-free tree checks with the

/-!
# The self-supervised lemma synthesis and meta-inductive compression engine

A **library** is a list of synthesized lemmas (`SLemma`). Its invariant `WF` says that every
lemma passed the admission test of `Sovereign.Synthesis.Filter` against the lemmas *before* it:
it is kernel-certified citing only earlier closed theorems, it passes the cohomology filter
(non-circular, no vacuous hypothesis), it is anti-tautological and novel.

One engine round (`MetaEngine.round`) consists of
1. **self-supervised synthesis** (`synthStep`): an untrusted proposer, which sees the current
   library (and the round number), proposes candidate lemmas; each candidate that passes the
   admission test is appended;
2. **meta-inductive compression** (`compressStep`): an untrusted rewriter proposes, for every
   lemma, a replacement proof DAG (for instance the cut-elimination-and-sharing pipeline of
   `Sovereign.Synthesis.CutElim` via `cutElimRewriter`, or `dedupRewriter`); the replacement is installed only if the
   new lemma still passes the admission test against the same earlier lemmas **and** its
   Kolmogorov certificate size (`csize`, bit length of the encoded proof DAG) is strictly
   smaller.

Main results:
* `compression_monotone` — iterating compression with arbitrary (round-dependent) rewriters:
  the sequents of the library, hence its deductive power, never change; the total certificate
  size is antitone and at every round either the library is unchanged or its size **strictly
  decreases**; the compression ratio is antitone; at most `libSize L₀` rounds are strict, so
  strict decrease cannot go on forever (`not_forall_strict`); every certificate size bounds the
  Kolmogorov complexity of the lemma relative to the proof-checking decoder;
* `run_spec` — for the full engine: every lemma ever in the library meets the non-circularity
  and anti-tautology criteria of the cohomology filter (`admitted_spec`), deductive power only
  grows, lemmas are never lost, and the certificate size of every individual lemma is
  non-increasing over time;
* `run_valid` — with a sound kernel, every lemma of the library is valid;
* `MetaEngine.roundCertificate`, `compress_certificate_symm`, `round_strict` — each round is an
  admissible transition of `Sovereign.Meta.UpgradeEngine` (the library viewed as a sound
  refuter of non-theorems), compression rounds are admissible in both directions (no loss of
  power), and a round adding a new theorem is strictly admissible.
-/
/-- A library of synthesized lemmas. -/
/-- The sequents of a library. -/
/-- The closed theorems of a library. -/
/-- Total Kolmogorov certificate size of a library. -/
/-- A proof rewriter: given the library, the index and the lemma, propose a new proof DAG. -/
/-- The sharing rewriter: quotient every proof DAG into its minimum-size DAG. -/

/-- The cut-elimination rewriter: an untrusted oracle suggests a proof with cuts, which is
cut-eliminated and shared by `Sovereign.Synthesis.compress`. -/
/-- The library invariant: each lemma is admissible against the lemmas before it. -/
/-- **Self-supervised synthesis step**: admit the candidates one by one. -/

/-- Install a proposed proof DAG only if the lemma stays admissible and its Kolmogorov
certificate size strictly decreases. -/
/-- **Meta-inductive compression step.** -/
/-- **No loss of deductive power**: compression does not change any sequent. -/

/-- A compression step either leaves the library unchanged or strictly decreases its total
Kolmogorov certificate size. -/
/-- The idle rewriter leaves the library unchanged. -/
/-- Iterated compression with round-dependent rewriters. -/
/-- The compression ratio after `t` rounds. -/
/-- Strict decrease of the certificate size cannot go on forever. -/
/-- At a strict round with a nonempty certificate the compression ratio strictly decreases. -/
/-! ### Soundness of well-formed libraries -/

/-- **Soundness of the library**: with a sound kernel, every lemma of a well-formed library is
valid (its conclusion holds whenever its hypotheses do). -/
/-! ### The full engine -/

/-- The self-supervised synthesis and meta-inductive upgrade engine. Only the kernel is trusted;
the proposer and the rewriter are arbitrary. -/
/-- the trusted kernel, parametrised by the citable theorems -/
/-- the external triviality test (e.g. a truth-table tautology checker) -/
/-- the code for kernel rules, fixing the Kolmogorov certificate size -/
/-- the untrusted self-supervised proposer: round, current library ↦ candidates -/
/-- the untrusted round-dependent proof rewriter -/
/-- One engine round: synthesis, then compression. -/
/-- The library after `t` rounds. -/
/-- In one round, a lemma already present keeps its sequent and does not grow. -/

/-- **Per-lemma monotone compression**: once a lemma enters the library, its sequent never
changes and its Kolmogorov certificate size never increases. -/

/-- **Engine specification.** For every proposer and rewriter:
* every lemma in the library at any time meets the criteria of the cohomology filter against
  the lemmas before it (`admitted_spec`): kernel-certified, no circular loop, vanishing oriented
  `H¹`, a rank function, no vacuous hypothesis, all hypotheses cited, conclusion neither assumed
  nor trivial, and novel;
* deductive power only grows (the sequent list only extends) and lemmas are never lost;
* the Kolmogorov certificate size of each lemma is non-increasing in time. -/
/-- **Soundness of the engine**: with a sound kernel, every lemma ever synthesized is valid. -/
/-! ### Rounds as admissible transitions of the meta upgrade engine -/

/-- The "countermodel" relation: a statement is refuted when it is not a non-theorem, i.e. a
sound refuter of `ProvSat Valid` certifies validity. -/

/-- A well-formed library over a sound kernel, as a sound refuter: it refutes (the negation of)
exactly its closed theorems. -/
/-- The library after `t` rounds, as a sound refuter. -/

/-- **Every round is an admissible upgrade**, certified against the ledger of all previously
proved theorems. -/
/-- A round that proves a new closed theorem is a strictly admissible upgrade. -/

/-- **Compression is an equivalence of refutation power**: a compression step is certified as an
admissible upgrade in both directions. -/

/-!
# Synthesized lemmas and the cohomology filter

A **synthesized lemma** (`SLemma R F`) is a sequent `hyps ⊢ stmt` together with a proof DAG
(`Sovereign.Compression.Dag`) and a root index. The DAG is written in the *hypothetical* rule
system `hypSys S hyps` over the rules `R ⊕ ℕ`: `inl r` is a rule of the underlying kernel `S`,
and `inr i` is a leaf citing the `i`-th hypothesis.

From the proof DAG we derive a Clarifier certificate (`SLemma.cert`): its nodes are the DAG
nodes, the statement of a node is what the kernel derives there, the dependencies are the
premise references, the hypothesis nodes are the `inr` leaves and the goal is the root. The
**cohomology filter** (`cechGate`) runs the Clarifier kernel gate
(`Sovereign.Clarifier.Certificate.gate`) on that certificate: it rejects dependency cycles
(detected through the oriented first cohomology of the dependency graph) and vacuous
hypotheses.

*Terminology.* The cohomology used by the filter is the first cohomology `H¹(G; ℚ)` of the
dependency graph viewed as a 1-dimensional complex (`Sovereign.Clarifier.DepGraph.H1`), together
with its oriented refinement. We call the gate `cechGate` because this is the cohomology the
request refers to; no comparison theorem with Čech cohomology of an open cover is proved here.

The **admission test** `admitB K triv P l` (against the sequents `P` of the lemmas already in the
library, whose closed statements form the citable context `ctxOf P`) accepts exactly the lemmas
that are (`admitB_iff`)
* **kernel-certified**: the DAG proves `stmt` from `hyps` in the kernel `K (ctxOf P)`;
* **non-circular**: the derived dependency graph has no circular loop;
* **anti-tautological**: no vacuous hypothesis node (each is used by the conclusion and differs
  from it), every declared hypothesis is cited, the conclusion is not among the hypotheses, and
  the conclusion is not flagged trivial by the external triviality test `triv`;
* **novel**: the conclusion is not already a theorem and the sequent is not already in the
  library.

Consequences (`admitted_spec`): the lemma is sound, its dependency graph has vanishing oriented
`H¹` and an ordinal ranking, so the transfinite induction scheme of
`Sovereign.Synthesis.Ordinal` applies to it (`Certificate.toRankedDag`).

We also fix the Kolmogorov certificate size of a lemma, `csize`: the bit length of the
self-delimiting encoding of its proof DAG. `kc_le_csize`: it bounds the Kolmogorov complexity of
the conclusion relative to the proof-checking decoder.
-/
/-- Rules of the hypothetical system: kernel rules and hypothesis citations. -/
/-- The hypothetical rule system: the kernel `S` plus leaves citing the hypotheses `Γ`. -/
/-- A synthesized lemma: the sequent `hyps ⊢ stmt` and a proof DAG with a root. -/
/-- declared hypotheses -/
/-- claimed conclusion -/
/-- proof DAG in the hypothetical rule system -/
/-- index of the root node -/
/-- The sequent proved by a lemma. -/
/-- The lemma is certified by the kernel `S`. -/
/-- Soundness of certified lemmas: valid hypotheses give a valid conclusion. -/
/-- Premise references of a DAG node. -/
/-- Hypothesis-citation rules. -/
/-- The Clarifier certificate derived from the proof DAG of a lemma. -/
/-- **The cohomology filter**: the Clarifier kernel gate on the derived certificate. -/
/-- The derived dependency graph is free of circular reasoning. -/
/-- The derived certificate has no vacuous hypothesis node. -/
/-- Every declared hypothesis is cited by some hypothesis node. -/
/-- The citable context of a library: the conclusions of its closed (hypothesis-free) lemmas. -/

/-- **The admission test** for a synthesized lemma, against the sequents `P` already in the
library, with kernel `K` (parametrised by the citable context) and triviality test `triv`. -/
/-- The anti-tautology criteria. -/
/-- Novelty: not already a theorem, not already a lemma of the library. -/

/-- The admission test accepts exactly the certified, non-circular, anti-tautological, novel
lemmas. -/
/-! ### Consequences of admission -/

/-- The trivial proof system (every inference allowed), used to view a certificate's dependency
graph as a ranked DAG. -/
/-- An accepted certificate is an ordinal-ranked DAG (ranks from the gate's rank function). -/

/-- **Transfinite induction over an accepted certificate**: a property inherited along
dependencies holds at every node. -/

/-- **Every admitted lemma meets the non-circularity and anti-tautology criteria**, certified by
the cohomology filter: it is kernel-certified and sound, its derived dependency graph has no
circular loop, has vanishing oriented first cohomology and a rank function, every hypothesis node
is used by the conclusion and differs from it, every declared hypothesis is cited, the conclusion
is neither assumed nor trivial, and it is new. -/

/-- An admitted lemma is sound: if the citable context and its hypotheses are valid, so is its
conclusion. -/
/-- A circular proof DAG is rejected, and its dependency graph has `H¹ ≠ 0`. -/
/-! ### Kolmogorov certificate size -/
/-- Self-delimiting code for hypothetical rules. -/
/-- **Kolmogorov certificate size** of a lemma: the bit length of its encoded proof DAG. -/

/-- The proof-checking decoder: a bit string is read as a proof DAG and mapped to the statement
it proves from the hypotheses `Γ`. -/

/-- The certificate size of a certified lemma bounds the Kolmogorov complexity of its conclusion
relative to the proof-checking decoder. -/

/-!
# The synthesis engine over the NeuroBridge / Discovery stack

We instantiate the meta engine of `Sovereign.Synthesis.Engine` with
* the statement language `Sovereign.Bridge.Expr` and the strict, hole-rejecting kernel
  `Sovereign.Repair.strict` (citing the library's closed theorems);
* the truth-table tautology checker `Sovereign.Bridge.Expr.isTaut` as triviality test;
* a **self-supervised proposer** built from a NeuroBridge neural proposer
  (`Sovereign.NeuroBridge.NeuralProposer`) and Discovery structural analogies
  (`Sovereign.Discovery.Analogy`): the goals of a round are the analogical images of the
  library's own theorems (plus untrusted bootstrap seeds), the neural proposer suggests proof
  scripts for them, and each script is compressed into a proof DAG by `dedup`;
* optionally the **Kelly beam bridge** (`Sovereign.NeuroBridge.KellyBeamBridge`), whose beam
  prunes the neural proposals before admission (`bridgeProposer`).

`neuroEngine_valid`: every lemma ever synthesized by these engines is valid, and every lemma
meets the criteria of the cohomology filter (`MetaEngine.run_spec`).

A worked example (`demoEngine`) runs two rounds: round 0 admits `2 + 2 = 4` and rejects a
`sorry` hole; round 1 transports the theorem along the symmetry analogy and admits `4 = 2 + 2`,
citing the first theorem. Tautological and circular candidates are rejected.

own theorems. -/

current set of theorems. -/

/-- **Soundness of the NeuroBridge synthesis engine**: whatever the neural proposer, the
analogies, the seeds and the rewriter, every synthesized lemma is valid whenever its hypotheses
are. -/
/-- No synthesized lemma of the NeuroBridge engine is a propositional tautology. -/

/-!
# Formal proof systems and ordinal-ranked proof DAGs

A *proof system* (`ProofSystem F`) over statements `F` is given by its one-step inference
relation `Infers S φ`: the statement `φ` follows by one inference from the set of premises `S`.
Premise sets may be infinite, so infinitary rules such as the ω-rule are allowed.

An *ordinal-ranked proof DAG* (`RankedDag P N`) over the node type `N` assigns to every node a
conclusion, a set of premise nodes and an ordinal rank, such that
* every premise has strictly smaller rank than the node using it (`rank_lt`), and
* every node is a correct inference of the proof system from its premises (`infers`).

Nodes may be shared by several parents (a DAG, not a tree) and there may be infinitely many.

Main results:
* `RankedDag.induction` — the **transfinite induction scheme** over a ranked proof DAG: a
  property that is inherited from all premises of a node to the node holds at every node;
* `transfinite_induction_scheme` — the bounded ordinal scheme `TI(α)` holds for every `α`;
* `RankedDag.sound` — every node of a ranked DAG over a sound proof system has a valid conclusion;
* `rankable_iff_wellFounded` — a premise structure admits an ordinal ranking iff it is
  well-founded (the canonical rank is `IsWellFounded.rank`);
* `omegaDag`, `omega_le_rank_top` — an ω-rule proof DAG whose top node has rank `ω` under every
  ranking, so genuinely transfinite ranks occur; `omegaDag_sound` derives ordinary induction
  from it.
-/
/-- A formal proof system: the one-step inference relation on statements. -/
/-- `Infers S φ`: `φ` follows by one inference from the premises `S`. -/

/-- A proof system is sound for `Valid` if every inference from valid premises has a valid
conclusion. -/
/-- An ordinal-ranked proof DAG over the node type `N`. -/
/-- The statement proved at each node. -/
/-- The premise nodes of each node (possibly infinitely many, possibly shared). -/
/-- The ordinal rank of each node. -/
/-- Premises have strictly smaller rank. -/
/-- Every node is a correct inference from its premises. -/
/-- **Transfinite induction over a ranked proof DAG.** -/
/-- Transfinite induction restricted to the nodes of rank below `α`. -/
/-- The premise relation of a ranked DAG is well-founded. -/

/-- **Soundness by transfinite induction**: over a sound proof system every node of a ranked
proof DAG proves a valid statement. -/
/-- The bounded **transfinite induction scheme** `TI(α)` for a property `C` of ordinals. -/
/-- Every instance of the transfinite induction scheme holds. -/

/-- **Rankability is well-foundedness**: a premise structure admits an ordinal ranking in which
premises have strictly smaller rank iff the premise relation is well-founded. -/
/-! ### A genuinely transfinite example: the ω-rule -/
/-- Statements of the ω-rule example: `some k` is the instance `C k`, `none` is `∀ k, C k`. -/

/-- The ω-rule proof system: the axiom `C 0`, the step rule `C k ⊢ C (k+1)`, and the infinitary
ω-rule `{C k | k ∈ ℕ} ⊢ ∀ k, C k`. -/
/-- The semantics of the ω-rule system for a property `C` closed under zero and successor. -/
/-- Premises in the ω-rule DAG. -/
/-- The ω-rule proof DAG: node `some k` has rank `k`, the ω-node `none` has rank `ω`. -/

/-- The ω-node needs a transfinite rank: under **every** ranking of the ω-rule DAG its rank is
at least `ω`. -/
/-- Transfinite induction over the ω-rule DAG yields ordinary induction. -/

# `Sovereign.Synthesis`

Autonomous self-supervised axiomatic synthesis, meta-inductive upgrade engine,
transfinite proof DAG optimization, and cut-elimination with Kolmogorov compression.

/-!
# Acoustic vortex lines in three dimensions and their topological charge

A (time-harmonic) **complex acoustic velocity potential** on space `ℝ³` is `ψ = u + i v`
with real continuous components `u, v`. Its **vortex core** (phase singularity, nodal line)
is `{ψ = 0} = {u = 0} ∩ {v = 0}`, the intersection of the two real *nodal surfaces*.

* `AcousticPotential.charge`: the **topological charge** of a closed loop avoiding the core is
  the winding number of `ψ` along the loop.
* `phase_circulation_quantized`, `berry_phase_quantization`: the phase circulation
  `∮ dθ` around the loop is exactly `2π n`, `n ∈ ℤ` the charge; in integral form
  (`berry_phase_integral_loop`) `∮ (u dv - v du)/(u² + v²) = 2π n` for `C¹` data.
* `ChargeCertificate`: an immutable certificate — unique (`Subsingleton`) and always
  available (`certify`).
* `NonsingularDeformation.charge_conserved`: along any continuous deformation of the field
  (e.g. a frequency sweep) and of the loop keeping the loop off the vortex core, the charge is
  constant; `total_charge_conserved` for any finite family of vortex loops
  (`∑ nᵢ = const`).
* `chladniSuperposition`: multi-frequency fields `ψ = ∑ⱼ cⱼ ψ_{mⱼ}` built from the 3D Chladni
  box modes; `frequencySweep` is a sweep of box dimensions and amplitudes.
* `cubeVortex`: `ψ = ψ_{(2,1,1)} + i ψ_{(1,2,1)}` in the cube `[0, π]³` has a straight vortex
  line `x = y = π/2` (`cubeVortex_core`), of charge `+1` (`cubeVortex_charge`), and its
  conjugate `cubeAntivortex` has charge `-1`.
-/
/-- Points of three-dimensional space. -/
/-- A complex acoustic velocity potential `ψ = u + i v` on `ℝ³`. -/
/-- Real part of the potential. -/
/-- Imaginary part of the potential. -/
/-- The complex potential `ψ = u + i v`. -/
/-- The **vortex core** (nodal line, phase singularity) `{ψ = 0}`. -/
/-- The vortex core is the intersection of the two real nodal surfaces `u = 0` and `v = 0`. -/
/-- A closed loop in space that avoids the vortex core. -/
/-- The loop. -/
/-- The complex signal `t ↦ ψ (γ t)` recorded along a loop. -/

/-- The **topological charge** of the vortex lines threading the loop: the winding number of
the phase of `ψ` around the loop. -/

/-- **Quantization of the phase circulation**: around any closed loop enclosing (or not) the
vortex core, the phase circulation is `2π n`, `n` the integer topological charge. -/

/-- **Berry phase quantization**: for every continuous phase `θ` of `ψ` along the loop
(`ψ = |ψ| e^{iθ}`), the accumulated phase is `θ(1) - θ(0) = 2π n` with `n` the topological
charge, and `n` is the unique integer with this property. -/
/-- A continuous phase of `ψ` along the loop always exists. -/
/-- The restriction to `[0, 1]` of a `C¹` curve in space. -/
/-- A `C¹` closed curve avoiding the vortex core, as a core-avoiding loop. -/

/-- **Berry phase quantization, integral form.** For a `C¹` potential and a `C¹` closed curve
avoiding the vortex core, the phase circulation integral
`∮ (u dv - v du)/(u² + v²)` equals `2π n`, `n` the topological charge. -/
/-! ### Immutable charge certificates -/

/-- A **topological charge certificate** for a loop: an integer `n` such that every continuous
phase of `ψ` along the loop accumulates exactly `2π n`. -/
/-- The certified charge. -/
/-- Every loop has a charge certificate, carrying the topological charge. -/
/-- Charge certificates are **immutable**: any two certificates for the same loop coincide. -/
/-! ### Conservation of topological charge under non-singular deformations -/

/-- A **non-singular deformation**: a continuous one-parameter family of acoustic potentials
(for instance a frequency sweep) together with a continuous family of closed loops that never
meet the vortex core of the current field. -/
/-- The field at parameter `s`. -/
/-- The loop at parameter `s`, as the map `(t, s) ↦ γ_s(t)`. -/
/-- The loop at parameter `s`. -/

/-- **Conservation of topological charge**: the charge is the same at all parameters of a
non-singular deformation. -/

/-- **Conservation of total topological charge**: for any finite family of vortex loops, each
carried along a non-singular deformation, the total charge `∑ nᵢ` is constant. -/
/-! ### Multi-frequency Chladni fields -/

/-- A **multi-frequency acoustic potential** in the box `∏ [0, Lᵢ]`: the superposition
`ψ = ∑ⱼ cⱼ ψ_{mⱼ}` of Chladni box modes with complex amplitudes `cⱼ`; each mode `ψ_{mⱼ}` solves
the Helmholtz equation with its own wave number (`helmholtz_boxMode`). -/

/-- For a single mode with a nonzero amplitude there is no genuine vortex: inside the box the
"vortex core" is the whole Chladni nodal set of the mode. -/

/-- A **frequency sweep**: box dimensions `L(s)` (hence all modal frequencies `mᵢπ/Lᵢ(s)`) and
amplitudes `cⱼ(s)` vary continuously with the sweep parameter `s`. -/

/-- **Charge conservation under a frequency sweep**: if a continuous family of loops never meets
the vortex core during the sweep, the topological charge at the start and at the end of the
sweep agree. -/

/-!
# The phase circulation integral (Berry phase) of a smooth nonvanishing loop

For a `C¹` curve `t ↦ ψ(t) = u(t) + i v(t)` avoiding `0` on `[0, 1]`, the phase gradient
integral
`∮ dθ = ∫₀¹ (u v' - v u') / (u² + v²) dt`
equals the total change of the continuous phase (`phaseCirculation`); for a closed curve it is
exactly `2π n` with `n` the integer winding number (`berry_phase_integral`).

The proof is the classical one: with `G(t) = ∫₀ᵗ ψ'/ψ`, the function `ψ e^{-G}` has zero
derivative, so `log ψ(0) + G` is a continuous logarithm of `ψ`.
-/
/-- The complex curve `t ↦ u t + i v t` built from two real components. -/
/-- The restriction of `planeCurve u v` to the parameter interval `[0, 1]`. -/
/-- The total change of the continuous logarithm is the integral of `ψ'/ψ`. -/

/-- **Berry phase quantization (integral form).** For a `C¹` closed curve
`ψ = u + i v` avoiding the nodal point `ψ = 0`, the phase circulation integral
`∮ (u dv - v du)/(u² + v²)` equals `2π n`, where `n` is the integer winding number
(topological charge) of the loop. -/

/-- The phase circulation integral around a closed nodal-avoiding curve is an integer multiple
of `2π`. -/

/-!
# Chladni figures in two and three dimensions

Specialisations of the general box theory to

* **2D plates** `[0, a] × [0, b]` with modes `(p, q)`:
  `ψ(x, y) = sin(pπx/a) sin(qπy/b)`, `k² = (pπ/a)² + (qπ/b)²`, `p·q` nodal domains, Courant's
  bound, singular nodal points = the `(p-1)(q-1)` interior crossings of nodal lines, and the
  Euler-type relation `domains = crossings + lines₁ + lines₂ + 1`;
* **3D cavities** `[0, a] × [0, b] × [0, c]` with modes `(p, q, r)`: `p·q·r` nodal domains,
  Courant's bound, `(p-1)(q-1)(r-1)` interior triple crossings of nodal planes;
* the classical **degenerate Chladni pattern** on the square `[0, π]²`,
  `ψ = sin(px) sin(qy) - sin(qx) sin(py)`, a Chladni nodal manifold with `k² = p² + q²` whose nodal
  set contains the diagonal;
* kernel-checked integer certificates (`decide`) for concrete modes.
-/
/-! ### Two-dimensional plates -/
/-- The side lengths `(a, b)` of a rectangular plate. -/
/-- The mode `(p, q)` of a rectangular plate. -/
/-- **2D Chladni plate**: `sin(pπx/a) sin(qπy/b)` solves `Δψ + k²ψ = 0`. -/
/-- A `(p, q)` Chladni plate has exactly `p·q` nodal domains. -/
/-- **Courant's theorem on the rectangular plate.** -/
/-- On a plate, the singular nodal points are exactly the interior crossings of nodal lines. -/
/-- A `(p, q)` plate has `(p-1)(q-1)` crossing points of nodal lines. -/

/-- Euler-type relation for Chladni plates: the nodal lines and their crossings determine the
number of nodal domains, `domains = crossings + lines₀ + lines₁ + 1`. -/
/-! ### Three-dimensional cavities -/
/-- The side lengths `(a, b, c)` of a rectangular cavity. -/
/-- The mode `(p, q, r)` of a rectangular cavity. -/
/-- **3D Chladni cavity**: the separated mode solves `Δψ + k²ψ = 0`. -/
/-- A `(p, q, r)` cavity mode has exactly `p·q·r` nodal domains. -/
/-- **Courant's theorem in the rectangular cavity.** -/
/-- A `(p, q, r)` cavity mode has `(p-1)(q-1)(r-1)` interior triple crossings of nodal planes. -/
/-- Interior triple crossings are singular nodal points (`ψ = 0`, `∇ψ = 0`). -/
/-! ### The degenerate Chladni pattern on the square -/

/-- The classical Chladni superposition on the square `[0, π]²`:
`ψ(x, y) = sin(px) sin(qy) - sin(qx) sin(py)`. -/

/-- The degenerate Chladni pattern on the square as a Chladni nodal manifold with
`k² = p² + q²`. -/
/-- The diagonal `x = y` of the square is a nodal line of the degenerate Chladni pattern. -/
/-! ### Kernel-checked integer certificates -/

/-- The exact certificate of the `(3, 2)` plate mode: 2 + 1 interior nodal lines, 12 nodal
vertices, 2 interior crossings, 6 nodal domains, eigenvalue numerator `3² + 2² = 13`. -/
/-- A corrupted certificate (wrong domain count) is rejected. -/

/-- On every rectangular plate, the nodal geometry of the `(3, 2)` mode produces exactly the
certificate `cert32`, which decodes to the mode `(3, 2)`. -/
/-- The exact certificate of the `(2, 2, 3)` cavity mode. -/

declarations.name: hasDerivAt_chladni_fst
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem hasDerivAt_chladni_fst (m n x y : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun x => chladniEigenmode m n x y)
      (-m * sin (m * x) * cos (n * y) + n * sin (n * x) * cos (m * y)) x

declarations.name: hasDerivAt_chladni_snd
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem hasDerivAt_chladni_snd (m n x y : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun y => chladniEigenmode m n x y)
      (-n * cos (m * x) * sin (n * y) + m * cos (n * x) * sin (m * y)) y

declarations.name: deriv_chladni_fst
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem deriv_chladni_fst (m n y : ℝ) :
    deriv (fun x => chladniEigenmode m n x y) =
      fun x => -m * sin (m * x) * cos (n * y) + n * sin (n * x) * cos (m * y)

declarations.name: deriv_chladni_snd
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem deriv_chladni_snd (m n x : ℝ) :
    deriv (fun y => chladniEigenmode m n x y) =
      fun y => -n * cos (m * x) * sin (n * y) + m * cos (n * x) * sin (m * y)

declarations.name: deriv2_chladni_fst
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem deriv2_chladni_fst (m n x y : ℝ) :
    deriv (deriv fun x => chladniEigenmode m n x y) x =
      -m ^ 2 * cos (m * x) * cos (n * y) + n ^ 2 * cos (n * x) * cos (m * y)

declarations.name: deriv2_chladni_snd
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem deriv2_chladni_snd (m n x y : ℝ) :
    deriv (deriv fun y => chladniEigenmode m n x y) y =
      -n ^ 2 * cos (m * x) * cos (n * y) + m ^ 2 * cos (n * x) * cos (m * y)

declarations.name: helmholtz_chladni
declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem helmholtz_chladni (m n x y : ℝ) :
    deriv (deriv fun x => chladniEigenmode m n x y) x +
      deriv (deriv fun y => chladniEigenmode m n x y) y =
      -(m ^ 2 + n ^ 2) * chladniEigenmode m n x y

comments.text:
/-!
# The Chladni mode as a Helmholtz eigenfunction with a genuine `D₄` group action

`Sovereign.Taxonomy.ChladniNodalD4` checks the eight symmetries of the square one map at a
time.  This module lifts that into Mathlib's continuous and group-theoretic language:

* `helmholtz_chladni` — the mode `u(x, y) = cos(m x) cos(n y) - cos(n x) cos(m y)` satisfies the
  Helmholtz equation `∂²ₓu + ∂²ᵧu = -(m² + n²) u` at every point of the plane.
* `d4Hom`, `instMulActionD4` — the dihedral group `DihedralGroup 4` (order 8) acts on `ℝ × ℝ`
  through a group homomorphism into the permutations of the plane, with `r 1` the quarter turn
  `(x, y) ↦ (-y, x)` (`r_one_smul`) and `sr 0` the reflection `(x, y) ↦ (x, -y)`
  (`sr_zero_smul`).
* `d4_smul_isometry` — every group element acts by an isometry of the plane.
* `d4Char : DihedralGroup 4 →* ℤˣ` — the sign character `r i ↦ (-1)^i`, `sr i ↦ (-1)^i`.
* `modeAt_d4_smul` — equivariance: `u (g • p) = d4Char g * u p` for every `g : DihedralGroup 4`.
* `nodalSet_d4_smul` — the Helmholtz zero set `{p | u p = 0}` is invariant under the whole group,
  `g • nodalSet m n = nodalSet m n`; `isClosed_nodalSet` records that it is a closed subset of the
  metric space `ℝ × ℝ`, and `isCompact_nodalSet_square` that its trace on `[-π, π]²` is compact.
-/
/-! ### The Helmholtz equation -/

/-- **Helmholtz equation.**  The Chladni mode is an eigenfunction of the planar Laplacian with
eigenvalue `-(m² + n²)`, at every point. -/
/-! ### The dihedral group of the square acting on the plane -/
/-- The rotation `r i` acts as the `i`-th power of the quarter turn. -/
/-- The quarter turn as a permutation of the plane. -/
/-- The reflection `(x, y) ↦ (x, -y)` as a permutation of the plane. -/

/-- The action of `DihedralGroup 4` by permutations: `r i ↦ ρ^i`, `sr i ↦ σ ρ^i`, where `ρ` is the
quarter turn and `σ` the reflection in the horizontal axis. -/
/-- `d4Perm` is a group homomorphism `DihedralGroup 4 →* Perm (ℝ × ℝ)`. -/
/-- Concrete formula for the action. -/
/-- The quarter turn and the reflection are the generators `r 1` and `sr 0`. -/
/-- Every element of `D₄` acts on the plane by an isometry. -/
/-! ### The sign character and equivariance of the mode -/
/-- The sign character of the mode on group elements: `r i ↦ (-1)^i`, `sr i ↦ (-1)^i`. -/
/-- The sign character `D₄ →* {±1}` by which the Chladni mode transforms. -/

/-- **`D₄`-equivariance of the Helmholtz mode**: `u (g • p) = χ(g) · u p` for every element `g`
of the dihedral group. -/
/-- The Helmholtz zero set of the mode, as a subset of the plane. -/
/-- **`D₄`-invariance of the Helmholtz zero set**, for the full group action. -/
/-- The zero set is a closed subset of the metric space `ℝ × ℝ`. -/
/-- Its trace on the square `[-π, π]²` is compact. -/
/-- The square `[-π, π]²` itself is `D₄`-invariant. -/
/-- The trace of the zero set on the square is `D₄`-invariant. -/

    modeAt m n (reflX p) = modeAt m n p ∧
    modeAt m n (reflY p) = modeAt m n p ∧
    modeAt m n (diagonalReflection p) = -modeAt m n p ∧
    modeAt m n (reflAntidiag p) = -modeAt m n p

declarations.signature_heuristic:
theorem chladni_svg_d4_checks :
    (∀ (m n : ℝ) (p : ℝ × ℝ), isNodalPoint m n p ↔ isNodalPoint m n (rot90 p)) ∧
    (∀ (m n : ℝ) (p : ℝ × ℝ), isNodalPoint m n p ↔ isNodalPoint m n (reflX p)) ∧
    (∀ (m n x : ℝ), isNodalPoint m n (x, x)) ∧
    (∀ (m n x : ℝ), isNodalPoint m n (x, -x)) ∧
    (∀ (j k : ℤ) (y : ℝ),
