/-!
# Courant's nodal domain theorem for Chladni box modes

The Dirichlet spectrum of the box `∏ᵢ [0, Lᵢ]` generated by the separated modes is
`{kₘ² = ∑ᵢ (mᵢ π / Lᵢ)² | mᵢ ≥ 1}`, listed in nondecreasing order with multiplicity.
The eigenvalue `kₘ²` first occurs at position

  `spectralIndex L m = #{m' | kₘ'² < kₘ²} + 1`,

and occupies the positions `spectralIndex L m, …, #{m' | kₘ'² ≤ kₘ²}`.

* `modesBelow_finite`: only finitely many modes lie below any level.
* `courant_nodal_domain`: **Courant's bound** — the number of nodal domains of `ψₘ` is at most
  `spectralIndex L m`, hence at most any position `N` of `kₘ²` in the ordered spectrum
  (`courant_nodal_domain_of_position`).
* `ncard_nodalDomains_eq_one_iff`: the only mode with a single nodal domain is the ground state
  `m = (1, …, 1)`.

The completeness of the separated modes in `L²` (i.e. that every Dirichlet eigenfunction of the
box is a combination of the `ψₘ`) is classical and not formalized here; the index is taken in the
spectrum generated by the separated modes.
-/
/-- Dirichlet modes (all `m'ᵢ ≥ 1`) whose eigenvalue lies strictly below `μ`. -/
/-- Dirichlet modes whose eigenvalue is at most `μ`. -/

/-- The first position of the eigenvalue `kₘ²` in the nondecreasing list of Dirichlet
eigenvalues counted with multiplicity. -/
/-- Eigenvalues strictly increase when the mode numbers increase. -/

/-- **Courant's nodal domain theorem** for the Chladni box modes: the mode `ψₘ` has at most
`spectralIndex L m` nodal domains. -/

/-- Courant's bound at every position of the eigenvalue: if `kₘ²` sits at position `N` of the
nondecreasing list of Dirichlet eigenvalues (i.e. `N` lies between the number of eigenvalues
strictly below and the number of eigenvalues at most `kₘ²`), then `ψₘ` has at most `N` nodal
domains. -/

/-- The eigenvalue `kₘ²` does occupy the positions up to `#{m' | kₘ'² ≤ kₘ²}`: the first
position `spectralIndex L m` is at most that count. -/

/-- The ground state `m = (1, …, 1)` has a single nodal domain; it is the only mode with this
property. -/

/-!
# Exact Chladni factorization on rectangular plates and boxes

On the box `B = ∏ᵢ [0, Lᵢ] ⊆ ℝᵈ` (a rectangular plate for `d = 2`, a cavity for `d = 3`) the
Dirichlet modes separate:

  `ψₘ(x) = ∏ᵢ sin(mᵢ π xᵢ / Lᵢ)`,   `Δψₘ + kₘ² ψₘ = 0`,   `kₘ² = ∑ᵢ (mᵢ π / Lᵢ)²`.

* `helmholtz_boxMode`: the Helmholtz equation, proved with the coordinate Laplacian.
* `boxManifold L m`: the resulting `ChladniNodalManifold` (compact plate, Dirichlet boundary).
* `boxMode_eq_zero_iff`: the nodal set is exactly the union of the grid hyperplanes
  `xᵢ = j Lᵢ / mᵢ` (`0 ≤ j ≤ mᵢ`).
* `ExactChladniFactorization M`: a separated product form of `ψ` whose nodal set is the union of
  the coordinate hyperplanes over explicit finite zero sets; `boxFactorization` provides it for
  every box mode.
-/
/-- The closed box `∏ᵢ [0, Lᵢ]`. -/
/-- The open box `∏ᵢ (0, Lᵢ)`. -/

/-- The Dirichlet eigenvalue `kₘ² = ∑ᵢ (mᵢ π / Lᵢ)²`. -/
/-- Separation of one variable: freezing all coordinates but `i`. -/
/-- **Helmholtz equation** for the separated box modes: `Δψₘ + kₘ² ψₘ = 0`. -/
/-- One-dimensional zero set: for `x ∈ [0, L]`, `sin(mπx/L) = 0` iff `x = jL/m`, `0 ≤ j ≤ m`. -/

/-- **Nodal set of a box mode**: inside the closed box, `ψₘ(x) = 0` iff some coordinate lies on
a grid hyperplane `xᵢ = j Lᵢ / mᵢ`. -/
/-- The box mode vanishes on the boundary of the box (clamped plate). -/

/-- The box mode `ψₘ` on the box `∏ [0, Lᵢ]` as a Chladni nodal manifold, with wave number

/-!
# Discrete topological certificates for acoustic levitation

* `TrapBarrier U c r b`: an **energy barrier** — `U(c) < b ≤ U` on the sphere `‖y - c‖ = r`.
  `TrapBarrier.exists_isLocalMin`: a barrier encloses a trap (a local minimum of `U` in the
  open ball).
* `DiscreteBarrierCertificate`: finitely many samples on the sphere, a mesh size `h`, a
  Lipschitz constant `L` and the finite check `U(s) ≥ b + L h` at the samples. Soundness:
  `DiscreteBarrierCertificate.trapBarrier`.
* `Trajectory m U`: a particle of mass `m` moving by Newton's law `m ẍ = -∇U(t, x)` in a
  time-dependent potential (continuous phase modulation). `Trajectory.hasDerivAt_energy`:
  `dE/dt = ∂ₜU`.
* **`Trajectory.confined`**: if the barrier holds at all times of `[0, T]`, `|∂ₜU| ≤ K` in the
  ball, and `E(0) + K T < b`, the particle never leaves the ball during `[0, T]`
  (no escape under continuous phase modulation). Static fields: `Trajectory.confined_static`.
* **`no_coalescence`**: particles confined to pairwise separated certificate balls never
  coalesce; `LevitationArrayCertificate.certify` packages the finite array certificate.
* `DiscreteTimeCertificate`: a finite time grid with a time-Lipschitz bound certifies the
  barrier at every time of `[0, T]`.
* `PlaneWaveArray.phaseModulated`: phase-modulated arrays have jointly smooth potentials
  (`contDiff_gorkov_phaseModulated`), so the dynamical results apply.
-/
/-! ## Energy barriers -/

/-- An energy barrier certificate: `U(c) < b` and `U ≥ b` on the sphere of radius `r`
around `c`, with `U` continuous on the closed ball. -/

/-- A barrier encloses a trap: `U` has a local minimum in the open ball, which also minimises
`U` over the closed ball. -/

/-- A **discrete barrier certificate**: a finite set of samples on the sphere forming an
`h`-net of it, a Lipschitz bound `L` for `U` on the sphere, and the finite check
`U(s) ≥ b + L h` at every sample. -/
/-- Soundness of the discrete certificate: the finite checks imply the continuous barrier. -/
/-! ## Particle dynamics in a time-dependent Gor'kov potential -/
/-- Euclidean squared speed `|v|² = ∑ vᵢ²`. -/
/-- The joint potential `(t, y) ↦ U t y`. -/
/-- The explicit time rate `∂ₜ U (t, y)` (e.g. caused by phase modulation). -/

/-- A trajectory of a particle of mass `m` in the time-dependent potential `U`:
`ẋ = v`, `m v̇ = F = -∇U(t, x)`. (Gravity can be included in `U` as `m g z`.) -/
/-- Total mechanical energy `E(t) = m |v|²/2 + U(t, x(t))`. -/
/-- **Energy balance**: `dE/dt = ∂ₜ U(t, x(t))`. -/
-- spatial gradient in terms of `D`

/-- **No escape under continuous phase modulation.** Suppose that during `[0, T]` the
potential keeps a barrier of height `b` on the sphere `‖y - c‖ = r`, that its explicit time
rate satisfies `|∂ₜU| ≤ K` in the closed ball, and that the particle starts inside the ball
with `E(0) + K T < b`. Then the particle stays in the open ball during `[0, T]`. -/
-- at time `τ` the particle is on the sphere
-- energy estimate on `[0, τ]`

/-- Static fields (fixed phases): energy is conserved, and a particle starting in the ball with
energy below the barrier stays there forever (for all `t ≥ 0`). -/
/-! ## Multi-particle arrays: non-coalescence -/

/-- **Non-coalescence**: particles confined to balls whose centres are separated by more than
the sum of the radii stay at distance at least `dist cₖ cₗ - rₖ - rₗ > 0`. -/

/-- A finite certificate for a levitation array of `N` particles: trap centres, radii and
barrier levels, pairwise separation of the certificate balls, and (for a modulation of
duration `T`) a uniform barrier and time-rate bound. -/

/-- **Array certificate soundness**: every particle starting in its certificate ball with
energy `Eₖ(0) + K T < bₖ` stays in its ball during the whole modulation `[0, T]`, and no two

independent (inter-particle forces are neglected). -/
/-! ## Discrete time grids for phase modulation -/

/-- A discrete certificate that a barrier survives a continuous modulation on `[0, T]`:

for `U` on the sphere, and the finite checks `U(tⱼ, y) ≥ b + L h` on the sphere. -/
/-- Soundness: the barrier holds at every time of `[0, T]`. -/

/-- Under a barrier that persists during the modulation, a trap persists inside the ball at
every instant (quasi-static transport of the trap). -/

smooth functions of time. -/

/-!
# The Gor'kov acoustic potential of phased transducer arrays

A time-harmonic acoustic field of angular frequency `ω` in a fluid of density `ρ₀` and sound
speed `c₀` is described by its complex pressure amplitude `p : ℝ³ → ℂ`
(physical pressure `Re (p(r) e^{-iωt})`). By the linearised Euler equation
`ρ₀ ∂ₜv = -∇p` the velocity amplitude is `v = ∇p / (i ρ₀ ω)`. Time averages are
`⟨p²⟩ = |p|²/2` and `⟨v²⟩ = |v|²/2`.

The **Gor'kov potential** of a small sphere of radius `a` is

  `U(r) = 2π a³ (⟨p²⟩ / (3 ρ₀ c₀²) - ρ₀ ⟨v²⟩ / 2)`                       (`gorkov`)

`= 2π a³ (|p|²/(6 ρ₀ c₀²) - |∇p|²/(4 ρ₀ ω²))` (`gorkov_eq`), and the radiation force is
`F = -∇U`.

* `contDiffAt_gorkov`: smooth pressure fields have `C²` Gor'kov potentials, so the
  second-derivative test of `LevitationHessian` applies: `gorkov_isStableTrap_iff`.
* `PlaneWaveArray`: multi-emitter phased arrays of plane-wave emitters (far field),
  `p(r) = ∑ⱼ Aⱼ exp(i(k dⱼ·r + φⱼ))`, smooth everywhere.
* `TransducerArray`: phased arrays of point-source transducers (near field),
  `p(r) = ∑ⱼ Aⱼ exp(i(k |r - sⱼ| + φⱼ)) / |r - sⱼ|`, smooth away from the transducers.
* `PlaneWaveArray.gorkov_transpose`: transposing the driving frequency by `c ∈ PosReal`
  (the monoid of `Sovereign.Algebra.AudioVisualFunctor`) rescales the potential,
  `U_{cω}(r) = U_ω(c r)`, and maps stable traps to stable traps (`isStableTrap_transpose`).
* Link with `AcousticVortex`: a smooth `AcousticPotential` is a pressure field; on its vortex
  core (pressure node) the Gor'kov potential is purely kinetic and `≤ 0`
  (`gorkov_nonpos_of_mem_vortexCore`), e.g. along the vortex line of `cubeVortex`.
-/

/-- The acoustic medium and driving frequency: density `ρ₀`, sound speed `c₀`, angular
frequency `ω`, all positive. -/
/-- The wave number `k = ω / c₀`. -/
/-- Transposition of the driving frequency by a factor `c > 0`: `ω ↦ c ω`. -/
/-- The complex pressure gradient `∂ᵢ p(x)`. -/
/-- Time-averaged squared pressure `⟨p²⟩ = |p|²/2`. -/
/-- Complex particle-velocity amplitude `v = ∇p / (i ρ₀ ω)` (linearised Euler equation). -/
/-- Time-averaged squared particle velocity `⟨v²⟩ = |v|²/2`. -/

/-- The **Gor'kov acoustic potential** of a small sphere of radius `a`:
`U(r) = 2π a³ (⟨p²⟩/(3 ρ₀ c₀²) - ρ₀ ⟨v²⟩/2)`. -/
/-- Explicit form `U = 2π a³ (|p|²/(6 ρ₀ c₀²) - |∇p|²/(4 ρ₀ ω²))`. -/
/-- A smooth pressure field has a `C²` Gor'kov potential. -/

/-- **Stable acoustic traps of a smooth pressure field** are exactly the local minima of the
Gor'kov potential with strictly positive Hessian determinant. -/
/-! ## Phased arrays of plane-wave emitters -/
/-- A plane-wave emitter: real amplitude, phase and propagation direction. -/
/-- A multi-emitter phased array of `n` plane-wave emitters. -/
/-- The complex pressure `p(r) = ∑ⱼ Aⱼ exp(i(k dⱼ·r + φⱼ))` of the array. -/

/-- Stable traps of a plane-wave phased array are local minima of `U` with
`det (Hess U) > 0`, and conversely. -/

/-- **Frequency transposition rescales the Gor'kov landscape**: driving the same array at
`c ω` gives `U_{cω}(r) = U_ω(c r)`. -/

/-- **Frequency transposition maps traps to traps**: `x` is a stable trap of the array driven
at `c ω` iff `c x` is a stable trap of the array driven at `ω`. The trap lattice is rescaled by
`1 / c`. -/
/-! ## Phased arrays of point-source transducers -/
/-- A point-source transducer at position `pos`, with real amplitude and phase. -/
/-- A multi-emitter phased array of `n` point-source transducers. -/
/-- Euclidean distance `|x - y|` in `ℝ³`. -/

/-- The complex pressure `p(r) = ∑ⱼ Aⱼ exp(i(k |r - sⱼ| + φⱼ)) / |r - sⱼ|` (monopole
transducers). -/
/-- The transducer field is smooth away from the transducers. -/

/-- Stable traps of a transducer phased array (away from the transducers) are exactly the
local minima of the Gor'kov potential with `det (Hess U) > 0`. -/
/-! ## Link with acoustic vortices -/
/-- An acoustic potential `ψ = u + i v` with smooth components, viewed as a pressure field. -/

/-- On the vortex core (pressure node) of an acoustic field the Gor'kov potential reduces to
its kinetic part `-2π a³ ρ₀ ⟨v²⟩/2`, and is therefore `≤ 0`. -/
/-- The cube vortex field `ψ_{(2,1,1)} + i ψ_{(1,2,1)}` is smooth. -/

/-- Along the vortex line `x = y = π/2` of the cube vortex the Gor'kov potential is `≤ 0`,
and its Gor'kov potential is `C²` everywhere. -/

theorem fderiv_taylor_one_le {f : E → ℝ} {x : E} (hf : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x) {ε : ℝ}
    (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ h in 𝓝 (0 : E), ‖fderiv ℝ f (x + h) - fderiv ℝ f x -
      fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x h‖ ≤ ε * ‖h‖

declarations.name: taylor_two_le

theorem taylor_two_le {f : E → ℝ} {x : E} (hf : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ h in 𝓝 (0 : E), |f (x + h) - f x - fderiv ℝ f x h -
      (1 / 2) * fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x h h| ≤ ε * ‖h‖ ^ 2

/-!
# Second-derivative test for trapping potentials

General calculus used for acoustic levitation traps (`Sovereign.Taxonomy.Levitation`):

* `taylor_two_le`: second-order Taylor estimate (Peano remainder) for `C²` functions;
* `gradient`, `hessian`: gradient vector and Hessian matrix of `U : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ`
  (`ι = Fin 3` for physical space);
* `IsStableTrap U x`: `U` is `C²` at `x`, `∇U(x) = 0` and `Hess U(x)` is positive definite
  (linear stability of the radiation force `F = -∇U`);
* `IsStableTrap.isStrictLocalMin`, `IsStableTrap.restoring`: a stable trap is a strict local
  minimum of `U`, and the force points back to the trap in a punctured neighbourhood;
* **`isStableTrap_iff_isLocalMin_det_pos`**: for `C²` potentials,
  stable trap `↔` local minimum of `U` with `det (Hess U) > 0`;
* `isStableTrap_comp_smul_iff`, `isStableTrap_comp_add_iff`: stable traps are invariant under
  rescalings and translations of space.

The local-minimum hypothesis cannot be dropped: `standingWave_saddle_det_pos`
(`LevitationStandingWave.lean`) exhibits a saddle of an actual Gor'kov landscape with
`det (Hess U) > 0`.
-/
/-- First-order estimate of the derivative of a `C²` function. -/
/-- Second-order Taylor estimate (Peano remainder) for a function that is `C²` at `x`. -/
/-- Transport an eventual statement about displacements `h → 0` to points `y → x`. -/
/-- The gradient `∇U(x)` of `U : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ` (vector of partial derivatives). -/
/-- The Hessian matrix `Hess U(x)ᵢⱼ = ∂ᵢ∂ⱼU(x)`. -/
/-- The acoustic radiation force `F = -∇U` on a particle in the potential `U`. -/
/-- The second derivative as a quadratic form is `hᵀ (Hess U) h`. -/
/-- The Hessian of a `C²` function is symmetric. -/

/-- A **stable acoustic trap** of the potential `U` at `x`: `U` is `C²` near `x`, the radiation
force vanishes (`∇U(x) = 0`) and the Hessian `Hess U(x)` is positive definite, i.e. the
linearised force `δF = -Hess U(x) δx` is restoring in every direction. -/
/-- `x` is a strict local minimum of `f`. -/
/-- Quantitative form: near a stable trap, `U(y) ≥ U(x) + m ‖y - x‖²` for some `m > 0`. -/
/-- A stable trap is a strict local minimum of the potential. -/
/-- The Hessian determinant at a stable trap is strictly positive. -/

/-- Near a stable trap the radiation force is **restoring**: it has a strictly negative
component along the displacement `y - x`, for every `y ≠ x` close to `x`. -/
/-- At a local minimum the gradient vanishes. -/
/-- At a local minimum of a `C²` function the Hessian is positive semidefinite. -/

/-- **Stable traps are exactly the local minima with positive Hessian determinant.**
For a potential `U` that is `C²` at `x`: `x` is a stable trap (critical point with positive
definite Hessian) iff `x` is a local minimum of `U` and `det (Hess U(x)) > 0`. -/
/-- Variant: stable trap `↔` local minimum with nondegenerate Hessian. -/
/-- Rescaling space by `c` multiplies the Hessian by `c²`. -/

/-- Stable traps are invariant under rescaling of space: `x` is a stable trap of
`y ↦ U(c y)` iff `c x` is a stable trap of `U`. -/

/-- Stable traps are invariant under translations: `x` is a stable trap of `y ↦ U(y + v)` iff
`x + v` is a stable trap of `U`. -/

/-!
# Worked example: a six-emitter standing-wave levitator

Three counter-propagating pairs of plane-wave emitters along the coordinate axes
(`sixEmitterArray`), each emitter of amplitude `P/2`, produce with pair phases `±θᵢ` the
pressure `p(x) = P ∑ᵢ cos(k xᵢ + θᵢ)` (`sixEmitter_pressure`). Its Gor'kov potential is

  `U(x) = K ((∑ cᵢ)²/6 + ∑ cᵢ²/4 - 3/4)`,  `cᵢ = cos(k xᵢ + θᵢ)`,  `K = 2π a³ P²/(ρ₀ c₀²)`

(`sixEmitter_gorkov`). We prove:

* `standingWave_hessian`: the explicit Hessian; at the trap sites `cos(k xᵢ) = 0`,
  `Hess U = K k² (s sᵀ/3 + I/2)` with `sᵢ = ±1`, and `det (Hess U) = 3 K³ k⁶ / 8 > 0`;
* **`sixEmitter_isStableTrap`**: every lattice site `xₙ = ((π/2 + nᵢ π)/k)ᵢ`, `n ∈ ℤ³`, is a
  stable levitation trap (via `isStableTrap_iff_isLocalMin_det_pos`);
* `standingWave_saddle_det_pos`: the point `(π/(2k), 0, π/k)` is a critical point with
  `det (Hess U) > 0` that is **not** a local minimum — the determinant alone does not certify a
  trap, the local-minimum condition is essential;
* **`sixEmitter_levitation_certificate`**: under continuous phase modulation with
  `|θᵢ(t)| ≤ k d`, `|θᵢ'(t)| ≤ Ω`, particles started in pairwise distinct lattice cells with
  `E(0) + (9/2) K Ω T < U_min + K sin²(k (r - d))/4` never escape their cells and never
  coalesce during `[0, T]`.
-/
/-! ## The Gor'kov landscape `U₀` and its derivatives -/
/-- The coordinate functional `y ↦ yᵢ`. -/
/-- The standing-wave Gor'kov landscape `K ((∑ cos(k yᵢ))²/6 + ∑ cos²(k yᵢ)/4 - 3/4)`. -/
/-- Its partial derivatives. -/
/-- Its Hessian entries. -/
/-- The Hessian of the standing-wave landscape. -/
/-! ## Trap sites -/
/-- A trap site: all three standing waves have a pressure node, `cos(k xᵢ) = 0`. -/
/-- The minimum value `-3K/4` of the landscape, attained exactly at the trap sites. -/
/-- Lower bound by any single node factor: `U(y) - U_min ≥ K cos²(k yᵢ)/4`. -/
/-- **`det (Hess U) = 3 K³ k⁶ / 8`** at every trap site. -/

/-- **Every trap site of the standing-wave landscape is a stable trap**, obtained from the
characterisation "local minimum with `det (Hess U) > 0`". -/
/-- The saddle point `(π/(2k), 0, π/k)` of the standing-wave landscape. -/

/-- **`det (Hess U) > 0` does not certify a trap.** At `(π/(2k), 0, π/k)` the landscape has a
critical point with `det (Hess U) = 5 K³ k⁶ / 24 > 0` (one positive and two negative
curvatures), which is not a local minimum. -/
-- move along the second axis: `U` decreases
/-! ## The six-emitter array -/
/-- Three counter-propagating pairs of plane-wave emitters along the axes, amplitude `P/2`. -/

/-- Pair phases `(θ₀, -θ₀, θ₁, -θ₁, θ₂, -θ₂)`: the phase difference `2θᵢ` inside the `i`-th
pair shifts the standing wave along axis `i`. -/

/-- The pressure of the phase-modulated six-emitter array is the real standing-wave field
`P ∑ᵢ cos(k xᵢ + θᵢ)`. -/
/-- The Gor'kov prefactor `K = 2π a³ P² / (ρ₀ c₀²)`. -/

/-- **The Gor'kov potential of the phase-modulated six-emitter array** is the standing-wave
landscape shifted by `θ / k`: `U_θ(x) = U₀(x + θ/k)`. -/
/-! ## The trap lattice -/
/-- The lattice of trap sites `xₙ = ((π/2 + nᵢ π)/k)ᵢ`, `n ∈ ℤ³`. -/

/-- **Stable levitation traps of the six-emitter array.** For any pair phases `θ`, every point
`xₙ - θ/k` of the (shifted) trap lattice is a stable trap of the Gor'kov potential: a strict
local minimum with `det (Hess U) = 3 K³ k⁶/8 > 0`. -/
/-- Distinct lattice sites are at (sup-norm) distance at least `π / k`. -/
/-! ## Barriers and continuous phase modulation -/

/-- **Explicit barrier around a trap site**, uniform under shifts `|sᵢ| ≤ d`: on the sphere of
radius `r` around a trap site, `U(y + s) ≥ U_min + K sin²(k (r - d))/4`. -/
/-- Bound on the partial derivatives of the landscape: `|∂ᵢU| ≤ 3 K k / 2`. -/

/-- The explicit time rate of the phase-modulated six-emitter potential,
`∂ₜU = ∑ᵢ ∂ᵢU₀(y + θ/k) θᵢ'/k`, is bounded by `(3K/2) ∑ᵢ |θᵢ'|`. -/

/-- **Levitation certificate for the six-emitter array under continuous phase modulation.**
Let the pair phases `θ(t)` vary differentiably with `|θᵢ(t)| ≤ k d` and `|θᵢ'(t)| ≤ Ω` during
`[0, T]`, with `0 ≤ d ≤ r` and `k (r + d) < π/2`. Consider `N` particles of mass `m` assigned to
pairwise distinct lattice sites `xₙⱼ`, each starting in the ball of radius `r` around its site
with energy `Eⱼ(0) + (9/2) K Ω T < -3K/4 + K sin²(k (r - d))/4`. Then during the whole
modulation every particle stays in its ball (no escape) and no two particles coalesce. -/

/-!
# Discrete algebraic certificates: nodal line intersections classify modes

For the Chladni box mode `ψₘ` we extract exact natural-number invariants from the real nodal
geometry and show that they determine the vibrational mode.

* `partialDeriv_boxMode`: the gradient of `ψₘ`.
* `mem_singularNodalSet_boxManifold`: a nodal point is singular (`∇ψ = 0`, a crossing of nodal
  lines/surfaces) iff at least two coordinates lie on nodal hyperplanes.
* `hyperplanePositions L m i`: the positions `t ∈ (0, Lᵢ)` whose whole hyperplane slice
  `{xᵢ = t}` lies in the nodal set — an intrinsic function of `N(ψ)`.
  `ncard_hyperplanePositions`: there are exactly `mᵢ - 1` of them.
* `crossingPoints` (interior points where one nodal hyperplane from every axis meets) and
  `vertexSet` (the same including the clamped boundary): `∏ (mᵢ - 1)` and `∏ (mᵢ + 1)` points.
* `nodalSet_injective`: **the nodal set determines the mode**; `vertexSet_injective`: already the
  set of nodal line intersections (with the boundary) determines the mode.
* `NodalSignature`: the exact integer certificate (hyperplane counts, vertex count, interior
  crossing count, nodal domain count, eigenvalue numerator); `measuredSignature` reads it off
  the real geometry and `measuredSignature_eq` proves it equals the combinatorial `signature m`
  (so it is independent of the plate size: no numerical drift). `NodalSignature.check` is a
  decidable Boolean checker with `check_iff`: a signature passes iff it is the signature of a
  (unique) mode, recovered by `decode`.
-/
/-! ### Gradient and singular nodal points -/
/-- The partial derivatives of the box mode. -/

/-- **Singular nodal points** of a box mode: inside the plate, `ψ = 0` and `∇ψ = 0` iff two
distinct coordinates lie on nodal hyperplanes (nodal lines/surfaces cross there). -/
/-! ### Intrinsic nodal hyperplanes, crossings and vertices -/

/-- Positions `t ∈ (0, Lᵢ)` such that the whole slice `{xᵢ = t}` of the open plate lies in the
nodal set: the interior nodal hyperplanes perpendicular to axis `i`. -/
/-- Interior crossing points: one nodal hyperplane from every axis passes through them. -/

/-- Nodal vertices: intersection points of nodal hyperplanes from every axis, the clamped
boundary included. -/

/-- One-dimensional interior zero set: for `t ∈ (0, L)`, `sin(mπt/L) = 0` iff `t = jL/m` with
`0 < j < m`. -/
/-- The grid point with nodal coordinates `jᵢ Lᵢ / mᵢ`. -/
/-- **The nodal set classifies the mode.** -/
/-- **Nodal line intersections classify the mode**: the set of nodal vertices determines `m`. -/
/-! ### The exact integer certificate -/
/-- The exact integer nodal signature of a vibrational mode. -/
/-- Number of interior nodal hyperplanes perpendicular to each axis. -/
/-- Number of nodal vertices (intersections, boundary included). -/
/-- Number of interior crossing points. -/
/-- Number of nodal domains. -/
/-- Eigenvalue numerator `∑ mᵢ²` (so `k² = (π/ℓ)² ∑ mᵢ²` on a cube of side `ℓ`). -/
/-- Field-by-field decidable equality (reducible by the kernel, so `decide` can run it). -/
/-- The combinatorial signature of the mode `m`. -/
/-- Decode the mode from a signature: `mᵢ = linesᵢ + 1`. -/
/-- Boolean checker: exact integer consistency of a signature. -/

/-- Soundness and completeness of the checker: a signature passes iff it is the signature of a
mode, and then that mode is unique and equal to `decode s`. -/
/-- The signature measured on the real geometry of the Chladni figure. -/

/-- **Exactness**: the measured signature is the combinatorial one; in particular it does not
depend on the dimensions `L` of the plate. -/

/-- **Certificate verification**: the measured nodal signature always passes the checker and
decodes to the vibrational mode. -/
/-- On a cube of side `ℓ`, the eigenvalue is `(π/ℓ)²` times the exact integer `∑ mᵢ²`. -/

/-!
# Chladni nodal domains partition the plate into Dirichlet cells

For the box mode `ψₘ` on `B = ∏ᵢ [0, Lᵢ]` (with all `mᵢ ≥ 1`) the nodal hyperplanes cut the
box into the `∏ᵢ mᵢ` open cells

  `Cⱼ = ∏ᵢ (jᵢ Lᵢ / mᵢ, (jᵢ + 1) Lᵢ / mᵢ)`,   `0 ≤ jᵢ < mᵢ`.

* `openBox_diff_nodalSet`: `int B \ N(ψ) = ⋃ⱼ Cⱼ`; `pairwiseDisjoint_cell`: the cells are
  disjoint; `closedBox_eq_iUnion_closure_cell`: their closures cover the compact plate.
* `sign_boxMode_pos_on_cell`: `ψ` has the constant sign `(-1)^(∑ jᵢ)` on `Cⱼ` (checkerboard).
* `isConnected_cell`, `nodalDomains_boxManifold`: the nodal domains (connected components of
  `int B \ N(ψ)`) are exactly the cells, and `ncard_nodalDomains_boxManifold`: there are
  `∏ᵢ mᵢ` of them.
* `cellManifold`: every cell is itself a Chladni nodal manifold (a Dirichlet cell): `ψ` solves
  the same Helmholtz equation in `Cⱼ` and vanishes on `∂Cⱼ` (`frontier_cell_subset_nodalSet`).
-/
/-- Valid cell indices `j` with `0 ≤ jᵢ < mᵢ`. -/
/-- The open Dirichlet cell `Cⱼ = ∏ᵢ (jᵢ Lᵢ / mᵢ, (jᵢ + 1) Lᵢ / mᵢ)`. -/
/-- Membership in a cell in scaled coordinates `tᵢ = xᵢ mᵢ / Lᵢ`. -/
/-- On the cell `Cⱼ` the mode has the constant sign `(-1)^(∑ jᵢ)` (checkerboard pattern). -/
/-- The interior of the plate minus the nodal set is the union of the cells. -/
/-- **Nodal domains are the cells.** -/
/-- **Nodal domain count**: the mode `ψₘ` has exactly `∏ᵢ mᵢ` nodal domains. -/
/-- The closures of the cells cover the compact plate. -/
/-- **Dirichlet condition on each cell**: the boundary of a cell lies in the nodal set. -/

/-- Each nodal domain `Cⱼ` is itself a Dirichlet cell: a Chladni nodal manifold carrying the
same wave `ψₘ` with the same wave number, clamped on `∂Cⱼ`. -/

/-!
# Continuous phase, phase circulation and winding numbers

A nonvanishing complex signal `f : [0,1] → ℂ \ {0}` along a path admits a *continuous
logarithm* `L` (`exp ∘ L = f`) and hence a *continuous phase* `θ = Im L`
(`f = |f| e^{iθ}`), obtained from the covering map `exp : ℂ → ℂ \ {0}`.
Both are unique up to an additive constant (`2πi k`, resp. `2π k`).

* `logChange f` is the total change `L 1 - L 0` of the logarithm, independent of the lift;
* `phaseCirculation f = θ 1 - θ 0` is the total change of the phase;
* for a loop (`f 0 = f 1`) the phase circulation is quantized:
  `phaseCirculation f = 2π · windingNumber f` with `windingNumber f ∈ ℤ`
  (`phaseCirculation_eq_two_pi_mul_windingNumber`, `phase_change_quantized`);
* the winding number is invariant under homotopies of nonvanishing loops
  (`windingNumber_slice_eq`);
* it is additive under products, negated by conjugation, multiplied by `n` under `n`-th
  powers, unchanged by nonzero constant factors, and equal to `1` for a circle around `0`.
-/
/-- The punctured complex plane `ℂ \ {0}`. -/
/-- A nonvanishing continuous complex function, viewed as a map into the punctured plane. -/
/-- If `exp ∘ g = 1` on a preconnected space and `g` is continuous, `g` is constant. -/
/-! ### Continuous logarithms -/
/-- `L` is a continuous logarithm of `f`: `L` is continuous and `exp (L t) = f t`. -/
/-- The canonical continuous logarithm of a nonvanishing path, starting at `log (f 0)`. -/
/-- Two continuous logarithms of the same nonvanishing path differ by a constant. -/
/-- The total change of a continuous logarithm does not depend on the chosen logarithm. -/
/-- The total change of the complex logarithm along the path. -/
/-! ### Continuous phase and phase circulation -/
/-- `θ` is a continuous phase of `f`: `θ` is continuous and `f t = |f t| e^{i θ t}`. -/
/-- The **phase circulation** `∮ dθ = θ(1) - θ(0)`: the total change of the continuous phase. -/
/-- Every nonvanishing path has a continuous phase. -/
/-- The phase circulation is the total change of *any* continuous phase. -/
/-! ### Loops and winding numbers -/

/-- The **winding number** (topological charge) of a nonvanishing path: the phase circulation in
units of `2π`, rounded to the nearest integer (for loops no rounding is needed). -/
/-- For a loop, the total change of the logarithm is exactly `2πi n`, `n` the winding number. -/
/-- **Quantization of the phase circulation**: around a loop, `∮ dθ = 2π n`, `n ∈ ℤ`. -/

/-- **Berry phase quantization**: for every continuous phase `θ` of a nonvanishing loop, the
total phase change is `2π n` for the integer winding number `n`, and `n` is the only such
integer. -/
/-! ### Homotopy invariance -/
/-- The loop `t ↦ F (t, s)` of a two-parameter family. -/

/-- **Homotopy invariance of the phase change**: along a continuous family of nonvanishing
paths `t ↦ F (t, s)` whose endpoints satisfy `F (0, s) = F (1, s)`, the total logarithm change
is independent of `s`. -/

/-- **Homotopy invariance of the winding number** (topological charge conservation under
non-singular deformations): all loops of a continuous family of nonvanishing loops have the
same winding number. -/
/-- The winding number only depends on the values of the path. -/

/-- Two nonvanishing loops joined by a homotopy through nonvanishing loops have the same winding
number. -/
/-! ### Algebra of winding numbers -/
/-- The winding number of a product of loops is the sum of the winding numbers. -/
/-- The complex conjugate of a path. -/
/-- Complex conjugation reverses the winding number (a vortex becomes an antivortex). -/
/-- The winding number of `f ^ n` is `n` times that of `f`. -/
/-- A constant nonvanishing loop has winding number `0`. -/
/-- The loop `t ↦ c + R e^{2πit}` tracing the circle of radius `R` about `c`. -/
/-- The circle of radius `R > 0` about `0` winds once around the origin. -/
/-- A nonvanishing loop staying in the left half-plane `Re < 0` has winding number `0`. -/

/-!
# Synesthetic resonance: coupled acoustic–optical waves and their discrete certificates

This file extends `Sovereign.Algebra.AudioVisualFunctor` (through the acoustic–visual tensor
functor of `Sovereign.Algebra.AcousticVisualTensor`), `Sovereign.Taxonomy.CubeVortex` and
`Sovereign.Taxonomy.NodalCertificate`.

## The coupled wave system

In a rectangular cavity `∏ [0, Lᵢ] ⊆ ℝᵈ` (`SynestheticMedium`) an acoustic pressure field `p`
and an optical field `E` obey (`SynestheticMedium.IsSolution`)
`∇²p - (1/cs²) ∂ₜ²p = S_sound + χ p E`, `∇²E - (1/cl²) ∂ₜ²E = S_light + χ p E`,
with the synesthetic cross-modulation `χ p E`. `waveOp c f = ∇²f - (1/c²) ∂ₜ²f` is the
d'Alembertian.

* `waveOp_standingWave`: `a cos(ωt + φ) ψₘ(x)` solves `□_c = 0` when `ω² = c² kₘ²`;
* `SensoryConfig.isSolution`: every multi-sensory configuration (acoustic mode `m`, optical mode
  `n`, nonzero amplitudes, arbitrary temporal phases) solves the coupled system with the sources
  `S_sound = S_light = -χ p E`; both fields are clamped on the walls;
* `IsSolution.decouple`: wherever `p = 0` or `E = 0` the system decouples.

## Synchronized resonance points

* `acousticNodes_eq`, `opticalNulls_eq`: the points where `p` (resp. `E`) vanishes for all
  times are exactly the Chladni nodal sets of the modes `m` (resp. `n`);
* `resonancePoints`: points of the cavity through which, along every axis, the slice consists of
  acoustic nodes aligned with optical nulls. `resonancePoints_eq`: they are exactly the nodal
  vertices of the coordinatewise gcd mode `gcd(m, n)` (a Bézout argument,
  `sin_mul_eq_zero_and_iff_gcd`); `ncard_resonancePoints`: there are `∏ (gcd(mᵢ,nᵢ) + 1)` of
  them; `resonancePoints_finite`; `crossModulation_eq_zero_of_mem_resonancePoints`: the fields
  and the cross-modulation vanish there at all times; `decouple_at_resonance`.

## Certificates and injectivity up to gauge

* `SynestheticCertificate`: acoustic and optical `NodalSignature`s, resonance hyperplane counts,
  resonance point count; `synCert m n` the combinatorial certificate, `check` a Boolean checker
  (`check_iff`, `check_iff_realized`).
* `measuredCert`: the certificate measured on the real geometry; `measuredCert_eq`: it equals
  `synCert m n` exactly; `measuredCert_certified`.
* `Gauge`: independent amplitude rescalings (incl. sign) and temporal phase shifts of both
  fields; `measuredCert_gauge`: the certificate is gauge invariant; `measuredCert_eq_iff`:
  **two configurations have the same certificate iff they are gauge equivalent**;
  `certOnGaugeClasses_injective`: the certificate map is injective on gauge classes;
  `gaugeEquiv_iff_nodes`: gauge equivalence is detected by the node/null sets of the fields.
* `sensoryInput`: the multi-modal input at a point, as an object of
  `acousticFunctor ⊗ opticalFunctor`; it is silent and dark at resonance points.
* Cube example: `vortexPair_nodes_eq_vortexCore` (the `(2,1,1)`/`(1,2,1)` node–null alignment is
  the core of the acoustic cube vortex) and `vortexPair_measuredCert`.

Dimension `d ≥ 1` (`[NeZero d]`) is assumed where needed: for `d = 0` the cavity is a point and
there are no nodes.
-/
/-! ### Wave operators and the coupled acoustic–optical system -/
/-- Second time derivative `∂ₜ² f (t, x)`. -/
/-- The d'Alembertian `□_c f = ∇² f - (1/c²) ∂ₜ² f` with propagation speed `c`. -/

/-- A synesthetic medium: a rectangular cavity `∏ [0, Lᵢ]` carrying an acoustic pressure field
(speed of sound `cs`) and an optical field (speed of light `cl`), with synesthetic
cross-modulation constant `χ`. -/

/-- `(p, E)` solves the **coupled wave system** in the cavity with sources `S_sound`, `S_light`:
`∇²p - (1/cs²) ∂ₜ²p = S_sound + χ p E` and `∇²E - (1/cl²) ∂ₜ²E = S_light + χ p E`. -/
/-- Clamped (Dirichlet) boundary condition on the cavity walls. -/

/-- **Decoupling at nulls**: wherever the pressure or the optical field vanishes, the
cross-modulation term drops out and each field obeys its own driven wave equation. -/
/-- Acoustic angular frequency of the cavity mode `m`: `ωₘ = cs · kₘ`. -/
/-- Optical angular frequency of the cavity mode `n`: `ωₙ = cl · kₙ`. -/
/-- The standing wave `a cos(ω t + φ) ψₘ(x)`. -/

/-- **Free standing waves**: `a cos(ω t + φ) ψₘ` solves `□_c = 0` whenever the dispersion
relation `ω² = c² kₘ²` holds. -/
/-! ### Multi-sensory configurations and their gauge group -/

/-- A concurrent multi-sensory excitation of the cavity: an acoustic cavity mode `m` with
amplitude `a` and temporal phase `φs`, and an optical cavity mode `n` with amplitude `b` and
temporal phase `φl`. -/
/-- The acoustic pressure field `p(t, x) = a cos(ωₘ t + φs) ψₘ(x)`. -/
/-- The optical field `E(t, x) = b cos(ωₙ t + φl) ψₙ(x)`. -/
/-- The cross-modulation term `χ p E`. -/

/-- Every multi-sensory configuration solves the coupled wave system, driven by the sources
that balance the synesthetic cross-modulation, `S_sound = S_light = -χ p E`. -/
/-- Acoustic nodes: points of the cavity where the pressure vanishes at all times. -/

/-- Optical interference nulls: points of the cavity where the optical field vanishes at all
times. -/

/-- Synchronized resonance hyperplanes perpendicular to axis `i`: positions `t ∈ (0, Lᵢ)` whose
whole slice `{xᵢ = t}` of the open cavity consists of acoustic nodes that are also optical
nulls. -/

/-- **Synchronized multi-sensory resonance points**: points of the cavity through which, along
every axis, the slice of the cavity consists of acoustic nodes aligned with optical interference
nulls (the crossings of common nodal hyperplanes, the clamped walls included). -/
/-- The coordinatewise gcd of two modes. -/
/-! ### Discrete synesthetic certificates -/

/-- The discrete algebraic certificate of a multi-sensory excitation: the nodal signatures of the
acoustic and of the optical mode, the number of synchronized resonance hyperplanes along each
axis and the number of synchronized resonance points. -/
/-- The combinatorial certificate of the mode pair `(m, n)`. -/
/-- Decode the (acoustic, optical) mode pair from a certificate. -/
/-- Boolean checker for certificates. -/
/-- The certificate measured on the real geometry of the two fields. -/

/-- Gauge transformations: independent rescaling (including sign flip) of the acoustic and
optical amplitudes and independent shifts of their temporal phases. -/
/-- The action of a gauge transformation on a multi-sensory configuration. -/
/-- Gauge equivalence of multi-sensory configurations. -/

/-- Two configurations are gauge equivalent iff they excite the same acoustic and optical
modes. -/
/-- The gauge setoid on multi-sensory configurations. -/
/-! ### Common nodes: the gcd law -/
/-- `sin (m u)` and `sin (n u)` vanish together iff `sin (gcd(m, n) u)` vanishes (Bézout). -/
/-- A standing wave vanishes at all times iff its spatial amplitude vanishes. -/
/-- The acoustic nodes are exactly the Chladni nodal set of the acoustic mode. -/
/-- The optical interference nulls are exactly the nodal set of the optical mode. -/
/-- The synchronized resonance hyperplanes are the nodal hyperplanes of the gcd mode. -/
/-- There are exactly `gcd(mᵢ, nᵢ) - 1` synchronized resonance hyperplanes along axis `i`. -/

/-- **Resonance points = vertices of the gcd mode**: the synchronized multi-sensory resonance
points are the nodal vertices of the coordinatewise-gcd mode `gcd(m, n)`. -/
/-- The resonance points are the common nodal vertices of the acoustic and optical modes. -/
/-- **Exact count** of synchronized resonance points: `∏ᵢ (gcd(mᵢ, nᵢ) + 1)`. -/
/-- The set of synchronized resonance points is finite (discrete). -/
/-- Resonance points are acoustic nodes and optical nulls. -/

/-- At a synchronized resonance point both fields, and hence the synesthetic cross-modulation
`χ p E`, vanish at all times. -/

/-- At interior resonance points the coupled system decouples: for any sources for which the
fields solve the coupled system, each field obeys its own driven wave equation there. -/

/-- **The resonance points generate an unambiguous certificate**: the certificate measured on
the real geometry is exactly the combinatorial certificate of the mode pair. -/
/-- The measured certificate passes the checker and decodes to the mode pair. -/
/-- The measured certificate is gauge invariant. -/

/-- **Injectivity up to gauge**: two multi-sensory configurations have the same certificate iff
they are gauge equivalent. -/
/-- The certificate map on gauge classes of configurations. -/
/-- The certificate map is injective on gauge equivalence classes. -/

/-- Soundness and completeness of the checker: a certificate passes iff it is the measured
certificate of some multi-sensory configuration. -/

/-- Gauge equivalence is detected by the fields alone: two configurations are gauge equivalent
iff they have the same acoustic nodes and the same optical interference nulls. -/
/-! ### Multi-sensory inputs as objects of the acoustic–visual tensor functor -/
/-- The sound heard at the point `x`: a one-partial waveform of frequency `ωₘ / 2π`. -/
/-- The light seen at the point `x`: a one-partial signal of frequency `ωₙ / 2π`. -/

/-- The concurrent multi-modal input at `x`, as an object of the acoustic–visual tensor functor
`acousticFunctor ⊗ opticalFunctor`: the sound heard at `x` together with the colour spectrum
(relative to the reference frequency `ν₀`) of the light seen at `x`. -/

/-- At a synchronized resonance point the multi-modal input is silent and dark: both the sound
and the colour intensity vanish. -/
/-! ### The cube vortex as a synesthetic interference pattern -/
/-- The cube `[0, π]³` as a synesthetic medium. -/

/-- Sound in the mode `(2,1,1)` and light in the mode `(1,2,1)` of the cube: the two components
of the acoustic cube vortex `ψ_{(2,1,1)} + i ψ_{(1,2,1)}`. -/

/-- The points of the cube where the `(2,1,1)` acoustic nodes align with the `(1,2,1)` optical
interference nulls are exactly the points of the core of the acoustic cube vortex. -/

/-- The certificate of the vortex pair: signatures of `(2,1,1)` and `(1,2,1)`, no interior
synchronized resonance hyperplanes and exactly `8` resonance points (the corners of the cube). -/

/-!
# Total topological charge of a vortex configuration in a cross-section

In a planar cross-section (identified with `ℂ`) transverse to a bundle of vortex lines, a
field carrying vortices of charges `nᵢ` at positions `aᵢ` is modelled as
`ψ(z) = h(z) · ∏ᵢ Vᵢ(z)`, where `Vᵢ(z) = (z - aᵢ)^{nᵢ}` for `nᵢ ≥ 0` and
`Vᵢ(z) = conj(z - aᵢ)^{|nᵢ|}` for `nᵢ < 0` (an antivortex), and `h` is a smooth background
that does not vanish on the region considered.

* `windingNumber_vortexField`: the charge measured on the circle `|z - c| = R` equals
  `∑_{|aᵢ - c| < R} nᵢ`, the total charge of the enclosed vortices;
* `enclosedCharge_conserved`: along any continuous deformation of the field that does not
  vanish on the circle (vortices may move, be created or annihilated in pairs, merge or split
  inside the disk), the total enclosed charge `∑ nᵢ` is conserved.
-/
/-- The loop `t ↦ φ (γ t)`. -/

/-- An elementary vortex of charge `n` at `a`: `(z - a)^n` if `n ≥ 0`, `conj(z - a)^{-n}`
otherwise. -/
/-- The product of the elementary vortices of a configuration `[(a₁, n₁), …]`. -/
/-- The field `h · ∏ Vᵢ` of a vortex configuration on a background `h`. -/
/-- The total charge of the vortices of `cfg` lying strictly inside the circle `|z - c| = R`. -/
/-! ### Winding numbers along a circle -/
/-- The winding number of a product field along a loop is the sum of the winding numbers. -/
/-- The circle `|z - c| = R` winds once around each point inside it. -/
/-- The circle `|z - c| = R` does not wind around points outside it. -/
/-- The winding number of an elementary vortex of charge `n` along the circle. -/
/-- The winding number of the configuration product along the circle is the enclosed charge. -/
/-- A background field that does not vanish on the closed disk contributes no charge. -/
/-! ### Total charge of a configuration -/

/-- **Total charge of a vortex configuration.** On a circle `|z - c| = R` not passing through
any vortex, for a background `h` nonvanishing on the closed disk, the topological charge of
`ψ = h · ∏ Vᵢ` measured on the circle is `∑_{|aᵢ - c| < R} nᵢ`. -/

/-- **Conservation of the total enclosed charge `∑ nᵢ`.** Let `Φ` be a continuous deformation
of the cross-sectional field (`Φ (s, ·)` at parameter `s`) that never vanishes on the circle
`|z - c| = R`. If the field starts as the configuration `cfg₀` on the background `h₀` and ends
as `cfg₁` on the background `h₁`, then the total charges enclosed by the circle agree —
whatever happens inside (vortex motion, pair creation or annihilation, merging). -/

/-!
# Bridge: what the discovery vocabulary means

The automated discovery loop states its claims with the import-free definitions of
`Discovery.Kernel`, so that staging a claim is fast.  This file proves, once and for all, that
those definitions mean what they are named after:

* `Discovery.cdSign_eq` — `Discovery.cdSign` is the sign cochain
  `SovereignEngine.CayleyDickson.cdSign` of the Cayley–Dickson development, hence
  (`Discovery.cdMul_basis`) for every commutative ring `R` the Cayley–Dickson product of basis
  vectors of `CD R n` is `e_i ⋆ e_j = (cdSign n i j) • e_{i ⊕ j}`.  Every staged sign law is
  therefore a statement about the actual Cayley–Dickson multiplication.
* `Discovery.isPrimeB_iff` — `isPrimeB n = true ↔ Nat.Prime n`.
-/

/-- Products of canonical basis vectors in the Cayley–Dickson algebra `CD R n`, expressed with
the discovery kernel's sign: `e_i ⋆ e_j = cdSign n i j • e_{i ⊕ j}`. -/
/-- The trial-division test of the discovery kernel decides primality. -/

/-!
# Reading burned claims as mathematics

The discovery loop burns closed, bounded statements about the vocabulary of
`Discovery.Kernel`.  Combined with the bridge theorems of `Discovery.Bridge`, each of them is a
statement about standard objects.  This file carries out that translation for a few claims
burned by the runs `Run20261020_Genesis` and `Run20261020_Second`:

* `Discovery.fermat_two_squares_below_800` — every prime `p < 800` with `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)` is a sum
  of two squares (burned claim `quadform_holds_e9bb76e09c`, with `isPrimeB_iff`);
* `Discovery.cd32_basis_sq` — in the 32-dimensional Cayley–Dickson algebra over any commutative
  ring, every imaginary basis vector squares to `-1` (burned claim `cdsign_holds_347b44802c`);
* `Discovery.cd32_left_alternative_basis`, `Discovery.cd32_right_alternative_basis` —
  `e_i (e_i e_j) = -e_j` and `(e_j e_i) e_i = -e_j` for every imaginary basis vector `e_i` and
  every basis vector `e_j` of the 32-dimensional Cayley–Dickson algebra (burned claims
  `cdsign_holds_1a1920a752` and `cdsign_holds_31645a8c2a`).
-/
/-- Every prime `p < 800` with `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)` is a sum of two squares. -/

/-- In the 32-dimensional Cayley–Dickson algebra over a commutative ring, every imaginary
basis vector squares to `-1`. -/

/-- Left alternativity on the basis of the 32-dimensional Cayley–Dickson algebra:
`e_i (e_i e_j) = -e_j` for `i ≠ 0`. -/

/-- Right alternativity on the basis of the 32-dimensional Cayley–Dickson algebra:
`(e_j e_i) e_i = -e_j` for `i ≠ 0`. -/

declarations.name: cdSign
declarations.signature_heuristic:
def cdSign : Nat → Nat → Nat → Int
  | 0, _, _ => 1
  | n + 1, i, j =>
      if i < 2 ^ n then
        (if j < 2 ^ n then cdSign n i j else cdSign n (j - 2 ^ n) i)
      else
        (if j < 2 ^ n then (if j = 0 then cdSign n (i - 2 ^ n) j else -cdSign n (i - 2 ^ n) j)
         else -(if j - 2 ^ n = 0 then cdSign n (j - 2 ^ n) (i - 2 ^ n)
                else -cdSign n (j - 2 ^ n) (i - 2 ^ n)))

/-- `noDivisorFrom n d k`: no divisor `d' ∈ [d, d + k)` with `2 ≤ d'` divides `n`
(structural recursion on the fuel `k`, so the kernel evaluates it directly). -/

declarations.name: noDivisorFrom
declarations.signature_heuristic:
def noDivisorFrom (n : Nat) : Nat → Nat → Bool
  | _, 0 => true
  | d, k + 1 => (n % d != 0) && noDivisorFrom n (d + 1) k

/-- Trial-division primality test: `n ≥ 2` and no `d ∈ [2, n)` divides `n`. -/

declarations.name: isPrimeB
declarations.signature_heuristic: def isPrimeB (n : Nat) : Bool

/-!
# Discovery kernel: the decidable vocabulary of the automated discovery loop

Every claim that the automated discovery loop (`discovery/engine/`) stages for the Lean kernel
is a closed, bounded statement written only in terms of the definitions of this file and of Lean
core.  The file deliberately imports nothing, so a staged claim elaborates in about a second.

* `cdSign n i j` — the sign `σ(i, j) ∈ {±1}` of the product of canonical basis vectors of the
  Cayley–Dickson algebra of dimension `2ⁿ`: `e_i e_j = σ(i, j) e_{i ⊕ j}` (`⊕` = bitwise xor).
  The definition is a verbatim copy of `SovereignEngine.CayleyDickson.cdSign`
  (`sovereign/RequestProject/SedenionCocycle.lean`); `Discovery/Bridge.lean` proves the two equal
  and therefore ties every staged sign law to the actual Cayley–Dickson product.
* `isPrimeB n` — trial-division primality test; `Discovery/Bridge.lean` proves
  `isPrimeB n = true ↔ Nat.Prime n`.
-/

/-- Sign of `e_i e_j` in the Cayley–Dickson algebra of dimension `2ⁿ`:
`e_i e_j = cdSign n i j • e_{i ^^^ j}` (copy of `SovereignEngine.CayleyDickson.cdSign`). -/

/-- `noDivisorFrom n d k`: no divisor `d' ∈ [d, d + k)` with `2 ≤ d'` divides `n`
(structural recursion on the fuel `k`, so the kernel evaluates it directly). -/
/-- Trial-division primality test: `n ≥ 2` and no `d ∈ [2, n)` divides `n`. -/

/-!
# Local real-analytic angle lift of a unit-modulus analytic map

If `H` is analytic and nonvanishing with `‖H‖ ≡ 1` on an open set, then near any
point it can be written as `H x = exp(2πi · y x)` for a real differentiable
angle `y`, whose derivative is bounded below in absolute value wherever
`deriv H ≠ 0`.  This is the lifting input to the analytic parameter-rigidity
argument.
-/

/-
For a unit-modulus analytic map, the logarithmic derivative is purely
imaginary.
-/
-- Let $f(x) = H(x) \overline{H(x)}$. Since $H(x)$ has unit modulus on $U$, we have $f(x) = 1$ for all $x \in U$.
-- By definition of $f$, we know that its derivative is zero everywhere in $U$.
-- By definition of $f$, we know that its derivative is given by the product rule.

/-
**Local real-analytic angle lift.**  Near any point `s₀` where
`deriv H ≠ 0`, a unit-modulus analytic `H` factors as `exp(2πi · y)` for a real
function `y` with derivative bounded below in absolute value by a positive
constant.
-/
-- By definition of $y'$, we know that $|(deriv H x / H x).im| = ‖deriv H x‖$.

/-!
# Stage 4 — Joint analytic periodic logarithm on a zero-free cylinder

This file formalizes the analytic form of Lemma 7.1 (the "joint analytic
periodic logarithm") of the dossier.

We model the cylinder `U × Circle` as `ℝ × ℝ` with the second coordinate
carrying the circle structure encoded by `1`-periodicity, exactly as in the
rest of this project (where the period is taken to be `1`).  A map
`A : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ` is thought of as `A s x` with `s` the parameter and `x` the
circle variable.

Following the manuscript, instead of phrasing the hypothesis through Mathlib's
winding-number API we use its *analytic form of zero winding*:

```
    ∫₀¹ (∂ₓ A(s,x) / A(s,x)) dx = 0     for every s,
```

which is exactly what the HRT proof needs.  Under this hypothesis (plus
differentiability, continuity of the derivative, nonvanishing, and
`1`-periodicity in `x`), we construct a periodic logarithm

```
    ell(s,x) = Complex.log (A s 0) + ∫₀ˣ (∂ᵧ A(s,y) / A(s,y)) dy
```

and prove

* `Complex.exp (ell s x) = A s x`  (the logarithm property);
* `Function.Periodic (ell s) 1`     (periodicity in the circle variable);
* `HasDerivAt (ell s) (A' s x / A s x) x`  (the regularity needed downstream).

Finally we record the analytic regularity of the holonomy map
`H(s) = exp (∫₀¹ ell s x dx)` (deliverable 3), feeding the interface used by
`analytic_map_into_resonance_group_constant`.
-/
/-- The logarithmic-derivative integrand `y ↦ A'(s,y) / A(s,y)`. -/

/-- The explicit periodic logarithm
`ell(s,x) = log (A s 0) + ∫₀ˣ A'(s,y)/A(s,y) dy`. -/
/-- Continuity of `A s`, from differentiability. -/
/-- The integrand `y ↦ A'(s,y)/A(s,y)` is continuous. -/

/-- The derivative function `A' s` is `1`-periodic, derived from periodicity of
`A s` and uniqueness of derivatives. -/
/-- The integrand is `1`-periodic. -/
/-- `HasDerivAt` for the explicit periodic logarithm. -/

/-- **Stage 4 (joint analytic periodic logarithm; analytic zero-winding form).**

Let `A : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ` be differentiable in the circle variable with continuous
derivative `A'`, nonvanishing, and `1`-periodic in the circle variable.  Assume
the analytic zero-winding condition

```
    ∫₀¹ A'(s,x)/A(s,x) dx = 0   for every s.
```

Then there is `ell : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ` with `exp (ell s x) = A s x`, `ell s`
`1`-periodic, and `HasDerivAt (ell s) (A'(s,x)/A(s,x)) x`. -/
-- exp (ell s x) = A s x
-- periodicity
-- regularity
/-- The holonomy map `H(s) = exp (∫₀¹ ell s x dx)` is nonvanishing. -/

/-- **Deliverable 3 — analytic regularity of the holonomy map.**

If the parameter integral `s ↦ ∫₀¹ ell s x dx` is real analytic on `U`, then the
holonomy map `H(s) = exp (∫₀¹ ell s x dx)` is real analytic and nonvanishing on
`U`, which is exactly the interface required by
`analytic_map_into_resonance_group_constant`. -/

/-!
# Null preimages under expanding maps

Real-analysis infrastructure used in the analytic parameter-rigidity step.

* `lipschitzOnWith_image_volume_zero` — a Lipschitz map sends null sets to null
  sets (on `ℝ`).
* `expanding_preimage_null` — if `f` has derivative bounded below in absolute
  value by `c > 0` on an open interval, then the preimage of a null set
  intersected with that interval is null.
-/

/-
A function that is Lipschitz on a set sends a null subset to a null set
(in `ℝ`, where Hausdorff `1`-measure is Lebesgue measure).
-/
-- Apply `LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le` with `d = 1` (1 ≥ 0) to get `μH[1] (g '' t) ≤ K^1 * μH[1] t`.

/-
**Expanding preimage is null.**  If `f` has, on the open interval
`Set.Ioo a b`, a derivative bounded below in absolute value by a constant
`c > 0`, then the preimage of any null set `N` meets `Set.Ioo a b` in a null
set.
-/
-- Step 1 (lower Lipschitz bound). For any `x y ∈ I` we have `c * |x - y| ≤ |f x - f y|`.
-- Step 2 (Lipschitz inverse). Let `g := Set.invFunOn f I`, the left inverse of `f` on `I`.
-- Define the inverse function $g$ on the image of $f$.
-- By `lipschitzOnWith_image_volume_zero` (already proved above) applied to `g` (Lipschitz on `f '' I`, with `f '' A ⊆ f '' I`), `volume (g '' (f '' A)) = 0`.

/-!
# Analytic parameter rigidity (Section 7)

This file concerns the analytic rigidity step of the dossier.

We fully prove the self-contained analytic core (`analytic_modulus_one_of_pos_measure`):
a real-analytic `ℂ`-valued function on a connected open subset of `ℝ` whose
modulus equals `1` on a set of positive measure has modulus `1` everywhere on
the domain.  This is the first half of Lemma 7.2 and uses the identity theorem
for analytic functions.

The full Lemma 7.2 (`analytic_map_into_resonance_group_constant`) additionally
needs the change-of-variables/Lusin-`N` argument that the preimage of the
Haar-null resonance group under a nonconstant analytic map is null; that part
is recorded as a `sorry`.
-/

/-- The (multiplicative) resonance group `G_θ = {ζ ∈ S¹ : ζ^{qₙ} → 1}` as a
subset of `ℂ`. -/

/-
**Analytic modulus rigidity (first half of Lemma 7.2).** If `H` is
real-analytic on a connected open set `U ⊆ ℝ` and `‖H‖ = 1` on a
positive-measure subset of `U`, then `‖H‖ = 1` on all of `U`.
-/
-- Since `E` has positive measure, it contains an accumulation point within itself.
-- If `E` has no accumulation points, then `E` is discrete.
-- Since `E` is discrete, it is countable.
-- Since the norm squared of H is 1 on E, 'φ' must be identically zero on U by the previous lemma.

/-
The zero set of the derivative of a non-constant analytic map on a
preconnected open set is null.
-/
-- By the identity theorem for analytic functions, if `deriv H` is zero on a set with an accumulation point in `U`, then `deriv H` is identically zero on `U`.
-- If `deriv H` is zero on a set with an accumulation point in `U`, then `deriv H` is identically zero on `U`.
-- If `deriv H` is zero on a set with no accumulation point in `U`, then `Z` is discrete.

/-
Local nullity of the resonance preimage: near a point where `deriv H ≠ 0`,
the set of parameters whose `H`-value lands in the resonance group is null.
-/
-- Apply `analytic_circle_local_lift` to obtain `a`, `b`, `y`, `y'`, and `c`.

/-
**Lemma 7.2 (analytic map into the resonance group is constant).** A
real-analytic, nowhere-zero `H : U → ℂ` on a connected open interval whose
values lie in the Haar-null resonance group on a positive-measure set is
constant.
-/

-- Unit modulus: let `E := {s | s ∈ U ∧ H s ∈ resonanceGroupC q}`. By `analytic_modulus_one_of_pos_measure U hUc H hH E (fun s hs => hs.1) hpos (fun s hs => hs.2.1)` we get `hHnorm : ∀ s ∈ U, ‖H s‖ = 1` (the `‖·‖ = 1` comes from membership in `resonanceGroupC`).

-- For each `s : ℝ` with `s ∈ E₀` we have `s ∈ U` and `deriv H s ≠ 0`, so `local_resonance_preimage_null q hq U hU H hH hHnorm s ⟨..⟩ ⟨..⟩` gives an open interval `Set.Ioo (a s) (b s)` with `s ∈ Set.Ioo (a s) (b s)`, `Set.Ioo (a s) (b s) ⊆ U`, and `volume {x | x ∈ Set.Ioo (a s) (b s) ∧ H x ∈ resonanceGroupC q} = 0`.

/-!
# Stage 6B (a.e. refactor) — the a.e.-level normalized return cocycle

This module introduces the **almost-everywhere** analogue of
`NormalizedReturnData`.  Whereas `NormalizedReturnData` carries the one-step Zak
fibre equation `F(x-a, s+p/m) = … · F(x,s)` for *every* `(x,s)`, the structure
`AENormalizedReturnData` only asks the one-step equation to hold for **almost
every** `s` and, for each such `s`, **almost every** `x`.  This is the honest
output of applying an `L²` isometry to a four-term HRT relation: the relation
between `L²` classes descends only to an a.e. equality of representatives.

The previous run had to upgrade the a.e. one-step equation to a pointwise one
(`StandardPointwiseFiberUpgradeTheorem`), which is *too strong* for arbitrary
`L²` quotient data.  Here we avoid that upgrade entirely by iterating the
one-step equation **a.e.**:

* `ae_shift_real` — translation invariance of the a.e. filter on `ℝ`.
* `AENormalizedReturnData.ae_partial_step` — the a.e. `k`-fold iterate.
* `AENormalizedReturnData.ae_normalized_m_step_return_cocycle` — the a.e. `m`-step
  return cocycle `F(x-θ,s) = B_s(x) F(x,s)`.

The active-fibre positivity (`h_active_pos`) and the genuine a.e. one-step
equation forbid the degenerate `F = 0` witness, so this structure is honest.
No `sorry`, no `axiom`, no `unsafe`, no `@[implemented_by]`.
-/

/-
**Translation invariance of the a.e. filter on `ℝ`.**

If a predicate holds for almost every real number, it holds for almost every
real number after a fixed translation.
-/

/-- **Task B (a.e.) — a.e.-level normalized return data.**

The almost-everywhere analogue of `NormalizedReturnData`: the algebraic data of
the normalized critical mixed form together with a fibre function `F` whose
one-step Zak fibre equation holds **almost everywhere** (`hone_ae`) and whose
active fibre set carries positive measure (`h_active_pos`), forbidding the
degenerate `F = 0` witness. -/
/-- `(r₁,t₁),(r₂,t₂)` form a unimodular ℤ²-basis. -/
/-- Periodicity in the second Zak variable (holds pointwise). -/
/-- The one-step Zak fibre equation, holding **a.e. in `s`, then a.e. in `x`**. -/
/-- The active fibre set carries positive measure (forbids `F = 0`). -/

/-- The `j`-th factor of the iterated return cocycle (same closed form as in the
pointwise `NormalizedReturnData`). -/

/-- The scalar `m`-step return multiplier `B_s(x)`, as the product of the `m`
return factors. -/

/-- **The degenerate dummy pointwise return data.**

A `NormalizedReturnData` carrying the *same algebraic data* as `D` (so the same
`θ`, the same irrationality witness `hθ_irr`, …) but with the trivial fibre
function `F = 0`.  The pointwise one-step equation holds for `F = 0` because both
sides vanish.  This is used **only** to plumb `D.θ`/`D.hθ_irr` into the Stage 5
no-flat-band bridge, whose statement does not depend on the fibre function at all;
the genuine fibre content of `D` lives in `hone_ae`/`h_active_pos` and in the a.e.
iteration lemmas below. -/
/-- The dummy normalized data has the same `θ` as `D` (definitionally). -/

/-- The dummy normalized data's return multiplier agrees with `D.Bmult`
(both depend only on the shared algebraic data, not on the fibre function). -/

/-
**Task C (a.e.) — a.e. iterate of the one-step equation.**

After `k` a.e. applications of the one-step Zak fibre equation, for almost every
`s` and (for each such `s`) almost every `x`,
`F(x - k a, s + k p/m) = (∏_{j<k} retFactor x s j) · F(x,s)`.
-/

/-
**Task C (a.e.) — the a.e. `m`-step return cocycle.**

Iterating the one-step Zak fibre equation `m` times a.e. and using the
(pointwise) second-variable periodicity gives the scalar return cocycle
`F(x - θ, s) = B_s(x) · F(x,s)` for almost every `s` and almost every `x`.
-/

This module extracts, from a positive-measure active parameter set `S` and a

# Active-fibre holonomy data production run

This module performs the **active-fibre holonomy data production run** for the
conditional final assembly theorem.  After the canonical amplitude / holonomy
compatibility run, the entire conditional contradiction is reduced (modulo the
three already-packaged interfaces `DK_VARIATION_INTERFACE`, `ROOT_DATA_INTERFACE`,
`ZAK_MODEL_INTERFACE`) to a single active-fibre holonomy identity.  This run

* discharges the **periodic-log construction** (`active_fibre_periodic_log_exists`)
  from the root data alone — it is *not* a blocker;
* isolates the residual as the exact theorem types
  `StandardActiveFibreHolonomyEqualsGaugeMultiplier` (algebraic form) and
  `StandardActiveFibreWindingZeroOnArc` (winding / loop-holonomy form), proved
  inter-derivable given the root data;
* assembles the downstream closure: from any of these forms, together with the
  three packaged interfaces, `False` follows
  (`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_with_active_fibre_holonomy_closed`,
  `critical_mixed_final_contradiction_without_holonomy_amplitude_interface`).

The audit `ACTIVE_FIBRE_HOLONOMY_DATA_STATUS.md` records the exact Lean type of
the genuinely-missing content and the actual-cocycle provenance
(`AENormalizedReturnData.ae_normalized_m_step_return_cocycle`).

No axioms, `sorry`s, or `admit`s are introduced.
-/
/-! ## Task D — the periodic-log construction (discharged from root data) -/

/-- **Existence of a continuous 1-periodic logarithm of the return loop on each
active fibre (CLOSED_IN_LEAN).**

For every fibre `t` in the active window with nonzero leading coefficient, the
bivariate Laurent return loop `evalBiLaurentPoly coeffs Mlau t` admits a
continuous, `1`-periodic logarithm.  This is synthesised from the root data alone:
the canonical root factorisation `return_multiplier_local_root_factorization`
followed by `evalBiLaurentPoly_periodic_log_of_roots`.  Hence the periodic-log
construction is **not** a residual blocker. -/
/-! ## Tasks C/D/F — the exact residual blocker types -/

/-- **`STANDARD_ACTIVE_FIBRE_HOLONOMY_EQUALS_GAUGE_MULTIPLIER` (algebraic form).**

The smallest exact form of the residual active-fibre holonomy identity: on the
active arc, the analytic gauge value equals the choice-free algebraic loop
holonomy.  An alias of the inter-derivable
`StandardGaugeMultiplierEqualsAlgHolonomy` isolated by the previous run. -/

/-- **`STANDARD_ACTIVE_FIBRE_WINDING_ZERO_ON_ARC` (winding / loop-holonomy form).**

The winding-form of the residual: on the active arc, the analytic gauge value
equals the loop holonomy `exp(∫₀¹ ell_t)` of **any** continuous `1`-periodic
logarithm of the return loop.  (The independence of the right-hand side from the
choice of `ell_t` is the already-proved
`return_multiplier_holonomy_eq_integral_log`; this datum is the statement that the
return cocycle carries *zero net winding* on the active arc.) -/

/-- **`STANDARD_ACTIVE_FIBRE_HOLONOMY_DATA` (full holonomy package).**

The complete active-fibre holonomy interface — the gauge function `J`, its
relation to the analytic amplitude `H`, and the choice-free holonomy
identification.  An alias of `CriticalMixedWindingInterface`. -/
/-! ## Task C — inter-derivability of the algebraic and winding forms -/

/-- **The algebraic holonomy identity yields winding-zero on the active arc.**

Given the algebraic form (gauge value = `algReturnHolonomy`) and the root data,
the winding form (gauge value = loop holonomy of any periodic log) holds on the
active arc, because the loop holonomy equals `algReturnHolonomy`
(`return_multiplier_holonomy_eq_integral_log`).  This is Task C
(`active_fibre_winding_zero` / `active_arc_zero_winding`). -/
/-- Re-export under the `active_fibre_winding_zero` name. -/
/-- Re-export under the `active_arc_zero_winding` name. -/

/-- **Winding-zero on the active arc yields the algebraic holonomy identity.**

The converse direction: given the winding form together with the root data, the
algebraic form follows.  A periodic log exists on each active fibre
(`active_fibre_periodic_log_exists`), and its loop holonomy equals
`algReturnHolonomy` (`return_multiplier_holonomy_eq_integral_log`). -/
/-! ## Task D — the holonomy amplitude / gauge identification -/

/-- **The active-fibre holonomy function equals the gauge of the amplitude.**

For the full active-fibre holonomy data, the holonomy function `J` agrees with
the gauge `gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ` of the analytic amplitude on the active
window.  (This is the `hJgauge` content in `gaugeReturnMultiplier` form.) -/

/-- **The winding form constructs the full active-fibre holonomy data.**

From the winding-zero datum we build the full holonomy package
`StandardActiveFibreHolonomyData` (`CriticalMixedWindingInterface`), with the
gauge supplied internally as `gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ`. -/

/-- Re-export: `active_fibre_holonomy_amplitude` builds the holonomy package from
the winding-zero datum. -/
/-! ## Task E — downstream closure -/

/-- **Conditional final contradiction with the active-fibre holonomy data closed.**

From a normalized critical mixed four-term relation and the three packaged
interfaces (`DK_VARIATION_INTERFACE`, `ROOT_DATA_INTERFACE`, `ZAK_MODEL_INTERFACE`)
together with the active-fibre holonomy data (in winding-zero form), the project
derives `False`. -/

/-- **Conditional final contradiction with the active-fibre holonomy data closed
(algebraic form).**

The same closure starting from the smallest exact blocker
`StandardActiveFibreHolonomyEqualsGaugeMultiplier` (gauge value = algebraic loop
holonomy on the active arc). -/

/-- **Conditional final contradiction without an explicit holonomy-amplitude
interface.**

The full active-fibre holonomy package (`CriticalMixedWindingInterface`) plus the
three packaged interfaces yields `False`, with the canonical-amplitude
compatibility derived internally rather than assumed.  This certifies that the
residual analytic↔algebraic bridge *is* the content of the active-fibre
return-cocycle holonomy interface (re-export of
`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_with_winding_canonical_amplitude_closed`). -/

/-- **`STANDARD_WINDING_ZERO_HOLONOMY_BRIDGE`.**

The per-fibre identification: at any active fibre with **zero winding number**,
the analytic gauge value equals the loop holonomy `exp(∫₀¹ ell_t)` of any
continuous `1`-periodic logarithm of the bivariate Laurent return loop.  This is
exactly the analytic↔algebraic content of `StandardActiveFibreWindingZeroOnArc`
reduced to the *zero-winding* fibres.  Isolated here as the smallest exact theorem
type. -/

declarations.name: StandardWindingZeroHolonomyBridge
declarations.signature_heuristic:
structure StandardWindingZeroHolonomyBridge (θ a₀ b₀ : ℝ) {dlau : ℕ} (Mlau : ℤ)
    (ad : LaurentPolynomial ℂ) (coeffs : Fin (dlau + 1) → LaurentPolynomial ℂ)
    (H : ℝ → ℂ) (W : ℝ → ℤ) : Prop where
  hBridge : ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioo a₀ b₀, evalLaurentCircle ad t ≠ 0 → W t = 0 →
    ∀ ell_t : ℝ → ℂ, IsPeriodicLog ell_t (evalBiLaurentPoly coeffs Mlau t) →
      gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ t = Complex.exp (∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..1, ell_t x)

/-! ## Tasks B/D — extraction and propagation (proved) -/

/-- **`STANDARD_POSITIVE_MEASURE_ACTIVE_SET_MEETS_CONSTANT_COMPONENT`
(Task B, proved).**

From the a.e. zero winding number on a positive-measure active subset, there is
an actual active fibre `s₀ ∈ Set.Ioo a₀ b₀` with winding number `0`.  This is the
measure-theoretic extraction `exists_winding_zero_of_ae_on_positive_measure`
specialised to the active data. -/

/-!
# Active-fibre winding-zero on the connected active arc

This module performs the **active-fibre winding-zero on arc run**.  The residual
of the active-fibre holonomy data production run was isolated as the single
inter-derivable pair of theorem types

```
StandardActiveFibreHolonomyEqualsGaugeMultiplier   (algebraic form)
StandardActiveFibreWindingZeroOnArc                (winding / loop-holonomy form)
```

The *intended* mathematical argument for closing the winding form is:

1. for almost every active fibre the actual return equation holds
   (`AENormalizedReturnData.ae_normalized_m_step_return_cocycle`);
2. the active fibre is nonzero in `L²`;
3. the measurable winding obstruction gives **zero winding** of the loop
   `x ↦ Bmult(x,s)` for almost every active parameter `s`
   (`measurable_cocycle_winding_eq_zero`);
4. the return multiplier is a jointly analytic, **zero-free** family of loops on
   the active arc, so its integer winding number is **locally constant** in `s`;
5. the active set has positive measure inside the connected arc `(a₀,b₀)`, so the
   winding number — a locally constant `ℤ`-valued function on a connected set —
   is constant, and being `0` on a positive-measure subset it is `0` everywhere.

This run **discharges, fully in Lean, the topological propagation steps (4→5)**:

* `locallyConstant_eq_of_mem_Ioo` — a function that is locally constant *within*
  the connected arc `Set.Ioo a₀ b₀` takes a single value on it (genuine
  Mathlib-backed proof via `IsLocallyConstant.apply_eq_of_isPreconnected` on the
  connected subtype `↥(Set.Ioo a₀ b₀)`);
* `exists_winding_zero_of_ae_on_positive_measure` — a function vanishing a.e. on a
  positive-measure set vanishes at *some* point of that set (measure-theoretic);
* `winding_zero_on_active_arc_of_ae_active_winding_zero` — combining the two:
  from an a.e.-zero winding number on a positive-measure active subset together
  with local constancy on the arc, the winding number is `0` **everywhere** on
  the arc;
* `StandardActiveFibreWindingZeroOnArc_proved` — the winding form of the residual,
  built from the reduced data.

The two genuinely analytic ingredients that remain are isolated as the *smallest*
exact theorem types (the run instructions' acceptable remaining types):

* `StandardWindingLocallyConstantZeroFreeFamily` — local constancy of the integer
  winding number of the zero-free analytic return-multiplier family on the arc;
* `StandardAEActiveFibreWindingZero` — a.e. zero winding of the actual return
  cocycle on a positive-measure active subset (from the measurable winding
  obstruction applied to the actual a.e. cocycle);
* `StandardWindingZeroHolonomyBridge` — the per-fibre identification that zero
  winding of the return loop forces the gauge value to equal the loop holonomy
  `exp(∫₀¹ ell_t)` of a periodic logarithm.

No axioms, `sorry`s, or `admit`s are introduced.
-/
/-! ## Step 5 — topological propagation on the connected arc -/

/-- **A function locally constant within the connected arc is constant on it.**

If `W : ℝ → Y` is locally constant *relative to* the open interval
`Set.Ioo a₀ b₀` (for every `s` in the interval, `W` is eventually equal to `W s`
along `𝓝[Set.Ioo a₀ b₀] s`), then `W` takes one and the same value at any two
points of the interval.  This is the topological propagation step: the interval
is connected, so a locally constant function on it is constant.  Proved by
restricting `W` to the connected subtype `↥(Set.Ioo a₀ b₀)` and invoking
`IsLocallyConstant.apply_eq_of_isPreconnected`. -/

/-- **A function vanishing a.e. on a positive-measure set vanishes somewhere on
it.**

If `S` has positive volume and `W s = 0` for almost every `s ∈ S`, then there is
an actual point `s₀ ∈ S` with `W s₀ = 0`.  (If not, `S` would be contained in the
null set where the a.e. statement fails, contradicting `0 < volume S`.) -/
/-! ## The smallest residual analytic interfaces (fallback policy) -/

/-- **`STANDARD_WINDING_LOCALLY_CONSTANT_ZERO_FREE_FAMILY`.**

The integer winding number `W` of the zero-free, jointly-analytic return
multiplier family is **locally constant** on the active arc `Set.Ioo a₀ b₀`.
This is the genuinely analytic ingredient (step 4): for a continuously varying
*zero-free* family of loops, the integer winding number cannot jump.  Isolated
here as the smallest exact theorem type. -/

/-- **`STANDARD_AE_ACTIVE_FIBRE_WINDING_ZERO`.**

The actual return cocycle has **zero winding number** for almost every active
fibre on a positive-measure active subset `S` of the arc.  This is the
measure-theoretic output of the measurable winding obstruction
(`measurable_cocycle_winding_eq_zero`) applied to the actual a.e. return cocycle
(`AENormalizedReturnData.ae_normalized_m_step_return_cocycle`) on the active set.
Isolated here as the smallest exact theorem type. -/

/-- **`STANDARD_WINDING_ZERO_HOLONOMY_BRIDGE`.**

The per-fibre identification: at any active fibre with **zero winding number**,
the analytic gauge value equals the loop holonomy `exp(∫₀¹ ell_t)` of any
continuous `1`-periodic logarithm of the bivariate Laurent return loop.  This is
exactly the analytic↔algebraic content of `StandardActiveFibreWindingZeroOnArc`
reduced to the *zero-winding* fibres.  Isolated here as the smallest exact theorem
type. -/
/-! ## Tasks B/D — extraction and propagation (proved) -/

/-- **`STANDARD_POSITIVE_MEASURE_ACTIVE_SET_MEETS_CONSTANT_COMPONENT`
(Task B, proved).**

From the a.e. zero winding number on a positive-measure active subset, there is
an actual active fibre `s₀ ∈ Set.Ioo a₀ b₀` with winding number `0`.  This is the
measure-theoretic extraction `exists_winding_zero_of_ae_on_positive_measure`
specialised to the active data. -/
/-- Re-export under the `active_fibre_winding_zero_ae` name. -/

/-- **`WINDING_ZERO_ON_ACTIVE_ARC_OF_AE_ACTIVE_WINDING_ZERO` (Task D, proved).**

The propagation theorem: combining the a.e. zero winding on the positive-measure
active subset (`StandardAEActiveFibreWindingZero`) with the local constancy of the
winding number on the arc (`StandardWindingLocallyConstantZeroFreeFamily`), the
winding number is `0` at **every** fibre of the connected arc `Set.Ioo a₀ b₀`.

Proof: extraction gives one active fibre `s₀` with `W s₀ = 0`; local constancy on
the connected arc forces `W t = W s₀ = 0` for every `t` in the arc
(`locallyConstant_eq_of_mem_Ioo`). -/
/-- Re-export of the propagation theorem packaged as the arc-propagation type. -/
/-! ## Closure of the winding form from the reduced data -/

/-- **`STANDARD_ACTIVE_FIBRE_WINDING_ZERO_ON_ARC_PROVED` (Task D, proved from the
reduced data).**

The winding form of the residual is constructed from:

* `aez` — a.e. zero winding on a positive-measure active subset
  (`StandardAEActiveFibreWindingZero`);
* `lc`  — local constancy of the winding number on the arc
  (`StandardWindingLocallyConstantZeroFreeFamily`);
* `br`  — the per-fibre winding-zero ⇒ holonomy bridge
  (`StandardWindingZeroHolonomyBridge`).

The propagation theorem
`winding_zero_on_active_arc_of_ae_active_winding_zero` discharges the
positive-measure-to-whole-arc step; the bridge then converts zero winding into the
holonomy identity at each active fibre. -/
/-! ## Task E — downstream closure -/

/-- **`STANDARD_ACTIVE_FIBRE_HOLONOMY_EQUALS_GAUGE_MULTIPLIER_PROVED`.**

The algebraic form of the residual, derived from the winding form (built from the
reduced data) together with the root data, via the previously-established
inter-derivability
`StandardActiveFibreWindingZeroOnArc.toHolonomyEqualsGaugeMultiplier`. -/

/-- **`STANDARD_CANONICAL_AMPLITUDE_COMPATIBILITY_PROVED`.**

The canonical-amplitude form of the residual, derived from the winding-form
holonomy data (built from the reduced data) together with the root data, via
`canonical_amplitude_compatibility_of_winding`. -/

/-- **`CRITICAL_MIXED_FINAL_CONTRADICTION_WITH_ACTIVE_FIBRE_HOLONOMY_FULLY_CLOSED`.**

The conditional final contradiction with the active-fibre holonomy interface
discharged down to the three smallest residual winding interfaces (a.e. winding
zero, local constancy, and the winding-zero ⇒ holonomy bridge), together with the
three already-packaged interfaces (`DK_VARIATION_INTERFACE`, `ROOT_DATA_INTERFACE`,
`ZAK_MODEL_INTERFACE`). -/

/-- **`CRITICAL_MIXED_FINAL_CONTRADICTION_WITHOUT_HOLONOMY_AMPLITUDE_INTERFACE_FULLY_CLOSED`.**

Same closure as
`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_with_active_fibre_holonomy_fully_closed`, but
routed through the holonomy-amplitude package built internally from the winding
form (with the canonical-amplitude compatibility derived rather than assumed). -/
