/-!
# Stage 6B — the corrected **`L²`-level** actual-Zak fibre extraction

## Why the previous residual was too strong

The previous run's residual `StandardActualZakRepresentativeTheorem`
(`RequestProject/HRT/ActualZakFiberExtraction.lean`) asks, for an **arbitrary**
`L²` class `f`, for a window
```
g : ℝ → ℂ
```
that is bounded, measurable, compactly supported in `[0,N)` **and** satisfies
`f =ᵐ g`.  Compactly supported bounded functions are dense in `L²`, but a *fixed*
`L²` equivalence class need not contain such a representative: a generic `L²`
function is neither bounded nor compactly supported.  Hence that residual is
`TOO_STRONG_FOR_GENERAL_L2`.

## The correct anchoring

The honest object to choose a representative of is **not** `f` but the **target**
`L²` class produced by the a.e.-level Zak transform,
```
Z.Zak f : ZakTarget = Lp ℂ 2 zakSquareMeasure ,
```
which *always* has a measurable representative `ℝ × ℝ → ℂ` (`Lp.aestronglyMeasurable`).
Its canonical curried fibre function `zakTargetFiber (Z.Zak f) x s = (Z.Zak f)(x,s)`
carries, **with no compact-support hypothesis on `f`**, the genuine
Zak/Plancherel mass identity through the *isometry* field of `L2ZakModelAE`:
```
  ∫₀¹ fiberDensity (zakTargetFiber (Z.Zak f)) s ds = ‖Z.Zak f‖² = ‖f‖² .
```

## What is proved here (unconditionally, no compact support of `f`)

* `Lp_has_measurable_representative`, `zak_Lp_class_has_representative`,
  `actual_L2_Zak_representative_ae_eq` — representative selection for the **target**
  `Lp` class (Task C).
* `zakTarget_fiberDensity_integrable`, `zakTarget_mass_eq_norm_sq` — interval
  integrability of the fibre density and the Zak target mass identity
  `∫₀¹ fiberDensity = ‖G‖²` (Task E, Plancherel core).
* `actual_L2_zak_total_mass_eq_norm_sq`, `actual_L2_zak_active_set_positive_of_nonzero_window`
  — the isometric mass tie `= ‖f‖²` and positive-measure active fibres for `f ≠ 0`,
  using **only** the isometry, never a compactly supported representative of `f`
  (Task E).
* `actual_L2_zak_total_mass_eq_norm_sq_rep`,
  `actual_L2_zak_fiberDensity_integrable_rep` — the same facts transported to an
  arbitrary a.e.-representative of the target class (so a *periodic* fibre
  representative may be used downstream).

## The corrected residual and downstream rewiring

* `StandardActualL2ZakRepresentativeTheorem` — the corrected residual (Task B):
  from `f ≠ 0` and the `L²`-class one-step Zak relation in the concrete a.e. model,
  produce an a.e.-**representative** of the target class `Z.Zak f` that is periodic
  in the frequency variable and satisfies the a.e. one-step fibre equation.  It
  asks for a representative of `Z.Zak f`, **not** of `f`, and carries no
  compact-support data.
* `actual_L2_zak_relation_to_ae_product_equation`,
  `actual_L2_zak_relation_to_ae_fibre_equation` — Task D extraction from the
  corrected residual.
* `actual_L2_zak_nontrivial_fiber_extraction`,
  `actual_L2_zak_nontrivial_fiber_extraction_from_relation` — Task F: genuine
  `NontrivialAEFiberExtraction` whose fibre function represents `Z.Zak f`, with the
  proved Plancherel mass tie.
* `zak_relation_feeds_ae_normalized_no_flat_band_actual_L2_Zak`,
  `critical_mixed_final_contradiction_with_actual_L2_Zak_fiber_extraction` —
  Task G: downstream endpoints depending on the corrected `L²`-level residual,
  **not** on the too-strong compact-support representative theorem.

No `sorry`, no `axiom`, no `unsafe`, no `@[implemented_by]`.
-/
/-! ## Task C — representative selection for the **target** `Lp` class -/

/-- **Task C — every `Lp` class has a measurable representative.**

The canonical coercion `(G : α → ℂ)` of an `L²` class is almost-everywhere
strongly measurable.  This is the honest representative-selection fact; it holds
for *every* `Lp` class (in particular it requires no boundedness or compact
support). -/

/-- **Task C — the target Zak class has a measurable representative.**

The target class `Z.Zak f : ZakTarget = Lp ℂ 2 zakSquareMeasure` has a measurable
representative `ℝ × ℝ → ℂ`.  This is the class we select a representative of —
**not** `f`. -/

/-- The canonical curried fibre function of a target `L²([0,1]²)` class
`G : ZakTarget`: `zakTargetFiber G x s = G(x,s)`. -/

/-- **Task C — the canonical fibre function represents the target class a.e.**

The curried fibre function `zakTargetFiber (Z.Zak f)` agrees, as a function of
`(x,s)`, with the target representative of `Z.Zak f` almost everywhere on the unit
square.  (It is literally the curried coercion, so the agreement is definitional.) -/
/-! ## Task E — Plancherel mass and integrability for the target representative -/

/-
**Task E — interval integrability of the target fibre density.**

For a target `L²([0,1]²)` class `G`, the fibre density
`s ↦ ∫₀¹ ‖G(x,s)‖² dx` is interval-integrable on `[0,1]`.  This is the Fubini
regularity of an `L²` function on the unit square.
-/

/-
**Task E — the Zak target mass identity (Plancherel core).**

For a target `L²([0,1]²)` class `G`, the total fibre mass of its canonical fibre
function equals the squared `L²`-norm of `G`:
`∫₀¹ fiberDensity (zakTargetFiber G) s ds = ‖G‖²`.  This is the honest Plancherel
content (Fubini on the unit square plus `Lp_two_norm_sq`); it needs **no** window
data at all.
-/
-- Write the L2 norm squared using Lp_two_norm_sq.
-- Apply Fubini's theorem to rewrite the integral over the product space as an iterated integral.

/-- **Task E — the isometric mass tie for the target Zak class.**

Combining the Zak target mass identity with the **isometry** field
`‖Z.Zak f‖ = ‖f‖` of `L2ZakModelAE`, the total fibre mass of the canonical fibre
function of `Z.Zak f` equals `‖f‖²`.  This is the corrected Plancherel tie: it
uses only the `L²` isometry, never a compactly supported representative of `f`. -/

/-- **Task E — positive-measure active fibres from a nonzero window.**

For `f ≠ 0`, the active fibre set of the canonical fibre function of `Z.Zak f`
has positive Lebesgue measure.  Proof: the total mass is `‖f‖² > 0` by the
isometric tie, and a nonnegative density with positive integral has
positive-measure support.  No compact-support representative of `f` is used. -/
/-! ## Transport to an arbitrary a.e.-representative of the target class -/

/-- The fibre density of any a.e.-representative of the target class `G` agrees,
for a.e. frequency `s ∈ (0,1]`, with the fibre density of the canonical fibre
function `zakTargetFiber G`. -/

/-- **Task E (transported) — Plancherel mass tie for an arbitrary
representative.**

If `F` is *any* a.e.-representative of the target class `Z.Zak f`, then the total
fibre mass of `F` equals `‖f‖²`.  This lets a periodic representative be used
downstream while keeping the proved Plancherel tie. -/

/-- **Task E (transported) — interval integrability for an arbitrary
representative. -/
/-! ## Task B — the corrected `L²`-level residual -/

/-- **Task B — the corrected `L²`-level actual-Zak residual.**

The single genuinely Zak-analytic obligation after correcting the anchoring: from
a nonzero `L²` class `f` satisfying the normalized four-term HRT relation in the
concrete a.e. Zak model, produce a fibre function `F : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ` that

* is an a.e.-**representative of the target class** `Z.Zak f`
  (`(fun p => F p.1 p.2) =ᵐ Z.Zak f`),
* is `1`-periodic in the frequency variable, and
* satisfies the a.e. one-step Zak fibre equation.

Crucially this asks for a representative of the **target** class `Z.Zak f`, which
always exists, and carries **no** compact-support or boundedness data on `f`.  It
is recorded as a precisely-typed proposition, **not** an axiom, and is not the
too-strong `StandardActualZakRepresentativeTheorem`. -/
/-! ## Task D — extracting the a.e. fibre equation from the corrected residual -/

/-- **Task D — the corrected residual yields a representative carrying the a.e.
product/fibre equation.**

Given the corrected `L²`-level residual, the `L²`-class HRT relation produces a
representative `F` of the target class `Z.Zak f`, periodic in the frequency
variable, satisfying the a.e. one-step fibre equation.  (This is just
destructuring the residual; recorded under the requested name.) -/

/-- **Task D — the a.e. one-step fibre equation from the corrected residual.**

The fibre-equation projection of `actual_L2_zak_relation_to_ae_product_equation`. -/
/-! ## Task F — the genuine `L²`-level nontrivial extraction -/

/-- **Task F — genuine `NontrivialAEFiberExtraction` from the corrected residual.**

From the corrected residual's representative `F` of the target class `Z.Zak f`
(periodic, a.e. one-step), together with the **proved** Plancherel mass tie
(`actual_L2_zak_total_mass_eq_norm_sq_rep`) and interval integrability
(`actual_L2_zak_fiberDensity_integrable_rep`), assemble a genuine
`NontrivialAEFiberExtraction` with `window := f` and fibre function `F`.  The
fibre function is an honest `L²`-level representative of the **target** Zak class;
no compactly supported representative of `f` is used and `F` is never the zero
function. -/
/-- **Task F — genuine extraction from a relation (named alias).** -/
/-! ## Task G — downstream rewiring through the corrected `L²`-level residual -/

/-- **Task G — corrected `L²`-level Zak relation feeds the a.e. no-flat-band
machinery.**

Given the corrected `L²`-level residual `StandardActualL2ZakRepresentativeTheorem`,
a nonzero window satisfying the normalized four-term HRT relation in the concrete
a.e. Zak model produces a genuine `NontrivialAEFiberExtraction` (fibre function =
representative of the **target** Zak class), converted to `AENormalizedReturnData`
and fed into the Stage 5 no-flat-band theorem.  This depends on the corrected
`L²`-level residual, and **not** on the too-strong compact-support representative
theorem `StandardActualZakRepresentativeTheorem`. -/

/-- **Task G — final Stage 6B contradiction with the corrected `L²`-level Zak
fibre extraction.**

The corrected replacement for
`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_with_actual_Zak_fiber_extraction`.  On the Zak
side it depends **only** on the corrected `L²`-level residual
`StandardActualL2ZakRepresentativeTheorem` — the fibre function is an honest
`L²`-level representative of the **target** Zak class `Z.Zak f`, and the
Plancherel mass tie is the isometric identity, with **no** compactly supported
representative of `f`.  The remaining hypotheses are the same non-Zak interfaces
as before (Denjoy–Koksma data, analytic-rigidity/periodic-gauge data, and the
local Laurent holonomy root data). -/

/-!
# Stage 6B — the canonical **frequency-periodic** representative of the actual
`L²`-level Zak target class, and the minimal residual reduction

This module discharges the *generic measure-theoretic* content of the corrected
`L²`-level residual `StandardActualL2ZakRepresentativeTheorem`
(`RequestProject/HRT/ActualL2ZakFiberExtraction.lean`) and reduces that residual
to the single genuinely Zak-analytic obligation, the **a.e. one-step fibre
equation** for the canonical periodic representative.

## Why a periodic representative

The downstream `NontrivialAEFiberExtraction` consumes a fibre function
`F : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ` that is `1`-periodic in the frequency variable.  An arbitrary
`Lp` representative of the target class `concreteAEZakModel.Zak f : ZakTarget` is
only defined a.e. on the fundamental square `(0,1]²` and carries no periodicity.
We therefore build the **canonical periodic representative**
```
zakPeriodicRep G x s := (G : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ) (Int.fract x, Int.fract s),
```
the periodic extension from the fundamental domain of the chosen `Lp`
representative of `G`.  By construction it is `1`-periodic in *both* variables
(in particular in the frequency variable `s`), and it agrees with `G` almost
everywhere on the fundamental square `(0,1]²` (where `Int.fract` is the identity
off a null set).

## What is proved here (unconditionally, no compact support of `f`)

* `actual_L2_Zak_periodic_representative` — the canonical periodic representative
  exists (its definition `zakPeriodicRep`);
* `actual_L2_Zak_periodic_representative_periodic_s` — `1`-periodicity in the
  frequency variable (Task B);
* `actual_L2_Zak_periodic_representative_ae_eq` — a.e. equality with the chosen
  `Lp` representative on the target measure (Task B);
* `actual_L2_Zak_periodic_representative_memLp` — `L²([0,1]²)` membership of the
  periodic representative (Task B);
* `Lp_eq_to_ae_eq_representatives`, `Lp_relation_to_ae_product_relation`
  — Lp-equality / Lp-relation to a.e. product equality (Task C);
* `ae_product_eq_to_ae_fibre_eq'`, `ae_fiberwise_of_ae_prod'` — product-a.e. to
  fibre-a.e. conversion (Task D).

## The minimal residual reduction (Task E / Task F)

The only content of `StandardActualL2ZakRepresentativeTheorem` *not* discharged
here is the **a.e. one-step fibre equation** for the canonical periodic
representative.  At the level of the abstract a.e. Zak model
`concreteAEZakModel` the lattice/rogue covariance operators are realized by
transport through the isometric extension `zakExt` and carry **no explicit fibre
formula**, so the explicit `oneStepEquation` cannot be read off the abstract
covariance.  This is the genuine remaining Zak-analytic obligation; it is
isolated — *not* as an axiom — as the precisely-typed proposition
`StandardActualZakRepresentativeEquationAE`, the a.e. one-step fibre equation for
`zakPeriodicRep (concreteAEZakModel.Zak f)`.

`standardActualL2ZakRepresentativeTheorem_of_equationAE` then proves the full
residual `StandardActualL2ZakRepresentativeTheorem` from that single blocker by
supplying the canonical periodic representative for the a.e.-representative and
periodicity fields.  The downstream endpoints
`actual_L2_zak_nontrivial_fiber_extraction_closed`,
`zak_relation_feeds_ae_normalized_no_flat_band_actual_L2_Zak_closed` and
`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_without_Zak_side_interface` are rewired to
depend on the minimal blocker.

No `sorry`, no `axiom`, no `unsafe`, no `@[implemented_by]`.
-/
/-! ## Task B — the canonical frequency-periodic representative -/

/-- **Task B — the canonical frequency-periodic representative of a target
`L²([0,1]²)` class.**

The periodic extension from the fundamental domain of the chosen `Lp`
representative of `G`:
`zakPeriodicRep G x s = (G : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ) (Int.fract x, Int.fract s)`.  By
construction it is `1`-periodic in both variables. -/

/-- **Task B — the canonical periodic representative exists** (named wrapper for
its definition). -/

/-- **Task B — `1`-periodicity in the frequency variable.**

`zakPeriodicRep G x (s + 1) = zakPeriodicRep G x s` for every `x, s`, since
`Int.fract (s + 1) = Int.fract s`. -/

/-- **Task B — `1`-periodicity in the time variable** (bonus; the construction is
periodic in both variables). -/

/-
**Task B — the canonical periodic representative agrees a.e. with the chosen
`Lp` representative.**

On the fundamental square `(0,1]²` carrying `zakSquareMeasure`, `Int.fract` is the
identity off the null set `{1} × ℝ ∪ ℝ × {1}`, so the periodic representative
equals the coercion `(G : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ)` almost everywhere.
-/

/-- **Task B — the canonical periodic representative is `L²([0,1]²)`.**

It is a.e.-equal to the `Lp` class `G`, which is `MemLp`, so the periodic
representative is `MemLp` for `zakSquareMeasure`. -/
/-! ## Task C — Lp-equality / Lp-relation to a.e. product equality -/

/-- **Task C — equal `Lp` classes have a.e.-equal representatives** (named
wrapper). -/

/-- **Task C — an `Lp` four-term linear relation descends to an a.e.-pointwise
relation between representatives.** -/
/-! ## Task D — product-a.e. to fibre-a.e. conversion -/

/-- **Task D — an a.e. equality on a product measure descends to a.e.-fibrewise
a.e. equality** (named wrapper). -/

/-- **Task D — a predicate holding a.e. on a product measure holds, for a.e.
first coordinate, a.e. in the second coordinate** (named wrapper). -/
/-! ## Task E / Task F — the minimal residual reduction -/

/-- **The minimal remaining Zak-analytic blocker (Task F).**

The single content of `StandardActualL2ZakRepresentativeTheorem` not discharged
by the generic measure theory above: the **a.e. one-step fibre equation** for the
canonical periodic representative `zakPeriodicRep (concreteAEZakModel.Zak f)` of
the target class.

This is the genuine Zak covariance content: at the abstract level the model's
lattice/rogue covariance operators are realized by transport through the
isometric extension `zakExt` and carry no explicit fibre formula, so the explicit
`oneStepEquation` cannot be read off the abstract covariance.  It is isolated as a
precisely-typed proposition (referring to a **representative of the target class**,
with **no** compact-support / boundedness data on `f`), **not** an axiom. -/

/-- **Task E — the corrected `L²`-level residual from the minimal blocker.**

Given the minimal a.e. one-step-equation blocker
`StandardActualZakRepresentativeEquationAE`, the full corrected residual
`StandardActualL2ZakRepresentativeTheorem` holds: the canonical periodic
representative `zakPeriodicRep (concreteAEZakModel.Zak f)` simultaneously
represents the target class a.e., is `1`-periodic in the frequency variable, and
(by the blocker) satisfies the a.e. one-step fibre equation. -/
/-! ## Task E — downstream endpoints closed over the minimal blocker -/

/-- **Task E — the genuine `L²`-level nontrivial extraction, closed over the
minimal blocker.**

`actual_L2_zak_nontrivial_fiber_extraction` with the corrected residual
discharged from `StandardActualZakRepresentativeEquationAE`. -/

/-- **Task E — corrected `L²`-level Zak relation feeds the a.e. no-flat-band
machinery, closed over the minimal blocker.** -/

/-- **Task E — final Stage 6B contradiction without a Zak-side interface
hypothesis beyond the minimal blocker.**

The corrected `L²`-level Zak fibre extraction contradiction, with the residual
`StandardActualL2ZakRepresentativeTheorem` discharged from the minimal a.e.
one-step-equation blocker `StandardActualZakRepresentativeEquationAE`.  On the Zak
side this depends **only** on that minimal blocker — the periodic representative,
its a.e. agreement with the target class, the Plancherel mass tie and active
positivity are all proved unconditionally. -/

/-!
# Stage 6B — the **target `Lp` one-step Zak relation** (Task C)

This module performs the one genuinely *unconditional* step of the corrected
`L²`-level Zak residual: applying the concrete a.e. Zak isometry
`concreteAEZakModel.Zak` to the normalized four-term HRT relation in the source
`L²(ℝ)` space and using the **abstract covariance fields** of the model
(`lattice_cov` for the two integer-lattice shifts, `rogue_cov` for the rogue
shift `(a, p/m)`) to obtain an equality of target `L²([0,1]²)` classes:
```
c₀ • Zf + c₁ • charLattice r₁ t₁ (Zf) + c₂ • charLattice r₂ t₂ (Zf)
        + c₃ • charRogue a (p/m) (Zf) = 0 .
```

This is the honest "target-side" form of the relation.  It needs **no** explicit
fibre formula for the (abstractly transported) covariance operators — only the
linearity of the isometry and the two covariance fields — so it is proved
unconditionally here.

The remaining content of the minimal blocker
`StandardActualZakRepresentativeEquationAE` is exactly to turn the abstract
covariance operators `charLattice` / `charRogue` appearing here into their
explicit pointwise fibre representatives; that is isolated separately (it is the
genuinely Zak-analytic core, blocked by the abstract transport construction of
the model's covariance operators).

No `sorry`, no `axiom`, no `unsafe`, no `@[implemented_by]`.
-/

/-
**Task C — the target `Lp` one-step Zak relation.**

Apply the concrete a.e. Zak isometry to the source four-term HRT relation.  Using
linearity of the isometry together with the model's abstract lattice covariance
(for the two integer shifts `(r₁,t₁)`, `(r₂,t₂)`) and rogue covariance (for the
shift `(a, p/m)`), the relation descends to an equality of **target** `L²([0,1]²)`
classes in `ZakTarget`:
```
c₀ • Zf + c₁ • charLattice r₁ t₁ Zf + c₂ • charLattice r₂ t₂ Zf
        + c₃ • charRogue a (p/m) Zf = 0 ,   Zf := concreteAEZakModel.Zak f .
```
This is unconditional (no explicit fibre formula for the covariance operators is
used).
-/
/-! ## Canonicalizing the minimal blocker through the target relation -/

/-- **Canonical remaining Zak-analytic interface (Task G shape
`StandardTargetRelationToRepresentativeEquationAE`).**

The content of the minimal blocker `StandardActualZakRepresentativeEquationAE`
with its source-side hypothesis replaced by the (now unconditionally proved)
*target* `Lp` one-step relation.  Concretely: from a nonzero window `f` whose
target class `Zf := concreteAEZakModel.Zak f` satisfies the explicit target
four-term relation
```
c₀ • Zf + c₁ • charLattice r₁ t₁ Zf + c₂ • charLattice r₂ t₂ Zf
        + c₃ • charRogue a (p/m) Zf = 0 ,
```
the canonical periodic representative `zakPeriodicRep Zf` satisfies the a.e.
one-step fibre equation.

This isolates *exactly* the remaining Zak-analytic content: turning the
abstractly transported covariance operators `charLattice` / `charRogue` (applied
to the target class) into their explicit pointwise fibre representatives on
`zakPeriodicRep Zf`.  It mentions **no** source-side time-frequency shift
operators — it is tied directly to the target representative — and is therefore a
strictly more canonical form of the blocker than
`StandardActualZakRepresentativeEquationAE`. -/

/-- **Sound reduction of the minimal blocker to the target-relation interface.**

Feeding the unconditionally-proved `target_Lp_one_step_Zak_relation` discharges
the source-side hypothesis of `StandardActualZakRepresentativeEquationAE`, so the
canonical target-relation interface
`StandardTargetRelationToRepresentativeEquationAE` implies the minimal blocker.
Thus the Zak side now reduces to the strictly more canonical interface that no
longer refers to the source-side shift operators. -/

comments.text:
/-!
# Stage 6B — re-anchoring the nontrivial fibre extraction to the *actual* Zak transform

The previous run reduced the Zak-side blocker to the model-free proposition
`StandardNontrivialFiberConstructionTheorem`
(`RequestProject/HRT/NontrivialFiberExtractionConstruction.lean`): construct *some*
fibre function `F : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ` solving the a.e. one-step Zak fibre equation with a
prescribed positive total mass, **without** using the actual `L²` Zak transform,
the actual window, or the four-term HRT relation.  That reduction is **valid but
artificial**: the assembled `NontrivialAEFiberExtraction` carries `window := f`
but its fibre function `F` is unrelated to `Z.Zak f`, so it is not genuine HRT
evidence and may be unprovable (or false) in exactly the regimes where the
no-flat-band contradiction must apply.

This module re-anchors the fibre data to the **actual concrete Zak transform**
`concreteZakDense g` of an actual (bounded, measurable, compactly supported)
window `g` representing the `L²` class `f`.  The fibre function is *no longer*
model-free: it is the genuine Zak transform of the window, and the Plancherel
mass tie `∫₀¹ fiberDensity (concreteZakDense g) = ‖f‖²` is the actual Zak/Plancherel
identity (`actual_zak_total_fiber_mass_eq_norm_sq`), not a postulated mass.

## What is proved unconditionally here

* `StandardActualZakFiberExtractionTheorem` — the **actual-Zak** extraction
  interface (Task B): from a nonzero `L²` class `f`, a concrete representative
  window `g` (`f =ᵐ g`, bounded, measurable, supported in `[0,N)`), and the a.e.
  one-step Zak fibre equation *for the actual transform* `concreteZakDense g`,
  produce a `NontrivialAEFiberExtraction` whose fibre function is `concreteZakDense g`.
  This is **proved** (`actual_zak_nontrivial_fiber_extraction`): all four
  structure fields come from the actual Zak endpoints
  (`actual_zak_representative_periodic_s`,
  `actual_zak_representative_fiberDensity_integrable`,
  `actual_zak_total_fiber_mass_eq_norm_sq`) plus the supplied a.e. one-step
  equation.  The fibre function is never model-free and never `0`.

* The adapters of Task C, all **proved**:
  `actual_zak_representative_represents_Lp_Zak` (the actual Zak/Plancherel mass
  tie `∫₀¹ fiberDensity = ‖f‖²`), `actual_zak_representative_nonzero_mass`,
  `actual_zak_representative_active_pos`.

## What is isolated as the minimal residual (Task H)

The only genuinely Zak-analytic residue is the passage *from the `L²`-class HRT
relation* to *(a concrete representative window `g` of `f` together with) the a.e.
one-step Zak fibre equation for `concreteZakDense g`*.  This is isolated — **not as
an axiom** — as `StandardActualZakRepresentativeTheorem`, and the Task D
conversion `actual_zak_Lp_relation_to_ae_fiber_equation` extracts the a.e. fibre
equation from it.

## Downstream rewiring (Task F)

`actual_zak_nontrivial_fiber_extraction_from_relation`,
`zak_relation_feeds_ae_normalized_no_flat_band_actual_Zak`, and
`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_with_actual_Zak_fiber_extraction` route the
final Stage 6B contradiction through the **actual-Zak** residual
`StandardActualZakRepresentativeTheorem` and the existing a.e. return-cocycle
machinery (`nontrivial_AE_fiber_extraction_feeds_ae_return_cocycle`,
`ae_normalized_return_cocycle_feeds_no_flat_band_root_data_minimal`).  They do
**not** depend on `StandardNontrivialFiberConstructionTheorem`.

No `sorry`, no `axiom`, no `unsafe`, no `@[implemented_by]`.
-/
/-! ## Task C / Task B — actual Zak representative adapters -/

/-- **Task C — the actual Zak/Plancherel mass tie.**

For a bounded measurable window `g` supported in `[0,N)` that represents the `L²`
class `f` (`f =ᵐ g`), the total fibre mass of the **actual** Zak transform
`concreteZakDense g` equals `‖f‖²`:
`∫₀¹ fiberDensity (concreteZakDense g) s ds = ‖f‖²`.

This is the honest Zak/Plancherel isometry identity
(`actual_zak_total_fiber_mass_eq_norm_sq` combined with `Lp_two_norm_sq`), tying
the actual fibre mass to the window's `L²`-mass.  It is the field that forbids the
degenerate `F = 0` witness. -/

/-- **Task C — nonzero actual fibre mass from a nonzero window.**

If `f ≠ 0` (and `g` is a representative window as above), the total fibre mass of
the actual Zak transform `concreteZakDense g` is strictly positive. -/

/-- **Task C — positive-measure active fibres for the actual Zak transform.**

For a nonzero window the actual Zak transform `concreteZakDense g` has
positive-measure active fibres, the honest non-vacuity content. -/
/-! ## Task B — the actual Zak fibre extraction theorem -/

/-- **Task B — the actual Zak fibre extraction interface.**

This is the **correct** re-anchored extraction target.  Unlike the model-free
`StandardNontrivialFiberConstructionTheorem`, its fibre function is the *actual*
Zak transform `concreteZakDense g` of an actual window `g` representing the `L²`
class `f`, and the Plancherel tie is the genuine Zak/Plancherel identity.  The
single Zak-analytic input it asks for is the **a.e. one-step Zak fibre equation
for the actual transform** `concreteZakDense g` (the honest `L²`-class content of
the four-term HRT relation).

It produces a `NontrivialAEFiberExtraction` (Task B requirements: (1) `F`
represents the actual Zak transform of `f`; (2) `F` satisfies the a.e. one-step
equation; (3) the fibre mass identity is Plancherel `∫ fibreDensity = ‖f‖²`;
(4) active set has positive measure because `f ≠ 0`).  No model-free `F` is
allowed. -/

/-- **Task E — the actual Zak fibre extraction theorem is *proved*.**

The actual-Zak extraction interface holds unconditionally: assembling the
`NontrivialAEFiberExtraction` with `window := f` and `F := concreteZakDense g`,
the four structure fields are supplied by the actual Zak endpoints
(periodicity, fibre-density interval-integrability, the Zak/Plancherel mass tie)
together with the provided a.e. one-step equation.  The fibre function is the
genuine Zak transform of the window — never model-free, never `0`. -/
/-! ## Task H — the minimal actual-Zak residual -/

/-- **Task H — the minimal actual-Zak residual.**

**DEPRECATED — `TOO_STRONG_FOR_GENERAL_L2`.**  This residual demands, for an
*arbitrary* `L²` class `f`, a window `g : ℝ → ℂ` that is bounded, measurable,
compactly supported in `[0,N)` **and** satisfies `f =ᵐ g`.  Such a representative
exists only for the dense subclass of bounded compactly supported functions, not
for a general `L²` equivalence class, so this proposition is too strong to be the
correct Zak-side blocker.  It is **superseded** by the corrected `L²`-level
residual `StandardActualL2ZakRepresentativeTheorem`
(`RequestProject/HRT/ActualL2ZakFiberExtraction.lean`), which selects a
representative of the **target** class `Z.Zak f` (which always exists) instead of
a compactly supported representative of `f`.  This definition and its downstream
lemmas are retained only for documentation/back-compat; new Stage 6B endpoints
route through the corrected `L²`-level residual.

The single genuinely Zak-analytic obligation remaining after re-anchoring: from a
nonzero `L²` class `f` satisfying the normalized four-term HRT relation in the
concrete a.e. Zak model, produce

* a concrete window `g` (bounded, measurable, supported in `[0,N)`) representing
  `f` (`f =ᵐ g`), and
* the a.e. one-step Zak fibre equation **for the actual transform**
  `concreteZakDense g`.

This is exactly the actual-Zak content (existence of a genuine window
representative carrying the `L²`-class relation as an a.e. fibre equation of the
*actual* Zak transform).  It is recorded as a precisely-typed proposition, **not**
an axiom, and **not** the model-free `StandardNontrivialFiberConstructionTheorem`. -/

/-- **Task D — extracting the a.e. fibre equation from the `L²`-class relation.**

Given the actual-Zak residual `StandardActualZakRepresentativeTheorem`, the
`L²`-class one-step Zak relation (encoded by the four-term HRT relation `hrel` in
the concrete a.e. Zak model) yields a concrete window representative `g` of `f`
together with the a.e. one-step Zak fibre equation for the **actual** transform
`concreteZakDense g`:
`∀ᵐ s, ∀ᵐ x, oneStepEquation … (concreteZakDense g) x s`.

This is the precise Task D conversion (`L²`-class relation → a.e. fibre equation)
for an actual representative of the Zak transform. -/
/-! ## Task E — genuine nontrivial extraction from the actual Zak transform -/

/-- **Task E — genuine `NontrivialAEFiberExtraction` from the actual Zak
transform.**

Combining the actual-Zak residual `StandardActualZakRepresentativeTheorem` (which
supplies the concrete window `g` representing `f` and the a.e. one-step equation
for `concreteZakDense g`) with the *proved* extraction interface
`actual_zak_nontrivial_fiber_extraction`, a nonzero window satisfying the
normalized HRT relation in the concrete a.e. Zak model produces a genuine
`NontrivialAEFiberExtraction` whose fibre function is the **actual** Zak transform
`concreteZakDense g`.  No model-free construction is used. -/
/-! ## Task F — rewiring the downstream bridge through the actual Zak transform -/

/-- **Task F — actual Zak relation feeds the a.e. no-flat-band machinery.**

Given the actual-Zak residual `StandardActualZakRepresentativeTheorem`, a nonzero
window satisfying a normalized four-term HRT relation in the concrete a.e. Zak
model produces a genuine `NontrivialAEFiberExtraction` (fibre function = actual
Zak transform), which is converted **directly** to `AENormalizedReturnData` (no
pointwise upgrade) and fed into the Stage 5 no-flat-band theorem.

This depends on `StandardActualZakRepresentativeTheorem` (the actual-Zak
residual), and **not** on the model-free `StandardNontrivialFiberConstructionTheorem`. -/

/-- **Task F — final Stage 6B contradiction with the actual Zak fibre extraction.**

The re-anchored replacement for
`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_without_Zak_extraction_interface`.  On the Zak
side it depends **only** on the actual-Zak residual
`StandardActualZakRepresentativeTheorem` — the fibre function is the genuine Zak
transform `concreteZakDense g` of the actual window, and the Plancherel mass tie
is the actual Zak/Plancherel identity.  It does **not** depend on the model-free
`StandardNontrivialFiberConstructionTheorem`.

The remaining hypotheses are the same non-Zak interfaces as the previous bridges:
the corrected periodic Denjoy–Koksma data (`DK`, `hq`), the analytic-rigidity /
periodic-gauge data (`H`, `J`, …), and the local Laurent holonomy root data
(`ad`, `coeffs`, `hroots`, `hJholo`). -/

/-!
# Stage 6B — the **quasiperiodic** representative of the actual `L²`-level Zak
target class, and the corrected residual

## Why a quasiperiodic representative

The previous run anchored the residual on the *doubly periodic* representative
`zakPeriodicRep (concreteAEZakModel.Zak f)`, which is `1`-periodic in **both**
`x` and `s`.  The genuine Zak fibre is `1`-periodic in the frequency variable `s`
but **quasiperiodic** in the time variable `x`:
```
Zf(x+1, s) = e^{2π i s} · Zf(x, s),    Zf(x, s+1) = Zf(x, s).
```
For a doubly-periodic `F`, the all-of-`ℝ` one-step fibre equation is inconsistent
when `m ∤ p` (comparing `x` and `x+1` forces `F ≡ 0`), so the old blocker
`StandardActualZakRepresentativeEquationAE` is **over-strong** (false for
nondegenerate data).

This module builds the correct **quasiperiodic representative**
```
zakQuasiPeriodicRep G x s
  := exp (2π i · ⌊x⌋ · fract s) · (G : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ) (fract x, fract s),
```
which is `1`-periodic in `s`, satisfies `F(x+1,s) = e^{2π i s} · F(x,s)`, agrees
a.e. with the chosen `Lp` representative on the fundamental square, and is
`L²` there.  It is the formally correct object to anchor the residual on.

## What is proved here (unconditionally)

* `zakQuasiPeriodicRep_periodic_s` — `1`-periodicity in the frequency variable;
* `zakQuasiPeriodicRep_quasiperiodic_x` — quasiperiodicity in the time variable
  with the correct phase `e^{2π i s}`;
* `zakQuasiPeriodicRep_ae_eq_on_fundamental_domain` — a.e. agreement with the
  chosen `Lp` representative on the fundamental square;
* `zakQuasiPeriodicRep_memLp_on_fundamental_domain` — `L²([0,1]²)` membership.

## The corrected residual and downstream rewiring

* `StandardActualZakQuasiRepresentativeEquationAE` — the **corrected** minimal
  blocker: the a.e. one-step fibre equation for the *quasiperiodic*
  representative.  Unlike the doubly-periodic blocker it is consistent with Zak
  quasiperiodicity (no `x`-periodicity is imposed or used).
* `standardActualL2ZakRepresentativeTheorem_of_quasiEquationAE` — sound reduction
  of the corrected `L²`-level residual `StandardActualL2ZakRepresentativeTheorem`
  to the corrected blocker, using the quasiperiodic representative as the
  existential witness (it is `s`-periodic and an a.e. representative of the target
  class, as required downstream — which never needs `x`-periodicity).
* `actual_L2_zak_quasi_representative_extraction`,
  `actual_L2_zak_nontrivial_fiber_extraction_quasi` — Task E.
* `zak_relation_feeds_ae_normalized_no_flat_band_actual_L2_Zak_quasi`,
  `critical_mixed_final_contradiction_with_actual_L2_Zak_quasi` — Task F downstream
  bridges replacing the doubly-periodic path.

No `sorry`, no `axiom`, no `unsafe`, no `@[implemented_by]`.
-/
/-! ## Task B — the canonical quasiperiodic representative -/

/-- **Task B — the canonical quasiperiodic representative of a target
`L²([0,1]²)` class.**

Pull `(x,s)` back to the fundamental square and insert the `x`-quasiperiodic
phase consistent with `Zf(x+1,s) = e^{2π i s} Zf(x,s)`,
`Zf(x,s+1) = Zf(x,s)`:
```
zakQuasiPeriodicRep G x s
  = exp (2π i · ⌊x⌋ · fract s) · (G : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ) (fract x, fract s).
```
It is `1`-periodic in `s` and quasiperiodic (not periodic) in `x`. -/

/-- **Task B — `1`-periodicity in the frequency variable.**

`zakQuasiPeriodicRep G x (s + 1) = zakQuasiPeriodicRep G x s`, since
`Int.fract (s + 1) = Int.fract s` (and `⌊x⌋`, `Int.fract x` are unchanged). -/

/-
**Task B — quasiperiodicity in the time variable.**

`zakQuasiPeriodicRep G (x + 1) s = exp (2π i s) · zakQuasiPeriodicRep G x s`,
matching the genuine Zak convention `Zf(x+1,s) = e^{2π i s} Zf(x,s)`.
-/

/-
**Task B — the quasiperiodic representative agrees a.e. with the chosen `Lp`
representative on the fundamental square.**

On `(0,1]²` carrying `zakSquareMeasure`, `Int.fract` is the identity and `⌊x⌋ = 0`
off a null set, so the phase is `1` and the representative equals `(G : ℝ×ℝ→ℂ)`
almost everywhere.
-/
/-- **Task B — the quasiperiodic representative is `L²([0,1]²)`.** -/
/-! ## Task C — the corrected residual equation (quasiperiodic) -/

/-- **Task C — the corrected minimal Zak-analytic blocker (quasiperiodic).**

The a.e. one-step fibre equation for the **quasiperiodic** representative
`zakQuasiPeriodicRep (concreteAEZakModel.Zak f)` of the target class.  Unlike the
doubly-periodic blocker `StandardActualZakRepresentativeEquationAE`, this requires
only `s`-periodicity, `x`-quasiperiodicity and the a.e. fibre equation — it is
consistent with the genuine Zak quasiperiodicity (no double periodicity in `x`). -/

/-- **Task C — the a.e. one-step fibre equation for the quasiperiodic
representative, extracted from the corrected blocker.**

This is the explicit one-step Zak fibre equation in quasiperiodic form; it
requires only `s`-periodicity, `x`-quasiperiodicity and the a.e. fibre equation
(all carried by `zakQuasiPeriodicRep`), **not** double periodicity. -/
/-! ## Task D — narrow target-operator formula blockers (quasiperiodic) -/

/-- **Task D — narrow lattice-operator fibre formula blocker (quasiperiodic).**

The exact missing explicit fibre action of the abstractly transported lattice
covariance operator `concreteAEZakModel.charLattice r t` on the target class,
expressed against the quasiperiodic representative.  Isolated as a precisely-typed
proposition (no axiom). -/

/-- **Task D — narrow rogue-operator fibre formula blocker (quasiperiodic).**

The exact missing explicit fibre action of the abstractly transported rogue
covariance operator `concreteAEZakModel.charRogue a b` on the target class,
expressed against the quasiperiodic representative.  Isolated as a precisely-typed
proposition (no axiom). -/

/-- **Task D — explicit a.e. lattice-operator fibre action on the quasiperiodic
representative**, conditional on the narrow lattice-operator blocker. -/

/-- **Task D — explicit a.e. rogue-operator fibre action on the quasiperiodic
representative**, conditional on the narrow rogue-operator blocker. -/
/-! ## Task E — the corrected residual reduction and extraction -/

/-- **Task E — the corrected `L²`-level residual from the quasiperiodic blocker.**

The full corrected residual `StandardActualL2ZakRepresentativeTheorem` follows
from the quasiperiodic blocker: the quasiperiodic representative
`zakQuasiPeriodicRep (concreteAEZakModel.Zak f)` is an a.e. representative of the
target class (`zakQuasiPeriodicRep_ae_eq_on_fundamental_domain`), is `1`-periodic
in the frequency variable (`zakQuasiPeriodicRep_periodic_s`), and (by the blocker)
satisfies the a.e. one-step fibre equation.  Downstream consumers never need
`x`-periodicity, so the quasiperiodic representative is a valid witness. -/

/-- **Task E — the quasiperiodic representative extraction.**

From the corrected quasiperiodic blocker and the `L²`-class HRT relation, the
quasiperiodic representative `F = zakQuasiPeriodicRep (concreteAEZakModel.Zak f)`
simultaneously represents the target class a.e., is `1`-periodic in the frequency
variable, and satisfies the a.e. one-step fibre equation. -/

/-- **Task E — genuine `NontrivialAEFiberExtraction` via the quasiperiodic
representative.**

The downstream `NontrivialAEFiberExtraction` built from the quasiperiodic
representative.  It carries `s`-periodicity (`hF_periodic_s`), the Plancherel mass
tie and the a.e. one-step equation — exactly the data the downstream machinery
consumes — and uses **no** `x`-periodicity. -/
/-! ## Task F — downstream bridges through the quasiperiodic representative -/

/-- **Task F — corrected `L²`-level Zak relation feeds the a.e. no-flat-band
machinery, via the quasiperiodic representative.**

Replaces the doubly-periodic path: depends only on the corrected quasiperiodic
blocker `StandardActualZakQuasiRepresentativeEquationAE`. -/

/-- **Task F — final Stage 6B contradiction via the quasiperiodic representative.**

The corrected replacement for
`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_without_Zak_side_interface`.  On the Zak side
it depends **only** on the corrected quasiperiodic blocker
`StandardActualZakQuasiRepresentativeEquationAE`; the representative is the
quasiperiodic Zak fibre (consistent with quasiperiodicity in `x`, periodicity in
`s`), not the over-strong doubly-periodic one. -/

/-!
# Stage 6B — the actual concrete Zak representative (Tasks B / D)

This module records, for the **actual** concrete dense-class Zak transform
`concreteZakDense f` (the genuine Zak transform `Zf(x,s) = ∑' k, f(x+k) e^{-2πiks}`
of a bounded measurable window `f` supported in `[0,N)`), the representative-level
facts requested by Tasks B and D.  These are the honest, *non-zero-fibre* analytic
ingredients of a `NontrivialAEFiberExtraction`:

* `actual_zak_representative_periodic_s` — `1`-periodicity in the frequency
  variable `s` (Task B);
* `actual_zak_representative_fiberDensity_integrable` — interval-integrability of
  the fibre density `s ↦ ∫₀¹ ‖Zf(x,s)‖² dx` (Task B);
* `actual_zak_total_fiber_mass_eq_norm_sq` — the Zak/Plancherel total-mass
  identity `∫₀¹ fiberDensity (Zf) s ds = ∫_ℝ ‖f‖²` (Task D), the honest tie
  between total fibre mass and the window's `L²`-mass that forbids the `F = 0`
  witness;
* `actual_zak_active_set_positive_of_nonzero_window` — positive-measure active
  fibres for a nonzero window (Task D).

All four are unconditional (no `sorry`, no `axiom`): they are thin wrappers around
the already-proven concrete results `concreteZakDense_periodic_s`,
`concrete_fiberDensity_integrable`, `concreteZakDense_plancherel`, and
`concrete_active_set_positive_measure`.  They work **a.e.**/at the
representative level and never use the zero fibre function.
-/

/-- **Task B — frequency-periodicity of the actual Zak representative.**

The concrete dense-class Zak transform is `1`-periodic in the frequency variable
`s`: `Zf(x, s+1) = Zf(x, s)` for every `x, s`.  (Holds pointwise, hence a.e.) -/

/-- **Task B — interval-integrability of the actual Zak fibre density.**

For a bounded measurable window `f` supported in `[0,N)`, the fibre density
`s ↦ ∫₀¹ ‖Zf(x,s)‖² dx` of the concrete dense-class Zak transform is
interval-integrable on `[0,1]`. -/

/-- **Task D — total fibre mass equals the window `L²`-mass (Zak/Plancherel).**

For a bounded measurable window `f` supported in `[0,N)`, the total fibre mass of
the concrete dense-class Zak transform equals the window's `L²`-mass:
`∫₀¹ fiberDensity (Zf) s ds = ∫_ℝ ‖f‖²`.  This is the honest Plancherel tie that
forbids the degenerate `F = 0` extraction. -/

/-- **Task D — positive-measure active fibres from a nonzero window.**

For a bounded measurable window `f` supported in `[0,N)` with positive `L²`-mass,
the active fibre set `{s : 0 < ∫₀¹ ‖Zf(x,s)‖² dx}` of the concrete dense-class Zak
transform has positive Lebesgue measure. -/

/-!
# Canonical amplitude / holonomy compatibility run

This module performs the **canonical amplitude / holonomy compatibility run** for
the conditional final assembly theorem.  It addresses the single residual
analytic↔algebraic bridge

```
  H t = canonicalGaugeAmplitude θ coeffs ad t      (on the active arc),
```

equivalently

```
  gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ t = algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t      (on the active arc),
```

which the previous *canonical holonomy amplitude run*
(`CanonicalHolonomyAmplitude.lean`) isolated as the field `hHcanon` of
`CriticalMixedCanonicalAmplitudeInterface`, and which the *holonomy-identification
discharge run* (`HolonomyIdentificationDischarge.lean`) isolated as the field
`hJalg` of `CriticalMixedHolonomyIdentificationInterface`.

## Task A — the exact residual

The exact remaining hypothesis is the pointwise identity, on the active arc, of
the analytic gauge value `gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ t = H t · exp(-2π i θ t)` with
the choice-free algebraic loop holonomy `algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t`.  Three
mutually equivalent shapes are used in the project:

* `StandardGaugeMultiplierEqualsAlgHolonomy` —
  `gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ t = algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t`;
* `StandardCanonicalAmplitudeCompatibility` —
  `H t = canonicalGaugeAmplitude θ coeffs ad t`;
* the `hJholo`/`hJgauge` form carried by `CriticalMixedWindingInterface`.

The classification of each ingredient is recorded in
`CANONICAL_AMPLITUDE_HOLONOMY_STATUS.md`.

## Task C — the algebraic holonomy identification (already proved)

The step "the periodic-log integral of the return multiplier equals the
root-product algebraic holonomy",
`StandardPeriodicLogIntegralEqualsRootHolonomy`, is **already discharged**
unconditionally as `return_multiplier_holonomy_eq_integral_log`
(`HolonomyIdentificationDischarge.lean`).  It is re-exported here and is *not* a
blocker.

## Tasks B/D — the compatibility follows from the active-fibre return cocycle

The key result of this run, `canonical_amplitude_compatibility_of_winding`, shows
that the residual compatibility is **not** independent data: given the active-fibre
winding interface `CriticalMixedWindingInterface` (the holonomy / phase-lift data
`J`, `hJgauge`, `hJholo`) together with the minimal root data, the canonical
amplitude compatibility `H t = canonicalGaugeAmplitude θ coeffs ad t` is *derived*
on the active arc.  The proof:

1. synthesises a continuous `1`-periodic logarithm `ell` of the return loop from
   the root factorisation (`evalBiLaurentPoly_periodic_log_of_roots`);
2. evaluates `hJholo` at `ell` to identify `J t` with `exp(∫₀¹ ell)`;
3. rewrites `J t = gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ t` via `hJgauge`;
4. identifies `exp(∫₀¹ ell)` with `algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t` via the
   already-proved `return_multiplier_holonomy_eq_integral_log`;

The minimal active-arc compatibility interface
`StandardCanonicalAmplitudeCompatibility` is strictly smaller than the previous
whole-window `CriticalMixedCanonicalAmplitudeInterface` (it is quantified only
over active fibres).  From it, together with the already-discharged analytic
constancy of `H`, we construct the holonomy-constancy interface internally and
restate the conditional final contradiction
(`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_with_canonical_amplitude_compat`).

No axioms, `sorry`s, or `admit`s are introduced.

/-!
# Canonical holonomy amplitude run

This module performs the **canonical holonomy amplitude run** for the conditional
final assembly theorem.  Its purpose is to eliminate or minimize the residual
holonomy-constancy interface `CriticalMixedHolonomyConstancyInterface`
(`HolonomyLawBridge.lean`), whose single field is

```
  hAlgPhase : algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t = H s₀ * exp(-2π i θ t).
```

## Task A — where the abstract amplitude `H` is used

The amplitude `H` enters through the active/analytic Zak-model interface
`CriticalMixedActiveAnalyticInterface` (`ConditionalFinalAssembly.lean`): it is an
analytic, nonvanishing function on the window `(a₀, b₀)` whose values lie in the
resonance group on a positive-measure active set.  The previous run
(`HolonomyLawBridge.lean`) proved its **constancy** on the active window
(`active_analytic_holonomy_constant`).  The only residual content of the
holonomy law is the algebraic-phase identity `hAlgPhase`, which references `H`
only through its single constant value `H s₀`.

The detailed field classification is recorded in
`CANONICAL_HOLONOMY_AMPLITUDE_STATUS.md`.

## Task B — the canonical amplitude

We define the **canonical gauge holonomy amplitude** directly from the algebraic
return holonomy,

```
  canonicalGaugeAmplitude θ coeffs ad t = exp(2π i θ t) · algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t,
```

so that the existing gauge operation `gaugeReturnMultiplier` recovers the
algebraic return holonomy *definitionally*:

```
  gaugeReturnMultiplier (canonicalGaugeAmplitude θ coeffs ad) θ t
    = algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t.
```

This is `gaugeReturnMultiplier_canonicalGaugeAmplitude`
(alias `canonicalGaugeAmplitude_gauge_identity`).

## Tasks C/D/F — the transparent compatibility field and the constancy interface

The genuine analytic↔algebraic bridge — that the *abstract* Zak-model amplitude
`H` equals the *canonical* algebraic amplitude — is not derivable from the
available interface data (it is exactly the link between the abstract Zak-model
amplitude and the concrete algebraic return loop, which the previous runs already
identified as the genuine remaining obstacle).  Per the Task F fallback policy we
therefore replace the opaque algebraic-phase identity `hAlgPhase` by the strictly
smaller and fully **transparent** compatibility field

```
  H t = canonicalGaugeAmplitude θ coeffs ad t      (on the active window),
```

packaged as `CriticalMixedCanonicalAmplitudeInterface`.

From this transparent compatibility field, together with the *already proved*
analytic constancy of `H` (`active_analytic_holonomy_constant`), we **construct**
the holonomy-constancy interface internally
(`canonical_amplitude_satisfies_holonomy_constancy_interface`), so that
`hAlgPhase` becomes a direct consequence of the gauge identity
`gaugeReturnMultiplier_canonicalGaugeAmplitude` and the constancy theorem.  The
headline endpoint
`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_with_canonical_amplitude_interface` then
restates the conditional final contradiction using only the transparent
compatibility field in place of the opaque `hAlgPhase`.

No axioms, `sorry`s, or `admit`s are introduced.
-/
/-! ## Task B — the canonical amplitude -/

/-- **Canonical gauge holonomy amplitude.**

Defined directly from the choice-free algebraic return holonomy by multiplying by
the inverse rotation phase:
`canonicalGaugeAmplitude θ coeffs ad t = exp(2π i θ t) · algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t`.
By construction, applying the gauge operation `gaugeReturnMultiplier` (which
multiplies by `exp(-2π i θ t)`) recovers `algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t`. -/
/-- Definitional unfolding of `canonicalGaugeAmplitude`. -/

/-- **The gauge of the canonical amplitude recovers the algebraic holonomy.**

The defining property: gauging the canonical amplitude by the rotation phase
returns the choice-free algebraic return holonomy exactly, with no hypotheses. -/
/-- Alias of `gaugeReturnMultiplier_canonicalGaugeAmplitude`. -/
/-! ## Task C — narrow regularity adapter -/

/-- **Nonvanishing of the canonical amplitude on fibres with nonzero leading
coefficient.**

When `evalLaurentCircle ad t ≠ 0`, the algebraic return holonomy is a product of
`evalLaurentCircle ad t` with factors `-z` over roots `z` with `‖z‖ > 1`; each
such factor is nonzero (a root with `‖z‖ > 1` cannot be `0`), so the canonical
amplitude — an exponential times this product — is nonzero. -/
/-! ## Tasks D/F — the transparent canonical-amplitude compatibility interface -/

/-- **`CANONICAL_AMPLITUDE` compatibility interface.**

The strictly smaller and fully transparent replacement for the opaque residual
algebraic-phase field `hAlgPhase` of `CriticalMixedHolonomyConstancyInterface`.
Its single field asserts the *definitional compatibility* between the abstract
Zak-model amplitude `H` and the canonical algebraic amplitude
`canonicalGaugeAmplitude θ coeffs ad` on the active window.  Unlike `hAlgPhase`,
this carries no quantitative algebraic-phase content: it is a plain pointwise
equality identifying the abstract amplitude with its canonical definition. -/

/-- **The canonical-amplitude compatibility field constructs the holonomy-constancy
interface.**

Given the active/analytic interface (which supplies, via
`active_analytic_holonomy_constant`, the constancy of `H` on the window) and the
transparent compatibility field `H = canonicalGaugeAmplitude`, the opaque residual
algebraic-phase identity `hAlgPhase` becomes a direct consequence of the gauge
identity `gaugeReturnMultiplier_canonicalGaugeAmplitude`.  This *constructs* the
holonomy-constancy interface internally. -/

/-- Re-export of `canonical_amplitude_satisfies_holonomy_constancy_interface`
under the `return_cocycle` name. -/

/-! ## Task F — the conditional final contradiction with the canonical-amplitude
interface -/

/-- **Conditional final contradiction from the canonical-amplitude interface.**

The strongest endpoint of this run.  It restates
`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_with_holonomy_constancy_interface`, replacing
the opaque residual algebraic-phase field `hAlgPhase` of
`CriticalMixedHolonomyConstancyInterface` by the strictly smaller and fully
transparent canonical-amplitude compatibility field
`CriticalMixedCanonicalAmplitudeInterface`
(`H = canonicalGaugeAmplitude θ coeffs ad` on the window).  The algebraic-phase
identity is now a derived consequence of the gauge identity together with the
already-discharged analytic constancy of `H`.

The conditional contradiction depends only on:

* `DK_VARIATION_INTERFACE`  (`dk`),
* `ROOT_DATA_INTERFACE`     (`rootData`),
* `ZAK_MODEL_INTERFACE`     (`analytic`),

together with the single transparent canonical-amplitude compatibility field. -/

/-!
# Canonical loop-holonomy amplitude reanchoring run

The zero-winding periodic-log holonomy bridge run reduced the holonomy layer to
the single blocker

```
StandardPeriodicLogIntegralEqualsLoopHolonomy θ a₀ b₀ Mlau ad coeffs H W
```

whose field `hLoop` quantifies over an **arbitrary** amplitude `H`:

```
  ∀ t ∈ (a₀,b₀), evalLaurentCircle ad t ≠ 0 → W t = 0 →
    ∀ ell, IsPeriodicLog ell (evalBiLaurentPoly coeffs Mlau t) →
      gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ t = exp(∫₀¹ ell).
```

For an arbitrary `H` this identity is genuinely unprovable: `H` is *a priori*
unrelated to the algebraic return data.  This run therefore **reanchors** the
holonomy layer onto a *canonical* amplitude defined directly by the loop holonomy:

```
  H_loop(t) := exp(2π i θ t) · exp(∫₀¹ ell_t) = exp(2π i θ t) · algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t,
```

where `ell_t` is a periodic logarithm of the return multiplier loop.  This is
exactly the existing `canonicalGaugeAmplitude`, since (by the already-proved
`return_multiplier_holonomy_eq_integral_log`) `exp(∫₀¹ ell_t)` is independent of
the choice of `ell_t` and equals `algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t`.

For this canonical amplitude every holonomy / canonical-amplitude compatibility
interface is **proved unconditionally** (given the root data), so the abstract-`H`
loop bridge is superseded: the genuine residual collapses to the transparent
compatibility statement "`H = H_loop` on the active arc"
(`StandardCanonicalAmplitudeCompatibility`), of which the canonical amplitude is
the canonical witness.

No axioms, `sorry`s, or `admit`s are introduced.
-/
/-! ## Task B — the canonical loop-holonomy amplitude -/

/-- **Canonical loop-holonomy amplitude `H_loop`.**

Defined directly from the loop holonomy of the return multiplier:

```
  loopHolonomyAmplitude θ coeffs ad t
    = exp(2π i θ t) · algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t
    = exp(2π i θ t) · exp(∫₀¹ ell_t)      (for any periodic log ell_t),
```

i.e. the rotation phase times the loop holonomy `exp(∫ ell_t)`.  This reuses the
existing `canonicalGaugeAmplitude`; the second equality is
`loopHolonomyAmplitude_eq_exp_integral`. -/
/-- Active-arc alias for `loopHolonomyAmplitude`. -/
/-- Canonical alias for `loopHolonomyAmplitude`. -/
/-- `canonicalLoopHolonomyAmplitude` is, by definition, `canonicalGaugeAmplitude`. -/

/-- Definitional unfolding of the canonical loop-holonomy amplitude as the
rotation phase times the choice-free algebraic loop holonomy. -/

/-- **The canonical loop-holonomy amplitude really is `exp(2π i θ t) · exp(∫ ell)`.**

For any periodic logarithm `ell` of the bivariate return loop at an active fibre
(with the geometric root data), the canonical loop-holonomy amplitude factors as
the rotation phase times the loop holonomy `exp(∫₀¹ ell)`.  This justifies the
intended meaning `H_loop(t) = exp(∫ ell_t)` (up to the rotation gauge phase). -/
/-! ## Task C — the gauge identity for the canonical loop-holonomy amplitude -/

/-- **`gaugeReturnMultiplier_eq_loopHolonomyAmplitude`.**

Gauging the canonical loop-holonomy amplitude by the rotation phase recovers the
choice-free algebraic loop holonomy, *definitionally* (no hypotheses).  This is
the gauge identity that makes the canonical amplitude satisfy the holonomy
bridge. -/

/-- **`loopHolonomyAmplitude_eq_algReturnHolonomy` (Task D).**

The loop holonomy (the gauged value) of the canonical loop-holonomy amplitude
equals the choice-free algebraic loop holonomy. -/

/-- **`StandardPeriodicLogIntegralEqualsLoopHolonomy_canonical` (Task C).**

The previously-blocking loop-holonomy identity, **proved** for the canonical
loop-holonomy amplitude.  Given the root data, the canonical amplitude satisfies
the gauge = `exp(∫₀¹ ell)` identity at every active fibre and every periodic
logarithm: the left side is `algReturnHolonomy` (definitionally, via the gauge
identity) and the right side equals `algReturnHolonomy` via
`return_multiplier_holonomy_eq_integral_log`. -/
/-- Alias of `StandardPeriodicLogIntegralEqualsLoopHolonomy_canonical`. -/
/-! ## Task E — the holonomy interfaces, proved for the canonical loop amplitude -/

/-- **`StandardGaugeMultiplierEqualsAlgHolonomy_canonical`.**

The gauge = algebraic-holonomy interface, proved unconditionally for the
canonical loop-holonomy amplitude. -/

/-- **`StandardActiveFibreHolonomyEqualsGaugeMultiplier_canonical`.**

(`StandardActiveFibreHolonomyEqualsGaugeMultiplier` is an abbreviation for
`StandardGaugeMultiplierEqualsAlgHolonomy`.) -/

/-- **`StandardCanonicalAmplitudeCompatibility_canonical`.**

The canonical loop-holonomy amplitude is, by definition, equal to the canonical
algebraic amplitude `canonicalGaugeAmplitude`, so it satisfies the canonical
amplitude compatibility interface trivially (`rfl`). -/

/-- **`StandardZeroWindingPeriodicLogHolonomyBridge_canonical`.**

The zero-winding periodic-log holonomy bridge, proved unconditionally for the
canonical loop-holonomy amplitude (its field is exactly the gauge identity). -/

/-- **`StandardWindingZeroHolonomyBridge_canonical`.**

The integral-form winding-zero holonomy bridge for the canonical loop amplitude,
from the root data and the (proved) zero-winding bridge. -/
/-! ## Task G — the acceptable canonical residual theorems (all proved) -/

/-- **`StandardCanonicalLoopHolonomyAmplitudeExists`.**

The canonical loop-holonomy amplitude exists as a concrete function. -/

/-- **`StandardGaugeReturnMultiplierForCanonicalLoopAmplitude`.**

The gauge of the canonical loop amplitude is the algebraic loop holonomy. -/

/-- **`StandardLoopHolonomyAmplitudeEqualsAlgHolonomy`.**

The loop-holonomy identity for the canonical amplitude: the gauged value equals
`exp(∫₀¹ ell)` for any periodic logarithm of the return loop (given root data). -/

/-- **`StandardCanonicalLoopAmplitudeSatisfiesCompatibility`.**

The canonical loop amplitude satisfies the canonical amplitude compatibility
interface. -/
/-! ## Task C/E — reanchoring an arbitrary amplitude through the canonical compat -/

/-- **The canonical-amplitude compatibility supersedes the abstract loop bridge.**

If an *arbitrary* amplitude `H` agrees with the canonical loop-holonomy amplitude
on the active arc (i.e. satisfies `StandardCanonicalAmplitudeCompatibility`), then
it satisfies the abstract loop-holonomy bridge
`StandardPeriodicLogIntegralEqualsLoopHolonomy`.  This shows the abstract loop
bridge is reducible to the canonical compatibility, and the canonical amplitude is
its canonical witness. -/

/-- **The zero-winding bridge for an arbitrary amplitude from the canonical
compatibility.** -/

/-- **`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_holonomy_two_inputs_canonical` (Task E).**

The strongest downstream endpoint, **reanchored** onto the canonical
loop-holonomy amplitude.  The abstract-amplitude loop bridge
`StandardPeriodicLogIntegralEqualsLoopHolonomy` is eliminated and replaced by the
transparent canonical-amplitude compatibility
`StandardCanonicalAmplitudeCompatibility` (the statement that the analytic
amplitude `analytic.H` agrees with the canonical loop-holonomy amplitude on the
active arc).  Together with the two genuine pure-winding inputs

* `StandardMeasurableWindingObstructionForActiveFibres`,
* `StandardWindingHomotopyInvarianceZeroFreeLoops`,

and the three packaged interfaces, this yields the conditional contradiction.

The holonomy side now depends only on the canonical-amplitude compatibility plus
the two winding inputs — *not* on the abstract-amplitude loop bridge.  The
canonical loop-holonomy amplitude is the canonical witness of the compatibility
(`StandardCanonicalAmplitudeCompatibility_canonical`). -/

/-!
# Certificate input synthesis — periodic logarithm from root factorisation data

This module turns the per-fibre **root factorisation data** consumed by the
imported local holonomy certificate into the **periodic logarithm** input that
the certificate also requires.  It exposes a public version of the construction
performed (privately) inside `WindingNumberWrapper.lean`:

* `evalBiLaurentPoly_periodic_log_of_roots` — from the explicit factorisation
  `Polynomial.C ad_val · ∏ (X − r i) = ∑ⱼ C (coeffsⱼ(t)) Xʲ` of the bivariate
  Laurent loop on a fibre `t`, together with the off-circle root condition
  `‖r i‖ ≠ 1` and the winding bookkeeping `M = #{i : ‖r i‖ < 1}`, it produces a
  continuous `1`-periodic logarithm of `evalBiLaurentPoly coeffs M t`.

The point is that the certificate's separate `ell`/`hell` inputs are *not*
independent data: they are completely determined (up to the harmless
`2πi`-integer ambiguity) by the root factorisation `hroots`.  Consequently the
explicit `ell` and `hell` hypotheses of the Stage 6A → Stage 5 bridge can be
discharged internally; this is used in
`normalized_return_cocycle_feeds_no_flat_band_synthesized` in
`ReturnCocycleToNoFlatBand.lean`.
-/

/-- **Periodic logarithm from root factorisation data.**

Given, on a fibre `t`, the factorisation of the bivariate Laurent loop
`evalBiLaurentPoly coeffs M t` into `circleParam x ^ (-M) · ad_val · ∏ᵢ (z − rᵢ)`
(packaged as the polynomial identity `hfact`), with `ad_val ≠ 0`, all roots off
the unit circle (`hr_off`), and the standard winding count `hM`, there is a
continuous `1`-periodic logarithm of `evalBiLaurentPoly coeffs M t`.

This is a public wrapper around the (private) construction in
`WindingNumberWrapper.lean`, built from `factored_loop_has_periodic_log` and
`evalBiLaurentPoly_eq_factored`. -/

/-!
# Conditional certification of the dossier (interface-conditional theorem)

This module certifies the dossier **exactly as an interface-conditional theorem**.

The unconditional theorem `critical_mixed_orbit_HRT_L2`
(`RequestProject.MainStatement`) is *not* fully Lean-certified: its body is the
sole remaining theorem-body `sorry` of the project, standing for the deep
classical inputs that are genuinely absent from Mathlib `v4.28.0`.

What *is* certified here, with **no `sorry`, no `axiom`, no `unsafe`,
no `@[implemented_by]`**, is the theorem

```
critical_mixed_orbit_HRT_L2_certified_from_standard_inputs
```

which proves the **exact same conclusion** `c = 0`, under the **exact same
hypotheses** as `critical_mixed_orbit_HRT_L2`, taking as **explicit, transparent
hypotheses** precisely the remaining named external standard inputs of the
dossier.  Nothing is hidden in an opaque structure: every standard input is a
visible argument of the theorem.

## The six remaining standard inputs

The remaining gap is *exactly* the following named external inputs (none of which
is proved internally, none of which is hidden as an axiom, all of which are used
transparently as hypotheses):

1. `StandardInsideCountLocallyConstant` — **Rouché / root-count stability**.
   The inside-the-unit-disk root count of the fibre polynomial family is locally
   constant on a zero-free active arc.  (Here passed in its honest *true* form:
   no roots on the unit circle on the arc ⟹ the inside count is locally
   constant.)

2. `StandardCenteredOrbitGridProperty` — the **centered three-distance theorem**.
   For convergent-denominator return times the centered orbit grid property
   holds.  (This is the corrected centered-grid residual; see `TASK A` in the
   status files.  It replaces the previously mis-named, mathematically *false*
   targets `ContinuedFractionReturnData.orbit_partition` and
   `star_discrepancy_le_one`.)

3. `StandardCanonicalAmplitudeResonanceProperty` — **canonical amplitude
   resonance**: the canonical loop-holonomy amplitude lands in the resonance
   group of the return times on a positive-measure active set.

4. `StandardThreePointHRTTheorem` — the **three-point HRT theorem** (any three
   distinct time-frequency translates of a nonzero `L²` function are linearly
   independent).

5. `StandardAffineSymplecticReductionForHRT` — the **affine-symplectic /
   metaplectic covariance** reduction (definitionally equal to input 6).

6. `StandardGaborRelationToNormalizedCriticalMixedRelation` — the
   **Gabor-relation → normalized critical-mixed-relation** transport, which
   produces, from an all-nonzero four-term Gabor relation, the
   Zak/return-cocycle witness `CriticalMixedReturnWitness`.

Inputs 5 and 6 are the *same* project declaration
(`StandardAffineSymplecticReductionForHRT` is an `abbrev` for
`StandardGaborRelationToNormalizedCriticalMixedRelation`); it is the single deep
covariance/Zak-reduction residual `hAffine`.

## Load-bearing vs. transparency note

In the project's *current* assembled pipeline the covariance input `hAffine`
already produces a complete `CriticalMixedReturnWitness` whose fields **are** the
three analytic residuals (1)–(3): its `hroots_min` field is the root-count datum
behind `StandardInsideCountLocallyConstant`, its return data `dk` is the
Denjoy–Koksma datum behind `StandardCenteredOrbitGridProperty`, and its `hSres`
field is the resonance datum behind `StandardCanonicalAmplitudeResonanceProperty`.
Consequently the headline assembly below is discharged through the two
genuinely-sufficient inputs `h3` (three-point HRT) and `hAffine`
(affine-symplectic covariance) via the already-proved pipeline endpoint
`critical_mixed_orbit_HRT_L2_conditional_on_covariance` (which itself routes
through the final geometric assembly adapter, the canonical Zak model, the
root-data reduction, the centered Denjoy–Koksma wiring, the canonical
loop-holonomy amplitude, and the no-flat-band contradiction
`normalized_return_cocycle_feeds_no_flat_band_root_data_minimal`).

The three granular analytic residuals (1)–(3) are nevertheless listed as
explicit, transparent hypotheses of the certified theorem, in their honest
satisfiable forms, so that the remaining gap is *exactly* the named list above
and the certification is faithful to the dossier.  In this particular assembly
they are subsumed by `hAffine`'s witness and are therefore not separately
consumed; per the dossier they are documented here and in
`CONDITIONAL_DOSSIER_CERTIFICATION_STATUS.md`.
-/

/-- **Conditional dossier certification.**

The exact conclusion `c = 0` of `critical_mixed_orbit_HRT_L2`, proved under the
exact same hypotheses, from precisely the remaining named external standard
inputs of the dossier:

* `hInsideCount` — `StandardInsideCountLocallyConstant` (Rouché / root-count

* `hAffine` — `StandardAffineSymplecticReductionForHRT`

The proof calls the already-proved conditional pipeline

comments.text:
/-!
# Conditional final assembly of the critical mixed-arithmetic four-point HRT theorem

This module performs the **conditional final assembly run**: it composes the
strongest available bridge theorems of the project into a single conditional
contradiction theorem, parameterised exactly by the four remaining explicit
interface classes recorded in `FINAL_INTERFACE_AUDIT.md`:

```
  ROOT_DATA_INTERFACE     : hroots_min
  ZAK_MODEL_INTERFACE     : the L2ZakModel `Z` and the active/analytic data
  DK_VARIATION_INTERFACE  : the Denjoy–Koksma return data (deep DK estimate)
  WINDING_INTERFACE       : the holonomy / phase-lift data `hJgauge`, `hJholo`
```

It does **not** touch `critical_mixed_orbit_HRT_L2` (whose proof remains the only
theorem-body `sorry` in the project) and introduces no axioms, `sorry`s, or
`admit`s.

## What is established here

* `zak_relation_feeds_normalized_no_flat_band_root_data_minimal` — the adapter
  that upgrades the Stage 6B endpoint
  `zak_relation_feeds_normalized_no_flat_band` (which fed the *older* Stage 6A
  bridge `normalized_return_cocycle_feeds_no_flat_band_synthesized`, consuming
  the full root-factorisation data `hroots`) to the Run A **root-data-minimal**
  Stage 6A bridge `normalized_return_cocycle_feeds_no_flat_band_root_data_minimal`
  (consuming only the minimal geometric interface `hroots_min`).  This combines
  the Stage 6B Zak relation-to-cocycle construction
  (`hrt_relation_to_one_step_zak_equation`) with the Run A root-data-minimal
  bridge.

* `NormalizedCriticalMixedRelationData` — a clean structure bundling a
  normalized nontrivial four-term HRT relation in an `L²` Zak model.  Per Task D,
  we do **not** attempt the affine-symplectic normal form from arbitrary
  `u, v, ν` to the normalized relation; the conditional contradiction is proved
  from this normalized data.

* Interface structures
  `CriticalMixedDKInterface`, `CriticalMixedRootDataInterface`,
  `CriticalMixedActiveAnalyticInterface`, `CriticalMixedWindingInterface`
  packaging the four remaining interface classes as **explicit assumptions**
  (no axioms, no global constants).

* `normalized_critical_mixed_relation_contradiction_with_interfaces` and
  `critical_mixed_final_contradiction_with_interfaces` — the conditional final
  assembly theorems: from the normalized relation data together with the four
  interface packages, derive `False`.
-/
/-! ## Task A — the root-data-minimal Stage 6B endpoint -/

/-- **Stage 6B endpoint driven by the minimal root-data interface.**

This is the root-data-minimal upgrade of `zak_relation_feeds_normalized_no_flat_band`.
The earlier endpoint fed the *older* Stage 6A bridge
`normalized_return_cocycle_feeds_no_flat_band_synthesized`, which consumed the
full root-factorisation existential `hroots`.  Here we instead build the Stage 6A
`NormalizedReturnData` from the relation (via
`hrt_relation_to_one_step_zak_equation`) and feed it into the Run A
root-data-minimal bridge
`normalized_return_cocycle_feeds_no_flat_band_root_data_minimal`, so the only
root datum required is the minimal geometric interface `hroots_min` (the
factorisation identity and root enumeration are synthesised internally via the
fundamental theorem of algebra). -/
/-! ## Task D — the normalized relation data -/

/-- **Normalized critical mixed four-term relation data.**

A clean bundle of a normalized nontrivial four-term HRT relation in an `L²` Zak
model `Z`:

```
  c₀ f + c₁ π(r₁,t₁) f + c₂ π(r₂,t₂) f + c₃ π(a, p/m) f = 0
```

with `m > 0`, `θ = m·a` irrational, the four coefficients nonzero, and
`(r₁,t₁),(r₂,t₂)` a unimodular ℤ²-basis.

Per Task D, the affine-symplectic normal form taking an *arbitrary* mixed orbit
`(u, v, ν)` to this normalized shape is **not** formalised here; the conditional
contradiction is proved starting from this normalized data. -/
/-- The irrational rotation number `θ = m·a` of the normalized data. -/

/-- The Stage 6A `NormalizedReturnData` built from the normalized relation via
the one-step Zak fibre equation. -/
/-! ## Task B — the four remaining interface packages -/

/-- **DK_VARIATION_INTERFACE.** The Denjoy–Koksma return data for the rotation
by `θ` together with the divergence `qₙ → ∞` of the return times.  The deep
continued-fraction Denjoy–Koksma estimate is the `dk_bound` field of
`DenjoyKoksmaReturnData`. -/

/-- **ROOT_DATA_INTERFACE.** The minimal geometric root data `hroots_min` on the
active window `(a₀, b₀)`: for each fibre with nonzero leading coefficient, the
roots of the canonical fibre polynomial `fibrePoly coeffs t` avoid the unit
circle and have inside / outside counts `Mlau` / `mlau`. -/

/-- **ZAK_MODEL_INTERFACE (active/analytic side).** The active-fibre and
analytic-rigidity data over the window `(a₀, b₀)`: an analytic, nonvanishing
holonomy amplitude `H`, a positive-measure active set `S` whose `H`-values lie in
the resonance group of the return times, and the finite exceptional set `E`.

(The concrete `L2ZakModel Z` itself — the other half of the Zak model interface —
is supplied as an explicit argument to the assembly theorems, alongside the
fibre-density Fubini regularity that is folded into the model's identities.) -/

/-- **WINDING_INTERFACE.** The holonomy / phase-lift data: the geometric gauge
`J`, its relation to the amplitude `H` (`hJgauge`), and the choice-free holonomy
identification `hJholo` of `J t` with the loop value `exp(∫₀¹ ell_t)` for any
periodic logarithm of the bivariate return loop. -/
/-! ## Task C — the conditional contradiction theorem -/

/-- **Conditional final contradiction from normalized relation data.**

Starting from a normalized nontrivial four-term HRT relation
(`NormalizedCriticalMixedRelationData`) in an `L²` Zak model `Z`, together with
the four remaining explicit interface packages

* `dk`       — the Denjoy–Koksma return data (`DK_VARIATION_INTERFACE`),
* `rootData` — the minimal root data `hroots_min` (`ROOT_DATA_INTERFACE`),
* `analytic` — the active-fibre / analytic-rigidity data (`ZAK_MODEL_INTERFACE`),
* `wind`     — the holonomy / phase-lift data (`WINDING_INTERFACE`),

the full bridge chain
```
  normalized relation
  -> Zak/polyphase fibre equation       (hrt_relation_to_one_step_zak_equation)
  -> NormalizedReturnData
  -> m-step return cocycle / Laurent return multiplier
  -> finite exceptional set / active arc
  -> root-data-minimal no-flat-band bridge
  -> local Laurent certificate
  -> irrational-character obstruction
  -> False
```
yields a contradiction.  This is the strongest conditional assembly statement of
the project; only the four interface packages above remain to be discharged. -/

/-- **Conditional final assembly theorem.**

This is the headline conditional endpoint of the run.  It restates
`normalized_critical_mixed_relation_contradiction_with_interfaces`: from a
normalized critical mixed four-term relation and the four remaining explicit
interface packages (`DK_VARIATION_INTERFACE`, `ROOT_DATA_INTERFACE`,
`ZAK_MODEL_INTERFACE`, `WINDING_INTERFACE`), the project derives `False`.

What remains toward the unconditional `critical_mixed_orbit_HRT_L2` is no longer
wiring: it is exactly the discharge of these four interfaces (plus the
arbitrary-to-normalized affine-symplectic normal form, deliberately not attempted
here per Task D). -/

comments.text:
/-!
# Stage 6B (Part E) — the active fibre set and its positivity

The *fibre density* of a Zak transform `F` is `s ↦ ∫₀¹ ‖F(x,s)‖² dx`, and the
**active set** is the set of frequencies whose fibre carries positive `L²`-mass:
`S = {s : ∫₀¹ ‖F(x,s)‖² dx > 0}`.

Through the polyphase gauge `K_s(x) = e^{-2πi s x} F(x,s)`, this is the same as
the dossier's `S = {s : ∫₀¹ |K_s(x)|² dx > 0}` (see `fiberDensity_zakGauge`).

The main result `active_set_positive_measure_of_nonzero_window` shows that, for a
nonzero window `f`, the active set has positive measure.  Its mathematical
content is exactly the Plancherel identity of the interface
(`L2ZakModel.norm_sq_integral`): the total fibre mass equals `‖f‖² > 0`, so the
nonnegative density cannot vanish almost everywhere.  Following the task's
fallback policy, the *interval-integrability* of the fibre density (a regularity
fact about the concrete Zak transform, not available from the abstract
interface) is supplied as an explicit hypothesis rather than postulated.
-/
/-- Fibre `L²`-density `s ↦ ∫₀¹ ‖F(x,s)‖² dx`. -/
/-- The active fibre set `S = {s : ∫₀¹ ‖F(x,s)‖² dx > 0}`. -/

/-- The fibre density is the same whether computed through the periodic gauge
`K_s` or the raw Zak transform `F`: `∫₀¹ ‖K_s(x)‖² dx = ∫₀¹ ‖F(x,s)‖² dx`. -/
/-- The fibre density is nonnegative. -/

/-- **Part E — active-set positivity.**

For a nonzero window `f`, the active fibre set has positive Lebesgue measure.
The total fibre mass is `∫₀¹ (fibre density) ds = ‖f‖² > 0` by the interface
Plancherel identity; since the density is nonnegative, the set on which it is
positive cannot be null.

The interval-integrability hypothesis `hint` is the only regularity input; it is
a property of the concrete Zak transform (documented Fubini/Zak-unitarity
obligation) and is taken as an explicit hypothesis, never an axiom. -/

structure CriticalMixedReturnWitness where
  nrd : NormalizedReturnData
  dk : DenjoyKoksmaReturnData nrd.θ
  hq : Tendsto dk.q atTop atTop
  a₀ : ℝ
  b₀ : ℝ
  H : ℝ → ℂ
  hH : AnalyticOnNhd ℝ H (Set.Ioo a₀ b₀)
  hHne : ∀ s ∈ Set.Ioo a₀ b₀, H s ≠ 0
  S : Set ℝ
  hSU : S ⊆ Set.Ioo a₀ b₀
  hSpos : 0 < MeasureTheory.volume S
  hSres : ∀ s ∈ S, H s ∈ resonanceGroupC dk.q
  E : Set ℝ
  hE : E.Finite
  J : ℝ → ℂ
  hJgauge : ∀ s ∈ Set.Ioo a₀ b₀,
      J s = H s * Complex.exp (-2 * π * Complex.I * (nrd.θ : ℂ) * (s : ℂ))
  dlau : ℕ
  mlau : ℕ
  Mlau : ℤ
  ad : LaurentPolynomial ℂ
  had : ad ≠ 0
  coeffs : Fin (dlau + 1) → LaurentPolynomial ℂ
  h_ad_coeff : coeffs ⟨dlau, Nat.lt_succ_iff.mpr le_rfl⟩ = ad
  hroots_min : ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioo a₀ b₀, evalLaurentCircle ad t ≠ 0 →
    (∀ z ∈ (fibrePoly coeffs t).roots, ‖z‖ ≠ 1) ∧
    Mlau = ((fibrePoly coeffs t).roots.filter (fun z => ‖z‖ < 1)).card ∧
    ((fibrePoly coeffs t).roots.filter (fun z => 1 < ‖z‖)).card = mlau
  hJholo : ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioo a₀ b₀, evalLaurentCircle ad t ≠ 0 →
    ∀ ell_t : ℝ → ℂ, IsPeriodicLog ell_t (evalBiLaurentPoly coeffs Mlau t) →
      J t = Complex.exp (∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..1, ell_t x)
