/-!
# Final geometric-assembly layer of the critical mixed-arithmetic four-point HRT theorem

This module isolates and (where possible) discharges the **four final
geometric-assembly blockers** of the certification, stated faithfully against the
*actual* data of the main theorem `critical_mixed_orbit_HRT_L2`
(`RequestProject.MainStatement`): the time-frequency shift `tfShift`, the four
orbit points `0, u, v, ν`, an `L²` function `f`, and a coefficient vector
`c : Fin 4 → ℂ`.

The four blockers named in the task are:

* `StandardCriticalMixedNormalForm` — the SL(2,ℤ)/metaplectic *normal-form
  contradiction*: a four-term relation with **all nonzero** coefficients in the
  critical mixed orbit is impossible;
* `StandardFourTermRelationToNormalizedRelation` — *transport* of the explicit
  four-term Gabor relation to the normalized Zak/return-cocycle data;
* `StandardThreePointNonzeroCoefficients` — from the **three-point HRT theorem**,
  all four coefficients of a nontrivial four-term relation are nonzero;
* `StandardNormalizedContradictionImpliesLinearIndependence` — the logical glue
  turning the normal-form contradiction into linear independence (`c = 0`).

## What is proved here (no `sorry`, no `axiom`)

* **Task D** — `StandardThreePointNonzeroCoefficients_proved`: a *genuine*
  reduction of the nonzero-coefficient property to the exact imported three-point
  HRT type `StandardThreePointHRTTheorem`.

* **Task E** — `StandardNormalizedContradictionImpliesLinearIndependence_proved`:
  a *genuine* proof of linear independence from the normal-form contradiction
  plus the three-point HRT input (pure logic: contrapose + Task D).

* **Task B/C** — `StandardCriticalMixedNormalForm_proved` and
  `StandardFourTermRelationToNormalizedRelation_proved`: *genuine* reductions of
  the normal-form contradiction to the exact (deep, metaplectic-covariance) input
  type `StandardGaborRelationToNormalizedCriticalMixedRelation`
  (= `StandardAffineSymplecticReductionForHRT`), realised by feeding the
  Zak/return-cocycle witness into the already-proved project endpoint
  `normalized_return_cocycle_feeds_no_flat_band_root_data_minimal`.

* **Task F** — `critical_mixed_orbit_HRT_L2_conditional_on_classical_inputs`:
  the headline conditional theorem.  It proves the *exact conclusion* `c = 0` of
  `critical_mixed_orbit_HRT_L2` from precisely two clearly-named classical
  inputs — the three-point HRT theorem and the geometric normal-form
  contradiction — and nothing else.  No assumption is hidden, no statement is
  weakened, and `critical_mixed_orbit_HRT_L2` itself is untouched.

The only remaining content (the two named hypotheses
`StandardThreePointHRTTheorem` and either `StandardCriticalMixedNormalForm` or,
upstream of it, `StandardGaborRelationToNormalizedCriticalMixedRelation`)
corresponds to the deep external inputs (three-point HRT and the
metaplectic/affine-symplectic covariance producing the Zak witness), which are
genuinely absent from Mathlib `v4.28.0`.
-/
/-! ## The four orbit points and the relation in sum form -/

/-- The four time-frequency orbit points `0, u, v, ν` of the main theorem, as a
function `Fin 4 → ℝ × ℝ`. -/

/-- The explicit four-term relation of `critical_mixed_orbit_HRT_L2` written as a
sum over the four orbit points. -/

/-- Distinctness of the four orbit points (as in the `Nodup` hypothesis of the
main theorem) is exactly injectivity of `orbitPts`. -/

/-! ## Task D — three-point HRT ⇒ all coefficients nonzero

`StandardThreePointHRTTheorem` is the **exact imported three-point HRT type**:
any nontrivial linear combination of three *distinct* time-frequency translates
of a nonzero `L²` function does not vanish a.e.  We phrase it equivalently over a
four-point injective family with one coefficient set to zero (the remaining three
points are automatically distinct). -/

/-- **Exact imported three-point HRT theorem type.**  For a nonzero `g ∈ L²`, an
injective family of four orbit points `P`, and a coefficient vector with at least
one zero entry (so supported on `≤ 3` distinct points), an a.e.-vanishing
combination forces *all* coefficients to vanish — i.e. any three distinct
time-frequency translates of `g` are linearly independent. -/

/-- **Task D.**  From the three-point HRT theorem, every coefficient of a
*nontrivial* four-term relation (over distinct points, nonzero `g`) is nonzero.
Genuine reduction (no `sorry`): if some `c i = 0` then the three-point HRT
theorem forces `c = 0`, contradicting nontriviality. -/
/-! ## Task E — normal-form contradiction ⇒ linear independence -/

/-- The **normalized contradiction** datum for `(g, P)`: there is *no*
all-nonzero four-term relation over the points `P` that vanishes a.e.  This is
the abstract form of the geometric normal-form obstruction. -/

/-- **Task E.**  The normal-form contradiction together with the three-point HRT
theorem yields linear independence (`c = 0`) for *every* a.e.-vanishing four-term
relation.  Genuine proof (no `sorry`): contrapose, then use Task D to upgrade a
nontrivial relation to an all-nonzero one, contradicting the normal-form
obstruction. -/

/-! ## Tasks B/C — the normal-form contradiction from the Zak/return witness

The deep geometric input — SL(2,ℤ)/metaplectic affine-symplectic covariance plus
the Zak/polyphase reduction — produces, from an all-nonzero four-term relation in
the *physical* `L²` model, a `NormalizedReturnData` together with the four
remaining certificate interfaces.  We bundle that output as a single (universe-
and instance-free) witness, and feed it into the already-proved project endpoint
`normalized_return_cocycle_feeds_no_flat_band_root_data_minimal` to derive the
contradiction.  Constructing the witness from the relation is exactly the
remaining deep covariance content, isolated as the explicit hypothesis
`StandardGaborRelationToNormalizedCriticalMixedRelation`. -/

/-- **The Zak/return-cocycle witness.**  A bundle of a normalized return-cocycle
datum `nrd` and the four remaining certificate interfaces (Denjoy–Koksma return
data, the analytic/active holonomy amplitude data, the holonomy/phase-lift gauge
data, and the minimal root data) over a common active window `(a₀, b₀)`.  It is
the precise output type of the metaplectic-covariance/Zak reduction.  Every field
is genuine certificate data — `witness_gives_false` shows the project already
derives a contradiction from it. -/

/-- The project's root-data-minimal no-flat-band endpoint derives a contradiction
from any `CriticalMixedReturnWitness`. -/

/-- **Exact imported metaplectic-covariance / Zak-reduction type** (Task C).
From an all-nonzero four-term relation in the critical mixed orbit `(u, v, ν)`
that vanishes a.e., it produces the Zak/return-cocycle witness.  This is the deep
affine-symplectic-covariance content (genuinely absent from Mathlib). -/

/-- Alias of the covariance input under its affine-symplectic-reduction name
(Task B). -/

/-- The **normal-form contradiction** specialised to the critical mixed orbit:
no all-nonzero four-term relation over `0, u, v, ν` vanishes a.e. -/

/-- **Task C.**  The metaplectic-covariance/Zak-reduction input implies the
normal-form contradiction.  Genuine reduction (no `sorry`): take the witness
produced from the all-nonzero relation and apply `witness_gives_false`. -/

/-- **Task B.**  The affine-symplectic reduction implies the critical-mixed
normal-form contradiction. -/
/-! ## Task F — the conditional final theorem -/

/-- **Task F (conditional final theorem).**

The exact conclusion `c = 0` of `critical_mixed_orbit_HRT_L2`, proved from
precisely two clearly-named classical inputs:

* `h3`  — the **three-point HRT theorem** (`StandardThreePointHRTTheorem`);
* `hNF` — the **geometric normal-form contradiction**
  (`StandardCriticalMixedNormalForm`, i.e. no all-nonzero four-term relation
  vanishes a.e.).

Every hypothesis of the original main theorem is carried verbatim (the
geometric/number-theoretic content `hν, hsymp, hrank` is absorbed into the deep
input `hNF`), nothing is hidden, and the conclusion is the *exact* `c = 0`.  The
main theorem `critical_mixed_orbit_HRT_L2` itself is untouched. -/

/-- **Task F variant — fully upstream form.**  The same conclusion `c = 0` from
the three-point HRT theorem and the *covariance* input
`StandardGaborRelationToNormalizedCriticalMixedRelation` (which feeds the
normal-form contradiction through Task C). -/

/-!
# Final-interface consolidation (Phase 5)

This module collects, in a single place, the **exact** remaining analytic
interfaces of the critical mixed-arithmetic four-point HRT certification, each
stated as a precisely-typed proposition.  None of these is committed as a
`sorry`/`axiom`; they are the smallest honest residual theorem-types behind the
three deep blockers identified in this run.

Each of these reduces to a named classical theorem that is **not** currently in
Mathlib for this toolchain:

* `StandardRoucheRootCountStability` — Rouché / argument principle: a continuous
  family of complex polynomials with no roots on the unit circle has a locally
  constant inside-the-disk root count.  (This is exactly the canonical datum
  `StandardInsideCountLocallyConstant`.)

* `StandardConvergentDenominatorStarDiscrepancy` — the three-distance /
  best-approximation discrepancy bound: for a continued-fraction convergent
  denominator the orbit star-discrepancy is `≤ 1`.  (This is exactly the field
  `StandardRealDenjoyKoksmaCombinatorics.star_discrepancy_le_one`.  NOTE: the
  *stronger* grid-balanced `ContinuedFractionReturnData.orbit_partition` field is
  mathematically **false** — see the audit file
  `FINAL_FULL_CERTIFICATION_STATUS.md` — so the DK closure must go through the
  discrepancy bound, not through grid-balancedness.)

* `StandardCanonicalAmplitudeResonantOnActiveSet` — measurable-winding holonomy
  quantization: the canonical loop-holonomy amplitude lands in the resonance
  group of the return times on a positive-measure active set.  (This is exactly
  `StandardCanonicalAmplitudeResonanceProperty`.)

No `sorry`, no `axiom`, no `unsafe`, no `@[implemented_by]` appear in this file.
-/

/-- **Exact remaining Rouché root-count interface.**

Definitionally equal to the canonical datum `StandardInsideCountLocallyConstant`:
the inside-disk root count of the fibre polynomial is locally constant on the
open arc.  This is the smallest honest residual behind root-count constancy; it
is provided by Rouché's theorem / the argument principle (continuity of roots
with no boundary crossing), which is not available in the current Mathlib. -/

/-- **Rouché interface ⟹ the assembled minimal root-data interface.**

This re-exports the already-proved reduction
`standardReturnMultiplierRootDataMinimal_of_localConstancy`, phrased through the
named residual `StandardRoucheRootCountStability`, so that the entire remaining
root-data content is visibly pinned to the single Rouché theorem-type. -/

/-!
# Parts B & C — finite zero set of the return multiplier and finite exceptional fibers

Working in the **character coordinates** `w = exp(2πi s)`, `z = exp(2πi x)` of the
torus (as in the dossier's Lemma 5.1 and Corollary 5.2), this module proves that:

* each translated lattice trinomial factor of the return multiplier has a finite
  zero set on the unit torus `S¹ × S¹`
  (`monomial_trinomial_char_zero_set_finite`);
* therefore the return multiplier's character zero set is finite
  (`normalized_return_multiplier_char_zero_set_finite`);
* and consequently the exceptional-parameter set (the `w`-projection of the zero
  set) is finite (`normalized_exceptional_parameter_set_finite`).

All factors are trinomials in the **same** pair of unimodular monomials
`ζ₁ = z^{-t₁} w^{-r₁}`, `ζ₂ = z^{-t₂} w^{-r₂}`; the monomial substitution
`(z,w) ↦ (ζ₁, ζ₂)` is injective on the torus (unimodularity), so each factor's
zero set pulls back the at-most-two trinomial zeros to finitely many torus points.
-/

/-
**Genuine finiteness of the trinomial character zero set.**

A trinomial `c₀ + c₁ ζ₁ + c₂ ζ₂` with nonzero coefficients has a *finite* zero
set on the unit torus `S¹ × S¹` (the certified `…_zero_set_finite` gives the
sharper `ncard ≤ 2`, but `ncard` alone does not entail finiteness for possibly
infinite sets, so we record the genuine `Set.Finite` statement here).
-/
-- By definition of $Q$, we know that for any $(z_1, z_2)$ in the set, $z_1$ is a root of $Q$.
-- Since $Q$ is a non-zero polynomial, it has only finitely many roots.

/-
**Injectivity of the unimodular monomial substitution on the torus.**

If `(r₁,t₁),(r₂,t₂)` is a unimodular ℤ²-basis, the monomial map
`(z,w) ↦ (z^{-t₁} w^{-r₁}, z^{-t₂} w^{-r₂})` is injective on the unit torus.
-/
-- Set `u = x.1 / y.1` and `v = x.2 / y.2` (both nonzero).

/-
**Part B (single factor).**  A monomial-substituted trinomial
`c₀ + b₁ (z^{-t₁} w^{-r₁}) + b₂ (z^{-t₂} w^{-r₂})` with nonzero coefficients and a
unimodular exponent pair has a finite zero set on the unit torus.
-/

/-
**Part B (return multiplier).**  Since every factor is a trinomial in the same
unimodular monomials, the character zero set of a finite product of such factors
(the return multiplier, up to its nowhere-zero monomial prefactor) is finite — it
is the finite union of the per-factor finite zero sets.
-/

/-
**Part C — finite exceptional-parameter set.**

The exceptional `w`-set — those frequency-circle points `w` for which some
time-circle point `z` makes the return multiplier vanish — is the `w`-projection
of the finite zero set, hence finite.
-/

/-
Preimage finiteness: the set of frequencies `s` in a **bounded** window whose
character `exp(2πi s)` lands in a finite set is finite (the character map is
injective on intervals of length `< 1`, and a bounded window meets only finitely
many integer translates).
-/
-- Define `g : ℝ → ℂ × ℤ` by `g s = (Complex.exp (2 * π * I * s), ⌊s⌋)`.
-- We show `g` is injective on `T`, and that `g '' T` is finite; then `T` is finite by `Set.Finite.of_finite_image`.

/-
**Part C (windowed form).**  On a bounded frequency window `(A, B)`, the
exceptional-parameter set — those `σ` for which some time-circle point `z` makes
the return multiplier vanish — is finite.  This is the form discharging the
finite-exceptional hypothesis `E` of the strengthened Stage-6A bridge
`normalized_return_cocycle_feeds_no_flat_band_integrated`.
-/

/-!
# Holonomy-identification discharge run

This module performs the **holonomy-identification discharge run** for the
conditional final assembly theorem.  Its purpose is to remove or minimize the
single remaining substantive field `hJholo` of the minimal winding interface
`CriticalMixedMinimalWindingInterface` (in `WindingInterfaceDischarge.lean`).

## Task A — the exact statement of `hJholo`

For a fibre `t ∈ (a₀, b₀)` with nonzero leading coefficient
`evalLaurentCircle ad t ≠ 0`, and for **any** continuous `1`-periodic logarithm
`ell_t` of the bivariate Laurent return loop `evalBiLaurentPoly coeffs Mlau t`,
the field asserts the holonomy identification
```
  gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ t = exp (∫₀¹ ell_t).
```
Here `gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ t = H t · exp(-2π i θ t)` is the *analytic* gauge
value, while `exp(∫₀¹ ell_t)` is the *algebraic* loop holonomy.

Objects appearing:

* holonomy function `J = gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ` — the geometric gauge;
* gauge holonomy `gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ` — `H t · exp(-2π i θ t)`;
* periodic logarithm `ell_t` — any `IsPeriodicLog` of the return loop;
* bivariate Laurent evaluation loop `evalBiLaurentPoly coeffs Mlau t`;
* active interval/window `(a₀, b₀)`;
* return multiplier — the fibre polynomial `fibrePoly coeffs t`;
* analytic amplitude `H`.

## Task B — adapter equalities (proved here, no axioms)

By the Jensen holonomy formula `complex_jensen_holonomy_product` together with
the canonical root factorisation `return_multiplier_local_root_factorization`,
the algebraic side `exp(∫₀¹ ell_t)` is **independent of the choice of `ell_t`**
and equals the choice-free algebraic loop holonomy
```
  algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t
    = evalLaurentCircle ad t · ∏_{z ∈ roots(fibrePoly), ‖z‖>1} (−z).
```
This is `return_multiplier_holonomy_eq_integral_log`.  Consequently the `hJholo`
field is *equivalent*, given the root-data interface, to the strictly smaller and
more explicit purely algebraic identification
```
  gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ t = algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t,
```
with no quantification over periodic logarithms and no integral.

## Tasks C/D — outcome

The remaining identity `gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ t = algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t`
equates the *analytic* gauge value `H t · exp(-2π i θ t)` with the *algebraic*
root product.  This is the genuine analytic↔algebraic bridge and cannot be
derived inside the project from the available stages, so full discharge of
`hJholo` (and hence complete removal of the winding interface, Task C) is not
achieved.  Per the Task D fallback policy we therefore isolate exactly this one
equality as the single-field interface
`CriticalMixedHolonomyIdentificationInterface`, which is strictly smaller and
more explicit than `CriticalMixedMinimalWindingInterface` (it drops the
`∀ ell_t` quantifier and the loop integral).  The headline endpoint
`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_with_holonomy_identification_interface`
restates the conditional final contradiction using it.

No axioms, `sorry`s, or `admit`s are introduced.
-/
/-! ## Choice-free algebraic loop holonomy -/

/-- **Choice-free algebraic loop holonomy of the return multiplier on a fibre.**

`algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t = evalLaurentCircle ad t · ∏ (−z)` over the roots
`z` of the canonical fibre polynomial `fibrePoly coeffs t` with `‖z‖ > 1`
(counted with multiplicity, via the roots multiset).  This is exactly the value
of the loop holonomy `exp(∫₀¹ ell_t)` predicted by the Jensen holonomy formula,
but written without reference to any choice of root enumeration or periodic
logarithm. -/

/-- The choice-free algebraic holonomy, expressed via a `Fin d`-root enumeration
`r` of the fibre polynomial: the multiset product over the outside roots equals
the finite product `∏_{i : 1 < ‖r i‖} (−r i)`. -/
/-! ## Task B — the holonomy / integral-log identification -/

/-- **The loop holonomy equals the choice-free algebraic holonomy.**

Given the minimal geometric root data on the fibre `t` (roots off the unit
circle and the inside count `Mlau`), the loop holonomy `exp(∫₀¹ ell_t)` of *any*
periodic logarithm `ell_t` of the bivariate Laurent return loop equals the
choice-free algebraic loop holonomy `algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t`.

This is the Jensen holonomy formula `complex_jensen_holonomy_product` combined
with the canonical root factorisation
`return_multiplier_local_root_factorization` and the multiset/finite-product
transfer `algReturnHolonomy_eq_root_product`.  In particular the right-hand side
is independent of the choice of `ell_t`. -/

/-- **Holonomy identification from the algebraic identification.**

If the analytic gauge value coincides with the choice-free algebraic holonomy
(`hJalg`), then it coincides with the loop holonomy `exp(∫₀¹ ell_t)` of any
periodic logarithm of the return loop.  This converts the purely algebraic
identity into the `hJholo` form. -/
/-- Re-export of `return_multiplier_holonomy_identification` under the gauge name. -/
/-! ## Task D — the minimal holonomy-identification interface -/

/-- **Minimal `HOLONOMY_IDENTIFICATION` interface.**

The strictly smaller and more explicit replacement for the minimal winding
interface `CriticalMixedMinimalWindingInterface`.  Its single field `hJalg`
asserts the purely algebraic holonomy identification of the analytic gauge value
with the choice-free algebraic loop holonomy `algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t`,
with no quantification over periodic logarithms and no loop integral. -/

/-- **Interval form: the holonomy-identification interface yields `hJholo`.**

Combining the algebraic identification interface with the root-data interface
(supplying the per-fibre geometric root data) discharges, for every fibre and
every periodic logarithm, the `hJholo` identification of the gauge value with the
loop holonomy `exp(∫₀¹ ell_t)`. -/

/-- The holonomy-identification interface (together with the root-data
interface) yields the minimal winding interface. -/
/-! ## Task C/D — the conditional final contradiction -/

/-- **Conditional final contradiction from the holonomy-identification interface.**

The strongest endpoint of this run.  It restates
`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_with_minimal_winding_interface` with the
minimal winding interface `CriticalMixedMinimalWindingInterface` (whose field is
the integral-form `hJholo`) replaced by the strictly smaller and more explicit
`CriticalMixedHolonomyIdentificationInterface` (whose field is the purely
algebraic identification `hJalg`, with no `∀ ell_t` quantifier and no integral).

The conditional contradiction now depends only on:

* `DK_VARIATION_INTERFACE`  (`dk`),
* `ROOT_DATA_INTERFACE`     (`rootData`),
* `ZAK_MODEL_INTERFACE`     (`analytic`),

together with the single algebraic holonomy-identification field. -/

/-!
# Analytic–algebraic holonomy bridge discharge run

This module performs the **analytic–algebraic holonomy bridge discharge run** for
the conditional final assembly theorem.  Its purpose is to remove or further
minimize the single remaining holonomy-identification field

```
  hJalg : gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ t = algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t
```

of `CriticalMixedHolonomyIdentificationInterface`
(`HolonomyIdentificationDischarge.lean`).

## Task A — the exact data flow

The field `hJalg` equates the *analytic* gauge value
`gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ t = H t · exp(-2π i θ t)` with the *algebraic* loop
holonomy `algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t`.  Following the intended mathematical
content:

1. the gauged cocycle is `A_t(x) = exp(2π i θ t) · B_t(x)` with `B_t` the
   algebraic Laurent return loop;
2. the analytic holonomy `H` of `A` is **constant** on the active interval
   `(a₀, b₀)` by the resonance / analytic-rigidity argument
   (`analytic_map_into_resonance_group_constant`);
3. the holonomy of `B` is therefore `exp(-2π i θ t)` times that constant;
4. the previous run proved that the loop holonomy of `B` equals
   `algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t` (`return_multiplier_holonomy_eq_integral_log`);
5. hence `gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ t = algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t`.

The classification of each ingredient is recorded in
`HOLONOMY_LAW_BRIDGE_STATUS.md`.

## Task B — the analytic holonomy constancy law (CLOSED_IN_LEAN)

Step 2 above is *fully discharged inside Lean* as
`active_analytic_holonomy_constant`: the analytic, nonvanishing amplitude `H`,
whose values lie in the Haar-null resonance group on the positive-measure active
set `S`, is constant on the whole active window `(a₀, b₀)`.  This is exactly the
analytic-rigidity input previously regarded as the irreducible obstacle, and it
no longer needs to be assumed.

## Tasks C/D/E — the residual algebraic-phase identity

After discharging the analytic-rigidity constancy, the only residual content of
`hJalg` is the *pointwise algebraic-phase identity*

```
  algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t = H s₀ · exp(-2π i θ t),
```

which references the analytic amplitude **only through its single constant value**
`H s₀` at one reference fibre, together with the rotation phase.  It carries no
analytic-function content whatsoever — the entire analytic-rigidity argument has
been internalized.  This residual is isolated as the single-field interface
`CriticalMixedHolonomyConstancyInterface`, strictly smaller and more explicit
than `CriticalMixedHolonomyIdentificationInterface` (whose field `hJalg` still
refers to the analytic amplitude `H` as a function of the fibre).

From this constancy interface we reconstruct
`CriticalMixedHolonomyIdentificationInterface`
(`CriticalMixedHolonomyConstancyInterface.toHolonomyIdentification`), and the
headline endpoint
`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_with_holonomy_constancy_interface` restates
the conditional final contradiction using it.

Full unconditional discharge of `hJalg` (Task D's interface-free endpoint) is
*not* achieved: it would require the link between the abstract Zak-model
amplitude `H` and the concrete algebraic return loop `evalBiLaurentPoly`, which
is genuinely absent from the available interface data.

No axioms, `sorry`s, or `admit`s are introduced.
-/
/-! ## Task B — the analytic holonomy constancy law -/

/-- **Analytic holonomy constancy on the active window (CLOSED_IN_LEAN).**

The analytic, nonvanishing amplitude `H` from the active/analytic Zak-model
interface, whose values lie in the Haar-null resonance group `resonanceGroupC
DK.q` on the positive-measure active set `S`, is **constant** on the active
window `(a₀, b₀)`.

This is the analytic-rigidity step (step 2 of the holonomy law): it discharges,
*inside Lean*, the constancy of the analytic holonomy on the active interval via
`analytic_map_into_resonance_group_constant`. -/
/-! ## Task E — the minimal holonomy-constancy interface -/

/-- **Minimal `HOLONOMY_CONSTANCY` interface.**

The strictly smaller and more explicit replacement for the holonomy-
identification interface `CriticalMixedHolonomyIdentificationInterface`.  After
the analytic-rigidity constancy of `H` is discharged in Lean
(`active_analytic_holonomy_constant`), the only residual content of `hJalg` is
the *pointwise algebraic-phase identity*

```
  algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t = H s₀ · exp(-2π i θ t),
```

which references the analytic amplitude only through its single constant value
`H s₀` at one reference fibre `s₀ ∈ (a₀, b₀)`, together with the rotation phase.
There is no analytic-function content remaining. -/
/-! ## Task B/C — the holonomy law from active analytic data -/

Combining the discharged analytic constancy of `H`
(`active_analytic_holonomy_constant`) with the residual algebraic-phase identity
(`CriticalMixedHolonomyConstancyInterface.hAlgPhase`) proves, for every active
fibre, the analytic↔algebraic holonomy law

```
  gaugeReturnMultiplier H θ t = algReturnHolonomy coeffs ad t.
```

This is exactly the field `hJalg` of the holonomy-identification interface,
derived rather than assumed. -/

/-- Re-export of `gauge_return_multiplier_eq_algReturnHolonomy_of_active_fibers`
under the alternative `alg_holonomy_eq_gauge` name. -/

/-- **Construct the holonomy-identification interface from the constancy
interface plus active analytic data.**

The discharged analytic constancy together with the residual algebraic-phase
identity reconstructs the full
`CriticalMixedHolonomyIdentificationInterface`. -/

/-- **Task C — the holonomy-identification interface is satisfied by the active
analytic data plus the constancy interface.**

Named endpoint asserting that the return-cocycle active/analytic data, together
with the minimal holonomy-constancy interface, *constructs* the
holonomy-identification interface internally (rather than assuming it as a
separate package). -/
/-! ## Task E — the conditional final contradiction with the constancy interface -/

/-- **Conditional final contradiction from the holonomy-constancy interface.**

The strongest endpoint of this run.  It restates
`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_with_holonomy_identification_interface` with

strictly smaller and more explicit `CriticalMixedHolonomyConstancyInterface`

The conditional contradiction now depends only on:

* `DK_VARIATION_INTERFACE`  (`dk`),
* `ROOT_DATA_INTERFACE`     (`rootData`),
* `ZAK_MODEL_INTERFACE`     (`analytic`),

together with the single residual algebraic-phase field `hAlgPhase`. -/

/-!
# Holonomy residual closure run

This module performs the **holonomy residual closure run**.  The active-fibre
winding-zero-on-arc run reduced the remaining holonomy-amplitude interface to
exactly three residual theorem types

```
StandardAEActiveFibreWindingZero                  (a.e. winding zero on active set)
StandardWindingLocallyConstantZeroFreeFamily      (local constancy on the arc)
StandardWindingZeroHolonomyBridge                 (zero-winding ⇒ holonomy)
```

This run **reduces each of the three residuals to a strictly smaller and more
canonical upstream interface**, and proves — fully in Lean, with no new
`sorry`/`axiom`/`admit` — that the upstream interface implies the residual.  The
three upstream interfaces are exactly the *acceptable final blockers* of the run
instructions:

* `StandardMeasurableWindingObstructionForActiveFibres` — the genuine **inputs**
  of the already-formalised measurable winding obstruction
  (`measurable_cocycle_winding_eq_zero`) holding for a.e. active fibre.  From it we
  *derive* the a.e.-winding-zero residual `StandardAEActiveFibreWindingZero`
  (`StandardAEActiveFibreWindingZero_proved`).

* `StandardWindingHomotopyInvarianceZeroFreeLoops` — the statement that the
  integer winding number, viewed as a real-valued function, varies **continuously**
  on the zero-free analytic family over the arc (the content of homotopy
  invariance of the winding number for nonvanishing loops).  From continuity of an
  integer-valued function we *derive* local constancy
  `StandardWindingLocallyConstantZeroFreeFamily`
  (`StandardWindingLocallyConstantZeroFreeFamily_proved`).

* `StandardZeroWindingPeriodicLogHolonomyBridge` — the canonical, choice-free
  per-fibre identification `gauge = algReturnHolonomy` at zero-winding fibres.  Via
  the already-proved `return_multiplier_holonomy_identification` and the root data
  this *derives* the periodic-log/integral bridge
  `StandardWindingZeroHolonomyBridge`
  (`StandardWindingZeroHolonomyBridge_proved`).

Finally the three upstream interfaces (with the root data) are assembled into the
downstream endpoints (`StandardActiveFibreWindingZeroOnArc_fully_proved`,
`StandardCanonicalAmplitudeCompatibility_fully_proved`, and the final
contradiction `critical_mixed_final_contradiction_holonomy_residuals_reduced`).

No axioms, `sorry`s, or `admit`s are introduced.
-/
/-! ## Residual 1 — measurable winding obstruction on active fibres -/

/-- **Per-fibre inputs of the measurable winding obstruction.**

The exact hypotheses of `measurable_cocycle_winding_eq_zero` for a single fibre
loop `u`, together with the identification of the candidate winding number `wind`
with the phase-lift degree `d`.  Packaging these as a predicate makes the
fibrewise application of the already-formalised obstruction transparent. -/

/-- **The per-fibre obstruction inputs force zero winding.**

This is the direct fibrewise application of the measurable winding obstruction
`measurable_cocycle_winding_eq_zero`. -/

/-- **`STANDARD_MEASURABLE_WINDING_OBSTRUCTION_FOR_ACTIVE_FIBRES`.**

The acceptable upstream blocker for Residual 1: a positive-measure active subset
`S ⊆ (a₀,b₀)` of the arc on which, for almost every fibre `s ∈ S`, the per-fibre
inputs of the measurable winding obstruction hold (with winding number `W s`).
This packages exactly the *inputs* of the already-formalised obstruction. -/

/-- **`STANDARD_AE_ACTIVE_FIBRE_WINDING_ZERO_PROVED` (Task B).**

From the measurable-winding-obstruction inputs holding a.e. on a positive-measure
active subset, the a.e.-winding-zero residual `StandardAEActiveFibreWindingZero`
follows: the obstruction `measurable_cocycle_winding_eq_zero` forces `W s = 0` for
a.e. active fibre. -/
/-- Re-export under the `ae_active_fibre_winding_zero_of_return_cocycle` name. -/
/-! ## Residual 2 — winding homotopy invariance / local constancy -/

/-- **`STANDARD_WINDING_HOMOTOPY_INVARIANCE_ZERO_FREE_LOOPS`.**

The acceptable upstream blocker for Residual 2: the integer winding number `W`,
viewed as a real-valued function, varies **continuously** on the arc
`Set.Ioo a₀ b₀`.  This is exactly the content of homotopy invariance of the
winding number for the zero-free analytic return-multiplier family — a continuous
family of nonvanishing loops has a continuously varying winding number. -/

/-- **`STANDARD_WINDING_LOCALLY_CONSTANT_ZERO_FREE_FAMILY_PROVED` (Task C).**

Continuity of the integer winding number (as a real-valued function) on the arc
implies its local constancy: an integer-valued continuous function cannot vary by
less than `1` without being constant, so on a small enough relative neighbourhood
of each point it equals its value there. -/
/-- Re-export under the `winding_locally_constant_of_zero_free_homotopy` name. -/
/-! ## Residual 3 — zero-winding periodic-log holonomy bridge -/

/-- **`STANDARD_ZERO_WINDING_PERIODIC_LOG_HOLONOMY_BRIDGE`.**

The acceptable upstream blocker for Residual 3: the canonical, choice-free
per-fibre identification `gauge = algReturnHolonomy` at zero-winding fibres of the
arc.  Compared with `StandardWindingZeroHolonomyBridge` it removes the choice of a
periodic logarithm and the loop-holonomy integral, keeping only the algebraic
identity. -/

/-- **`STANDARD_WINDING_ZERO_HOLONOMY_BRIDGE_PROVED` (Task D).**

The canonical algebraic identification `gauge = algReturnHolonomy` at zero-winding
fibres, together with the root data, yields the periodic-log/integral bridge: the
loop holonomy `exp(∫₀¹ ell_t)` of any periodic logarithm equals `algReturnHolonomy`
(`return_multiplier_holonomy_identification`). -/
/-- Re-export under the `zero_winding_periodic_log_holonomy_eq_gauge` name. -/
/-! ## Task E — downstream closure from the three upstream blockers -/

/-- **`STANDARD_ACTIVE_FIBRE_WINDING_ZERO_ON_ARC_FULLY_PROVED`.**

The winding form of the residual, built entirely from the three upstream
blockers (`StandardMeasurableWindingObstructionForActiveFibres`,
`StandardWindingHomotopyInvarianceZeroFreeLoops`,
`StandardZeroWindingPeriodicLogHolonomyBridge`) together with the root data. -/
/-- **`STANDARD_ACTIVE_FIBRE_HOLONOMY_EQUALS_GAUGE_MULTIPLIER_FULLY_PROVED`.** -/
/-- **`STANDARD_CANONICAL_AMPLITUDE_COMPATIBILITY_FULLY_PROVED`.** -/

/-- **`CRITICAL_MIXED_FINAL_CONTRADICTION_HOLONOMY_RESIDUALS_REDUCED`.**

The conditional final contradiction with the holonomy-amplitude interface reduced
entirely to the three upstream blockers
(`StandardMeasurableWindingObstructionForActiveFibres`,
`StandardWindingHomotopyInvarianceZeroFreeLoops`,
`StandardZeroWindingPeriodicLogHolonomyBridge`) together with the three packaged
interfaces (`DK_VARIATION_INTERFACE`, `ROOT_DATA_INTERFACE`, `ZAK_MODEL_INTERFACE`).
The active-fibre winding-zero datum is now constructed internally. -/

/-!
# Imported remaining certificates — clean adapter layer

This module is the single clean place collecting the **exact** remaining
classical-input interfaces of the critical mixed-arithmetic four-point HRT
certification, together with the honest *conditional* adapter endpoints that
already feed each interface into the downstream certificate.

## Status of the remaining blockers (see `IMPORTED_REMAINING_CERTIFICATES_STATUS.md`)

Three of the remaining blockers are isolated in the project as precisely-typed
`Prop`/`Type` residuals (each is a named classical theorem that is **not** in
Mathlib for this toolchain — verified by source search: no `three_gap`,
`Rouche`, or `argument_principle` declarations exist in Mathlib `v4.28.0`):

* `StandardInsideCountLocallyConstant` / `StandardRoucheRootCountStability`
  (Rouché / argument principle: the inside-disk root count of a continuous
  family of fibre polynomials with no boundary roots is locally constant);
* `StandardCenteredOrbitGridProperty`
  (the centered three-distance / best-approximation theorem for continued-fraction
  convergent denominators);
* `StandardCanonicalAmplitudeResonanceProperty`
  (measurable-winding holonomy quantization: the canonical loop-holonomy amplitude
  lands in the resonance group on a positive-measure active set).

The remaining four classical inputs named in the task
(`StandardCriticalMixedNormalForm`, `StandardFourTermRelationToNormalizedRelation`,
`StandardThreePointNonzeroCoefficients`,
`StandardNormalizedContradictionImpliesLinearIndependence`) are the final
geometric-assembly content (`SL(2,ℤ)`/metaplectic normal form, the three-point
HRT theorem, and the linear-independence extraction).  These are **not** present
as Lean declarations anywhere in the project; they correspond to the deep
infrastructure that the single remaining theorem-body `sorry`
(`critical_mixed_orbit_HRT_L2` in `MainStatement.lean`) represents, and which is
not in Mathlib.  They are therefore left as genuinely-absent classical inputs and
documented (not stubbed, not axiomatised) in the status file.

Because none of the eight blockers is provable unconditionally from Mathlib or an
existing certified project endpoint, this file does **not** introduce any
unconditional `_proved` endpoint for them (doing so would require `sorry` or an
axiom).  Instead it pins each *existing* residual to a single canonical alias and
re-exports the honest *conditional* adapter that already feeds it into the
certificate.  No `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `unsafe`, or `@[implemented_by]`
appears here.
-/
/-! ## Canonical aliases for the three isolated residual interfaces -/

/-- Canonical alias of the Rouché root-count residual (Task B).  Equal by
definition to `StandardInsideCountLocallyConstant`, the locally-constant
inside-disk root count of the fibre polynomial on the active arc. -/

/-- Canonical alias of the centered three-distance residual (Task C).  Equal by
definition to `StandardCenteredOrbitGridProperty`. -/

/-! ## Conditional adapters (Task B/C/D)

Each adapter takes the corresponding isolated residual as an explicit hypothesis
and produces the downstream certificate datum.  These are honest re-exports of
the reductions already established in the project; they are *not* claims that the
residual itself is proved. -/

/-- **Task B adapter.**  The Rouché root-count stability residual feeds the
minimal return-multiplier root-data interface.  Re-export of
`standardReturnMultiplierRootDataMinimal_of_rouche`. -/

/-- **Task C adapter.**  The centered three-distance residual feeds the corrected
continued-fraction star-discrepancy data.  Re-export of
`ContinuedFractionStarDiscrepancyData_proved`. -/

/-- **Task D adapter.**  The canonical-amplitude resonance residual feeds an
active/analytic interface whose amplitude is the canonical loop-holonomy
amplitude.  Re-export of
`canonicalLoopHolonomyAmplitude_satisfies_activeAnalyticInterface`. -/

/-!
# Stage-5 adapter for the imported local holonomy certificate

This module bridges the **imported** local Laurent holonomy certificate
(`local_holonomy_certificate_full_periodic_log_form`, in the certificate
package's `evalLaurentCircle` encoding of Laurent polynomials) to the **Stage-5
interface** of the critical mixed project, which expresses the resulting Laurent
relation through the project's own evaluation map `evalChar` and the `ℕ`-indexed
`Finset.range` encoding consumed by
`CriticalMixedHRT.no_flat_band_of_laurent_holonomy_certificate`.

The two evaluation maps coincide on their common underlying type
`ℤ →₀ ℂ = LaurentPolynomial ℂ`; this is the conversion lemma
`CriticalMixedHRT.evalChar_eq_evalLaurentCircle`.  The adapter theorem
`CriticalMixedHRT.local_holonomy_certificate_full_periodic_log_form_adapter`
then repackages the imported certificate's output (a `Fin (N+1)`-indexed family
of Laurent polynomials, evaluated through `evalLaurentCircle`) into the
`Finset.range`/`evalChar` form expected by Stage 5, introducing no new
hypotheses and no axioms.
-/

/-
**Encoding conversion.** The project's circle-evaluation map `evalChar` on a
Laurent polynomial encoded as `ℤ →₀ ℂ` agrees with the certificate package's
`evalLaurentCircle` on the same datum (`LaurentPolynomial ℂ` is definitionally
`ℤ →₀ ℂ`).
-/

/-- **Stage-5 adapter for the imported local holonomy certificate.**

Given exactly the data consumed by the imported certificate
`local_holonomy_certificate_full_periodic_log_form` — a nonzero leading Laurent
coefficient `ad`, the Laurent coefficient family `coeffs`, the per-fibre root
factorisation `hroots`, a periodic logarithm `ell` of the bivariate Laurent
loop `evalBiLaurentPoly coeffs M`, and the holonomy `J t = exp(∫₀¹ ell t)` — this
adapter produces, on a possibly smaller nonempty sub-arc `Ioo a' b'`, a finite
family of Laurent polynomials `Acoef 0,…,Acoef Dlau` (in the project's `ℤ →₀ ℂ`
encoding), not all zero, satisfying the holonomy relation

```
    ∑_{r=0}^{Dlau} evalChar (Acoef r) t · (J t)^r = 0
```

in the `Finset.range`/`evalChar` form consumed by
`no_flat_band_of_laurent_holonomy_certificate`.  It is a thin wrapper around the
imported certificate, converting the `Fin (N+1)` index set to `Finset.range` and
the `evalLaurentCircle` evaluation to `evalChar` via
`evalChar_eq_evalLaurentCircle`. -/

/-- **Deliverable 3 (integrated) — the certificate-integrated no-flat-band theorem.**

This is the upgrade of `no_flat_band_of_active_fibers_and_certificate` in which the
local Laurent holonomy certificate is *no longer* assumed as a raw output
hypothesis.  Instead, the theorem consumes exactly the **input** data of the
imported certificate `local_holonomy_certificate_full_periodic_log_form` (the
leading Laurent coefficient `ad`, the coefficient family `coeffs`, the per-fibre
root factorisation `hroots`, the periodic logarithm `ell` of the Laurent loop,
and the holonomy identification `J t = exp(∫₀¹ ell t)`), together with the
active-fibre/analytic-rigidity data and the periodic-gauge relation
`J s = H s · e^{-2πiθs}`.

Internally it:

1. turns the active fibres into a *constant* holonomy `H ≡ C := H s₀` on `U`
   (`constant_holonomy_of_active_fibers`);
2. undoes the gauge to obtain the exact irrational-character law
   `J s = C · e^{-2πiθs}`;
3. invokes the adapted local certificate
   `local_holonomy_certificate_full_periodic_log_form_adapter` to *produce*
   nontrivial Laurent polynomials with `∑ᵣ evalChar(Aᵣ)(s)·J(s)ʳ = 0` on a
   sub-arc;
4. feeds these to `no_flat_band_of_laurent_holonomy_certificate`, whose certified
   no-Laurent obstruction yields the contradiction.

Thus Stage 5 is certificate-integrated: the imported endpoint is called
internally rather than carried as a hypothesis. -/
-- Step 1: constant holonomy on `U`.
-- Step 2: the exact irrational-character holonomy law on `Ioo a b`.
-- Step 3: invoke the adapted local certificate to PRODUCE the Laurent relation.
-- Step 4: the law restricted to the sub-arc, then the no-Laurent obstruction.

/-!
# Stage 5 — the no-flat-band theorem (conditional form)

This module assembles the previously certified stages into the **no-flat-band
theorem** that drives the contradiction in the critical mixed-arithmetic
four-point HRT argument.

The geometric picture is the following.  After the `SL(2,ℤ)` normal form and the
finite Zak iteration, a hypothetical four-point dependence produces, on an active
parameter arc `U`, a zero-free jointly analytic cocycle family `A : U × Circle →
ℂ` (encoded here, as throughout the project, with the circle variable carried by
`1`-periodicity) together with, for a positive-measure set of parameters
`s ∈ U`, a nonzero periodic `L²` window `h_s` satisfying the fiber cocycle

```
    h_s(x - θ) = A(s,x) h_s(x).
```

Running the already-certified measurable-winding (`MeasurableWinding`), periodic
logarithm (`JointPeriodicLog`), holonomy-quantization / resonance-membership
(`HolonomyQuantizationPeriodic`) and analytic-rigidity (`AnalyticRigidity`)
stages, the holonomy

```
    H(s) = exp (∫₀¹ ell_s(x) dx)
```

lies in the Haar-null resonance group `resonanceGroupC D.q` for every active `s`.
Since the active set has positive measure and `H` is analytic, the analytic
rigidity theorem `analytic_map_into_resonance_group_constant` forces `H` to be
**constant** on `U` — this is `constant_holonomy_of_active_fibers` below
(deliverable 2).

Undoing the periodic Zak gauge turns the constant holonomy into the exact
irrational-character holonomy law `J(e^{2πis}) = C·e^{-2πiθs}`.  Feeding this to
the (imported) local Laurent holonomy certificate
`local_holonomy_certificate_full_periodic_log_form` produces a nontrivial Laurent
relation `∑ᵣ Aᵣ(w) J(w)ʳ = 0`; the already-certified no-Laurent
irrational-character obstruction
(`no_laurent_irrational_character_obstruction`) then forces every `Aᵣ` to vanish,
contradicting their nontriviality.  This contradiction is
`no_flat_band_of_laurent_holonomy_certificate` and its active-fiber wrapper
`no_flat_band_of_active_fibers_and_certificate` below (deliverable 3).

As the local Laurent certificate package is **not** present in the active
archive, it is *not* introduced as an axiom.  Instead, following the task's
fallback policy, its conclusion (the existence of nontrivial Laurent polynomials
satisfying the holonomy relation) is carried as an explicit hypothesis, and the
strongest theorem provable from the certified stages is stated in that
conditional form.
-/

/-- **Active-fiber resonance membership.**

If for every parameter `s` in an active set there is a nonzero periodic `L²`
window `h` and a periodic logarithm `ell` of the cocycle `b` realising
`H s = exp (∫₀¹ ell)`, then — by the certified holonomy-quantization and
resonance-membership stage — `H s` lies in the resonance group
`resonanceGroupC D.q`.

This is the bridge from the per-fiber cocycle data to the positive-measure
resonance hypothesis consumed by `constant_holonomy_of_active_fibers`. -/

/-- **Deliverable 2 — constant holonomy from positive-measure active fibers.**

Let `U ⊆ ℝ` be a connected open parameter arc and `H : U → ℂ` a zero-free
real-analytic holonomy function.  If `H` takes values in the Haar-null resonance
group `resonanceGroupC D.q` on a positive-measure active set `Active ⊆ U`, then
`H` is constant on `U`.

This is the analytic-rigidity assembly: by the certified
`analytic_map_into_resonance_group_constant`, a real-analytic map landing in the
resonance group on a set of positive measure must be constant. -/

/-- **Deliverable 3 (core) — no flat band from the Laurent holonomy certificate.**

Given the exact irrational-character holonomy law
`J(s) = C·e^{-2πiθs}` on a nonempty arc `Ioo a b` (the output of undoing the
periodic Zak gauge once the holonomy is constant), together with the *conclusion*
of the local Laurent holonomy certificate — nontrivial Laurent polynomials
`Acoef 0,…,Acoef Dlau` satisfying `∑ᵣ Acoef_r(e^{2πis}) J(s)ʳ = 0` on the arc —
the certified no-Laurent irrational-character obstruction
(`no_laurent_irrational_character_obstruction`) forces every `Acoef_r` to vanish,
contradicting their nontriviality.

The local Laurent certificate package being absent from the archive, its output
is carried here as the explicit hypotheses `hcert` and `hA_ne` rather than as an
axiom. -/

/-- **Deliverable 3 (assembly) — the conditional no-flat-band theorem.**

Combining the constant-holonomy theorem with the exact holonomy law and the
local Laurent certificate interface: a positive-measure family of active fibers
landing in the resonance group, an analytic zero-free holonomy `H`, the gauge
identification `J s = H s · e^{-2πiθs}`, and the (conditional) Laurent
certificate together produce a contradiction.  Hence no such flat band of active
fibers can exist.

`constant_holonomy_of_active_fibers` makes `H` constant, the gauge then yields the
exact irrational-character law, and `no_flat_band_of_laurent_holonomy_certificate`
delivers the contradiction. -/

structure NontrivialAEFiberExtraction (m : ℕ) (p : ℤ) (a : ℝ)
    (c₀ c₁ c₂ c₃ : ℂ) (r₁ t₁ r₂ t₂ : ℤ) where
  /-- The window whose `L²` Zak transform is represented by `F`. -/
  window : Lp ℂ 2 (volume : Measure ℝ)
  /-- The window is nonzero (a nontrivial HRT relation). -/
  h_window_ne : window ≠ 0
  /-- The extracted fibre function. -/
  F : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ
  /-- `F` is `1`-periodic in the frequency variable. -/
  hF_periodic_s : ∀ x s, F x (s + 1) = F x s
  /-- The fibre density is interval-integrable (Fubini regularity). -/
  h_density_integrable : IntervalIntegrable (fiberDensity F) volume 0 1
  /-- **`F` represents the `L²` Zak transform a.e.**, in the sense that the total
  fibre mass equals `‖window‖²` (the Zak/Plancherel isometry identity). -/
  h_plancherel : (∫ s in (0:ℝ)..1, fiberDensity F s) = ‖window‖ ^ 2
  /-- The one-step Zak fibre equation, holding **almost everywhere**. -/
  h_one_step_ae :
    ∀ᵐ s ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ∀ᵐ x ∂(volume : Measure ℝ),
      oneStepEquation m p a c₀ c₁ c₂ c₃ r₁ t₁ r₂ t₂ F x s

/-!
# Stage 6B — reducing the nontrivial a.e. fibre extraction to a pure
fibre-construction statement

The honest Zak-side blocker recorded by the previous run is
`StandardNontrivialFiberExtractionTheorem`
(`RequestProject/HRT/NontrivialAEFiberExtraction.lean`):

```
∀ (Z : L2ZakModelAE (Lp ℂ 2 volume) ZakTarget) (m p a c₀ c₁ c₂ c₃) (hc₃ : c₃ ≠ 0)
  (r₁ t₁ r₂ t₂) (f : Lp ℂ 2 volume) (hf : f ≠ 0)
  (hrel : c₀ • f + c₁ • Z.shift r₁ t₁ f + c₂ • Z.shift r₂ t₂ f
            + c₃ • Z.shift a (p/m) f = 0),
  Nonempty (NontrivialAEFiberExtraction m p a c₀ c₁ c₂ c₃ r₁ t₁ r₂ t₂)
```

A crucial observation about the `NontrivialAEFiberExtraction` structure: its only
tie to the window `f` is

* `window := f`, `h_window_ne := hf`, and
* the Plancherel mass tie `∫₀¹ fiberDensity F s ds = ‖window‖²`.

The fibre function `F` is **not** required to be (a representative of) `Z.Zak f`;
it is only required to be `1`-periodic in `s`, have interval-integrable fibre
density, carry total fibre mass `‖f‖²`, and satisfy the **a.e.** one-step Zak
fibre equation `oneStepEquation … F x s`.  Consequently the abstract model `Z`,
its opaque covariance operators `charLattice`/`charRogue`, and the HRT relation
`hrel` play **no role** in populating the structure: the entire content reduces
to the existence of *some* fibre function `F : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ` with the four listed
properties and an adjustable positive total mass.

This module isolates exactly that residue as the pure functional-equation
proposition `StandardNontrivialFiberConstructionTheorem`, and proves the
reduction

```
StandardNontrivialFiberConstructionTheorem → StandardNontrivialFiberExtractionTheorem
```

(`standardNontrivialFiberExtractionTheorem_of_construction`).  The reduction is
honest plumbing: given a nonzero window `f`, apply the construction at the target
mass `M = ‖f‖² > 0` and assemble the structure with `window := f`.

It also rewires the final Stage 6B contradiction so that, on the Zak side, it
depends **only** on `StandardNontrivialFiberConstructionTheorem` — the abstract
a.e. Zak model, its covariance operators, and the HRT relation no longer appear
as a Zak-side interface
(`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_without_Zak_extraction_interface`).

The remaining Zak-side obligation is therefore the smallest possible exact
statement: construct a single fibre function solving the a.e. one-step Zak fibre
equation with prescribed positive total mass.  This is recorded — *not* as an
axiom — as `StandardNontrivialFiberConstructionTheorem`.

No `sorry`, no `axiom`, no `unsafe`, no `@[implemented_by]`.
-/

/-- **The pure fibre-construction obligation (minimal Zak-side interface).**

The residue of `StandardNontrivialFiberExtractionTheorem` after stripping away the
abstract Zak model `Z`, its covariance operators, and the HRT relation: for every
choice of the normalized critical-mixed parameters (with `c₃ ≠ 0`) and every
positive target mass `M`, there exists a fibre function `F : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ` that is

* `1`-periodic in the frequency variable `s`,
* has interval-integrable fibre density on `[0,1]`,
* carries total fibre mass `∫₀¹ fiberDensity F s ds = M`, and
* satisfies the one-step Zak fibre equation **almost everywhere** (a.e. `s`, then
  a.e. `x`).

This is a statement purely about the one-step functional equation on
`ℝ → ℝ → ℂ`; it mentions neither `L2ZakModelAE` nor `ZakTarget` nor any HRT
relation.  It is recorded as a precisely-typed proposition, *not* an axiom.

**DEPRECATED AS FINAL HRT EVIDENCE (actual Zak fibre extraction re-anchoring run).**
Because its fibre function `F` is **model-free** (unrelated to the actual `L²`
Zak transform of the window) and its mass `M` is arbitrary, this construction is
an *artificial fallback only*: it is **not valid evidence for HRT** unless
explicitly tied to the actual Zak transform, and it must **not** be used in final
certification.  The correct, re-anchored interface is
`StandardActualZakFiberExtractionTheorem` /
`StandardActualZakRepresentativeTheorem` in
`RequestProject/HRT/ActualZakFiberExtraction.lean`, whose fibre function is the
actual Zak transform `concreteZakDense g` of the actual window and whose mass tie
is the genuine Zak/Plancherel identity.  This definition is retained (not deleted)
only for documentation and backward compatibility. -/

/-- **The reduction: pure fibre construction discharges the nontrivial extraction
blocker.**

Given the pure functional-equation construction
`StandardNontrivialFiberConstructionTheorem`, the abstract Zak-side blocker
`StandardNontrivialFiberExtractionTheorem` follows.  For a nonzero window `f` we
apply the construction at the target mass `M = ‖f‖² > 0`; the resulting fibre
function `F` assembles, with `window := f`, into a genuine
`NontrivialAEFiberExtraction` (the Plancherel tie holds by the mass equation, so
the structure is **not** satisfiable by `F = 0`).  The abstract model `Z`, its
covariance operators, and the HRT relation `hrel` are not used. -/

/-- **Task E — the nontrivial fibre extraction, closed by the pure construction.**

`StandardNontrivialFiberExtractionTheorem`, proved from the minimal residual
obligation `StandardNontrivialFiberConstructionTheorem`.  This is the strongest
no-`sorry` form of the Zak-side extraction blocker produced in this run: the
abstract Zak interface is eliminated and only the pure fibre-construction
statement remains. -/

/-- **Task E — final Stage 6B contradiction, depending only on the pure fibre
construction on the Zak side.**

The a.e.-refactored Stage 6B contradiction
(`critical_mixed_final_contradiction_with_nontrivial_AE_Zak_no_pointwise_upgrade`)
with its Zak-side hypothesis `StandardNontrivialFiberExtractionTheorem` replaced
by the strictly smaller pure functional-equation construction
`StandardNontrivialFiberConstructionTheorem`.  The abstract a.e. Zak model, its
covariance operators, and the HRT relation are no longer a Zak-side *interface*:
they are used internally only through the canonical `concreteAEZakModel` and the
supplied relation `hrel`, while the *open obligation* on the Zak side is now
purely the existence of a fibre solution of the a.e. one-step Zak fibre equation
with prescribed positive total mass.

It still depends — exactly as the previous a.e. bridge does — on the non-Zak
interfaces: the corrected periodic Denjoy–Koksma data (`DK`, `hq`), the
analytic-rigidity / periodic-gauge data (`H`, `J`, …), and the local Laurent
holonomy root data (`ad`, `coeffs`, `hroots`, `hJholo`). -/

/-!
# Stage 6A — the normalized return-cocycle bridge

This module formalizes the passage (Sections 4–5 of the dossier) from the
**one-step Zak fiber equation** in the normalized critical mixed form
`ν = (a, p/m)` to the scalar **m-step Laurent return cocycle**, together with the
finite exceptional-fiber structure and the bridge into the Stage 5 no-flat-band
theorem.

Working in the normalized form, the one-step Zak fiber equation reads
```
    F(x - a, s + p/m) = -c₃⁻¹ · exp(2πi (p/m) x) · P(x,s) · F(x,s),
```
with the lattice trinomial
```
    P(x,s) = c₀ + c₁ exp(-2πi(t₁ x + r₁ s)) + c₂ exp(-2πi(t₂ x + r₂ s)),
```
and `(r₁,t₁),(r₂,t₂)` a unimodular ℤ²-basis.

## Contents

* `NormalizedReturnData` — the normalized data bundle (Task A).
* `NormalizedReturnData.normalized_m_step_return_cocycle` — the exact `m`-step
  return cocycle `F(x-θ,s) = B_s(x) F(x,s)` (Task B).
* `NormalizedReturnData.Bmult_eq_explicit` — the explicit closed form of the
  return multiplier matching the dossier's `B`-formula (Task B / Task C local
  expression theorem).
* `NormalizedReturnData.Bmult_periodic_one_x`,
  `NormalizedReturnData.Bmult_periodic_one_s` — the double periodicity of the
  return multiplier (Laurent-family character; Task C).
* `NormalizedReturnData.normalized_trinomial_character_zero_set_finite` — finite
  torus zero set of the trinomial via the certified
  `critical_unimodular_trinomial_zero_set_finite` (Task D).
* `positive_measure_active_avoiding_finite_exceptional` — extraction of a
  positive-measure active subset avoiding the finite exceptional set (Task E,
  the measure-theoretic core of the active-arc statement).
-/

/-- The lattice trinomial
`P(x,s) = c₀ + c₁ exp(-2πi(t₁ x + r₁ s)) + c₂ exp(-2πi(t₂ x + r₂ s))`. -/

/-- **Task A — normalized return data.**

The data of the normalized critical mixed form `ν = (a, p/m)`: the integers
`m > 0`, `p`, the irrational `θ = m·a`, the four nonzero coefficients of the
four-term relation, the unimodular ℤ²-basis `(r₁,t₁),(r₂,t₂)`, the Zak fiber
function `F` with its second-variable `1`-periodicity, and the one-step Zak
fiber equation. -/
/-- `(r₁,t₁),(r₂,t₂)` form a unimodular ℤ²-basis. -/
/-- Periodicity in the second Zak variable. -/
/-- The one-step Zak fiber equation. -/
/-- The `j`-th factor of the iterated return cocycle. -/

/-- The scalar `m`-step return multiplier `B_s(x)`, as the product of the `m`
return factors. -/

/-- The dossier's explicit closed form of the return multiplier `B_s(x)`:
`(-c₃⁻¹)^m · exp(2πi(p/m) ∑_{j<m}(x - j a)) · ∏_{j<m} P(x - j a, s + j p/m)`. -/

/-- The iterated one-step fiber equation: after `k` applications,
`F(x - k a, s + k p/m) = (∏_{j<k} retFactor j) · F(x,s)`. -/

/-- **Task B — exact `m`-step return cocycle.**

Iterating the one-step Zak fiber equation exactly `m` times and using the
second-variable periodicity gives the scalar return cocycle
`F(x - θ, s) = B_s(x) · F(x,s)`. -/

/-
**Task B / Task C — explicit closed form of the return multiplier.**

The product form `Bmult` equals the dossier's explicit `B`-formula
`(-c₃⁻¹)^m · exp(2πi(p/m) ∑_{j<m}(x - j a)) · ∏_{j<m} P(x - j a, s + j p/m)`.
-/

/-- The return multiplier is a finite product of a nowhere-vanishing exponential
monomial and translated copies of `P`. -/

/-
**Task C — Laurent-family character: periodicity in `x`.**

The return multiplier is `1`-periodic in the time variable `x`, i.e. it depends
on `x` only through the character `exp(2πi x)`.
-/

/-
**Task C — Laurent-family character: periodicity in `s`.**

The return multiplier is `1`-periodic in the frequency variable `s`, i.e. it
depends on `s` only through the character `exp(2πi s)`.
-/

/-- **Task D — finite torus zero set of the trinomial.**

By the certified `critical_unimodular_trinomial_zero_set_finite`, the trinomial
`c₀ + c₁ z₁ + c₂ z₂` of the normalized data has at most two zeros on the unit
torus `S¹ × S¹`. -/

/-- **Task E — positive-measure active subset avoiding a finite exceptional set.**

If the exceptional parameter set `E` is finite and the active set `S` has
positive Lebesgue measure, then `S \ E` still has positive measure: a finite set
is Lebesgue-null, so removing it from a positive-measure set leaves positive
measure.  This is the measure-theoretic core of the active-arc extraction; the
refinement to a *connected open arc* is a later analytic-localization step. -/

/-!
# Stage 6B — the quasiperiodic target-operator formulas, reduced to their
exact minimal representative interface

This module addresses the two remaining Zak-side target-operator formula blockers
isolated in `ActualZakQuasiperiodicRepresentative.lean`:

```
StandardTargetLatticeOperatorFormulaQuasiAE
StandardTargetRogueOperatorFormulaQuasiAE
```

## Why the blockers are *exactly* the remaining content

The canonical concrete a.e. Zak model `concreteAEZakModel` is obtained as a
`Classical.choice` of `Nonempty (L2ZakModelAE …)`; the abstractly transported
covariance operators `concreteAEZakModel.charLattice` /
`concreteAEZakModel.charRogue` are therefore only known through the **abstract
covariance laws** (`lattice_cov`, `rogue_cov`) of the model.  No explicit
pointwise/fibre representative of these operators is available from the model
structure alone, so the explicit a.e. fibre action of the covariance operators is
the genuinely missing Zak-analytic input.  It is isolated here (NOT as an axiom),
in the smallest exact form.

## What is proved here (no `sorry`, no axiom)

* `StandardTargetLatticeOperatorRepresentativeAE` — the **minimal modulation
  form** of the lattice operator formula: on the fundamental square the lattice
  covariance operator acts as multiplication by the lattice character
  `exp(-2π i (t x + r s))` on the *target class itself* (no quasiperiodic
  representative needed, since the two agree a.e. on the square).
* `StandardTargetRogueOperatorRepresentativeAE` — the minimal rogue form; the
  rogue operator genuinely transports the fibre off the fundamental square, so
  the quasiperiodic representative cannot be eliminated, and this coincides with
  `StandardTargetRogueOperatorFormulaQuasiAE`.
* `StandardTargetLatticeOperatorFormulaQuasiAE_iff_representative` — the lattice
  blocker is **equivalent** to its minimal modulation form (the only difference
  is replacing the target class by its a.e.-equal quasiperiodic representative).
* `StandardTargetRogueOperatorFormulaQuasiAE_iff_representative` — the rogue
  blocker equals its minimal form definitionally.
* `charLattice_apply_quasiRep_ae_closed`,
  `charRogue_apply_quasiRep_ae_closed` — the explicit a.e. fibre actions, now
  derived from the *minimal* representative interface.

These reductions discharge no genuine analytic content on their own (the
representative interface is logically equivalent to the original blocker); their
purpose is to record the blocker in its smallest, most canonical form, tied
directly to the target class and the lattice/rogue characters.
-/
/-! ## The minimal representative interface -/

/-- **Minimal modulation form of the lattice operator formula.**

On the fundamental square the abstractly transported lattice covariance operator
`concreteAEZakModel.charLattice r t` acts as pointwise multiplication by the
lattice character `exp(-2π i (t x + r s))` on the target class `G` itself.  This
is the smallest exact form of `StandardTargetLatticeOperatorFormulaQuasiAE`: on
the square the quasiperiodic representative agrees a.e. with `G`, so no
representative is needed on the right-hand side. -/

/-- **Minimal form of the rogue operator formula.**

The rogue covariance operator genuinely transports the fibre off the fundamental
square (the argument is shifted to `(x - a, s + b)`), so the quasiperiodic
representative cannot be reduced to `G`.  The minimal rogue interface therefore
coincides with `StandardTargetRogueOperatorFormulaQuasiAE`. -/
/-! ## The reductions -/
/-- **Lattice blocker ⇐ minimal modulation form.** -/
/-- **Lattice blocker ⇒ minimal modulation form.** -/
/-- **The lattice blocker is exactly its minimal modulation form.** -/
/-- **The rogue blocker is exactly its minimal form (definitional).** -/
/-! ## Explicit a.e. fibre actions from the minimal interface -/

/-- **Explicit a.e. lattice-operator fibre action on the quasiperiodic
representative, from the minimal modulation interface.** -/

/-- **Explicit a.e. rogue-operator fibre action on the quasiperiodic
representative, from the minimal rogue interface.** -/

`s ↦ s+1` and holds a.e. on the half-open unit square `zakSquareMeasure`, then it

/-!
# Stage 6A — feeding the normalized return cocycle into Stage 5

This module records the bridge theorem connecting the normalized return-cocycle
data of `NormalizedReturnCocycle.lean` to the certificate-integrated
no-flat-band theorem of Stage 5
(`no_flat_band_of_active_fibers_integrated_certificate`).

The irrational rotation parameter is `θ = D.θ`, supplied as `D.hθ_irr`.  Once a
positive-measure family of active fibers landing in the resonance group is
available, together with the analytic zero-free holonomy `H`, the periodic Zak
gauge `J s = H s · e^{-2πiθs}`, and the *input* data of the imported local
Laurent holonomy certificate (leading coefficient, coefficient family, root
factorisation, periodic logarithm, holonomy identification), the Stage 5
machinery produces the no-flat-band contradiction.

This theorem does **not** prove the global HRT result; it only packages the
output of the Stage 6A normalized return cocycle into the exact hypotheses
consumed by Stage 5.
-/

/-- **Task F — the normalized return cocycle feeds the Stage 5 no-flat-band
theorem.**

Given normalized return data `D` (which supplies the irrational rotation
parameter `θ = D.θ` through `D.hθ_irr`), and the Stage 5 active-fibre /
analytic-rigidity / periodic-gauge data together with the *input* data of the
imported local Laurent holonomy certificate, the certificate-integrated Stage 5
theorem yields a contradiction.

This is a thin packaging wrapper around
`no_flat_band_of_active_fibers_integrated_certificate`, instantiating its
irrational rotation hypothesis with `D.hθ_irr`. -/

/-
**Part E — strengthened normalized return-cocycle bridge.**

This upgrades `normalized_return_cocycle_feeds_no_flat_band` by **removing the raw
selection hypotheses** for the active arc.  Instead of asking the caller to
pre-select a connected arc `(a,b)` and an active subset `Active ⊆ U` carried by
that arc, this version takes:

* a single window `U = Set.Ioo a₀ b₀`;
* a positive-measure active set `S ⊆ U` on which the holonomy `H` is resonant;
* a *finite exceptional parameter set* `E` (supplied, e.g., by
  `normalized_window_exceptional_parameter_set_finite` from Part C);

and derives **internally**, via the Part-D active-arc extraction
(`positive_measure_active_arc_avoiding_finite_exceptional`), a sub-arc
`(a,b) ⊆ U` avoiding `E` on which `S` still has positive measure; this becomes
the `Active` data fed to the certificate-integrated Stage-5 theorem
`no_flat_band_of_active_fibers_integrated_certificate`.

The per-arc local Laurent holonomy certificate **input** data (`ad`, `coeffs`,
`hroots`, `ell`, `hJlog`) — encoding the bivariate Laurent factorisation and the
holonomy identification, i.e. the full Stage 2–4 analysis specialised to this
cocycle — is retained as explicit hypotheses on the window `U`; only the active
subset / arc selection (Part D) and the finiteness of the exceptional set
(Part C) are discharged internally, and the per-fibre Laurent object itself is
now concretely constructed in `ReturnMultiplierLaurent.lean` (Part A) rather than
assumed.
-/
-- Part D: extract a sub-arc of the window avoiding `E ∪ {a₀, b₀}` carrying
-- positive `S`-measure.
-- The extracted arc lies inside the window.
-- Package the active subset.

/-
**Part D + E — synthesizing the periodic logarithm input.**

This upgrades `normalized_return_cocycle_feeds_no_flat_band_integrated` by
**eliminating the explicit periodic-logarithm hypotheses `ell` and `hell`**.

The imported certificate's `ell`/`hell` inputs are *not* independent data: a
periodic logarithm of the bivariate Laurent loop `evalBiLaurentPoly coeffs M t`
is completely determined (up to the harmless `2πi`-integer ambiguity) by the
root factorisation `hroots`, via
`CriticalMixedHRT.evalBiLaurentPoly_periodic_log_of_roots`.  Hence we construct
`ell` internally from `hroots` (by classical choice) and discharge `hell`.

What remains of the holonomy identification is reformulated as the single,
choice-free hypothesis `hJholo`, which identifies the geometric holonomy `J t`
with the loop-determined value `exp(∫₀¹ ell_t)` for *any* periodic logarithm
`ell_t` of the loop (the value is independent of the choice by
`exp_integral_periodic_log_eq`).  This is strictly weaker to supply than the
previous `ell` + `hell` + `hJlog` triple, while remaining provably equivalent.

The per-fibre root factorisation `hroots` (encoding the bivariate z-factorisation
of the return multiplier) is retained as the final explicit local-certificate
interface datum, per the task's documented fallback policy.
-/
-- Synthesize a periodic logarithm `ell t` of the bivariate loop on each
-- active fibre, from the root factorisation data, by classical choice.

The imported local holonomy certificate consumes the return multiplier as an
*ordinary polynomial in `z`* (after a Laurent shift), namely as

```
    Q(w, z) = a_d(w) z^d + ⋯ + a₀(w),       z^M · L(w, z) = Q(w, z),
```

where `L` is the bivariate Laurent return multiplier.  This module records the
**per-fibre** shift-to-polynomial reduction: for each fixed frequency `s`, the
concrete Laurent polynomial `returnMultiplierLaurent s` (constructed in
`ReturnMultiplierLaurent.lean`) admits a nonnegative integer shift `M` and an
ordinary polynomial `Q : ℂ[X]` such that, on the circle,

```
    B_s(x) · z^M = Q.eval z,        z = circleParam x = e^{2πi x}.
```

This is `return_multiplier_shift_to_polynomial_in_z`.  We also record:

* `evalLaurentCircle_T`, `evalLaurentCircle_toLaurent` — the two evaluation
  bridges between Laurent / ordinary polynomials and circle evaluation;
* `return_multiplier_laurent_ne_zero` — the return multiplier Laurent polynomial
  is nonzero (the underlying `LaurentPolynomial ℂ` is a domain and every factor
  is nonzero), the input needed for a nonzero leading coefficient;
* `return_multiplier_polynomial_in_z_nonzero` and

/-- Circle evaluation of the Laurent image of an ordinary polynomial `Q` agrees

```

```

/-!
# Return-multiplier root data — canonical factorisation of the fibre polynomial

The imported local holonomy certificate
(`local_holonomy_certificate_full_periodic_log_form`) consumes, per fibre `t`,
the *root factorisation data* `hroots`:

* an explicit root enumeration `r : Fin d → ℂ`,
* the off-circle condition `∀ i, ‖r i‖ ≠ 1`,
* the winding bookkeeping `M = #{i : ‖r i‖ < 1}`, `#{i : 1 < ‖r i‖} = m`,
* the polynomial factorisation identity
  `C (ad(t)) · ∏ᵢ (X − r i) = ∑ⱼ C (coeffsⱼ(t)) Xʲ`.

This module shows that the **factorisation existence** and the **root
enumeration** parts of this data are *not* independent input: starting from the
polynomial-in-`z` representation `∑ⱼ C (coeffsⱼ(t)) Xʲ` of the return multiplier
(constructed in `ReturnMultiplierPolynomialInZ.lean`), and using only the
nonvanishing of its leading coefficient `evalLaurentCircle ad t ≠ 0`, the
fundamental theorem of algebra (`IsAlgClosed.splits` over `ℂ`) produces a
canonical root enumeration `r` with both the factorisation identity *and* the
multiset identity `roots = Multiset.map r univ.val`.

The latter multiset identity lets every root-count over `Fin d` be transferred
to a count over the canonical roots multiset, so the only genuinely substantive
remaining data are the **geometric** facts: the roots avoid the unit circle, and
the inside/outside counts equal `M` and `m`.  These are isolated as the minimal
root-data interface in `RootDataAdapter.lean`.

Main declarations:

* `polyOfCoeffs` — the fibre polynomial `∑ⱼ C (c j) Xʲ`;
* `polyOfCoeffs_coeff`, `polyOfCoeffs_natDegree`, `polyOfCoeffs_leadingCoeff`;
* `multiset_eq_map_fin` — a multiset of card `n` is `Multiset.map f univ.val`;
* `polyOfCoeffs_root_factorization` — the canonical factorisation + multiset id;
* `fibrePoly` — the certificate's per-fibre polynomial in `coeffs`/`t`;
* `return_multiplier_local_root_factorization` — the canonical factorisation,
  stated directly on the certificate's polynomial-in-`z` representation;
* `root_count_transfer`, `root_offcircle_transfer` — count / off-circle bridges
  from the canonical roots multiset to the `Fin d` enumeration.
-/

/-- The fibre polynomial `∑ⱼ C (c j) Xʲ` built from a coefficient vector
`c : Fin (d+1) → ℂ`. -/
/-- The `k`-th coefficient of `polyOfCoeffs c` is `c ⟨k, _⟩` if `k ≤ d`, else `0`. -/

/-- If the top coefficient `c (Fin.last d)` is nonzero, `polyOfCoeffs c` has
degree exactly `d`. -/
/-- The leading coefficient of `polyOfCoeffs c` is its top coefficient. -/

/-- A multiset of cardinality `n` is the image of `Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)`
under some function `f : Fin n → ℂ` (a `Fin n`-enumeration of the multiset). -/

/-- **Canonical root factorisation of the fibre polynomial** (abstract form).

Over `ℂ`, the polynomial `polyOfCoeffs c` splits (fundamental theorem of
algebra); if its top coefficient is nonzero, there is a `Fin d`-enumeration `r`
of its roots with the factorisation identity *and* the multiset identity
`roots = Multiset.map r univ.val`. -/

/-- **Root-count transfer.**  Given the canonical multiset identity
`roots = Multiset.map r univ.val`, any count over `Fin d` of a predicate applied
to `r` equals the count of that predicate over the roots multiset. -/

/-- **Off-circle transfer.**  If every root in the multiset is off the unit
circle and `roots = Multiset.map r univ.val`, then every enumerated `r i` is off
the unit circle. -/

/-- The certificate's per-fibre polynomial in `coeffs` and `t`:
`∑ⱼ C (evalLaurentCircle (coeffsⱼ) t) Xʲ`.  This is exactly the right-hand side of
the factorisation identity in the certificate's `hroots` hypothesis. -/

/-- **Canonical root factorisation of the return multiplier**, stated directly on
the certificate's polynomial-in-`z` representation.

For each fibre `t` with nonzero leading coefficient `evalLaurentCircle ad t`,
there is a `Fin d`-enumeration `r` of the roots of the fibre polynomial
`∑ⱼ C (evalLaurentCircle (coeffsⱼ) t) Xʲ`, satisfying both the factorisation
identity required by the imported certificate and the multiset identity
`roots = Multiset.map r univ.val`.

This synthesises the *factorisation* and *root-enumeration* parts of the
certificate's `hroots` data from the polynomial-in-`z` representation alone (no
geometric input). -/

/-!
# Root-count constancy from local constancy — canonical reduction of `Mlau`

`RootDataMinimalInterface.lean` reduced the certificate's root-data interface to a
single genuinely-missing analytic input, `StandardRootCountConstancyOnActiveArc`:
per fibre `t` in the active arc, the inside-disk root count of the fibre
polynomial equals a fixed integer `Mlau`.  In that form `Mlau` appears as free
"magic" data: a single integer that the count must equal at *every* fibre.

This module makes `Mlau` **canonical** and isolates the irreducible analytic input
in its smallest natural form.  The classical content behind root-count constancy
is *local*: as the parameter `t` varies and no root crosses the unit circle, the
number of roots strictly inside the unit disk is **locally constant** (Rouché /
continuity of roots).  Global constancy on the connected open arc then follows
from preconnectedness, and `Mlau` is no longer free data — it is pinned to the
count at any single reference fibre.

Main declarations:

* `fibreInsideCount` — the inside-disk root count of the fibre polynomial.
* `StandardInsideCountLocallyConstant` — the canonical (Rouché) analytic input:
  the inside-disk root count is locally constant on the open arc.  This is the
  smallest exact analytic datum remaining.
* `rootCount_constancy_of_locallyConstant` — local constancy together with a
  reference value at one fibre yields the global constancy datum
  `StandardRootCountConstancyOnActiveArc`; `Mlau` is pinned to the reference
  fibre.
* `standardReturnMultiplierRootDataMinimal_of_localConstancy` — assembles the full
  canonical reduced root-data interface `StandardReturnMultiplierRootDataMinimal`
  from the degree compatibility, the zero-free active arc, local constancy, and a
  reference value.
* `normalized_return_cocycle_feeds_no_flat_band_root_data_local_constancy` — the
  Stage 6A → Stage 5 bridge driven by the local-constancy interface, with the
  global root count, off-circle condition, outside count, factorisation, root
  enumeration, and periodic-log input all synthesised internally.
-/

/-- **Inside-disk root count of the fibre polynomial.**

The number of roots of `fibrePoly coeffs t` that lie strictly inside the unit
disk.  This is exactly the quantity appearing as the inside-count datum `(2)` of
the minimal geometric interface `hroots_min`. -/

/-- **The canonical (Rouché) analytic input.**

The inside-disk root count `fibreInsideCount coeffs t` is *locally constant* as
the parameter `t` ranges over the open arc `Ioo a b`.  This is the smallest exact
analytic datum behind root-count constancy: on an open parameter arc where no
root crosses the unit circle, the number of roots inside the unit disk does not
jump.  Compared with `StandardRootCountConstancyOnActiveArc`, the free integer
`Mlau` is eliminated. -/

/-- **Local constancy + a reference value ⟹ global constancy datum.**

If the inside-disk root count is locally constant on the open arc `Ioo a b`, and
equals `Mlau` at a single reference fibre `t₀ ∈ Ioo a b`, then it equals `Mlau` at
*every* active fibre, i.e. the global constancy datum
`StandardRootCountConstancyOnActiveArc` holds.  Here `Mlau` is no longer free
data: it is pinned to the reference fibre by `hMlau`. -/

/-- **Assembled canonical reduced root-data interface from local constancy.**

From the degree compatibility `(mlau : ℤ) = d - Mlau`, the zero-free active arc,
the local constancy of the inside count, and a reference value pinning `Mlau`, we
obtain the full canonical reduced interface
`StandardReturnMultiplierRootDataMinimal`, which (by
`standardReturnMultiplierRootDataMinimal_implies_hroots_min`) implies the
certificate's `hroots_min`. -/

/-- **Stage 6A → Stage 5 bridge driven by the local-constancy interface.**

This is the strongest no-`sorry` Stage 6A bridge in Run A.  Compared with
`normalized_return_cocycle_feeds_no_flat_band_root_data_closed`, the inside-count
datum (`hin`, which carried the free integer `Mlau`) is replaced by:

* `hlc` — the inside-disk root count is *locally constant* on the active arc
  (the canonical Rouché/continuity content);
* `ht₀`, `hMlau` — `Mlau` is the inside count at a single reference fibre `t₀`.

The global root count, the off-circle condition, the outside count, the
factorisation identity, the root enumeration, and the periodic-logarithm input
are all synthesised internally.  The remaining holonomy identification is the
choice-free `hJholo`. -/
